# Google Book Search

This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world's books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the copyright to expire and the book to enter the public domain. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that's often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other marginalia present in the original volume will appear in this file - a reminder of this book's long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

### Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to digitize public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

* *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
* *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
* *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
* *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

### About Google Book Search

Google's mission is to organize the world's information and to make it universally accessible and useful. Google Book Search helps readers discover the world's books while helping authors and publishers reach new audiences. You can search through the full text of this book on the web at `http://books.google.com/`

## [PDF Page 8 — Preface]

# P R E F A C E.

AFTER extraordinary delay, the Dictionary of the Nika Language in Eastern Equatorial Africa is at length given to the public. This language is described at page 355 of my "Modern Languages of Africa" (Trübner : 1883).

A fatality seemed to attend this work. A fair copy ready for the printer had been prepared by Rebmann, and had been seen and handled by many Missionaries. It is presumed to have found its way to Salisbury Square, but there is no further trace of its existence. Search has been made by Widow Rebmann at Kornthal, in Germany, and I myself, with her permission, in October, 1886, searched the book-case of her lamented husband, and brought away some scattered leaves of manuscript, but the bound volume has disappeared.

Fortunately, the rough copy was found among the papers sent to Salisbury Square, but several sheets were wanting. These lacunæ have been supplied by the Missionaries now in the field, and the whole has been edited by the Rev. T. H. Sparshott, a retired Missionary, and the best available scholar for the purpose.

**ROBERT CUST,**
*Member of Committee of Church Missionary and British and Foreign Bible Societies, and Foreign Translation Committee of the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge.*

LONDON,
*May* 14, 1887.

## [PDF Page 10 — Introduction (Page v)]

# INTRODUCTION.

IT having pleased God to call His two veteran servants, the Rev. Dr. Krapf and the Rev. J. Rebmann, to their rest, the Church Missionary Committee invited me to prepare the manuscript Dictionary of the Nika Language for the printer, and to see it through the press.

The work has taken much longer than the time estimated. The manuscripts were very imperfect, and there were notes on scores of odd pieces of paper; and the labour of putting all materials in their proper place, to avoid loss on the one hand and repetition on the other, was about double what I had calculated. I had hoped, too, to have had the invaluable assistance of my beloved wife, who had really given her life for Africa, and whose correct knowledge of the languages would have been of great help. Instead of this help, it was my lot to attend her as her strength declined, and to sorrow for her loss, while praising God for the blessed hope of her being for ever with the Lord.

The Mission among the Wa-Nika was commenced by Dr. Krapf in 1844, when expelled from Abyssinia. These tribes are about twelve in number, and speak the same language, with sundry dialectic variations. The first effort to reduce the language to writing was made by Krapf, and was followed up by Rebmann during twenty-nine years.

Many words are inserted without their meanings, and the great majority of the phrases are not translated. This is much to be regretted. I have inserted a con-

---

## [PDF Page 11 — Introduction (Page vi)]

**vi** — **INTRODUCTION.**

siderable number of both, but not where I had any doubt of accuracy.

The pronunciation of the language does not present any great difficulty to a European student. The German requires care to pronounce the dentals, and the Englishman requires the same care to give the vowels their continental sounds. The Arabic gutturals, which are pronounced in Ki-suahili, and which require patient perseverance, in an Englishman, to acquire, are softened down in Kinika. The **ع** is omitted; the **غ** becomes *g*; the **خ** becomes *h*; and the **ق** becomes *k*.

There has been some difficulty in deciding the accentuation, owing to a European standard having been imitated. The late Bishop Steere believed, and I think he was quite correct, that the natives invariably put the accent on the penultimate, and that two vowels like *ai* in *Rabai*, are really two syllables, and are pronounced *Ra-ba-i*, taking the accent according to the rule.

The transliteration is imperfect. The *b*'s and *p*'s, *d*'s and *t*'s, *f*'s and *v*'s, *s*'s and *z*'s, will often be found to be interchanged. Not having heard the language spoken for eight years before I commenced the work, I felt quite unequal to the task of attempting a correction of these letters, but have often put both writings together. The *th* has to do duty for two sounds, as in the English *thigh* and *thy*. The *t* has also two sounds—the common English sound, and a sound somewhat like a *th*, as in *Kisulutini*. The language is spoken with great accuracy, and the natives have a great natural eloquence, and are not slow to make a joke at a foreigner's mistakes.

**T. H. SPARSHOTT.**

CHOLMONDELEY PARSONAGE,
MALPAS, CHESHIRE,
*May*, 1887.

## [PDF Page 12 — Alphabet & Abbreviations (Page vii)]

**( vii )**

### ALPHABET.

THE alphabet used is as follows:— A, B, Ch, D, Dz, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P, R, S, T, U, V, W, Y, Z, the sound of each being explained as it comes in order in the work.

### ABBREVIATIONS.

* **K.** = Krapf, and indicates that in Rebmann's opinion further examination is necessary.
* **Kid.** = Kidigo, the dialect of the Wadigo.
* **Kig.** = Kigiriama, the dialect of the Wagiriama.
* **Kij.** = Kijomba, the Kinika for Kisuahili, the language of the Coast.
* **Kik.** = Kikamba, the language of the Wakamba.
* **Kim.** = Kimvita, the language of Mvita or Mombas.
* **Kins.** = Kiniasa, the language of the Waniasa.
* **Kir.** = Kiravai or Kirabai, the dialect of the Waravai.

## [PDF Page 14 — Dictionary Page 1 (A — Abe)]

# D I C T I O N A R Y
###### OF THE
# N I K A   L A N G U A G E.

**A,** (1) the first letter of the alphabet, uniformly pronounced as in "father."—[ED.]
(2) *Gen. particle*, of. Ya, ka, la, ma, na, and za are also used to denote the genitive case. They vary according to the class of nouns which they qualify.
(3) *Plural prefix*. Words beginning with Mu- in the singular form the plural by changing the *mu* into *a*: Mutu, a man, Atu, men.
(4) *Pron.*, used with the same class of nouns; they, them. Atu osi a kaya. *See* Chengera; Chinga.
(5) *Aux. v.*, 3rd pers. pl. *See* Mbawa; Ako. They are there. In composition, Aka, Ana, Adzi, Anda, Anga, Ari, Aere, Arie, Arivio, Ariko.
(6) The final letter of most of the verbs in this and cognate languages.
**Aa.** *See* Futa.
**Aba,** *n.* (= Baba), father. Used only with the poss. pron. Si-abaye gnania? Is he not the father of So-and-so? (= babaye). Na-mu ivuisira aba-yo wari-yanenda kaya, says a mother to her child. Resp., Babayo yabu uere.
**Abahe** (= Abau).
**Abau,** *adj.*, many. Atu hio, aojira hiva zi-airi wala si ahahu, ni abau (= angi).
**Abe,** *n.* (ya, pl. za). *See* Ame. Father, the male parent of men and animals. It is used for Baba with reference to men when the pron. pl. poss. is used: Abe-yehu; Abe-yenu; Abe-yao; Abe-yehu; Abe-zenu; Abe-zao; Abe-yao-ziratu gnombe-ni huya, or, Babe-yao, etc. Abe-Gunja, The father of Gunja. A parent thus takes the name of his son, the reverse of the Arab custom—Bin, son of. Sometimes, for the sake of distinction, the father's name is also retained: Abe-Chindua Muambawa, Muamba, the father of Chindua. Abe-Mkusi Dzama, Dzama, the father of Mkusi. Abe-mutu, The father of a man. Yudzi-kala abe-mutu mudzima. Abe-muana, The father of a child. Abe-muana yulavi? Abbrev., Abe-ana. Ni-abe-zenu? Are they your father's? Resp., Ni abezehu. Hara achirao ni abezenu, ni-bu-dze (= Hara achirao ni babazenu-nibudze).
**Abeviala,** *n.* *See* Ameviala. Fa-

ther-in-law. The word is being superseded by Baba in a general sense. Abe-vialayo yuvavo.
**Abisa, Apisa.** *See* Kikokoto. From Ku apa (Kij.). Na' nenda kua muganga, ni-ka-mu apise iye akaye hala kitu changu.
**Abudi, Abudu,** *n.* *See* Fioga. Doubt. Kana abudi (pronounced Kanabudi), There is no doubt. Sina abudi rero, kana ku ni riva. Sina abudi ela ku enenda mundani tu kuenda rima, I have no doubt but that I shall go to my field to cultivate it. Sina abudi rero, sudi u-ni-rive, or, Sudi ku ni riva, rero sinda-uka-sodi u-ni-rive. Kana abudi kana ku-m-tema tu. Neno hiro ni Kiduruma ka-ri-na-abudi, There is no doubt.
**Abuka** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to separate. Maneno higa-ni abuka (= Kig., Ndeto idzu iku-ni athuka = Kadziuka na-mi, or, Kadzidana na-mi). Mutu hiye abuka na na-ye-sihende ukienenda na ye, yunda ku guiza zani, or, yunda ku buma zani, Separate yourself from that man; do not go with him, he will cause you misfortune. Mutu hiye ni muivi uabukane naye, That man is a thief; separate yourselves from him.
**Ada, Ata,** *v.a.* (= Ku ela), to leave, to quit. Ku ata chingo. Ku ata mukoa.
**Adika, Atika, Achika,** (1) *v.n.* Chingo hi idzi achika tu.
(2) *v.a.* Mu-veni cho alonda cho asa-ni-atika-akani vo! si-ni atikeni (= si-ni hendereni lonso).
**Adira.** *See* Kakoa.
**Ada,** *n.* (ra and ya, pl. Maada and Adaza), custom.
**Adalia, Achalia, Ajalia,** *v.a.*, to grant. Mulungu aku-achalie afia na nguvu, May God grant you health and *strength*.
**Adi,** *n.* (ra) (= Magadi), rough soda (?).
**Adi.** *See* Nognonesa; Gusika. Ni maneno ya ku ika adzomba adi. Kitu kino nda-ku-va adi.
**Adi, Achi.** Hu-achi na Fimboni.
**Adina, Ajina.** *See* Mudina.
**Adui,** *n.* *See* Onia; Ruma; Ereka; Ndui; Udui. An enemy.
**Adzako.**
**Adzala** (Kig.), *v.a.* (= Idzala, Kir.).
**Adzano,** *adj.*, five.
**Adzarikiza,** *v.*, to fill up.
**Adzaza,** *v.a.*, to fill.
**Adzaye,** or **Adzeye.** *See* Dongoria; Karada; Kidzadza. Fumula simunga.
**Adzie.** *See* Dzeresa.
**Adzio.** *See* Mugafie; Adzavio, etc.
**Adzoko** (Kid.) (= Adzako).
**Aenzi, Ainzi, Enzi,** *n.* (pl. Maaenzi), power, authority. Atu hara ana maaenzi sana, These men have much power.
**Afia,** *n.* (ya), health. Luanda hilo luna vidziwe, ka-lu rimika, ka-lu-na-afia.
**Afia,** *v.a.* (= Ku lavia), (1) to cause to pass through an ordeal.
(2) To prove guilty by ordeal. Used only of God in this sense. *See* Ku afu. Mulungu yudzi-mu-afia (= Kiravo kidzi-m-guira).
**Afikana,** *v. reit.*, to agree in a bargain.
**Afiwa,** *v.p.*, to be proved guilty by ordeal. Yudzevia, basi-yudziafiwa, or, Yukuenda afiwa, yudzivia. Yukuenda afiwa, ela Mulungu yudzi-mu-afu, yudziakoka.
**Afu,** *v.a.*, to save, to prove guiltless by ordeal. Mulungu na-mu-afu. And may God save him. Mulungu yudzi-mu-afu yudziokoka.
**Afuisa,** *v.a.*, to help. Hudzikuenda ku-mu-afuiza ku dzuma. Na-mu-afuiza nguvu.
**Afuizana,** or **Afnizania,** *v. reit.*, to help one another.
**Afiere,** *n.* Pl. of Mufiere.
**Afufu, Ufufu** (K.), *n.*, a consistory.

**Amba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a reef in the sea. Ku fuma amba (or, Ku fumamba), To pilot past a reef. Maamba ga kambi gadzigura ni mafutia; ku ogova kambi hebudzi? Akariwa makota aka-i-futa. Amba ra zulu. *See* Nguo.
**Amba,** *v.a.*, (1) to pass. Ku amba ngoma, To beat a drum. Ku amba kitanda, na chingo, To cord a bedstead with chingo.
(2) *See* Chingira. To be about. Yudziamba, He was about. Nidziamba, na a kirimushe atu ela era abake kakashuka.
  **Ambala,** *v.a.* *See* Nambala. To measure. Ku ambala, or, Muambalo, wa murima, The extent of a mountain.
  **Ambana,** *v.n.*, to pass each other. Vitu vidziambana niunguni, ni muanzo wa ku via.
  **Ambaza,** *v.a.* *See* Chururika. To make pass along, to let pass along, by the side of a vessel. Munazi wangu udziambaza (kukafunga tu) kabaria kidzikobaka. Ukipiga kitamba, uchi ukigira na kanda, be ndo, ku ambaza.
  **Ambika,** *v.a.*, to fix. Ku ambika ludzadza (*see* Mfuo), To fix ludzadza in the water to catch fish.
  **Ambira,** *v.d.* Ku mu ambira ngoma.
  **Ambuka,** *v.n.*, to ascend a mountain. Not used in any other sense.
  **Ambusa,** *v.a.* Ku ambusa muzigo.
  **Ambusika,** *v.n.* Ka ku ambusika kanda hio murima ni mubomu.
  **Ambusira,** *v.d.* Der., Chamba; Chambo; Luambe; Muamba; Wambo.
**Amba,** *v.n.* *See* Larira; Mumiro; Kidia; Muigni. To say, to think. Gnania ukuenda-m-foya, wamba; "sina," He says you go to beg of him; not so. Wamba is used both in the pres. and imperf. tenses—he says, and he said. In the pres. it is used for Yuamba. *See* Malola, thou sayest. Amba ye ku amba (lit. saying to say), That in order that. Ki amba cho ri amba ro, etc. *See* Zumbe. Mkongo wa ambadze, Sick man, what sayest thou? = How art thou? Yudzi amba apigue, He said he would be beaten. *See* Chingira.
  **Ambana,** *v. ref.* *See* Dzunana.

## [PDF Page 19 — Dictionary Page 6 (Amb — Ana)]

  To say to one another, to converse.
  **Ambira,** *v.d.*, to say to, to tell. For the difference between Amba and Ambira, *see* Luambo.
  **Ambirika.**
  **Ambiriza,** *v.a.* *See* Niense. To sing, to make tingle. Said of the ear. Ku ambiriza kua kikokoto.
  **Ambua,** *v.p.* *See* Kidzupo; Fira. To be told. Ku-ambua ni mulongo, To be told (deceived) by a liar.
**Ambamba,** *adj.* *See* Rambamba. Lean, thin. Root of Chambamba, Muambamba, Niambamba, etc.
**Ambari,** *n.*, ambergris.
**Ambue.**
**Ambuka** (?), **Ambula** (?).
**Ame,** *n.*, mother. Used also in a general sense for aunt, elder woman, etc. Madzere ganadana na ame zao, etc. Ame viala wangu, The mother who bore me—my actual mother, in contradistinction to aunt, elder friend, etc. Ame mutu, A man's mother. Ame atu, The mother of people, used in a general sense (= mameye atu). *See* Mayo. Ame ngudu (*see* Ngudu), The mother of cowries, a shell larger than the common cowry. Ame zenu, Our mother. Ame yenu, Your mother. *See* Lamusua. Ame yao, Their mother. Ame yehu is not used, but simply Mayo, The mother. Ameyatu (contracted from Ame ya atu) akaye viala gnombe sisi sirise vava sosi-ni kuya-goma ra gnombe hiri rinaviala tu. Ameni-be! utu hiu udze? Ameni mambo gano gadze? (= Alumeni munda galaze mui, or, muino).
**Amekala,** *n.*
**Amia,** *v.n.*
**Amini,** *v.n.*, to believe, to trust.
**Amua,** *v.a.*, to suck.
  **Amuisha,** *v.a.*, to suckle.
**Amula,** *v.* *See* Gaga. To judge, to condemn. Amulani muimui; muimui mukere nao vilungoni. Ku amula kiriro. Atu adziamula viriro anarira. Ukifua, Mulungu yadzi ku amula?
  **Amulua,** *v.p.*, to be judged, condemned. Yudzi-lavia tia (pehe, etc.) yudzi-mu-amula nduguye avu ye, etc. Yudzi amulua ni mbari zao, na ku shongolua. Aye amula niani hata uki hendavio we? Aye ku amurira niani?
  **Amurira,** *v. rel.* Chogolo wa ku amurira kiriro cha muanza. Ku amurua ugnaro. *See* Guiere. Afiere ndio aamulao ugnaro, ela Mulungu yudzi amula, yudzi-hu-amurira amuri kumi, or, yudzi-hu-amurira kuamba hu hende kazi hino.
**Amuri,** *n.*, a command. Nidzi-m-lenga, ela ni amuri ya Mulungu kaka henza kuamba ni-m-fumage, niuni hiyu afue.
**Ana,** *v.*, to have. Ku ana niumba, To have a house. Nipa mavalu niane niumba, Give me poles, that I may have a house. Ku ana ngano, To have wheat.
  **Anamira,** *v. rel.* Ku anamira ni ku noa mura kirengeni. *See* Gudiugudiu. Yudzianamira uchi udzikala sinda. Yudzi-n'-amba ni-pa uchi, nidzumburire, be yudzi-u-anamira hata kirenge kidzikala sinda.
  **Anana,** *v.n.* (= Kuenda; Karakara), to tally with, to fit (as a lid). Binikiza nuingu tu, vianane. Nidzi-binikiza ki dzungo kidzi anana.
  **Ania,** *v.a.* (= Ku timiza), to complete. Sidza ngue ku ania, ni chari dema.
**Anika,** *v.n.*, to be finished, covered in. Niumba hi idzianika tu.
  **Anika,** *v.a.*, to spread, to cover. Nidzi anika madzere zangu, ela kagaka kauma, ka kuari na dzua.

## [PDF Page 20 — Dictionary Page 7 (Ana — Ang)]

  **Anikira,** *v.d.*
  **Anira,** *v.d.* *See* Gaula. Usave wa ku anira niumba. Nalaeka usave nianire, or, nivaerire. Mkauma aka anira Punga sana. Der., Danamiro; Daniro; Dano; Muana; Nganasa; Ngano.
**Anane,** *adj.*, eight.
**Andala,** *v.a.* Ku-mu-andala muchi.
**Andama,** *v.a.*, to follow after, to follow at some distance. Muivi aki-zolua, basi atu ni ku mu andama, The thief has gone, but men are following. Mutu akiuka mbere, be muyawe ni ku-mu-andama.
  **Andaniza,** *v.n.* *See* Kalangirua; Kudzi andaniza. To be sufficient. Nafuha porepore ku-dzi-andaniza. Madzi ni ga ku-dzi-andaniza; usipige malo bule; lit. There is water to please one's self; do not be in needless haste = There is plenty of water, so that you may draw whenever you like. *See* Ku anganira.
**Andi.** *See* Angi.
**Andika,** *v.a.*, to begin, to introduce, Ku niala ni ku andika ku ama (= ku anza ku uma).
  **Andikirana,** *v.* (?).
  **Andikua,** *v.p.*, to be fined. Aka-andikua malu ya mbuzi, He was fined a fine of a goat. Mutu hiye nahu-mu-andike malu bomu, ndo anda vo richa-yuna gnombe tano yuna gnombene. Udzi-andikua malu ya mbuzi mbiri, Thou art fined a fine of two goats.
**Andula,** *v.a.* *See* Koa. To strip off (as the fibre of a cocoa-nut). Opposed to Ku ambiga. Ku andula nazi, na kombe, na kigongo, etc., To strip off a cocoa-nut with a large nail or stick sharpened for the purpose. Nidzi-ambika ludzadza, basi bikara na-lu-andula (ku-lu-lafia). Der., Luanda; Muando; Chansa; Chanso.
**Ane,** *adj.*, four.
**Anga,** *verbal prefix*, 3rd pers. sing. and pl. in the conjugation Nga. *See* Hadi.
**Anga,** *v.a.* *See* Muani. To heal. Ndiye adzaye aki-anga? Kironda kina anga, peho ki luasa. Peho ina-anga kironda.
  **Angama,** *v.* Yudzebua ela yudziangama, ka kabuadzi (= Ku kuama and Ku sikua).
  **Angamika,** *v.n.*, to go astray, to be lost, to vanish.
  **Angamisa,** *v.a.* *See* Kosa.
  **Anganikua,** *v.p.* *See* Dukia.
  **Anganira,** *v.n.*, to go out (as a fire). Ndzo-hu-anganira moho, hu-u-zimie, usakuenda dzoma niumba za atu. Ndzoni, hu anganire muthia hiu, hu-a-zole. Narauka, nikahege madzi ni ga ku anganira.
  **Anganirua,** *v.p.* Ku anganirua ni atu.
**Angala** (Kid.), *v.n.* Mali hiyi idziangala. Viakue ka-vi-angala.
  **Angalala,** *v.n.* (= Sanga in Kij.). *See* Engelele; Nundu; Belewa. To be without advice, at a standstill, helpless.
  **Angalaza,** *v.n.*, to perplex, to admonish, to terrify. Kikuankuara kidzi ni angalaza maneno higo milomo hio-idzi-mu-angalaza. Utu ni-dzua-ambirua adzi-ni-angalaza, sika-idima ku nena. Ukongo uno, wa kikuadulo, udzi-ni-angalaza, This sickness, the whooping-cough, alarms me.
**Angasha,** *v.a.*, to surprise. Utu hia adzi-ni-angasha, This matter surprised me.
**Angaliani.** Yudzi usa angaliani.
**Angao.**
**Angavi,** *adj.*, how many.
**Angi,** *adj.*, many. Root of Mangi, etc.
**Angindo,** *n.* Pl. of Mungindo.
**Angira.** *See* Anga.
**Angira** (Kig.), *v.n.* (= Ingira in Kir.), to enter. Ku angira vitu ku niala. Peho yudzi, or, idzi, ni angira, A spectre

## [PDF Page 21 — Dictionary Page 8 (Ang — Ari)]

  appeared to me. Nidzi-kuenda va-vo-dzakani, nidziangirua.
  **Angirua,** *v.p.* Ku angirua ni masuka, Missal, book. Der., Wangu; Wanguangu; Muanguangu, etc.
**Ango,** *n.* (ra, pl. Maango). *See* Gangira. Any turn or twist made for a sign in tying a door, a bag, etc. Ku piga ango, To make a twist. Ku piga, nidzi funga, nidzi piga ango, pl. maango.
**Angu,** *poss. pron.*, my. Root of Wangu, Yangu, etc.
**Angue,** *n.* *See* Noerera. Angue ambue, Hearsay report. Kadzambue or Kadzangue. Prov., Angue nduguye ni ulongo, The brother of hearsay is a lie. *See* Kibini. Kikulu in ku ona megnie na madzo.
**Angura,** *n.* *See* Kifudu; Idula. Ku piga angura.
**Ani,** *inter. pron.* *See* Hala. Who. Ndiwe ani? Who art thou? Ni ani? Who is it? Adzie dumula uchi wangu ni ani?
**Anika.** *See* Ana.
**Anira.** *See* Ana.
**Ano.** Ano baba, ano mayo, ano kuro abe yao yuluavi? Ano muamkemba.
**Ano,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Fiarira; Dirira. Ano ni mufui usio dzambue ku buma kigumba, An arrow without the head or wing. The reed or wood of which arrows are made.
**Ansa,** *n.* (ra). Mulomo wa ansa. Ansa ra mwidza ra kambani, ra muezi-ya yombo.
**Ansa, Anza,** *v.a.* *See* Mugeni; Guiririra. To begin. Siansini sitadeni muka anzi arideni, a-mu-anze-ao ndivo hupigane, Do not taste, ye have begun, ye leave them, they begin with you, then let us fight. Sinda ku anza, ni anza uwe. Aye-mu-anza, muyawe niani?
  **Ansika.**
  **Ansira, Anzira,** *v.d.*, to begin to, for any one. Na gula nguo, ni mu ansire ndugu yangu, or, muchangu.
  **Ansirua, Anzirua,** *v.p.* Yudzianzirua nguo pia; lit. He has been commenced a new cloth = A new cloth has been given to him. Aki sikira muche yudziangirua ni nduguye, basi (fua?) aka-kudza-m-hala.
**Ansaza,** *v.a.* (= Dzansasa).
**Anula** (?).
**Ao,** *pron.* (pl.), (1) they; (2) these. Ao kua ao (K.), Each other.
**Ara,** *v.n.*, to spread, to go off (as the voice). Kitu changu kidziara, sinda-ki-ona, To be lost. Kitu kikiambua kidziara, basi ka-ki-yarua kaviro.
**Arau,** *adj.* *See* Rau; Aarau; Maarau; Viarau. Atu hia ni arau, be ni angi.
**Ari.** *See* Chari; Gari; Wari; Ari-ro ha ro, etc.
**Ari** (= Uduka). Kikuankuara kina arika.
**Aria,** *v.n.* *See* Lenga. Ku aria moro.
**Arie,** *pron.* *See* Mbawa; Dangamuka. Who is, which is, etc.
**Arika,** *v.n.* Mawe gaka arika.
**Arika,** *v.a.*, to circumcise, to marry, to buy, to beat, to strike. Ku arika pembe, To buy a tusk of ivory. Mudzomba gnania yuna-arika pembe tu.
  **Arikana,** *v. ref.*
  **Aririana,** *v. ref.* *See* Lafirana; Niacha. Kuna miario mibomu. Gnania na gnania ana aririana; aka-singana udzai, usinsi, uifi, etc.
**Ariko.**
**Arisa,** *v.n.*, to get dry. Used only of Indian corn when beginning to ripen.
**Arisa,** *v.a.*, to shepherd, to pasture a flock, herd, etc. Gnania yunagomba ku arisa—yuna rira ku arisa, ela gnania yu-

## [PDF Page 22 — Dictionary Page 9 (Ari — Azi)]

  narira muno, ka niamala wala kaarisa. Iye ni Ku enenda tu, ka oya wala ka arisa. Uchi hiu i noa ku arisa, ndivo undivo undavo-u belelesa ka-u-nda-ku-rifia. Mvula ya gnia i ki-arisa; *i.e.* at intervals of a day or two, like the Vuri rains. Der., Luario; Maario; Wariko.
**Arive.** *See* Murive; Musimu.
**Arivo.**
**Aro.** Kilima nda aro.
**Aruka** and **Arukua** (= Vavayuka).
**Asa,** *v.a.* *See* Aka. To make to burn, to kindle.
**Asa,** *n.* (= Akasa). *See* Sa. A species of grain.
**Asa, Aza,** *v.n.* *See* Ririra; Ko. To think, to consider, to desire. Yubui ku aza and Asuka. Yuna-mu-aza nduguye, auye. Nidzi-aza kurira (= Nidzi-londa ku rira).
  **Asira** (K.). *See* Goma. To doubt, to be sorry. Mutu hiye yuna-ni-asira mia, kula niki-mu-ona, iye yuna, ni lota ki tongo tongo.
**Asie,** *adv.*, without. Asie kalavo. Asie haja, One without shame. *See* Muthua muthua. Asie kidzambalasi.
**Askari** (Ar.) (Kin. pronunciation, Asikari), *n.*, a soldier. Adzomba ana atu aka oikua asikari ya wali, The Wasuahili have men who are called soldiers of the governor.
**Asuka** (Kid.). Der., Miazo.
**Atha,** *v.n.* and *a.* Ku-mu-atha maneno (= Ku-m-funiaja). Ndzo ni-ku-athe maneno ga kifieri. *See* Ku funda.
**Aura** (Kig. ?), *v.a.*
**Ava.**
**Avaha,** *v.a.*, to borrow.
  **Avahira,** *v.n.* Msihende ku-m-avahira, nadza, ni-mu-ve migniewe na mukono, ela as'ende n'avahira.
  **Avahiwa,** or **Ahahiwa,** *v.p.* Wa henda avahiwa.
  **Avasa, Avaza,** *v.a.*, to lend. Ni avaza uchi, Lend me some toddy.
**Avu,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Mjomba in Kij.), a maternal uncle. Avuye, His uncle. Avuyao, Their uncle. Avuzao, Their uncles.
**Avuka,** *v.n.* *See* Kufia. To pass, to cross.
  **Avukira,** *v.d.* Ku-mu-avukira niashini.
**Avusa,** *n.* *See* Kochokocho; Awali. First beginning. Mvula i avuse. Mvula idzignia; be idi avusa, It has been raining; now it is passed off. Machero matembe.
**Aya,** *v.n.* *See* Dzoya. Kuaya kua langa ni ku sala kikonde kivuvu, ha-mugasija ni ku aya, udzi-kala madzi, ka-u-na. Langa ridzi-aya mdzangani. Ku aya mikono.
  **Ayira,** *v.d.* Gnombe yangu idzionda. Mathunia gadzi aya, ku-mu-ayira mikono kuamba a-ni-pe.
  **Ayula,** *v.* Ku ayula nakidzoka. Ku ayula na chembeu ajula?
  **Ayuka,** *v.n.*, to echo, to resound. Uki gomba dzaka rina-ayuka.
  **Ayusa,** *v.a.*, to cause an echo. Bunduki ridzi pigua, ridzi ayuka, ridzi-ni-ayusa masikiro. Musinga udzi pigua, udzi ayuka.
  **Ayurira,** *v.d.* U-ni-ayurire muvini wangu. Umiro una-ayuka. Mutu aki dema muhi, dzaka rina-ayuka, angue, vana Shetani yudzi-ayuka cho ku-imba.
**Aye, Arie, Adzie, Ki-aye.**
**Ayika,** *v.a.*, to be at. Nalavia homu ra ku anika Muanzo wa ku lota.
**Azima** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to think. Ni-ku-foya kitu kuenda humira, kidza uka-mu-udzira megnie.

## B.

**B,** the second letter of the alphabet. Sometimes written for *p*, but the pronunciation is as distinct as it is in English.—[ED.]
**Baba,** *n.* *See* Abe. Father.
**Babarika,** *v.*, to flutter.
  **Babarikira,** *v.*, to fly at.
  **Babarikirana,** *v. ref.*, to fly at one another.
**Babasha,** *n.* and *adv.* *See* Bambara. Kikongo cha babasha.
**Bada, Pata,** *v.a.*, to get, to obtain.
  **Badana, Patana,** *v. ref.*, to get together; hence to agree.
  **Badanisha, Patanisha,** *v.*, to reconcile.
**Badi,** *n.* (pl. Ma-), a group, a drove.
**Bado,** *n.* (pl. Ma-), gain.
**Baha,** *n.* *See* Kuhinda, to get better.
**Baha,** *adv.*, somewhat better. Baha baha yehu, our rescue = Ponia ponia yetu (Kij.).
**Bahadi,** *n.*, fate, fortune. Bahadi mvidzo, good fortune. Bahadi mvi, misfortune.
**Bahari,** *n.*, sea.
**Bakuli,** *n.*, a basin.
**Bambahuka,** *v.a.*, to sprout.
**Bambahula,** *v.a.*, to flatten.
**Bambara.** *See* Bembere.
**Bamfuka,** *v.n.* *See* Gande. To admit of breaking off. Nenda nikadzole magova, gadzibamfuka (g'egnie). Der., Kibamfu.
  **Bamfula,** *v.a.* (= Bamfua in Kij.), to break off a piece or morsel. Ni-pa rino gogo, ni bamfule vibamfu, ngari viiri, nikachitire niunguyangu.
  **Bamfurika,** *v.n.* U-ni bamfurire katite, u-ni-pe, Break off a little for me and give (it) me. Resp., Ah-ni kitite, ka-ki-bamfurika.
  **Bamfurira,** *v.a.* M-bamfurire ki-bamfucho, u-mu-ve, arie.
**Bana, Bwana,** *n.*, lord, master, owner.
**Bananga,** *v.a.* *See* Mukodo. To spoil, to destroy, to annul. Prov., Mubananga chakue kana kondo. *See* Fio.
  **Banangika,** *v.n.*, to be spoilt.
  **Banangira.**
**Banda, Panda,** *v.a.* *See* Koko. To bruise, to break by blows. Ku banda nazi, To break a cocoa-nut. Ku banda misosa.
  **Bandabanda,** *v. reit.* Gnania kaidima ku saga, ku saga kuakue yunabanda (= Banda ungawe; ku saga kue ku-foroforo).
  **Bandika,** (1) *v.n.*, to admit of bruising. Ka-ki-bandika, ni chomu.
  (2) *v.a.* (= Ku badika), to apply, to put on, to put above, as an additional load; lit. to let come down upon. Ku dema sinde na ku bandika, To cut with the root, and put it on, *sc.* a leaking thatch.
  **Bandikira.**
  **Bandikisa,** *v.a.*, (1) = Bandika, when used of an additional load.
  (2) (= Ku badikisa). To pile up; lit. to make come down upon. N.B.—Of a first or single load, Ku huika is used.
  **Bandikizira,** *v.a.*, to hit. Gnania yunaidima ku bandikizira ka-kosa. Yudzi-m-fumaga niuni, yudzi-m-bandikizira.
**Banda,** *n.*, a shed. Niumba yangu idzikala banda (= idzikala ya kare). Dim., Kabanda and Kibanda, sheds of different shapes.
**Bandabanda,** *adv.* (= Kurekure), in a dispersed manner. A term of agriculture. Madzere yakaniatua bandabanda (or, kurekure).
**Bandari** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), a landing-place. Der., Bansi.
**Bandu.** Prov., Bandu na bandu ya mala gogo (= in Kij., Haba na haba hujaza kibaba, Little by little fills a kibaba).
**Banduka** (Kid.), *v.n.*, to get loose,

---

## [PDF Page 24 — Dictionary Page 11 (Ban — Bas)]

  to put (itself) off. Ku kanduka and Ku omoka.
**Bangala** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Kibaria in Kir.). *See* Divula. A vessel used in drawing toddy, a small calabash.
**Bangalalo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Azina hiri ni bangalalo, ni ralamu ni vevi na ku henda chebo. Dim., Kibangalalo.
**Bangana** (Kij.), *v. reit.* Lukolo hilo adzibungana, hara a-luao na hara a-luao.
**Bangula,** *n.* *See* Kuangula.
**Bansi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a species of cricket. Dim., Kabansi or Kibansi.
  **Bansikucha** (Kariwa).
**Bao** (Kij.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a board, a plank. Ku piga bao, To saw boards, to cleave planks. Ku lagurirua na bao, or Ku pigirua bao.
**Bara** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Kir., Kalansa; Pada in Kns.), a space between plants. Udziricha mabara mabara, Thou hast left (large) intervening spaces (unplanted).
**Bara** (Kij.), *n.* (ya). *See* Ludzidzi. Land, the mainland.
**Bara,** *v.a.*, to get accustomed, familiar; to get fixed by long continuance. Muhoho yudzi ui bara.
  **Barabara,** *v. reit.* Kifiu hiki uka-ki-barabara (= dzadzigira), kina-ku-chegnia. Unabarabara atu afiere, kuna ishima.
  **Barana,** *v. reit.*
  **Barania** (Kid.), *v.a.*, to ask in marriage. In Kir., Ku usa muche, To ask a woman.
**Baraka,** or **Bariki,** *v.a.* *See* Thalimu. To bless.
**Baraka,** or **Bariki,** *n.*, a blessing.
**Barara.**
**Barare,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a kind of cricket. Kuna barare dide; ndo ri-riwa-ro. Kuna barare bomu, ka-ri-riwa. In the absence of a cock, people know when it dawns by the barare beginning to chirp.
**Bararika,** *v.n.*, to trickle. Only used of tears.
**Barasa, Baraza,** *v.n.*, (1) to make the noise "b-r-r-r, b-r-r-r," only ascribed to the dzange and madali.
(2) To make smooth (an arrow). Gnania yuna barasa mano; but now they say, Yuna dzonga to.
**Barasa, Baraza,** *v.n.* (= Ku ima lulolongo), to answer. Atu aimire baraza. Atu asegere baraza.
  **Barasha,** (1) *v.a.*, to miss (the weapon passing close by).
  (2) *v.n.*, to pass close by, so as to touch, but not graze. Yudzi-m-fumaga, ela yudzi-m-barasha. Yudzi-m-dema, ela yudzi-m-barasha. Gnania wabigua fumo, rikibarasha; ka-ri-ingirire ndani. Yudzi-m-dzuva mufui, ela mufui udzi-m-barasha.
**Barasadi** (Kij.), *n.*, a kind of coloured cloth.
**Baridi** (Kij.), *n.* (ya) (in Kir., Teho), cold, coldness.
**Baru.** Hudzisinda vavo di, hata dzua ku baru (= Hata dzua ku bodoka).
**Barika, Bariki,** *v.a.*, to bless.
**Barudi, Baruti** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), gunpowder.
**Barusa.** *See* Bara, *v.a.*
**Basa.** *See* Bara, *v.a.*
**Barusa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (in Kij. and Kir., Ku kuarusa), to scratch as a thorn, Miya idzi-ni-barusa, The thorns have scratched me.
**Basa, Baza,** *v.a.*, to accustom. Mutu hiyu una-m-basa vava, naye ni muifi, kanda kudza iya fio? Yudzi-m-basa hata yudzibara; ka-m-kanide. Ku-m-basa muhoho ku enenda, a bare.
**Basaradi,** *n.*, a kind of coloured cloth (from Bozra?).
**Bashe,** or **Buashe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Muchiri), a species of wild animal.
**Basi,** *adv.* *See* Duka; Chisa, 2;

*Footer: 11*

## [PDF Page 25 — Dictionary Page 12 (Bas — Bek)]

  Fedeheka; Kigumba; Kilome; Kutu; Dzadza. Well! enough!
**Bazia** (Kij.), *n.* (ra). *See* Zia. A screen, curtains, anything hung round a bedstead. From Kuzia. Ku henda bazia (in Kir. proper, Ku kata ngao).
**Bata,** *v.a.* (= Ku batua in Kij.), to break off pieces, to chip off. Ku bata mugasija, To break off pieces of cassava. Mutu wabata hiva, hangi waguira mani, hangi dze. Kuonere hiro bato nikarobata? Muhi hio ukabatua bato.
**Bata,** *n.* (pl. Ma-), a duck.
**Batili,** *v.a.*, to pervert.
  **Batuka,** *v.n.* (= Bamfuka and Ku mfaniuka). Kigome kidzibatuka, A chip is cut off. Muhi hio ka-u-batuka, ni m'omu, This tree which is chipped is hard.
  **Batula,** *v.a.* (= Sugula and Bamfula), to begin to. Ku batula kigome, To cut out a chip.
**Bato,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a speck. Gnombeyangu ina bato ra usoni, My ox has a speck on its face. Ku piga muhi bato, or, Ku dema bato. Ku onire rino bato we, muhi ni wangu? Nguoye idzi-guira tove, ina mabato mabato. Dim., Kibato.
**Batubatu.** Only used in the Prov., Batubatu rinamala gogo.
**Bawa, Pawa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a ladle, consisting of the half of a cocoa-nut shell with a stick passed through it. Dim., Kabawa and Kibawa; magn., Ribawa.
**Bawasi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), white spots on the skin, generally confined to the hands and feet, and quite harmless in their nature.
**Bawawa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a species of bird. Onomatop.; from its cry.
**Bayo,** *n.* (ra) (= Luvayo), idle talk, prattle, chattering. From Ku vaya. Muna bayo muno, kamu niamala? Mtumche hiye yuna bayo or luvayo, ni muzinzi. Unavayavaya muno, ndosa ukaambua: una bayo. Dim., Kabayo; Kavayo.
**Bayuka,** *v.n.* *See* Ku vavayuka. To become mad.
  **Bayuza,** *v.*, to make or drive mad. Uchi wa mulala unabayuza. Uchi udzi-ku-bayuza.
**Be,** *interj.* *See* Hanuka; Kilome; Lola; Mugema; Rindisa; Siwa; Dzua; Nundu; Gundisa; Mbotherua. Well. Nenda nikalole utu usiku, be niuye. Be ndo vi-ri-vio, Well, so it is = Be basi = Ri-vira. Wari ndiye gnania, be wafua, or Dzinare rari ndiye gnania, be wafua. Be-we! enenda be udzisho.
**Bea,** *n.*, the top leaves of the cassada plant. The Wadigo use these leaves as a vegetable.
**Beberu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), an old he-goat.
**Beda** (Kij.), *v.a.* (Kig., Veda; Kir., Veha).
**Beduka,** *v.n.* *See* Ereka. To turn off, to tumble, to get tilted. Kidzibeduka chegnie, ka-ki-kabedulua ni mutu.
  **Bedukira,** *v.d.* *See* Pindui. To turn off, to tumble to, towards (anything).
  **Beduza,** *v.a.* (= Kugausa), to turn over.
  **Bedula,** *v.a.*, to turn off.
  **Bedurika,** *v.n.*, to admit of turning off. Ni kisiho, ka-ki-bedurika.
  **Bedurira,** *v.d.*, to turn off *to* or *for* (another). Ndzo, u-ni-be-durire cho kiviuda.
**Bei** (Kij.), *n.*, trade.
**Bekebeke.** Onomatop. Ku vekedza bekebeke.
**Bekeda** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to vex, to harass, to set at enmity.
**Bekedebekede,** *n.*, bickerings, continued acts of harassing people, by causing quarrels. Gnania yuna bekedebekede muno, dzua ka-ri-fika kidzoani, a-sivoheha na muyawe.

## [PDF Page 26 — Dictionary Page 13 (Bek — Bia)]

**Bekerebekere,** *n.* and *adv.* *See* Lulaka; Harazaharaza. Ukigomba, mino sisikira, unagomba bekerebekere.
**Bekula,** *v.a.*, to measure in a pishi. Der., Kibeku kibekule, a small basin.
**Belelesa,** *v.a.* *See* Arisu. (1) To look steadily, intently, to fix the eyes upon anything. (2) To observe, to watch, in order to ascertain. Ku sagala we hata ukabelelesa? Can you not be quiet until you have watched and ascertained the matter?
**Belewa** (Kij.), *v.p.* Dalu ridzibelewa, madzi gadzita. Yudzi kudza ku londa niama, ku gula, hata yunadza sidzisera, basi yudzibelewa, yudziuya. Nidziamba nikege madzi, niuye hiraka, hata nin'enda gadzisira, basi nikabelewa, nikaangalala. Yudzikana hata gnania yunadza aki-m-sima, basi akabelewa.
**Bemba,** *v.a.* *See* Mfarusa. (1) To wheedle, to coax, to hoax, to humour. Nidzi-m-bemba na maneno hata yudzi-ni-ambira garigo ndani mua-kue, yuere akilonda ku gundisa, ku-m-bemba kua maneno maerefu. Nidzi-m-bemba hata nidzi-m-koba. Nidzi-m-bemba hata nidzi-m-harira kitu che, I coaxed him until I took from him his thing; *i.e.* until I got from him the thing I wanted. Nidzi-m-bemba hata nidzi-m-korera. Kufuli hi sifugule kua ngufu, fugula pore pore ku henda bemba.
(2) To put off one's guard. Ana-hubemba sayao, They put us off.
**Bembea,** *n.*, a term of abuse, for which there is no corresponding word in English. Ahoho auaansa uira, anafuina bembea. They sing, "Bembea hio-bembea! Bembea hio-bembea!"
**Bembea,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Obs. Ni dzina ri sana, It is a very bad name. Mutu hiye yudzikala bembea kua hikura kuzinga muno. Be ni mutu wani huyu — ridzikala bembea?
  **Bembeleza,** *v.n.* Obs.
**Bembere,** *n.* *See* Dzango and Dzaya. A box, a calabash, a pot when old and broken. Only used as predicate. Kasha rikala bembere. Kirenge kikala bembere. Niungu ikala bembere, or, dzaya. Kasha rino ridze? What is the matter with that box? Resp., Rikala bembere, or, Ni bembere.
**Bembere,** or **Bambara,** *adv.* Onomatop. Kirenge hiki, mbona, kinarira bembere, kikafunsika hibudze?
**Bengo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Dzomo). Yudzirima, yudziika bengo. Muvaga hiu mudzi-u-bananga, mudzi-u-henda mabengo mabengo. Bengo ra murima. Dim., Kabengo and Kibengo.
**Bereu** (Kij.), *n.* (= Bayo; Luvago; in Kir., Ubishi), tar (?), black stuff. Gnania yuna bereu.
**Berua,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the guava.
**Beshe** (Kij.). Maneno higo kaka-ku-beshe, haya-u-dzi-bumirani we? Maneno higano si gako, u-ga-ingirira-ni?
  **Beshere.** *See* Disia. Ga-ku-beshere-ni we? hata uki-ga-ingira maneno gano. Ku-ga-monia, wala si gako.
**Beshe** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Kumba in Kir.), a sweet-water fish.
**Bi.** Kitu changu birokho. Ukilafia nduguyo birokho bai, ndo unda vo henda uzungu, usiulage mutu kahiri, ela kitu cha ku siirua, ka-ki-ku-luma muno.
**Bi.**
**Bia** and **Bie, Pia** and **Pie,** *adv.* *See* Geshi. Wholly, com-

## [PDF Page 27 — Dictionary Page 14 (Bid — Bim)]

  pletely, entirely. It is often used with Asi in a way which seems redundant, but it strengthens the sense. Muniuwangu udziyaya bia kua mfula.
**Bida, Pita** (Kij.), *v.* (in Kir., Ku chira), to surpass. Gnania yuna akili, wala kavana mutu a-m-bidaye (= a-m-chiraye), A B has sense; there is not a man who surpasses him.
  **Bidikiza** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to prevent, to take by surprise, to hinder. Mvula idzi-ni-bidikiza, si dzangue ku dzusa munda wangu (= Mfula idzi-ni-udulukiza in Kir.). Yudzi-ni-bidikiza, sina kitu cha ku-m-riva (= ku udulukiza). Ningari nidzikudza kare, ela nidzibidikizua ni mfula (= Mfula idzi-ni-ziza in Kir.).
  **Bidubidu** (= Bidukiza).
  **Biduka,** *v.n.* (= Ku beduka).
  **Bidukira.** *See* Pindui. Ku bidukira kufua-bidubidu.
  **Bidula,** *v.a.* (= Ku bedula).
  **Bisa** (Kij.), *v.r.* (Kir., Ku visa), to cause to pass, to let pass (by giving place to another in walking).
  **Bisania.**
**Bidaa, Bithaa** (Kij.), *n.*, goods, merchandise.
**Bidi** (Kid.), *n.*, a herd. Bidi ra gnombe, A herd of cattle (= Kir., Gundi ra gnombe).
**Bidibidi** (Kid.), *adv.*, diligently. Modo (moto) unahaka bidibidi (in Kir., Moho unaaka biribiri).
**Bie** (= Bia, Pia).
**Bidza,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Dzakudza and Dzamundi), a handful, a bundle. Bidza ra mifui. Dim., Kabidza.
**Biga, Piga,** *v.a.* *See* Peho. To beat, to strike. Ku kuta. Ku piga muhama, To beat (out) guinea-corn, to thresh. Mfula idzi-ni piga. Ku piga niasi, To cut grass. Ku piga madzansu, To make a hedge (= Ku piga cha and Ku piga luchigo). Ku piga kima, To fix a price. Ku piga kimia, To observe silence. Ku piga thora, To strike a bargain. Ku piga daraka, To become surety. Ku piga viha, To wage war. Ku piga chamba, To waylay. Ku piga neno, To strike (one with) a word; *i.e.* to offend. *See* Neno. Yudzi-ni-piga manino, hada yudzi-ni-gniagnania, He struck me with words (= he teased me) until he robbed or defrauded me. Ku pigadzi. Prov., Pigadzi, uriche muiriwangu.
  **Bigabiga, Pigapiga,** *v. reit.* Moyo una-ni-bigabiga (= una-ni-sumba), My heart beats. In Kid., Ku pigapiga (in cooking) means Bosa in Kij.
  **Bigana, Pigana,** *v. reit.*, to fight, to be at war. Muki pigana, mudzipata-ni vo?
  **Bigebige, Pigepige.** Prov., Pigepige rinamala muiri.
  **Bigibigi, Pigipigi.** Maneno ga pigipigi.
  **Bigira, Pigira,** *v.d.* and *instr.* *See* Pondo; Daraka. Wa-m-pigira-ni? What do you beat him for? U-ni-pigire kima uwe.
  **Bigiribigiri, Pigiripigiri.**
  **Bigirira, Pigirira,** *v.a.*, to put together, from smaller vessels into a large one; but only used of what is put into calabashes. Na bigirira uchi, nirive, I put toddy together. Nafaka in kadzama.
**Bilashi** (Kij.), *adj.* (= Bule), for nothing. Nidzi pigirua bilashi ela sina, kondo na mutu, I am beaten for nothing; indeed, I have not a quarrel with any man.
**Bima, Pima,** *v.a.* *See* Wau. To measure, to weigh. Ku-m-pima mutu nguvu, kua ku-migniana, To test a man's strength by wrestling.
  **Bimira, Pimira.** *See* Pishi. Der., Kipimo; Pima.

## [PDF Page 28 — Dictionary Page 15 (Bim — Bod)]

**Bimba,** *n.*, a large belly. Rarely used. Magn. of Mimba. N.B.—Of pregnancy the word is never used, though this is the principal meaning of Mimba.
**Bimbinda,** *v.a.* *See* Ukira. To drub, to thwack, to give a sound beating. Gnania yudzipigua, yudzibimbindua. Kidzoka hiki ka-ki-dema, kihenda bimbinda. Der., Kibimbinda.
**Binda,** *v.* (= Ku binda).
**Bindo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a bundle in a cloth (K., parcel). Magn. of Luvindo or Rivindo? Gnania akafuala nguo-yuna bindo. Mo bindo ni nini?
**Binga,** *v.a.*, to thwart. Getting obsolete.
  **Bingana,** *v. reit.* (= Ku dezana, when used of aganga), to balk, to thwart one another. Yuma-ni-binga, be hunabingana kua muche. Anabingana ku luanira muche. Der., Pingu; Pingua.
**Binikiza,** *v.a.* (= Ku finikira). *See* Lukoko; Yamba. To cover, to obscure. Maingu gadzi binikiza dzua, A cloud has obscured the sun. Ku-dzi-binikiza amba.
  **Binikizira.** Mbengio ya ku binikizira muado.
**Biramu** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za), a flag.
**Biribiri,** *adv.*, in a blazing, flaming manner. Moho unaaka biribiri, or, chekecheke, The fire has burst forth in a blaze (but Dzua ramba mirimiri). Atu anadza biribiri, or, dziridziri. Acharo adzichira na vavo biribiri.
**Biririka,** *v.n.*, to blaze. Moho unabiririka (= unachekacheka). Dzua rinabiririka (rikidzoma muno, rikikola dzi). Atu anabiririka ku chira nchirani).
**Biru** (Kid.). Ku bida biru (Kij., Ku bida buru; said in a high, singing voice).
**Biruka,** *v.n.*, to be bent (as going aside). Muhi hiu ukabiruka This tree is bent.
**Biruka** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku deruka, Kns.), to pass by swiftly, to rush past.
**Bisa** (Kij.). *See* Bida.
**Bisania,** *v.a.*, to join. Ku bisania chuma (= Ku dzangania), To weld iron. Ku bisania uchi, To mix toddy, *i.e.* old and new (= Ku bigania tembo in Kij.). Uchi ni ufu hiu, uhensa ku bisaniua, ka-u-noika. Ku bisania ushanga (= Ku bigania in Kij., and Ku ingisisa in Kid.), To mix, to intersperse beads, of different colours in stringing them. Ku bisania atu kondo, To mix up men in a quarrel.
**Bisha,** *v.n.*, to veer about; to contend. Peho inabisha, inalonda ku galuka, ikale ya furi (hebu ya muaka). Atu hia anabisha, kavana akubaliye ga muyawe.
  **Bishana,** *v.*, to tease one another. Hiyu ysegere kuria mongo wa huyani atu a bishanao.
  **Bishuka,** *v.n.* Moyo udzi-ni-bishuka, nidziamba, ni-m-bige. Nidziamba nihambe, ela moyo udzi-ni-bishuka. Nidziamba nidzagule hiki, ela moyo udzi-ni-bishuka. Der., Mubishi; Ubishi.
**Bita** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku dieka in Kir.), to throw down, to lay down, to lay (eggs).
**Bo, Po,** *particle of time or place*, when, where. Ku piga mbalahi po.
**Bobo** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). In Kir. proper, Bumba, which word, however, is being superseded by Bobo, a bunch of tobacco leaves tied together.
**Bochabocha,** *v.n.* *See* Kirimira.
**Bochoreka,** *v.n.*, to leak. Said of a roof. Kamu larika niumbayehu inafudza inabochoreka idzikala banda.
**Bodoka,** *v.n.* *See* Kibamfu; Tarare. To drop. Mudzi udzibodoka hibudzi?

## [PDF Page 29 — Dictionary Page 16 (Bod — Bor)]

  **Bodokera,** *v.d.* Dzua ridzedzua, nikienenda, rinda-ni-bodokera nchirani. Dzua ridzi-hu-bodokera vatu vasiku (= Ku dzuerera).
  **Bodoza,** *v.a.*, to drop, to let fall. Kuku yudzibodoza lunioga, The fowl has dropped a feather.
  **Bodozabodoza,** *v. reit.*, to drop, to let fall repeatedly. Mutu yudzikuenda aki bodozabodoza madzere ndirani, or, akibodoza madzere nchira nchira, A man went on letting fall Indian corn in the road.
  **Bodozera,** *v.d.* Ku-m-bodozera kuro, To drop (something) for a dog.
**Bodza** (Kid.), *n.* *See* Ku-m-guiza.
**Bofo.**
**Bofola,** *v.a.* (= Ku bigadzana and Ku humbula). *See* Futa; Dzolola. To break through, to rip open. Ku bofola kavu, To open a basket. Ku bofola gnonsi, To open a sheep. Mutu aki dovola kiruvo cha dzaya, or, niungu.
  **Bofoka,** *v.n.* *See* Tundu; Bomu. Nguoyangu idzibofoka. Kivinda kidzibofoka. Niungu idzibofoka.
  **Boforera,** *v.d.* Gnania yudzi-ni-boforera pfukoyangu.
**Bofuko,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), thin, lean. Ni kala asienona. Kala hiri ni bofuko, ka-ri-kanona.
**Bogi,** *n.* (ra) (= Gundi and Viedi; Geshi in Kij.), a host, a great multitude. Vadzichira viedi via gnombe, u-ni bogi ra gnombe, ka-vi-neneka. Vadzichira bogi ra atu-angidu. Amasai avokudza, akudza bogi ra atu, dzi nzima, na ku uya adziuya bogi.
**Bogo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kimo. A giant. Bogo ra mulume; pl. Mabogo ga alume. Bogo ra muganga.
**Bohoya,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the fruit of the mubohoya, a creeper.
**Boka, Poka,** *v.n.*, to plunder, to deprive. Ku boka ndzala. Huari ndzalani, ela vino hudziboka.
  **Bokera,** *v.d.* Huniale vitu via nguangu, hundabokera. Podzo na maere-ndo atu abokera fio kuansa.
  **Bokua,** or **Bopua,** *v.p.* (in the active voice the *k* is very clear and decided, but in the passive a sound is produced in which *k* and *p* seem united). Kudzibokua, kakuna ndzala kaviri.
**Bokonia** (Kij.), *v.a.* (in Kir. proper, Ku voka and Ku gniagnania), to deprive, to take from. Yudzi-ni-kenga, hata yudzi-ni-bokonia.
**Bokoro** (?). Muana ni bokoro.
**Boma,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a palisade of poles, stones, etc., serving as a fortification. Afiere adzikutana, adzikuenda bomani.
**Bomboroko** (Kid. ?).
**Bomu,** *adj.* (dz, ra and ya, za). *See* Mafufufu; Samia. Great. Ku bomu ni hiko.
**Bona, Pona,** *v.n.* *See* Singa. To put, to place. Nidzi-m-bona.
**Bona** (Kij.), *v.n.* (in Kir. proper, Ku dia, tia). *See* Ku vona. Hudzizolua, hata atu adziulagua, ela mino nidzibona.
  **Bonia,** *v.a.* (in Kir., Ku difia and Ku okola). *See* Kongo. To cure, to save. Ukongo hio ka-u-nda-m-bonia. Gnania yudzi-ni-bonia, nari nafua na ndzala.
**Bongo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the skull.
**Bopo** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Gopue in Kir.), a hollow.
**Bora,** *n.* *See* Mufaranga; Muansa; Munguchi; Vima. A cockerel. Bora ni mutu ayemala vihendo mbere, ndiye mufiere adzagulaye niama.
**Borasoroko** (= Fiala muansa ?). Dim., Kibora? Kabora.
**Bori,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Mugama

## [PDF Page 30 — Dictionary Page 17 (Bor — Buk)]

  and Ndzao. A tusk of a young male elephant. It is about an arm's length, and is still hollow. Pembe ya bori ni ya ndzofu chume, ambao ka-dza-kala abomu. Pembe za mabori. Udzigula pembe yani? Resp., Nidzigula bori. Dim., Kabori.
**Bororo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) the shell of a cocoa-nut made into a hookah.
(2) The hookah itself. The word is evidently onomatop. It is rarely used among the Wanika, who use the common pipe in smoking, which habit also is confined to the southern tribes called Wadigo. Bororo-ro riluavi, nikafuhire? Where is your hookah, that I may smoke with?
**Bosho.** *See* Kidogo.
**Boso.** Boso ni gniere-ku dzanga uchi ku va Kambi. Hivo mbere machira ga ndzala. Wali wa Kisiwani yuere akilafia boso, aka-a-va Anika.
**Bosu** (Kigiriama), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Uso sura), the face.
**Bu.** *See* Bo; Bumuka. Ku kua bu. Ku umalala bu. Muhamawangu ka-u-ka-mera, udziamba bu hata mize ka-u-ka oloha ngari. Hurere bu na ndzala. Amasai adziulaga atu bu bu bu.
**Bu,** *n.* Fumbi ra bu.
**Bu-buni dzamua Buni** (?). *See* Kibeku and Kibekuli.
**Bua, Pua** (Kij.), *n.*, steel. Achogni ndio agulao mabua, akabumirua vidzokani ku dema dzaka.
**Bua, Pua,** *v.n.* (enclit.). *See* Badama; Dulama; Nona; Muniala; Okola; Rungusa. To fall, to alight, to subside. Ku bua munazini, To fall from a cocoa-nut tree. Yudzikuala, yudzebua, He stumbled and fell. In Kij., the word is used of the ebb—Maji yabua; in Kir., it is Ku la. Madzi ga-dza-go furungua, be ga funsu, ukaamba: ga-riche, gabue, basi uhege. Muana yudzebua madzi hangu dzana yunadzekera viero. Moyo udzi-ni-bua (= udzi-ni-hurira). Muaka udlebua. Kondo idzebua, atu anabigana.
**Buaga** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to cast down. In Kitaita, this word means to kill.
**Bubunda** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku bimbinda in Kir.), to beat severely; to border or drape.
**Budzania.** *See* Buzania.
**Budzo.** *See* Buzo.
**Buga,** *v.a.* (= Ku yeya muno), to search. Muana yudzibuga ifu, or, midzanga yu dze. Nidzibuga jemberangu hata nidzidzoka. Nidzi-ri-buga hata nidzi-ri-ona.
**Bugudika** (Kij.), *v.n.* (in Kir. proper, Ku vukuhika), to fall in plenty. Maembe gadzibugudika, ga-dele dze.
  **Bugurika,** *v.n.*, to corrupt, to rot, to putrefy. Nidzichita mbalazi hata zidziifua, zidzibugurika. Kidziola, kidzibugurika, ka-ki-rika kaviri (Kij. = Ku tumburujika).
**Bugno,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a corn-pipe (made of the stalk of muhama).
**Bugubugu,** *adv.* *See* Mumunika; Buka. Niama idziola bugubugu, ka-i-hama kahiri (= idzi-bugurika).
**Bui.** Yudzenua uchi, yu bui. Yudzirea, yu bui. Yu bui-ku aza and Ku asula.
**Buibui,** *adj.*, deaf and dumb.
**Buibui,** *n.*, a mute.
**Buka,** *v.n.* (1) *See* Ku buka in Kina. Hangu dzana yudzibuka, kana mafuha.
(2) (Kid.). Hasa moho, hata ubuke (in Kir., Busa moho hata uchuke).
**Bukuabukua** (Kid.), *n.*, a clamour, a tumult. Vadz'amba

## [PDF Page 31 — Dictionary Page 18 (Bul — Bur)]

  vakue kondo, yaribukuabukua (in Kir., yari dukaduka, or, vari budzo sana).
**Bula, Pula,** of a yam.
**Bula,** *v.n.*, to bud. Muhi ukihenda makodza mavia, basi ni ku ambua: unabula. Na muhi ukidemua, be ukilafia madzavukuzi kahire, wamba; muhi unabula.
  **Burira.** *See* Kihari.
**Bule,** *n.* (ra) (= Zuza). *See* Kengeka. Nothing. Yudzi-ni-ika bulere.
**Bule,** *adj.*, gratis.
**Bule,** *adv.* *See* Lika. For nothing, without cause. Nidziriva bule, I paid without a cause (*i.e.* a debt which, in fact, was none of my own).
**Bulu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a maggot.
**Buluzanga,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the larva of the cockchafer.
**Buma,** *v.a.* *See* Fua. To put into. Halani madzere, mubume kavuni. Kudzi-buma deni, To get one's self into debt. Ku buma tembe. Dzano na-dzi-buma ya ulongo; nari nidzi-ukuha kare, ela niki-dzi-buma deni ya ulongo.
  **Bumika,** *v.n.* Ka-va-bumika, ni vafufu.
  **Bumira,** (1) *v.d.* and *instr.* *See* Kevesa. Ndere ni kirenge abumiracho uchi, ku-dzi-noe-ra (m'egnie).
  (2) *v.a.*, to repair, when it is done by way of inserting. Ku bumira niumba. Ku bumira mavalu, To splice spars. Ku-ki bumira kikahana, To mend a basket (= Ku ingirisira).
  **Bumuka,** *v.n.* Kundi ra dzongo ridzi bumuka mumo mundani-bu.
**Bumba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a clod, a lump, a packet. Bumba ra luzi, A ball of cotton. Bumba ra milala. Bumba ra niuchi, A swarm of bees. Mabumba ga ufuha.
**Bumbafu.** *See* Langasua.
**Bumbala,** *v.n.* (= Ku fua), to be dull. Dzana hiri ri bumbala (Kid.).
  **Bumbaza,** *v.a.* *See* Mufui; Aganga. To stupefy.
  **Bumbu.** Obs. Bumbu-enda kuenu, asie kuao 'ende dzoniani—"buaja"!
  **Bumbuana.** *See* Kibumbuana.
**Bumbumbu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Bumiriro** (?).
**Bumsika, Pumsika** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to rest. Ku bumsika nchimua.
**Bunda,** *v.a.* *See* Kalanga; Kishombo. To pound. Only used of what is soft. *See* Ku vonda. Kinu cha bunda madzere (= katakata).
  **Bundika.** *See* Ku doka; Chuma.
  **Bunduka** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku bunda).
  **Bundunga** (Kid.) (= Ku bunduka). Ku bundunga jora (Kir., Ku bunda jora).
**Bundu** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kamasi in Kij.; Fua in Kir.), mucus from the nose. Ku usa bundu, To take off a cold (Fig. = Ku limbuka in Kij.).
**Bunduki** (Kij.), *n.*, a gun.
**Bungo,** *n.* (= Chocho). Obs. Yudzi-ni-ika bungo kamoe, ka-ni-ogova. Niumbayangu yudzi-i-ika bungo, akida ni ku ingira tu, idzikala yakue. Mundawangu yudzi-u-ika bungo.
**Bunguani** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Kisifu. A defect.
**Buniaka.** *See* Ku buniuka.
**Bura** (Kij.), *v.a.* *See* Pungire. To thresh, or beat out. Ku bura muhama (= in Kir. proper, Ku biga muhama).
  **Burana.** Ku burana mavindada.
  **Buruga,** *v.a.* *See* Fumbula. To fallow, to cultivate. Yudziburuga mundawe, yudzi-u-dzusa.
  **Burugana,** *v. reit.* (= Ku bigana muno), to fight severely. Adzibigana, adziburugana hata adzihenda daniua.
  **Burugira,** *v.d.* Ku burugira p'ekue, To turn

  the ground *to*, *i.e.* *on account of* the weeds or tares (said when these are still small, soon after planting, in contradistinction to Ku rimira p'ekue, when both the plants and the weeds have become larger).
**Buru,** *n.* (ra) (= Harufu in Kij.), a smell. Kunanuka buru ri ra ku ola. Kunanuka buru ridzo ra ufumba. Kunanuka buru ra niama (= Kunanuka muzingo, obsolete).

**Busa,** *v.n.* *See* Bula. To bud. Huhi anabuza makodza.

**Buzania, Budzania.** Atu anabudzania, alonda neno ra keri, be ka-dza-ri-bada; ndo a hendavo lonso, hata huya alengaye neno akidza gomba, atu akaamba: ndio keri hio.

## CH.

**Ch,** the third letter of the alphabet, pronounced as in English. The *c* is not used by itself. *Ch* is sometimes put for *j*. The *ch*, as in Cha and Cho, is often interchanged with *k* for the sake of euphony.—[ED.]
**Cha,** (1) the particle indicating the genitive of nouns belonging to the ch and ki class.
(2) Prefixed to a cardinal numeral, it forms an ordinal: Tahu, Three; Cha tahu, Thrice; Kumi, Ten; Cha kumi, Tenth. *See* Lasirua.
(3) Followed by a verb, it stands as pronoun for the same class of words, and at the same time it implies the imperf. tense.
**Cha,** *v.n.* (enclit.), to dawn. Radically, to part, to go asunder, as will be seen from the immediate branches of the word. Kudzi cha, kudzignala, It has dawned, it is bright, daylight. Peho za kucha, The coolness of the morning; lit. of to dawn. Machero kukicha, To-morrow when it dawns.
  **Chera,** *v.a.*, to split, to cleave, to cut into slices. Only used of what is soft, as fruits and vegetables, but never of wood. *See* Ahula. Kuchera mugazija, maembe.
  **Cherera,** *v.d.*, (1) to split, to cut into slices *to*, *for*. Musena yudzikudza ku-ni-cherera mugazijawangu.
  (2) To dawn *to*, *at*, *upon*. Nidzienenda na usiku hata kudzi-ni-cherera nchirani, I went with the night until it dawned to me in the way, while I was still on my way; they also say, Hata kudzi-ni-cherera nchira nchira, Until it dawned to me, as to the way way (in the Aus. = nchirani). Ni kuenda ni cherera akimu-raramira? Ni kuku ku halua ni kiniegere. *See* Kivia.
  **Chererua,** *v.p.*, (1) to have a thing split, etc., *to for*. Nidzichererua mugazija, ni musena.
  (2) To be dawned upon, to be met by daybreak. N.B.—This form of the word is very much in use, especially in the morning salutations. Rero nidzilala hata nidzichererua, n'kauka niumbani, dzua rinakorera miiri, To-day I slept until I was dawned upon,

*Footer: 19*

---

## [PDF Page 33 — Dictionary Page 20 (Cha — Cha)]

  until daybreak, when I started from the house the sun was hot to the bodies, *i.e.* the sun felt already hot. Moho uchererua. Muezi uchererua, or, udzichererua, The moon is (has been) dawned upon when it is still visible after daybreak. Ku chererua na mukongo, To be dawned upon by a sick person.
  **Cheresa** and **Keresa,** *v.a.*, (1) to cut asunder (with a saw), to saw; to hurt, to irritate (only used of dust, etc., in the eye). Nidziona Adzomba, anacheresa muhi na mufiumeno, ku henda kinu, I have seen Suahilis cutting a tree asunder with a saw, to make a mortar. Midzanga ina-ni-cheresa dzidzoni, Sand is hurting me, or hurts me, in the eye.
  (2) To cause anything to dawn; *i.e.* to keep till the next morning, to continue doing anything through the night till daybreak.
  Also *v.n.*, to spend the night. Construed with Na. Ku cheresa moho, To keep a fire in through the night. Ku cheresa uira, To continue a dance until daybreak. Lukuni hilu lunda cheresa moho. Ku cheresa na mukongo, To spend the night with a sick person.
  **Cheruka,** *v.n.*, to be in a state of parting asunder or breaking forth.
  **Cherusa,** *v.a.*, to half boil.
  **Chesa,** *v.n.*, to watch, to keep awake the whole night.
**Cha,** or **Chaa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Via), an enclosure for cattle.
**Chaa,** *n.*, tea.
**Chaba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viaba), a fillip, a jerk of the finger from the thumb. Yudzi-ni-piga chaba, He has filliped me, He has struck me a fillip.
**Chache,** *adj.*, few.
**Chache,** *n.*, a few.
**Chacho** (= Bungo).
**Chadi,** *n.*, diligence. Only used in the predicate. Yuna chadi, He has diligence (= Yuna rukudzu).
**Chafu,** *n.* (pl. Viafu). *See* Hafunika; Regesera. A fall, a tumble, especially when severe, but never used of a fall from a height.
**Chagabu** (Kid.), *n.* (pl. Viagabu) (in Kir., Ndzusi), a species of wild cat, spotted like a leopard.
**Chagina,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a prodigy, what is bigger, stouter than usual for its age. Used of men and animals. Muana hiyu ni chagina; pl. Ana hia ni machagina. Kuna bora hiva-chagina.
**Chaje,** *n.* (cha), dust of worm-eaten muhama.
**Chaka,** *n.* *See* Taka. The name of a certain fruit.
**Chakana,** *v.a.*, to stir in cooking when the food thickens. Ku furunga, To stir when it is thin. A chakana mfaya?
**Chako,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class; pl. Viako), thy, thine.
**Chakue,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class). *See* Che. His; her, hers; its.
**Chakuria,** *n.* (cha), food. Pl. Viakuria, eatables, provisions; lit. that of to eat, from Ku ria, to eat.
**Chala,** or **Chaala,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viala and Mala), a finger, a toe; one out of a cluster of bananas. Radically, a ray, a radius, what is beaming or shooting forth side by side and from one body; from Ku ala, to shine. The pl. Viala shows that the sing. is contracted from Ki and Ala. *See* Chalo. Kuna chala cha mukono, na chala cha kigulu, There is a chala of the hand and a chala of the foot. Their names for the different fingers are the following: (1) Chala cha dzalagumba, The

## [PDF Page 34 — Dictionary Page 21 (Cha — Cha)]

  thumb. (2) Chala cha muoloho, The forefinger (lit. the pointing or showing finger; in German, Zeigefinger). (3) Chala kibomu, the large finger (the middle finger). (4) Chala kisicho dzina, The finger without a name. (5) Chala cha kanda; lit. The finger of the side; *i.e.* the little finger. Kufua na chala, To die with the finger; *i.e.* to die snapping one's finger in desperation (a perfect picture of the death of a heathen; the expression is also used of one who dies with words of bitterness on his lips, though he may not actually move a finger).
**Chalamu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), wide, broad. Contracted from Ki and Alamu, and derived from Ku alama.
**Chalamu,** *n.*, what is wide, open, clear (used of speech). Kakafimbafimba, yudzigomba chalamu, atu adzisikira.
**Chalavulo** (Kig.), *n.*, sleeplessness.
**Chalo,** *n.* (cha), shine, the state of shining or giving light. Contracted from Ki and Alo, and derived from Ku ala.
**Chamanda,** *n.*, a little basket.
**Chamangale** (Kid.), *n.* (cha, pl. Viamangale). *See* Fugo. Name of a calabash of a particular size.
**Chamba,** *adv.*, whether. Contracted from Ku amba, to say.
**Chamba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viamba), an ambush. Radically, something ready to be drawn over as a covering. From Ku amba. Chamba hicho—ku pata mathara, That ambush—to get loss or damage.
**Chambamba** (Kij.), *adj.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), thin. Contracted from Ki and Ambamba.
**Chambire.**
**Chambo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viambo). Contracted from Ki and Ambo, and derived from Ku amba. Radically, something laid over or across, both by way of covering and fastening together; also one thing used for keeping and drawing another to itself. (1) The sticks laid crosswise on a litter or bier. *See* Ludara.
(2) The sticks laid across in the grave, resting on the ledges between which the corpse is laid. *See* Mudzi wa mbira.
(3) A peg, as used for stretching a skin on the ground when drying it. Chambo cha ku kotera tingo.
(4) A bait; lit. something that attracts.
**Chambuacho,** *n.*, a saying, an expression, as peculiar to any one. Contracted from Kiambuacho, It said which; from Ku amba, to say.
**Chamia,** *n.*
**Chamo.**
**Chanache** (Kid.), *adj.* (= Kihoho in Kir.), childish. Derived from Muanache. Yudzi-ni-hendera mambo ga chanache.
**Chanache,** *n.*, childishness.
**Chanamiro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a draught, the quantity drunk at once. Derived from Ku anamira. The word refers to a peculiar custom observed by drinking companies, according to which an equal quantity of toddy is dealt out, and as much as is not swallowed at one draught must be returned to the common store.
**Chanda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vianda), the workshop of a smith, consisting only of a slight shed.
**Chando,** *adv.*, together. Ndzoni hurie chando, Come, let us eat together.
**Chane.** *See* Tane.
**Changa,** *n.* (= Muanga), a clearing up, a break in the weather, after it has been rainy. From Ku anga. Kudzihenda changa, It has cleared up. Changa dzulo (Kid.) (= in Kir., Kilanga dzulo).

**Chango,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small wickerwork holder, in form resembling the half of a pair of scales, hung up in the cottage for receiving a pot with ready-cooked food until the time of eating; now rarely used. Contracted from Ki and Ango, and derived from Ku anga.
**Changu,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class; pl. Viangu), my, mine. Composed of Cha and Ngu.
**Changuangu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), light, not heavy. From Ku anga. *See* Anguangu. Kitu changuangu, ka ki merera.
**Chani,** *inter. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), what, which. Contracted from Cha and Ani.
**Chani.**
**Chaniro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), any bit of wood used as a wedge to fasten a handle with. From Ku anira.
**Chano,** *n.*, the name of a complaint incidental to young children.
**Chano,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a large wooden tray. From Ku ana. Two such trays are to be procured by every new kambi, to be used during the festival-time of their initiation, after which they are laid up in the rungu and are no more used. Dim., Kadzano.
**Chansa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), an area, a place cleared and levelled to build upon, or for beating out Caffre-corn (muhama); any free and open space suitable for dancing and playing. From Ku ansa.
**Chanse.** *See* Chandze.
**Chanso,** *n.*
**Chao,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class; pl. Viao), their, theirs.
**Chare,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viare), a heap. Only used of cocoa-nuts. From Ku ara, of which it is the opt. preceded by the pron. Ki. Kiare, May it be lost sight of, the single cocoa-nut being lost in the many. *See* Charo. Chare cha nazi, A heap of cocoa-nuts.
**Chari** (rel. to a noun of the ch and ki class). *See* Kidisa. It was. Contracted from Cha and Ari. Note: It is only the older people from whom Chari is still heard, the younger ones say Chere.
**Chari,** *verb. adj.* *See* Fia; Koloma; Kidamfira; Luhosi; Madzula; Muifu; Ari; Ere. To be yet, to remain, to continue, in the same state or condition. The word is only a modification of Ku kala, to be, procured in the same way in which adjectives and nouns are derived from verbs, namely, by a change of the final vowel into *i*. The change of the *k* into *ch* is optional, and therefore unessential. In the pronunciation of some, especially the younger people, the word has been further compressed into Chere or Kere, as is the case with the preceding word, so that we have no less than four variations, *sc.* Chari and Chere, Kari and Kere, of which, however, the two former are the most in use. In Kij., the word answers to Kali and Kele. Ku chari mapema, It is still good time. Ku chari peho za ku cha, There is still the cool of daybreak.
  **Chari,** or **Cheri,** or **Kere.** Nichari, I am. Uchari, Thou art. Yuchari, He is. Huchari, We are. Muchari, You are. Achari, They are. Yuchari mayo; lit. He is still with it = He still has it.
**Charo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viaro). *See* Chare. A journey, a caravan. Contracted from Ki and Aro, and derived from Ku ara. Radically, something that disappears from view, is lost sight of, both as regards dis-

  tance and the multitude of men, among whom the single individual is lost. Charo ni-ku-dzi-fungofunga.
**Chatahu,** *n.*, the name of a calabash of a particular size; lit. that of three, *i.e.* a third.
**Chathi** (Kid.), *n.* (cha, pl. Viathi) (= Mbatha in Kir.), an appointment, time specified and fixed, direction. Yudzinipa chathi. Yudzinipa, or, Yudzinilaga) viathi vieri.
**Chausa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Sababu), reason, cause.
**Chayu,** *n.* (cha). *See* Fimira. Distaste. From Ku aya; Ayuka.
**Che,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), his, her, its. Abbreviated from Chakue, from which it differs in this, that it can never be detached from its noun, while Chaque may be used alone, and be itself treated as a noun.
**Che,** the radical part of the words Kiche, Kuche, Mache, Muche, Riche. When it relates to a noun of the ya and za class, it is hardened into Te. Form and meaning alike indicate this particle of speech as the opt. form of Ku cha, and it denotes the female as to her true nature and destination with regard to offspring.
**Checha,** *v.a.*, to cut out, to cut off by small pieces, to cut into slices.
**Cheche,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a slice. The word simply consists of the opt. form of Ku checha, and is not formed by way of the usual contraction; hence the difference in the gen. particle and the pl. form.
**Chede,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viede), a market.
**Chedi** (Kid.), *n.* (cha, pl. Viedi), a host, a multitude, a large body of men.
**Chefu.**
  **Chefuka.**
  **Chefusa.**
**Chegnia,** *v.a.*, to graze, to wound slightly.
**Chegnie,** *pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), itself.
**Chegnie,** or **Tegnie,** *n.* (= Ngingingi), of a hoe.
**Chego,** *n.* *See* Jego.
**Chehu,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), our, ours.
**Chekacheka,** *v.n.* (= Ku biririka), to flame, to blaze. Radically, to be in a state of breaking forth, exclusively applied to fire. In form, the word is an immediate branch of Ku cha, the *a* being changed into *e*, to which Ka is added. The word thus obtained in the regular mode in which the language proceeds, is then doubled, the single form Ku cheka not being in use. Nor does the meaning militate against this derivation, as will be seen from the further derivatives, in which the idea of breaking and dividing easily and gently is still the prevailing one. Vungusa moho, unachekacheka muno, usadzoma niumba.
  **Chekecheke,** *adv.* *See* Biribiri. In a flamy, blazing manner. Only used of a fire.
  **Chekuka,** *v.n.*, (1) to break, with the same limit in its use as Chekula.
  (2) To fluctuate, as water in a jar when carried.
  **Chekukira,** *v.d.*
  **Chekula,** *v.a.* (1) (= Ku diekula), to break off a piece. Only used of what is soft and breaks easily, as a cob of Indian corn, bananas, etc.
  (2) To throw up, as flour from a sieve, in order to catch it with the hand.
  **Chekurira,** *v.a.*, to break off *to*, *for*.
**Chekecha** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Kir., Ku kiekedia, and in Kij., Ku degenia), to tickle. Ku chekechua, ri chekechue.
**Cheketeka,** *v.*, to become brittle. Mulala unacheketeka kua

**Chelele** (Kid.), *n.*, the name of a species of bird.
**Chelula,** *v.n.*, to chew the cud.

**Chenakuenu** (Kid.), *n.*

**Chende.** *See* Tende.
**Chendesi,** *n.* (cha) (= Niegnie), aversion, disgust. Contracted from Ki and Endesi, and derived from Ku endesa; lit. what makes one go off.

**Chenu,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), your, yours.

**Chererua.** *See* Cha.
**Cheresa.** *See* Cha.

To throw at a butt; *i.e.* to practise shooting at a mark, a play almost forsaken by boys. Gnania yunalenga; hudzidzuva chero,

**Chidui** (?).
**Chiga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viga), the thigh.
**Chignie,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Koloka. The stalk of the vanda or sansu. The word is composed of the particle Ki and the opt. of Ku gnia. Munazi uki kala na chignie kire, vandare ukisa ri zamia porepore, ni ku funsika. Vanda ridzifuusika chignie; basi ka ri lafia uchi, ni ku umalala. Mutu aki-zamia vanda viomu, rindafunsika chignie kura tu koloni.
**Chignio,** *n.* (cha), the anus. From Ki and Ku gnia.
**Chiho,** *n.* *See* Tiho.
**Chiie,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viie), the horse-fly; lit. something given to stealing, something that lives on theft, the word being composed of the particle Chi or Ki and the opt. of Ku ia, to steal.
**Chika,** *v.a.* *See* Pingu. To give a hint, to suggest. Radically, to afford the instrument or means of knowing; to be a cause or a stimulant to any one. The termination -ka modifies the idea of mere existence to that of effect = to matter. Ku chika ka ku dzoma moyo muno, ku ri ko ku chinchikira.
  **Chikisa,** *v.a.*, to urge, to stimulate, to hasten.
  **Chikisika,** *v.n.*, to admit of being urged, etc.
**Chila** (Kid.), *v.a.*, to surpass, to overcome. The termination -la or -ra, as in the following word, adds the idea of motion. Hudzipiga malau nika m chila (= nika m thima in Kir.).
**Chira,** *v.n.* and *a.* *See* Fiusa; Fiusira; Mutha; Enenzia. To pass, to surpass. Masika gadzichira, The time of scarcity is passed. When the adv. of place is added, it is construed with Na; *e.g.* Ku chira na vavo, To pass by there. Ku m chira muana; lit. To pass a child;—a standing expression, used of a mother who is in the family way before her previous child has learned to walk, who, by being weaned and having no

*Footer: 25*

---

## [PDF Page 39 — Dictionary Page 26 (Chi — Chi)]

  other proper nourishment, suffers from it, and is thus passed by. The expression is also used of a mother guilty of *crim. con.*
  **Chirana,** *v. reit.*, to pass one another.
  **Chirika,** *v.n.* *See* Fufu. To be passable, to admit of passing.
  **Chirira,** *v. rel.* *See* Michocho.
  **Chirisira,** *v. rel.*, to pass beyond, to exceed due measure, *e.g.* in drinking. Nidzenoa, nidzi-u-chirisira. Der., Machira.
  **Chisa,** or **Chiza,** sometimes pronounced Kiza, *v.c.* *See* Golokera; Ludzunga; Dzupia. To make pass, to exceed. Mfananiko ka-u-chiza mahoni. Ku chiza mawe, To cause stones to pass over a house, etc., by throwing them. Ku chiza mihi, To cause trees to pass; *i.e.* to splice them (= Ku mutikiza). Ku chiza kipimo, To exceed the measure; to be beyond one's time. Mutu akikala yuta ndzalani, akenda kutu ku ri ko nioha, be arie na kipimo; arie, asichize; akichiza, akiria muno, ni ku dzi zumburira ukongo.
  **Chisa,** or **Chiza,** often pronounced Kiza, *v.a.*, to pass one's self off or aside, to take one's self aside. Always construed with the reflexive Dzi, and only used of taking shelter from rain. The meaning "off," "aside," is implied in the pure or sharp *z*, which is negative. *See* Za and Zi. Mvula idzegnia, nika dzi chiza muhini, It rained, and I passed myself aside under a tree; or, niumbani, in a house (= Nika-dzi-fidza niumbani, I concealed myself in a house). Na dzi chisa mfula, ichire, basi nienende, I pass myself off from rain, may it pass away, then may I go, *i.e.* I take shelter from rain until it passes off, when I will go.
  **Chisana,** or **Chizana,** *v. reit.*, to make a thing pass another, by throwing them from opposite directions, as arrows, stones, etc.
**Chika.** *See* Chia.
  **Chikisa.** *See* Chia.
  **Chila.** *See* Chia.
**Chiko.** *See* Kiko.
**China.** *See* Kina.
**Chinchikiro,** *n.*, ancient sayings, dark obscure sayings. Maneno ga kare ga nsimo ga hadzidzi.
**Chindi, Kindi** (Kid.), *n.* (pl. Rindi), a squirrel.
**Chindikira.** Ku henda-m-jimba.
**Chindula.** *See* Jindula.
**Chinga,** *v.a.* *See* Jinga. To urge, to incite.
  **Chingira.** *See* Jingira.
**Chinga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a log of wood when used for keeping in a fire all night. Composed of Ki and Nga, and often pronounced Kinga, the change of the *k* into *ch* being unessential. Radically, something coming between, viz. the fire and its extinction, a preventive of the fire going out. Chinga cha ku cheresa moho. Magn., Dzinga; dim., Kadzinga and Kidzinga.
**Chinga,** *v.a.*, to intervene, to interpose, as an obstacle, by way of protection and diversion; hence to obstruct the view; to screen, to protect; to shield from, to parry; to intercept. Atu hara adzi hu chinga, kuani ambere zehu. Hundaricha ku chinga muiri, ukale luasu, makongo gakidza, gaingire? Shall we leave off to screen the body, let it be open, maladies if they come, they may enter? This is the natives' argument for charms. Gnania musiku yudzilonda ku pigua, ela yudzichinga, Mr. So-and-so was about to be struck, or beaten, but he parried it off. Ku chinga madzi na mudzungurisi, To intercept water

## [PDF Page 40 — Dictionary Page 27 (Chi — Cho)]

  with a branch of a cocoa-nut tree tied to the stem, a pot being placed underneath it.
  **Chinchikira,** *v.d.*, to lay across *to*, *for*. Trop., to hint at (implying taunt. *See* Ku chika).
  **Chingama, Kingama,** *v.n.*, to form an obstacle, to prove an obstruction, to stick, especially used of what lies across. Radically, to intervene within. N.B.—In this and the two following words, the pronunciation *k* seems more frequently used than *ch*.
  **Chingamia, Kingamia,** *v.a.*, to obstruct, to lay across.
  **Chingamiza.**
  **Chingika** (also pronounced Chinchiga), *v.* (= Ku chingamia). Ku chingika mihi, To lay trees across. Nidzichinchika gogorangu mohoni, kuamba rikatike vinga viiri.
  **Chingira,** *v.d.* and *instr.*, to screen, to parry, to intercept for, with. Yudziamba apigue, be nidzi-m-chingira mufiu; lit. He said may he be beaten (*i.e.* he was about to be beaten), but I screened him with a sword. Der., Muchinchiko; Muchingiko; Tinchikiro; Tingo.
**Chingirisi** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*), the name of a species of bird.
**Chingo.** *See* Tingo.
**Chio,** or **Kio,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vio), a small kind of basket, formerly used to eat from. Kare, atu ari akihenda vio na vititi.
**Chira.** *See* Chia.
  **Chirika.** *See* Chia.
  **Chirira.** *See* Chia.
  **Chirisira.** *See* Chia.
**Chiramuko,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), morning. From Ku lamuka, or Ku ramuka, an awaking, starting or setting out. Chiramuko kiidzi, The raw or unripe, *i.e.* the early, morning. Chiramuko kukuni, The morning in the fowl; *i.e.* at cock-crow. *See* Lurauko. Chiramuko cha Mulungu. Hangu chiramuko cha Mulungu hudzisinda vavo chi hata dzua ku bodoka. Chiramuko che, On its morning; *i.e.* on the next day.
**Chiru,** *n.*, thirst. *See* Tiru.
**Chiru,** *adj.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), black (used of any dark colour). Contracted from Ki-iru, and sometimes also pronounced Kiru. Kitu hiki ni chiru, or, kiru, This thing is black.
**Chiru,** *n.*, the black (colour), something black. Chiru cha dzidzo, The iris, the black of the eye.
**Chisana,** or **Chizana,** *v.* Ku chazana maneno.
**Chita,** *v.a.* *See* Jita. To boil.
**Chita,** *v.a.* *See* Kita. To fix.
**Cho,** (1) *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class). *See* Kipiga; Kirufu; Komba. Thy. It is abbreviated from Chako, and is enclitic. When the stress lies upon it, Chako must be used.
(2) *rel. pron.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), which. Kitu udzacho ria, be ndicho chako; ela hikira wa ambacho ku dzangue ku ki ria, be si chako, hata Mulungu a ku amurire m'egnie, basi ndo urie. N.B.—When preceded by Na, with, or Ndi, it may be considered either the simple pron. it or the rel. pron. which. *E.g.* Kana cho kazi, He or she or they not with *it*, or, not with *which* business; *i.e.* He has nothing to do with it. Ndicho, It is it, or It is which; or, The same it, which.
(3) *dem. poss.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), that. Abbreviated from Kicho.
**Cho.** *See* Fuzirua; Idzui. A particle enclitic, denoting the whole night, as Chi denotes the whole day. Derived from Ku cha, to dawn. Used with verbs, it has an accent of its own, and may be re-
