## [PDF Page 41 — Dictionary Page 28 (Cho — Cho)]

  peated at pleasure. Usiku cho (= Usiku osi), The whole night. Ku busa moho usiku wa cho hata ku ka cha, ndo ku cheresa moho. Nidzichesa cho, sikalala hata kudzecha ba. Nidzi sumbasumba cho, sika ona usinsisi. Yudz'enenda cho cho cho cho cho, He has gone all the night long. Yudz'enenda for Yudzienenda.
**Cho, Choo** (Kik.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vio), (1) a branding-iron, used by the Wakamba to mark cattle.
(2) The mark made by it. Radically, something which enters, from Ki and Ku oa. Cho ndicho ki dzomerua cho gnombe, iki hendua mumfano. Cho hiki ni cha gnombe za gnania musiku (= Mumfano hiu ni wa gnania musiku).
**Choa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vioa). *See* Kukuta. A sheath. Radically, something to enter, an entrance. From Ki and Oa in Kij.
**Chobo,** *n.* (= Mburi in Kins. ?). *See* Tobo; Bangalalo.
**Chocha,** *v.a.*, to dip into.
**Chochoki** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Msonga in Kins.), an arrow made of wood only, without an iron head.
**Chofu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), bad, spoiled. From Ki and Ofu.
**Choga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vioga), (1) a mushroom. Choga ki meracho muhini, ka ki riwa, ela ki meracho dzi, ndicho kiriwacho; hata vimerafio dzi vingine ka vi riwa, A mushroom growing on a tree is not to be eaten, but when growing on the ground the same is eaten; but others growing on the ground are not eaten; *e.g.* growing where a euphorbia, mufumakua, has decayed, they are bad.
(2) The name of a cutaneous disease, the beginning of what is called mahana. Ki ronda hiki kina choga. Gnania yunahenda ukongo wa kioga; yuna mabato ga vioga, vanadengelesa. Angue: ni vioga; ni vioga viani? nago ni mahana, gadzimanikana kare.
**Chogaifu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viogaifu), the name of a species of bird.
**Chogandzofu,** *n.* (pl. Vi-), a kind of mushroom; lit. the elephant-mushroom. Formerly, when gathering these mushrooms, the natives first held a lamentation over them, lest, for eating them without it, their relatives should die!
**Chogni,** *n. pr.*, (1) the name of a kaya, or town, in the Duruma country.
(2) The name of a town and tribe of Wanika, a day's journey to the north of Rabai.
**Choho** (Kid.), **Joho.** *See* Kisisi.
**Chokaifu,** *n.*, a small ash-coloured bird.
**Chokocho.**
**Chokola,** *v.a.* (= Ku shokoda). *See* Gundizika. To pick out, to scoop out. Ku chokola meno. Ku chokola madzo. Ku chokola tosa. Ku chokola kisingihi.
  **Chokoreka,** *v.n.*
  **Chokorera,** *v.d.* Unachokorera hino.
**Chokolo, Jogolo,** *n.* (ra and wa, pl. Ma-), a cock.
**Cholofu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ch and ki class). *See* Mafu. Soft. Contracted from Ki and Olofu.
**Chombo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viombo). *See* Kigongogo; Muzuzi; Zuza. Radically, something knocking or being knocked about; from Ki and Omba, which, in Kns., means to knock, and, in Kij., to beg. (1) A corner.
(2) (Kij.) A vessel, an instrument (in the latter sense = Chia).
(3) Anything buried in the ground as witchcraft. Minazi yo-mukazikua chombo samiani, As for your cocoa-nut trees, there is buried a vessel somewhere in the grove for

*Footer: 28*

---

## [PDF Page 42 — Dictionary Page 29 (Cho — Chu)]

  bewitching them. The *mu* in Mukazikua refers to *ni* in samiani, and is not the 2nd pers. pl. of the per. pron. *See* Mu and Mumo.
**Chomoe** (Kid.), *n.* (cha) (in Kir. = Mafi ga chuma), the dross of iron.
**Chomu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ch and ki class), hard, difficult; dear, expensive. From Ki and Omu.
**Chonda** (= Kiherehere in Kij.).
**Chondo** (Kig.), *n.* (cha, pl. Viondo), a kind of bag, made of the fibres of some plant or tree. From Ku onda.
**Chonga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vionga). *See* Kinundu. The name of a kind of beetle, injurious to young cocoa-nut trees; it eats off the top. From Ku onga.
**Chongo,** *n.* *See* Tongo.
**Chongoe.**
**Chongua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a species of wild aloe; its leaves are shorter than of the konche, but the points are much sharper. From Ku onga.
**Choni,** *n.* (pl. Vioni).
**Chonsue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Dzekeka. A cripple. The word is composed of the particle Ki and the opt. of the pass. voice of Ka onsa; lit. be he, or she, diminished or lessened.
**Chopola** (Kid.), *v.a.* (in Kir., Ku dzopola; Kij., Ku dosa jito), to make the eye run with water, from a blow or an accident. Ku chopolua ni kidudu, To be made to run with water by an insect.
**Chora,** *n.* *See* Jora.
**Choro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vioro) (= Cho, of which it is merely an assimilation to their own tongue, which generally avoids the collision of two vowels by putting a consonant between them), a branding-iron. Choro cha ku dzomera gnombe, A piece of iron for burning cattle.
**Chota** (Kid.), *v.a.* (in Kir., Ku dzota), to peck, to pick up, as birds.
**Chotherua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viotherua), an eye-witness. Radically, one who has been on the spot. From Cho and Ku therua. This appears to be the only instance of Cho being used instead of Ki in the formation of a noun. It was discovered after eleven years' residence in East Africa. Chotherua changu ni gnania na gnania, ndio aokala vavo.
**Choyo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vioyo). The particularized and diminutive form of Moyo, heart, life. From Ki and Oya. Radically, a species of heart, as that which beats or throbs; a little heart, but only in the moral sense. *See* Moyo. (1) A beating or throbbing. Choyo hiki-kina-ni piga (= Pa-ni-dukuda in Kij.). Nina vatu-vana ni piga choyo (or, vioyo).
(2) Avarice, covetousness, stinginess, a little heart. Gnania yuna choyo-yuna ku lafia muana wa ndani, Gnania is so avaricious as to take from you a child of within, *i.e.* still in the womb. Yuna choyo na niama, na uchi, etc., He is stingy with his meat, with his palm-wine, etc.
**Choza.** Ku henda choza muhogo.
**Chu,** *n.* Maere ga viuni.
**Chuguta,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a cob of Indian corn after the grains are taken off.
**Chukuchu.**
**Chula,** *n.* *See* Chulua, which is more frequently used.
**Chulo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viulo), any stick when pointed for digging or for ripping up the husk of a cocoa-nut, in order to get out the nut. Derived from Ki and Ua in Kij. and Kig., something to undo with. Kimulo, of which it is the particularized and diminutive

*Footer: 29*

## [PDF Page 43 — Dictionary Page 30 (Chu — Chu)]

  form. Chulo cha ku dzimbira gopue. Chulo cha ku furira madafu, hebu nazi, A stick sharpened for ripping off the husk of unripe cocoa-nuts or of ripe cocoa-nuts.
**Chulua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a frog. They distinguish between the following kinds: (1) Chulua kibomu, The great frog, kiambuacho ni shaha ra chulua, which is said to be the chief of the frog species; or, the frog-chief. (2) Chulua mukonsue. (3) Chulua musafula. (4) Chulua nchombe. Chulua higi ndicho ki rira cho kilekile.
**Chuma,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), iron; also the dross of iron when reduced to powder and applied, as medicine, to a kind of boils called firangi. Derived from Ki and Uma, something hard. Muana hiyu yuna firangi, murututu ka u mu hensa, basi na m-badika chuma ( = in Kid., chomoe). Chumachumachi (= Kisike-ki na bunduka ku vonda mavunga).
**Chumba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), an enclosure; a small space enclosed; a small room. Derived from Ki and Umba, and the particularized and diminutive form of Niumba, a kind of house. N.B.—In the meaning of room or apartment, the word always refers to Swahili or Arab houses, their own huts being not divided into such. With the Wanika the word is applied to: (1) An enclosure for fowls, chumba cha kuku, made by sticks driven into the ground and covered over. In this the fowls are confined during the day, but only during the time of planting. Atu ahenda chumba, machira ga ku niala, kuamba kuku asafukula madzina, hata vitu vikihenda makodza mahahu, basi kuku akaupusua chumbani.
(2) Chumba cha Govu, The temporary enclosure of the Govu company, made of sticks and palm leaves, without any roof. Men and women have each a separate one, in which, during the festival called Niambura, they are for a certain time entirely excluded from all intercourse with others. Mutu akithura, ndo vahenduavo chumba cha alume, na cha ache; kuani-akisagala niumbani, andaguirua ni vidio. *See* Kidio.
**Chumfi, Chumvi,** *n.*, sea-water. In Zanzibar the word means salt. Madzi ga chumvi ndigo Aravai a chitago muniu, Water of the sea is it which the Ravais boil salt; *i.e.* they procure salt from sea-water by boiling it. Only such, however, is taken as gathers in a small pit made in the sand near the beach. *See* Niongo.
**Chunga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Luyeyo; Kodzola. (1) Any food eaten about noon; a luncheon, a refreshment.
(2) (Kij.) (= Samia in Kir.), a grove of cocoa-nut trees; Contracted from Ki and Unga. Radically, something that joins, a joining: in the one case with regard to strength—gathering up one's strength, the full meal being eaten in the evening; in the other case it is the being near together—an assemblage. In the first meaning, the idea of joining might also be referred to time, as that which comes in between breakfast and dinner. *See* Wari. Ndzoni, huoye, hurie chunga, Come, let us rest, let us eat a luncheon, take refreshment. Sifikire Kisiwani, nari mumo viungani ku gula uchi, I did not arrive in the island, I was in the groves to buy toddy.

## [PDF Page 44 — Dictionary Page 31 (Chu — Dah)]

**Chungua,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), an orange.
**Chunu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the hip or haunch, the loins. From Ki and Unula, something that raises, lifts up. Chunu cha ushanga; lit. A hip or loin of beads; *i.e.* a string of beads of the length to go round the loins. It is measured by looping it over the thumb and bringing it double to the elbow. When worn it is called vindi. Ku ona chunu, To see the loins.
**Chuo** (Kij.), *n.* (cha, pl. Viuo). *See* Kutania. A book.
**Chururika,** *v.n.*, to leak, to pass aside or sideways. Only used of fluids. Uchi wangu unachururika kanda, My toddy leaked out by the side (= Unagera na kanda). When the tree itself is spoken of, Ku ambasa is used.
**Chusu, Chuzu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a kind of small lizard. Yukala munazini, yufiala kigovani.

## D.

**D,** the fourth letter of the alphabet, sometimes written for *ch*, sometimes for *j*, sometimes for *t*, and sometimes for *th* as in "thy." The pronunciation is the same as in English.—[ED.]
**Da, Ta,** *n.*, a lamp.
**'Da,** *adv.* *See* Niaha; Hata. At all. Sihensa 'da, I don't like it at all.
**Dabadaba,** *v.n.* (= Ku daba, Kns.). *See* Elemea; Ku babarika; Ku galagala; Ku futafuta; Ku vayavaya. To struggle, to flounce, to talk idly, against evidence, to jangle. Kaidima ka okerera, yunadabadaba, yulonda ku hoha. Mutu arie vevi na kufua, be yunadabadaba. Yudzikana, angue-seye, be yunadabadaba.
**Dabira,** (1) Yudzihenda-ki-dabira kasidi kitu hicho.
(2) (Kid.) Si lukolo lua vevi, ni lua ku dabira (in Kir. = lua kure). Muana naye yuna-ku-dabira.
**Dabuikiza,** *v.a.* (= Honge; Tonsi?), to be *hasty*, unsteady. Unadabuikiza mdzuzi, una-u-mala ke. Amegnania yudzilafia mboga ningi, hudzidabuikiza hata hudzivozera wari. Der., Mudabidabi.
**Dabakero** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (in Kir. proper, Luduba).
**Dabaulo** (Kir.), *v.* *See* Gozola. Nenda nikadabaulo.
**Dada,** *v.a.* *See* Ansa. To taste. Dada kitu hiki, kinahama, ki-mdzuano. Ka-vi-upukika kabisa, sidadeni. Sidadeni mukalalama. Dada ku dzuva ga! (= Gesa ku dzuva ga).
**Dadalika,** *v.n.* *See* Dziudauda. To take a leap, for dealing a blow. Trop., to be forward, hasty. Yudzidadalika, yudzi-m-kota mbalahi ya madzo, mairi. Gnania kaambirua neno; ukisumurira na-ye, uki-mu-ambira neno, 'ye nikudadalika, akakuenda sema; yuna lusemo muno.
  **Dadalikira,** *v.d.*, to take a leap to, for. Yudzi-m-dadalikira ku-m-dzuva iwe.
**Dadarika,** *v.n.*, to be in a state of irritation, to itch all over. Muhoho akibadikua murututu, akirira muno, nikuambua: yunadadarika. Muiri una-ni-dadarika kua luambe (= ku wawiwa).
**Dado,** *n.* (= Bungo). Obs.
**Dafu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a cocoa-nut partly ripe, when full of water. (1) Dafu rakukoa. (2) Dafu regnie. Dim., Kidafu; Kadafu.
**Dafuda** (Kij.), **Tafuta,** *v.a.* *See* Lavalava; Ulula. To seek, to search.
**Dahayari** (Kij.), **Tahayari,** *adj.* (= Dayari). *See* Iikira. Ready.

## [PDF Page 45 — Dictionary Page 32 (Dah — Dal)]

  Ku ika dahayari. Na-dzi-ika dahayari, machero nirauke, nienende. U-dzi-funge, ukale dahayari. Viakuria viangu nidzi-vi-ika dahayari.
**Dahayari** (Kij.), *v.n.* (in Kir. proper, Ku guirua ni haya), to be ashamed.
**Dahiri** (Kij.), *v.a.* (in Kir. proper, Ku arika and Ku hina), (1) to circumcise; (2) to cut the tails of sheep. Na-a-dahiri gnonsi angu (= Na-a-kata michira), I cut the tails of my sheep. Zangu may stand for Angu.
  **Dahiriwa,** *v.p.*, to be circumcised; to have the tails cut (sheep).
**Dai.** Aravai a kare ari na dai sana, ela hikara kana dai kabisa a-nga adziomfaruka; hikara ahaho ni ai; na afiere na-o ni ai. Dai kavana hangu dzana, adzi-ri-richa, ahendaye dai basi ni mutu dubani. Mutu hiye ni rika ra babayo, uki-mu-ona ndirani, mu-avukire kure, mu-hendere dai. Muana hiyu yuna dai, aki-ku-ona, ni ku avuka kure, akagomba na-we kua dai. Mutu hiyu yuna dai aki-ku-va kita, ka-ku-golosera mukono mumenga, yu-ku-golosera mikono miiri, ndio dai. Yudzigomba neno ra dai (ra mbasi, ku-mu-makira, or, ku-mu-lombera muyao).
**Daifu, Thaifu,** *adj.* *See* Duku. Weak, infirm, badly disposed. Vatu hiva ni vadaifu mudzangawe. Yudzigomba neno daifu.
**Daka, Taka** (Kij.), *v.a.* *See* Risasi. To want, to desire.
  **Dakira.** *See* Farasi.
**Daki,** *n.* (ra). Nidzibunda daki ra mugazija muidzi. Udzibuma madzi mangi hata madzere gadzikala daki, ka-ga-veteka.
**Dakuma,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the wild custard-apple.
**Dala,** *v.a.* *See* Remesa. To refuse. Ku-m-dala muche. Nidzikudza-ku-dala, huenende kua mulumeo. Muche yudzikuenda dalua, ela kahensi, wari ku-hu-usatu. Nidzikuza ku-ku-dala, kuamba uze kuangu nawe, umanie mudziwangu. Usikuse mifu, unda-a-dala, andakudza-ku-luma. Mifu hio ka-nga-ku-luma, udzi-a-dala m'egnie.
  **Darira,** *v.d.* Nidzihumua ni gnania, kuenda-m-darira muchewe.
**Dasa,** *v.a.* (1) Nidzi-m-dasa nduguyo-kisinde nda kuenda lala kuenu niumbani, kikuangule niungu. Nidzi-ku-dasa.
(2) (Kid.) (= Ku vaka in Kir.), to border.
  **Dasana,** *v. reit.* *See* Kuari. (1) H'endeni hukadasane kidaso.
  (2) (Kid.) (= Ku vakana in Kir.), to border on each other. Der., Kidaso.
**Daladala,** *v.* *See* Lindana. Straggling separately. Muhama hiu u-daladala. Ndio muhama urio na masuche mabomu, ela hura urio mukuku, masuche-ge ni mavudzu. Niumba za kaya zi-daladala. Zere hiri-tembeze zi-daladala.
**Dalalia,** *v.a.*, to throw, to shoot at a venture. Hudzikuenda insa, nikaona niama-yudzichira kare; basi nika-m-dalalia, Mulungu akaerekisa, nika-m-fumaga. Nidzi-mu-ikira cheneso, be nika-m-dalalia-karakara na ku-m-piga kadi, na ku-m-dieka vavo. Ela Mulungu kaka-ni-pa! Der., Mudalasa.
**Dalale,** *n.* (Kig., Ku henda dalale), polygamy (?).
**Dalamu** (Kij.), **Thalamu,** *v.a.*, to defraud, overreach. Yu chari muanafundi, kadzangue ku dalamu uganga. Kadzankue ku dalamu, yukere madzifundi. Atu akaodalamu ufufi, ndio amaniao madzi ga bahari garifio.

## [PDF Page 46 — Dictionary Page 33 (Dal — Dan)]

**Dali,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Nende in Kid.; Rondoe in Kins.), the mole (?). Madali ga lufusa. Madali ga niumba.
**Dalu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a canoe.
**Dama** (= Dadidadi).
**Dama,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Ku sama. (1) A gulp, as much as can be swallowed at once. Only used of palm-wine. Ku piga dama, To swallow once. Ni-pa, nipige dama menga, Give it to me; let me take one gulp. Nidzenoa uchi, nidzipiga dama kana mbiri (= Nidzi-u-dzumburira). Note: The word is said to be getting obsolete, Ku dzumburira being more frequently used.
(2) The state of being swallowed or lost in oil. Said of a new cloth, saturated with oil and perfume; a woman never wearing a cloth without having first removed its whiteness in this way. Nguo-yo idziguira dama, ni mbidzo, This cloth, being covered with oil, is good.
**Dama, Tama,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), validity, legality. Madama ndio ahendao makoro.
**Dama** (Kij.), *n.* (ya). *See* Pungua; Gancheganche. Validity, legality. Ku-mu-ika mutu na dama. Gnania wa-ni-laga kitu kisiku, ka-dza-kudza; be nina dama naye; dama ka-i-dza-ni-la, namania yundakudza. Kitu kisiku kina ni damani kina-ku-damanidze to?
  **Damaika,** *v.n.*
  **Damani** (Kij.), *v.a.* *See* Ekemeza. To desire. Uchi una-ni-damani. Kitu kisiku kina-ni-damani. Nadamani kitu kisiku.
  **Damaniwa,** *v.p.*, to be desired. Nadamaniwa ni kitu kisiku, A certain thing is desired. Nadamaniwa ni chakuria kingine, Other food is desired.
  **Damasha,** *v.* Nina damasha ya niama,—ya uchi, etc. (= Nina damani), I wish for meat, for toddy, etc. Nidziusa damasha (= damasha idziuka). Nina damasha na kitu kisiku, ela basi si-ki-ona.
  **Damauka.** Yudzi-ni-amba; yunda-ni-rehera wari, nikahenda damaa, nika-m-rinda hata nidzidzoka, hata damaa idzidamauka (= idzi-ni-la).
**Damana** (also **Ku damani**) (Kij.), *v.a.*, to render safe by charms; to stay the blood, when you have cut yourself. Yudzi-mu-damana hata yudzilala usinsisi, basi aka-kuenda iya; yudzikuenda na damana. Miladzo inarua muno; londani mutu amaniaye ku damana, aze, a-m-damane.
**Damana,** *n.*, the name of a special charm, supposed to have the property of sending those into a deep sleep whom its possessor intends robbing; lit. something that renders safe. Muifi wakudza na muhi wa damana, udziingira, yudzihala gnombe.
**Damani** (Kij.), *n.*, desire, wish.
**Damau,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (in Kig., Namu), the name of a species of large wild animal, remarkable for its immense dewlap. Damau yuna moro mbomu sana, The damau has a very large dewlap. It is said that wasps (mifu) build their nest in it! Yunga za niahi.
**Damba.** Muana yuna hambala damba-damba-damba.
**Damfa,** *v.a.*, to carry away, as plunder or booty.
  **Damfira,** *v.d.* Amasai adzi-hu-damfira gnombe ak'enda na-zo, The Masai have taken the cattle and gone their way.
**Dambi, Thambi** (Kij.), *n.* (ra), sin.
**Damini, Tamini.**
**Damu** (Kij.), *n.*, blood. Kuingira damu.
**Dana,** *v.n.* *See* Kunche; Fururisa;

## [PDF Page 47 — Dictionary Page 34 (Dan — Dan)]

  Dzua. To part with, to separate from. Dzua ridzidana nadzi, The sun has left, set. Ku dana na muche, To separate from a wife. Nari na miaso, ela be ku sikira higo maneno madzo, basi muiri udzi-ni-dana. Nidzi amba, niumbayangu ka-i-nda sira, ela basi nikihenda mbiriri, nikisa oya hata niki-i-mala basi vino muiri udzi-ni-dana, or, vilungo vidzi-ni-dana. Adzi danira-ni, kondo nini? or, Kondo niyani hata ku dana?
  **Danadana,** *v. reit.* *See* Lurauko; Mu. To dawn. Usiku udzidanadana.
  **Dania,** *v.a.* *See* Mafu; Muenensi. To separate. Yudzi-u-vula muzigowe, aka-u-dania, ndo ukadzukurika. Ku dania atu ahehao. Ku dania madzo. Kadzomba kavudza akadania madzo nidanie, or, ku danie? Kuansa ni fuhuse manina.
  **Danika,** *v.n.*, to admit of separating or being separated. Nidzi-a-dania, ela kakadanika, be hudzi-a-richa. Adzidaniua, adzidanika.
  **Danikana,** *v. reit.* *See* Niambura. To part asunder, to part from each other.
  **Danira,** *v. rel.* Der., Dano (pl. Ma-).
**Danava** (Kig.), *v.n.*, to appear like a youth, as becometh a mudana, by being well greased, ochred, and ornamented. N.B.—The word is never used of females.
**Danda,** *v.a.*, to clamber, to climb with hands and feet, in contradistinction to Ku shombera. Yudzi-u-danda muhi hata yudzi-u-ingira. Muhi urio na kidina, usio pandiso, usio tahi vevi (= Ku danda and Ku shombera).
  **Dandanda,** *v.n.*, to step over from one stone to another in fording a river, to pass along a tree laid across a river. Nidzi dandanda maweni hata nidzifuka. Na dandanda na mudandando, or, mudandandoni hata nikiupuka, or, hata nikifuka. In both cases Nika may be employed as well. Ku dangadanga na njira yudzi guirua na ye, or, adzi guirua osi, or, adzi lalana. Der., Mudandando.
**Dandamuka,** *v.n.*, to become brisk, lively, cheerful. Dzua na riale, udandamuke vilungo.
  **Dandamusa,** *v.a.*, to make brisk, etc.; to animate, to cheer. Ku dandamusa muiri, vilungo. Ku dandamusa mugeni.
**Dandara,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a hurdle; lit. something spread out or extended. (1) Strings of beads wound round the legs above the ankles by females.
(2) Thin sticks, cut in equal lengths, and laced together in the form of a mat. This, being spread on a frame, fixed into the ground, completed formerly the bedstead of a Rabai man. *See* Uriri. Mutu ku suka dandara, rina wenga, or, kuna wenga.
**Dandasa,** *v.a.* (= Ku handika; Ku anika; and Ku kunsula), to expand, to lay open, to spread out. Ku dandasa nguo kuamba i ume. Ku dandasa gumo (= Ku-ri-kunsula sana).
**Dandauka,** *v.n.* (= Dandamuka; Dangamuka). *See* Fuiha. (1) To get unwound, to unwind itself.
(2) Trop., to feel free and easy after some indisposition. Muiriwangu hangu dzana-udzidandauka ku la ukongonia.
  **Dandaula,** *v.a.* *See* Niacha; Vindi. To unwind, to wind off. Trop., to explicate, to explain. Ku dandaula madzango. Ku dandaula maneno.
**Danga, Tanga** (Kij.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a sail.
**Danga, Tanga,** *v.*, to sail.
**Dangadanga,** *v.n.* *See* Hanga.

## [PDF Page 48 — Dictionary Page 35 (Dan — Dar)]

  To wander about. Muana hiye wari akidangadanga, kavana mutu aye-mu-umia; ela hangu dzana yudziuma; gnania ndiye akaye-mu-guira to, aka-mu-umia.
**Dangamana** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to mix, as people of different places and tribes. Midzi na midzi idzidangamana (= idzikutana vamenga; in Kir. = Kutana).
**Dangamuka,** *v.n.* (= Ku dandamuka), to feel at ease, to be comfortable, lively, cheerful; to be at liberty or at large. Dzadziga na ayao, ndo muiri undavo-ku-dangamuka. Nere siwesa, ela hangu dzana nasikira muiri ukidangamuka. Nidzioha moho, muiri udzi-ni-dangamuka. Mutu hiyu yu peho, kakadangamuka vilungo, yu nga dza arie mukongo. Kuku azidangamuka, The fowls have got at liberty, or are at large. Said of such as had been confined, as also of such as have grown up and keep no more with the mother. N.B.—This word is more properly used of fowls, and not Ku dandamuka. Note: Of a stranger both words, Ku dangamuka and dandamuka, may be used, but of fowls only the former.
  **Dangamusa,** *v.a.* (= Ku dandamusa), to enliven, to cheer. Dzua rizi-ni-dangamusa muiri. Dzadziga na ayao, u-dzi-dandamuse.
**Danguedangue** (Kid.), *adj.* and *adv.* (= Daladala in Kir), dispersed, in a dispersed state or manner. Munda-we umera danguedangue, His field grew in patches.
**Dangulia** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to go before, to go first. Nadangulia mbere, akidza, na a-ni-due.
**Dangadza,** *v.a.*, to open up. Only used of the tapping a new vanda. The agema proceed in the following way. The vanda is first bound up tightly for about three days, when they begin to tip it. As the sap is some days in coming, no vessel is attached. When the vessel is required, the first toddy obtained is poured out on the ground, as a libation to the komas, to get their favour and influence for causing the tree to flow richly. As soon as the liquor flows freely, the business of drawing is called by the regular name, Ku gema. Ku dangaza mianso; lit. To open up beginnings; *i.e.* to begin tapping new vandas. *See* Muanso. The following expressions mark the gradation of the business from the binding of the vanda to the flowing of the toddy:—(1) Nafunga vanda. (2) Nadangadza muanso wangu. (3) Nakueza vibaria. (4) Nanoerera dzulu; or, Nadzumburira dzulu. (5) Naonsa na kibaria; or, Naonsa miansoyangu. (6) Miansoyangu idzimuta kifulo. (7) Miansoyangu idzihumbuka. (8) N'enda nikageme.
**Dano,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), lit. that which separates, goes off in another direction. From Ku dana, a way branching out from another. Dano ra nchira, A byway. Ukiona madano, basi guira mukono wa ku modzo hebu wa ku lume. Puku ni ku fula, akahenda madano mangi.
**Dara,** *v.a.*, to count, to number; to reckon, to esteem. Mutu hiye kadara mameye.
  **Darana,** *v. reit.*, to count or number one another. Said of a party of men, when going to divide meat amongst themselves. This is done by cutting a slip of wood for each man, and these are then counted instead of the men, from a superstitious dislike of being pointed at. Lafiani

## [PDF Page 49 — Dictionary Page 36 (Dar — Ded)]

  vigongo, hudarane, hugafie niama, huenerue, Give ye out the slips, small pieces of wood; let us number each other; let us divide the meat; may we all be reached; *i.e.* each get his portion. *See* Enira.
  **Darika,** *v.n.*, to admit of being counted, etc. Kadarika, ni angi.
  **Darira,** *v.d.* *See* Madaro. To count to, for another. Ni-darira hizo nazi, ni-zi-manie isabu-ye.
  **Dariza,** *v.a.*, to reckon upon, to expect. Na-m-darisa hata dziku hizo adzi-zo-laga, akisa kudza, basi ndamania si mutu wa kudza. Na dariza madzi, nifuke na magulu. Ni-zi darize nguo, I shall wait for the clothes.
  **Darizania,** *v. reit.*, to reckon upon, to expect one another.
**Daruka,** *v.n.*, to tear, to get torn.
  **Darura,** *v.a.*, to tear, to rend. Der., Madara; Madaro; Midaramidara; Mudaro.
**Daradasi,** *n.* (ra and ya). *See* Kidanga. Paper. Pepo hiye yulonda pingu ya daradasi ikayoandikua, This ghost wants a charm of paper which is written on.
**Daradia** (Kij.), *v.*, to claim, to ask for payment. Yuna uifu, yuna-m-daradia muchewe.
  **Daradiana,** *v. reit.*
  **Daradiwa,** *v.p.* *See* Sherehe.
**Daradibu, Taratibu** (Kij.), *n.* and *adv.* (= Porepore in Kir.), order, a steady and regular way of acting without either force or haste; orderly, steadily, cautiously. Sudi uhende utu wa daradibu, ela ukihenda wa ngufu, kundaidima.
**Daraka** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za). *See* Ririka; Fereheka. Surety, responsibility for paying the debt of another. Ku piga daraka. Mu-ve kitu hicho alondacho, daraka niyangu, akisa-ku-riva, ninda-ku-riva mimi. Gnania musiku yudzi-ni-pigira daraka, na kuamba si iye, singapata. U-mu-ve, daraka ni zangu.
**Darazira,** *v.a.* *See* Cheneso. To throw, to shoot. Only used of an object indistinctly seen at a great distance, or through a small opening between the branches of trees. Note: The word seems to be derived from Ku dara, and the primary idea would therefore be to guess, to calculate in taking aim. Nidzi-mu-ona wiriwiri, na ku-m-darazira mufui, na ku-m-fumaga keri.
**Daro.** *See* Charo.
**Daruka.** *See* Dara.
**Darura.** *See* Dara.
**Dasa, Dasana** (= Ku vaka in Kir.). *See* Dala.
**Dava** (Kitaita), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Adaida akudza na madava ga tumbaku.
**Davula** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku limbua in Kij.; Ku dovola in Kir.), to eat the first fruit of a plantation.
**Dawala** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to reign.
  **Dawaza,** *v.a.*, to install. Hivo mbere-mashaha ga kinika ari akidawasua ni Wali.
**Dayari, Tayari.**
**De.** De de de. *See* Ge ge ge.
**Deba,** (1) *v.n.*, to shake, to sway, to swing. Pfuiho nire zinadeba. Yudzikula haraka, yu-mure, kidza ni muvudzu, yunadeba.
(2) (Kid.), *v.a.*, to shake by beating. Udebe hata ubite.
  **Debadeba,** *v. reit.*, to continue swaying.
  **Debuereka,** *v.n.* *See* Umiria. To faint.
**Debe.** Akudza alulu-akohenda debe-lukadeba. Dziku ya kure.
**Debedebe,** *adv.* Pfuiho z'enda debedebe. Der., Mudebe.
**Dedema,** *v.n.*, to tremble, to shiver.
  **Dedemeka,** *v.n.*, to be precipitate,

*Footer: 36*

---

## [PDF Page 50 — Dictionary Page 37 (Ded — Den)]

  rash. Especially used of one always ready to join a fight or quarrel. Gnania ni musiru, akiona kondo, yunadedemeka. Unadedemeka-hio kondo ni yako hebu dze?
  **Dedemera,** *v. rel.*, to tremble, to shiver for, from. Only used in asking. Nadedemera peho, mvula, etc. Nidzipigua ni mvula ndosa ni dedemera. Wadedemera-ni? What are you trembling from? Der., Kidedemeza; Kidedemo.
**Dederuka,** *v.n.* (= Ku fiola muno), to be clamorous, to be vehement in scolding. Dzana nasikira lonso-na-m-sikira abe gnania akidederuka; be wahendua-ni, or, wahendua-dze?
**Degadega,** *v.n.* (= Ku regarega), to totter, to shake, to be loose. Nguzo inadegadega, ka-i-ka uma.
**Dekerua,** *v.p.*, to be left, to remain. Atu osi adzienenda, nikadekerua hecheyangu vavo. Atu osi adzikimbira, hukadekerua alume airi tu. Gnania na gnania ndo Malande adzio dekerua.
**Dekeredekere.** *See* Ngorongoro.
**Dele,** *n.*, *adj.*? *adv.*? *See* Dziridzire. Kirenge ki-dele. Kitu hiki ki-dele kuangu. Ludzaga ludzi idzala dele lua madzere. Usi idzase dele mudzuri.
**Delevuka.**
**Delevula** (= Ku deleva?).
**Delevusa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku voniosa and Ku dzuluvula in Kir.), to let go what was held in the hand, to let slip, to let escape.
**Dema,** *v.a.* *See* Kibago. To hew down, to fell: to cut. Ku dema mihi, To hew down trees. Ku dema mutu, To cut somebody. Ku dema tengere (= Ku niola tengere). Ku dema nguo, To shorten one's garment, by tucking it up. Ku dema lulongo, To form a row. Ku dema mbere, To go before, to walk in front.
  **Demadema,** *v. reit.*, to cut repeatedly, to chop. Especially used with regard to business of no importance, as building a small hut, etc. N'enda nikademedeme vikuni, I go to cut a little firewood.
  **Demana,** *v. reit.*, to cut one another. Ku demana mifiu.
  **Demeka,** *v.n.* *See* Momu. (1) To admit of being cut; (2) to vent, to let out. Kironda kidzidemeka miladzo, miladzo inata ki-si-vo-honesua.
  **Demela** (Kid.), *v.d.* (= Demera in Kir.; Ku dulira in Kins.).
  **Demera,** *v.d.* *See* Muthia. (1) To cut to, for. Gnania yuna malu, kahensi ku-hu-va, h'edeni huka-m-demere gnombe. Ku-m-demera mutu na maneno.
  (2) To cut off in pursuit. Hudzi-a-demera, hudzi-a-ika kahikahi. Piga malo, u-i-demere, u-i-udze niuma gnombe. M-demere na hiko.
  **Demerua,** *v.p.*, to have anything cut down to, for, against one's self. Muifi ni ku demerua gnombe hebu mbusi.
**Demana,** *v.a.* (= Damana and Damani), to stay the blood.
**Demu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Gniere. Lit. something cut or rent; a large rag (a large piece of cloth when rent). Ni nguo bomu i-dza-yodaruka. Ni-pa-ro demurangu, ni-dzi-binikise, Give me that rag of mine, that I may cover myself. Dim., Kademu; Kidemu.
**Denda, Tenda** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku dzula in Kir.), to ridicule; in Kij. the word means to make, to do. Hangu dzana ka-ku-na nduma hizo za kare; uki-m-denda muya-o hikara, akidzukirua, yuna-ku-piga rungu, ama yuna-ku-dema. Ku denda na ku dzula ni kuamba mutu adzekue.

## [PDF Page 51 — Dictionary Page 38 (Den — Des)]

  **Dendana,** *v. reit.*, to ridicule one another. This is said to have been much the practice in former times, when they lived more together in their kayas.
**Dendere** (Kid.). Kirenge kinarira dendere. Mutu hiyu yugomba dendere (= in Kins., Mauyke ya malere, or, ya daznsamua).
**Denga,** *v.a.*, to put aside, to remove, to take away. Konda (K.), to shun. Kudenga kanda (= Ku ika kanda). Ku-dzi-denga. Ku denga na dzi; or, Kudenga na urumengu. Said of a mutu musinsi ayeya-ye muno.
  **Dengana,** *v. reit.*, to put aside one another. Used of relatives who shun or avoid each other. Azidengana; hara a-luao, na hara nao a-luao.
**Dengeleka,** *v.n.* (= Ku sunguluka). *See* Kidengelesa. To move about, to go round. Kidzoa kina-ni-dengeleka; lit. The head goes round to me; *i.e.* I am giddy. Muana hiyu yunadengeleka nadzi, This boy is roving about the country (but Ku yeya is more frequently used).
  **Dengeleza,** *v.a.*, to move about, to go round (anything). Usikate luvande lumenga, dengeleza, ndo ka-i-nda-ahuka. Mutu muche akipiga nkerekere, ni ku dengeleza lurimi.
**Dengura,** *v.a.* (= Ku tharau and Ku mena), to slight, to contemn, to scorn.
**Denguri,** *n.* (ra and ya). *See* Mukema. Contempt, something provoking. Ela kuna denguri we? Ku-ni-hukana mimi;—u-mutu wani ku-ni-hukani mimi? Kuamba ku-muhoho, singa-ku-piga? Ela si denguri keri hiro? nduguyangu ku pigua hecheye-za ku amba yudziiya. Ela si denguri ku kala hecheyangu, ku pigua ni atu angi, ku sunganirua (or, ku mamaniraa)? Gnania yudzi-dzi-kakata dala kua usiru, kudza kalavo ni denguri; kuamba nari vavo, kahungapigana? ela be manire nika-dza-kalavo; or, Mulungu nika dza kalavo.
**Denge,** *n.*, (1) Ra kirenge; (2) Ra mbuzi; (3) = Dzidzi?
**Deni,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-; but also ya, za). *See* Lasima. A debt. Nin'enda nikaise deni rangu. Deni ningi; or, Madeni mangi, Many debts.
**Dera,** *adv.*, together. Only used in connection with the word Ku bua, To fall. Ku bua dera, To fall together; trop., To be equal in strength or property. Adzimigniana, adzebua dera, They wrestled and fell down together. Atu hio adzebua dera; maliyao i-karakara, ka-va-na a-m-pitaye muyawe.
**Derema,** *v.n.*, to become quiet after quarrelling or fighting. Deremani, kalani to! Be quiet, and behave yourselves well! Adziderema, adzihurira. Adziamba ahehe, ela adzikaniua, adziderema.
**Deremuka,** *v.n.*, to descend. Ku deremuka murimani, To descend a mountain. Opposed to Ambuka.
  **Deremusa,** *v.a.* *See* Ku fulumusa and Nderemo in Kij. To take anything down a mountain. Ku deremusa musigo, To carry a load down a mountain.
**Deria, Teria,** *v.a.*, to assist, to help. The word Nguvu, strength, is often added, as, Ndzo, u-ni-derie nguvu; lit. Come and make my strength equal; *i.e.* Come and assist me.
**Desa, Tesa,** (1) *v.n.*, to swing.
(2) Trop., *v.a.*, to play a trick. Mihi mire ni ku desa kua peho, Two trees are played with by the peho. Ku desa

*Footer: 38*

---

## [PDF Page 52 — Dictionary Page 39 (Des — Dia)]

  lufundo, To sling in a swing. H'endeni hukadese lufundo. Ku-m-desa mutu kua uganga hebu kua udzai.
  **Desana,** or **Ku desania, Tesania,** *v. reit.*, to play tricks upon one another. Especially used of aganga, the medicine-men, charmers. Aganga anadesania.
  **Desera,** *v. instr.*, to swing with. Lufundo lua ku desera.
**Deza** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to afflict. Rero Mulungu yudzi-ni-desa, To-day God has afflicted me.
**Dezeka, Dezeka.** Gnania ka-dezeka, uki-m-deza ka-vi-mu-guira.
**Dete,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a low, swampy place, suited for planting rice; a valley. Dete is used of a broader, and Mueha of a narrower, place.
**Deteleka** (Kij.), *v.n.* (= Ku hetereka; Ku kukutika; Ku yuayua), to reel, to stagger.
  **Detelesa** (Kij. and Kid.), *v.*, to cause to stagger by giving one a push.
**Dewadewa,** *v.n.* *See* Ku lewalewa. To suspend one's self by the arms as in play. Ahoho anadzadziga ku dewadewa.
**Di,** *adj.* and *adv.*, straight, erect, vertical. Used as adv., the particle is joined to the verb—Ku goloka, To be straight—and strengthens the sense. It may be repeated at pleasure, but the threefold repetition is used the most, and almost forms a word by itself. Muhi u-di, The tree is straight. Munazi hiu u-di, This cocoa-nut tree is straight. Muhi hiu ukagoloka di, This tree is very straight. Muvaka hiu ukagoloka, u-di, This boundary line is straight, it is perfectly straight. Nchira i-di, The way is straight. Nchira hi ni ya di di di, ka-i-na madano, This way is perfectly straight, goes right on, it has no byways. Dzua ri-di, na vidzoa; lit. The sun is straight with the heads, *i.e.* is vertical. Dzua ri-di di di na vidzoa, The sun is perfectly vertical. Ku ima di, To stand erect.
**Di,** *a particle*, denoting the whole day, all the day long without interruption. It also may be repeated at pleasure, like the preceding. It corresponds to Cho, all the night. Dzua ra di-ni hangu chiramuko hata dziloni. Hangu chiramuko di, Since morning all the day. Hudzienenda di hata kudzedzua, We have been going all the day long till sunset. Nidzisinda vava di, I have spent the whole day at this very place. Mfula idzegnia-idziamba di, idziamba cho, idziamba di, idziamba cho, ndo ku fururisa, ndo dzi i-humbuka-vo kiwawai. Ku ima di, To stand all the day long.
**Di,** *a sound*, onomatop. of thundering. This is always repeated many times. Mvula inadidimiza di di di di di.
**Dia,** *v.n. enclit.* (Ku dia) (= Kudzi-kania m'egnie), to repent. Nidzedia, sindahenda kahiri.
**Dikania,** *v.a.* *See* Madano; Musa. To cross, to cut across, to cut crosswise.
  **Dikaniadikania,** *v. reit.*, to cut into small pieces crosswise.
**Dililia,** *v.a.*, to joke, to trifle with. Only used between grandparents and their grandchildren; lit. to make nothing of one, to treat one as of no account by maneno ga ku dzeana na ga ndumo. Muana hiyu yudzi-ni-dililia, says a Dzawe or Wawe.
  **Dililiana,** *v. reit.*, to joke with each other. Dzawe hebu wawe ni ku dililiana na mudzukula-we.
**Dilisa,** *v.a.*, to revoke, to abrogate, to break up an agreement), to countermand. Ku dilisa mbatha. Endani, mu-

*Footer: 39*

## [PDF Page 53 — Dictionary Page 40 (Dia — Dib)]

  ka-m-dilise gnania, machero asidze, kandakudza-ni-dikisa, asidze bule.
**Dira,** *v.n.*, to fail in obtaining. Nidziamba nigule kitu hicho, ela nidzi-ki-dira. Ku unsuliwa ndivo a vo dira.
**Diza,** *v.a.* and *n.* (= Ku hulu in Kij.), to omit, to intermit. Kadiza kuenda rima. Rero yudzidiza, kakakuenda. Nadiza dziku menga.
**Dia,** *v.n.*, to escape, to get out of danger, to come off safe, to recover.
  **Difia,** *v.a.* *See* Lagurika; Kutuka. To deliver, to save, to let escape.
  **Difira,** *v.d.* *See* Kimbisira; Muduka. To save to, for, in behalf of.
  **Dikiza,** *v.a.* *See* Mutha; Pima. To meet with, to find. Nidzikudza dikisa niuni mundani. Kuamba nidzi-ku-dikiza hiva, be hukaenenda, hungari hudzifika kare.
**Dia, Tia** (Kij.), *v.a.* (= Ku buma in Kir.). *See* Nia; Lasima. To put into. Udzi-ni-tia lasima (= Udzi-ni-dongea). Ndo machero unda-vo-tia.
**Dieka, Tieka,** *v.a.* *See* Odi; Pumuzi; Kulo. To put down, to throw down, to lay as a fowl. Ku dieka moyo, To put down the heart; *i.e.* To become quiet (= Ku duza moyo in Kij.). Naoya, nidieke vilungo. Ku dieka nazi, To throw down cocoa-nuts from a tree. Mfaya anadieka rero—a standing expression, meaning that the mfaya men appropriate a day's toddy, the drawer's portion alone excepted, to themselves. It is called Ku dieka, because for some years they actually take it down themselves. *See* Diekera dzula. Rero kakuna muengero, mfaya adzidieka. Muifi rero yudzidieka minazi pia yosi; or, pia pia pia, A thief to-day has put down all the cocoa-nut trees; *i.e.* he has taken down the *toddy* from the trees.
  **Diekera,** *v.d.*, to put down to, for, towards. Mfaya rero anadiekera dzulu—a standing expression; lit. The mfaya to-day put down from above: *i.e.* they climb the trees themselves to secure all the toddy. All the rest of the people must conceal themselves during the business, under penalty of a fine. This is always done by a new mfaya ana-dzi-diekera choyo, and continued until he becomes too old to climb.
  **Diekerana,** *v. reit.* *See* Kanani. To lay down (anything) one *to* or *for* another (as a wager). Ku diekerana mifunga, To lay wagers.
  **Diekudieku,** *n.* (ra), the taking out by driblets from a bag; lit. snap, snap. Only used in the following proverb: Prov., Diekudieku rinamala pinda, Driblets will at last finish a bag.
  **Diekuka,** *v.n.* (= Ku dekuka; Ku hemuka). *See* Mbambu. To snap (asunder), to get sprained, dislocated.
  **Diekula,** *v.a.*, to take out little by little (from a bag), to snap off, to sprain. (The idea of the word is that of dislocating.) Ku diekula muhama pindani (= Ku hega vichache). Ku diekula dzere, mugazija, etc. (= Ku chekula). Ku diekula mukono (= Ku hemula), To sprain the hand, *i.e.* the wrist.
  **Diekurira,** *v.d.*
**Dia** (Kid. and Kidigo), **Chia** (?), *n.* (ra, also wa, pl. Ma-) (= Kuro in Kir.), a dog. Dim., Kadia; Kidia.
**Dianga,** *v.n.* Only used in connection with Kululu. Ku dianga kululu (= Ku piga kululu), To scream, to shriek.
**Diba** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Mushada. Assistance. Aravai akudza

## [PDF Page 54 — Dictionary Page 41 (Dib — Dig)]

  ku-hu-bumira diba, ku-hu-afuiza viha, kahungaweza heche yehu. Yudzihewa diba ni Mulungu huya; angagula na-ni muchia muzimu; lit. He or she was given help by God; he had bought it with what? one so utterly poor! *e.g.* one presented with a new cloth. Mutu hiye yuna diba; Mulungu aka-mu-va-diba, 'enda-vo dzuma ni ku bada (pata). Munda hiu una diba, This plantation has assistance, *i.e.* a blessing (= mbaraka, kifuna, neema).
**Dibudibu,** *adv.* *See* Dula. Madzi gonagera dibu, dibu. Madzi gaki bigua—mutu akidula—madzi ganarira, ganaamba; dibu, dibu.
**Dida,** *v.n.* (= Ku pisha; Ku shindana). *See* Mfoda; Vindana. To contend, to dispute, to call in question. Gnania yuna mbiriri; yudzidida, hata atu akahensa gago. Gnania yuna kanani, yunadida.
  **Didira,** *v.d.*, to dispute with, to deny to, to gainsay, to contradict.
  **Didirana,** *v. reit.*, to dispute, etc., to contradict one another.
**Dide, Tite,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), small, little. The root-word of Kidide, Mudide, etc. It is changed into Tide when rel. to the ya and za class. Kasha dide, A small box; but Niumba tide, A small house.
**Di di di.** *See* Di. Always pronounced as separate words.
**Didika,** *v.a.*, to carry with both hands, to carry between two or more persons, to carry as ants and birds.
  **Didikira,** *v.d.*
**Didimiza,** *v.n.* *See* Madidimizo; Kure. To thunder. Mfula inadidimiza (di di di di di). *See* Ku dudumiza. Govu yunadidimiza.
  **Didimuka,** *v.n.* (redupl. of Ku dimuka), (1) to move suddenly, to start from being alarmed.
  (2) To start by growing. Only used of new grass when a few inches from the ground. Niasi zidzididimuka, zidzikala mugina; zidzikala niasi sa ku risa.
  **Didimusa,** *v.a.* (redupl. of Dimusa), to startle, to alarm, to put to flight. Mbusi zidzididimusua ni dzui, The goats are alarmed by the leopard. *See* Madidimuko. Gnombe zidzididimusua ni zimba, The oxen are alarmed by the lion.
**Die.** *See* Ndie; Diro. Yudzimfura die yudzienenda.
**Dieka.** *See* Dia. Gnania ndiye adzie ni dieka moyo.
  **Diekedia.** *See* Dia.
  **Diekera.** *See* Dia.
  **Diekuka.** *See* Dia.
  **Diekula.** *See* Dia.
**Difia.** *See* Dia. Usema unapita udugu; kuani, neno hiro ringa hu duru muno, lukoloni kuchu; ela Mulungu na uwe udzi-ni difia; kuani mimi, singasema hiraka kiravo kinga hupiga kinga huduru.
**Digidira** (Kid.), *v.n.*, to titter, to laugh foolishly.
**Digira** (Kig.). Moyo wa ku digira (= Moyo wa ku kania in Kir.).
**Digirika,** *v.n.*, to break, to crumble from being pounded. Madzere gadzidigirika.
  **Digirisa,** *v.a.*, to break by pounding. Nidzivonda madzere, hata nidzi-ga-digirisa, I pounded Indian corn until I broke it to pieces.
**Dignia,** *v.a.* *See* Dorosa. (1) To tighten, to cut from being too tight; to pinch, to gripe. Nguo hi ka-i-ka dignia luzi, inalangala. Yudzi-dzi-funga nguo, yudzi-dzi-dignia sana. Yudzi-m-funga hata yudzi-m-dignia. Madzango gadzialilua, gadzi-ni-dignia. Ku-m-

## [PDF Page 55 — Dictionary Page 42 (Dig — Din)]

  dignia mutu kombe. Yudzidigniua kombe ni dzui. Ndani ina-ni-dignia.
  **Digniana,** *v. reit.*, to pinch one another. Ku digniana kombe.
  **Dignira,** *v.d.*, to splash, to make stick to by splashing. Yudzi-ni-dignira tove.
**Digo,** *pr. n.*, the Wanika country south of Mombas. The portion to the north is called Lubangu, from Duruma to Kauma inclusive. Lubangu, however, is very seldom used. Rero hudzikuenda Digo.
**Diha,** *v.n.* (= Ku fidisa in Kid.).
**Dikania.** *See* Dia.
**Dikidika,** *v.*
**Dikidiki,** *adj.* (= Dzikidziki), fine, small, not coarse. Used of flour. Unga hiu u-dikidiki, ka-u-na dzenga.
**Dikiza.** *See* Dia. Pima hizo nidza zo kudza kuamba nidzi-ku-dikiza vava, be huka uya ku enenda, hungari hudzifika kare; kuani nikakudza kare kapindi kazima.
**Diko,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the hair of the head when grown long enough for being put back so as to cover the neck.
**Dililia.** *See* Dia.
  **Dilisa.** *See* Dia.
**Dima, Thima,** *n.* *See* Tambo. A defeat. Dima ya uganga, udzai wa dima. Dima ndzaiko, or, dzenga. Ku pigua dima.
**Dimbui** (Kidigo), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Gopue in Kir.), a pit, a hollow.
**Dimfa,** *v.a.*, to fling, to thrust. Yuna koro, yudzidimfa chala.
  **Dimfira,** *v.a.* *See* Ugulo. To throw on, to spatter, to sprinkle. Ku dimfira muhaso.
**Dimira,** *v.n.*, to be complete in number or quantity. Atu adzisonga charo hata kidzidimira, basi anaenenda ku hamba. Kuna pishi tide, isio dimira.
  **Dimiza,** *v.a.* *See* Kusa. To complete, to make up, to fulfil.
  **Dimizira,** *v.d.* *See* Mudumudu. To complete, etc., to, for, in behalf of.
**Dimula** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku dumula in Kir.), to diminish, to lessen.
**Dimuka** (Kid.) (= Dumuka in Kir.).
  **Dimusa** (Kid.) (= Ku dimula).
**Dimula,** *v.a.*, to erect, to raise. Ku dimula luera. Machogolo gakipigana, ni-ku-dimula mifuzi ya dzingoni.
  **Dimuka,** *v.n.* Kuku wa Kibarawa niogaze zikadimuka, si lola mbere kura tu aendako.
  **Dimurira,** *v.d.* (= Ku futurira). *See* Futuka. Na-ku-uza porepore, uwe una-ni-dimurira, nidzi-ku-hendadze?
  **Dimusa** (= Ku dimula).
**Dina,** *v.n.*, to leap. Nidzidzuva iwe madzini, madzi gadzidina.
  **Dinadina,** *v. reit.*, to skip, to gambol. Ana mbuzi anadinadina ku dzadziga.
  **Dinira.**
**Dindia,** *n.* (ra), refuse.
**Dindiria,** (1) *v.n.* Gnombe zinadindiria kidindirioni.
(2) *v.a.* Enda, ukadindirie gnombe, basi udze, urie chunga.
**Dindiridindiri,** *adv.* Ku hindirika dindiridindiri.
**Dingania,** (1) *v.a.* (= Ku badilisa; Ku filisi), to divert, to turn aside as to purpose or aim.
(2) *v.n.*, to differ from, to vary. Ku dingania maneno, To turn off words by gainsaying. Ndio upumbafu, udzaodingania atu, This is the foolishness which turned people aside. This refers to those killed by the Masai, who, by the absence of cattle in their neighbourhood, had thought themselves secure, and obeyed not the warning. Ku dingania vadide, To be a little different from.
  **Dinganika.**

## [PDF Page 56 — Dictionary Page 43 (Dio — Do)]

**Dingidia,** (1) *v.a.* (= Ku gnignigniza), to set in whirling motion.
(2) *v.n.*, to be in whirling motion. Ku dingidia ndzuga. Tulua inadingidia (= inafuina). Ngoma za ku dingidia.
**Dioko** (Kid.), *n.* (ra) (= Kidoko; Uhoko), the refuse of castor-oil berries, when pounded and boiled.
**Diokue,** *n.* (ra) (= Dioko in Kid.). Diokue ra mafuha ga mbano, The refuse of the castor-oil.
**Dipa,** *v.a.*, to take out from a large quantity. Madzi ga dele, ni ku dipa na ku uya tu.
**Dipuka,** *v.n.*, to get dug out. Used fig. of nausea and anger (in the first it is = Ku erera, in the second = Ku firuka). Moyo udzi-ni-dipuka, nidzivavika, The heart got dug out to me; *i.e.* I felt nauseous, I have vomited. Moyo udzi-ni-dipuka (= udzi-ni-firuka), The heart got dug out to me; *i.e.* I felt very angry.
**Dipula,** *v.a.* (= Ku dzimba and Ku dzimbula, but particularly used of agriculture), to dig into, to go deep in cultivating the ground. Mutu hiye yunarima ku dipula, That man cultivates the ground so as to dig; in contradistinction to Ku rima dzuludzulu, To turn merely the surface, to cultivate superficially, to hoe the top.
**Dira,** *v.* *See* Dia. To surpass, pita?
**Dirimfa,** *v.a.*, to edge, to border, as mats, baskets etc.; to strengthen the edge.
  **Dirimfika,** *v.n.*, to admit of edging, to turn out well edged. Nidziamba ni ka dirimfe, ela kavana milala, ka kinda-dirimfika. Kidzidirimfua, ela ka-ki-kadirimfika to.
  **Dirimfira,** *v.d.* and *instr.*, to edge to, for, with. Yudzi-ni-pa kikahana, kuamba ni-mu-dirimfire, kaidima ku dirimfa. Kavana milala ya ku dirimfira, ndosa nisidirimfe.
**Diro,** *n.*, that one. Referring to the word Dzitu, and seemingly only used in scolding. It is an abbreviation of Ndiro. Ridzimfura diro ridzienenda. *See* Dzitu. He has been scolding that one; he is gone.
**Disha** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to overawe, to strike with fear. Amasai anadisha, The Masai terrified. Gnania yunalonda ku disha atu, Gnania wants to overawe people. Gnania akadishua ni muchewe, Gnania is overawed by his wife.
**Disho,** *n.* (ra), the act of overawing. Gnania akadishua ni muchewe, yuna disho ri.
**Disia** (Kij.). Ga-ku-disie-ni maneno gano, ku-ga-mania, wala sigako? Maneno higo ga-ku-disie-ni? Una-ga-neno-ni ga go? Ga ku disie-ni maneno ga atu? U-ga-gombera-ni, u-ga-ne-nera-ni we?
**Divira** (= Ku diwa in Kins.). Mifui ya midzare, ndio ihenduayo ya ku divira, kuamba mufui usilae, kua ano-ku-merera, hata niama akiingira midodoni, jembe ki mumo na akuare; uzungu ukaria niama. Mufui wa ku divira ndio urio na akua. This is in contradistinction to Mufui wa kigumba, wa mumo kua mumo. Ku divira mufui, or, chembe.
**Divuka,** *v.n.*, to become loose. Munazi wangu u divuka, ka-u-gemeka kua niuchi (Kid.). Bangala rangu ridivuka (Kid.), My toddy-vessel has got loose.
  **Divula.** Nidzidivula bangala rangu (Kid.).
**Diza,** *v.a.* *See* Dia. To omit.
**Do,** *adv.* (= Pau in Kins.), very exceedingly. Only used in connection with the words Dune, Kidune, Tune, red. It may be repeated at pleasure. *See* Kosi. Madzoge ni madune do, His eyes are exceedingly red.

## [PDF Page 57 — Dictionary Page 44 (Do — Dok)]

**Do,** *n.* (?).
**Doba** (Kij.).
**Dobera,** *v.n.* *See* Kalanga; Kunsira. To look reddish like sound flesh; said of a wound when beginning to heal, to look brown or yellow as fruits, etc., when ripening; also used of meat when being roasted.
  **Dobesa,** *v.n.*, to turn reddish, brown, or yellow. Madzere yanadobesa, The Indian corn is turning brown when ripening. Der., Madobesa; Madofia.
**Dodola,** *v.n.* (= Kij., Dodoa (?); Dagada), to pass or break through. Only used with regard to wood or bushes. Nidzidodola dzakadzaka hata nidzikuenda upuka vatu vasiku, nidzikuenda guira nchira dziku. Niama hiye yunadodola dzakani (= in Kid., Mumenga yunadodola ko musuhuni; simania kahi ni niama, kahi nini).
  **Dodoreka,** *v.n.*, to crackle as something exposed to fire. Madzere gangu gadzidodoreka. Der., Ndodo.
**Dodomera,** *v.n.*, to sink into. Used of mud. Ku dodomera toveni. Vatu hivo vana dodomera; lit. That place is with to sink; *i.e.* You sink in it when passing.
**Dofu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a protruding navel. Magn. of Tofu.
**Doi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a young bull. Doi ra gnombe; yudzita uanani, or, si muana kahiri.
**Doka, Toka,** *v.n.* (= Ku katika). *See* Ndodore. To break, to part asunder, to come off. Trop., to be decided or finished, a palaver. Lukue ludzidoka, The string is broken. Sikiro menga ra kavu ridzidoka, One handle of the basket is broken. Nidzimemena muhi, ela kaukadoka. Muana hiyu kadzadoka tofu. Mala ge gakadoka, gadzikala vigutu. Maneno gadzi komadze? How did the palaver end? Resp., Ah gadzidoka; or, Yadzi katika, It is finished.
  **Dokadoka,** *v. reit.* (= Ku dukaduka in Kins.), to break repeatedly, to have a tendency to break; to be agile in dancing. Konche hiri ka-ri-vonoreka, rinadokadoka. Mtumche hiyu yunamania ku fuina, yuhenda dokadoka.
  **Dosa,** *v.a.* *See* Ngombo; Vovola. To break off or asunder, as a thread or string, etc.; but to break to pieces is Ku funsa, to crack or stretch the fingers. Trop., to decide, to settle, to finish a palaver. Ku dosa lugue, To break a string. Ku dosa mala (= Ku golola mala), To crack the fingers. Yudzidoka mala kua ukongo wa mahana, ndio ukongo udosao mala. Ku dosa maneno, To finish a palaver; but Ku kata is more frequently used. Maneno higano gandaenderera, mukisa-ga-dosa. Gama ku dosua misosa; said of pain.
**Doka, Toka** (Kij.), *v.n.* *See* Dueda; Sia; Dzoloka; Ku pundika. To come out. In Kir., the word is invariably used of the roho, instead of their own word Ku la. Yutoka roho, yudzimar'kisika (yudzefua) (not Yudzila roho).
**Dokola** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku liga; Kins., Zogora), to praise, extol.
**Dokomera,** *v.n.*, to vanish from sight, to get out of sight. Note: The form previous to this, Ku dokoma, does not occur in Kir., neither in Kij. Atu hara anaenenda, adzifika kure, nichari-a-ona; ela hikara adzizimira, adzidokomera. Uka vo, dokomera, nisi-ku-one! Get away from here; be out of my sight, or vanish, that I may not see thee! Note: In this instance the pass. Do komerua may be used as well.

## [PDF Page 58 — Dictionary Page 45 (Dok — Don)]

  **Dokomesa.**
  **Dokoza,** *v.a.*, to disturb, to instigate, to provoke. Ku dokoza mifu. Nidzi-m-dokoza kasidi, kuamba huhehe. Der., Mudokozi.
**Dokosa,** or **Tokosa,** *v.*, to boil.
**Dokola,** *v.a.* (= Ku gotola), to take off as a scab from a wound. Udzi-m-dokola muyao kikoko cha kironda; ela ka kinda-riwa ni mainsi fio, kilonde ku uya?
**Dola** (?) (Kig.). A ki ni dola = dora (Kir.).
**Doma,** *v.a.* (= Ku fumagu). *See* Chero. To prick, to pierce, especially by shooting.
  **Domadoma,** *v. reit.* (= Ku dungadunga), to keep pricking. Used of pain.
  **Domeka,** (1) *v.n.* (= Ku fumagika), to be pierceable.
  (2) *v.a.*, to be pricking the food of others. Only used in scolding or finding fault with an unwelcome guest. Gnania yunaevera muno, kadomeka. Yudzihenda domeka wariwehu, hata egniee kahuka ukuha, He kept pricking our food, so that we ourselves were not satisfied.
**Domo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a projection, a jutting out of land into the sea, or of a mountain into a plain; lit. a large lip. Magn. of Mulomo. Domo ra dzi, A cape. Doma ra murima, The peak of a mountain.
**Domosi,** *n.* (ra). *See* Luasa. The pit caused by a tumour which was not opened, or by a wound when returning. Wari muoga, kahensere ku humbulua hata ivu ridziifua, ridzihumbuka regnie, be rikahenda domosi, kua ufira ku risa, moyo ukiola mumo; ndo domosi. Kironda kidzihenda domosi, kinauya (= kidzimomoka).
**Dona,** *v.a.*, to kiss.
  **Donera,** *v. rel.* Ku donera kua kuku, To peck with a fowl; *i.e.* the pecking of a fowl (= Ku dzota). Ku-m-donera muana, To kiss a child.
  **Donerana,** *v. reit.*, to kiss one another.
  **Donesa,** *v.a.*
**Doniola,** *v.a.* *See* Mudzundu. To scarify the skin slightly, in contradistinction to Ku dzodza; lit. to prick open. This is often done to relieve local pain; a little gunpowder is then put over the scratches, kindled, and rubbed over. Ku doniola vidzoga vidide vidide (= Ku-m-dzodza dzoga tidetide). Unaria ku-dzi-doniola, mbuzi zienende kure (= porepore). Der., Dono; Donorioka (?).
**Donche.** *See* Donde.
**Donda,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma- and Mi-), a large ulcer or wound. Magn. of Kironda.
**Dondola,** *v.a.*, to glean, to cull, to pick out from. Trop., to follow up an argument by answering it. *See* Ku rondora in Kins. Note: The word seems to be the enlarged form of Ku londa, to want, to will, the *l* being changed into a hard *d*, as is often the case. It implies the seeking out, the being after, anything for its removal. Ku dondola luguani (= Ku dzaira), To glean in the straw-field. Muvunga wa kirinsi udzifuna kare, be usere wa lugua, ndo uambuao; n'enende nikadondole. Nadondola mudzerewangu mawe, I pick out the stones from my Indian corn. The idea of "from" lies in the termination -ola. Ku dondola ndodo, To pick out dry twigs. Gnania yuna luga, yudzi-ga-dondola maneno gara tu a-go-ambirua; kana menga aka-ro-ri-sahau, kava, gosi pia yuna-ga-mania.
  **Dondorera,** *v.a.*, to glean, to cull, etc., to, for.
**Donera,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of an insect of a red colour; lit.

## [PDF Page 59 — Dictionary Page 46 (Don — Dor)]

  a pecking, or something to peck at; the superstition about it being this, that when people see it they give it a touch, believing that then they will shortly fall in with some fresh meat. This seems, however, to be confined to children. Ahoho oki-ri-ona, ni ku-ri-donera, angue: ndo andavo dzola niama.
**Donera.** *See* Dona; Miamba; Vioni. Uki-ri-ona, rina ku kolosera ukapata niama ya milazo tuni kuani riro ni tuni.
**Dongea** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to bring into a scrape, to cause mischief to any one; lit. to hew off to. Nduguyo yuna-ku-dongea. Ningapigua hivino, ni ndugu yangu, ndiye adzie-ni-dongea. Sigombe maneno higo, ganda-ku-dongea, m'egnie akasikira, indakala kondo, kandahensa. Udzi-ni-dongea (= udzi-ni-dia lazima).
**Dongoria,** *v.n.* and *a.*, to precede, to go before as to space or time, to take the lead. Hunadongoria mbere, huka-ku-rinde mbere, We go on first and wait for thee further on. Huere vava, ela iye gnania ela si'ye adzeyedongoria mbere, si'ye adzeyedongoria atu, kudzapiga kuku? Ndiye aye-a-dongoria (= ku dora). Gnombe yudzidongoria iyae, or, ayae.
**Donge,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a morsel; lit. something taken off. Ku mega donge ra wari, To break off a morsel of food.
**Dongolos,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a clod.
**Doniola, Toniola.** *See* Dona.
**Dono, Tono,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a spot or speck of colour. Used of such as are at a distance from one another. Mbuziyangu ina matono matono, or, i-madono madono. Kuku hiyu yuna matono matono; or, yu madono madono. Dim., Kadono; Kidono.
**Dononoka,** *v.n.* (= Dona).
**Dora,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Rora.
**Dora,** *v.a.* (= Ku dongoria; Ku virika), to lead the way. Ataita ndio aodora Amasai, kudza ulaga atu na ku damfa gnombe, The Taitas, it is they who led the Masai the way, to come killing people and to carry off cattle. Amasai adzihenda dorua nchira ni Ataita, The Masai have been led the way by the Taitas. Gnania ndiye ayedora atu hata akifika vatu vasiku, Gnania, it is he who led the people the way, until they arrived at a certain place. Yudzikudza mugeni, yudziuza kua gnania, nidzilafia muhoho, yudzi-m-dora, kuenda-mu-onia, There came a stranger and asked after gnania, I therefore directed a child, and he took him and went to show him.
**Doroka,** *v.n.*, to get loosened, to get slack. Uha wangu udzidoroka luvohe, My bow has got slack as to the string. Luvohe ludzidoroka madoro. Musigo wangu udzidoroka, adziefugula niani? My load has got loosened; who opened it?
  **Dororeka,** *v.n.* *See* Kolovondo.
  **Dororesa,** *v.a.* (= Ku gororesa), to trail.
  **Dorosa,** *v.a.* (= Ku regesa). *See* Regesa. To relax, to loosen, to slacken; to droop the wings. Fig., to let out a row; *i.e.* to form into a row (a war term). Ku dorosa mukumbu uki-ni-dignia kua ku ukuha. Nadorosa uha wangu, kunadza mfula, luvohe lusa toka na peho. Kuku huya yudorosa mamfamfa, ganalewalewa, ni mukongo. Ni-dorosani mui, nalumira, Loosen me, O ye! I am being hurt; said by one whose hands are tied closely on his back. M-doroseni punda, mudzi-m-dignia muno, Loosen ye the

*Footer: 46*

## [PDF Page 60 — Dictionary Page 47 (Dos — Dud)]

  donkey; you have tied him too tightly. Atu adzidorosa lulongo, or, muthia, The men have extended themselves into a row to outflank the enemy.
  **Doroseka,** *v.n.* Amasai kadoroseka muthia; kuani aidzala dzi nzima; kula uendavo-ndeo; kula ukimbiravo ndeo; muthia unda-u-dorosa dze o? basi hunawania rokho tu ku kimbira.
**Dosha, Tosha,** *v.n.* *See* Samu. To suffice, to make enough. Der., Madoro.
**Dosa,** *v.a.* *See* Doka.
**Doti,** *n.* (ya, za), a measure of eight mikono, cubits = four yards.
**Dovola,** *v.a.*, to uncharm, to undo a charm, to spoil a charm. Ku dovola kiravo, To undo a curse or imprecation. Munahenda luhusa muno; na huhendeni haraka, hulonde gnonsi, hudovole kiravo, vivi, ki mohomoho; muino munahenda luhusa hata kiguire mutu, ndo mulondafio? Ku dovola marinda (?). *See* Pepo; Ndaro.
  **Dovoka,** *v.n.*, to get uncharmed.
**Dovola** (Kir.). *See* Davula.
**Dovoreka** (= Unadovoreka?).
**Du, Tu,** *adv.* *See* Fa. Only, merely, indeed. The word is sometimes repeated three times, and then the accent is put on the middle one, as Du dù du.
**Dua,** *v.n.* (= Kid hula). *See* Dahiri; Sunguluka. To follow. Yudzidua nchira iviyo? Which way has he followed? Iviyo, It where which—the *yo* being the rel. pron. to *i*. Yudzidua na nchira hi; lit. He followed with this way, He took this way.
  **Duadua,** *v. reit.* *See* Kimbirika. To keep following. Mvula iki duadua, The rain keeps following, keeps pace with the wants of the ground or crops.
  **Duana,** *v. reit.*, to follow with, to accompany.
  **Duika,** *v.n.*, to admit of following. Prov., Nchira mpiri ka zi duika, saremesa fisi.
  **Duira,** *v. rel.*
  **Duiwa,** *v.p.*, to be followed. Der., Luduo.
**Dubani,** *adv.*, sometimes repeated, rarely, seldom. Ku onekana dubani, To be rarely seen or met with. In the following instance the word may be considered as an adj. or a noun: Kuako kunaoneka mboga, nidze, nihunde? Are vegetables to be seen with thee in thy fields or plantation, that I may come and pluck? Resp., Zari ko, ela zikasira; ela ndzo, ukalole m'egnie; ni tupani.
**Dubari,** *n.* (= Bahadi).
**Dubu, Tubu** (Kij.), *v.n.* *See* Muigni. To be sorry, to repent.
**Dubuluka,** *v.n.*, to get subdued, to become submissive. Fig., to be in a reduced or feeble state; said of the blood. Miladzoye idzidubuluka, idzikala madzimadzi, His blood has been reduced, it has become watery. This is said to be the cause of ku dzadzuka.
  **Dubulusa,** *v.c.*, to subdue, to cause to submit by chastisement. Der., Kidubulu.
**Dude,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a thing, an instrument. Anything of which the name is not known or remembered; something remarkably large. Also used of very stout people, though partly in jest. Magn. of Mudude, of which the dims. are Kadude and Kidude. Dude ra ku didikira mawe, A thing for carrying stones; *i.e.* a cart. This is the circumscription the natives used for the cart, first introduced by the missionaries.

## [PDF Page 61 — Dictionary Page 48 (Dud — Duk)]

**Dudu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) an insect when large.
(2) The name of a disease. Magn. of Mududu. Dim., Kadudu; Kidudu.
**Duduka,** *v.n.*, to come forth by way of escape, as grass from the fire, to break out as an eruption on the skin. Niasi siduduka, ka zi viere; or, Ka zi ka via, zidzihenda duduka. Uvere udzi-ni-duduka muiri osi; or, Muiri osi udzi-duduka uvere.
**Dudula,** *v.a.*, (1) to bore, to work a thing through by turning it about, as in putting a stick into the shell of a cocoa-nut for a handle.
(2) (Kid.) (= Ku dodola in Kir.), to work one's self through, to penetrate into a jungle. Tundu nidzivekedza kare, be vano nadudula ku buma muvini.
  **Dudulika** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Ku vegnieka), to be penetrable. Vatu hiva vadzalangua, vanadudulika. Hiva vana viougua (or, vana miya), ka va dudulika.
**Duduma** (Kid.), *v.n.*, to be in a state of agitation; to thunder. In Kig., the word is *v.a.*, and means to beat violently, thoroughly. Mvula inaduduma konda hiyi; lit. The rain is in commotion on this side; *i.e.* It thunders on this side or in this direction. Moyo una ni duduma, in Kir., Moyo una-ni hutahuta; lit. The heart agitates me (= I am agitated).
  **Dudumiza,** (1) *v.n.* (= Ku duduma). *See* Hindirika; Hindirisa. Only used of thunder. Mvula inadudumiza.
  (2) *v.a.*, to produce a bubbling noise as in dipping a jar into water for filling. *See* Zididi. Ku dudumiza puko, To cause a bubbling noise as to or with the water-jar.
  **Dudumuka,** *v.n.* (= Didimaka).
  **Dudumusa.**
  **Dudurira** (Kid.), *v.d.* (in Kir., Ku dundumira and Ku dundurira), to penetrate to, for. Nidzi-m-dudurira, hata dzi-m-fikira ariko (*sc.* Niama).
  **Dudusa,** *v.c.*, to make or to let come forth by way of escape. Said of fire with regard to patches of grass which remain unburnt. Der., Madudusi.
**Dudumui,** *n.* *See* Kifudu.
**Dudusa.** *See* Dudula.
**Dueda,** *v.n.* *See* Sia. To struggle, as one dying. Kadzatoka rokho, yuchari dueda.
**Dueka** (Kij. ?). *See* Zazuka.
**Duena,** *v.n.* *See* Kadzanda. To drop, to drip. The word is also pronounced Ku huegnia and Ku huena.
  **Duenaduena,** *v. reit.*, to keep dripping, to trickle.
  **Duenekesa,** *v.c.*, to let drip.
  **Duenekesera,** *v.d.*, to let drip to, on, upon. Yudzi ni duenekesera miladzo, He has dropped blood on me. Yudzi ni duenekesera madzi, gana-ni zisimira.
  **Duenera,** *v.d.*, to drop upon, to infuse, to instil.
**Duene,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a drop. Maduene ga mfula, Drops of rain.
**Dugnagna,** *v.n.*, to swing violently in a swing, as children. Ku teza viomu ndo ku dugnagna.
  **Dugnagnira,** *v. rel.*, to swing with. Lufundo lua ku dugnagnira.
**Duika,** *v.n.* *See* Dua. To admit of following.
**Duika,** *v.n.* *See* Ambika.
  **Duikaduika,** *v. reit.* *See* Nemuka; Dzadzarika.
**Duira.** *See* Dua.
**Dukaduka.** *See* Dula.
  **Dukana,** etc. *See* Dula.
**Duka,** *v.n.*, to rise, to grow up from something small and apparently hopeless; to come out, to turn out as something else, to get changed into something else. Nidzi-

## [PDF Page 62 — Dictionary Page 49 (Duk — Duk)]

  busa dzedze ya moho, kari kadide, nidzi-i-busa hata idzi duka, idziguira. Muana hiyu warichua ni mameye mudzanga, kadzatoka tofu-mameye akifua; basi nidzi-m-rengarenga mimi, hata yudziduka, This child was left by his mother a tender infant, the navel-string not having come off when his mother died; well, I cherished him myself until he grew up. Yudziduka muhi (= Yudzigaluka, Yudzikala muhi), He has come out a tree (= He got changed; he became a tree; *i.e.* according to witchcraft).
  **Dusa,** or **Duza,** *v.c.*, to cause to rise out of or come forth; to originate, to produce, to cause; to invent, to devise; to give out, by way of false accusation. Ku duza uira, To originate a song. Ku duza kondo, To originate or cause strife. Ku duza nchira, To originate a path; To open up a new road. Ku-dzi-duza kuro, To produce one's self as a dog; *i.e.* to change one's self into a dog.
  **Dusana, Duzana,** *v. reit.*, to give out one another, accuse one another falsely.
  **Dusira, Duzira,** *v.d.*, to originate, to invent *to*, *against*. Generally used of calumny.
  **Dusirana,** *v. reit.*, to invent stories one against another = to slander, to calumniate.
**Duta,** *v.a.* *See* Dzuva. To throw one out, to overcome in a game called Ku dzuva gnombe. Der., Tusi.
**Dukaduka, Tukatuka,** *n.* (= Bukuabukua in Kid.), a clamour, a tumult, fuss.
**Dukana, Tukana,** *v. reit.* *See* Kidamfira. To break with, to be separated from, to be out of anything, to be freed from, to get rid of. In Kig. the word means, to despise, which in Kir. is Ku hukana. Atu hio kadukana na nafaka kabisa, ni akurima sana.
**Dukanika,** *v.n.*, to shake. Nidziona makue gakidukanika, ni niama wani? ni tima hebudze? Resp., Ah be ni tima, ndiye adukanisaye makue.
  **Dukanisa,** *v.a.*, to shake, to wag the tail. Ku dukanisa kidzoa, To shake the head. Nidzigomba naye, yudzidukanisa kidzoa, yudzikahala. Baba yudzidzukirua, nidzi-mu-ona akidukauisa kidzoa, be nikahenda vifio, yunadza ni piga, The father is angry—I saw him shaking the head; so if I do it notwithstanding, he will come to beat me. Ku dukanisa masia, To shake milk. This use of the word is rare. *See* Thingiria. Ku dukanisa muchira, To wag the tail. Ku dukanisa muhi miembe, To shake a tree, as a mango tree.
  **Dukanisira,** *v.d.* *See* Manina. To shake to, upon.
**Dukia** (Kij.), *v.d.* *See* Muisho; Pingu. To break off to. Only used in the sense of to end in. Maneno gano gandadukia dze? Gana ngufu; hudzaguleni afiere, kahuangamikua ni neno.
**Duku,** *n.* *See* Aka. A shake, as in the grass, referring to light objects. Trop., turbulent behaviour; anything repulsive or disagreeable. Kitu kinadukusa niasini—duku, duku, Something keeps shaking in the grass—shake, shake. Mutu hiye yuna duku, yunadukudika, ni gara tu mabishi ahendago. Yuna dzina duku (= yuna dzina daifu), risiro ku hamira moyoni. *See* Toga (Kij.). Yuna dzina rani, ni duku vivi.
  **Dukudika,** *v.n.* Atu hio anadukudika (= anasumba, anahenda ubishi).
  **Dukuduku,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).

## [PDF Page 63 — Dictionary Page 50 (Duk — Dum)]

  **Dukuma,** *v.a.*, to push, to give a push. Obs. The word now in use is Ku sukuma. Yudzi ni dukuma, aka-ni-dieka, He gave me a push and threw me down.
  **Dukumira,** *v.d.* *See* Hokoha. To push one's self forward to others; *i.e.* to be arrogant, haughty. Always construed with the reflexive Dzi. Ela ka dzi dukumira 'ye? Be yureadze fio? yu dzi dukumira.
  **Dukusa,** *v.a.* *See* Fiurira; Zira. To shake. Especially used of light objects, or of what is easily moved. In Kid. the word is also *v.n.* Lola! niasi zinadukusua; ni kitu chani kidukusacho niasi? Der., Kidukusa; Madulusi; Muduku; Mudukuso; Mudula.
**Dula,** *v.a.* (Dura in Kns., and Dua in Kij., Hula), (1) to castrate.
(2) To break. Only used with respect to water when playing in it; but in Kig. the word means, to break, generally (= Ku funsa in Kir.).
(3) To single out, to choose for dancing. This use of the word has been borrowed from the Kig.; in Kir. proper they say, Ku hala. Ku dula madzi-ku piga kifudu-madzi gakahenda musindo, dibudibu, or, gubugubu. Anadula ahoho hio. Mulume ni ku dulua ni muche uirani.
**Dulama, Duluka.** *See* Duka.
**Dulama,** *v.n.* (= Ku badama), to alight, as a bird. Both these words are, however, rarely used, the common expression being Ku bua muhini.
**Duluka** (Kid.), *v.n.*, to break through, to rush out. Ku duluka na tulu. Yudziduluka niumbani, yudzikimbira.
  **Dulukiza.** Der., Tulu.
**Dulisa** (Kij.), *v.a.* (in Kir. proper, Ku hurisa). *See* Maenensi; Mbulukambuluka. To quiet, to calm; to steady, to compose.
**Dumaini** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to trust.
  **Dumania,** *v.a.*, to trust in; to steady, to fix the mind. Na-m-dumania muse nangu, akikala na kitu iye, basi-ninga nirie na cho mimi. Yudzigula kitu kua ku dumania moyowe, kana fingi moyoni muakue, He bought something by fixing his mind, *i.e.* confidently; He has no hesitation in his mind.
  **Dumani,** *n.* (= Mudumani), a surety, one engaged to pay the debt of another.
**Dumbaku, Tumbaku,** *n.* (ya and ra), tobacco.
**Dumbele, Tumbele,** *adj.*, scattered about in plenty. Yuna muhama mungi, vivinda vi dumbele (= vi ye and vi dele).
**Dumbi** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), an egg.
**Dumbu,** *n.* (ra), a kind of beer, made of the flour of muhama, Caffre-corn, or of the small seeds called maere and wimbi, which are put into cold water, and on the next day mixed with malt, or merely with what they called chaje, and covered over, when, on the third day, it is ready for use. The Kiriamas, for want of toddy, use it still; but the Rabais, since the increase of cocoa-nut trees, have discontinued it.
**Dumbui,** *n.* *See* Gonda. The name of a dance peculiar to the young. Adana ndio afuinao dumbui.
**Dumbula,** *v.a.* (= in Kij., Ku dumbua), to open wide the eyes, as in staring. Ku dumbula midzidzo (= Ku kodola midzidzo), To stare. Midzidzo is the magn. form of Dzidzo, the eye, generally used in language of disapprobation and contempt, as also in ridicule.
**Dumburia** (Kid.), *v.a.*, to finish

## [PDF Page 64 — Dictionary Page 51 (Dum — Dun)]

  killing, a man or animal, left wounded by another.
**Dumburira,** *v.d.* (= in Kij., Ku dumbulia), to open wide the eyes, in staring at one. Yudzi ni dumburira midzidzo (= in Kir. proper, Yudzi ni godorera midzidzo), He stared at me.
**Dume,** *adj.* *See* Bori. Male.
**Dumia,** *v.a.* and *n.*, to use, to make use of, to finish by using Germ. Verbrauchen, to be used up, to have served out.
**Dumuka,** *v.n.*, to become less; to die suddenly. Only used of animals; of men, Ku katika is used. Madzi, hangu dzana, gadzidumuka, gadzikala matembe.
  **Dumula,** *v.a.* (= Ku dimula in Kid.), to diminish.
  **Dumurira.**
**Dumu** (Kij.), *v.n.*, (K.) to continue.
**Duna,** *v.a.* *See* Muluchiluchi. To sever, to take off, as flesh from a skin or a bone. Ku duna tingo. Tingo mudzi-i-richa na niama, ni-pani kifiu, nidune. Ku duna niama (= Ku-i-dania na misosa).
**Dunda,** *n.* (ra), the name of a dance, which is now forsaken. Uira wa dunda.
**Dunda,** *v.a.*, to bruise. Na-dzi-dunda na kinu.
  **Dundika.**
  **Dundisa,** *v.a.*, to press, to urge.
  **Dundua** (Kig.).
  **Dundumira,** *v.n.* *See* Mfueresi. Ku dundumira dzakani.
  **Dundurira.**
**Dune, Tune,** *adj.*, red. This radical form of the word is used when relating to a noun of the ra class; pl. Madune. Relating to other classes of nouns, it receives their preformatives, as, Mudune (pl. A- and Mi-); Kidune (pl. Vi-); but relating to the ya class, it is changed into Tune, and remains the same in sing. and pl. *See* Tune.
**Dunga,** *v.a.* *See* Lingila. To put to, to put on by winding round. The word was formerly used of winding brass wire round the arms and legs, Ku dunga madzango, or, mikodo; in which sense it has been superseded by the Kig. Ku alila. In Kij. it means, to string, as beads, which in Kir. is Ku hunga. The idea of the word is that of adding one thing to another of the same kind. *See* Ku hunga.
**Dunsa, Tunza,** *v.a.*, to watch, to take heed to, to attend to, from the idea of being near, close to anything (?).
**Dunga, Tunga,** (1) *v.a.* *See* Kidosi; Kigota. To prick, to pierce, to stab, to thrust into.
(2) *v.n.*, to break forth, to come forth (Hervorstechen in Germ.). Muiya udzi-ni-dunga, A thorn has pricked me. Nidziona nioka, nika-m-dunga na mufiu, I saw a snake, and I pierced it with a sword, or merely, nika-m-dunga mufiu, I thrust the sword into it. Ku dunga dzana (= Ku piga dzana), To stab, to rip open. Mutu wa ku dungaa milomo, A human being with a pierced or perforated upper lip, as the Wahiao females. Dzua rinadunga, The sun is coming forth, when beginning to rise. Madzere ganadunga, The Indian corn is springing up. Niere zinadunga, The hair begins to grow after being shaved. Mahombo ganadunga, The breasts begin to form.
  **Dungadunga, Tungatunga,** *v. reit.*, to keep pricking; said of pain.
  **Dungira,** *v.d.*, to pierce to, for, with.
  **Dungula** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku doniola in Kir.), to slightly scarify the skin; lit. to prick open.
**Dungu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a basket platted from a branch of the

*Footer: 51*

## [PDF Page 65 — Dictionary Page 52 (Dun — Dza)]

  cocoa-nut tree, generally made just for the occasion.
**Dungulua,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of thick hairy worm, with bright coloured spots. It is particularly fond of the leaves of the small trees called muniala and mudzekedze, which it eats off in no time.
**Dunsa.** *See* Dunga.
**Dunza** (?).
**Dura, Thura, Rura,** *v.n.*, to be able.
  **Duria,** *v.a.*, to test, to put to the test, especially as to one's courage.
  **Durika,** *v.n.*, to be weary, to be tired. Nidzirima hata nidzidurika. Nidzika = dzoka.
  **Durisa,** *v.c.*, to weary, to tire. Yudzi-ni-durisa na maneno. Nidzi-m-piga hata nidzi-m-dùrisa. Yudzi-hu-durisa mutu hiye, machero shenda rungani kuakue kahiri.
  **Durisana,** *v. reit.*, to tire one another.
**Duraha** (Kij.), *n.* and *adv.*, rest, quietness, peace; quietly, peaceably, orderly. Kana duraha kahiri.
**Durasi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the fruit of a creeping plant called mudurasi.
**Duru, Thuru** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to matter, to be of consequence. Ka vi duru, It matters not; It is of no consequence. The Vi is the pl. of Ki; lit. Not they (the things) matter; but it stands here in a general sense like the English "it."
**Duruka,** *v.n.* *See* Kihako. To come out. Muiya uduruka. Pass., Ku durukua.
**Duruma,** *v.n.* (= Ku koma), to go to, to go no further, to go to and return from, to limit one's going to a given place. The going lies in Duru, and the limiting in -ma. The word is not uniform, as the accent is sometimes also put on the second or middle syllable, or rather both the first and the second seem accented equally, as, Dùrùma. *It is very doubtful if a native ever pronounces a word with the accent on the antepenultimate. Arabs and Europeans often do.*—[ED.] Niama yudzikudza, kadzafika uimoni aka-ni-duruma, akauya niuma. Nidzienenda, nikakuenda duruma hivara, nalola nchira seyo, basi nikauya, nikakudza guira nchera bomu.
  **Durura,** *v.a.* *See* Pungo; Suhira. To take out, to draw forth, to pull out. Ku durura muiya. Ku durura muhogo, To pull up cassava, when comparatively young or when the ground is soft after rain.
**Duruma,** *v.n.* *See* Dura.
**Duruma,** *n.*, the name of a territory to the west of Mombas, stretching far into the wilderness to within a day's journey of the mountain Kilibasi. The Arabs generally pronounce *Dúruma*, but the natives always *Durúma*. The people are Aduruma (sing. Mu-) (in Kis., Wa-, sing. M-), and constitute one of the tribes of the Anika (Kij. Wanika).
**Durume,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a large ram. Magn. of Turume. Durume ra gnonzi; ka ri kula kaviri. Dim., Kadurume; Kidurume.
**Duta.**
**Duza.** *See* Duka.
  **Duzana.** *See* Duka.
  **Duzira.** *See* Duka.
  **Duzirana.** *See* Duka.

**Dz** is a compound sound, and should be represented by two letters. The sound does not occur in Kisuahili.—[ED.]
**Dza,** *conj.* (Hudza = Hudzi), as. Ku rua dza vio. Ka-dza-pata.

## [PDF Page 66 — Dictionary Page 53 (Dza — Dza)]

**Dza.** *See* Lurauka; Hangu. Iki dza kasa ku dza.
**Dza,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Dzafue; Lukuni. Point, tip; (K.) top. Kuadza ni luavi, lukuni hilu? Kuona we? kuamba kuno ni kua kolo, kuno ni dza, or, kuno ni dza-ni. Maneno higa ka-ga-na dza. Lomba ludzi funsika dza.
**Dza,** *v. enclit.* (Ku dza). *See* Dukanisa; Richisa; Gurira; Huari; Shuhuli; Hungakudza; Hungari; Huakudza. To come. Ahi! dzina ridza, rikiuya! Ei, the name comes, returning, or, It comes and goes. Rinadza, etc.
  **Dzira,** *v. rel.* *See* Kozi; Dzi; Mbotherua. To come to, to come upon; befall, happen. Rero, mutu muche wa Kisiwani yudzi-hu-ku-dzira.
  **Dzirira.**
  **Dzirirana,** *v.*, to come to one another, to meet.
  **Dziririka,** *v.n.*
  **Dzirirua,** *v.p.* Ku dzirirua ni atu. Nidzikudzirirua ni utu moyoni. Ku sema utu wa mbere.
  **Dzirua.** Nidziamba niuke, ela nidzikudzirua ni mugeni. Nidzikudzirua ni ageni, nalonda uchi, nika-a-dzumbuse.
  **Dziwa.** Nidzikudziwa ni utu, or, Nidzidziwa ni utu.
**Dzadza,** *n. coll.* (ra). *See* Kidunganguo. The name of a species of weed. Munda ukimera p'ekue ya dzadza, na fuka na muambaniama, basi una baraka.
**Dzadza,** *n.* Ku rima dzadza kandakanda ya mudzi. Hudzilarikirua ku rima dzadza (= Kid., Adzikuenda diekua dzadza; Kir., Adzikuenda arikua, or, hinua).
**Dzadza,** *v.a.* Ku dzadza wari mdzusini; or, Ku honge muzusini.
  **Dzadzania** (Kig.) (= Kudzolodzolo ku ondoka in Kij.).
  **Dzadzarika** (= Kupiga mikindui, nguo ika duika). *See* Kidosi. Yunadzadzarika, yunaduikaduika, muiriwe ni muolofu.
  **Dzadzarisa,** *v.c.* Ku-m-dzadzarisa muhoho.
  **Dzadzira,** *v.d.* Mu-dzadzire muana wari, u-mu-ve.
  **Dzadzuka,** *v.n.* *See* Dubuluka; Mfignio. Gnania wari mukongo, muiriwe udzidzadzuka, miladzo idzidueka. Nguo idzifulua, idzidzuka-idzidzadzuka nieruve dze.
  **Dzadzura** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku pokoa in Kij.). *See* Sazura in Kns.
  **Dzadzurika.**
**Dzadzabiri,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) a multiplicity of uses.
(2) Industry. Munazi unadzadzabiri ningi, A cocoa-nut tree has many uses. Gnania yuna dzadzabiri yudzipata vitu vingi kua uchiwe, ela muino muagemera kanoani tu, Gnania is industrious.
**Dzadzaza,** *n.* Mbaga za dzadzadza, za murenge.
**Dzadziga,** *v.n.*, to play.
  **Dzadzigira,** *v. rel.* *See* Nangananga. (K.) deride. Ahoho anakutusa kififiro ku dzadzigira.
**Dzadzu,** *n.* *See* Chaje; Nknadu. Nidzibuma muniu, udzikala dzadzu. Nidzibuma kabu mbogani, sikala dzadzu. Wishua hiu u-dzadzu. Kanoa rangu ridzadzu kua ukuaju. Uchi udzikala ufu hata udzikala dzadzu. Ukuaju u-dzadzu. Wari hiu u-dzadzu. Wishua udzikala dzadzu. Uchi hiu ni dzadzu (= Uchi hiu u-dzadzu). Ukuaju ndo urio na dzadzu.
**Dzafu,** *n.*, cheek. Ku piga dzafu, To strike on the cheek.
**Dzafue,** *n.* (ra). *See* Ganjaganja; Kunde. Ku hunda dzafue ra mukunde.
