## [PDF Page 67 — Dictionary Page 54 (Dza — Dza)]

**Dzafulo,** or **Dzavuka,** *n.* (ya, pl. Ma-), the placenta. Nda-ku-guira dzafulo dze. Yudzi-m-guira dzafulo yudzi-m-guira mumu mua dzafulo, maganda ya mimba (in Kij. = ifu ra gnombe, etc.). Yumfuna, yuna ifu bomu.
**Dzaga,** *n.*, (1) (za). Pl. of Ludzaga.
(2) (ya, za), one of the sticks or boughs of cocoa-nut trees of which the uriri is composed. Makumbi gano n'enda-ya-henda dzaga za uriri.
**Dzaga,** *v.n.* *See* Kins., Zagana; Zagaika. To be rude, to be rudely familiar. Gnania yudzidzaga muno vio; dzusi na-mu-ambira: usijire na hiva, njira hi nidzi-i-sisa; ela iye na ku usa dzansu, akajira na vava, be kadzidzaga muno hiyu? Yudzidzaga muno naye, He has become rudely familiar with him. Mutu kadzidzaga yuyu (= Mutu kadzignieta yuyu)?
  **Dzagadzaga,** *v. reit.* Sa yudzidzagadzaga mundani, kuria kunde. Vatu hiva adzi-va-dzagadzaga, vana vidzagodzago.
  **Dzagamira** (= Ku fuino msego = Ku-m-piga pambaja in Kij.; Kuafumira), (K.) to embrace.
  **Dzagula,** *v.a.*, to pick out, to choose, to select. Ku dzagula dzaha muirini, To catch fleas on one's body. Ku dzagula maneno moyoni, To consider.
  **Dzagurika,** *v.n.*, to admit of being picked out, etc.; to be eligible. Tembe ya maere na ya wimbi ka-i-dzagurika, idzagurikayo ni tembe ya madzere na ya muhama.
  **Dzagurira,** *v.d.*, to select to, for. M-dzagurire madzere ganagnanikago, u-mu-ve, akaoche, Select for him her cobs which are smooth, not yet dry; give them to her, that she may roast them.
  **Dzaguza,** *v.c.*, to make choose.
**Dzagadza,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kikombe. The leaves of a cob of Indian corn, when taken off. When on, they are called makanda. Ku vavula madzagadza. Ku vavula madzere.
**Dzagayadzagaya** (Kid.), *adj.*, the sound caused by pounding. Madzere ganarira dzagayadzagaya.
**Dzago,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Luala. Dzago ya luala.
**Dzaha,** *n.*, a flea (?). Yudzibuma dzahani.
**Dzahasi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (Kij., Jahazi), a vessel, a ship. Prov., Dzahasi ni menga, ela kula mutu yuua kidumbache mumo, be fugula kivindacho, ela usifugule cha muyao.
**Dzahu,** *n.* (wa, hiya, pl. *id.* (a), hia), the name of a large serpent, described by natives as from two to three times the length of a bow. Muana dzahu, A young dzahu. Dzahu ni ku rira dza mbuzi. Mathuniage ni muhaso wa tambasi.
**Dzaira,** *v.a.* (= Ku dondola; Ku valadza). *See* Mumo. To glean. Ku dzaira madzere luguani. N'enda nikadzaire lugua.
  **Dzairadzaira,** *v. reit.* N'enda kuangu luguani, nikadzairedzaire madzere, nipate kilariro, nidze, nivonde.
  **Dzairana,** *v. reit.* Atu ari adzifumukana kua viha, be vio anadzairana.
**Dzaje,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Dzajidzaji,** *adv.*, in a dispersed manner. Atu adzikudza dzajidzaji, kaka rindana. Ku kimbira dzajidzaji. Atu anaaka niumba dzajidzaji, kakaaka vamenga.
**Dzaka** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Kuta in Kir.).
  **Dzakadza.**
**Dzaka,** *n.*, a forest. Dim., Kadzaka.
  **Dzakadzaka,** *n.* *See* Fufuma. Muana wa dzakadzaka; lit. A child of the jungle, or forest, An illegitimate child.
**Dzakadza,** *v.a.* Nari nikafidza uchi, adzi-u-dzakadza hata adzi-u-ona.

## [PDF Page 68 — Dictionary Page 55 (Dza — Dza)]

  **Dzakadzika,** *v.n.* *See* Kunsui. Niasi zidzakadzika, ukadieka moho, basi dzansala in'enda kure.
**Dzakadzapania,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a snake. Ni nioka amisaye panis muno.
**Dzakala,** *v.n.* (= Sukuruka in Kins., as used of the soil). *See* Zumbakala. Niungu za kijomfu ka-zi-dzakala, ela za kidigo ndo sikalazo muno. Niungu za kidigo zinadzakala, zina ulongo udzo. Munda wangu udzidzakala, udzihenda p'ekue ningi, ni wa kare. Mufiere hiyu yudzidzakala, yudzeria-dzi, yudzihenda masiku mangi.
**Dzakapala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a snake.
**Dzakaza,** *v.a.* Wahala nguo yangu ak'enda-i-fuala hata yudzi-i-dzakaza; basi angue: yuna-ni-rehera; ela sinda-i-hala; kadzi-i-dzakaza kare vio? Udzi-ki-dzakaza kidodi changu, si-vio cho-vio kala. Gnania yudzakasa mundawe.
**Dzaku** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), heads of Guinea-corn when beaten out. Dzaku ra muhama (= Madoa ya mtama in Kij.; Zache in Kins.; in Kir., Masuche gadzagokutua kure).
**Dzakudza,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Bidza), a handful, a small bundle. Only used of things of some length. Dzakudza ra maonsa, ra pani, ra gnongo.
**Dzakula** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku yeya in Kir.), to seek.
**Dzala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Ta in Kij.), the act of laying an egg. Dzala rinagnala.
**Dzala,** *n.* (= Dzalani?).
**Dzaladzala,** *v.n.* Muana akipigua tuaha, basi yunadzaladzala nikusa, hurira vamenga kudinadina kusumba.
**Dzalarira,** *v.n.*, to spread, as news. Khabari zidzidzalarira dzi yosi.
**Dzalula** (Kidigo), *v.a.* (= Dzagula in Kir.), to choose, to select.
**Dzalafu,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). *See* Dadamusa. A black ant.
**Dzalagumba,** *n.* *See* Chala. (K.) a digit.
**Dzalakasa,** *v.a.* and *n.* (= Sororeka, to scrabble). *See* Fira. To make a small, frequent noise. Pania hiye yunadzalakasa. Der., Mudzalakaso.
**Dzalakushe,** *n.* (ra). *See* Mudzungu. The name of a kind of vegetable. Ni mboga.
**Dzalalua** (Kid.), *n.*
**Dzalankua,** *adj.* *See* Dudulika; Dzangula. Dzaka hiro ri-dzalankua; ka-rina mihi ya ga ga ga; kamuna ndodo ndodo. Muhama wangu ka-u-merera, wa-u-laga madzina, ukimera kurekure; be udziingira muruo ndani, ni dzalankua.
**Dzalula.** *See* Dzaladzala.
**Dzama,** *n.* (za), dirt, filth. Manai gana dzama muno. Dzama hizi.
**Dzama,** *v.n.* *See* Kigniesi. To emigrate.
  **Dzamia,** *v.a.* Nikadzama, ela sidzangue ku dzamia vitu nikamala, na ahoho alala kuko ku larira vitu, niumba. Nikadzamia ahoho, ela mino nilala kuko.
  **Dzamira,** *v. rel.* Gnania wala hiko a-ko-kala, akidzama, aki-ni-dzamira mimi; be hu jirani vavo vamenga.
  **Dzamuka,** *v.n.* *See* Loamia.
  **Dzamukadzamuka,** *v. reit.*, to be scattered about. Mifusi idzidzamukadzamuka.
  **Dzamukana,** *v. reit.*, (K.) to disband, to disperse. Nidzidzuva mufui, adzidzamukama. Nidzidzimba puku, hata adzidzamukana, I have dug after field-rats, and they have dispersed.
**Dzamula,** *v.a.* (= Ku fumula; Fomola).

## [PDF Page 69 — Dictionary Page 56 (Dza — Dza)]

  Ku dzamula niasi za niumba. Ku dzamula mifusi.
**Dzamba** (for **Nidziamba**), *v.* (*1st pers. sing.* of Ku amba), I have said. Nidzizama kolo ra muhi ku-dzi-fidza mvula, dz'amba: ni chache, inajira; hata nikiona ni ningi, basi nikaenenda nayo.
**Dzamba,** *v.a.*
  **Dzambula,** *v.a.*, to trim, to strip. Ku dzambula mboga, To strip vegetables. Ku dzambula lukue, To pick a rope or string, cutting off the endings.
  **Dzamburira,** *v.d.*
  **Dzambuza,** *v.a.* *See* Serema. To edge, to drive to an edge; (K.) enucleate. Navirika kifiu changu kua musana, kidzambuzue.
  **Dzambuzira,** *v.d.*
  **Dzambuzua,** *v.p.* Vitu vinda dzambuzua, mvula ikidza.
**Dzambala,** *n.* Madzere gadziifua dzambala; or, Gadzihenda dzambala (= Ganaansa ku gauka maganda). This is said in contradistinction to Gadziifua ga ku veta.
**Dzambo,** *n.* Pl. of Ludzambo. Adzi-dzi-funga dzambo ache.
**Dzambo,** *n.* (ra) (= Thara). *See* Fidzania; Shuku. A matter, an affair, concern; (K.) case, condition.
**Dzamudzamu,** *adv.*, without order, dispersedly. Vitu hivi mudzi-vi-ika dzamudzamu, ku-sa-vi-ika to nini?
**Dzamundi,** *n.* (ra, pl. ) (= Bidza). Dim., Kidzamundi.
**Dzana, Ni dzana,** *adv.* *See* Luiko. Yesterday. Dzana usiku, Yesterday night. Hangu dzana, Since yesterday. Muaka wa dzana, Last year.
**Dzana,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) Dzana ra isu. Isu hiri rina madzana mane hebu madzano.
(2) A stab. Ku piga dzana, To rip open; to stab. Ku-dzi-piga dzana, To stab one's self. Yupigua dzana ela kafuere, or, kakafua. Yupigua dzana ra kigulu.
**Dzana,** *n.* (ra). *See* Bumbala. A large child. Magn. of Muana.
**Dzana,** *v.a.*, to split, to cleave. Ku dzana milala, To split palm leaves.
  **Dzania** (= Ku ika in Kig.). Niama zina dzanira.
  **Dzanira,** *v. rel.* Yudzi-ni-dzanira milala. Kifiu cha ku dzanira milala.
  **Dzaniuka,** *v.n.* (= Ku ahuka).
  **Dzaniula,** *v.a.* (= Ku futa, when used of leaves). *See* Gaula; Kulula. To tear off, to strip off or asunder. Ku dzaniula lukano. Ku dzaniula niere, To disentangle the hair, to dishevel.
  **Dzaniurika,** *v.n.* Lukuni hilu ludziremesa, ka-lu-dzaniurika.
  **Dzaniurira,** *v.d.*
**Dzanche, Dzanje,** *n.* (1) (ya, za), (*a*) a place cleared of wood for cultivating the soil, in contradistinction to muhema. (*b*) The wood thus cut down. Ku dzoma dzanje.
(2) (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). *See* Kiriangoe. The name of a species of field-rat. Prov., Dzanje ukifua na murira udzefua (= Ukikala ku-vo, na rako ka-ri-vo). Una mulomo mure, unga wa dzanje, You have a long lip, it resembles that of dzanje, said in ridicule. Mulomowe wa dzulu ni mure, ukadzupa wa dzini.
**Dzanga,** *adj.* (pl. Madzanga), (1) (rel. to the ra class), tender, young, fresh. Renge hiri rijari dzanga, ka-ri-dza-komala to.
(2) (rel to the ya and za class). *See* Venurika; Fopala. Niama dzanga. Mbalazi dzanga. Niere dzanga, Young

## [PDF Page 70 — Dictionary Page 57 (Dza — Dza)]

  or fresh hair, ziansazo ku mera, kua mutu ayeniolua luvala. Niasi zidzibula dzanga, or, zidzimera dzanga.
**Dzanga,** *v.a.* (= Kij., Shanga), to cleave, to split. Trop., used of pain. Ku dzanga kuni, To cleave firewood. Misosa yangu inanidzanga. Muiri osi una-ni-dzanga.
  **Dzangika,** *v.n.* Lukuni ludzidzangika to hilu.
  **Dzangira,** *v. rel.* Ku-mu-dzangira mutu kuni.
  **Dzangula,** *v.a.* Gnania yudema dzaka, yudzi-ri-dzangula ku henda munda. Dzaka rikademua mihi, rikadzangulua, rikala dzalankua.
**Dzanga,** *v.a.* (Kij., Danga), to take up carefully; *e.g.* water from a hole, so as not to make it muddy. Gnania na gnania adzidzanga vitu ku-m-kombola ndugu yao, or, muhua wao.
  **Dzangania,** *v.a.* *See* Dzongonene. To put or bring together, to mix. Alonda ku-hu-dzangania uwe na mimi, huhehe.
  **Dzanganika,** *v.n.*, to be in a mixed state. Nidzi-vi-dzangania vi-dzi-dzanganika.
  **Dzanganikana,** *v.n.*, to be mixed up with. Sinda dzanganikana na utu hiu, machero undakudza u-ni-thuru.
  **Dzangira,** (1) *v. rel.* Kirenge cha ku dzangira uchi. Avu kavo, be dzansiye na-m-dzangira mimi.
  (2) *v.a.* *See* Kiganga. To welcome. Muana yuna-m-dzangira mameye, akila mundani. Neno ra ku dzangira, ra eshimu, A word of welcome, of honour.
  **Dzangirua,** *v.p.* Mutu asiekalavo, ndiye adzangirua, or, ndiye aambuaye yudzangirua ni gnania.
  **Dzangiza,** *v.a.* *See* Humira. To put together, to contribute. Hudzidzangiza fetha yehu ku gula gnombe.
  **Dzangizana.**
  **Dzangizira,** *v.d.*
**Dzansa,** or **Dzanza,** *v.a.* Ku dzanza mvula. Nidzanze mvula cho. H'endeni hukadzanse.
  **Dzansasa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Kir., Ansasa).
  **Dzansula,** *v.a.* (= Vangula). Der., Dzansi; Dzansu; Kidzansa; Kidzansu.
**Dzangakuza** (?).
**Dzangalawe,** *n.* (ya, za), a pebble, gravel. Dzangalawe ni ya muniu ni kidonche kimenga.
**Dzangasimi,** *n.* (ya, za, -yangu and -wangu, pl. -zangu and -angu), an aunt, but only a father's sister—a mother's sister being called Mayo mufiere or Mayo muhoho, mother senior or mother junior, according to her being older or younger than your mother.
**Dzange,** *n.* (= Dzanche; in Kij., Shangasi).
**Dzango,** *n.*, (1) (ra, pl. Ma-), (*a*) a basket when worn out. Dzango ni kavu i-dza-yo taruka. Dim., Kidzonga. (*b*) A term given to a particular pain in the womb. Gnania ni mukongo, yuna dzango ra ndani, She is unwell, she has pain internally.
(2) (ya), travail. Yuna dzango ya mimba.
**Dzango,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* pl. Madzango. Wire, of brass or copper, of a given length. Dzango ra pima-ni; ra pima tahu, etc. Na-ku-va dzango ra pima mbiri na kisiku. Kaha za madzango. Kisiku cha dzango, A piece of wire, but not Kidzango.
**Dzangodzango,** *n.* (= Dzango; in Kins., Visuani). Reha ro dzangodzango ra kavu, nibumire mifusi.
**Dzangukeni.**
**Dzaniuka.** *See* Dzana.
**Dzaniula.** *See* Dzana.
**Dzano.**
**Dzano,** *n.* (ya, za).

## [PDF Page 71 — Dictionary Page 58 (Dza — Dze)]

  Mutu hiye adzayehala kitu hicho ni dzano. Dzano hira na tandaduye. Dzanoyo yahamba Unguja, ka-i-dzakudza.
**Dzansi, Dzanzi,** *n.* (ya, za), (K.) contribution. Dzansi hino ni ya gnania musiku.
**Dzansu, Zansu, Sanzu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kue. A branch of a tree, but only when cut off. Ku piga madzansu (= Ku piga luchigo). Hunakururia madzansu, hukabige cha. Dim., Kadzanzu and Kidzanzu; magn. Ridzansu.
**Dzanzala,** *n.* (Kij., Tanda). *See* Luandala; Lunialu; Guisa. (K.) plain. Moho wa dzandzala udziguira gogo.
**Dzapa** (Kidigo), *v.n.* (= Ku jira in Kir.), to pass.
**Dzapuka,** *v.n.*
  **Dzapukadzapuka.** Mutu yudzijira, ela kakakuta manina, yudzihenda dzapukadzapuka.
  **Dzapukira,** *v. rel.*, to pass from one thing to another, as in climbing, to pass from one bough to another, and from one tree to another, etc. Nidzikuera na muhi hura, nidzidzapukira, nikakuenda muhi hura mungine. Nidzisona luvande hilu lumenga hata nidzi-lu-mala, be nidzidzapukira luvande lungine. Der., Dzapiu.
**Dzapiu,** *n.* Kakuenendeka, kuna dzapiu; rindani, dzua rivunge, basi huenende. H'enendeni, for, huenendeni, dzua rindakola, kuhende dzapiu, Let us go, the sun will be hot, to make dzapiu. (Ku, the infin. particle in connection with the opt. let it make = so that it makes dzapiu.) Gniere ni ku dzanga uchi wa dzapiu ku va kambi.
**Dzaragadza,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Dzagadza).
**Dzarakasa,** *v.n.* (= Dzalakasa).
**Dzasa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (Chasa in Kij. ?), the oyster. Madzasa garigo mikokoni. Nidzichegniua ni dzasa.
**Dzasa** (Kidigo), *v.a.* (= Dangadza in Kir.). N'enda nikadzase dzonge, basi niwihe (= Kir., N'enda nika-geme lua mudzana, be nienende).
**Dzasi,** *n.*, a bottle.
**Dzavuka,** *n.* (ya, za, also ra, pl. Ma-), the temple, the upper part of the side of the head. Dzavuka ina-ni-luma. Nalumua himu madzavukani.
**Dzavukusi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Dzawe,** *n.*
**Dzaya,** *n.* *See* Bembere; Dzango. A large potsherd. Magn. of Luaya. Ku piga dzaya. *See* Kiravo.
**Dze,** *interr. pron.* *See* Henseka; Kirenge; Ludi; I-ri-o; Yu. What? how?
**Dze,** *interj.* (= Ke). *See* Enesa. Nda ku tunga za. Nda ku tunga ke. Ku dze fua; ku dze cha; ku dze dzua, etc.
**Dze,** *adv.* *See* Fusa; Era. Mueruve dze dze dze dze.
**Dzea,** *v.a.* *See* Musiro. Si-ni-dzee, ni mameye atu, zi rikaro mino. Si ni dzee unga-ni ona vivi, ni mameye atu, zi rikaro mino.
  **Dzeana,** *v. reit.* Aravai na adzukuluao, kaogovana, ni ku dzeana. Adzeanao ni ku dzuvirana ndumo.
  **Dzeka,** *v.n.* and *a.* *See* Gesagesa; Kamare; Guisua. To laugh, to laugh at, to laugh to scorn. Used also of things inanimate.
  **Dzekana,** *v. reit.*, to laugh at one another.
  **Dzekeka,** *v.n.* Utu uko usiodzekeka wa chonsue asieidima ku enenda; haya! unda-m-dzeka-dze we?
  **Dzekera,** *v. rel.* Ukiona utu ui basi ni ku dzekera kanda. Ku-m-dzekera

## [PDF Page 72 — Dictionary Page 59 (Dze — Dze)]

  mugeni, To be friendly, cheerful, to a stranger.
  **Dzekerana,** *v. reit.* Atu hio anadzekeza, ana niemi. Atu hio ni ai, kanadzekesa, ana choyo. Der., Kidzeko.
  **Dzekesa,** *v.c.*
  **Dzera** (= Chakura in Kij.). Munda hiu ni wa kare, pekue ni ningi, ukirima ka-u-dzera; ela hio, or huno, ni muvia, ukirima, unadzera.
  **Dzerera,** *v.n.*, to descend, to let go wrath. Moyo udzi-ni-dzerera, The heart has come down to me; *i.e.* I have become quiet, said after anger.
  **Dzererua,** *v.p.* *See* Mualukisua. Ku dzererua ni dzua njirani; lit. To be descended by the sun on the road; *i.e.* to be overtaken by sunset, and consequently by night, while on a journey. Note: When used of the sun, the word has the same meaning as Dzuererua. *See* Dzua.
  **Dzeresa,** *v.a.* *See* Munazi. To make quiet, to appease. Gnania ndiye adzie-ni-dzeresa moyo, Gnania it is who made me quiet—made my heart go down. Der., Udzerero.
  **Dzesha,** *v.c.* (= Dzezia).
  **Dzezia,** *v.c.* *See* Ku bua. To make laugh. Muana ka-dza-dzeka muegnie, ela uki-m-dzezia yunadzeka.
**Dze-dze-dze.**
**Dzedzefu,** *n.* Yuguirua ni dzedzefu.
**Dzedzera,** (1) *v.n.* *See* Mudada. To halt, to limp.
(2) *v.a.* (= Zozera). Ku dze dzera niungu moho.
  **Dzedzeza,** *v.a.* *See* Makira.
  **Dzedzezua,** *v.p.* Gnania wadzedzezua ku rehua kaya kua mameye.
**Dzedzo,** *n.* (ya, za). Dzedzo ni ya ku dzongera kinu hebu muansa. Dim., Kidzedzo.
**Dzefu,** *adj.*, thin, tender. Nguo hino ni dzefu. Niama hi ni dzefu.
**Dzegahera,** *n.* (ya, za), a sty, a swelling on the eye. Dzegehera ni kadzivu uzungu lukungoni muadzidzo.
**Dzeha,** *n.* Magn. of Mueha.
**Dzehui,** *n.* Maere na wimbi ni ku henda dzehui, visuche via makua vani. Maere ga dzehui, in contradistinction to Maere ga kirinsi.
**Dzeka.** *See* Dzea.
  **Dzekera.** *See* Dzea.
  **Dzekesa.** *See* Dzea.
**Dzemba** (Kik.), *v.*, to run.
**Dzemba** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Lemba in Kir.), a comb. Dzemba ra jogolo, The comb of a cock; pl. Madzemba ga majogolo.
**Dzembera,** *v.n.*, to walk about.
  **Dzembereka** (for **Zembesa**), *v.n.*, worth while. Kuako kunadzembereka ndakudza nami, ni-dzi-sare mafuha.
  **Dzemberera,** *v.d.*
  **Dzembererana,** *v. reit.* Be kahudzembererana, usena wehu ni wa mumo njira njira tu?
  **Dzembeza,** *v.a.* Ku dzembeza magulu. Ku-m-dzembeza mugeni, amanie dzi.
**Dzenga,** *v.a.*, to cut off. Ku dzenga nazi. H'endeni hukadzenge nazi, sindasisua hikara.
  **Dzengadzenga.** Iwe ri-ri-ro na dzengadzenga (= Iwe ra thatha). Wari wa dzengadzenga (= Wari wa kidzomba).
**Dzenga,** *n.* *See* Ndzaiko. Ku pigua dzenga. Dim., Gima; Ndzaiko.
**Dzenga** (Kidigo), *v.a.* (= Ku aka in Kir.), to build.
**Dzengo,** *n.* Pl. of Ludzengo.
**Dzengo,** *n.* (ra). *See* Uiji. Dzengo ra niumba. Nina dzengo naaka niumba.
**Dzera.** *See* Dzea.
  **Dzerera.** *See* Dzea.

*Footer: 59*

## [PDF Page 73 — Dictionary Page 60 (Dze — Dzi)]

  **Dzeresa.** *See* Dzea.
**Dzere,** *n.* (ra, pl. Madzere), a cob of Indian corn. Dzere ra a arisa, A cob given to a shepherd-boy. Dim., Kadzere and Kidzere; magn., Ridzere.
**Dzerere,** *n.* (ya, za), the fruit of a tree called mudzerere. It is also called madzere ga arisa. The Indian corn of herd-boys, because it is mostly eaten by them.
**Dzezia.** *See* Dzea.
  **Dzesha.** *See* Dzea.
**Dzeveka** (Kik.), *v.n.* (= Dziradzira in Kir. ?), to dance sideways.
**Dzevuka,** *v.n.* Ah-ku gnieta ari-ko-na-ko! yudzihenda muno halisi, yudzidzevuka.
**Dzevula,** *v.a.* Ukikuera na kidzoka, unadzevula. Der., Madzevuso; Dzafukusi.
**Dzi,** *adv.* (= Si), not.
**Dzi,** *part.* *See* Kasira; Ongosa; Reherera; Dudurira. Used in conjugating the verb, implying the preterite.
**Dzi,** *reflex. part.*, only. A dzi endera tu, He who goes only—for pleasure—without purpose. Na dzi endera tu-ela moyo ka u kagoloka. Baha hunda dzi kudzera nidzi (= nika).
**Dzi,** *n.*, earth, land, country, continent.
**Dzi,** *n.* Muvaga wa dzi, The boundary of a country.
**Dzia,** *n.* *See* Mageiroa. (1) Yudzi-m-guira muyawe dzia, yulonda ku-mu-ulaga.
(2) (= Umira). Midafu ya unga.
**Dziche,** *n.*, a very large woman. Magn. of Muche.
**Dzidzi,** *n.* (ra). Pl. of Ludzidzi. Ku fua dzidzini.
**Dzidzi,** *n.* Mudzi ukikala mbomu, wamba: ni dzidzi.
**Dzi dzi dzi,** *adv.* Ku enenda dzi dzi dzi, ndani ya niasi, as the mfueresi.
**Dzidzo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Madzo), the eye. Ku bumua dzidzoni. Gnania yuna dzidzo ri, akilola kitu cha mutu, kinabanangika. Dzidzo ra kisima. Kisima hicho kina dzidza, madzige ka-ga-uma. Ku fuma dzidzo, To darn. Magn., Madzidzo.
**Dzidzoa,** *n.*, a great head. Magn. of Kidzoa. Dzomfi yuna dzidzoa bomu.
**Dzifiu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma- or Mi-), a very large knife. Magn. of Kifiu.
**Dzignia,** *v.a.* Ku dzignia ndo ku saga to. Opposed to Valasa. Mutu kiye yunadzignia, ungawe u-dziki dziki dziki.
  **Dzignie.**
  **Dzigniua,** *v.p.* Wari huno ukadzigniua, ni udzigni.
**Dzihu,** *n.* *See* Fuhika. Pl. of Lusihu.
**Dziji,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*), the name of a species of small speckled bird fond of maere.
**Dzijidziji,** *adj.*, like the dziji in colour, *i.e.* speckled. Kololo yudzijidziji. Mbuzi hino i-dzijidziji.
**Dzikidza,** *v.a.* (= Ku girida; in Kins., Ku gara), to rub, to rub in. Ku dzikidza nguo ufumba hebu mafuha, To rub a cloth with perfume or oil. Ku-dzi-dzi kidza madzo, To rub one's eyes. Yudzi-m-dzikidza umiro, He rubbed, *i.e.* seized, him at the throat.
  **Dzikidzira,** *v.d.* Na-m-dzikidzira ufumba nguoye.
**Dzikidziki,** *adj.* and *adv.* (= Vevivevi; Bikibiki; Ngi-ngi-ngi; Dikidiki). *See* Didzaya. Close, closely. Kikahana hiki kidzisukua dzikidziki. Lukue hilu lu-dzikidziki, lukafuihewa to.
  **Dzikiridzikiri,** *adv.*, very closely, too closely. Himo gadziandikua dzikiridzikiri; himo ga-

*Footer: 60*

---

## [PDF Page 74 — Dictionary Page 61 (Dzi — Dzi)]

  dziandikua gagaga (kama gadzigo gandamirama). Udziniala dzikidziki, or, dzikiridzikiri, You have planted (too) closely.
**Dzikirua,** *v.* (= Dzukirua), (K.) grieve.
  **Dzikirirua,** *v. rel.* *See* Mufundo; Fiarira. Nidziamba; n'enende kua asena nikadzadzige, hata nin'enda — asena aka-ni-dzikirirua, basi nika uya.
  **Dzikiriruana,** *v. reit.* Gnombe zikidzikiriruana, silonda ku pigana.
**Dziko,** *n.* (= Meko in Kij.). *See* Zi-ri-zo. Hala o mugasija, ubume mo dzikoni, uoche. Dziko ra kuche dziko ra ku lume. Dziko ra ku chakanira. Homa ra ziko. *See* Gana.
**Dziku,** *adj.* *See* Linkua; Uganga. Gnombe dziku. Kasi dziku. Niumba dziku. Dziku dziku, A certain appointed day.
**Dziku,** *n.* (ya, za; but the pl. Madziku is also used), a day. Dziku hizi and Madziku higa. Yudzi-ni-pa dziku.
**Dzila** (Kik.), *v.n.*, to consult, to deliberate privately. Atu adzikutana, anadzila. Atu adzionana, adzi nadzi, anadzila. Nadzi, contracted from Naadzi.
**Dziloni,** *n.*, evening. Nidzigema lua dzulo dziloni muno.
**Dzima,** *n.* (ya, za), wari when put into a dish; food; a kind of porridge, not made so thick as the wari, but thicker than the uchi, gruel. Dzima ni wari udza-o evulua luigani. Dim., Kadzima.
**Dzimba,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), a lion. Dzimba ya alume ni i vo? Dzimba ya ache ni i vio?
**Dzimba,** *v.a.* *See* Padza; Dzamukana. To dig. Aki-m-ririra na lingua, yuna-dzimba, akale muko. Na dzimba dzina, ni bume nguso, ni ake niumba. Jogolo yudziihika na usiku; jogolo hiri ni ri, rinadzimba, basi ni ku ulagua. Muana hiyu yunadzimba rohoye.
  **Dzimbika,** *v.n.* Vatu hivo ni vomu, ka-va-dzimbika; ubume madzi, valuame, basi ndo vanda-vo-dzimbika.
  **Dzimbira,** *v. rel.*, to dig to, to dig for. Ni-dzimbira gopue hiva, ni bume nguso. Nadzimbira nguso (= Nadzimba, nibume nguso). Gnania yuna-m-dzimbira muyawe dzina ra kujua (= yuna-m-loga). Mutu hiye yuna-ni-dzimbira roho yangu, ka-ni-henzi.
  **Dzimbuka,** *v.n.*, to appear as clouds. Niumba yangu i-dzimbukadzimbuka (= i-henda vigopue vigopue). Maingu mairu gadzidzimbuka; muaka u-vevi, Black clouds have come forth; spring is near. Der., Dzimfi; Kidzimbuiriri.
  **Dzimbula,** *v.a.* Muna-i-dzimbula niumba, muna-i-bananga. Gnania yunarima ku dzimbula (= ku dipula).
**Dzimfi,** *n.* (= Vioni). Mutu hiyu ni dzimfi, yunahenza ku rira ulongo-ulongo; utu uchache na ku rira, yunadzimba atu. Kuku hiyu ni dzimfi, yunadzimba, mutu afue yudzihehera na usiku.
**Dzimia.**
**Dzina,** *n.*, a name. Dzina ra ku fialua na-ro; or, Dzina raku hadzua u-muhoho. Dzina ra sare, ra ku-dzi-hadza m'egnie, or, ra ku-dzidusira m'egnie.
**Dzina,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Dzimbira. Magn. of Uina. Ku piga madzina. Madzina gangu gadzimera.
**Dzinga,** *n.* *See* Familala; Ni dzinga; Za tia; Ni dzinga. Pl. of Luzinga. Dzinga za miradzo (Kid.). *See* Tunde.
**Dzinga,** *n.* Dzinga wa moho.
**Dzingo,** *n.* (ya, za), the neck.

## [PDF Page 75 — Dictionary Page 62 (Dzi — Dzo)]

**Dzini,** *prep.*, down, under, beneath.
**Dzino,** *n.*, (1) (ra, pl. Meno). *See* Hanuka. A tooth. Dzino ra kuro, An eye-tooth; lit. the tooth of a dog.
(2) (pl. Madzino). A link. Dzino ra mukufu; pl. Meno ga mukufu.
**Dzinsa,** *v.a.* *See* Ku zira. To sever. Ku dzinsa gnombe. Ku dzinsa vanda. Ku dzinsa kiseho.
  **Dzinsika,** *v.n.* *See* Chenchereka. Kuna viniama vikavio dzinsika niena dza mulonzi.
  **Dzinsikirua,** *v.p.* Nidzidzinsikirua ni nguo—atu adziingira uira, be hivi sina wiji. Ku dzinsikirua ni uchi kilariro.
  **Dzinsikisa,** *v.a.* Ku dzinsikiza vinianda via koe.
  **Dzinsira** (= Ku singa). Neno ra ku-m-dzinsira muyao. Yuna-m-dzinsira muyawe maneno osigo gomba.
  **Dzinsirana,** *v. reit.*
  **Dzinsirua,** *v.p.* Yudzidzinsirua, ela kagombere.
**Dzio** (Kid.), *n.* Wari wa dzio.
**Dzira.** *See* Dza (Ku dza, To come).
  **Dzirira.** *See* Dza.
  **Dzirirana.** *See* Dza.
  **Dziririka.** *See* Dza.
**Dzira,** *n.* (za), the dregs of palm-wine or toddy.
**Dzira** (Kid.) (= Kins., Chira), the name of a sweet-water fish.
**Dzira,** *v.n.* (= Ku gnieta). *See* Dimula; Muelo. To be naughty, sportful, gaysome.
  **Dzirira.** U-dzirirani (for, Udzirira ani)? 'Ye u-dziriraye, rikaro vano ni ani?
  **Dzirirana.**
  **Dzisadzisa** (Kid.) (= Ku dzadzarisa in Kir.).
**Dziridziri,** *adv.* *See* Biribiri. Continually; in one stream. Viombo vinaingira dziridziri. Kirenge kinafudza dziridziri, dza muridza. Kirenge kina dzuiri, uchi unadziririka. Au adzidziririka dziridziri, adziidzala dele.
**Dziru,** *adj.* *See* Thina; Kisisi. Fierce. Gnombe dziru. Niuchi dziru.
**Dzitu,** *n.* *See* Kusada; Diro. (K.) repetition. Nidziona midzitu mibomu.
**Dziuda.** *See* Kiniume.
**Dzivo,** *n.* Magn. of Kivo.
**Dziwa,** *v.p.* *See* Dza (Ku dza, To come).
**Dziwe.** Magn. of Iwe.
**Dzo.** N' dzo vio, etc.
**Dzo** (Kik.), *n.* (ra, pl. Madzo) (= Gurudumu in Kir.).
**Dzoa.** *See* Mera. Ku nioka dzoa. Mu-ulageni nioka hiye, basidzoa! Kill ye that serpent, to be sure.
**Dzoa,** *n.* (wa, hiya, pl. *id.*, a, hia). Dzoa afialua ni ludzoa.
**Dzoa,** *v.* *See* Fusika; Muvuye; Kigniesi. Ku dzoa akili. Hosi hudzoe; 'ye asipate nami nisipate; musena a-mu-dzoe, na mi ni-mu-dzoe.
  **Dzoeka,** *v.n.* Uchi udzi-ni-dzoeka rero.
  **Dzoekua,** *v.p.* *See* Kuluvirana. Nidzidzoekua ni kitu kisiku.
  **Dzoera,** *v.d.* Gnania yudzidzoera gnania haya, yudzi-mu-ambira uso na madzo.
**Dzofia,** *v.a.* Amasai akudza-hu-dzofia, akihala gnombe sehu zosi, kuamba hu-dzi-sare mafuha ga niono kaviri. Usi-m-dzofie muyao, ku-m-voka kituche ni vi.
  **Dzofiwa,** *v.p.* Gnania ni mudzofi wa haya-akadzofiwa haya.
**Dzoka,** *v.n.*, to be tired. Prov., Murima dzoka kadzoka.
**Dzola,** *v.a.* *See* Nionio; Kihenso. To pick up; to find, to get. Gnombe ayeangamika, ni ku-m-dzola. Musunie akimbi-

*Footer: 62*

---

## [PDF Page 76 — Dictionary Page 63 (Dzo — Dzo)]

  raye, ni ku-m-dzola. Nidzidzola neno, ni-ku-ambire, I have picked up a word, I have heard a something by the way; let me tell you. Nidzidzola koma, namba, ni-mu-ambire.
  **Dzoladzola,** *v. reit.* Vakamuagika vitu madzere ya mabila, nikakuenda dzoladzola.
  **Dzoloka,** *v.n.* Udzidzoloka wegnie, ka-u-ka-dzololua ni mutu (mufui, etc.). Una dzoloka ka-u-toka sana.
  **Dzolola,** *v.a.* (= Ku dzoniola; Ku futa), to draw out, as a piece of wood from a heap. Ku dzolola mufiu choani. Ku dzolola mufui riakani.
  **Dzolorera,** *v.d.* Yudzi-m-dzolorera kifiu, yulonda ku-m-bofola. Kid., Udzoloka wegnie, ka-u-dzolorerue ni mutu.
  **Dzolosa,** *v.a.* Yudzifuma pinda, yudzidzolosa to. Yudzidzolosa pinda ne, or, pinda tahu.
  **Dzolosera,** *v.d.* Yudzi-ni-dzolosera mulomo, kakagomba nami, yudzukirua, simania aka-vio-kosua. Adzolosera milomo, They shoot out their lips (Ps. xxii. 7).
**Dzoreka,** *v.n.* Wimbi na ufuha ka-u-dzoreka. Prov., Madzi gaki muagika, ka-ga-dzoreka. Niamala! vidzihendeka kare; hata ukirira, unda-m-pata? roho ikihalua ni m'egnie Mulungu, basi ka-i-patikana kahiri.
  **Dzorera,** *v. rel.* Nidzi-m-dzorera madzere, niki-mu-va, yudzikuenda henda kilariro.
  **Dzorerana,** *v. reit.* Nidzi-m-sia kuko mudzini, anadzorerana madzere na nduguye.
  **Dzorerua,** *v.p.* Der., Dzore.
  **Dzosha,** *v.c.* (= Dzosia).
**Dzoa,** *adv.* Basi zoa, Certainly, by all means, to be sure.
**Dzodza,** *v.a.* Kidisa a ya ki dzuza.
  **Dzodzeka,** *v.n.* Gnania kadzodzeka, ni muoga.
  **Dzodzera,** *v. rel.* Sina kifiu cha ku dzodzera.
  **Dzodzerua,** *v.p.* Ni-pa baruti-ge, nikadzo-dzerue.
  **Dzodzua,** *v.p.* Der., Mudzodzi.
**Dzodzera** (= Ku dzedzera, moho). Ku dzodzera moho, ni ku-u-udza vamenga.
  **Dzodzerera,** *v. rel.* Moho wangu hiu mu-ni-dzodzerere, n'enda vatu vasiku.
**Dzodzo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-, *q.v.*).
**Dzodzomera,** *v.*
**Dzodzomeza,** *v.n.*, to go on tiptoe. Ku dzodzomeza ni ku fioga na dza sa mala.
**Dzodzota,** *v.n.* *See* Lambika. Kironda kinadzodzota.
**Dzodzosa,** *v.a.* (= Ku dadisi in Kij.), to pry into things, to ask inquisitive questions. Ku dzodzoza ni ku-mu-usa muyao neno, amba-ro ka-rihenzi ku-ri-gomba; be uka-m-dzodzoza hata aka-ku-ambira. Nidzi-m-dzodzoza hata yudzi-ni-ambira.
  **Dzodzozana,** *v. reit.* Nidzi-a-sia, anadzodzozana vavo; be simania kuamba yunda-mu-ambira.
**Dzofia,** *n.* Gnania ni dzofia; pl. Atu hio ni dzofia. Kiravo cha dzofia kina dzofia roho.
**Dzoga,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Abisa; Hulukisa; Doniola. The marks made by tattooing. Dzoga za kiduro. Dzoga za gunga. Dzoga yangu idzihenda kironda, nina muiri mui. Musichana akadzodzua dzoga, sika-mu-agira. Ku ria dzoga. Ku lomborera dzoga. Kakuna vi kaviri, hudzeria dzoga. Yuguirua ni dzoga. Kuna

*Footer: 63*

---

## [PDF Page 77 — Dictionary Page 64 (Dzo — Dzo)]

  muhi wa ku dovola dzoga. Dim., Vidzoga.
**Dzoho,** *n.* (ra). *See* Lumisa. (1) A large fire. Magn. of Moho.
(2) Heat. Udzihenda dzoho ringi na-we! unamala kuni. Udzihenda dzoho bomu, kundadzoma niumba vio? Niumbani mu dzoho-ka mu vegnieka.
  **Dzohodzoho.** Madzi higa, or, gano ga dzoho, or, ga-dzohodzoho, gadzikolua ni dzua.
**Dzoka,** *v.n.* *See* Dzoa. To be tired.
**Dzoka,** *n.* Ku-m-longosa mutu dzokani.
**Dzola.** *See* Dzoa.
  **Dzoloka.** *See* Dzoa.
  **Dzolola.** *See* Dzoa.
  **Dzolosa.** *See* Dzoa.
**Dzoma,** *v.a.* *See* Okoka. To burn, to sear, to cauterize. Dzua ridzikola, rinadzoma.
  **Dzomeka** (= Kij., Domeka). *See* Fudzulua. (K.) to insert, to stick. Ku dzomeka muleli.
  **Dzomekera.** Ku dzomekera madzere kavuni (Kij. = Ku tomelia mahindi kapuni), To put Indian corn into a basket.
  **Dzomekeza.** *See* Fudzirua; Wasimu.
  **Dzomera.** *See* Makansa; Choro; Luansa. N'enda, nikadzomere minazi ludzengo, moho mubomu ukidza, usiingire minozini.
  **Dzomerua,** *v.p.* *See* Cho.
  **Dzomola,** *v.n.*, to shoot forth. Maere gadzidzomola. Muhama unadzomola suche rikiansa ku la kura-tu mimbani; rikila rosi, rikisira, ukaamba: muhama udzifumula.
  **Dzomba.** Kid., Wali wa muana dzomba ni muerefu muno, wahala madzi, aki-ya-henda njira.
**Dzombo,** *n.*, a large vessel. Magn. of Chombo.
**Dzomfi,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). *See* Dzidzoa; Mugunga.
**Dzomo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Bengo). Dzomo ra munda. Ukirima, ukirija bengo, ndo riihuaro dzomo. Dim., Kadzomo; Kidzomo.
**Dzona,** *adv.* (= Kid., Mbona? Kahiri, likewise?). Dzona warija-dze?
**Dzonga,** *v.a.*
  **Dzongera.** Kidigo and Kid., Ku dzongera lua mdzana; Kir., Ku gema lua mdzana.
  **Dzongoka,** *v.n.* Yudzidzongola, ela ka-u-ka-dzongoka to, ka-u-kahenda dza. Gnania ni mufuhi, ela nduguye akadzongoka, yuna kimo punde. Yunamania Kiravai, ela mangine yunagofia, ka-ga-dzongoka. Der., Madzongi.
  **Dzongola,** *v.a.*, to point, to make pointed. Nadzongola muhi nihende chulo. Ku dzongola maneno, To point words; *i.e.* To speak to the purpose. Maneno higo gere ganasirimia atu, ela gnania musiku ndiye adzeye-ga-dzongola.
  **Dzongorera,** *v. reit.* Reha, ni-ku-dzongoreredza, Bring it, let me cut a point, let me point it for you.
**Dzonge** (Kidigo), *n.* *See* Dzasa. The afternoon. Only used in connection with Dzua. Trop., the toddy drawn in the afternoon. Dzua ra dzonge (= Dzua ra lua mudzana in Kir.). Dzua ridzifika ra dzonge (= Dzua ridzifika lua mudzana).
**Dzongo,** *n.*, the name of a bird. Dzongo adza tiramuko, akaria muhama hata dzua rikikola; basi akakuenda peho za mihi, akasagala ku oya; wau-hata dzua rikivola, akakudza kaviri kuria muhama, ku pata kilariro cha dziloni; dzua rikisama, basi akaenenda.
**Dzongolurisi.**
**Dzongonene,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Fuma. The seam formed in

*Footer: 64*

---

## [PDF Page 78 — Dictionary Page 65 (Dzo — Dzu)]

  mending a cloth by turning the sides or ends into the middle—a thick back. Ku piga dzongonene, ku dzangania midza na midza. Dim., Kadzongonene; Kidzongonene.
**Dzoni,** *n.*, (K.) mum, silence, inveigh. Ku piga dzoni, To make a smacking noise when vexed. Ku-m-pigira dzoni.
**Dzonia,** *n.* Pl. of Luzonia.
**Dzonioka,** *v.n.* *See* Kifiu, from its handle. Kinavalala, kinalonda ku dzonioka. Nidzikita, nidzifuha, ka-ki-dzonioka. Mufiu wangu udziguira kanga, ka-u-dzonioka choani (= ka-u-ta).
  **Dzoniola,** *v.a.*, to draw, to draw out, especially from a sheath. Ku dzoniola mufiu. Be ndo lualodzoniolua muirini mua nsoya.
  **Dzonioreka,** *v.n.*
  **Dzoniorera,** *v. reit.* (= Gongoloka), to break a secret, to broach to, to draw out a secret. Nidzimuta kifu changu hiva muhini, na-ki-dzoniola. Ka-ki-dzonioreka, be ndzo u-ni-dzoniorere.
**Dzonso, Dzonzo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Dim., Kidzonso (?).
**Dzonsoka,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of lizard, remarkable for its colours, in streaks or lines. Dzonsoka rina ndzora ne.
**Dzopola,** *v.a.* (= Kid., Chopola). Niere ka-zi-ku-dzopola? Niere sino sina-ni-dzopola. Nidzidzopolua ni luniasi.
  **Dzopolana,** *v. reit.* Dzadzigani to, maniani, musadzapolana.
**Dzora,** *v.a.*, to engrave, to carve, by way of ornament. Ku dzora kiravo. Ku dzora kirenge, To carve a calabash. Adzomba ni ku dzora waraka. Aravai akare ori akidzora ndere, aka-si-henda ndzora sa dzonsoka.
  **Dzorera,** *v. rel.* Na-mu-dzorera gnania kirengeche cha ndere.
  **Dzorerua,** *v.p.* Yudzikuenda virika kirengeche ku dzorerua.
  **Dzorua,** *v.p.* *See* Gondoera. Kirenge hiki kikadzorua to, mutu hiye yuna madzo.
**Dzore.** *See* Mukuamba; Kifungudzore.
**Dzore,** *n.* Nidzidzola kifiucho, basi u-ni-pe dzore; ukisa-ni-pa dzore, naenenda nacho. Yudzidzola kitu, be yudzihewa dzore.
**Dzoreka.** *See* Dzoa.
**Dzorera.** *See* Dzoa.
**Dzosha.** *See* Dzoka (Dzoa).
**Dzosi,** *n.* (ra, Dzidzo), tear, droplet.
**Dzosia,** *v.c.* *See* Era. To tire, to weary, to trouble, to annoy. Udzi-mu-va musigo mubomu, unda-m-dzosia, kanda-u-fisa.
**Dzota,** *v.a.* (Kid., Doto; Kins., Tura). *See* Nche; Donera. To peck, to pick up as birds, to throb. Trop., to intimate slightly. Kozi yudzi-ni-dzota, The vulture pecked me. Kironda kinadzota, The wound throbs. Udzi-ni-dzota neno, ela kuka-ri-gomba.
  **Dzotadzota,** *v. reit.*, to throb; lit. to keep pecking. Kironda kina-ni-dzotadzota.
**Dzova,** *v.a.* (= Ku gera in Kidigo), to drink, said of others, not of one's self. Halani uchi, mudzove, hunoe. N.B.—The word is only used with reference to others, but when drinking by one's self alone, you say, Nabuma uchi kibariani, ni-noe.
  **Dzovadzova,** *v. reit.* *See* Kota.
  **Dzovera,** *v. rel.*
  **Dzoverana,** *v. reit.* Der., Ludzovo; Mudzovi; Udzovi.
**Dzoyo,** *n.* (ra), a large heart. Magn. of Moyo. Mugasija udziaya, udzihenda dzoyo, unalonda ku ola ka-u-na unga kahiri.
**Dzua,** *n.* (ra), the sun. The pl. Madzua is often used instead

## [PDF Page 79 — Dictionary Page 66 (Dzu — Dzu)]

  of Dziku. Nasinda madzua mairi, ela dziku ya hahu ninadza. There are standing expressions, marking with great exactness the particular position of the sun during the course of the day:—(1) Dzua ridziupuka; or, Dzua ridziombola. (2) Dzua ridzidana nadzi. (3) Dzua ridzifika murauko wa gnombe mudzanga. (4) Dzua ridzifika murauko wa gnombe wegnie. (5) Dzua ridzifika murauko wa gnombe mubomu wa ku radira vidzoa. (6) Dzua rinaradira vidzoa. (7) Dzua ridzifikavidzoani; or, Ridziima na kidzoa, or, vidzoa; or, Dzua ri-dididi na vidzoa. (8) Dzua ridziogoka. (9) Dzua ridzifika lua mudzana lukulu; or, Dzua ridzikoma lua mudzana; or, Dzua ridziguira lua mudzana. (10) Dzua ridzifika lua mudzana luegnie. (11) Dzua ridzifika lua mudzana lua ku vola. (12) Dzua ridzisama rinalewalewa. (13) Dzua ridzibodoka; or, Dzua ridzedzua. Dzua bomu, Early in the afternoon. Ninadza dzua bomu, sindakudza dziloni. Thus, instead of asking, What is the time? they will ask, Dzua ri luavi? Where is the sun? or, Dzua raambadze? What says the sun? The only expression which is often improperly used is that of, Dzua ridzedzua, The sun is set, which is often heard early in the afternoon. The wish suggests the expression.—[ED.] Mutu akilonda ku-m-jinga muyawe, yu-mu-amba: henda haraka, dzua ridzedzua, husaenenda na usiku. Dzua ni Mukuavi, kadumfa; *i.e.* Dzua rikiuichirira ku ulaga, be ka-ri-sasa, ka-ri-na mbazi, ela mvula i na mbazi, yuulaga vatu vamenga, kungine kukadifia.
  **Dzua** (*Ku dzua*), *v.n.*, to set. Only used of the sun. Dzua ridzedzua, The sun is set. Kudzedzua, It is sunset. *See* Guika. Kudzedzua ge, enda, ukafunge mbuzi.
  **Dzuerera,** *v. rel.* (= Bodokera), to set to. Sikakuenda vatu, nidzisinda vava, hata dzua ridzi-ni-dzuerera vava. Yudzienenda hata dzua ridzi-m-dzuerera vatu vasiku. Der., Udzuerero.
  **Dzueza,** *v.* Ku dzueza mundani. Nidzikuenda dzueza mundani, be nidziingira vivi dziloni. N'endarima, ela sindadzueza, nindakudza mapema.
**Dzudza,** *v.a.* (= Ku kamula). *See* Kemba. To strain by pressing and squeezing. Ku dzudza hui (in Kid., Ku dzudza uchi = Kir., Ku kemba uchi).
  **Dzudzama** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Ku dutama in Kij., and Ku fumbama, or, Ku piga kignioto in Kir.), to half-sit, to squat.
  **Dzudzira,** *v. rel.* Ni-pa ndifu nidzudzire hui. Kuku hiyu ni mugeni, kamania niumba, be kukidzua, mudzudzire, mubume niumbani.

**Dzudzua,** *v.n.* *See* Manionioda. To drizzle. Kunche rinadzudzua. Mvula inadzudzua (= Inagnia tatetate).
  **Dzudzurira,** *v.n.* *See* Nona. To hop. Only used of certain birds. Mbuda yunadzudzurira kuenda kidzungini muakue. Hepe, Nona, Kimbule, Handala anadzudzurira (= anaenenda-dzi).

## E.

**E,** the fifth letter, uniformly pronounced nearly like *a* in "gate."—[ED.] The vowel-sound represented by this letter bestows, on this South-African family of languages, one of its most remarkable features in the change or modification of the meaning of verbs. It appears to be radical only in a few words, while its principal use is: (1) To indicate the opt., the usual termination *-a* being changed into *-e* without any exception. (2) Like that of *i*, to render help in expressing the ideas of possibility, state, or condition, -eka; transition, behalf, instrumentality, -era; and cause, -eza. The termination *-a* of such verbs as contain an *e* or *o* in their roots, is changed into *-e*, in order to receive the terminations *-ka*, *-ra*, and *-za*, while all other verbs containing the vowels *a*, *i*, and *u* in their roots, take *i* in receiving those additions, -ira. As to -era, -ira, respectively, it must be remarked that the consonant *r*—in other dialects *l*—is merely euphonical, not radical, as is proved by the corresponding -ea, -ia, respectively, in Kij. We may therefore say that the ideas of transition, behalf, and instrumentality lie merely in the vowels *e* and *i*. *See* Ma. Lastly, it is added to any word at the end of a sentence, and then serves for rousing attention, or is expressive of surprise. This is especially the case with names, when calling for any person at a distance. *See* Balu; Kidzeko; Nonogneza; Tonga.
**E,** *poss. pron.* (enclit.; rel. to words

  which form their pl. by *a*), his, her. When the pron. is used without mentioning the noun to which it refers, Akue must be used. Asunie-e, His or her slaves. Ana-e, His or her children. Atu-e, His or her people.

**Egnie.** *See* Muegnie.
**Ekemera,** *v.n.*, to lean, to rely, to trust. Derived from Ku-a, to be, in Kij.; a branch of this would be Eka, which, receiving the termination -ma and changing its *a* into *e*, would become Ekema, of which Ekemera is *v.d.* Eka and Ekema do, however, not exist in Kij. and Kin., but may be found in other dialects. Prov., Muhi ukibua u-ekemera muyawe.
  **Ekemerana,** *v. reit.*, to lean, to rely on each other. Atu adzaopatana ni ku ekemerana.
  **Ekemereka,** *v.n.*, to be reliable, trustworthy. Gnania kaekemereka, yu mui.
  **Ekemesa,** *v.c.*, to cause to lean, to lean up or put up anything against another. Trop., to lay upon, let rest upon, said of the debts of another; in this sense the passive form only is used. (N.B.—This is an excellent word for expressing the gospel truth that Christ had our sins laid upon Him.) Nidziekemesua deni ni zi ro ri mania, or, ni zi ro ri larira. Nidziekemesua deni ra ndugu yangu, ela ninda riva vifio, nindahenda dze? Adzomba akaekemesua ushuru ni Saidi, The Suahilis have had duty laid upon them by the imâm.
  **Ekemeseka,** *v.n.*, to admit of leaning up against, or laying debts upon any one. U mulongo! kuira; ka ekemeseka kabisa.
  **Ekerera** (Kid.), *v.a.*, to fletch arrows. Radically, to let be upon. Also to be derived from Ku-a in Kij. A, Eka, Ekera; *see* Ekemera. Ku ekerera mifui.
**Ela,** *conj.*, but. The Arabic Illa. Purely African dialects seem to have no word for this conjunction; in Kins., for instance, it is not found.
**Elefuka.** *See* Erefuka.
**Elekania,** *v.a.*, to guess, to conjecture; to adjust one's thoughts or words. Radically, to make come up with. This and all the following words down to Elezania are all derived from Era, the *r* being interchanged for *l*. Mutu hiye yunaelekania maneno; akegomba, manenoge gan'enda karakara. Ndio nguo ini elekaniayo.
**Elela,** *v.n.*, to float. *See* Erera.
**Elelia,** *v.a.* (= Ku insa), to keep an eye upon, to watch one's conduct; to suspect. Radically, to keep afloat. Mutu hiye na-mu-elelia hata ni-m-pate. Uk'enda kua gnania, yuna ku elelia; angue, una muchewe, When you go to Gnania, he suspects you; he says you are with his wife. Yudzihenda mu elelia, kuamba ndiye ayeiya kituche ela kaka-mu-ona. Prov., Muifi kaeleliua, sudi mu guire na kisuche; lit. A thief is not suspected; you must seize him with the head of the corn (*see* Kisuche); *i.e.* One is not proved a thief by mere suspicion; you must seize him in the act.
**Elemea** (Kij.), *v.n.* *See* Eremera. To press upon, to hold

*Footer: 71*

---

## [PDF Page 85 — Dictionary Page 72 (Eli — End)]

  on. In this instance it is especially clear that the *l* in this whole group of words serves to distinguish the abstract meanings from the concrete ones, which have the *r* unchanged. Hudzemfodua, ela hunaelemia vifio, hata ahense maneno gehu, We have been confuted, but we hold on notwithstanding, or in the same manner, until they like ours—until they come over to our side of the question.
  **Elemeana** (Kij.), *v. reit.* (= Gandamirana), to be close on one another in pursuing, etc. Adzielemeana hata adzizola ayao.
**Elesa,** or **Eleza** (Kij.), *v.c.* *See* Ereza. To make understand, to inform about anything. Radically, to make come up to one's understanding. 'Ndzo, ni ku eleze maneno yangu, Come, and let me explain my words.
  **Elezania,** or **Elesania,** *v. reit.*, to make understand one another. Nidzia sia akielezania maneno.
**Elimu** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za), science, erudition. With the Wanika, the knowledge of medicine and magic.
**Embe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the mango fruit. The word refers to the flat shape of the mango, as is clear from its forming the radical part of the words Chembe, Chembeu, Jembe, and Luembe. It is the opt. form of a verb, Ku emba, which does not exist in the dialects known to me.
**Enda,** *v.n.*, to go, to move. The conjugation of this verb presents some irregularities:—
(1) In the present tense, in which the vowels of the pronouns are dropped. This is done even in the case of a pronoun consisting of a single vowel without a consonant, as is seen in the following table:—

*(a) Indicative Mood, in which the vowel a is dropped.*
* *Sing.* 1. Nin'enda *for* ninaenda
* *Sing.* 2. Un'enda *for* unaenda
* *Sing.* 3. Yun'enda *for* yunaenda
* *Pl.* 1. Hun'enda *for* hunaenda
* *Pl.* 2. Mun'enda *for* munaenda
* *Pl.* 3. An'enda *for* anaenda
* *Or*—
* *Sing.* 1. N'enda *for* naenda
* *Sing.* 2. W'enda *for* waenda
* *Sing.* 3. 'Enda *for* aenda
* *Pl.* 1. Hu'enda *for* huaenda
* *Pl.* 2. Mu'enda *for* muaenda
* *Pl.* 3. 'Enda *for* aenda

*(b) In the Optative the vowels i and u are dropped, and in one instance u becomes w.*
* *Sing.* 1. N'ende *for* niende
* *Sing.* 2. Wende *for* uende
* *Sing.* 3. 'Ende *for* aende
* *Pl.* 1. H'ende *for* huende
* *Pl.* 2. M'ende *for* muende
* *Pl.* 3. 'Ende *for* aende

*(c) In the Subjunctive Mood (resp. the Participle) i is dropped.*
* Nik'enda *for* Nikienda, If I go. Etc., etc.
* *Resp.*, I going. *See* Grammar.
* Remark: This form of the verb may also be taken for the aorist, which in this instance coincides with the subj. mood, Nik'enda for Nikaenda, and whether if it is the one or the other in a given sentence can only be known by the connection. The same elision of vowels takes place in the negative personal pronouns, as also in the impersonal ones, which represent the various classes of nouns.
(2) In the past and future tenses, the infinitive particle Ku is retained in the same way as is the case with monosyllabic and enclitic verbs:—
* Nidzikuenda, I have gone. Etc., etc.

## [PDF Page 86 — Dictionary Page 73 (End — Ene)]

* Ntakuenda, I shall go. Etc., etc.
The peculiarities of this verb in syntax are the following:— (1) When followed by an infinitive, the infinitive particle Ku is omitted; *e.g.* Gnania na gnania 'enda ria kiravo, for, ku ria; or, Gnania na gnania an'enda ria kiravo, Mr. So-and-so and Mr. So-and-so they go to eat an ordeal. (2) When expressing a resolution, wish, or command, the verb, by which it is followed, always stands in the aorist ka in its opt. mood; *e.g.* N'enda nikalale, I go to lay myself down. N'enda sokoni, nikagule tumbaku, I go to the market to buy tobacco. Enda, uka mu ve, Go and give him. Enda, ukause tandiko, Go and remove the bedding, anything spread out. Endani, mukaoke, Go ye and bathe. H'ende, hukaoke, Let us go and bathe. *See* Be; Ulozi. Yukuenda fua kala, akagusa kilariro; na muche akuenda rimira runga aka hewa kunsa.
  **Endeka,** *v.n.*, to admit of going. Dzi ya Ravai kakuendeka hikara, kuna Amasai.
  **Endera,** *v.d.*, to go to. Simania adza ko kuendera, I know not whence they go. Mudzi kuendera luavi? or Mudzi kuendera nchira i vio? Hunda kuenderavi? Where are you going?
  **Enderera,** *v. cont.* *See* Ufiasi. To go further; to continue, to spread. Moho unaenderera. Chinga kinaenderera. Mutu hiye, akienenda, be ni ku enderera kamare. W'amba w'enda Kisiwani be auye, ela fio yudzienderera kamare, He said he would go to Mombas and return, but he has gone further; W'amba for Waamba.
  **Endereza,** *v.c.* and *n.* *See* Kata; Keke. To cause to go further, to protract, to prolong, to continue doing anything, to be long in continuance. Yuna gomba moro wa ku endereza, kaveza, He makes a long speech, he does not conclude. Lingua ra ku endereza, A prolonged voice; lit. A voice of to prolong. Ukiendereza, uodamania, If you continue doing it, you will get to know. Nchira inaendereza, The way is long, prolongs itself.
**Enche.** *See* Enge.
**Enehu.** *See* Muenehu.
**Enenda,** *v.n.* *See* Kizungu; Kuisa; Dzikirirua; Dzongo. To go, to walk. This word is derived from Ku enda by a reduplication of the first syllable. The conjugation of this verb does not present the same elision of vowels as Ku enda, except in the opt. or imper. H'enende, or, H'enendeni, Let us go; the *u* in Hu being omitted, but in the first instance it may as well be retained. Ni mufiere, yunaenenda na mudada, He is an old man; he walks with a stick.
  **Enendeka,** *v.n.* *See* Madofia. To admit of going or walking. Dzi hio ka i enendeka kua Amasai.
  **Enendera,** *v.d.* *See* Kigulu. To go to, against, with; to be hostile to, to oppose. Muana hiyu yuna dzi enendera kua asena tu, ndo ku dzi hensia ku yeya. Mutu hiye yudzi ni enendera hata nidziriwa malu, That man opposed me until I was fined.
  **Enenderana,** *v. reit.*, to oppose one another. Atu hio anaenenderana, kahensania alonda ku logana.
  **Enenzia,** *v.c.*, (1) to cause to go or walk a child by leading him.

## [PDF Page 87 — Dictionary Page 74 (Ene — Ens)]

  (2) To have a child who has learned to walk—always said with reference to succeeding pregnancy. Ku-m-guira mukono na ku mu enenzia muana. Ka dza enenzia, ela yudzi-m-chira, yuna mimba. Yudzienenzia, ka dza henda mimba, yuna lukuzo.
**Enera,** *v.n.* *See* Ludara; Mukambe. To suffice, to extend, to reach. Radically, to be with to a given limit in space, number, etc. The word contains the conj. Na, with, in the dative form. Nguo hi kai-mu-enera muana, i tide.
  **Enerua,** *v.p.* *See* Darana; Hofiana; Kidamfira; Makalo. To be reached in getting one's portion of anything; to find room.
  **Eneza,** *v.c.* To cause to suffice, to make a thing reach to a given limit, to get a sufficiency; to have a good supply, to have enough. Udzigafiadze niama mbona kuka eneza atu? Gafia niama to, ueneze, kula mutu apate. Yudzieneza kivesa na mavalu na fuiho, yuirua ni niasi tu. Gnania yuna ana anga vi? Resp., A yudzieneza, yuna ana ahandahu; or, yunapata ana kumi kamoe. Si thalimu Mulungu, nidzieneza, Mulungu bariki, nidzi pata viakuria, naukusha ndani yangu; nidz'eneza mino, sina hata utu; also merely, 'Ze'-neza for Nidzi eneza.
  **Enezana,** *v. reit.*, to make a thing suffice or reach to one another. Si gniagnianireni, gafiani, mu enezane. Der., Chenezo.
**Eneza,** *n.* *See* Mugafu. Sufficiency, enough.
**Enga** (Kid.), *v.a.*, to scum.
  **Engula,** *v.a.*, to scum, to clear off the surface, to hatch. Ku engula mafuha. Kuku yudziengula ana, The hen has hatched her chickens; she has taken off the surface, *i.e.* the shells (= Ku kokota).
  **Engulula,** *v.a.*, to skim, to take off what is on the surface. Ku engulula luhandu, To skim off the cream. Ku engulula fulo, To skim off froth. Ku engulula madzere ga ka go anikua dzuani, To spread Indian corn in the sun. Nidzianika madzere, ela ka ga dza kolua to, be nidziengulula gaga ga dzulu, ga ka go kola dzua. Der., Chengo; Chense; Enge; Muengero.
  **Engurira,** *v.d.* and *instr.* *See* Kola. To scum to, for, with.
**Enge,** or **Enche,** *n.* (ra), crust of salt only, as deposited by the sea in open and sandy places, during spring tides. *See* Luangua. Radically, something to be skimmed off. The opt. form of Ku enga. Enche ridzi hendeka; hendeni huka kuue enche. Nidzikuna enche, basi na zola ku buma kavuni.
**Engelele,** *adj.* (*verb adj.*, from Ku angalala), to be pausing, to be in a pause, state of hesitation or suspense. Madzi ga engelele, ka ga ira, ka ga hokoha. Madzere ga engelele; gadzi henda ushanga. Yu engelele; ka gomba a ri-ro naro ndanimua kue, yu hurira hu. Nidzi mu ona, yu vavo, yu engelele; ka gomba na mutu, na gara a dzo go lagizua ka gomba, yudziangalala.
**Ensi, Aenzi** (ra and ya), *n.*, a chief. Gnania yudzipata ensi—yudzikala shaha. In former times, especially under the Masrue dynasty of Mombas, the Wanika chiefs had a Kihi cha ensi, a Pehe ya ensi, and an Ndada ya ensi given to them, and the two latter were taken to Mombas whenever a matter of importance was to be discussed. Ensiye, or, Ensire, ikasidi ayae; or, rikasida ayae. Gnania yundakala shaha, yudzihewa ensi ni Mulungu. Muaka hiu una

## [PDF Page 88 — Dictionary Page 75 (Era — Era)]

  ensi—atu adzipata nafaka ningi muno.
**Era,** *v.a.* *See* Kishongo. To proportion, to make adequate. Ku era madzi; madzi gakale karakara na unga. Ku era niuni, To take a bearing of birds, in seeking an omen from them. If the bird consulted cries at the right or left hand, the omen is good; if before you, it is bad. *See* Kokota. Ninaera ndani yangu chakuria (= Naera chakuria ndani yangu; or, Ninaera chakuria cha ndani yangu). Msigo sodi ubume wa ku era—wa ku-dzi-unurisa m'egnie. Kazi ihendua ya ku era haya, ukarime di, hata dzua ribodoke kudzoka we? Be minazi igemua ya ku era ngufuzo—ukagema minazi samia zima, kumania kuamba inadzosia we? Gnania kaera, yumania kuria tu. Inoa uchi wa ku era—ukinoa ungi wa ku chiza, undavavika zu inoa. *See* I. Iye yuna-ni-era ngufu. Yulonda hu migniane, a-ni-ere ngufu. Nidziera madzi, ni mare, vana kina. *See* Ku esa. Moyowe udzi-mu-era; neno adzi-ro-ambirua, ri dzi-mu-hamira, ni ridzo. Yudzifiera vatu hiva, vadzidzuka, vadziera dze.
  **Erefuka,** *v.n.* *See* Ere.
  **Erefusa,** *v.c.* *See* Ere.
  **Ereka,** *v.a.*, to suspend, to hang on one's back. Ku kua. Ku-mu-ereka muana, To hang a child on the back. The native women carry their children hung in a cloth. Niani ni ku ereka ana mongoni, ela akiona adui, muanawe akabeduka, akakudza lagani; mameye akikimbira, muana yulagani.
  **Erekana,** *v. reit.*, to carry one another. Ahoho hara anaerekana. Menoge gakaerekana, gana papadzi.
  **Erekeka,** *v.n.*, to be carried. Muana hiyu ni mkongo muno, kaerekeka kaviri. M'ana yudzierekeka to habudze? Resp., Kakaerekeka to, yulonda kubua.
  **Erekera,** (1) *v.d.* Ni-erekera m'anangu geu-ni-oyese. Ndze-uhale mkamba wa m'ana, u-mu-erekere. Mkamba ni nguo, ya ku erekera m'ana.
  (2) *v.n.* *See* Udzerero. To be towards anything, to be in the direction of or to anything. Vidzierekera to (= Vidzikuenda karakara). Muriango wa niumbayangu udzierekera ulairo wa dzua; or, uomborero wa dzua, The door of my house opens to the east. Kaziye idziereke ra.
  **Erekeza,** *v.a.* *See* Kosa; Mudzundu; Langarisa. To direct, to adjust; to take for, to make out to be, to be of opinion.
  **Erekezana,** or **Erekezania,** *v.a.* *See* Adzogo; Engelele.
  **Erekezeka,** *v.n.* *See* Gomia; Iya. Hudzierekeza hata vidzierekezeka. Gnania msiku-moyowe ka-u-erekezeka.
  **Erekezera.**
  **Eremera,** *v.a.*, to press upon.
  **Eremerana,** *v. ref.*, to press upon one another.
  **Eremesa,** *v.c.*, to cause to press upon. The formation Erema is not used in Kir., but in Kiniasa.
  **Erera,** *v.*, to float, to heave. Moyo una-ni-erera; lit. My heart heaves (= I am sick). Muana yudzihenda utu, nidzidzukirua, moyo udzi-ni-erera, nidziamba: ni-m-pige.
  **Ererua,** *v.p.* Ku ererua ni moyo (= Ku eresua ni moyo).
  **Eresa,** *v.a.*, to cause to heave. Ku-mu-eresa muana muyawe. Madzere ganaeresa. Chakuria hiki kina-ni-eresa moyo, This food makes my heart heave (= makes me sick).
  **Eresania.**

## [PDF Page 89 — Dictionary Page 76 (Ere — Eve)]

  **Eresua,** *v.p.*, to be lifted up. Ku eresua ni moyo-ni vevi na ku vavika.
  **Erua,** *v.p.* (= Eresua). Bewe! chakuria ka-ki-erua-vakikala na ageni. Yudzierua ni moyo, He is pleased.
  **Esa, Eza,** *v.a.* *See* Kasi. To measure, to reach, as the heart. Lusihuluangu na-lu-esa pima,—nimanie zindala ningavi? Uchi wangu nidzi-u-eza, mbona usinda, niani adzaye-u-noa na-u-ona, usinda. Si-ni-ese chera! Resp., Nidzi-ku-esa du-nidzi-ku-dema vo? Una-ni-esa kigongo, nidzi-ku-henda dze? Simania kitu ninda cho-mu-va, cha ku-mu-eza moyo, naye ahende mumfera; or, naye ku-ni-hendera mumfera. Madzi ga hiva ni mare, ukiesa na muhi, basi muhi ni ku niamala, ela ka-u-ka gota dzi. Mulu hiye yudzi-ni-esa moyo, sina kishongo kahiri. Yudzi-ni-pa kitu kikacho-ni-esa moyo. Gnania kakaesa moyo, yudzi-ni-pa tu. Nimbo uneza moyo, A hymn has measured, reached, the heart. Atu a ki kala angi.
  **Esana,** or **Ezania,** *v. ref.*, to measure one another. Hudziesana, hu-karakara; Hudziesana, hiyu ni mure.
  **Eseka.** *See* Kirobo.
  **Esera,** *v.d.* and *instr.* Gnania msiku ndiye aye-hu-esera niumba hiso, si karakara. Nindakudza machero-ni-ku-esere niumbayo. Ndzo uka-ni-esere niumba, u-ni-hendere musirero, nidzimbire kivesa.
  **Eserana,** *v. reit.* Nidzi-a-siya, anaeserana niumba.
  **Eserua, Ezerua,** *v.p.* Yunaeserua niumba.
  **Esua,** *v.p.*, to be reached—said of the heart. Yudziesua moyo ni nduguye. Der., Cheso; Muesi.
**Ere, Aere, Ari,** *verb. prefix.* *See* Fumukana; Muanemuane. Imp. of A; Chere, Kiere, Kaere, Yuere, etc. Ari (= Alikua in Kij.), a neg. termination. Kahendera. Possibly in a few verbs, Niemere, Rere, Segere, and Kere (= Kij., Ali). Akamba ere akirima na miulo.
**Ere,** *n.* (pl. Maere). *See* Muesa. A kind of grain, millet.
**Ere,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), udder. Dim., Kaere; Kiere.
**Erefuka,** *v.n.* (= Lacha; Kig., Ku iwa), to be clever, cunning.
  **Erefusa,** *v.a.* (in Kig., Ku manidzia). Prov., U-muerefu muno, unaerefusa kidzinga.
**Eremera, Erekezera, Erera,** *v.n.*, to weigh down upon, to press upon, to contract, pinch. Chuo hiki kinaeremera muyawe.
  **Eremerana,** *v. reit.*, to press upon one another. Na ona ahoho arere adziere-merana tandala andaye kuka akaeremera muyawe-andayekuka akaeremera muyawe.
  **Eremesa,** *v.a.*, to cause to press upon. Yudzi-mu-eremesa m'ana musigo mubomu, kanda-u-fisa, una-m-lumisa.
  **Eruka,** *v.*, to ascend. Yupiga mbidzui, yudzieruka madzini. Uina hiu unaeruka, This hole goes upwards. Pongo idzieruka.
**Erera, Eresa,** etc. *See* Era; Kidzimbuiriri.
**Eria.** *See* Ria.
**Eruve,** *adj.*, white; (K.) coral.
**Esa, Esania, Esera.** *See* Era.
**Eshima,** *n.* (ya). *See* Lorera; Ishima. Honour; present given in honour of anybody, or in acknowledgment of services rendered.
**Evera,** *v.a.* (Eba in Kij.), to avert a blow, an arrow, etc., to turn aside, to avoid.
  **Evula,** *v.a.*
  **Evulua,** *v.p.* Uevulue, wari. *See* Hokoha.
  **Evurira,** *v.d.*

## F.

**F.,** the sixth letter of the alphabet, often confused with *v.*—[ED.]
**Fa** (Kij.), *v.n.* *See* Vindi; Muzungu; Kunso. To be of use. Nahenda neno hiri, rifae, hebu risifae. Muana ni-mu-hensaye ni hiyu, osi ni anangu tu, ela ka-ni-fa dza hiyu.
**Faira** (?).
**Fana.** Maneno higa ka-ga-dza fana.
  **Fania,** *v.a.*, to make, to mend. Hudzifania maneno higa, ela ka-ga-ka fanika. Hudzihenda utu hiu, ela ka-u-ka hendeka.
  **Fanika,** *v.n.*
  **Fanikira,** *v.d.* Utu hiu yudzi-u-fania-ela ka-uka-mu-faniki ra. Nidziamba ni fanie utu hiu, ela ka-uka-ni-fanikira.
  **Fanira,** *v.d.* Nidzi-mu-fanira neno hiri-hata ridzi-mu-fanikira.
  **Fanirana** (Kir.), *v. reit.* (= Ku faniana in Kij.). *See* Fanirua; Kilinge. Atu hia anapatana anafanirana utuwao. Atu hio kabadana kabisa, hata muyawe akikala yundzialumira, kafanirana. Kuna, or, Yudzi lumira.
  **Fanisa,** *v.a.* Gnania musiku yudzifanisa maneno higo hata gadzifana. Kir., Yudzierekesa maneno higo hata dzadzierekera kuamba si iye kudza, atu hio angalumisana muno.
  **Fanisika,** *v.n.*, to succeed, to prosper, to prove successful. Maneno higa gadzifanisika (= gadzikuenda karakara). Utu hiu ka-u-ka fanisika kuani atu kahensi. Maneno higa hunda-ga-fania-hata gafanisike.
**Fafira,** *n.*, a glutton. Ugeri a kua ku.
**Faga** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Fumaga in Kir.; Rasa in Kins.). *See* Fuaga. To shoot.
**Fahali,** *n.* (pl. Ma-) (= Afiere), elders, valiant men.
**Faida, Faitha,** *n.*, silver, money, sufficiency.
**Fana.** *See* Fa.
  **Fania.** *See* Fa.
  **Fanika.** *See* Fa.
  **Fanira.** *See* Fa.
  **Fanisa.** *See* Fa.
**Fancho, Fuancho,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Chenene in Kid.), a kind of cricket, eaten by the Wanika. It burrows in the ground, and only comes out during the night to seek for its food. Machira ga dziloni akafugula midzanga, akasundula, akakuenda dzuma; akamala basi akauka, akakudza uinani, akaengira; akasindika, akagandisa. Madira ga dziloni akafugula midzanga, akasundula, akaupuka, akarira; akimala ku rira, akaenenda dzuma; akamala basi akauya, akakudza uinani, akaingira-akasindika-akagandisa. Uinawe una madano; uina umenga wenda mundani, umenga wenda mudzini alalavo, or, kuratu alalako. Fancho rinafula, or, yunafula-ela burare kafula.
**Fara,** *n.*, a measure, a brim. Bima kunsa fara. Bima kavu fara. Buma kikahana fara. Bumaikale karakara na mukungo. Ubume-ela isi muagike, etc.; usiidzase dele mudzuri, etc.
**Faraga,** *n.* *See* Mfugnia. Privacy, secrecy.
**Faranga,** *n.* *See* Fa; Fasa. Dim., Kafaranga.
**Farasi** (Kij.), *n.*, a horse. Munemo wangu na farasi-wangu, mu-ni-dakire, wa ku rinda kihichangu.
**Fasa,** *adj.*, doubtful. Gnania

**Fe** (Kig.) (= Ge in Kir.).
**Feda** (= Fetha).

**Feida,** *n.* *See* Faida; Faitha. Gain, profit.
**Fesafesa.** Kie-dzi-fesafesa.
**Fetha** (Kij.), *n.* (ra, pl. za), silver.
**Fewa.** *See* Fuewa; Fua.
**Fiaha,** *v.n.*, to be pregnant. Gnombe hino idzifiaha, ina mimba, ere ridziyaya.
**Fiahika,** *v.n.* (= Ku fopala), to shrivel. Kififiro kinafiahika, peho ikila. Ere ridzifiahika, The udder has shrivelled; not Ridzifopala.
**Fiakadza** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku henda fidina in Kir.), to make mischief, to set at enmity, to stir up strife.
**Fiakadzi,** *n.* (ya and za), instigation of enmity and strife.
**Fiala,** *v.a.*, to beget, to bear.
  **Fialukisa** (Kid.) (= Lavukisa in Kir.).
  **Fialusa,** *v.a.* *See* Mufiasi.
  **Fiarira.** Anae wa-a-fiarira haraka haraka, dza kuamba anadirua. Ku-m-fiarira mutu uniama. Ela ano gnania ana choya, e! chiramuko adzidzukula migande migande ya uvolue, adzi-i-fidza; vano huenenda, fua hata hunauya, huna ocha, koe, basi ao aka-hu-fiarira uniama, uka-mu-dzukirirua, kuamba akate niama, arie migande yao ya uvolue.
  **Fiarirua,** *v.p.*
**Fiasa,** *v.a.*, to dry, on a stone put over a fire, for the purpose of pounding. Especially used of grain not quite ripe. When dried in the sun Ku anika is used. Kalanga is to fry, to roast, as in making ndodore, to scorch.
**Fiasa,** *v.a.*, to gripe (?). Ku-m-fiasa mutu. Muhana hiu-u-ka-fiasika to, uchari muidzi. Ka-u-ka-kola moho; or, Ku ka-u koza moho.
  **Fiasira,** *v.d.* Madzira gana wengu.
**Fialo,** *n.* (ra), (1) the womb. Nalumua hivano fialoni.
(2) Trop., the nature, disposition, one is born with; but only used in a very limited manner, when a defect is to be noticed. Ni fialore-anae kasikira, It is her womb, her children are disobedient; *i.e.* owing to the mother. Ni fialoro kundahenda akili; kahi wala-vi we? nduguso ni adzo, a-peho; or, Ni fialoro hiro kusikira, si fio ana akalafio, It is thy own nature that, *i.e.* it is not from me, that thou art disobedient, etc. Ni fialorao-anao kasikira, It is their own nature, their children are disobedient. Der., Mfiala; Mufiasi; Kifialo; Kifiarira; Kifiasi.
**Fidina, Titina,** (1) *n. abstr.* (ya, ya). *See* Madumaini; Bekeda; Sadikira; Muthalimu. Enmity, hatred. Ku henda fitina, To cause enmity.
(2) *n. concr.*, one who causes enmity, stirs up strife. The preformative Mu is some-

## [PDF Page 92 — Dictionary Page 79 (Fid — Fig)]

  times employed. *See* Mufitina. Mutu hiye ni fitina; pl. Atu hio ni fitina (!).
**Fidina, Titina,** *v.a.* *See* Madumaini; Sadikira; Muthalimu. To set at enmity. Gnania yudzi-ni-fitina, kuamba niriwe malu. Gnania ndiye afitinaye atu (= afiakadzaye).
  **Fidinua, Fitinua,** *v.p.*, to be set at enmity. Muche hiye-angauka, akahenda fitinua.
**Fidini, Fitini,** *n.* (= Fitina). This form of the word belongs more to the Wadigo and Wajomba.
**Fidio,** *n.* Uganga wa fidio Uganga wa lumfo.
**Fidisa** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Ku diha in Kir.). Obs.
**Fidza,** *v.a.* *See* Sasira. To hide, conceal, keep secret from any one. Madzere ganafidza kuku, The Indian corn hides the fowl. Nifidza, nalonda ku ulagua, Thou art hiding, I want to say good-bye. Yudzi-ni-fidza neno hiro; kaka-ni-ambira, Thou dost hide this matter from me; thou dost not tell me. Ku-dzi-fidza mvula, To take shelter from rain.
  **Fidzana,** *v. ref.*, to keep secret from one another. Atu hio anafidzana maneno kaambirana, Those men kept the words from one another; they told not each other. Atu hio anapatana sana kafidzana neno ra muao ndani, These men agree well; they keep no matter secret of what is within.
  **Fidzania,** *v. reit.*, to hide one another. Atu hio anafidzania asapata dzambo (= asipate dzambo), Those men hide one another, lest they should get into trouble.
  **Fidzika,** *v.n.*, to be hidden. Mutu hiye kafidzika yunafidzua ye yuna-dzi-zumbula.
  **Fidzira,** *v.* *See* Kihenso.
  **Fidzirana,** *v. reit.*
  **Fidzua,** *v.p.*, to be hidden.
**Fiehana** (Kid.), *v. reit.*, to throng.
**Fiela,** *v.* *See* Mfiela.
**Fiera,** *v.a.*, to sweep.
  **Fierera,** *v.a.*, to scold. But Fiera is to sweep.
  **Fiererana,** *v. reit.*, to scold each other.
  **Fierereka,** *v.n.* *See* Fialo; Mafiasi; Ufiasi; Muanafiale. Mutu hiye na-mu-ogova kafierereka.
**Fieta** (Kid.), *v.a.*, to press, to crush, to push. Uka-ni-fieta muani (= Kir., Uka-ni-sukuma we). Lola kasi-udzi-ki-fieta, hata kidzi humbuka.
  **Fietana,** *v. ref.* (= Hofiana; Gandamisana; Sukumana), to press one another.
**Fifia** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku rusha in Kij., and Ku chekula in Kir.), to winnow, to blow about. Ku fifia muha ma.
  **Fifira,** *v.n.* *See* Kulukira. Nguo yangu idzififira, idzikala mbidzo.
  **Fifira,** *v.a.*, to blow. Nidziingirua ni kifusi dzidzoni-ni-fifira. Ku fifira moho. Nilonda moho? Resp., Moho ka-u-dza kota, ka-u-dza gurira; ka-u-dza aka, nafifira kuaha (= ku ansa, ni kere fifira ni chari fifira. Prov., Pania yuria akififira). Dzusi wahala kitu-changu, ku-ni-rivire; na dzu-si-ukihala kitu kua gnania musiku, kurivire; rero kaviri unadza londa deni kuangu; be kumania kuamba: Pania yuria akififira; mbona na we unakasa muno. Be rero kundapata, muiri udziingira uzungu. Lolo ridzielefuka.
**Figa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Fignia,** *v.n.* (= Ku-lukove; Ku chala). *See* Lola; Kigungu; Muadza. To beckon, wink, nictate, to blink, to jam. Ku fignia madzo, To shut the eyes.
  **Fignira,** *v.d.* Ku-m-fignira madzo, To blink to any one, To wink with the eyes. Yudzi-ni-fignira

*Footer: 79*

---

## [PDF Page 93 — Dictionary Page 80 (Fig — Fin)]

  madzo, He winked with his eyes to me. Yudzi-ni-fignira midzidzo (midzidzo = madzo).
  **Fignirana,** *v. reit.*, to wink at one another.
  **Figniala,** *v.n.* Mugasija udzignolua hikara, makodzage kagadza-figniala. Muhi hiu ukafua, makodzage gadzifigniala. Dzua ni ringi, madzere gadzifigniala.
  **Fignianga.** *See* Finianga.
**Fignia,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), prepuce. Muvunga ku fignia.
**Figo.** *See* Fuigo.
**Fiho.** *See* Fuiho.
**Fika,** *v.n.*, to reach, to arrive.
  **Fikika,** *v.n.* *See* Manisika.
  **Fikira,** *v.n.* (= Shogoda; Guira). *See* Funsikira; Kathia. To attain, to take hold of. Udzifikira vi we? Resp., Nidzifikira niumba ya Abe-Gunja. Prov., Nioka aluma afikirevo.
  **Fikirana,** *v. reit.* *See* Sengererana. To take hold of each other.
  **Fikirika,** *v.n.* *See* Gunika. Ni vare-ka-va-fikirika.
  **Fikirira.** (K.) incur, refer; and Fikirirana, relatively. Yudzifikirira-vi? Resp., Yudzifikirira kutu kusiku.
  **Fisa, Fisha,** *v.a.* *See* Ufiasi; Ludzaga; Ansana. (K.) accompany, to further. Ku-m-fisa mbere. Ela wa fisa? Resp., Nafisa kua Abe-Gunja, niki-mu-va. Muche hiyu yudzifisa (= Yu vevi na ku fiala).
  **Fisha,** or **Fisa,** *v.a.* *See* Uaki.
  **Fisika,** *v.n.* Mutu iye kafisika chanse, hu-m-sike vavo avofua.
  **Fisira,** *v.d.* Unda-m-fisira hebudze? A-sindafika mino hiko.
**Fikidza,** *v.a.* (= Vogodza in Kir.; Fikicha in Kij.; Fikisa in Kins.), to rub between the thumb and fingers, to crumble.
**Filisa** and **Filisi** (Kij.), *v.a.* (in Kir. proper, Ku dingania). *See* Badilisa. To seize goods and sell them for debt, to distrain.
**Fimba, Vimba,** *v.a.*, to cover over, to enclose so as to make invisible, to palm. Ku vimba niumba, To roof a house with makuti palm leaves. Ku vimba pia niumba; or, Ku fimbia luvia. Ku vimba uso, To cover the face. Ku vimba milomo, To shut the lips. Ku vimba konde; lit. To clench a fist. Maneno ga ku vimba, Covert language.
  **Fimbafimba,** *v. reit.* *See* Chalamu.
  **Fimbana,** *v.*, to symbolize.
  **Fimbika,** *v.n.*
  **Fimbira,** *v.d.* (= Kua kuria; Kunoa), with food and drink; (K.) surfeit.
**Fimbo,** *n.* *See* Nsimo. Neno ra fimbo; lit. A word of enclosure, a parable.
**Fimira** (?).
**Finama,** *v.*, to lie down.
  **Finamira,** *v.d.*, to lie on. Ku finamira moyo, To lie on one's heart; or, Ku finamira mimba (= Ku hambalala).
**Finanga,** *v.a.*
**Fingilika,** *v.n.* (= Fulumuka), to roll.
  **Fingilisa,** *v.a.* (= Fulumusa), to roll.
**Fingi,** *n.* *See* Dumania; Nudzira. Doubt, uncertainty, hesitation. Fingi ni kukahasa kira-tu kitu, mayo kahensi.
**Finia.** *See* Fignia.
**Finianga** and **Fignianga,** *v.a.*, to crush; (K.) quash, contuse. Ku-dzi-finianga na iwe. Nafiniangua ni iwe, lukombe lukauka, nidzihenda kironda cha chala.
  **Finiangika,** *v.n.* Idzebua, idzifiniangika, ka-i-na luaya, It has fallen and has been dashed to pieces, it has no large sherd. *See* Miungu.
**Finika,** *v.a.* (= Binikiza), to cover.
  **Finikira.** Ku-dzi-finikira nguo (= Ku-dzi-kutira nguo = binikiza).

## [PDF Page 94 — Dictionary Page 81 (Fin — Fio)]

  **Finikisa,** *v.a.* (= Binikiza).
  **Finikiro,** *n.* (ra), a large jar for keeping water.
**Finingi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Firigisi in Kij.), the gizzard; (K.) the stomach. Finingi ra kuku, The gizzard of a fowl.
**Finiongola,** *v.a.* (= Fioniongola?). *See* Fuiha. To squeeze, to crumble, to crush. Nafiniongola lukue, luhendedza, ni hungire ushanga.
**Fio, Vio.** *See* Nioniosa; Dzukisa; Kibimo; Luuso; Koso; Maongo; Kutula; Miaso; Ganira; Oha; Clafio; Enderera. *A particle used in composition with* ga, vi, cho, yu, na, si, etc., which. Ndivio, Which are (= yes). Sivio, Which are not (= no). Ndo, a-vio gomba. Ndi-vio, a-dzo-vio gomba. Unakolola muhama, ka-u-chari mudzanga vio? You pluck off Guinea-corn, but is it not still unripe as it is? Resp., Ah be sindakolola, ela nikakute nihofune. Be ku bananga muhama vio? Ka-u-chari mudzanga vio? Resp., Ah-mubananga chakue, kana kondo. Mainsi gagnierera vio niama ika henda mabulu akadzigaula aka kala mainsa.
**Fioda,** *v.a.*
**Fioda,** *n.*, pods, cobs.
**Fioga,** *v.a.*, to tread, to tread upon. Udzi-ni-fioga ge! Resp., A-sika-ku-ona Shaha, shambe dzi-ku-uchirira ndugu yangu. Nidzi-ku-fioga-be ukifiogua unani, basi idzikala kondo? I tread upon thee indeed! thou art trodden upon by whom? Well, seek not a quarrel. Gnombe iki-ku-fioga, wamba, idzi-ni kunula, or, gaula, kikonde; nelai idzi-ni-lumisa, ela ka-ika ni kuniula. Ku fioga kua ala, To trample upon.
  **Fiogana,** *v. reit.*, to tread upon one another.
  **Fiogeka,** *v.n.* Dzua ridzikola dzi, ka-ku-fiogeka.
  **Fiogua,** *v.p.*, to be trodden upon. Udzi-ni-fioga ge! Resp., Hata ukafiogua-unda-ni-henda dze? Kuna utu wa ku henda, Dost thou tread upon me? Reply, Even thou trodden upon, who has done it? No one has done it to thee; said in a kondo, quarrel.
**Fioka,** *v.n.* (= Hara in Kij.), to be loose, relaxed in one's bowels, to have dysentery.
  **Fiokodza,** *v.c.*, to cause diarrhœa.
**Fiola,** *v.a.*, to scold.
  **Fiolana,** *v. ref.*, to scold one another.
  **Fioreka,** *v.n.*, to be relaxed.
  **Fiorera,** *v. rel.*, to scold for; (K.) blame, rebuke.
  **Fiorerana,** *v. reit.*, to rebuke one another.
  **Fiosa,** *v.a.* Chakuria hiki kina-ni-fiosa. Kunsui ina fiosa. Der., Mafioka; Mafiolo; Mafiorerano; Mafiorero; Mafiosi.
**Fiola,** *v.a.* *See* Mudzala. To cut through. Ku fiola niama, To cut through an animal. Yudzifiola niama bomu, akakuenda nacho, He cut through a large animal, and it went its way. Ku fiola muhama, To cut millet; *i.e.* to cut off the heads in reaping. Ku fiola masuche, To hurt by words. Yudzi-ni-fiola neno, ka-ri-ndala moyoni muangu; nindafua na-ro ku-ri-asa. Yudzi-ni-chegnia na neno ri.
  **Fiolana,** *v. reit.*, to cut through one another.
  **Fiorera,** *v. rel.* Udzi-m-fiorera niama bomu nawe.
  **Fiosa,** *v.a.*, to cut through the throat. Ku fiosa kidzoa, To cut off the head. Ku fiosa mbuzi, To kill a goat by cutting his throat. The throat is cut from ear to ear in slaughtering animals.
  **Fiosera,** *v. rel.* Ndzo u-ni-fiosere kuku, Come, kill for me a fowl.

## [PDF Page 95 — Dictionary Page 82 (Fio — Fiu)]

  **Fiosua,** *v.p.*, to be killed by having the throat cut.
**Fiolo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a butcher; lit. a cutter. Enenda to, muna mafiolo, gasa ku dunga. Mania! muna mafiolo, gasa ku dunga.
**Fioma,** *v.a.*, to read.
  **Fiomeka,** *v.n.*, to be read.
  **Fiomera,** *v. ref.*, to be read for, or to.
  **Fiomesa,** *v.c.*, to cause to read, to teach.
**Fiombera,** *v.* (= Paraga, Kij.). Ku kuea mti kua mikono na magu, To climb a tree with the hands and feet.
**Fioni, Vioni** (Kid.), *n.* (= Rogo in Kir.).
**Fioniongola.**
**Fionsa,** *v.a.* *See* Mumunia. To sip, suck, smack, soak. Ku fionsa mdzusi. Yunabanda misosa, akafionsa.
**Fiosa.** *See* Fiola.
**Fira, Vira,** *v.n.*, to prove barren, unproductive. Muhama wangu udzifira, My millet is unproductive. Muhama wa ku fira (= Usio tembe ela kimo kidzidimira). Mutu huya unga-mu-ona aka akafira dza munama (kana niumbaye, kana muchewe, kana chakuriache-ni mutu wa ku sunguluka du), basi ndiye a-ambuaye akafira, This man whom you see is barren of millet; as to his house, as to his wife, as to his food, he is a man who just idles about. Well it is said of him, akafira, he is barren. Mutu huya, viratu unga-mu-ona akafira; ni mukaha kana munda wala kana muche, ndo kufira kuko.
  **Firira,** *v.d.*
  **Firuka,** *v.n.*, to whirl, to become angry. Mukasa gnania akafiruka kua mulume we nidziamba ni due atu hio ela moyi udzi ni firuka ka ukahenza. Moyo udzi-ni-firuka, ndzipigana nao.
  **Firusania,** *v. reit.*, to provoke one another. Adzifirusania, adzidana.
**Fira,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*; also ra, pl. Mafira, ga), the name of a species of serpent. Fira ni ku sororeka, basi na ku ima kisiku cha kidzoa, aka ku, dzuvira mahe; or, Fira rikilonda ku-m-dzuvira mutu mahe, ri ku sororeka basi na ku imisa kidzoa, rikadzuva mahe. Fira rinadzalakasa, kuamba ridzuve mahe.
**Firangi,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Mbuba in Kij.), a kind of itch; (K.) measles. Muana hiyu yudzihenda firangi. Firangise ka-zi-dza-vola.
**Firangignandu,** *n.* *See* Mbanga. (K.) Firi blot.
**Firinga,** *v.a.* (in Kij., to be and to make round). Ku firinga machembe midiri ma vidanga. Jembe hiri ka-ri-na mufiringo. Musana ka-ri-firingire to. Jembe hiri ri-firinge kari firingirue to.
  **Firingira,** *v.r.*, to make round for. Uwe musana jembe hiri ka-ri-firingirue to, be ni-firingira to.
  **Firingirua,** *v.p.*, to be made round for. Jembe hiri ka-ri-firingirue to. Musana hiyu ni madzifundi, kaza, mania to ka-ri-kafiringua to.
  **Firingua,** *v.p.*, to be made round.
**Firingania.** *See* Viringania.
**Firu,** *n.* (pl. Mafiru), a fruit.
**Fisa,** *v.a.* *See* Fika.
  **Fisika.**
**Fisa.** *See* Fira. (In Kid., Dumbi hiri ni fisa; pl., Madumbi mfisa.) Der., Mfiza.
**Fisi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the hyena. Kiravo cha fisi. Prov., Fisi rikiria mukongo, nawe muzima sindika niumba to.
**Fitina** and **Fitini.** *See* Fidina and Fidini. Strife, mischief.
**Fiufia** (Kid. ?), *v.a.*, to remove. Ku fiufia kondo kua uganga, To remove a quarrel by witch-
