## [PDF Page 96 — Dictionary Page 83 (Fiu — Fom)]

  craft. Ku fiufia ivu (kua muhaso).
**Fiuka** and **Fiukira.** *See* Fiula.
**Fiula,** *v.a.*, (1) to remove, to take out of the way. Kitu hiki kinchirani, ki-fiule kanda, This thing is in the way; move it on one side. Ninga-ki-fiula kanda, ela kavana makalo, be simania ndafio ki-henda. Pania hiyu yuna muka-m-fiuleni kanda, This cat has a smell; remove it out of the way.
(2) Ku fiula luhamba, hebu luembe. Nidzi-lu-fiula, ela ka-lu-ka guira. Be ka-luria basi.
(3) Trop., to shock, to offend. Mutu hiye yudzi-ni-fiula moyo, sintakuenda kaviri kuakue. Maneno mai adza-go-amba, be gadzi-ni-fiula moyo. (K.) Ku-m-fiula moyo, irritate.
  **Fiuka,** *v.n.*, to go off, to start aside, to be far from. Muhambo udzifiuka, The trap is gone off—said when nothing has been caught; but when an animal is caught, they say, Muhambo udziguira. Yudzifiuka navi, naye huere hosi? Yudzifiuka na nchira i vi o? Resp., Simania adzovofiuka. Maneno mai nagafiuke. Madzo nagadze-mai nagafiuke; said at a kiravo. Nidziona utu hio be moyo udzi-ni-fiuka nidziamba hubigane. Nidziona wari-ka-u-ka ni hamira moyo udzi-ni-fiuka.
  **Fiukafiuka,** *v. reit.*, to stagger, to reel as one who is drunk. Ku fiukafiuka nchirani.
  **Fiukira,** *v. rel.*, to go off for, to lead astray. Simania nchira adzio fiukira, or, adzayofiukira, I do not know by which way he went off.
  **Fiurira,** (1) *v.d.*, to remove a thing to or for another. Mu-fiurire muyao miya-achire to. To stroke to or for another. Luembe hilu u-ni-fiurire; nidzi-lu-fiula, ela ka-lu-kaguira-be ka-luria basi.
  (2) *v.n.*, to pass on crouching without shaking the grass. Yudzichira navi nawe uvava-kuka-mu-ona? Resp., Sika-mu-ona akidugusa niasi; batu simania chamba yudzihenda fiurira; or merely, batu yudzihenda fiurira; or, labuda yudzihenda fiurira.
**Fiusa,** *v.a.*, to let off, as a trap. Yudzifiusa muhambo wangu kasidi, na kuamba ka fiusire, niama angakuenda guirua, kuani yudzichira na vavo. Metaph., Maneno mai, fiusa muiri.
  **Fiusira,** *v. rel.* Si chire na hivo, uka-ni-fiusira muhambo wangu nidzihega, or, nidza-o-hega. Der., Kifiu; Lufiusa; Mafiari; Mufiu.
**Fo, Vo** (= Mfo?). Mufo unachira fo (Kid.).
**Fo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mafo). Nini hiri? Resp., Ni fo. Ni fo nidzihunda riri menga, ela mangine ni maidzi, kaga-dza-ifua. Riro fo, That fo; pl. Gago mafo.
**Fognafogna,** *v.n.* *See* Kotola. To be eager to devour. Yunaria ku fognafogna, yuna moyo, He is eating greedily; he has a mind for devouring all.
**Fogoda** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Shokoda), to poke, poke into.
**Fomola,** *v.a.* (= Ku famula; Ku dzamula), to demolish.
  **Fomoka,** *v.n.* *See* Pombolo; Fumuka. To decay, to go to ruin, to fall down. Niumba yangu ya kaya idzifomoka, My house in the kaya is gone to ruin, hata fiho sidzibanangika. Kivinda changu kifomoka, My shed is gone to ruin.
  **Fomorera,** *v.d.*, to demolish to or for another. Mutu hiyu yudzi-ni-fomorera niumba

*Footer: 83*

---

## [PDF Page 97 — Dictionary Page 84 (Fop — Fu)]

  yangu; or, Yukudza ni-fomorera niumba yangu. This happened especially when one built his hut on the chansa of another in the kaya.
**Fopala,** *v.n.*, to shrivel. Mahombo gadzifopala (= gadzifiahika, and, gadzikala mikunso mikunso) masia gadzisira. Kififiro kikafopala. Mabalazi hiu ukafopala; hata uka-si-chita, ka-zi-hama; ka-zi-ifua; zinga dza kuamba, zikahundua dzanga, zikaniauka.
**For'dani,** or **Forodani, Forothani,** *n.*, the custom-house of Mombas. Hudzienenda Kisiwani, basi hudzidzembera hata hadzifika forodani kua Zete.
**Forodani.** *See* For'dani.
**Foro,** *n.* (wa and ra, pl. a and ga), the zebra. Foro ni kama nsoya, muiri we unga nsoya, ela urembo we wa ndzora ndzora ndio udzoa-m-dingania, ku kala luakue. Maforo higara ganarisa, Yonder zebras are grazing. The pl. Maforo seems more in use than Fora hia.
**Foroforo,** *adj.* (= Kij., Kusurukusuru). *See* Lani. Clumsy, bungling, awkward. Gnania yudziaka niumba i foroforo. Gnania yudzidzonga mifui, ela ka-i-hama i foroforo. Gnania yudzifuma kavu, ela i foroforo. Gnania yudzikotera kifiu, ki-foroforo. Gnania yudzidzonga muvini, u-foroforo. Gnania kaidima ku fuma nguo dzongonene-kufumakue ku foroforo. Rero kuforoforo. Kakuna, dzua, wala kakuna mfula dzi i foroforo, or, irungurungu. Kurimako ku foroforo. Kugema ko ku foroforo. Be ni ndimua yani ino irio foroforo. Be ni maneno gani go yunagomba maneno ga foroforo. Gnania kaidima ku saga ku saga kuakue, yunabandabanda, ungawe yudzi-u-valasa ufurufuru ku sagakue ku foroforo.
**Foromoka, Voromoka,** *v.n.* (= Fumbuluka, when animals are spoken of), (1) to tumble, to flounder.
(2) To start suddenly. Yuforomoka gopueni yudzebua yudzihemuka. Ai! waforomoka munazini-akifulula mbulu. *See* Fulula. Ndzoni porepore vana mabopo-mudzidze foromoka; or, mudzidze mukaforomoka; Kid., mudzidze; in Kir., musidze.
  **Foromosa,** *v.a.*, to cause to flounder.
  **Foromosana,** *v. reit.*, to tumble each other. Dzerani-msaforomosana; or, Msiforomosane.
  **Foromosania,** *v. reit.* (= Foromosana). Dzerani-msaforomosania mkabua; or, Msiforomosanie.
  **Foromoseka,** *v.n.*, to be thrown down. Lukuni hilu ludziangama-ka-lu foromoseka.
  **Foromosera,** *v.d.* (U)si-ni-foromosere mawe ge unda-ni-piga. Si-ui-foromosere ge unda-ni-piga.
**Foya, Voya,** *v.a.*, to beg.
  **Foyana,** *v. reit.*, to beg of or from one another.
  **Foyeka,** *v.n.* Ni mutu yuya tu huya, yunafoyeka kitu? Resp., Ai yunafoyeka, uki-m-foya ni-ku-ku-va. A be kuamba munapatana, be nda uka-ni-fo yere, mimi ka-ni-pa.
  **Foyera,** *v.d.* and *instr.*, to beg with another. Nda uka-m-foyere muanangu mboga, adze aririre wari. Nadzukula kitu hiki-n'ende kua gnania msiku nikafoyere mbiu.
**Fu.** *See* Fuo (pl. Mufuo).
**Fu, Vu,** *adj.* *See* Koloma. Root-word of Mufu, Mafu, Kifu, etc. Rotten, dead, meat which has died. Niamafu ya ku a nika. Ni pfu-ni kama i ka yo fua. Ka ria fu, He or

*Footer: 84*

---

## [PDF Page 98 — Dictionary Page 85 (Fu — Fua)]

  she eats not dead flesh, *i.e.* of an animal which died of itself. In Kir. proper such flesh is called kombo. Nazifu nazi, Rotten cocoa-nuts. Madzere mafu, Bad Indian corn. Muhama mufu, Bad millet. Uchi ufu, Bad toddy. *See* Uchi.
**Fu.** *See* Mafufufu.
**Fua.** Vidziamba fua-ku mera (vidzimera to).
**Fua,** *v.n.* *See* Ziana; Thalimu; Kima. To die. Trop., to go off, to be sold. Kitu hiki ka-thi-fua hivio. Minazi yangu idzefua lua mudzana. *See* Kungurira. Kufua madzo. *See* Kigungu. Gnania akafua, masikiro, kasikira. Mutu hiyu akafua madzo, kaona ni mudzofi wa madzo. Kitu hicho ki-fua dze kimache? Kuamba si yuyu, ningere nidzefua. Yudzifua kua sababu yangu, Died for me. Ku ni henza mimi-ku ni kombola mimi; or, Yudzifua vatuangu, ningavofua mimi; also, Wafua kua hali kangu.
  **Fuerera.** *See* Hulukisa. (K.) Umiru udzi-mu-fua idzui, hoarse. Kudzifuerera miladzo. Akaye fua kari, be kakuna viruba viiri. (K.) Uriri wa, ku fua, death-bed.
  **Fuererana.** Nidzifiniangua ni iwe, vadzifuererana miladzo, or, muladzo. Hosini hu lukolo, ela vana fugo ra vevi afuereranao. Hu-lukolo ela kahufuererana. Der., Uferero wa, dzua.
  **Fuererua,** *v.p.*, to be killed. Mutu iye angakudza, ela yudzifuererua ni nduguye. Mukamba akifuererua ni atu, kadzama haraka, ela akifuererua ni gnombe, basi yudzidzama kare; angue: gnombe sangu sindasira.
  **Fuewa.**
  **Fuisa,** *v.a.* Wafiala ana ahahu-ela yudzifuisa osi, s'ambe ni mgumba, s'ambe for siambe. M'tum'che (= mutumuche) huya ni mfiasi, ela yunafuisa.
**Fua,** *v.n.* (= Fira (Kij., Fia) bumbala). *See* Kunsua. To back out of anything; to quail, to fail in resolution, to shrink, to recoil, to be restive. Ku henda uire (?). Ku fua ni kudza mania kitu, To fail in performing, To default. Kitu kisichobuma tembe, kikafua. Ivurangu-ridzifua-ridzehua-dzana rari rika kanagnana muno, rari rinaluma. Murenge hiu ukadieka marenge, ela gadzifua na mudzungu hiu wadieka vidzungu-ela vidzifua. Muhamawangu udzifua, ka-u-kabuma tembe.
  **Fuira,** *v.r.* Mutu hiyu yudzifua, yudzifira. Nidziamba nihende utu huno, ela udzi-ni-fuira. Der., Kifua (?).
**Fua,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the chest, chest-disease. Ku henda fua. Pula idzihenda kahe. Ku guirua ni fua ra kahe. Anangu ana-angu adzihenda mafua; or, ana mafua.
**Fua,** *v.a.*, to draw, beat, forge, to undress. Ku fua sui. N'enda nikafue sui, nikipata, nidze, ni-ku-ve. Fua rifua, It failed; said when blasting.
  **Fuika,** *v.n.* Hiva ka-va-fuika, vana kifua. Madzi, hangu dzana, gadzisoena, ganafuika.
  **Fuira,** *v.d.* and *instr.* *See* Chavu; Ludzadza. Kunsa hi uka-ni-fuire kala.
  **Fuirua,** *v.p.* Ludzadza lu-fuirua-lo kamba, An enclosure by which shrimps are caught.
**Fuadula,** *v.* *See* Kikuacha.
**Fuaga** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku fumaga in Kir.), to shoot, to kill by shooting.
  **Fuagafuaga.**
  **Fuagarika,** *v.n.*, to die away as fire; to become very lean, to

*Footer: 85*

---

## [PDF Page 99 — Dictionary Page 86 (Fua — Fue)]

  waste away. Moho udzifuagarika, unalonda ku fua. Gnania yudzionda, yudzifuagarika.
  **Fuagika,** *v.n.* (= Fumagika in Kir.), to admit of being shot. Mutu hiyu wafika kure, kafuagika.
  **Fualala,** *v.n.*, to die away, to cease burning, to subside. Moho udzifualala (= udzifuagarika). Niungu idzicheruka hata idzifualala (= hata idzirera).
**Fuala,** *v.a.*, to wear.
  **Fuarira,** *v. ref.* *See* Kakoa. Muambo wa ku fuarira nguo.
  **Fuika,** *v.a.* *See* M'adungo; Madzodzo; Fuiho. To put on.
  **Fuikira,** *v.* (= Mufuiko).
  **Fuira** (= Vua?). Der., Mafuiko.
**Fuanda,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Shudu in Kij.), the refuse left from the semsem when the oil is pressed out. Mafuanda ga ufuha, gasindikuago ni ngamira (= Kigodo in Kins.; Mavanda in Kij.) mafunda ra mihi, makodza dzu dovola fuo. Muhafunire muana mafuanda. Fuanda ra mbalazi ri na kundika muana ka idima ku miza.
**Fuando, Fuancho,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mafuancho), a kind of cricket.
**Fudi,** *n.* (= Kuafulo), surprisal, suddenness. Gnania yudzi-ni udulukisa na charo, nika-mu-amba: charo cha fudi ki-dze cho? usie-ni-ambira hangu dzana, nika-dzi-funga? uka-ni-ambira rero fudi, vi-dze fio? Nidziamba: n'ende Ruruma, ela H. yudzikudza, aka-ni-amba fudi. Ndzo, uka-ni-virike Duruma, basi nikaenenda. Be-chari charo cha fudi, ela sikarire nacho (Sikarire, neg. imperf. of Ku kala, I was not). Yudziguirua ni ukongo wa fudi, He has been attacked by a sudden illness. Utu wa fudi, An arrow of surprise.
**Fudia, Futia** (Kij.), *v.n.* (= Ku fuhira in Kir. proper), to wipe off, to seduce. Gnania yudzigula kitu ku fudia, yuhenda fuhira, si thorare ela yudzihenda gula ku fudia, It is not its bargain, its price. Kima. Yugomba ku-dzi-fudia, ku-dzi-va haki muegnie.
**Fudu,** *n.* (Kij., Fufu). *See* Mfudu. An eatable fruit of a tree; (K.) fun.
**Fudumadzi.**
**Fudunga** (Fudu ya unga).
**Fudza,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a small quantity left in a bag.
**Fudza,** *v.n.*, to leak.
  **Fudzira,** *v.*, to expel. Kirenge kidzifunsika uchi udzi-mu-fudzira. Niumba yangu niasi zikafumuka idzini fudzira usiku to.
  **Fudzirua,** *v.p.* *See* Wazimu. Nidzifudzirua to hata kudzecha kua niumba kudaruka, be nenda piga niasi, nidze nidzomekese tundu zi fudza-so.
**Fudzula,** *v.a.*, to pluck, to pluck asunder, deplume. Ku fudzula nioka. Hufudzule kuku hiyu, hugafie. Ku fudzula kifudza, opposed to Ku niola luvala.
  **Fudzulua,** *v.p.* Prov., Ku henzi ku niolua ulonda nu fudzulua. Hiyu kakahenza ku niolua. Yudzihenda fudzulua be, lole we kifudzu. Mudana angafudzulua kahenzi luvala kuani ka-zi-nda mera haraka za ku sigika na ku dzomeka muleli.
  **Fudzurira** (Kid.), *v.d.* (= Gniekurira in Kir.), to tear off to.
  **Fudzurirana** (Kid.), *v. ref.* Hufudzurirane kuku hiyu hugafie pia hosi.
**Fudzu,** *adj.* *See* Vudzu; Pudzu. Der., Kifudza.
**Fue,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Luanda. Fallow ground. Mafue gangu ni mahahu ukilonda, nika-ku-ve menga, urime.
**Fuemfere,** *n.*, sleepiness, drowsi-

*Footer: 86*

---

## [PDF Page 100 — Dictionary Page 87 (Fue — Fug)]

  ness, especially from the influence of the weather.
**Fuende,** *n.* (ra) (= Kondue; Uere; Rero), languor, dulness, heaviness, tardiness. Nasikira fuende rero, I feel languid, or heavy, to-day. Mutu hiyu yuna fuende sana, That man is very heavy, sleepy. Si hende fuende (= Sihende kondue), Do not be lazy. Fuende ni riro na ro.
**Fuera** (= Fuira). *See* Fua.
  **Fuerera.** *See* Fua.
  **Fuewa.** *See* Fua.
**Fuerera,** *v.*, to get accustomed to, or to accustom one's self to. Akifuerera kuku.
**Fufu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a thicket. Vara vana fufu, vakafungu, ka-va-vegnieka, or, ka-va-dirika. Nchira hino ina mafufu mafufu. Dim., Kafufu; Kifufu; magn., Rifufu (pl. Mifufu).
**Fufu, Vuvu,** *adj.* Root-word of Mufufu, Mifufu, Kifufu, etc. Sometimes pronounced Pfupfu. Worn out, rotten. Niumba yangu ni fufu. Ka-i-na makalo ga geri ga kuenerua muimui. Nguo hino m'fufu. Ka-i-na vana.
**Fufu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma- and Mi-), anything worn.
**Fufula,** *v.a.* (= Chindula), to quicken, reanimate, to resuscitate exhausted lands. Na-u-fufula munda wangu. Munda wangu nidzaoricha muaka dzana, na-u-fufula. Munda wangu nao u richa muaka dzusi-na-u-fufula, na-u-rima kaviri. Gnania msiku yukuenda fufula mina-siye-yere ika richua hangu dzusi, ela rera yunagema kaviri.
  **Fufuka,** *v.n.* *See* Pengo. To increase, to arise, revive. Munda wangu udzifufuka, udzikala munda basi, si vue kahiri. Minasi yangu idzifufuka hangu dzana, uchi udziuya wifio kamili kama mbere, My cocoa-nut trees have improved since yesterday; the toddy is quite equal to twice as much. Wari mkongo, ela hangu dzana yudzifufuka, yudzivola. Gnania wasimia moyo, ela wafufuka yuchere mukongo wifio. Yudzefua, ela yudzifufuka. Mulungu yudzi-mu-udza moyo.
**Fufuma,** *v.a.*, to surprise one. Kufufuma dzakadzaka, hata yukuenda guira nchira, To surprise one in the forest until he goes and finds the right way.
  **Fufumuka,** *v.n.* *See* Kimo. To be surprised. Muana hiyu yudzifialua nikara, ela yudzi-fufumuka, yudzihenda kimo, yudzikula, ela ni m'ana mdzanga, kafiarirue kare. Hiku ni muv'aha wangu, ela yudzi-ni-chira, kimo, yudzifufumuka.
**Fuga,** *v.a.* *See* Fuidza; Furura; Hua. To knead (in Kidigo, to stir in cooking = Chakana in Kir.). Ni-pani masia, ni nifuge wariwangu, Give me some milk, that I may stir it into my wari, cooked grain, rice, etc. Nidzi-mu muche hiyu yunafuga ulongo, aumbe niungu.
  **Fugafuga,** *v. reit.*, to mix thoroughly. Ku fugafuga wari na masia, To mix cooked rice and milk.
  **Fugira,** *v.d.* *See* Fua (Sui).
**Fuga, Vuga,** and **Vuka, Fuka,** *v.a.* (= Ku rera). *See* Mukari. To rear, to breed.
  **Fugika,** *v.n.*, to be reared. Niama hiye kafugika, ela hiku yunafugika.
  **Fugira,** *v.d.* *See* Hala. To rear, to bring up to, for. Na-m-fugira gnonsi-kukue, etc., I reared his sheep for him. Kuku hia u-ni-fugire, or, ni-fugira nta-kui-va lurero, Rear those chickens for me, I will give thee lurero—a

*Footer: 87*

---

## [PDF Page 101 — Dictionary Page 88 (Fug — Fuh)]

  proportion, percentage—of those reared.
  **Fugirana,** *v. reit.*, to rear for one another. Atu ni ku fugirana mufugo; ukisa fuga mufugo wa muyao, u mutu wani we? u mui.
  **Fugisa,** *v.a.*, to cause to rear, or bring up.
**Fuguka,** *v.n.* *See* Kukuhala. (1) To get unfastened, to get loose. Musigowangu udzifuguka-rindani nifunge. Mbusi hiyu lukuelue ludzifuguka. Mbusi, hiyuno hangudzana udzi fuguka muiriwe, yunarisa niasi.
(2) Trop., to get free, easy; said of the body. Waambadze muirio? Resp., A-Hangu dzana muiri udzi-ni-fuguka, napa'ta usinsisi-na-dzi-sikira to. Abe-Gunja muiriwe udzi-mu-fuguka rero, nikura ku henda baha mianso ya ku vola.
  **Fugula,** *v.a.*, to untie, to unfasten, to release. Nta ukafugule mbusi, ukarise, I will let the goats go, that they may graze. Nidzifugula lukue-ku sundula niumba. Niani adzaye-mu-fugula, nami nidzi-m-funga? Trop., *see* Mugomfi; Girida. Ndzo-ukafugule kasha.
  **Fugulana,** *v. reit.* Atu hia adzi fugulana, adzikimbira.
  **Fugurida** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Fugura; Fagurira; Fugurisa in Kir.).
  **Fugurika,** *v.n.* Nidziamba nifugule-ela ka-lu-fugurika, ludzi-ni-remesa.
  **Fugurira,** *v.d.* Nidziiha mutu yukudza-ni-fugurira.
  **Fugurirua,** *v.p.* Udzifugula m'egnie, hebu udzifugurirua?
  **Fugurisa,** *v.a.* (= Ku fugurisa kidonda). Nidzi-m-fugurisa kigongo, nidziamba ni-m-pige, ela nidzi-m-kosa. Yudzi-m-fugurisa kigongo, aka-m-piga. Na-m-fugurisa kigongo, ni-m-pige.
**Fugo,** *n.*, (1) (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Lukolo. Kindred, descendants from one female. Fugo rao ni menga, rila vamenga, anafuererana; wawesao ala ndani menga.
(2) (Kid.) (Fugo hiyi, pl. Fugo hisi). *See* Kibiga. A vessel for palm-wine, either of a large calabash or of a large earthen jar, used at festivities. Fugo ya muansani, ndio kigerochao abimiracho uchi yiingira viamangale viiri.
**Fugu, Fuku,** *n.*, bickerings, strife.
**Fuguda,** *v.a.*, (1) to blow as bellows.
(2) To throw with force so as to cause a wind, to hurl, to fling. Ku fuguda mifuo. Ku fuguda kigongo ukikala unapiga, kitu kama makoma, hebu mauyu.
  **Fugudira.** Der., Mufugudira.
  **Fugusa** (Kid. and Kij.), *v.* (= Ku sola in Kir.), to drive away, to chase.
  **Fugusika** (= Soreka in Kir.).
**Fuha,** *v.a.* *See* Polokania. To draw, to pull, to wipe; (K.) stroke. Ku fuha madzi—a proverbial expression, To draw water (= To act with cunning). Gnania yunafuha madzi (= Ni muerefu sana wa maneno). Suino hudziukuha, ela iye yuchari hensa kuria, be ndo huambavo ku amba; ei, yunafuha madzi. Ku fuha magulu, To draw the feet, to mark with the feet, as a way. *See* Rindika. Ima nichiri mbire ni ku fuhe magulu.
  **Fuhana,** *v. reit.* (= Gunsumana).
  **Fuhika,** *v.n.*, to be pulled, drawn.
  **Fuhira,** *v.* *See* Luana. To attract. Gnania yuuahensa muno ku gula kitu cha ku fuhira, kamania ukomawe; or, Kamania mathora, yuhenda fuhira.

## [PDF Page 102 — Dictionary Page 89 (Fuh — Fuk)]

  **Fuhuka,** *v.n.* *See* Gaansa; Madzimadzi; Taka; Kilongo; Kidolue. To wither, to dry.
  **Fuhusa,** *v.a.* *See* Dania. Ku fuhusa vilongo (= Ku lafia beridi). Mtumche hiyu kafuhusa muana. *See* Lukuso anae kafuhuka. Ku fuhusa manina.
**Fuhi,** *adj.*, short, with prefixes mu-, ki-, etc., Mufuhi, Kifuhi, etc.
**Fuidifuidi,** *adj.*, short and round. Mufuidifuidi, Kifuidifuidi, etc.
**Fuidza,** *v.a.* *See* Kuangurira. To stir by whirling the lufuidzo between the hands. Ku fuidza miladzo, isiguirane miniama miniama.
  **Fuidzika.**
  **Fuidzira** (= Chakamira wari). *See* Tharou; Lufuidzo; Fuidzo.
  **Fuidzo.**
**Fuignia,** *v.a.* (= Dignia); (K.) Ku fuignia lukombe, to pinch.
  **Fuignia,** *v.a.*, (K.) mock. Fuinira ku fuignia tulua.
**Fuigo,** *n.* (ya, za), the kidneys.
**Fuiha,** *v.a.* (= Valasa), to beat severely. Ku-lu-fuiha lukue, na ku-lu-finiongola, ku-lu-henda luvudzu. Meno ga lukue. Lukue lukidandauka, basi uka-lu-fuiha. Luvohe nidzi-lu-suka, ela si-dza-lu-fuiha. Navalasa lukue, kidza ni-lu-fuihe.
  **Fuihika,** *v.n.*
  **Fuihiwa,** *v.p.* *See* Menomeno.
**Fuiho** (often pronounced Pfuiho), *n.* (za), long sticks, such as are used in building huts. Pl. of Lufuiho.
**Fuika,** *v.a.* *See* Mufuiko; Risasi. (1) To dip into. Ku fuika fuko, kaha. Nidzifuika mbugu zangu madzini, kuamba siloame. Ku fuika nguo muirini. Ku fuika ngoma (= Ku amba ngoma). The latter is more frequently used.
(2) (= Ku-m-fuika msigo), to lade, to dress.
**Fuina,** *v.a.* and *n.*, to dance. Prov., Mufuina vi kaigua. Tulua inafuina.
**Fuindi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the knee. Ku piga; or, Ku muta mafuindi, To kneel.
**Fuira.** *See* Fua. (K.) ball?
**Fuira.** *See* Fua.
**Fuisa.** *See* Fua.
**Fuka,** *n. coll.* *See* Dzadza. The name of a species of weed.
**Fuka,** *v.a.* (= Ngirisira). *See* Fula. To sprout, to grow. Midzanga ina fuka fumbi. Muhama wangu udzi fuka; kaukamera kua mfula ku kala tembe, udzi upusa midze, ela udzifuka kua dzua ku kala ringi. Muhama wangu wamera, ela dzifuka ukua dzua.
  **Fukafuka.** Kuku hiyu yunafukafuka kuamba aoke. Kuku akioka, yunafukula midzanga akafukafuka (akahenda fukufuku-fukufuku).
**Fuka,** *n.*, a sprout, a shoot.
**Fuka,** *v.n.* *See* Fula. To cross, to ford. Ku fuka miho, To ford a river.
**Fukara,** *n.*, a term of abuse. Muche huya ni fukara; ka-dzi-sara mafuha, ni mkolo. Si muche, ni fukara ye!
**Fukiza,** *v.n.* (= Fula; Fuka), to perfume. Muche akifiala, nguose ni ku fukisua na ndago. Ku fukiza kirenge, To perfume a calabash. The wood of the following trees is used for the purpose: Muhepe, mudzala, murungu, mukuamba, mufumulandola. Ku ufumba. Ku kisuki. Ku fuko, kirenge, etc. Ku dzidzo.
**Fuku,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), an animal. Yukala dzakani-yunaria makodza na adudu-ludzua na migniolo.
**Fukufuku.** *See* Fukafuka.
**Fukula,** *v.a.* *See* Chumba. Midzanga ni ku fukula-ela lukue ni ku fugula.
  **Fukulafukula,** *v. reit.* Fukulafukula dzi, u-ki-simike (*e.g.* Kirenge).

## [PDF Page 103 — Dictionary Page 90 (Ful — Ful)]

**Fula,** *n.* (ra, no pl.). *See* Kafula. Barrenness. Ni utu dza wanamo; and Ra wimbi, -ere. Madzere gadzihenda fula. Ukiona muhama udzifira, be ka-u-kahenda fula. Fula ni ra maere. Muvunga unahenda kalonio tu, fulare ka-ri-manikana. Ndani mua-fula muna vidzi vichache. Dim., Kafula.
**Fula, Vula,** *v.a.* *See* Alama; Fua; Sui; Lafia. To put off, to draw off, to draw out. Ku fula, vula, nguo, To put off one's cloth; but Ku fula nguo is to wash a cloth. Ku fula ushanga, madzango. Ku fula tingo ya ngoma, To draw off the skin from a drum. Mutu yudzihoha, basi uka-m-fula, A man has sunk in the water when you drew him out. Nidzifuika kitu madzini, be kidziloama, nidzikuenda kifula.
  **Fuka,** *v.n.* *See* Dzupisa; Luarisa. Nguo yangu idzi-ni-fuka. Muho ni ku fuka. Kondo ikafuka kuchu.
  **Fukuza** (Kij. and Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku zola in Kir.).
  **Fusa,** *v.a.* Madzi ganafusa hebudze? Resp., Ah! nidzi-ga-sia ganala; hata undivo, or, undavo, fika Makuba, gandakala gadzidzuka dze dze dze, basi undafuka na magulu. Der., Mafulo.
**Fula,** *v.a.* *See* Madano; Mungu; Humbula. To strip, to take off. Ku fula nazi, To unhusk a cocoa-nut. Ku fula nguo. Ku fula uina. Ku fula mira. Mungu anafula muhama. Fulamoyo mimba, To miscarry. *See* Guiognomira.
  **Fuka,** (1) *v.a.* Ku fuka ndzugu.
  (2) *v.n.* Mosi unafuka; Fumbi rinafuka. Atu akipiga misindo, ndo fumbi rifukavo. Dzoa anafuka, kula uinani. Wari udzifuka; ka-u-na mahuhu.
  **Fukisa.**
  **Fulafula,** *v. reit.* Moyo udzi-ni-fulafula, nidzisikira neno ri.
  **Fulula,** *v.a.*, to scrape. Ei! Waforomoka munazini-akifulula mbulu, ei! He tumbled from a cocoa-nut tree, scraping an mbulu; *i.e.* making his skin look like that of an mbulu by gliding down the stem and scraping himself; but falling down at some distance from the stem by a bough giving way, etc., is Ka bua kamare.
  **Furika,** *v.n.* Nazi hi ka-i-furika, ina maganda momu, ela hino ni niolofu, inafurika haraka. Nguo yako idziola, ni ya kare, ka-i-furika kaviri, ukifula, unta-i-darura.
  **Furira,** *v.d.* and *instr.* Ndzo u-ni-furire nazi zangu. Ni badire chulo, nifurire nazi. Uk'enda fula nguoyo, na yangu u-ka-ni-furire kamare.
  **Furirua,** *v.p.* Gnania nidzi-mu-hundira nazi, nidzi-mu-va fungure, ela be yudzilonda mutu wa ku-m-furira-yudzipata hebudze? Resp., A-yudzifurirua kare. Resp., Ndo vidzo.
**Fulani** (Kij.). *See* Madzongi; Gnania. Such a one, a person. It is sometimes used in addition to their own word Gnania.
**Fulawe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), an anvil, generally about three or four inches square. Ravai yehu ilako, isikako, kasana, be kuehu kakuna fulawe.
**Fulo,** *n.* (ra), cream; (K.) foam, spume, froth, yeast. Fulo rinala pafuni. Fulo ra mafuha ukasara miambo.
**Fuluka,** *v.a.* *See* Kifulusi. To enwrap, to tie up. Wafulukani (= in Kir., Wawea dau)? Udzifulukani mo vindoni (= Udzifungani mo)? What have you tied up in here?

## [PDF Page 104 — Dictionary Page 91 (Ful — Fum)]

  Yuna kanoa ra kudzuva na ra ku fuluka; or, Gnania yuna neno ra ku dzuva na ra ku fuluka, mutu muerefu hiyu; kahensi kuga dzukudza ndani-judi aike akiba. Ku hewa fetha u ka fuluka.
  **Fusa,** *v.a.*
  **Fusika.**
  **Fusira.** Der., Kifulusi; Lufulo; Mfula; Mamfula; Pula.
**Fuluka,** *n.*, black muambawa.
**Fuluka,** *n.* (ra). Nidzi-mu-ona dzawe akichira akafunga utu nguoni, fuluka bomu, ela kura ku-mu-usa: udzifungani mumo? be sika-mu-usa. Fuluka kirira ra gnania musiku ni bomu, ela ra gnania rakue ni dide. Gnania yudzichira vava na m'anawe, akadzukula fuluka nguoni chamba ni ra muhama chamba ni ra madzere simania anagusa uchi. Udzifungani mo fulukani? Ku funga fuluka, nguo ya amba.
**Fulumuka,** *v.n.* (= Fingilika), to roll, revolve, circumvolve. Ku fulumuka murimani, ela ku foromoka gopueni munasini.
  **Fulumusa,** *v.a.* (= Fingilisa), to roll. Ku fulumusa muhi iwe, To roll a tree.
**Fuma,** *v.a.*, to shoot with an arrow, to sew.
  **Fumaga,** *v.a.* (in Kij., Ku atha maneno). *See* Hansa. To kill by shooting. Ku fumaga pembe.
  **Fumagira.** *See* Gumba.
  **Fumagirua,** *v.p.* Ndo lu-dza-lofumagirua nsoya.
  **Fumika,** *v.n.* *See* Kidambara.
  **Fumuka,** *v.n.* *See* Niambura; Luago. (K.) to fuzz. Niumba yangu ya kaya idzifumuka niasi, ela fuiho ni nsima. Muiri wa-mu-fumuka kimbimbi.
  **Fumukana,** *v. reit.* (= Ku dzamukana). Atu ere dele hiva, be vino adzifumukana.
  **Fumula,** (1) *v.a.* *See* Dzomola; Gnarira. To extinguish. Ku fumula moho (= Ku simia moho). Gnania ndiye adze ye fumula maneno.
  (2) *v.n.* *See* Mudzundu. To shoot forth, as the ear from the blade; (K.) separate, rip, lavish.
  **Fumulafumula,** *v. reit.*, (1) to scatter about. Nidzipiga niasi zangu, ela uwe udzikuenda buma gnombe vavo, sikafumulafumula niasi sana—be ni ku-ni-mena hebu nini? Kudza uka, To come going off, to come to go off; *i.e.* No sooner was he off, etc.
  (2) To divulge. Wa-mu-ona gnania musiku yudziiya, be aki-mu-amba: si seme ndakudza ni-ku-ve kitu, ela iye kudza uka hivo, basi na ku-ga-fumulafumula-kula mutu aki-ga-mania.
  **Fumulana,** *v. ref.*
  **Fumurika,** *v.n.*
  **Fumurira,** *v.d.*, (K.) indulge, tolerate, suffer.
  **Fumuririka,** *v.n.* *See* Golola. To be bearable. Polly hemuka kigulu.
  **Fumusa,** *v.a.*, to disperse. Nidzidzimba puku, nidzi-a-fumusa.
  **Fumusa,** *v.a.* *See* Fumusira; Kombora.
  **Fumusira,** *v.d.* *See* Kombora.
**Fuma,** *v.a.*, (1) to sew or weave; (2) to shoot with an arrow; (3) to breathe hard.
**Fuma,** *v.n.* *See* Muamba; Peho. To growl, to roar. Niuchi ana fuma; kukasikira kifumi muao muadoni? Ukiona niuchi anafuma sana maereni, basi gandaingisa tembe sana. Dzimba yunafuma, The lion roars. Madzi gadziingira, muho unafuma. Peho inafuma. Mufuananiko unafuma. Mvula inadza, inafuma; or, Kunafuma mvula, inadza.

## [PDF Page 105 — Dictionary Page 92 (Fum — Fum)]

  **Fumikisa,** *v.n.* (= Idikia in Kij.), to sing in chorus. Ngoi yunaimba hata akivesa, basi atu akafumikisa.
  **Fumira.** Kuro yudzi-ni-vekera, yudzi-ni-fumira. Dzimba yudzi-ni-fumira, yudzi-ni-ogofia.
  **Fumirana.** *See* Vekerana.
  **Fumurira,** *v.n.* Der., Fumi; Kifumi; Mfumi.
**Fumaka, Fumaga,** *v.a.*, to kill by shooting.
**Fumba, 1,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) an open handful. Ni-hegera fumba menga ra muniu, nikalungire, sina muniu, naria vidzufu. Yudzi-ni-hegera mafumba mairi ga muhama, n'enda henda musua ninoe.
(2) Paw. Fumba na paka, The paw of a cat. Niama a mafumba, Animals with paws; in contradistinction to Niama a makuacha, Animals with hoofs.
**Fumba,** *n. prop.* *See* Kifumba.
**Fumba** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Ku dzadziga in Kir.), to play.
  **Fumbama,** *v.n.* (= Odama in Kij.). *See* Dzudzama. To half-sit, to sit on one's heels, to squat; (K.) to skulk. Dzui akilonda ku-m-guira mbusi-ni ku fumbama, hata akadina, akaguira.
  **Fumbamika,** *v.n.* Ka-va-fumbamika hiva va luasu.
  **Fumbamira,** *v.d.* Adzi-hu-fumbamira nchirani, hata adzi-hu-guira.
**Fumbika,** *v.a.* (= Vumbika), (1) (Kir.). *See* Dungulua. Ku fumbika masu. Nafumbika mgasiya, uifue, nirie. Yudzifumbika mifuiye niasini, ku-i-fidza.
(2) (Kid.) (= Fumbukisa in Kir.), to shoot at a venture, fancying by the shaking of the grass that there might be an animal.
  **Fumbikira,** *v.d.* (1) Na-m-fumbikira musenangu mgasiya.
  (2) (= Ku angira). Yudzihala mbeyu, yudzifumbikira mundawe. Mbeyu hino nikikala nayo, nda-i-ria, baha kuenda i fumbikira, mfula ikignia, indamera.
  **Fumbikisa.** *See* Fumbukiza. Nidzikuenda insa, nikaona mduguso, niama megnie sika-mu-ona be nikadzuva mufui ku fumbukisa, na ku-m-doma; or, be nikafumbukisa mufui, nika-m-kosa.
  **Fumbirua,** *v.p.* (= Vumbirua). Chihafuna madzere, kahiri nidzeria wari na mboga sa kunde, basi nidzifumbirua, ka-vi-neneka. Usambe ni kuria muno-ni ndani tu ku galuka, hebu ku galukua ni ndani. Nidzifumbirua, ninaheruka migeri uzungu. Wangine wana midzango mi-kafumbirua.
  **Fumbisa,** *v.a.* (= Vumbisa). Nidzeria kitu, kidzi-ni-fumbisa. Mutu akihafuna madzere madzanga-akiria wari na mboga za kunde hebu mboga za podzo basi kakomia ku fumbirua, or, kasi komia ku-m-fumbisa. Muhama mdzanga ka-u-komia ku fumbisa.
  **Fumbukiza,** *v.a.* (= Fumikisa). *See* Dalalia; Darazira. Ka fumbukisa uira, To join, to fall in with a song, in a chorus. Ku fumbukisa mufui niama. *See* Fumbikiza. Nere sika-mu-ona niama hiye; nidzidzuva mufui tu ku fumbukisa; karakara na ku-m-doma. Mulungu yudzierekesa; ela kuamba Mulungu kakahensa, singa-m-doma, kuani nari si-mu-ona. Fumbukisani huhende kivumi.
  **Fumbula,** *v.a.* (= Ku piga mkambe). Nafumbula niasi mdzombe, niburuka wimbi. Nafumbula, niunge, nidzome, niniale ufuha. Narima nikiricha tu hata ni enese ueru-basi nidze, nifumbule niunge nidzome; basi ni buruke wimbi.

## [PDF Page 106 — Dictionary Page 93 (Fum — Fun)]

**Fumbuluka,** *v.n.* (= Bingiria in Kij.; Fumburuka in Kins.), to start, to move suddenly from alarm, especially from sleep. Nari rere hata nafumbuluka, nikasikira kululu. *See* Foromoka. Nidzila la hata nafumbuluka kudzecha atu adzienenda kare. Niama yudzifumbuluka malo, or, yudziforomoka malo.
  **Fumbulukisa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Udulukisa in Kir.), to startle, to surprise. Only used of men, while Fumbulusa is used of both men and animals.
  **Fumbulukisua** (Kid.), *v.p.*, to be startled. Charo cha ku fumbulukisua si-ki-hensi. Uchi hiu ka-u-lagirue, udzifumbulukisua.
  **Fumbulusa,** *v.a.*, to startle, to alarm, to rouse. Muana wari rere yudzi-mu-fumbulusa.
  **Fumbulusira** (Kid.), *v.d.*, to rouse to. Muana yukala yudzirerere, yukudza ni fumbulusira.
  **Fumbulusua,** *v.p.* Der., Fumbi; Mfumbi.
**Fumbi, Vumbi,** *n.* (ra). *See* Fuka. Dust; lit. that which covers.
**Fumfu** (Kid.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Pfumfu in Kir.), large eyes protruding. Fumfu za madzo (= Kogo za mato in Kij.).
**Fumi,** *n.* (ra). Atu hio anapiga rima, ana, fumi, ka-vi-neneka. Fumi ra bahari, ra madzi ra peho; ra atu akifuina uira. Atu hio achira na fumi. Vatu hiva vana fumi ra atu.
**Fumo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a spear. Yupigua fumo, He was speared. Amasai adzipiga atu mafumo; but, Nioka-ni ku-m-dunga fumo, or, ku-m-dunga na fumo.
**Fumuka.** *See* Fuma.
  **Fumula.** *See* Fuma.
  **Fumurira.** *See* Fuma.
  **Fumusa.** *See* Fuma.
**Funa,** *v.a.* (= Kirinsi; Dondola). *See* Ifuisa, where it is used in a general sense. To reap. N.B.—The word denotes the act of bending a thing down before you cut it, and can therefore only be properly used of muvunga, maere, and wimbi; other words are therefore employed for other grains, as Ku tema, to cut, for muhama; Ku funsa, to break, for madzere; Ku hunda, to pluck off, for mbalasi, kunde, pozo. Of things growing in the earth, Ku dzimba, to dig, is used for miyokue; but Ku fuka, to scratch out, for ndzugu; Ku guola, and Ku dzimba, for mugasija. The word is, however, sometimes used in a general sense; *e.g.* Muaka wa rero atu adzifuna nafaka sana, This year people reaped much grain, made a good harvest. Muaka udziifua, atu anafuna kilariro, or, anadzuma kilariro. Gnania rero yudzifuna madzere; gadzidzukula hata atu adzidzoka.
**Funamira,** *v.n.* Yudzilala ku funamira moyo. Yudzebua ku funamira moyo.
**Funika** (Kid.). Muhama uchere muidzi, ka-u-dzankue ku funika.
  **Funira,** *v.d.* Ka-mu-funire muyao muvunga-muvungawe unabanangika, muegniewe ni mukongo.
  **Funirua,** *v.p.* Yudzifunirua maerege ni nduguye.
  **Funuka,** *v.n.*, to be opened. Kidzeka kidzifunuka, vitu vidzimuagika, kidzivevera na peho. Chuo kidzifunuka kua peho, The book is opened by the peho. Rero dzua ridzifunuka; rinaala, To-day the sun is uncovered; it shines out.
  **Funula,** *v.a.*, to uncover. Ku funula kithembe. Nidzibinikisa, kidza, nidzifunula. Ni-

*Footer: 93*

---

## [PDF Page 107 — Dictionary Page 94 (Fun — Fun)]

  dzibinikisa madzi gangu, adzayefunula niani, ku-ga-richa luosu?
  **Funulua,** *v.p.*, to be uncovered. Kidzeka kidzifunulua ni peho. Der., Kifuna; Kifune; Kifunefune; Kifuname; Mafune; Mafuno.
  **Funurira,** *v.d.* (= Jika). *See* Roho. To uncover to, to disclose to. Gnania yukudza-ni-ambira maneno, yudzi-ni-funurira korokoro, maneno gaambuago.
  **Funurirua,** *v.p.*, to have any thing uncovered, disclosed to one's self. Gnania wari akiambua luambo, ela rero yudzifunurirua, yudziambirua uso na madzo. Hufunurirua ni Mulungu keri.
**Funda,** *n.* (ra), food prepared from unripe grain, muhama or madzere; it is first pounded, then dried and boiled. Made of maere, it is called madasa. Rero hudzeria wari wa funda.
**Funda,** *v.a.* (= Funsia), to teach. Muana hiyu nidzi-mu-funda kasi, ela kahenda, ni mukaha. Na-m-funda kare ku rima; yudzikala mukurima yunamania ndimua. Muana wa gnania ndiye a-mu-fundaye m'anangu ku yeya. Kari na go higa ga ku yeya; be nasihende akidza hiva. Yuna-dzi-funda ku yeya (= Yuna-dzi-hensia ku yeya). Wavirikua niani, asie-ku-funda to, atu akalafio na alume? Kadzangue ku mania, yuchari-dzi-funda, or, yukere madzifundi.
  **Fundira.** Nafundira masikiro, nisasikira hifio ugombafio.
  **Fundirika,** *v.n.* Kirenge hiki kinafundirika to.
  **Fundirira.** Nalonda ndifu, ni-ku-fundirire kirengecho. Ka va ndifu ya ku fundirira uchi.
  **Fundula,** (1) *v.a.* (= Ku funula). *See* Kore. To open, to unstop, to remove a stopper. Opposed to Fundira.
  (2) *v.n.*, to bud, to sprout. Muhi hiu unafundula makodza.
  **Fundurika,** *v.n.* Ka-i-fundurika dzasi hi ya kisungu, ignie angafundula-dze?
  **Fundurira.** Kuamba, idzi-ku-remesa ku fundula, be reha, ni-ku-fundurire.
  **Funsia,** *v.a.*, to teach. Na-m-funsia ngemua, amanie ku gema. Na-m-funsia kare ku gema, ela ka mania to, ni mukaha. Yuna-dzi-funsia uziusi (= Ku-dzi-hensia uzinsi). Muana hiyu ni mulachu sana, kafunsirue ni mutu ku gema, yudzimania m'egnie.
  **Funsiua,** *v.p.* (= Funsua, Kij.). Der., Mafundukui.
**Funda,** *v.n.* *See* Mfu. To smell. Mafuha higa gadzifunda, This butter smells. (Mafuha may also be Ghu. *See* the word.) Kid., Niama i ifunda, for inafunda, The meat smells. Kirengechangu chafunda, My calabash smells.
**Fundisa** (Kid.), *v.a.*, to break. Ku fundisa kirenge (= Kir., Ku funsia kirenge), To break a calabash.
**Funsa,** *v.a.* *See* Vunga; Kolola. To break, to break off; (K.) Ku funsa; Kufua, rattle, entwine. Ku funsa muhi, To break a tree. Ku funsa madzere, To break off Indian corn. Nahufunseni kifuko.
  **Funsafunsa,** *v. reit.*, to break repeatedly, to keep breaking. Nin'enda nikalonde muhi, nifunsefunse, ni pate vikuni via kudza hendera wari. Ku funsa, or, ku hunda makodza ga tumbaku. Ku funsa dzingo ni ku venduka ku lola kanda. Nidzigomba naye, kaka-ni-lola, yudzifunsa dzi-

*Footer: 94*

---

## [PDF Page 108 — Dictionary Page 95 (Fun — Fun)]

  ngo ku lola kanda. Ku funsa mafuindi, To break the knees, said of the first endeavours of a child to make use of its legs. *See* Koko. Ku funsa chala, To break a finger—a figurative expression, meaning, to forgive. Dzusi wa-ni-amba neno hiri ri, nikifunsa chala; hunadza dzana aki n'amba, for, ni-amba, neno riro ri, nikifunsa chala; be dziku-andivo-ni-amba kahiri, hundaheha, hundapigana. Ku funsa dzadza kuku wakisimui.
  **Funsia,** *v.a.*, to entoil, to twist. Nafunsia kirenge, kiole mioyo.
  **Funsika,** *v.n.*, to break. (K.) Ku funsika maneno, to patter; lit. to break words. Nidziku-ala, nidzifunsika chala, cha kigulu.
  **Funsikira,** *v. rel.* Nidzi-u-mema, ela sika-u-fikira, u-kure, udzifunsikira ndani ya niama.
  **Funsira,** *v.d.*, to break to, for any one. Nina-m-funsira vikuni, nika-m-virikire. Rero na-ku-funsira chala; machero ukigomba kaviri neno riro, ni-ku-funsire chala; be hata lua hahu, basi indahahuka, or, lua hahu lu-ndahahuka. Yudzi-ku-funsira chala kana mbiri hebu kana tahu, haya-be ku mulongo fio?
**Fundika,** *v.a.* Ku fundika tumbaku, masu, etc.
  **Fundua,** *v.p.* (= Ku dzi fundisa; Mukumba = Kulinga). Udzifundua ni babayo hebu ni mameyo, kuamba uingise mbuzi mundani?
**Funga,** *v.a.* *See* Fufu; Viha. To bind, to tie. Ku funga minazi, To tie cocoa-nut trees. Atu adzikuenda funga minazi, anadzula (= anadangadza mianso). Madzo gadzifunga kisa, simania chamba gandaluma. Nidzi-dzi-funga kare mino, sina hata utu = I am quite ready.
  **Fungana,** *v.r.* (= Lingilana; Viringania), to tie one another, to entangle. Lukue ludzifungana, The rope, or string, has become entangled; lit. has tied one part another.
  **Funganafungana,** *v. reit.*, to be much entangled. Niukue zika funganafungana, The ropes are entangled.
  **Fungira,** *v.d.* and *instr.* *See* Mugomba. Ambush, waylay.
  **Fungirua,** *v.p.* Kibangala ki-si-vo dzankue ku fungirua, ndivo aihavo tembo. Mufimfira ndo ufungiruao mavanda.
  **Fungisa,** *v.a.* *See* Kuhu. (K.) suffocate. Ku fungisa mosi.
  **Fungisua,** *v.p.*, to be suffocated.
  **Fungua** (= Ku fungua ni utu). Gnania aka fungua kisiwani, akakotua pingu na mkatale. Fig., Ku fungua mbalahi (= Ku hafunua mbalahi; *i.e.* Ku pigua mbalahi).
  **Fungula,** *v.a.*, to make a present. Ndzoni hufungule. Muzungu yudzi-ni-fungula nguo, The European has made me a present of a cloth.
**Fungahe,** *adj.*, seven.
**Fungo,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the civet-cat.
**Fungu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Gafikana. A part, portion, share, lot, heap. Fungu bomu ra atu, A large group of men. Fungu ra mawe, A heap of stones. Fungu ridzo ra gnombe. *See* Kilungu.
**Funo** (sometimes pronounced Pfuno), *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a species of antelope. It is larger than the pala.
**Funsa.** *See* Funda. To break.
  **Funsia.** *See* Funda.
  **Funsika.** *See* Funda.
  **Funsira.** *See* Funda.
**Funsaniungu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the praying mantis.
**Funsarere,** *n.* (ra, wa, pl. Ma-;

*Footer: 95*

---

## [PDF Page 109 — Dictionary Page 96 (Fun — Fus)]

  and *id.*), the name of a species of snake. Ana wino uiru; risagala dzulu ya mihi; uki-ri-ona rinahambaladzi, basi mfula ni vevi na kudza. Kana haraka ya ku luma.
**Funsu,** *n.* (ra). *See* Lufunsu. Something broken up, disturbed, confused, stirred up. Especially used of water made dirty by being disturbed. Madzi higa gadzifurungua, gadzikala funsu, ka-ga-hegeka. Kuani kusa hega madzi madzo, ukahega funsu? Madzi higa gana funsu; or, Madzi higa ga funsu, ka-ga-hegeka. Funsu ra dindia.
**Funula.** *See* Funda.
  **Funurira.** *See* Funda.
  **Funuka.** *See* Funda.
**Fuo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Ugulo. Mihi ya mafuo.
**Fura,** *v.n.*, to swell (Kij., but used by the Wanika, beside their own word Kanagnana).
  **Furika,** *v.n.* *See* Ongo; Fula. To be swollen, grown. Munazi hiu ni momu, ka-u-furika, ela huno-makumbige ni molofu.
**Furaha** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za), joy.
  **Furahisha,** *v.a.*, to make joyful or glad.
  **Furahiwa,** *v.p.* *See* Kalanga; Kongue. To be rejoiced.
**Furi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Aluka. An animal (?). Mafuri higara gagochira gari gakanona, mfula yere ningi, ela furi hiri ra rero a kari na mvula, ka-ri-na kitu kamare, ni furi lume. Fuririche ndiro rinonaro. Furi rilume.
**Furufu** (Kig.), *adj.* (= Kavu, Kij.; and Fu, Kir.), hard, dry. Tangu niama ze ni furufu, The fish, tangu, its flesh is dry.
**Furufuru,** (1) *v.a.*, to wear in an untidy or slovenly manner; (2) *v.n.*, to be untidy. Yudzi-hu-hukana furufuru, hata adza-vo-dzoka, basi yudzienenda. Yugomba maneno gafurufuru na atu a dele; kana akili mutu hiye; kaasa kuamba atu asima avavo, hebu mdzedzawe yuvavo, atu aogovanao. Manenoge ga furufuru gasigoerekera, yuna dzangania atu osi ario vavo. *See* Lani; Bandabanda. Yunafuala nguo furufuru, He, or she, wears his, her, cloth slovenly.
**Furuma,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (in Kid., Jule), the squirrel. Furuma yunga mfare gisiye, ela mfare ni mtite furuma ni mbomu punde.
**Furunga, Vurunga,** *v.a.* *See* Bua; Funsu; Musesero. To stir, as in mixing anything. In cooking, a different word is used as soon as what is in the pot becomes thick. Ndzoni, hufurunge madzi, makumba garee ku rea hufue sui, or, hufue makumba. Der., Musesero.
  **Furungika.** Kakabadanishika maneno gadzifurungika.
**Furungu,** *n.*, (K.) cracknel.
**Furura,** *v.a.* *See* Fula; Vulumula. Musua na mboga ni ku furura—Musua na mboza. Kitu kidzacho fugua na masia, be ukinoa, ndo ku furura.
  **Fururira,** or **Fulurira,** *v.* Udzienenda vatu na muyao, be ukisa ima nchirani, uwe ukifika mbere-iye akidza niuma: yunda-ku-usa: udzifika kare? Resp., A-mimi sikaima, nidzifururira hata nidzifika.
  **Fururiza,** or **Fuluriza,** *v.n.* (= Furusa, Vurusa. Kid.). N.B.—Not to be confounded with Vulurisa. Ai! mfula nayo idzikasa muno-hangu yagnia ka-i-dana,—idzifururisa hata idzihenda dziku dzano; mfananiko udziidzala dele muhoni muho ka-u-chisa. *See* another instance at the word Di.
**Fusa,** *v.a.* *See* Fuka. To push on without stopping. Ku fusa

## [PDF Page 110 — Dictionary Page 97 (Fut — Fut)]

  fumbi, To stir up dust. Gnombe zinafusa fumbi, The cows stirred up the dust. Muhama wangu udzipigua ni atu ahahu, hudzipiga hata hudzimala, hudzifusa; udzivetua hata udzisira, basi hudzibuma misigo kudza mudzini; be nidzidzoka muno.
  **Fusika,** *v.n.* Nidzifusa muhama, ela kakuna peho, muhama ka-u-fusika kua ku dzoa peho.
  **Fusira,** *v. rel.* and *instr.* *See* Mulungu. Prayer before a journey. A., Una-ni-fusira luambe ge! B., Be-udzikarira ni ko mbere sa peho? A., Be-ku-ni-ona, kuna madzo hebudze? Gnania yudzi-hu-fusira midzangu (= muagira). Si-ni-fusire fumbi. Kusi ridzi lamuka-ra ku fusira muhama.
  **Fusua,** *v.p.* Muhama wangu-rero udzipigua, udzifusua. Der., Kifusi; Lufusi.
**Futa,** *v.a.* *See* Dzaniula. To tear off, to pluck off. Ku futa mitata. *See* Konje. Ku futa ludzere, To pluck out a hair. *See* Ku kula. Nenda nikafute uriro, nidze ni valase, ni hungire muambo. He'nde hukafute kansa, hudze hugule kolekole, hukarie na wari (= in Kid., Gnania yufuta madzi = Ni muerefu sana wa maneno; in Kir., Fuha madzi ku futa ndefu). Adzifiererana, hata akafuta kifiu, yulonda ku-m-bofola. *See* Dzolola. Trop., Nidzihenda dzi futa ku uka. Yukuenda ku-ni-kukutisa uchi, hata nikisa idima ku enenda, nikilala; na rero aka-ni-rausira uchi kaviri, naamba: aa, ka-vi-ndakala; be nikahenda-dzi-futa basi ndo kudza hivi; ela kuamba sika-dzi-futa, ningari nikere vavo, or, nik'enda-dzi-futa.
**Futafuta,** *v. reit.* *See* Dabadaba. Niama akikala yunafua, basi ni-ku-futafuta magulu na mikono. Mutu naye akitemua, hebu akifumagua, akikala vevi na kufua, basi ni ku futafuta.
  **Futafuta,** *v.a.* Ku futafuta magulu.
  **Futika,** *v.n.*, (1) to admit of being torn off. Konche rikalaro vevi na kolo, be ka-ri-futika.
  (2) To be suffocated. Una-m-guira muyao pula na mitomo, yunafutika, unda-mu-ulaga gi. Hudzipiga moho ku-u-simia, basi vari na mosi mungi tu, hudzifutika. Mutu, akihoha madzini, yufua kua ka futika.
  **Futira,** *v.d.* *See* Mugomba. To tear off to or for another. Ka-ni-futire madzere, nidze nioche, To break off ears of Indian corn for me, that I may parch them.
  **Futisa,** *v.a.* *See* Sohesa.
  **Futu,** *v.a.*, to inflate. Ku futu ma dzafu. Uki-m-rinda mutu hata ukadzoka, be ukaenenda, kadzakudza, be dziku uki-mu-ona uka-mu-ambira: na-ku rinda nikipiga futu hata nikidzoka, nikiguira nchira, nikienenda; be we wari luavi we? Kaviri apigaye futu ni mutu arie na moyo, aonaye atu adzichita niungu ya wari be naye kakaambua: rinda wari; ela akasagala m'egniewe, nafusiye, hata wari ukaifua, akaria, basi akaenenda; be hiko niuma ndo aambuavo: mutu hiyu yuna meyo hiyu; kakaambua: rinda wari, ela yudzipiga futu hata wari udziifua yudzeria.
  **Futuka,** *v.n.* *See* Migirimigiri. (K.) To become delirious. Ndaniyangu idzifutuka. Yudzidzukirua, yudzifutuka, yuna-ni dimurira.
  **Futukira** (= Futuko ra ku shoma). Der., Pfuto.
  **Futula.**

## G.

**G,** the seventh letter of the alphabet, pronounced uniformly hard, as in "go." Some dialects change the *g* into *k*, and *vice versâ*.—[ED.]
**Ga,** (1) *a particle* denoting the gen. to words of the pl. form Ma-. Baki ukira; Wanguangu. *See* Dada; Sororesa.
(2) *See* Oya; Vukulika; Engulula; Muluchiluchi; Manionioda; Chungua. It is the pronoun for that class of words, and as such means "they" and "them." Sometimes it has also verbal force—"they are." *See* Gadze; Mambo.
(3) *See* Nai. It implies the imperf. tense.
(4) *A particle* of exclamation. Sometimes it is pronounced Ge. Ni fifira ga, or, ge.
**Ga** (= Ku henda gaaa ga ga ga). Ga and Gna ni moho (= Ba and Gna ni kucha). Moho unaaka ga; or, Moho unaaka gna.
**Gaansa,** *n.* (za). Gaansa se lungoni uka ike dzuani, gafuhuke ndo gandavo veteka gaansase (= gafuhuke).
**Gaba** (Kid.), *n.* (ra) (= Nchini in Kir.), the vagina.
**Gabira** (Kid.), *v.a.*, to lap. Dia yunagabira madzi, The dog lapped the water.
**Gabu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a citron.
**Gada, Kara,** *v.n.* Kisima hiki kinarcha madzi muno, ela hangu dzana ka-ki-reha muno, kidzigada kinalonda ku una. Yudzirua m ladzo, be vino idzigada.
**Gadi, Kadi,** *n.*, chest.
**Gadiri, Kadiri.**
**Gadzago.** Madzere mafu, gadzago koniokera, Dry cobs of corn which are hanging down.
**Gadze.** Bua. *See* Usidana.
**Gadzi.**
**Gadzigo.** *See* Dzikiridzikiri.
**Gaere,** or **Gari** (rel. to the preformative Ma-), it was; they were. It is frequently contracted into Gere. Gaere madzodzigo mabomu, It was a great play.
**Gafia,** *v.a.*, to divide.
  **Gafika,** *v.n.* *See* Kulungana.
  **Gafikana,** *v.n.* Atu adzigafikana mafungu mari.
  **Gafira,** *v.d.*, to divide to, for. (K.) Gafisania magulu, Cover the legs.
  **Gafiwa.** *See* Kidamfisa.
**Gafue,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) the bush of the tail of a cow when uncommonly large.
(2) The beard of a he-goat when uncommonly large. Gafue ni tiho bomu, hebu kirefu kibomu, cha ndenge. Gnombe hi ina gafue ra tiho. Ndenge hi ina gafue ra kirefu.
**Gaga,** *pron.* *See* Engulula; Machira.
**Ga ga ga,** *adv.* *See* Dzalangua; Dzikiridzikiri; Vegnieka. Thickly crowded together, thickly set. Madzahasi higara ga ga ga ga, said of the vessels in the harbour of Zanzibar. Vana ondo sana hivo, riga ga ga.
**Gagahula** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Gangahula in Kir.).
  **Gagamisa,** *v.a.*, to press. Gnania yudzisindika niumba na kivangua, be nidzigagamisa, sikaweesa ku sundula. Mutu akidunga kitu kua ngufu, yunagagamisa.
**Gaganda** (Kid.), *v.* (= Ku gangunda in Kir.).
**Gago.** *See* Dida. Angakala waosa maneno gago.

## [PDF Page 112 — Dictionary Page 99 (Gah — Gam)]

**Gahe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a species of lizard, somewhat smaller than the mfaramfara. Dim., Kigahe; magn., Rigahe.
**Gaka.** *See* Tarare; Hasi.
**Ga-ka-go.** *See* Ngulula.
**Gaki.** *See* Mukondo.
**Gako.** Gako ni ga keri; udzi-ni-mfoda.
**Gakue,** *poss. pron.* *See* Mfoda; Vagira.
**Gala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kala (fai neno ra ku resa (enderesa), but Gala, ra ku kuesa). A species of wild animal, kinga, or, yunga. Kiniegere, ela rika uya, It is like the kiniegere, but somewhat smaller.
**Galagala,** *v.n.*, to wallow. Nsoya yunagalagala.
  **Galagasa,** *v.a.*
**Galagala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Radzini; Dzulu.
**Galakonche,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kalakonche. The same species of animal as the gala, but somewhat larger and different in colour. Gala regnie, muiriwe ni wamfuamfua. Galakonche ni bomu punde, na muiriwe ni mueruve dza konche. Galakonche ni ku vunsa miado, akaria mavalala ga niuchi.
**Galima,** *n.* (ra).
**Galuka,** *v.n.* *See* Kilagane. To turn round, to change. Galuka kuno, Turn round this way. Kaidima ku galuka m'egnie-yudzoka.
  **Galukira,** *v.d.*, to turn *to*, to change *to*. Ni-galukira kuno, Turn towards me this way. Navokala Lunguya, be dzua rari riki upuka hiku. Muakani-dzi iki-ni galukira.
  **Galukirana,** *v. reit.*, (1) to turn towards each other; (2) to get changed one to another. Nidziona atu aimire adzigalukirana. Atu hara akagalukirana analolana.
  **Galukisa,** *v.a.*, lit. to let a change take place, to continue changing; *i.e.* to replace the full kibaria, small calabash, by an empty one—an expression belonging to the art of drawing the palm-wine. Nagalukiza munazi wangu-uchi unamuagika.
  **Galukisira.** Der., Kigalugalu.
  **Galusa,** *v.a.*, to turn, to change.
  **Galusika,** *v.n.*, to admit of being turned round, to admit of being changed. Gogo hiri ka-ri-galusika, ni ziho rinamerera.
  **Galusira,** (1) *v.d.*, to turn anything to, for another. Ni-galusira mgasija wangu usavia.
  (2) (= Galukisa and Galukisira, munazi). Munazio ukagalusira? Resp., E-na-u-galusira. Ukibuma kibaria vandani hata riki idzala, be ukikala unabuma kingina ndo ku galusira.
  **Galusua,** *v.p.*, to be turned, to be changed. A ni mukongo-yuhenda galusua.
**Gama, Kama,** *v.a.*
  **Gamana, Kamana,** *v.n.*, to coagulate, to set, to thicken as eggs when boiled.
**Gamidza, Kamidza,** *v.a.*, (K.) to wrest. Hudzimigniana, yudzi-ni-gamidza, yudzi-ni-piga chafu kibomu.
  **Gamira, Kamira,** *v.d.*
  **Gamiria, Kamiria,** *v.a.* *See* Linda. Yudzifunga lukuva yudzikamiria.
**Gamuka, Kamuka.** *See* Uhumbo.
  **Gamula, Kamula,** *v.a.*, (1) to press out, to squeeze. Ku gamula uhombe.
  (2) Gutter, eventerate. Nidzi-ri-kamula, nidzi-ri-mimina, hata ridzidzuka. *See* Ivu. Ndzo-u-ni-kamule ivu (= Kumurira). Kugamula nguo, To wring out a cloth.
  **Gamulana,** *v. ref.*, to crowd.
  **Gamurira, Kamurira,** *v.d.* *See* Kombo.

## [PDF Page 113 — Dictionary Page 100 (Gam — Gan)]

**Gamba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Gnarira. A handful. Gamba ra niasi, A handful of grass. Gamba ra muvunga, A handful of rice; *i.e.* ears of rice, when reaping. Gamba in Kid. means a handle of a basket. Ku piga magamba ga niasi.
**Gambani.** *See* Mudzovi.
**Gana,** *adj.*, squint-eyed. Used with Mazi, Ira, etc. Madzoge gana malola.
**Gana,** *n.* (pl. Ma-), one hundred. Ni gana ku halua ni gana.
**Gana.** Yudzihalua gana, ka-dza-ngue ku chita dziko. Homa ra gana and Homa ra dziko.
**Gana, Kana,** *v.a.*, to deny, to disown, to renounce. Gnania yunaambua yudziiya, ela yugana. Mbari adzi-ni-gana, hata kuangu kadza, hata akachira na hiva, ka-ni-lamusa.
  **Gananirana,** *v. reit.* *See* Kanani.
  **Gania, Kania,** *v.a.* *See* Ora. To interdict, to forbid; (K.) abnegate. Ku-m-gania gnania.
  **Ganika,** *v.n.*, to be deniable. Utu hiu ka-u-ganika, yudzi-u-henda geri, This matter is undeniable; he has done it in truth; kaganika.
  **Ganira, Kanira,** *v.d.* *See* Shudia. To deny to or for another. Gnania ndiye akayehala kitu changu uwe una-m-ganira, na m'egniewe kavo una-m-ganiradze fio? Resp., Sinda-m-ganira dze naye kaharire, unahenda-m-singa kasidi kuamba akahala.
  **Ganirua,** *v.p.*, to have anything denied in one's favour. M'egniewe karivo-ela yudziganirua ni Shaha Chindaa.
  **Ganiua, Kaniua,** *v.p.* *See* Tharau. To be forbidden.
  **Ganiula, Kaniula** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Kuaniula in Kir.; Pfentura in Kns.), to graze. Mufui hiu udzi-ni-ganiula niama chache.
  **Ganua, Kanua,** *v.p.*, to be denied, disowned, Gnania musiku yudziganua ni lukololuao.
  **Ganuka, Kanuka** (Kid.), *v.n.*, to keep aloof from. Gnania yudzi-ni-ganuka, hangu dzana kadza kaviri. Der., Kanani; Kani.
**Gandaganda, Ganchagancha,** *v.a.* (= Gancha, -na, -ika, -ira), to repair slightly. Used when a real reparation can no more be thought of. Kuna kivinda uka-ni-pa, nikabumire kitu changu? Resp., A Kivinda kiko ela ni dzafue dzafue kika daruka; be uhale, wende, ukagancheganche, uikire ngari dziku mbiri, be undalonda kivinda kidzo. Ukongo ni ubomu naganchagancha vifio; na-m-foya iye Mulungu, hangi yundavola, says the muganga with regard to a hopeless patient. *See* Kiremba.
**Gandama** (Kidigo), *v.n.* (= Ku gandamira in Kir.), to stick, to adhere.
  **Gandamira,** *v.* *See* Mfalume. To press.
  **Gandamirana,** *v. reit.* *See* Dzikiridzikiri. To press one another, to be close. Ana pigana hata adzigandamirana.
  **Gandamisa,** *v.a.*, to press into.
  **Gandamisika,** *v.n.* *See* Kunsui.
  **Gandiza,** (1) *v.n.* *See* Chitana; Hanuka.
  (2) *v.a.*, to press, to twist. Ku gandiza tunde za mukufu, To press or twist together pieces of wire in making a chain. Ku gandiza pehe, kidzuvi, etc.
  **Gandizika,** *v.n.*, to admit of being pressed together, to appear, to prove being pressed together. Pehe yangu idzigandizika, To stick, to adhere, as a plaster.
**Ganduka,** *v.n.* (= Ku banduka and Ku omoka). *See* Gomoka. To become loose.
  **Gandula,** *v.a.* Ku gandula pehe sikironi.
**Gande,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Fiarira.

  A lump. Magande ga kishombo ga uvolue, etc. Gande ra unga, A lump of flour. Yudzeria gandere ra uvolue, nami ni vavo, ela kaka-ni-megurira, yudzeria hecheye, or, kaka-ni-bamfurira. Dim., Kagande.
**Gandegande,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of bird.
**Gandegande, Gancheganche,** *n.* Prov., Gancheganche ra mganga rinalasa mukongo na damaa.

**Ganga.** *See* Nga.

  **Gangahula,** *v.a.*, to draw asunder. Yudzi-m-guira umiro, be hudzi-m-henda gangahula mala.
  **Gangika,** *v.n.* Kunsa hi ka-i-gangika, idzifunsika korokoro, hata uka-i-ganga, ka-i-kodzoka.
  **Gangira,** *v.d.* Yudzi-ni-gangira kunsa yangu, yudzi-i-piga maango hata idzikala mbidzo.
  **Gangula,** *v.a.* (= Ku vendula). Gnania musiku wari mukongo, kaidima korokoro, akiambua walogua, be ak'enda hala muganga, akidza-mu-gangula.

**Gangu,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the pl. Ma-), my, mine.
**Gani,** *adv.*, why. Used with Ma, Bo, etc.
**Gani,** *adj.*, what.
**Gani, Gnani,** *n.* (= Zidza).
**Ganiula** (= Pfentura in Kns.). *See* Gana, *v.a.*
**Gano,** *dem. pron.* (rel. to the ma class) (= Higa, but Higo for a distance). *See* Mfiza.
**Gansa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the palm. Gansa ra mukono; pl. Magansa ga mikono, The palm of the hand. Nidzidungua ni muiya gansani siidima ku guira kitu. Yudzi-m-bumira fumba ra muhama gansani, ela muyawe yudzi-m-bumira kikahanani.
**Gansa,** *v.a.*, to warm. Yunagansa madzere, hebu mgasija, waochua dzana. Na-dzi-gansa moho nina peho. Na-dzi-gansa dzua, muiri udzi-ni-ingira peho nasikira vi.

**Gansi,** *n.* Kigulu kidzefua gansi, My foot or leg is asleep.
**Ganso,** *n.* (= in Kid., Gancho). *See* Kusa. A forsaken place.
**Gao,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Gao ni munazi urio mukinda, usio dzankue ku kala mure. Gnania yuna magao ga minazi, ina ngufu, ela yangu ni vinazi tu, ka-vi-na haja. Dim., Kigao.

**Ga-si-go.** *See* Umba.

**Gasi, Kazi** (?).

  **Gesagesa,** *v. reit.*, to make small attempts. Gnania yudziniala minazi miiri hebu mihahu, be idzihenda uchi ungi, ina-m-dzeka; ndo mutu achiraye agombavo. Ai! utu wa ku gesagesa ni ui, kuamba waniala minazi mingi, basi angari na uchi ungi. *See* another instance, Kamare. Der., Muengero; Lugesigesi.

**Geri, Keri,** *adv.*, truly. *See* Koma. Si muhambo wa keri, It is no real trap. Niosi sa geri, Grass of truth; *i.e.* worth speaking of. Muhambo wa koma. *See* Risika.
**Gesi,** *v.n.* Majoma agesi dza gunia (= A-nga).
**Gesi, Geshi** (Kij.), *n.* (ra). *See* Vieti. A host, a great multitude. Amasai aokudza vuri hiri, ari geshi rikidzala, dza nsima ya Aravai gnombe sosi zikidamfua pia.
**Gessi.**
**Gi** (= Ngi?), *adv.*, well, thoroughly. Ku fungua-gi.
**Gia,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a species of bird.
**Giema** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Gema in Kir.; Ku giema minazi). In Kid. they also say, Ku giema mbono (= Ku chita mbono in Kir.). Rero hunagiema mbono, ueruve udzihenda muno, To-day we make ourselves castor-oil, because our skin has become quite white.
**Gigiri.**
**Gigirigigiri,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Kikirikikiri and Kekerekekere), a confused noise.
**Gigirisha,** *v.a.*
**Gigisa,** *v.a.* (= Gomia? Ku gigisha in Kij.), to perplex. Maneno higa gana ni-gigisa, What words are these? I am perplexed.
**Girida,** *v.a.* (= Dzikidza). *See* Fuiha; Ngogomue. To rub. Ku girida luvohe, na madzi na viguguta via madzere. Manenogao ni m'omu, ganagirida, ka-ga-manikana hiraka. Maneno ga Kitaita gagirida (Maneno ga Kikamba ri mapesi). Ah! gnania yunagirida! yufungua na maneno, ela yudzikuenda nago hata yudzi-ga-fugula. Maneno gara tu ganagirida ni ku dza-ga-mania. Maneno ga Kikamba ganagirida, si-ga-mania.
**Gisi** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kalifu. Sort, manner; (K.) kind, race, genus, gender, family. Ni gisi gani? What manner is this? Muaka hia u-gesi mbi, hata furire ri gisi. Gnania yuna gisi mbi. Muiri wangu rero u-gisi u-nga dza urie mukongo, My body to-day has gisi; it is like one who is sick.
**Gizigizi** (Kig.), *v.* *See* Ore. A chamber-vessel.
**Gna.** *See* Ka; Ba.
**Gnagnazika,** *v.n.*, to glitter. Mufiu unagnagnazika. Muezi ukiala muno, basi ni ku ambua: unagnagnazika. Chombo hikira, kinagnala, kihenda gnagnazika.
**Gnala,** *v.n.* *See* Kigungu; Ala; Cha. To shine, to be bright, to be of white complexion. Niegniezi zinagnala. Dzala rinagnala. Moho hura unagnala. Niumba ya Muzungu inagnala dze dze dze, inagnagnazika.
  **Gnarira.** Gana-ku-gnarira. Anafumula niumba gamba menga ra niasi ku-u-gnarira, or, kuamba agnarirue; *i.e.* himura ndani muhende mulangasa.
  **Gnarirua,** *v.p.*
**Gnasa, Gnaza,** *v.a.*, to brighten. Ku gnasa meno, To show one's teeth, by laughing. Ela ku luma meno ni ku-ga-gandamisa kua koro.
**Gnambo,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) the fruit of the tree mgnambo.
(2) Opposite coast.
**Gnandu,** *n.*, copper.
**Gnania,** *n.*, a person; (K.) Gnania-gnania, thingummy, Mr. and Mrs. So-and-so. Gnania musiku, Somebody, A certain person. Gnania fulani. *See* Sura. Gnania nisagalaye naye kula dziku, ka-ni-ambira, ela gnania musiku, a laye kure, ndiye a ni henzaye adzie kudza, ni

## [PDF Page 117 — Dictionary Page 104 (Gna — Gni)]

  ambira maneno gaambuago pia (ndivo undu uansavo). Mimi na gnania huna matumaini ga ku tumaniana; kuangu kukikala na uchi-akina thora ni ku dza a valia akakuenda gula, na mimi dzavivio; nikikala sina uchi kuangu, be kuaka yunao be nikiona thora ni kuenda hala kikakudza kula.
**Gnansa,** or **Gnanzi,** *n.* (ya, za), conversation, discourse.
**Gnara** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Ringa in Kir.; Ringia wida in Kij.). Der., Ugnaro.
**Gnare,** *n.*, abyss (?).
**Gnaza,** *v.a.* *See* Gnala. (K.) Illuminate, illustrate. Ku gnasa meno, etc.
**Gnegna,** *v.a.* (= Ndzuoni aka-a-gnegna).
**Gnegnie** (Kid.), *n.* (= Dzama in Kir.).
**Gnia** (Ku gnia), *v.n.*, (1) to rain; (2) to ease nature.
  **Gnieka.**
  **Gniekererua,** *v.n.*, (1) to stay away, to remain absent, by being fascinated with the conversation of the people you have gone to, or being pleased with the country to which you have gone. Uwe uk'enda vatu, ku rurukua ku uya haraka-ukisagala basi ni ku gniekererua, kuasa niuma. Gnania wakuenda hamba-kauya haraka-yudzi-gniekererua ni dziio ariyo. Ku gniekererua ni ku noa uchi, To be detained to drink toddy.
  (2) To be fast asleep; lit. to become absent; *i.e.* unconscious, by sleep. Nidzi-lala-si-dza-gniekererua-nikalamusua. Yuna-m-lasa muana hata akigniekererua kua usinsisi, She lays down the child until he becomes absent by sleep.
  **Gniela,** *v.n.* Nai rinagnielagniela ku upuka usivo kuenda thaka.
  **Gnieragniera** (= Gnaro; Kambi?). Aduruma ni ku gnieragniera, akakudza gema mua mthina. Der., Gniere; Gnieregniere; Kignieresa; Mugnierere.
  **Gnierera,** *v.d.*, (1) to ease nature to, upon. Muhoho yudzi-m-gnierera mameye. Prov., Muana akignierera kiga, ka-ki-katua.
  (2) (= Yaya). *See* Mfu. To disappear, to get out of sight. Ku gnierera ni kusa henda misindo, ni ku enenda porepore, To go away by stealth. Yudzi-ni-gnierera. Wari vava hikara hata punde malola kavo yudzihenda gnierera; or, yudzignierera kakalaga. Niama yunagnierera porepore-yunakimbira, The animal has gone away quickly; it has run away. Kuku hiyu yunaenenda ku gnierera, ni mukongo. Mutu azoluaye, naye akiingira dzakani, basi yunagnierera ku-dzi-fidza.
  **Gnierereka,** *v.n.* (Kid., Gniererera; Gnierereka; Gniereresa in Kij.), to steal one's self away. Muana huya yunagnierereka yulonda ku kimbira, aenende kua asena. Ei gnania ni mkobi yunisuaa yunadza-mu-ona mdeni we kure, basi akagnierereka akaenenda.
  **Gniesa,** *v.a.* Mulungu unagniesa mfula.
  **Gniewa,** *v.p.* Vara vadzi gniewa ni mutu.
**Gniaba, Gniapa.**
  **Gniabagniaba** (= Niada in Kij.).
  **Gniabira,** *v. rel.*
**Gniada** (Kid., **Niada**), for anything.
**Gniafula,** or **Gniafura** (= Muaula?).
**Gniagnania,** *v.a.* (Kir., Voka). *See* Piga. Spoil, rob with violence; to take up, as an instrument, with a view to do violence.

  **Gniagnianira** (= Gniagnanira?). Signiagnianireni gafiani muenezane.
**Gniaka,** *v.a.* (= Niaka, snatch; Ku gnia?). Mue yudzigniaka muana kuku. Muana wari yunaria niama, ela mue yukudza i 'niaka. Na Kosi yuguira kuku, ela ka'niaka niama.
  **Gniakira,** (1) *v.d.* Reha ni-ki-gniakire uwe kuidima, una-ki-fimba. Ku gniakira kavu kuamba ya alamuke. Ku gniakira kivinda (= Kij., Ku toolia ganda).
  (2) To be swift in going. Gnania yunaenenda ku niakira (= lilima and signia).
  **Gniakua,** *v.p.* Niama yangu idzivokua idzi'niakua ni mue.
**Gniala.** *See* Ku niala.
  **Gniasa.** *See* Ku niala.
**Gniamala.** *See* Niamala.
  **Gniamarira.** *See* Niamala.
  **Gniamasa.** *See* Niamala.
  **Gniemere.** *See* Niamala.
**Gniegera** (Kidigo), *v.n.* (= Gniegniesa and Wawa in Kir.), to itch.
**Gniegniesa** (= Ku gniegera in Kidigo). *See* Diekedia. (1) *v.a.*, to tickle.
(2) *v.n.*, to itch. Ku gniegniesa ni muirini kuegnie, ela mutu aki-ku-henda hivi, yuna-ku-diekedia.
**Gniekererua.** *See* Ku gnia.
**Gniekula,** *v.a.* *See* Muafula. To tear off as meat.
  **Gniekua,** *v.n.* Nidzigniekula, ikagniekuka katite; be ni hara ahoho a niumbani ahendao hifio-ku gniekula niama.
  **Gniekulua,** *v.p.* Muhanda umenga udzigniekulua-be niuni 'ye adziehenda-fio, asiesema? Niama idzigniekulua niani?
  **Gniekurika,** *v.n.* Londani kifiu, mu-ni-pe, nikatire niama hi, ka-i-gniekurika.
  **Gniekurira,** *v.d.* Ndzo-kuno, ni-ku-gniekurire kaniama, udade. Ni-gniekurira kaniama katite, u-ni-pe (in Kid., Ni-fudzurira).
  **Gniekurirua,** *v.p.* Nidzikuenda vatu vasiku, nikadikisa niama, be nikagniekurirua kaniama katite.
**Gniela.** *See* Gnia.
**Gniemere.** *See* Niemere.
**Gniense,** *n.* (ya, za), the fruit of the mugniense tree. It is eaten in time of famine.
**Gniere,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a; Gniere hiyu, sing.; Gniere hia, pl.). Gniere ka-dza-hakisua mbira, Sudi aende ugnaroni kuansa, be akimala ugnaro, ndo ahakisuavo mbira.
**Gnierera.** *See* Gnia.
  **Gnierereka.** *See* Gnia.
  **Gniesa.** *See* Gnia.
  **Gniewa.** *See* Gnia.
**Gnieregniere,** *n.* Ku guirua ni muiri wa gnieregniere.
**Gnieta,** *v.a.*, to be naughty, wanton.
  **Gnietagnieta.** Ku gnietagnieta ko a-ri-ko-na-ko, ela si kubomu e! yunudziria, be yugnietera-ni vira?
  **Gnietera,** *v.* *See* Muasi. (K.) To rail, to prank; and Nietera, deride, flout. Ndizo agnieterazo gnombe.
  **Gnietesa.** *See* Kignietesa.
**Gnigni** (= Kid., Ngoro).
**Gnignignisa,** *v.a.* *See* Dingidia. Ku gnignignisa ndzuga. The word is getting obsolete, being superseded by Dingidia.
**Gnignira,** (1) *v.a.*
(2) *v.n.* *See* Gniunira.
**Gnimbo** (= Viliko?). *See* Nimbo. Gnania yunaimba, yuna gnimbo.
**Gnindi,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lurindi.
**Gniognoniera,** *v.n.*, to feel heavy and languid; to be overdone with food. Kidziifua muno, kidzigniognoniera chakuria. Magulu gana-ni-gniognoni-

## [PDF Page 119 — Dictionary Page 106 (Gni — Gob)]

  era, siidima ku enenda. Muiri rero siwesi unamerera una-ni-gniognoniera, kama hensi ku uka, uhensa ku sagala hebu ku lala tu.
  **Gniognonierua,** *v.p.* M'anangu yudzi gniognonierua ni magulu, kaidima ku enenda, My child is heavy in his feet; he cannot go.
  **Gniognorera** (Kid.), *v.n.* (in Kij., Ku gniognonia). *See* Gniognoniera. To slacken, to be weary, especially the legs.
  **Gniognonio,** *n.*, weariness, weakness. Nawe una gniognonio dza muche m'egnie mimba?
**Gniotola,** *v.a.* (= Hunda). *See* Niotola; Ku dzuluvuka; Ku toka; Ku katika. To pluck off. Used of what breaks off easily from ripeness or brittleness. Ku gniotola isu, when ripe; but Ku dzaniula isu, when green. Ku gniotola mapapayu; with these Ku hunda also is used. Ku gniotola makodza ga dumbaku. Ku funsa and Ku hunda may be used as well.
  **Gniotoka,** *v.n.*, to break off by itself, to fall off as fruit in small quantities. Maembe gadziguiotoka, gadzebua (said of a few, but when the ground seems covered with them, Vukuhika or Kutika is used). Nazi zidzigniotoka, zidzebua, A few cocoa-nuts have broken off and fallen down. Kidzigniotoka chala kimenga cha isu, ela vingi ni kuvu kuhika. Ni-gniotorera isu, nirie.
  **Gniotolua,** *v.p.* Maembe gahenda gniotolua.
  **Gniotorera,** *v.d.*
**Gniri,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name of a species of bird, remarkable for its fine tail-feathers, which are always used for decorating the kiru. It is said to have a black neck and a white body. It is rarely seen, and only in forests. Ku gniririka in Kisugula means, to flee.
**Gnirigniri,** *adj.*, smooth. Madzi ga, gniri gniri gniri ei! ganaogofiu, vatu hivo vana kina. Gnombe hi ikanona, i gniri gniri.
**Gniukula,** *v.a.* *See* Gniekula. (K.) To cramp, convulse, squeeze.
**Gniutika** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Doncheka in Kns.), (1) to fix loosely an arrow-head.
(2) To hit slightly. Yudzi-m-gniutika tu, ka-m-fumagire.
**Gno.** Sinda-ku-va gno.
**Gnoda.** Ndzo! u-ni-gnode nierezangu. Niere za ku gnoda na za ku luka.
  **Gnodua,** *v.p.* Yudzignodua (= Yudzisukua niere).
**Gnogna,** *v.a.* (= Mumenga yunaenga yoma). *See* Usiri; Yoma. To hum, to buzz.
**Gnognogniera.**
**Gnola,** *v.a.*, to pluck out.
  **Gnoreka,** *v.n.*
  **Gnorera,** *v.d.*
  **Gnorerana,** *v. reit.* (= Ndo ku gnorerana niumba ku gnola kivesa).
  **Gnorerua,** *v.p.*
**Gnombe,** *n.* (ya, za), a bull, a cow, an ox. Muana gnombe, A calf. Vachira rigombe chuche. Dim., Kagombe and Kigombe; magn., Gombe and Rigombe.
**Gnongo,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lugnongo.
**Gnonsi,** *n.* (ya, za, and also wa, pl. *id.* and Ma-), a sheep.
**Gnugnunika** (= Kembera; Mutamuta; Machiraago, etc.). *See* Baki; Kuignia; Nugnunika.
**Go,** *prep.* *See* Su; Modidimuko. That.
**Goba,** *n.* (pl. Ma-).
**Gobia, Kobia,** *v.* Ku gobia papayu.
**Gobola, Kobola,** *v.a.* Ku gobola madzere (= Kins., ku gobora bamanga). Kala-

## [PDF Page 120 — Dictionary Page 107 (Gob — Gog)]

  konche ni ku gobola mbengeo ya muado, akaria mavalala ga niuchi.
  **Goboka, Koboka,** *v.n.*
**Goboa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kidzoe; Kigua. Such muhama-stalks, the juice of which is not sweet, and therefore are not chewed.
**Goda,** *v.a.*, to suck, to suckle. Ai! muana gnombe yunagoda yudzireherua yunagoda masia. Yunavesa kare ku amua, basi mameye yudzikudza yunagoda masia muana.
**Godola.** Ku godola madzo, To gloat over.
  **Godorera,** *v.d.* Una-ni-godorera madzo nidzi-ku-henda-dze? Hangu dzana Aravai adziricha ku godorera atu madzo-kuani ni dambi, ukihenda hifio undaguirua ni Kiravo cha msafula; ela muanao, akihenda utu ui, be una-m-godorera madzo, ku-mu-ogofia kama a-m-pigaye.
**Godza,** or **Kodza,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-; but Kodza (za) is the pl. of Lugodza), a leaf.
**Godza** (Kidigo), *v.n.* (= Rinda in Kir.). to wait. U-ni-godze-niredza hudze-huwihe.
  **Godzera,** *v.d.*, to wait for. Ku-m-rinda mutu ni ku-m-godzera.
**Godza, Kodza,** *v.a.*, (1) to roll up; (2) to gather up with between the fingers, a cloth. Ku godza kidzeka.
  **Godzeka, Kodzeka,** *v.n.* Ndzoni! mu-ni-afuise kidzeka ku godza, ka-ki-godzeka ni heche yangu.
  **Godzera, Kodzera,** *v.d.* Ka-ni-godzerani singe rangu, risabanangika na umande.
**Godzo,** *n.*, the name given to the loma while they are in the act of digging for it—from the superstitious dread that, if they called it by its real name, it would go further from them in its hole, and, if caught, would not prove as fat as it ought to be! A lamentation also is held over it when killed. Loma aki-m-dzimba, ni ku-mu-iha godzo.
**Godzoka,** or **Kodzoka,** *v.n.*
  **Godzola, Kodzola,** *v.* Reha hirira kasha kuno? Resp., Sinda-ri-godzola (= Sinda-ri-idima). Kilariro hiki uvonda, usage? Resp., A-sindagodzola ku vonda. Rero kahukakodzola ku henda chunga (= Rero kahuka idima, or, wesa).
**Godzola,** *v.n.* (= Ku godza), to pass water, to urinate, to stale.
  **Godzoreka,** *v.n.* Nidziamba nigodzole, ela vana atu, ka-va-godzoreka.
  **Godzorera,** *v.d.* Muana hiyu yudzi-ni-godzorera makodzo.
  (2) *Sperma profundens* (vir).
  **Godzorerua,** *v.p.* Nidzigodzorerua ni muana.
**Gofi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Midafu. Gofi ra ndani uriro, urihi, etc.
**Gofia,** *v.a.* (= Hegera; Kuafia). *See* Dzongoka; Kolia. Yunagofia yunagomba kikuao. Be ukigofia maneno fio, u-mumidzi hebudze?
  **Gofiana,** *v. reit.* Atu hia adzi migniana-adzigofiana, ela kavana adziedieka muyawe ngufusao sikarakara. Der., Lugofia.
**Gogo,** *n.* *See* Muanga.
**Gogo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) the trunk of a tree.
(2) The stocks, a machine for confining the legs.
**Gogoda,** *v.a.* *See* Ku gogoda meno; Vinionda. To crunch. Mutu akiria akihafuna kitu chomu chosi-be ni ku gogoda. Yuhanda gogodo gogodo, etc. Mutu iye yunagogoda musosa. Yudzigogoda meno kua koro.
  **Gogodeka,** *v.n.* *See* Nazi; Mfungu. To admit of crunching. Musosa hiu unagogodeka hebudze? Resp., Ka-u-gogodeka.
**Gogolo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Gogo,

## [PDF Page 121 — Dictionary Page 108 (Gog — Gol)]

  2), the stocks. Yudzipigua hebu yudzikotua gogolo.
**Gogomoka,** *v.n.*, to be on the wane. Muezi ugogomoka (= dodoa in Kins.) unaingira ndaniunalonda ku sira. *See* Muezi.
**Gogoreka,** *v.n.*, to cackle. Kuku hiye yunadieka, nidzi-m-sikira yunagogoreka.
**Gogota,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Ku era niuni), a bird. Its cry is, "Ndi nda nde!"
**Gogota,** *v.a.* *See* Momu; Kola. (1) (K.) To strike; of birds, to peck. N'enda nika gogote, kakurimika, ni komu be niku henda gogota. Nidzigogota vadide vivi.
(2) (= Ku meno). (K.) To gnash. Kuku hiyu wari akikarira, ela yudzigogota ana (= Yudzifiala yudziengula).
  **Gogotera.** *See* Halahala. Nidzi-m-gogotera kuamba asihende utu hio. Dambi rari ridzikala ringi, basi Mulungu akidza-a-kokotera hi fio.
  **Gogoterua,** *v.p.* Amasai kudza Ravai ku ulaga atu dzi nsima, ndo ku kokoterua ni Mulungu, kua dambi ku kala ringi.
**Goja,** *v.* Sikari anagoja ngome. Der., Kigojo, or Kigocho.
**Goka** (Kid.), *v.n.*, to be sleepy.
**Gola.** Machero ni kuri, be rero hu'enda gola; machero hurie kuri. Atu akapiga mahungue, kiasi cha mane hebu madzano, akanoa, be ndo ku gola. Angue: Huenda lola kirenge, kuamba andahenda cha tahu, hebu cha kumi, huka-ki-manie.
**Goli,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a play with vidagna via nazi put into small hollows; to gamble.
**Golo, Kolo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Golo ra kuku hiri ndiro ririro na ana hia osi niakue.
**Golola,** *v.a.* *See* Kidzumbi; Kishongo. To stretch, to straighten. Ku golola kigulu. Ku golola mufui-kuamba urungarare. Nagolola muhi na moho, I straighten a tree, or stick, with fire. Na-u-zira, ni-u-golole, I heat it that I may straighten it. Ku-dzi-golola, To stretch one's self. N'enda nikakome hivo, nigolole magulu. Ku golola kigulu. *See* Fumuririka.
  **Goloka,** *v.n.*, to be straight. Ku goloka na muhi na muriango.
  **Golokera,** *v.d.*, to be straight, equal to, in the sense of justice. Hangu dzana kakuna maalamusi madzo kaviri kuehu Ravai; mutu huya arie mulongo-ela akipata vitu via ku ukusha afiere, basi yunaalamulua to, yunahewa-geri, nenore rina-m-golokera. Mariadzi ndo adzogo ga chisa mbere, be kamania ku alamula.
  **Goloza,** *v.a.* *See* Bora. To stretch out, to straighten. M-golozeni hu-mu-vinde. Ku goloza magulu. Ku goloza mala. Ku goloza njira. Gnombe vara udzavoenenda nayo, idzigolosa ndjira, hebu idzihenda ubishi? Resp., Ka-i-kagoloza nchira; idzi-ni-lafia malo hata idzila ngufu. Trop., Ku goloza maneno (= Ku alamula keri). Ku goloza umiro. Yudzigoloza moyo, yudzi-ni-pa kitu. Dzagula ri goloza ro moyo; lit. Choose that which straightens the heart; *i.e.* which pleases you.
  **Golozera,** *v.d.*, to stretch out to, to make straight, equal to. Yudzi-ni-golozera mukono ku-ni-pa kitu. Rero gnania yudzi-ni-golozera maneno to na kuamba ndo agombavio kula dziku-angari mualamusi mbomu yudzigomba ubanga wa Mungu.
**Golovolo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Ludaba. The sheath which encloses the twigs on which are the flower-buds of a palm tree. Also called bambangao.

## [PDF Page 122 — Dictionary Page 109 (Gom — Gon)]

  Golovolo ni gofi ra vanda. Golovolo ra mugomba, The rind of a banana tree.
**Goma,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Mgoma. A woman who is not a virgin.
**Goma,** *n.* (ra), a large drum (a term of abuse).
**Goma,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kimo. Goma ra gnombe; ra kare na kare (= Kiveti cha gnombe). Goma ra gnombe hiri rinaviala to. *See* Ame. Waviala goma ra muche (= Kidzana kisiho, kiguiriguiri), She bore a bouncing girl. Nidziona goma ra muche-bomu. Dim., Kagoma; Kigoma.
**Goma,** *v.n.*, to end, to terminate. Uina udzigoma; but, Njira idzisika hiva. Nidzidua njira hata ikagoma hivara (= koma and sika).
  **Gomala, Komala,** *adj.* *See* Mafuadzi; Mugumo. Mature. Hangu dzana yudzikomala, yudzikala mudumia.
  **Gomana, Komana** (Kig., but used in Kir.), *v.* (= Gutana; Onana; and Ku visania njirani in Kir. proper), to meet, to come up one to another.
  **Gomasa, Komaza,** *v.a.*, to abuse, to curse. Gnania musiku yunagomaza vitu to.
  **Gomeza, Komeza.** Nidzi-m-gomeza-kuamba machero asigombe maneno higo.
  **Gomezana, Komezana.**
  **Gomezania, Komezania,** *v. reit.*, to execrate one another. The one says, Goma hiwe! The other replies, Goma nawe!
  **Gomezua, Komezua,** *v.p.* *See* Goma.
**Gome,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) an overhanging rock.
(2) A chip. Vatu hivo vana gome bomu. Gome ra muhi, A chip of wood. Gome ralonda vatu, vadzavo vogoka. Abe Gonge wakuenda goma Lunguja na Musungu, basi rero udziingira, or, yudzikudza. N'enda nika kome Ruruma, be ni uye. Yudziamba, yun'enda koma Ruruma, be auye. Der., Ngome.
**Gomia, Komia,** *v.a.* (= Gigisa?). *See* Munoadzi. To make an end of, to stop one in one's wits; *i.e.* to perplex. Kakomia ku, He stops not to—a standing expression, meaning, no sooner than.
**Gomoka,** *v.n.*, to flounder, to tumble, to break off or down. Gopue ridzigomoka (= omoka). Tahi idzigomoka (= omoka). Ulongo udzigomoka (= omoka, also = ganduka), but this latter is less frequently used.
  **Gomola,** *v.a.*, to demolish. Uere ukilonda ku gomoka wegnie be nika u gomola.
  **Gomomera.**
**Gomba,** *v.n.* *See* Lola, to look. To speak. Ku gomba vioma. Adze m'egnie, agombe na vio-m-henda, na mi nigombe a-vio-ni-henda.
  **Gombeka,** *v.n.*, to be spoken. Maneno higa ka-ga-gombeka, ni mai.
  **Gombera.** *See* Rondzofia. Muche una-m-gombera. Uchi ni ku kombera.
  **Gomberana,** *v. reit.* *See* Sindikana.
  **Gombola, Kombola,** *v.a.*, to redeem.
**Gombe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a large cow or bullock. Magn. of Gnombe.
**Gombo, Kombo,** *n.* (ra). Gombo ka-ri-ingirakaya. Niama hino ni gombo hebu ni wa ku fumagua? Ni kombo-ikafua yegnie. Niama ya gombo siria.
**Gonda,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Kagonda; Kigonda; Rigonda).
**Gonda,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Gundaya. (1) Little bags or cases made of milala, into which pebbles are put. A number of them tied round the legs serves as a sort of music to young people in dancing. Adana na ahoho

## [PDF Page 123 — Dictionary Page 110 (Gon — Gor)]

  akifuina uira wa dumbui, basi ndivo afualavo magonda.
  (2) (Kidigo) (= Kolokovue in Kir.), the name of a species of crab. The Wadigo eat it, but the Warabai do not.
**Gondaya** (= Gundaya).
**Gonde.** *See* Konde.
**Gonde,** or **Gonje.**
**Gondoefia, Kondoefia** (Ku konda in Kir.). Ku-m-kondoefia mutu tove. Yudzinena maneno mangu-angu, ka ka gondoefia. Ku kondoefia maneno ni ku gomba ukiaza. Yunusoma ku kondoefia.
  **Gondoera, Kondoera,** *v.n.* Mdzuzi wa ku gondoera. Wino ukidzorua, unagondoera, ka-u-uka. N dz gondoerua ni mafuha ga gnombe, ga thugnia.
  **Gondoeza, Kondoeza** (Kid.). Ku-mu-gondoeza mutu tove. Ku gondoeza maneno.
**Gonga,** *v.a.*, to strike, to beat, to become old (?). Ku piga gonga (= Ku muta gonga, and Ku jita gonga).
**Gongo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a club. Ku-m-piga mutu mugongo. Dim., Kagongo; Kigongo.
**Gongolo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (Jongo in Kij.), a hump, a boss. Gongolo ni ku-dzi-kunsa, rikakala dza ri-dza-ro kufua. Dim., Kagongolo; Kigongolo; magn., Rigongolo.
**Gongoloka,** *v.n.*
**Gongolola.**
**Gongonda.** *See* Mbanga.
**Gongoro.** Gongoro ra gnombe.
**Goniola, Koniola,** *v.a.* (= Kobola; Kuaniula), to scrape, to scratch.
  **Gonioka, Konioka,** *v.n.*, to get a scratch.
  **Goniokera, Koniokera,** *v.n.* Madzere gadziuma hata gadzigoniokera.
**Gopoka, Kopoka,** *v.n.* Madzere nidzi-ga-vonda-gadzigopoka wisua wa mbere. Nidzijita madzere, gadziifua, gadziahuka ahuka-hata magovi gadzigopoka.
  **Gopola, Kopola.** *See* Govi. Ku gopola renge. Mutu uki-m-fioga-kuna 'budi uda-m-gopola kikonde. Ku gopola ni muhi.
**Gopue,** *n.* (= Kij., Handaki), a pit, a dry ditch, a trench dug round the hut.
**Gora,** *n.* (ya, za, and ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kuruja. A piece of cloth. Gora ya Americano. Gora ra nguo.
**Goragora** (= Ngolangola). Mutu yudzidzukirua, be una-m-goragora, kuamba ariche koro, ahende mbasi.
**Goroa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a species of bird; (K.) sparrow. Magoroa higa ganaaka kidzunchi. Goroa rina kidzudzu, kidza kina kidzoa chiru.
**Goroadzaka,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the goroa of the forest, the forest being its favourite abode. This has no bush, and is of a different colour from the goroa.
**Gorofu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), what is emaciated in men and animals. Gorofu hiri ka-ri-rika. Gnania wari mkongo, akaonda-yudzikala gorofu.
**Goromue,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a species of lizard remarkable for its deafness, and for the cleanness of its cave. Magoromue higa gakadzusa uina dze dze dze dze dze; hata varatu muhalani vakue asagalavo aka-va-fiera navo vakadzuka dze. It is therefore also called kifiera muhala. Nidzi-mu-ona goromue, akifiera muhala. It sweeps with its tail its cave, as well as the place before it where it stops to bask in the sun. Kuna masikiro we; u-goromue!
**Gororeka,** *v.n.* (= Sororeka). *See* Ridambi; Golola (mi fui).
**Gororeza,** *v.a.* (= Dororeza). Yugororeza nguo (= amba).
