## [PDF Page 124 — Dictionary Page 111 (Gos — Gua)]

**Gosa,** *v.a.* *See* Gola. To dandle.
**Gosa,** *v.a.* and *n.*
  **Gosana.**
  **Goseka.**
  **Gosekana.**
  **Gosera.**
  **Gosesira.**
**Gosi,** *adj.*, all. Maneno gosi.
**Gosigosi.**
**Gota,** *v.a.* (= Fumbula; Kidzoa ni ku gota; but, Kigonga ni ku kota). *See* Kunche; Eza; Mignio. To knock. Ku-m-gota kigota. To knock one with the knuckles. Mihi si mingi, ni mitembe, ka-i-nda gota. Kibaria kidzigota. Udzi-ni-gota kidzoa, We have knocked heads together. Osi pia adzigota, mishigo ku dzukula.
  **Gotana,** *v. reit.* (1) to knock one another with the knuckles, vigota.
  (2) Trop., to put heads together (for consultation). Hudzi gotana vidzoa, neno hiro ridzikula menga, We put our heads together, we have come to an agreement.
**Gotegote,** *n.* (= Pigepige). Only used in the prov., Gotegote rinamala muiri, Continual knocking finishes the body. Pigepige is more generally used.
**Gotola** (Kir.), (1) *v.a.* and *n.* (= Ku dokola), to take off, as a scab from a wound; to eat greedily, to be eager to devour. Yudzidikisa chakuria-be yudzihenda gotola, yudzihenda ria muafu muafu, kana haya yuna moyo. Ana a Dume, ndio ariao ku gotola; be akiria, ahenda fognafogna. Ku gotola kikoko cha kironda, ku lafia ufira, To take off the scab from a sore in order to take out the matter.
(2) (Kid.) (= Ku mala in Kir.), to finish.
  **Gotoka,** *v.n.* Gnania ni m'omu, kagotoka, kalafia kitu.
**Gova,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Muvilivili. Bark, rind; (K.) cuttings, parings, shivers. Dim., Kigova.
**Govi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) the skin of an animal.
(2) A bit of skin knocked off. Nidzigopolua ni muhi, vadziuka govi, or, kikonde be na-ri-gata; or, Nidzipigua ni muhi, vadziuka govi-be nalonda kifiu, ni-ri-gata. Nidzikuala, nidziuka govi.
**Govu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Mudzovi; Niambara. A cancer.
**Goya** (?), *adj.*, sensual.
**Grafu, Garafu,** *n.* (ya, za), cloves. The Wanika know them, but none are growing in their country.
**Gu,** *n.* (pl. Ma-), the foot.
**Gua,** *v.n.* (= Ku kua). *See* Bua. To fall. Mutu yudzekua, The man has fallen. Dzi ikakua-i-herera, ka-i-na mirima. Vatu hiva vakakua, va-herera. Ueru hiu ukokua-u-herera, ka-u-na mirima wala ka-u-na ndundu.
  **Guafia, Kuavia.** Yudziguafia maneno.
  **Guala, Kuala,** *v.n.*, to stumble, to be ready to fall.
  **Guaza, Kuaza,** *v.*, to make stumble, to make fall.
**Gua, Kua,** *v.a.* Ku kua mzigo, in contradistinction to Ku ereka.
  **Guika, Kuika,** *v.n.* Musigo hiu ka-u-guiga, ni mbomu.
**Gua,** *v.a.* *See* Chera. To peel, to pare; to break open the pods of beans. Mudzi-zi-gua sa kunde? Resp., A-Kahuka zi-gua; zi mumo na magandage, ka-zi-ka guiwa ni mutu. Ku gua nanazi, isu, mugasija.
  **Guika,** *v.n.* Dzana nahunda mboga za podzo nikiamba: ninadza nigue, nichete; lola vino kunacha nikiambua; m'ana wa ame gnania ni mukongo, be

  nikakuenda m-lola hata nauya kudzedzua; mboga ka-zi-ka guika, zi mumo na kavuye.

  **Guirua,** *v.p.* Mbalazi hizi nidzihenda guirua ni mayo.
  **Guiwa,** *v.p.* *See* Lukadza.
**Gua** (Kid.), *v.a.* (Guua = Kns., Guula; Kunkua). *See* Gaula.
**Guachira** (Kid.) (= Buakia in Kij.; Buirira in Kns.).
  **Guachisa,** *v.a.* (= Kuakisa), to plan.
  **Guachisana,** *v. reit.*
**Guachula,** *v.a.*, to give a private sign by a touch.
**Guafulo,** *n.* (= Gafula in Kij.). Neno ra guafulo.
**Guafumira,** *v.a.*, to fall upon, to bounce upon.
**Guangula,** *v.a.* (= Wari; Kns., Ra niangu).
**Guaniula,** *v.a.* (= Ganiula in Kid.), to graze, to touch or rub slightly in passing. Mufui hiu udzi-ni-kuaniula; but, Muiya udzi-ni-kuarura, This arrow has grazed me; but, A thorn has scratched me.
**Guarura.** *See* Guala.
**Guasa** and **Guasiwa** (= Kuala). Midzanga ina-ni-guasa kanoani.
**Guava,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the armpit. Ya mutu, ya kuku, ya gnombe, Of man, of a fowl, of an ox. Dim., Kiguaba.
**Guba** (?).
**Gubu.** *See* Yungumika.
**Gubugubu.** *See* Dibudibu.
**Gubula,** *v.a.* Vidzere ndio agubulao minazi.
**Gude,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of bird. Machira ga dziloni, mudzeria viakuria kare, basi munalonda, ku lala, ndo Magude gariravo-atu akaamba. Magude higo gana vosa niungu mahako. Gude ka-ri-kaingira kaya. Mutu agudie gudie.
**Gudiagudia,** *v.a.* Ku gudiagudia dzenga.
**Gudiugudiu.** Lola muana hiyu, yunanoa uchi kikafiri, akinoa yuhenda anamira: gudiugudiu-dza kuamba yunasolua.
  **Gudiula,** *v.a.*, to gulp down, to guzzle. Only used of drink. Be uchi unahenda gudiula, kunoa pore, unasolua niani?
**Gufuli, Kufuli,** *n.* (ya, za, Kufuli hiri; pl. Makufuli, higa) (= Kubuli), a lock.
**Gugu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (in Kir., Mugugu), a species of vulture. It goes after madzonsoka, madali, pugu, pania, during the night, and takes chickens also early in the morning, but sleeps during the day. Vana gugu hiva ka-va-chirika. Ela dzi hiyi ina magugu.
**Gugumuka,** *v.n.*, to laugh with restraint, to titter. Gnania yudzigomba neno-ata adzigugumuka-ela kadzesia atu e? Nidziamba nidzeke-ela nikidzeka ni vi-be nidzidzudzumu-ka.
**Guguna,** *v.a.*
**Gugusa** (Kid. ?), *v.a.* (= Kigugusi in Kir.), to drag along. Ku gugusa njirani.
**Guguta,** (1) *v.a.* *See* Kukuta. To shake out. Gnania yudzifiola hata yudziguguta moyowe, Gnania has been scolding until she has emptied herself—until she has shaken out all. Nidzivavika, hata nidziguguta-hata nidzihenda vavika niongo madzi mavuvu.
(2) *v.n.* Madzere gadzi kukuta (= Gadzila mura choani).
**Gugutika,** *v.n.*, to reel, from being intoxicated. *See* Hetereka. Gnania yudzenoa uchi ungi, yudzirea, yuenda, or, wenda akigugutika. Ai-yudzenoa yudzirea mdumia hiye, wendo ukidzugutika, ela kadzenoa uchi ungi mdumia'ye (for, iye).

  **Gugutira,** *v. rel.* Mifai yangu udzi-i-gugutirani. Resp., Nidzila fia ku-i-lola tu, ela usiambe nalafia ku-i-hala-a. Resp., Be adzie-kuamba, u-i-lafie, niani? udzihenda vi. Resp., Be na kuamba nidzihenda vi-basi nidzikosa.
  **Gugutisa,** *v.a.*, (1) (Kid.). Gnania yudzi-dzi-gugutiza yamba. Ku dzi binikiza nguo.
  (2) (Kir.) *See* Futa. Ku-m-kukutisa mutu uchi.
**Guika.** *See* Gua.
**Guira.** *See* Gua.
**Guira,** *v.a.* *See* Madzadzigo. To seize, to lay hold of; to fix on a day, etc. Trop., to take to anything. Ku guira zani, To meet with an accident. *See* Sani. Usena, cleave, cohere, adhere. Ku guira usena. Hiko Duruma sina vatu va ku fikira be namba: ni-ku-guire usena, dziku nikidza, ni bade va ku fikira. Resp., A-usena ka-u-kahalua. Mukodo udziguira nongo, udzikala muiru. Muhambo udziguira, The trap has caught. *See* Ku fiuka. Nidzizignia hata nika-m-guira njirani, I ran until I overtook him. Trop., Nidziguira dziku. Nidzikuenda guira dziku. Nidzikuenda guira mani. Ku-dzi-guira to, To be in readiness, to get one's self ready. Ku guira mukono, To seize by the hand. Trop., to take care of. *See* Chiachia.
  **Guiraguira,** *v. reit.* Ku-dzi-guiraguira (= Ku-dzi-dunsa), To attend to one's self, to take care as to one's person with regard to dress and ornaments, grease and oil.
  **Guirana,** *v. ref.*, to seize on another.
  **Guirika.**
  **Guirira,** (1) *v.d.* or *rel.* *See* Kidzeko. To seize to or for another. Hata kuku hiyu-u-ni-guirire, nami nendaguira angina. Ni-guirira lufuiho, nivagale.
  (2) *v.a.* Guirira nguso hi hino nisirire. Guirira muganganga, nihangike ngusoni.
  **Guiririra,** (1) *v.d.* Ndzo-u-ni-guiririre niuni-ne-ndakoma hivara, niihuavo, be niuye. Ku-m-guiririra mutu urinsi; or, Ku-m-guirira urinsi.
  (2) *v.n.*, to stick fast. Mufui ka-u-kaguiririra, niama si wako. Mufui ukikala ukaguiririra, ka-u-kabuadzi, basi hata niama akafumagua ni mutu mungine, aki-mu-ulaga, niama hiye ni wako; kuani ndiwe udzaye-mu-ansa.
  **Guiririsa** (= Guiririra, 2).
  **Guirua,** *v.p.* Ku guirua ni haya, To be seized with shame.
  **Guiza,** *v.a.* *See* Dengeva. Yudzi-ni-guisa haya. Ku-m-guiza njira. Ku guiza oga. Yudzigomba maneno mai ga ku hukana, hata yudzi-ni-guiza haya. Lola kosi! nguo yangu udzi-i-guiza kama, or, nongo. Ndiye adzieguiza moho, ukiguira dzandzala hata ukokuenda dzoma niumba ni zani. Niama hi u-dza-yo henda-i-nangananga uki-i-guiza nongo, be sihensi. Enenda naye hata u-m-guize njira bomu, basi hiko yundaenenda hecheye, uwe uuye.
  **Guizua.** Yudzihala kitu cha mutu, hata m'egnie yunaupuka, be aka-ki-dieka, ai! yudzignizua haya; atu adzi-m-dzeka. Der., Guiru; Kiguiriguiri; Mguisi.
**Guiru,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a greedy desire, a violent longing after meat only. With regard to other food, Moyo is used. Muna maguiru muno muimui.
**Gula** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Chula and Chulua in Kir.), a toad.

## [PDF Page 127 — Dictionary Page 114 (Gul — Gum)]

**Gula, Kula,** *v.n.*, to grow. Ku kula kowe. Ku futa ndefu.
  **Gurira,** *v.d.* Vitu hivi vidzi-ni-gurira haraka. Muana hiyu na-m-vesa ni mutite vino yudzikala mbomu, kakakomia ku-ni-gurira.
  **Gusa,** *v.a.* *See* Kadudusi. (1) To make grow. Mfula hino inagusa vitu haraka. Vatu hiva ni ganso-vari vakifugua gnombe, be vanagusa vitu, ka-vi-neneka.
  (2) To enlarge the mind, to soothe, to comfort. Nidziamba nihende utu ubomu wa kondo, ela gnania musiku ndiye adzeye-ni-gusa moyo, nikarida; ela ku amba si iye ku-ni-gania, ningari nidziulaga mutu, hebu nika uladzua mimi.
  **Gusania,** *v.a.*, to gather, to call together.
**Gula,** *v.a.*, to buy. Munazi ni ku kula, na muhoho ni ku kula, ela mutu yunagula minazi.
  **Gulua,** *v.p.*, to be bought.
  **Gurika,** *v.n.* Nidziamba nigule-ela ka-ki-gurika, kina kima, kibomu. Kituche yudzi-ki-kuesa kima-be ka-ki-ka gurika. Kitu hiki ki-hali, ka-ki-gurika; ki-ngufu, rorare ni romu.
  **Gurira,** *v. rel.* Na-m-gurira gnania kitu hikino, yuna-ki-londa. A., Mbuzi hino una-i-gusa, ni-ku-gurire hebudze? Resp. B., Na-i-gusa reale; ka-i-dza-pata muhidaji tu ku gula. A., Ah-kuamba ni reale, nina-yo; ndakudza ni-ku-gurire, nihende mbeyu; kuani-sigurira kuria, nagurira mbeyu? B., Ah-kuamba ni hifio, basi, hudzipatana kare; ukidza, udza, kua ku hala mbuzi tu, kavana maneno kahiri.
  **Gurirua,** *v.p.*
  **Gusa, Guza,** *v.a.* *See* Fuluka. To sell.
  **Gusana,** or **Guzana,** *v. ref.*, to sell one another.
  **Gusania, Guzania,** *v.*, to sell each other.
  **Gusika, Guzika,** *v.n.* Mudumua hiye ka guzika, yuna-ni-fa sana adi. Muhama ka-u-gusika hikara, ka-u-na thora.
  **Gusira, Guzira,** *v. rel.*, to sell to or for any one. Na-mu-gusira reale yangu, naye akiamba; ndzo, ni-ku-gurire, be nik'enda ku-ni-susurisa tu na nchira; be mino nda-i-gusa kungine.
  **Gusirana, Guzirana,** or **Gusirania.** Ana gusirana vavo, anagomba, be kadzamkue ku dosa, or, afikana.
  **Gusirua, Guzirua.** A. yudzi gusirua gnombe ni? B., Be yudzikuenda i-lola, agule.
  **Gusua, Guzua,** *v.p.*
**Gulu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Magulu) (= Gulu ridzi hendo hende). *See* Kigulu. The leg. Ku henda gulu. Lola kigulu rikala gulu.
**Guma, Kuma** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Buma in Kir.).
**Gumia, Kumia,** *v.a.* (in Kid., Nadza madzena; in Kns., Dantamusira), (1) to praise, to extol.
(2) To exaggerate.
  **Gumira, Kumira,** *n.*, places.
**Gumo,** *n.* (= Ra mugumo). N'enda nikademe gumo, nikaite, muakani ninda-dzi-binikisa mfula, ni mufuri wa mfula. Ni-pani-ro gumo rangu, ni-dzi-binikise mfula, nienende. Gumo uki-ri-kunsula, be ri-ngakana mufuri wegnie.
**Gumba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Magumba). *See* Kigumba. A large arrow-head. Gumba hiri ni ridzo ra ku fumagira ngulue. A gumba ni bomu rino. Gumba si bomu riri? A ni bomu we? A., Udzi-ki-gumba kirenge changu, kidzebua uchi udzimuagika? B. Resp., A-sika-ki-ona nidzihenda kua-

## [PDF Page 128 — Dictionary Page 115 (Gum — Gun)]

  la, ela sika-ki-uchirira. A., Udzi-ki-uchirira u mulongo? B., Gamba una-ni-amba hifio-be nidzi-ki-uchirira kamoe kamoe-be utaka-ro-henda. Basi ika kala kondo vavo. *See* Kidzupo. Lasima ya ku hala kitu cha mutu; ka-i-ni-kumba.
**Gumbo,** *n.* (ra). Si ndzala ni gumbo. Ridzikala gumbo si ndzala kaviri; kakuna kitu korokoro; ndi-vo atu agusana-vo.
**Gumigumi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Guna,** *v.n.* *See* Kuignia. To give a slight growl or sound of disapprobation. Kahikahi ya mongo ka-va-gunika, ka-va-fikirika sodi ama sudi ugunue ni mutu. Nasi hi ka-i-gunika-ichari nognona, ka-i-dza komala ku gunika to.
**Gunda,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Gundaya. A rattle, or small bag.
**Gundaya,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (in Kik., Gunda udza = Furura musua in Kir.), a very small bag made of milala, into which beads, or grains, or beans were put. A number of them being tied round the legs, they served as a sort of music to them while dancing. The same little bags are still used, but they have improved upon them by using pebbles instead of grains, etc., for producing the noise. Obs. The word has been superseded by Gonda.
**Gundi,** *n.*, the name given to the rites and ceremonies the young women have to pass through on their promotion from the gniere to the kambi state, exactly answering to the ugnaro of the young men. The smearing themselves with clay and being switched by the older women, on being admitted to their mysteries in the forests, also form prominent parts of the gundi as of the ugnaro. Ache ni ku hakidzua gundi.
**Gundika, Kundika.** Mukahe hiu unagundika.
**Gundiza,** *v.n.* *See* Bemba. Nidzipiga, mpidzui, madzi gadziingira masikironi, be masikiro gadzigundisa. Sisikira, masikiro gadzigundisa; simania sebabuye; chamba mundahenda ivu mumo sikironi ndani; simania vinda fio hendika. Gnania wahala tosa yangu a kinda fuhira tumbagu hata aki-i-gundiza bewe unalonda ukafuhe u-i-gundize, be sinda-ku-va. Tosa yangu idzigundiza. Yudzinena-ela yudzi-ri-gundiza. Yudzigundiza (= Yuchziricha musika). *See* Musika.
  **Gundizika,** *v.n.* Kama tosa ikisareha mosi-wamba idzigundizika. Resp., Be reha ni-i-chokole.
  **Gundizira.** Gnania musiku yudzilonda tosa kuenda fuhira tumbaku, nidzi-mu-va-be adzivo-i-udza, nidzibuma tumbaku na fuha, ka-i-ka reha-be ndiye adziye-ni, gundizira tosa yangu.
**Gundo.** Only used in connection with Mfaya. Mfaya akapigua gundo Kana ngufu kahiri-anofoya-adzivokua kihi.
**Gunga,** *n.*, ornaments. Only used in connection with Dzoga or Ku dzodza. Dzoga za gunga. Such as are made round the body. *See* Dzoga. Yudzodzua gunga-ni urembo wa ache, Ornaments of women.
**Gungana** (Kij.), *v.* (= Gandofio kala in Kir.). Atu adzigungana hata adziidzala kaya chele. Adzigungana mbari hio, hata m'ana wao, adziidzala dele hivo muhalani ka-va-dzuvika mahe; ai maneno higo dzana ngufu, kahumania gandofio du kia.
**Gungu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kik., Ngungu. A widower, a

*Footer: 115*

## [PDF Page 129 — Dictionary Page 116 (Gun — Gus)]

  widow. Ayefuererua ni mulumewe hebu muchewe, ndiye gungu. Ela akaye dana na mulume du, ndiye muthaka. Gungu ra kiche ni ridzo, ela gungu ra kilume ni rikuani hirira gungu ra kiche yuna kidzungu che, ni ku chita-akahenda wari, akaria, ela gungu ra kilume kana kidzungu, yuhendafoya mahonche. Muche gungu; pl. Ache magungu. Mulume gungu; pl. Alume magungu. Seldom used.
**Guugucha, Kungucha,** *v.a.* (= Dunta in Kns.). *See* Heha. To stimulate, to instigate.
**Gunguchu** (Kid.), *adv.* (= Kodobere in Kns.). Yu niumbani gunguchu.
**Gungula,** *v.a.* (= Gungula in Kns.), to take toddy or to take honey. Ku kuesa vibaria na ku-vi-gungula. Ku gungula minazi (in Kij., Ku umua).
  **Gunguka.** Munazi wangu u gunguka, ka-u-na kitu kaviri. Kibangala kigunguka.
  **Gungukira,** *v.d.* Minazi yangu idzi-ni-gungukira.
  **Gungulua,** *v.p.* Minazi yangu ina-i-gungulua rere, My cocoa-nut trees have been robbed of their toddy to-day (= Kir., Minazi yangu idzigomberua rero; Ku umuliwa in Kij.).
  **Gungurira** (= Gemalumendza). N'enda, nikagungurire (minazi yangu)?
**Gunsa,** or **Kunsa,** *v.a.*, to fold.
  **Gunsigunsi,** *n.* (ra), cloudiness. Gunsigunsi ra Mulungu. Rero ku gunsigunsi, kakuna dzua, To-day it is cloudy; there is no sun.
  **Gunsula, Kunsula,** *v.a.*, to unfold.
  **Gunsumana,** *v.n.* Yudzeria papayu-yudzi-dzi-sarasara muiri nzima-be dzua ridziala-gara madzi ga babayu gadziumalala na dzua be muiri udzigunsumana.
**Guo,** *n.*, an offensive breath, as from a bad tooth, etc.
**Gura,** *v.a.* Lola nsoya agurafio.
  **Guragura.**
  **Gururia,** *v.a.* Ku gururia masansu, ga miya.
**Guro,** *n.* (= Mumbi), a slight haze. Rarely used. Rero-dzi idzifunga guro, kuna murenge. Rero kudzihenda guro.
**Guru,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the hamstring. Yudzikosa ku dema guru, yudzidema mulangu, basi ka-i-kabua, i-piga malo. Yudzihenda kironda cha guru, or, cha guruni.
**Guruba,** *v.a.* Adzi-u-guruba mugomba.
**Gurudumu,** or **Gur'dumu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-; also ya, za, when small), the name of a horn used for blowing.
**Gurufu.**
**Guruguru,** or **Gur'guru,** *n.* (ya, za), the thunder. Rero mfula idzihenda guruguru bomu, To-day rain has been and great thunder. Guruguru ya dzana ya-sidi; yari bomu ikihindirisa mahumbo.
**Guruya,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Gora), twenty doti of cloth. Guruya ya nguo.
**Gusa,** *v.* *See* Gula. To make grow.
  **Gusania,** *v.a.* *See* Gula.
**Gusa,** or **Guza,** *v.* *See* Gula. To sell.
  **Gusania,** or **Guzania.** *See* Gula.
  **Gusika,** or **Guzika.** *See* Gula.
  **Gusira,** or **Guzira.** *See* Gula.
  **Gusua,** or **Guzua.** *See* Gula.
**Gusa,** or **Guza,** *v.a.*, to touch.
  **Guzana,** or **Guzania,** *v. reit.* Mundakaladze mui-muambao kamuhenzi ku guzania be na mui mu vamenga, mundari, chadze ku guzania be kuamba muna hivio, be gula mutu aake niumbaye akale luakue-be ndo kanunda kuzania.

## [PDF Page 130 — Dictionary Page 117 (Gus — Hag)]

  Muna luvunsu lubomu, sifio ana akalafio.
  **Gusagusa,** or **Guzaguza,** *v. reit.* Si-ri-guseguse ge uka-ri-buma nongo daradasi.
  **Guzika,** *v.n.* Kumania moho ka-u-guzika we?
  **Gusira, Guzira,** *v. rel.*, to touch for anything. Udzi-ni-guzi rani-we? Resp., Nidzi-ku-guza kuamba ulole huya mutu. Yudzi-ni-guza ku-ni-onia mutu geri.
  **Gusua,** or **Guzua,** *v.p.*
**Guta,** *v.a.* *See* Muna; Gota. To knock together. Muhi udzi-ni-guta; but, Muhama ni ku kuta. Ku gutua ni ludzaga. Nidziima, nidzigutua ni ludzaga. Nidzigutua ni muhi kiduro kidzoano, etc. Mfananiko udziguta, hata kandakanda. *See* Lembelembe, Ku dzi guta.
  **Gutaguta.**
  **Gutana,** *v. reit.*, to knock one another. Hudzigutana vidzoa, We have knocked heads together. Der., Gutu; Kigutu.
**Gutu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Moma. (1) A stump, a body without its head.
(2) A knife or any weapon with the point broken. Kifiu kichoka kigatika kidzikala cha gutu. Yuna dzala ra gutu,—the language of exaggeration and ridicule; for, Chala cha kigutu. Dim., Kigutu.
**Gutula,** *v.a.* *See* Babarika. To push. Ku gutua ni muhi; or, Gutulua ni muhi.
  **Gutulana.**

## H.

**H,** the eighth letter of the alphabet. It is pronounced uniformly as a simple aspirate. The Arabic guttural *kh* is reduced in Kinyika to a simple *h*; *e.g.* Khabari becomes Habari, Rokho becomes Roho, etc.—[ED.]
**Ha.**
**Haba,** *adv.* *See* Masika; Mumfuno. Few. Nidzi-mu-va kitu haba, ela iye yudzi-ni-pa kitu kingi, yudzi-ni-dzupisa.
**Haba,** *n.*, sing. of Mahaba, which is more in use than the sing.
**Habari,** *n.* (ya, pl. za) (Kij., Habari), news. Atu ana sumurirana habari a-dzi-zo-zi-ona, or, a-dza-zo-zi-ona, hiko alako, Men converse about news which they have seen; they came from there.
**Hada, Hata** (Kij.), *adv.* and *prep.* *See* Tarira; Funga; Elelia; Lala; Lingana. Even, so much as, till, until. Often construed with the opt. Kakalamba lumenga-hata; yudzi-i-ria, viz. niuchi. Sina hata utu. *See* Funga.
**Hadaya** (Kij.), *v.a.* (= Ku kenga in Kir.), to cheat. Gnania yuna maneno ga uhadaya; dzana akidza ni hadaya, na ku hala reale yangu na kuamba: yuna mbuzi; kumba kana, wakudza ni goba.
**Hadi** (Kij. ?), *n.* (ra), a vow. Mutu akiika hadi, basi na-ri-hende a-ri-use; akisa-ri-henda, aki-ri-richa; hadi ni ku-m-guira, akaluma. Hadi adza-ro-ika, ka-dza-ri-usa, ndosa angaluma.
**Hadza,** *v.a.*, to name.
  **Hadzira.**
**Hadzidzi,** *n.* (ya, za), a story, fable. Hadzidzi ya kare, A story of old.
**Hafuna,** *v.a.* (= Afuna), to chew. Ku hafuna kidzeko, To delight in laughter.
  **Hafunika,** *v.n.* Ku hafunika chafu. Yudzi-(h)afunika chafu (= Yudzibua chafu, yudzi-dzi-piga chafu, and, yudzi-dzi-vula chafu). Mvula ya rero, ela ka-i-dzi-hafunika sana?
  **Hafunira,** *v.n.* *See* Toka.
**Hagahaga,** *v.a.*

*Footer: 117*

## [PDF Page 131 — Dictionary Page 118 (Hah — Ham)]

  Ku hagahaga ulu udzaoniala. Utu hiu nidzi-u-hagahaga, hata nidzi-u-mania, or, hata nidzi-u-kumbukira.
**Hahu,** *adj.* *See* Tahu. Three.
**Hai** (Kij.), *adj.*, alive. Babayo na mameyo achari hai? (= Kir., achari moyo? or, achariko?), Thy father and thy mother, are they alive?
**Hai,** *interj.* *See* Simila. A., Simila! B., Hai; Ndiwe ani? A., Ndimi gnania. Muyao akikuala, muambe "hai;" ukisa-mu-amba "hai," u-mu-unduwe, una-mu-asira mai.
**Haja** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Ufuha. Desire, want. Not to be confounded with Haya, shame. Gnania musiku kana haja; yuna kitu chani? hata chingo ya ku larira, kana unga mu-ona-ni mudzufu yudzikala kama mugua wa muhama.
**Haji** (Kij.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a pilgrim, especially one who has been to Mecca. Abe Gonge yudzisilimu Kisungu, yukata hajira Kisungu. By the Wanyika applied to one who follows the religion of Europeans; *i.e.* a Christian.
**Haka** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Aka in Kir.), to burn. Moto unahaka bibibiri.
  **Hakana,** *v. reit.*, (1) (Kid.) (= Tukana in Kij.), to abuse, slight.
  (2) (Kid.) (= Bakana in Kij.).
  **Hakisa,** *v.a.*
  **Hakisua,** *v.p.* *See* Gniere. Kambi ni atu aohakizua muansa.
**Haki,** *n.*, justice.
**Hako, Kako,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Ukoko. The seat, fundament; the bottom part of anything.
**Hala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Hala ra niumba.
**Hala,** *v.a.*, to take, to take after. Ku hala deni kua mutu, To take a debt with somebody; *i.e.* to borrow (= ku avaha). Muana hiyu aka-m-hala babaye, or, mameye, This child has borrowed from his father, or, his mother. Uifi hiu ukahalani kuehu kaku-na uifi; kuamba huamania undakala hivi, uugafugirua-ni? ungasindikua. Adzihalana na muchewe, yudzienenda kuao kua mulumewe dala.
  **Harika,** *v.n.*, to admit of taking. M'anao kaharika, yuna lufunzu muno.
  **Harira,** *v.d.* *See* Bemba; Kuluviza. To take from.
**Haladora.** *See* Haradora.
**Halahala** (Kij. ?). Ni neno ra ku-m-kogotera mutu. Halahala! usiniale, u-ga-seme, By all means do not forget it, tell it; do not forget telling it.
**Halali** (Kij.).
**Hali,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Muluchiluchi; Onsia. State, condition; account, reason, cause. Hali za atu ni ningi. Ni hali ya maneno tu, ela simania ukemowe.
**Hali,** *adj.* (corrupted from Gali). *See* Gurika. Dear, expensive.
**Halifu** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to destroy.
**Halisi** (Kij.), *adj.* and *adv.*, exact, exactly; real, really; indeed. Gnania yudz'eneza, yudzipata vitu halisi, Gnania has got a good supply of grain, etc.; he has got many things indeed (= he is rich).
**Halu** (?).
**Hama,** *n.* Ku guira hama.
**Hama,** *v.n.* *See* Dada. To be of use, to be fit, proper; (K.) worthy.
  **Hamia.**
  **Hamira.**
  **Hamirua,** *v.p.* *See* Sogoreka. Asungu hia alavi-adziohamirua ni dzi yehu. Ku hamirua ni uchi, To be fond of toddy.
**Hamba,** *v.n.*, to travel.
**Hambala,** *v.n.* *See* Vanga. To creep. Muiri uni-ni-hambala-sina hata urungo rero simania

*Footer: 118*

---

## [PDF Page 132 — Dictionary Page 119 (Ham — Han)]

  vindafio kala. Der., Muhambala or Muambala.
  **Hambalala,** *v.a.* (= Ku finamira mimba). Dzi idzaohambalala, or, ikayohambalala. Nika ya kuendera Taita ka-i-na miango na mirimaikahambalala (ikakuenda karakara dza bahari).
  **Hambalaza,** *v.a.*
  **Hambarira,** *v. rel.*, to creep for anything.
**Hambira.** Nidzihala kirengecho kuenda hambira, sika-ku-voya m'egnie, be kidzifunsika. Der., Tambasi.
**Hambo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (K.) solder. Pehe ya hambo.
**Handa,** (1) *v.a.* and *n.* *See* Kimirimiri. To cut meat into long strips. Nahanda niama muhandabasi ndiye ku handa niama.
(2) *v.n.*, to become dark. Kunahanda, It is getting dark. *See* Usiku unahanda. (= Kua zizira in Kns.) N.B.—The darkness begins as it were at a distance, and comes nearer and nearer, as the one cutting meat into long strips begins at the greatest circumference, and gradually approaches the centre. Usiku, udzihanda, unaidzaladzi, kama mutu adzo fiohandika jamvi. Der., Luhandu; Tandala; Tandiko; Tando.
**Handika,** *v.a.* *See* Tandiko. To spread as a mat, etc. Adzomba ana mido ku handika kidzoani, akaikira kidzoa. Na handika, nilale. Ku handika wala wa ludzaga.
  **Handikika,** *v.n.* Ka-va-handikika hiva, ni vafufu, vana via (Via, pl. of Chia or Kia), It is narrow; there are vessels.
  **Handikira,** *v.d.*, to spread to, for.
**Handikirira,** *v.a.* *See* Ndigo; Nderi. To fletch, to feather an arrow. Ni-pa nioga-nika handikirire mifui yangu.
  **Handikirua,** *v.p.*
  **Handira,** *v.d.*
**Handahu,** *adj.*, six. Wahandahu, Sixth.
**Handala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of bird. Yuna dzingo nire na magulu mare.
**Hanga,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Yusegere hangani. Be gnania yurere kuko hanga riro menga; ela kuno kadza lamusa atu ngari? To this the offended woman replies, Mahanga ni mairi-na osi ni ndugu zangu; be nda-vo-sagala basi ni hanga pia ridziuka. Ninda dzi gafia muiri hura, uenende hanga ringine-na hura nao uende hanga ringine be kuona ka-vi-hendeka fio? Nindadangadanga du hada rini? Hanga nda-ro-sagala, ni kana adziesagala gosi.
  **Hangahanga** (= Dangadanga). Wahangahanga, kuamba a-ki-hale-akisapata. Hudzi-mu-hangahanga, hudzi-m-voniosa (kamuumire). Yukuenda-mu-isa, yukuenda-m-hangahanga tu, na ku-m-richa, na ku uya. Yudzi-mu-isa kua haya. Nidzi-m-hangahanga, hata nidzi-m-kumbukira. In this instance Dangadanga may be used as well.
**Hangika,** *v.a.* *See* Guirira. (1) (Kid.) (= Ku kuadzika in Kir.), to hang up, to suspend.
(2) (Kir.), to put up, to place above, as a beam on posts.
  **Hangikira,** *v. rel.*, to hang up to, for.
  **Hangikua,** *v.p.*, to be hung up.
**Hangu.**
**Hanguka,** *v.n.*
  **Hangula.** Udzi-u-hangula, hebu u vavo (in Kid., Ku handzula maiya = Ka doa muiba in Kij.).
**Hangi.** *See* Gesa; Kirufu. Hangi ndefio, hangi sefio, ka-vi-manikana. Hangi yundavola. *See* Ganchagancha.

## [PDF Page 133 — Dictionary Page 120 (Han — Haw)]

  Hangi ni geri, hangi ni ulongo.
**Hango,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Dango in Kij.), the name of a kind of pumpkin, smaller than the renge.
**Hangu,** *adv.* *See* Kidambo. Since. Hangu tu (= Hangu kare), From of old. Neno hiri una-ri-mania? This word dost thou know? Resp., Hangu tu, Of old just. Hangu muanso hata muisho. Hangu Abraham ka-dza-kala mimi niko. Hangu viha ku vidza kua.
**Hano,** *dem. pron.* *See* Hia. Atu hano.
**Hansa.** *See* Mansa; Ku rua. Ku hausa miladzo. Yudzi-m-fumaga sana-yunahansa. Yudzifumagua, ela kahansa. Der., Mansa.
**Hanso** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Ndumo in Kir.).
**Hansula,** *v.a.* *See* Pengo.
**Hanuka,** *v.n.* (in Kij., Kitoa kina-mu-ada). *See* Midara. Mukufu udzidoka, dzino menga ridzihanuka, be na-ri-gandisa.
  **Hanula,** *v.a.* Ku hanula chuo nazi.
**Hapa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), one side of a cutting instrument. Ku-m-piga na hapa ra mufia, To strike one with the side of a sword. Hapa ra kifiu, One side of a knife.
**Hapa,** *adv.*, here.
  **Hapahapa.** *See* Mbanga.
**Hara,** *v.n.* (= Fioga).
**Hara,** *dem. pron.* *See* Hia. Those. Atu hara.
**Haradora,** *n.*, a term of congratulation, a benediction. Note: It is just possible that the word is a corruption of "El hamdul illahi!" which they constantly hear from the Mohammedans. Haradora! ndo atu ahendavio. Haradora nawe. Haradora! ndifio alume ahenda-vio! Haradora! m'ana'ngu, ndo ulume hiu; machero fumaga niama mbomu. The boy, in speaking of it, will say, Dzana nafumaga kidosho, baba aki-ni-liga. Haradora! Mulungu na uwe udzaye-ni-difia; Mulungu nau-ku-simike dza nguso ya chuma. Another, mentioning it, will say, Muche hiye yuna-ku-tombera Mulungu, That woman prays God for you. Haradora Mulungu udzaye-m-rinda hata yudziupuka kuehu na afia.
**Haraka,** *adv.* *See* Funsarere; Kisusuri. Haste, speed. Prov., Haraka ka-i-na mbaraka, Haste has no blessing.
**Hari** (Kidigo), *adv.* (= Hangi, Kahi, Kara, etc., in Kir.). Hari ni ndumo (= Kahi ni ndumo), Perhaps it is a joke.
**Haria!** (Kig.), *adv.* (= Varatu in Kir.).
**Harira.** *See* Hala.
**Harufu,** *n.*, (K.) litter, smell.
**Hasa,** *v.a.*, (1) (Kid.) (= Haka), to kindle a fire. Hasa moho hata ubuke.
(2) (Kir.). *See* Lomborera; Mulungu. Ku hasa koma-mbeyu-mufundo wa mayo samu.
**Hasara** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kimbisirua. Loss. Kuingira hasara, To sustain loss.
**Hasi,** *n.* (ra, hiri, pl. Ma-, higa; but also wa, hiyu, pl. *id.*, a, hia) (Kij., Hasai), an ox, a gelding. Mahasi gakikoma, gaka kakanua na mudamba.
**Hasira** (Kij.), *n.*, anger.
**Hasiri,** *v.a.* (= Kir., Ku lumisa). To injure.
  **Hasirika,** *v.n.* Mu-katireni niama iye muhoho, mu-mu-ve, ndiye adzeye-zi-difia; na kuamba si iye, be zi ngahasirika hivo njirani.
  **Hasiriwa.**
**Hata,** *adv.*, until.
**Hatahata** (Kid.), *v.a.* Ukihatahata unda-ga-richa maidzi.
**Hawa,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) a concubine.
(2) Lust.

## [PDF Page 134 — Dictionary Page 121 (Hay — Heh)]

**Haya,** *n.* *See* Onsia; Kisinde; Mfoda; Hangahanga; Lola. Shame. Yuguirua ni haya bomu, hata madzo ka-ga-idima ku unula, yuna loladzi tu. Sina madzo ga ku-ku-lola kua haya, kua uta hura wa-o-nihenda, uki-ni-difia.
**Haya,** *adv.* *See* Lalamirua; Kirema; Miaso; Koso. Well then! why then! Haya hurime-ge! Hayani, hayani! pigani muhama, kudzedzua, hufuse na mabema ndo ku kungucha.
**Hebu,** *adv.*, whether, or.
**Heche,** *n.* (ya).
  **Heche yangu.**
  **Heche yao.**
  **Heche-ye.**
  **Heche yehu.**
  **Heche yenu.**
  **Heche-yo.**
**Hechemula,** *v.n.*, to sneeze.
**Hecheyehecheye,** *adv.*, (K.) separately, severally.
**Hefi,** *n.*, curse. Ku pigua hefi, To be cursed.
**Hega,** *v.a.* *See* Tego; Choyo. To entrap, to ensnare, to entice, to draw. Kiravo huacho pigirua hicho kidzi zumbuka, hangi kidzi-m-guira mutu. Fig., Muiri udzi-ni-hega madzi. Der., Hege; Tego.
  **Hege,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a catch. Used of weeds or grass taking fresh root after having been cut. Niasizi dzimuta mahege; lit. The grass, weeds, have fixed catches (= Zidziguira misi, They have taken root). Mugasija wa hege, ni mugasija udzaomera wegnie, usionialua.
  **Hegera,** *v.a.* *See* Lungira. (1) To mingle together. Ka-mu-hegera mugao madzi, mu-rehere; yuna mugeni, adze, anoe. Nahenda viambo, nikahegere mawe, I make baits, that I may set stones, *i.e.* using them as traps. Gnania yudzi-mu-hegera Songoro aenendafio (= Ku igisa, Kid. ?).
  (2) (Kid.) (= Ku gofia in Kir.; Ku gotesa in Kij.), to speak a jargon of different languages. Gnania yunahegera maneno; yunakuafia.
  **Hegula,** *v.a.* (= Deua and Epua in Kij.), to take off, remove.
  **Hegurika,** *v.n.* Ka-ki-hegurika, moho ni mungi. Ka-ki-hegurika, kina-ni? nadza nihegule be.
  **Hegurira,** *v.d.* Nidzichita niungu, idzikola moho muno, siidima ku hegula, ndzo, ni-hegurire.
**Heha,** *v.n.* *See* Idima. To strive, to quarrel; to be in enmity with. Kangaheha-ela gnania ndiye adzeye-mu-gungucha (in Kid., Kangahehere, Gnania ndiye adzaye-m-gungucha). Der., Maheho.
  **Hehemesa** (Kid.), *v.a.* *See* Hensekesa. Only used with the reflexive Dzi. Muana kiya yuna-dzi-hehemesa (= Kir., Yuna lufunsu). Hema in Kij., to pant, Ku hema and Ku kehema.
  **Hehera,** *v. rel.* *See* Koma. To hate to, for another; to mediate, to defend. Atu anaheha anahehera chansa cha niumba. Anahehera kitu kimenga (= analuanira, etc.). Iye yudzi-hu-hehera, kuamba huokoke. Nidziamba niriwe malu, ela Mulungu na gnania ndiye aye-ni-hehera, hata nikiokoka.
  **Heherana.** *See* Zunganira.
  **Hehereka,** *v.n.* Mudzai kahehereka, kuani kana udugu kana mbazi. Na muifi naye kahehereka, kuani uki-mu-henda usena, basi yundakudza iya kuako. Ka hu hehereka, We are defenceless; there is none who can mediate for us.
  **Heherua,** *v.p.* Gnania yudziamba apigue, ela yudziheherua.
**Hemuka,** *v.n.* (in Kij. = Denguka). *See* Fumuririka. To

## [PDF Page 135 — Dictionary Page 122 (Heh — Hen)]

  sprain, to dislocate. Nidzikuala, nidzihemuka chala cha kigulu. *See* Diekuka. Nidzigutua, or, pigua ni muhi, nidzebua, nidzihemuka mukono. Nidzebua nikapigua ni muhi, nikahemuka mukono.
  **Hemula,** *v.a.*
  **Hemulana.** Maniani! musahemulana. Hi-mui anana, etc.
  **Hemurira** (Kid.), *v. rel.* Yudzi-ni-hemurira muanangu kigulu. Yudzi-ni-hemurira onsa rangu (in Kir., Yudzi vovola onsa rangu).
  **Hemurirua,** *v.p.* Yudzi hemurirua onsare.
**Hehera,** *v.n.*, to make. "He, he, he, he." Onomatop. Gogoreka (go, go, go, go, go). Kuku akisuluhia ku dieka, akihenda machi mangi, kuamba yuvevi na ku karira, basi ni ku richa kura ku hehera.
**Henda,** *v.a.* *See* Mioso; Vanga; Kilalo. (1) To make, to do. Ku henda luvia, To repair. Ku kipia henda pia, To repair. Ku muhenda rehema, To pity. Mutu hiye angalumua ni udende. Akahenda hendua (= ku logua. Nikuhenda-ni-singa. Yudzihenda domeka wari wehu, He kept picking my food. Yuhenda toka toka, She keeps breaking = is agile. Adzi henda dorua njira, They were shown the way. Nahenda ambirua, I was told. Wahenda nialua? Niumbayo i henda-ni? Resp., Ah-nikamuta nguso, ela sidzangue ku ana, or, ku-i-ana.
(2) To spend. Used only of time.
  **Hendana,** *v. reit.* Iye-niki-m-foya kitu. Ka-ni-pere, rero ye yunadza foya kuangu, be na mino sika-mu-va, ndo huhendana vio. Kondo sao ahendana-dze?
  **Hendeka,** *v.n.* *See* Dzoreka; Maka; Makira; Mambakundu; Enge. To be practicable.
  **Hendekana.** Utu hiu ukahenda mathe, undahendekana. Kid., Utu hiu ukahenda mare, undahendekana. Kij., Neno hili likafania msaha-lafanikana, neno la ku thani-lisilodasa ku fanikana.
  **Hendekera,** *v. rel.* Utu hiu udzi-mu-hendekera kasi hino idzi-ni-hendekera. Kari mcharo, ela kidzi mu-hendekera kuko nchirani. Madzere gangu mundani gadzi-ni-hendekera sana.
  **Hendekerua,** *v.p.*, to be prospered, to be successful (?). Muaka wa rero hudzihendekerua ni vitu mundani muehu; Mulungu rero yudzi-hu-hensa.
  **Hendera,** *v.d.*, to make for.
**H'ende, H'endeni.** *See* Enda. Contracted from Huende, Huendeni.
**H'enende.** Contracted from Huenende.
**Hende,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Kigulu cha hende; pl. Magulu ga mahende. Mutu hiyu yuna hende, or, yudzihenda hende. Yuna mahende kosikosi.
**Hendo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a deed, act.
**Henesa,** *v.a.* *See* Honesa. Obs.
**Hensa, Henza,** *v.a.*, to like, to love. Der., Henzo; Kihenzo; Mahenzi.
  **Hensana, Henzana,** *v. reit.*, to love one another.
  **Hensania, Henzania,** *v. reit.*, to love for one another.
  **Henseka, Henzeka,** *v.n.* Kid., Mutu huya kahenseka, hata uka-mu-henzadze ye kahenzeka. Mutu huya hata uka-mu-henza iye ka-ku-henzi. Neno hiri ka-ri-henzeka moyoni muangu (Kir.).
  **Hensekesa,** *v.a.* (= Pendekeza in Kij.), to indulge, to connive at. Akigomba munahenza, kamugania, ela mkiuka hivo

  mkanena luambo: Maneno higo ka-ga-hama, be mudzi-mu-henzekeza egnie fio. Kid., Muana hiyu muna-m-henzekeza muno punde kua punde aki-dzi-hehemeza, mudzi-mu-va. Muana wenu muna-m-henzekeza muno, yundakala mukaha.

  **Henserana, Henzerana.** Anahenzerana anao.

Ku-dzi-henzia uzinzi, To indulge in lasciviousness. Ku-dzi-henzia ku yeya ni ku-dzi-enendera kua azena tu, kava mutu a mu fundaye, ni muegniewe.

**Hera.** *See* Pera.
**Here** (Kig.), *conj.*, as, as if, as it were. Ni here dza oya, I am as it were resting.

  **Heruza.**

**Hetera** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Ku hindirika in Kir., or Hindira?). Nidzikudza hata nchirani, nikahetera nikalumira gulu rina-ni-luma minamba ridzihemuka kahi.
**Hetereka,** *v.n.* (= Ku deteleka; Ku kukutika; Ku yuayua), to stagger, to reel. Nidzihetereka nidzamba nibue. Yusukuma atu, adzihetereka ku bua. Ai! mutu yuna ngufu hiye yudzieukuma atu adzihetereka angine adzebua.
  **Hetereza,** *v.a.*, to press forward, to be energetic in doing anything. Muaka hiu-Amasai akudza akihetereza ku ulaga atu sanaka-vi-neneka (in Kid., Ahenda muno ku ulagua dezelesa). Nidzichira mundani kua Abe Gonge; yudzihetereza pekue mdzana wa rero; simania chamba, wari hecheye-na chamba wari na kigola simania yudzihetereza sana. Yudzirima luanda-yudzi-lu-ke-tereza. Yudema dzange yudzi-i-hetereza.

Niama yudzi-m-fumaga sana? Resp., A-yudzi-m-huka, yudzi-m-fumaga kikonde tu, ela ka-u-ka ingira ndani. A-ni mzima ye.

  **Hukanira.** *See* Ruma. Udzi-ni-hukanirani? Be ukihukanua, una-ni? Basi ikakala kondo. Ahoho a kare ere akipigana tu. Ku hukanira nika.
  **Hulana,** *v. ref.*
  **Hulua,** *v.p.*, to be taken down (a load). Yuhulua ni muyawe.
**Hula, 2,** *v.n.* Muiri wanguhangu dzana udzihula, ni ku sikira afia. Kavana vatu va-ni-lumavo kaviri. Muiri udzi-mu-hula.
  **Hurira,** *v.n.*, to be quiet, to be calm; (K.) humble. Peho idzihurira.
  **Hurire,** *adj.* *See* Kusi; Kilolua. Quiet, tranquil. Moyo wangu u huriri, My heart is quiet.
  **Hurisa,** *v.a.* *See* Nagnanagna; Ngoi; Hu. To quiet, to calm, to compose, the mind; to stay anything.
  **Hurisira,** *v. ref.*, to stay anything for. Ku hurisira dzidzo (= rangarisa).
**Hulu** (= Tisa).
**Huluka,** *v.n.* *See* Luniasi; Lui. Mbuzi idzeria luniasi lui idzi huluka, The goat has eaten poisonous grass (idzi huluka).
  **Hulukisa,** *v.c.* Gnania akidzodzua yunahulukisa, *i.e.* the dzogado hulukisa dzogase zikahulukisa, ni mbidzo. Uki-m-piga gnombe lufuiho luvudzu, ni ku hulukisa, or, niku kanagnana. Vatu o-dzo-vo pigua vadzihulukisa, vadzifuerera miladzo.
**Huma,** *v.a.*, to send.
  **Humika.** *See* Umbika. N'enda humika kasiyangu (= N'endahenda, etc.).
  **Humikira.**
  **Humira,** *v.* *See* Kiviakoe. Rahani; Mbeko; Kadzitu, 2; Rangi. To send for? (K.) employ; to use. Gnombe hi ni ya ku dzangisa, mimi si-

## [PDF Page 142 — Dictionary Page 129 (Hum — Hur)]

  idima ku-i-humira hecheyangu, naye kawesa ku-i-humira hecheye.
  **Humisa,** *v.a.* (= Lagisa). Nidzi humisa mutu 'endaye, for, aendaye Kisiwani, kuenda ni gurira nguo; be andivouya, undakudza ulole, k'amba yudzipata, be ni-kuve.
**Humbo,** *n.* (pl. Ma-). *See* Guruguru, where it means the bowels. Mutu hiye yuna humbo. Mutu hiye yuna mimba bomu, or, yuna humbo. Gnombe hiyu yuna humbo. Ulaidi wa kanike una humbo sana.
**Humburira.** *See* Lumba.
**Humbuka,** *v.n.* *See* Madzula; Kiwawai. To spring, to burst. Kasha hiri ri refu-ridzihumbuka tundu. *See* Ahuka; Muka. Minazi yangu-kaz'kazi ka rero idzihumbuka uchi, Mulungu bariki.
  **Humbukisa,** *v.a.* Der., Jumbulio.
  **Humbula,** *v.a.* *See* Komo; Kiwawai; Kikonde. To bore, to perforate, to rend open. Mungu anafula kirenge, aka-ki-humbula. Ku humbula ivu.
**Humili** (Kij.), properly **Ku hemili,** *v.n.*, to endure, to abide. Madzere ka-ga-humili dzua, ela muhama una mbiriri sana, ka-u-fua na na dzua haraka.
**Hunda,** *v.a.* *See* Gniotola. To pluck, to break off. Ku hunda mboga. Ku hunda nazi, kunde, etc. *See* Dubani.
  **Hundira.** *See* Furirua. Ni-rehera kikahana, nidze, nihundire mboga.
  **Hundisa,** *v.a.* *See* Laza. Ku hundisa uchi (= Ku laza uchi). U-ikeni, muhundise, hata ukale ungi (*sc.* wari wa lasinga).
  **Hundisua,** *v.p.* *See* Ta lusinga. Wari ukahundisua hata ukakala ungi.
**Hunde,** *n.* (ra) (= Dude). Hunde ndiro rihaluaro, mutu akakuenda ri-henda kiravo cha ndogoe.
**Hunelu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Dungu in Kir.; Tumbi in Kij.), a kind of basket used for fishing; an Aden basket.
**Hunga,** *v.a.* (= Ku dunga in Kij.), to add, to join one thing to another of the same kind, to splice; (K.) Ku hunga lukongoni, To broach. Ku hunga ushanga, To string beads. Ku hunga uchi ndereni, To add palm-wine in a calabash. *See* Ndere.
  **Hungika,** *v.n.* Ushanga hiu udzihungika to.
  **Hungira.** Nadzukula ndere nikahungire uchi. *See* Kuri.
**Hunga.** *See* Nga.
**Hungari.**
**Hungue,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Dzansi, but only used of toddy). *See* Gola. Contribution. Ku piga mahungue ga uchi, kula mutu hunguere. Nidzikudza na uchi wangu, be napiga hungue rangu rero, niuse; machero nikidza, nidze kua kunoa uchi tu, kuani hungue rangu nidzipiga rero. Hungue rao ranoewa dzana.
**Huno.** *See* Hiu.
**Huo.** *See* Hiu.
**Hura.** *See* Hiu.
**Hurira.** *See* Hula, 2.
  **Hurisa.** *See* Hula, 2.
  **Hurisira.** *See* Hula, 2.
  **Husa.** *See* Hula, 2.
**Hurivo.** *See* Nugnunika. Where we are.
**Huru** (Kij.), *adj.*, the state of freedom, as opposed to slavery. Ku-m-richa huru (= Kir., Ku-m-richa bure), To set free.
**Huruma** (Kij.), *n.* (in Kir. proper, Mbasi), compassion, pity.
  **Hurumia,** *v.a.*, to pity. Maneno ga ku-m-hurumia, Words of pity.
  **Hurumiana,** *v. reit.*, to pity one another, to sympathize. Akamba ana moyo wa ku hurumiana.

## [PDF Page 143 — Dictionary Page 130 (Hus — Idu)]

**Husa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ondosa in Kir.). *See* Fumbulusa. To startle, to drive away.
**Husa,** *adj.* (= Ku dieka moyo; K., Hurira, humble). Hangu dzana yudzihusa punde (= yudzihurira punde). Mutu hiye akahusa moyo, ni mufumurisi, hata akiona utu wa kondo, iye ni ku fumurira tu, yuna moyo musinde, moyowe ka-u-kakuenda kondoni, ukafumurira dza kisinde cha niasi. The opposite is the Mudabidabi.
**Huta,** *v.n.* (= Huga), to rebound, reverberate, hurtle.
  **Hutahuta,** *v.n.*, to be in a state of agitation. Moyo una-ni-hutahuta (= Duduma in Kir.; Tutusika in Kij.).
**Hutu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Divira. Hutu hiri nda-ri-londa kigumba, ni-ri-bume. Hutu ni mufui usio lomba, usio akua; ni mufui wa mumo kua mumo, hura wa kigumba.
**Huya** (= Hiyuya; Baha). *See* Lola, 2; Udiriri. Yuvatu huya. *See* Foyeka and Komba; Dorosa and Budzania.

## I.

**I,** the ninth letter of the alphabet, always pronounced as *ee* in "feel."—[ED.]
**I,** *aux. verb*, sing. and pl. 3rd pers. *See* Midara. Is, are. *See* instances, Era (Kasi i-; Minasi i-; etc.).
**I,** *pron.*, (1) (rel. to the sing. of the ya class). *See* Udzika; Disa; Yegnie. It. When standing in the accusative, and followed by a vowel, it becomes *y*; *e.g.* Gnombe nidzayo yona, for, nidzayo-i-ona, The cow which I have seen.
(2) (rel. to the pl. Mi-), they.
**I** *is put before the words* Noa and Ria when the imp. is used. I-noa. *See* Ariza. N.B.—This use exists, likewise in Kns. Iza; izani, Come, come ye; from Ku za, To come. I-ria.
**Ia,** *v.a.* (= Chiie). *See* Iya. To steal.
**Iai** (?).
**Ibu, Ipu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mabu, Maipu), a boil, a tumour.
**Idi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Madi), an egg.
**Idika** (Kig. ?).
**Idima,** *v.n.* *See* Jego; Bagaiwa; Kosa. To be able, to can. (The word is evidently borrowed from the Kimasai Idim. *See* Erhardt's "Vocabulary of the Enguduk Iloigob.") Neg., to be ill. Yukudza henda-ni, na-ye kaidima ku lumba? Hata atu akiheha, kaidima kondo yuya; be yukudza henda-ni?
  **Idimana,** *v. reit.*, to be equal in strength.
  **Idimika,** *v.n.* (= Kig., Donieka). Atu hio ana ngufu, kaidimika.
  **Idimira,** *v. rel.*, to be up to, for; (K.) to inure.
**Idirika,** (1) *v.a.* (= Ku henda hiroka), to hasten. Yudziirika wari haraka, hudzeria. Yudziidirika kuenda iha mtu, yudzikudza haraka. Adziidirika, azihenda miongo ya fisi, They have hastily erected slight sheds. *See* Mongo wa fisi.
(2) *v.n.*, to be quick. Idirika ku aka niumba hikara. Ku idirika ku guira mani maidzi, Thou art not quick enough to seize green grass. This relates to the Masai, who are said to spare a person when holding out to them a green leaf or a few blades of green grass.
**Idu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Madu). Funsani madu, mu-ikire niama. Yudzinsa mbuzi maduni. Mutu akaye lagana na muyawe kuenda vatu, be mumenga akihenda uere, yuya adziefika mbere madano ga nchira,

*Footer: 130*

## [PDF Page 144 — Dictionary Page 131 (Idz — Ika)]

  ni ku funsa idu, akadieka, kuamba amanie nchira adza-yodua.
**Idzala,** *v.a.* *See* Kururusi. To be full.
  **Idzarira,** *v.d.*, to be full, to be in plenty. Kuku azimu idzarira, He has plenty of fowls.
  **Idzarisa,** *v.a.* Kitu kikalacho sinda, ndicho nidzarisa cho.
  **Idzarisira,** *v.d.*
  **Idzaza,** *v.*, to fill.
  **Idzasira,** *v.d.*, to fill to, for another.
**Idze** (perf. Idzayo).
**Idzi,** *adj.*, fresh, green, raw. Der., Muidzi; Kiidzi, etc.
**Idzi** (= Ifunsika). *See* Kunga. Tuba idzi funsika.
**Idzio,** *part.*, used in conjugation.
**Idzui,** *n.* (ra). Yunaloga, yugomba na idzui. Ku henda idzui. Umiro udzi-mu-fua idzui. Mutu akichesa ku imba, umiro niku henda idzui. Yudziimba cho, yudzihenda idzui. Ku gomba na idzui, maninoge yagomba na idzui (= Yugombira ndani).
**Ifia,** *v.a.* Yudzi-dzi-ifia m'egnie. Prov., Mbuzi mbi inaifia murisa.
**Ifu** (Kid.), *adj.* (= Romu in Kir.). *See* Hofieka. Hard.
**Ifu,** *n.* (ra) (= Ndani). *See* Kibigatutu; Kidamfira; Kidambi; Dzafula. Intestine, gut. Ifu ra gnombe, The intestines of an ox. Ifu ra kuku, The crop of a fowl, the gizzard.
**Ifu, Ivu,** *adj.*, ripe.
**Ifu, Ivu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), ashes.
**Ifua,** *adj.*, ripe.
**Ifuisa,** *v.n.* *See* Songa. To be ripe.
  **Ifuira,** *v.n.* Isu hiri rikaifuira dzulu, basi ridzivukuhika viala vavodzi nikadzola.
  **Ifuisa.** *See* Alukisa; Songa. Atu adzichira hiva, hata adzilonda ku ifuisa nchira; be si mutu mumenga, atu hio ni angi, si mukondo wa mutu mumenga.
**Iga,** *v.a.* *See* Kirema. To imitate.
  **Igisa** (Kid.). *See* Hegera. Der., Luigo.
**Iha,** *v.a.* (Kij., Ita, which in Kig. means Lagula), to call, to invite, to name.
  **Ihana,** *v. reit.*, to call one another. Atu anapiga pembe moroni ku ihana.
  **Ihika,** *v.n.* *See* Mulamba; Dzimba; Ika. (1) To admit of calling, to be within call.
  (2) To answer a call, to attend. Ngoma hio idziihikua ni atu muno, That drum has been much attended by the people, meaning, by synecdoche, the dance in connection with it.
  (3) To yield. Muvunga uki-mu-ihika sana, The rice yielding him much; *i.e.* His rice grew well—the reference being to the field. Gnombe ziki-mu-ihika.
  (4) To crow.
  **Ihikira,** *v.d.* *See* Hikizo. To answer a call to or for, another.
  **Ihikisa, Hikisa,** *v.a.* *See* Mborera. (K.) To reply, To comply, to listen. Dzana hovolagana, na hikisa, ela basi hima ndani nari sihenzi to.
  **Ihikisira,** *v.d.*, to listen for another.
  **Ihira.**
  **Ihirua,** *v.p.* *See* Musikisi; Laira. To be called for anything.
  **Ihua,** *v.p.*, to be called. Unaihua ge! or, Ge unaihua! and Unaihiwa ge! Ndosa hu ihue gniere ihiwa? Ndosa huki ihiwa gniere!
**Ika,** *v.a.* (1) *See* Mafundango. To put, to lay, to delay. Ku ika to. Ndo utu oko-ni-ika. Ndo utu odzo-ni-ika.
(2) Contraction of Ku ihika, To crow. Jogolo rinaika (= rinaihika). Na gnombe inaika. Gnombe inaikato yo! or, hino.

  **Ikana,** *v. reit.*, to appoint one another, to meet at a place fixed upon. Huaikana vatu vasiku, kuamba hukaonane vavo, basi haenende.
  **Ikira,** *v.d.*, to put to, for; to lay up to, for. Ku-mu-ikira amana. Nidzi-mu-ikira vitu dahayari.
  **Ikua,** *v.p.* Ku ikua ni utu, To be delayed by a something.
**Ika.** *See* Kutuku.
**Iki,** *adv.* (rel. to the ya class), if, if they, if it.
**Ikisa,** neg.
**Iko** (rel. to the ya class). *See* Ko. It is there. Der., Muiko; Kiko, etc.; Luiko; Kiikane; Uikane.
**Ila** (Kij.), *n.* (ra), disgrace, shame. Waduruma, wana ila, The Duruma people have disgrace. Kula vatu vana ilare; in proper Kir., Kula vatu vana kiremache.
**Ima,** *v.n.* *See* Koko, 1 and 2. To stand, to stay. Muche hiye kaima va alume (= kahurira).
  **Imia,** *v.a.*
  **Imika.**
  **Imira.**
  **Imire.** *See* Madzodzo. Aimire galukirana, sengererana. Murima uimireo. Kirima kiimirecho.
  **Imirira,** *v. rel.* *See* Umbana. Endani, ka-mu-sikise, ka-mu-imirireni vavo, murinde atu andao kudza.
  **Imirirana,** *v. reit.* Mbariyenu ni mbi, kamu imirirana.
  **Imirirua,** *v.p.* Maneno higa ni makulu, galonda ku imirirua, gakagombua, gakadoka; kuani-gakisa gombua gakadoka, be hivo kare ganadza gahende kondo.
**Imani,** *n.*, trust, belief, faith.
**Imba,** *v.*, to sing. Of birds it seems to be only the kihui of which the word is used.
  **Imbika,** *v.n.*, to be sung.
  **Imbira,** *v.d.*, to sing to.
**Imbi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a wave. Der., Gnimbo (Kimbo); Muimbo.
**Imiza,** *v.a.*, to erect.
**Ina.** *See* Kunga.
**Inama,** *v.n.* (= Ku zama), to bow, to stoop. Trop., to submit, to yield to warnings, etc. Hudzi-mu-ambira hata yudziinama, ni ku richa ku dzukirua.
**Inda,** *v.a.*, to dip into.
**Ine.**
**Inevu,** *n.*, bird-lime.
**Inga.** *See* Nga; Kara.
**Inga,** *v.n.*, to enter.
  **Ingira** (Kig.), *v.n.* *See* Kansa; Fifira. To enter. Hiku ku ka ingira ndani. Ku ingira mumbani, To enter a house. Moyo ndiingira madzi kua oga. Nidzi kuenda ingira deni kua gnania, I incurred a debt with gnania.
  **Ingirika,** *v.n.* (= Ku damu). Vatu hiva ka-va-ingirika.
  **Ingirira,** *v. rel.* *See* Udumani; Beshe; Beshere. Ndo ulongo udzo-vo-ku-ingirira. Atu akifuina sayo moroni, basi hara ache akaingirira alumeao.
  **Ingirirana,** *v. reit.* Atu hio-ungaona arifio-anaingirirana niumba, *i.e.* anazingirana. Abumaniumba akaingirirana niumba.
  **Ingirirua,** *v.p.* Ku ingirirua ni ageni (= Ku dzirua ni ageni).
  **Ingiza,** *v.c.* (= Ku-mu-ingisa mimba). *See* Fuma. To cause to enter, to let enter.
  **Ingizana,** *v. reit.* Kahuingisana niumbani, hunaheha (= Kid., Kahu vegnierana niumbani; Kahubadana, Kir.).
  **Ingisika,** *v.n.* Ka-ki-ingisika himu, ni vafufu.
  **Ingizira,** *v.d.* Kituche hiki na-mu-ingisira hiva.

## [PDF Page 146 — Dictionary Page 133 (Ing — Ira)]

  **Ingiziza** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku bisania in Kir.), to insert, to intersperse, *e.g.* beads of different colours in stringing them.
**Inga,** *v.a.* (1) (Kir.), to scare, to drive away. Only used of birds. Ku inga kuku.
(2) (Kig.) (= Ku zola in Kir.), to chase, to drive away generally. Ku inga ngoma. Der., Muingo, Birds flying.
  **Ingana** (Kig.) (= Ku solana in Kir.).
  **Ingika,** *v.n.* Kuku yuna moyo hiyu-kaingika.
  **Ingira,** *v.d.* Ndzo, u-ni-ingire kuku, anaria madzere.
  **Ingirira.** Udziingirira-ni niumbani muangu, kumba u-mubishe?
  **Ingiriza** (Kid.). Ku ingiriza kivinda.
  **Ingirizira,** *v.a.* *See* Bumira. Nidziniala madzere, ka ga-kamera to, be nin'enda nikaingirizire. Nidziniala muhama, ela udzifuka kua mfula ku kala chache, be vino mfula idzegnia, nin'enda nikaingirizire. Ku ingirizira kikahana, kivinda, niumba, etc.
  **Ingirua,** *v.p.* (in Kins., Ku tobua), to repair. Nidziingirua ni kidudu, cha madzo, or, dzidzo.
  **Insa,** *v.a.* (in Kig., Ku inda, To dip into). *See* Elelia. To chase, to hunt; to be inimical to, to hate. Der., Insi; Uinsa; Uinsi.
  **Insana,** or **Insania,** *v. reit.* *See* Kondo; Zamana. To hate one another. Atu hio anainsana, ka-dza-onana.
  **Insika,** *v.n.*
  **Insira,** *v.d.* *See* Lukuidia. To chase for or with. Der., Inzi.
**Ingina,** or **Ingine,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya class), other.
**Ingu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Maingu), a cloud. Mfula idzipiga ingu ridzo, rinamesa. Kudzipiga ingu bomu; kudzipiga ingu ra keri, rinamesa.
**Ini,** *n.* (ra, pl. Maini), the liver. Yu-ini ra gnombe (= Yu-madzi ga kunde), He is brown, like the liver of cattle or like the water in which beans have been boiled. The former comparison is more used by the Wadigo, the latter more by the Rabais.
**Inika,** *v.a.* (= Inika in Kij.), to bend. Only said of a stick used in a trap. Properly, to bend. Ku inika muhambo, To set a trap. Na inika muhoto wangu-ni-u-hege. N.B.—The principal word, Ku ina, is contained in the Kig. language, and means to dance. Ku ina wathi, Kikamba (= Ku fuina uira in Kiravai).
  **Inikira,** *v.d.* Nda uka-ni-inikire muhambo wangu.
  **Inikua,** *v.p.*
**Inuka** (Kid.), *v.n.* *See* Unuka. To rise, to give way to being lifted.
  **Inula** (Kid.), *v.a.* *See* Unula. To lift. N.B.—In Kid. there are the three different pronunciations, Enula, Inula, and Unula, but in Kir. only Unula.
**Inoa.** *See* I. Inoa uchige! Drink away at the toddy! Yunanoa, He drinks, indic.; but Noa uchige! is correct.
**Insa,** *v.* *See* Inga. To chase.
**Insi, Inzi,** *n.* (pl. Mainzi). *See* Inga. A fly.
**Io.**
**Io** (= Hio-gnombe, io Hio). *See* Kara; Upusira; Nkue.
**Ira,** (1) *v.n.*, to boil, to ferment. Madzi ganaira. Niungu inaira. Uchi unaira.
(2) *v.a.* *See* Eneza; Indana; Zuruku. To claim a debt. Bakiye ni reale menga, a-ni-irayo. *See* Baki.

## [PDF Page 147 — Dictionary Page 134 (Ira — Ivi)]

  **Irana,** *v. ref.*
  **Irika,** *v.n.*, to faint, to swoon, from exhaustion or from blows; but from sickness it is Ku zimia moyo. Ku irika kua na ndzala, kua chiru. Yudzipigua kigongo hata yudziirika, akamuagirua madzi, akafufuka. Kuguirua ni mudzoare, ukairika.
  **Irikira,** *v.d.* Nidzi-ku-kania kuamba uya, kukahensa, ba lola ukziirika, be kudza irikira atu nini?
  **Irisa,** *v.a.* (= Irikisa in Kins.). Ndzala idzi-mu-irisa. Yudzi-m-piga, hata yudzi-mu-irisa (Kid.).
**Ira-tu** (= Hira-tu). *See* Niada.
**Iri.** Maneno ga ku iri.
**I-ria.** *See* I, 3.
**I-ri-o** (rel. to the ya class). *See* Lilia; Pafu. Which is, it is which, for I-ri-yo. Hata ukahenda pingu i-ri-o dze, ka-i-rinda mutu, Whatever charm you may make, it does not protect a person.
**Iru,** *adj.* *See* Mumemue. Black. The root-word of Muiru, Kiiru, Kiru, etc., Kuiru, Niru.
**I-ri-o,** for **I-ri-yo,** *pron.* *See* Nai. It is which (= which is), rel. to the sing. of the ya class; they are which (= which are), rel. to the pl. Mi-.
**Isa,** *v.a.* *See* Deni; Mudeni. To sue for payment, to solicit a debt, to dun. N'enda-nika-mu-ise a-ni-rive.
  **Isaisa** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Ku funga in Kij.). Mfula inaisaisa-muaka ufika. Kir., Mfula inainsa-indakudzagnia, and, muaka ufika.
  **Isana,** *v. reit.* (= Isania).
  **Isania.** Ku isania hakini (= kuenda hakini). Unga-mu-ona akichira kula dziku-be anaisania na gnania.
  **Isika,** *v.n.* Nidzikuenda hata n'enda-ni mkongo, ninalola kaisika kua vira arifio mkongo.
  **Isira,** *v.d.* Enda-uka-ni-isire, dziku hizo sindaidima kudza, or, sindaidima kuenda.
**Isa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Maisa), turn. Isare ridzifika. Ku gema maisa. Ku rima maisa. Ku risa maisa.
**Isa,** *v.a.* *See* Ira.
**Isa,** *v.n.* (= Mamfula = Isha in Kij.), to end, finish. Dziku ya ku ramuka. Dziku ya ku rima viri. Dziku ya ku isa. Machero ni ku isa, muhondo ni juma.
**Isabu** (Kij.), **Hesabu,** *n.* (ya), reckoning, amount. Isabuye kitu hiki-ni mirongo mine, etc. Mulume ka-ni-buma isabu-ni, ka-ni-dara.
**Ise** (Kidigo), *n.* (= I-si fio kala), father.
**Isha.** *See* Muisho.
**Ishima,** *n.* (ya), honour. The Kid. pronunciation is more Eshima; but both forms are used. Muana hiyu kana ishima; wakudza mufiere, kakauka ku-mu-visa kihi, yudzi-sagala vifio. Muana hiye yuna ishima: nachira, aka-n'amba (for, aka-ni-amba): "Baba, imani, ni-mu-dzumbuse kibaria!" yudzilafia uchi, nidzenoa, hata nidziukuha. Ai-muana yuna ishima hiye.
  **Ishimu,** *v.a.*, to honour. Yudzi-mu-ishimu sana.
  **Ishimiwa,** *v.p.*, to be honoured.
**Isilamu,** *n.* (pl. *id.*), the Kinyika name for Mohammedanism.
**Isio uina.** *See* Ndzira.
**Isu, Izu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mazu), the banana, the bunch of one tree. Mazu, bunches of a plurality of trees. Different kinds are the following: (1) Izu lume. (2) Izu riche. (3) Izu ra mudzafudzo. (4) Izu ra mkatha. (5) Izu ra kigulue. (6) Izu ra kivukuse. (7) Izu ra mbahasi. Dim., Kadzisu.
**Ivi** (Kidigo), *adj.* (= Fuhi in Kir.), short. Mutu muivi.

## [PDF Page 148 — Dictionary Page 135 (Ivi — Jeg)]

**Ivi** (Kir.), *n.* (ra, pl. Mavi) (= Mbalahi). *See* Konde; Linga. A slap. Ku piga ivi, To give a slap. Ku pigana, or, ku dzuvana mavi, To slap one another. This was formerly a favourite game among the Wanyika; and a cloth was wound round the left arm, which was used as a shield.
**Ivo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Maivo).
**Ivo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mavo) (= Valakahi in Kid.). *See* Kisinde. Ivo ra kahi.
**Ivu.** *See* Ifu.
**Ivu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mavu) (in Kij., Ipù), a tumour, a boil. Ivu ridzihumbulua, ela ridzifimba mulomo, rinakanagnana kahiri, kuani ka-ri-kadzuka. Dim., Kadzivu and Kidzivu.
**Ivua, Ifua,** *v.n.*, to be ripe. Isu hiri ridziivua rosi-ridzivonoka.
  **Ivuisa, Ifuisa, Ivuiza,** *v.a.*, to let ripen. Said of plants and fruits. Kitu kino udzi ki-ivuisa hebudze? Did you let this thing ripen? Gnania kaivuisa kitu mundani kituche yu-ki-funa kidzanga.
  **Ivuisa,** or **Ifuisa,** or **Ivuiza,** *v.n.*, to let ripen by boiling or cooking. Udziivuisa hebudze? asks a husband of his wife. Resp., A-nikaivuisa. H., Be hangu nakudza kuza-ni-pa nini u-rinda-ni? Resp., A-nikaniala kua hizo gnauzi hudza-zo-sumurira.
  **Ivuisira, Ifuisira,** *v.d.* Na-mu-ivuisira mulum'angu wari-yunenda kaya, Mulum'angu, contracted from Mulumewangu. Na-mu-ivuisira abeyenu wari yunaenenda kaya, says a mother to her children.
**Iwe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mawe), a stone. Panga ya iwe, Cavity in a stone, or rock. Dim., Kadziwe and Kidziwe; magn., Dziwe.
**Iya** (= Iyae (Gnombe); Dongoria). *See* Dongona.
**Iya,** *v.a.* *See* Lela. To steal. Usinsisi uhenda-ni-iya, nikavodzerua. Ah utu hiu ka-u-erekeseka, nidziamba, nagesa usinsisi uka-ni-iya, nikavodzerua; hata nafumbuluka-ngulue adzeria kare ndo vikafio kala, or, ndo vidzafio kalu. *See* the question by Lavira. Nidzirauka, nidziiya kuku, ni ku rauka jogolo ka-ri-dzaika, or, ihika.
  **Iyika,** *v.n.*
  **Iyira,** *v.d.* and *rel.* Udzi'yirani? (for, Udziiyirani).
  **Iyua,** *v.p.* Ku iyua. Ku iyua ni usinsisi na ku vodzerua.
**Iye,** *pers. pron.*, he, she.
**Iyi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Maiyi), a heap of grass, rooted out in cultivating the ground; (K.) rick. Ku kunsa iyi. Ku unga maiyi.
**Iyo** (rel. to the ya class). *See* Malu.

## J.

**J,** the tenth letter of the alphabet. It has a peculiar pronunciation, like *dj*. It must not be confounded with *ch*, although *ch* is sometimes written for *j*.—[ED.]
**Jamaa,** *n.*, company, family.
**Jamanda,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Mlambo.
**Jamfi,** *n.* (pl. Ma-). *See* Mudzeka; Handa. A mat of plaited palm leaves.
**Jega,** *v.a.* Yudzijega madzere hiva! yunahafuna muno mutu hiye.
**Jego,** (1) (Kir.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a double tooth, grinder. Gnania yuna majego, kaidima, He or she is with the double teeth—has them, because, when they are not aching, you do not know or feel that you have got them (= Gnania has the toothache; he is ill). Nalumua ni, or, Ninalumua ma-

*Footer: 135*

---

## [PDF Page 149 — Dictionary Page 136 (Jem — Ka)]

  jego, but, Nalumua ni, or, Ninalumua meno, or dzino, is toothache in the front teeth.
  (2) (Kid.) (= Vioni, and = Kijego and Rogo in Kir.).
**Jembe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a hoe, the only agricultural implement used by the Wanyika. Dim., Kajembe and Kijembe; magn., Rijembe.
**Jeri,** *n.* *See* Geri. Truth.
**Jia,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the turtledove. Yuna kilinga dzingoni, It has a ring on the neck.
**Jiba** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), turn. Sambi ni jibaro, Now it is thy turn.
**Jigajiga,** *v.a.*
**Jijimiza,** *v.n.* Sindauya kaviri, najijimiza. Gnania kauza mithana, wala kana oga, yumania ku jijimiza tu.
**Jika, Kika,** or **Chika,** *v.a.*, to give one a hint. Yudzi-ni-ambira maneno, ela yudzi-ni-jika, Ni utu wa fimbo, kuka-m-funurira. Nidzi-m-jika kua maneno, ela ni muerefu, yudzi-ga-mania. Be una-ni-jika na maneno, wamba ni muhoho, hebu dze? Yudzi-m-jika na maneno, ela ka-ga-ka mania. Ndo ku-m-jika.
  **Jikisa,** *v.a.* (= Ku kikisa), to stimulate, to hasten, to urge forward. Nidzi-mu-ona gnania na mutu, yuna-m-kikisa, yunaenenda naye.
  **Jikisika, Kikisika,** *v.n.* Kahenzi korokoro, hata uka-m-jikisa, kajikisika. It is to say, Hayani! huenende! Hayani, siniani! Hayani enendani haraka ge!
**Jimbulua, Chimbulua.** Yukuenda-m-hala muchewe, ela muche kahensi ku enenda, ela. Akajimbulua ni hara ana a avuye. Yudzi-m-kikisa, yudzienenda naye. Nidzi-mu-ona gnania, yudzifunga muana gnombe, yun'enda aki-m-kikisa.
**Jimbe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the heel.
**Jimbula,** *v.a.* (= Ku lombola), to make known any disgrace or stigma attached to one. Yudzi-ni-jimbula, *e.g.*, one born of a slave, because Usunie ka-u-dzuka hiraka.
**Jindula,** *v.n.*, to revive. Ku jindula munazi (= ku u udza moyo). Ku jindula mukoma.
**Jinga,** *v.a.*, to urge on, to impel, to incite. Ku-m-jinga mutu kazi. Ku jinga kuro.
  **Jingira.** Hunahala kuro, hukajingire tima.
**Jirani,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, za), a neighbour. Jirani wangu, My neighbour. Jirani zangu, My neighbours.
**Jita,** *v.a.*, to cook.
**Jitaza** (in Kij. = Mke wa nioka). Masikiro gadzijitana (= gadzigandiza).
**Jizira,** *v.d.* *See* Kibamfu.
**Jombajula** (?), *n.* (pl. Ma-), a brick.
**Jonchoe.**
**Jora** (Kidigo), *n.* (ra), a dish made of the flour of dried cassava. Wari wa jora. Formerly the Rabais simply called it Wari wa mugazija.
**Jule** (Kid.), *n.* (= Furuma).
**Juma** (Kij.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a week; the great day of the week, Friday. Juma pili ha i ka we ku fika (= in Kir., Juma ra viri ka ri gomia ku fika).

## K.

**K,** the eleventh letter of the alphabet, pronounced as in "king." It is quite unnecessary to retain the *q*, as the Arabic **ق** is but seldom used, and then sounded by the Wanyika as a common *k*; *e.g.* Karafu.—[ED.]
**Ka.** *See* instances Fieta; Makalo; and Uya. One of the leading particles in the South-African family of languages.

*Footer: 136*


---

## [PDF Page 150 — Dictionary Page 137 (Ka — Kad)]

  Preceded by the personal particles: Ni-, u-, a-, pl. Hu-, mu-, a-; the various particles relating to the different classes of nouns, Ga-, i-, ki-, ri-, zi-, u-, vi-; and the negative particles, Si-, ku-, ka-, pl. Kahu-, kamu-, ka-, it forms a tense, which answers very much to the Greek aorist.
**Ka.** (1) *See* Hegera; Enda; Niamola; Samu; Simamira; Muansa. Used in conjunction with Ka, Ku, Vo, Dzi, etc. Ka-a-ambire-'ende. Enda uka-a-ambire 'ende. Kaere kaere madzadzigo mabomu; or, Kuari ku dzadzika ku bomu. Kaere akignieta?
(2) (= Naka go rera; Hendika).
(3) *n.* and *adj.* *See* Zimira.
(4) *gen. part.*, of.
(5) *dim. prefix* (= Ki). Banda, A shed. Kabanda, A small shed.
**Ka.** *See* Kaya. Ni-kusa ka, ni-ku-onie utu. Kuamba u-mulume, ni-kusa ka, ni-ku-onie alume ahenda fio.
**Kabadu,** *n.* *See* Bada. Mu badurire kabadu katite, u-mu-ikire.
**Kabanda,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small shed or hut. Dim. of Banda (Kibanda), which is more frequently used.
**Kabansi,** *n.* (ka).
**Kabao,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a very small board. Dim. of Lubao.
**Kabawa,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a very small ladle. Dim. of Bawa.
**Kabayo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). *See* Bayo; Luvayo. (K.) Ku nchisa kabayo, To live. Kavayo (?).
**Kabengo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Bengo.
**Kabidza,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). *See* Bidza. Kabidza ka mifui. Nidzi-mu-ona yuna kabidza ka mifui, hangi ni mine, hangi ni mihandahu.
**Kabiga,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a very small basin. Dim. of Luiga.
**Kabila,** *n.* (ya and ka). *See* Mula. Kabila mbi. Kabila mbidzo. Kabila ya pugu nayo inafula; or, Kabila ka madali nako kanafula.
**Kabimbinda** (= Kafuli?).
**Kabindi** (but Kavindi is of beads), *n.* (ka) (= Kabindisana). *See* Dikisa. Kabindi kazima, A good while. Yudzikuenda kabindi kadzo, kazima, He has gone a good while ago (= He has been gone a good while). Kabindi hika, or, Kabindi kaka yudzifika kure. Udzihenda kabindi sana, uere na-ni, or, uere ukihenda-ni?
**Kabisa** (Kij.), *adv.* (Kir., Kamare). *See* Guara; Umiria. Actually, thoroughly. Muana hiye ni mudanganifu kabisa, kahama korokoro.
**Kabomu,** *adj.* *See* Kaya.
**Kabu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Makabu) (= Limau in Kij.), a citron (in Kijomvu, an orange = Chungua in Kij. and Kir.).
**Kabugu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Lubugu, *q.v.*
**Kabunde, Kapunde,** *adv.* *See* Punde. Dim. of Punde.
**Kabusi,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small goat. Dim. of Mbusi.
**Kachache,** *adj.* *See* Kafula. Little.
**Kachanda,** *n.* (ka). Dim. of Chanda.
**Kachari,** *n.* (ka). Kachari ni kaniama kadide.
**Kache,** *adj.* Kadzana kache.
**Kachigo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Luchigo.
**Kachingo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a very small skin. Dim. of Chingo.
**Kadaba,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ludaba, *q.v.* Nina kadaba kangu katite, na-ku-oniesa uwe, ela si ambire mutu kuamba nina tumbaku.
**Kadahi,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a twig. Dim. of Ludahi. Kadahi ka kisibidi.
**Kadama,** *n.* (hika, pl. Vidama). Dim. of Ndama.

## [PDF Page 151 — Dictionary Page 138 (Kad — Kad)]

**Kademu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small rag. Dim. of Demu.
**Kadenge,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small he-goat. Dim. of Ndenge.
**Kadi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the blossom of the mukadi tree, used for scent by the people on the coast, wherefore a Munika woman, sick of the pepo, is also to be supplied with it in order to please the pepo who belongs to the Mohammedans. Kadi ni ufumba wa kidzomba.
**Kadi,** *n.* (ra) (= Laga). *See* Thumba. The chest, thorax, the breast of animals. N.B.—Of men, both Laga and Kadi are used, but of animals only Kadi. Yudzi-m-fumaga kadi. When slaughtered, however, the breast is called Niama ya laga. Yudzi-m-fumaga kadi, He shot it through the breast, an animal; or, He shot him through the chest, when a man is spoken of. Kadi rina-ni-luma, I have a pain in my chest (= Laga rina-ni-luma). A lumua kadini, To be pained in the chest.
**Kadide, Katite,** *adj.* (rel. to the ka class), small. Kadungu kadide.
**Kadigo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Digo.
**Kadiri** (Kij.), *n.* (ka and ya), measure, capacity. Noani kadiri kenu, or, kadiri yenu. Kitu hicho ni kadiri yani? Jembe hiro ni kadiri yani? Ni kunsane hebu dzano. Chamba ni dzano sinda-ri-wesa, chamba ni-ne, ndagula. Yugusa kadiri kani, or, yani? or, Yugusa kadiri kadze, or, yadze? Kadiri hio ndagula.
**Kadofu, Katovu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small navel. Dim. of Tofu.
**Kadonche,** or **Kadonge,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). *See* Koma. A small lump or piece, of food only, broken off. Dim. of Donge.
**Kadono,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small spot or speck. Dim. of Dono.
**Kadude,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidude), a thing, an instrument. Ukigula, unapata kadude dza hika.
**Kadudu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), any insect, when very small. Dim. of Mududu.
**Kadudusi,** *n.* (ka). Sifiala kadudusi kamenga ngari, aka-ni-kusa moyo?
**Kadundu, Katundu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small hole. Dim. of Tundu.
**Kadungu,** *n.* (ka), a small quantity of mudungu, a kind of gum. Dim. of Mudungu. Ni-pa kadungu katite, nikabume mafuhani.
**Kadurume,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Kadurume ka gnonsi kanaansa ku dzi usa.
**Kadza,** *n.* (ka). *See* Dza.
**Kadza,** *adv.*, not as yet. Kadza pita, He has not yet got it. Kadzadza (= Kadzakudza), He is not yet come.
**Kadzaga,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ludzaga.
**Kadzagamba,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a little giant. Dim. of Ndzagamba. Used of the males of animals of a smaller sort.
**Kadzaka,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a brake, a grove.
**Kadzama,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Uganga. Kadzama mbidzo, niomu, zinala Daida. *See* Dzudzuri.
**Kadzambo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ludzambo.
**Kadzambo.** He is not yet bad; He is pretty well in health. Used of a person in answer to an inquiry (= There is nothing the matter with him = Kana dzambo kana utu).
**Kadzambu,** *n.* (ka). Dim. of Niambu. Uvuke kadzuho hika, basi ufike kadzambu hikara. Kadzanane, not yet Kadzaankue.
**Kadzana,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzana). Dim. of Muana. (K.) Babe. Kadzana kadzanga.
**Kadzanagnombe,** *n.*, a small calf.
**Kadzanda,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzanda), (1) Dim. of Chanda.
(2) Dim. of Luanda. Vana kadzanda kadzo ka ku

  enenda hata ukaduena mfukuhi.
**Kadzano.** Dim. of Chano.
**Kadzansu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-) (= Kasansu). Dim. of Dzansu.
**Kadzao,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzao), a young or small bullock. Dim. of Ndzao.
**Kadzeha,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small valley. Dim. of Mueha. Yunarima muvunga vavo vakue kadzehani.
**Kadzembe,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small razor. Dim. of Luembe. Kadzembe kanaria hika!

**Kadzeru.**
**Kadzidio,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small awl. Dim. of Muidio.
**Kadzidza,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-).
**Kadzidzi,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Kadzidzi ga mudzi.
**Kadzidzi,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small creek. Dim. of Ludzidzi.
**Kadzidzoa,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small head. Dim. of Kidzoa.
**Kadzifiu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzifiu), a little knife. Dim. of Kifiu.
**Kadzifui,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a little arrow. Dim. of Mufui.
**Kadzignie,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a little chicken. Dim. of Zignie.
**Kadzihi,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), (1) a small tree. Dim. of Muhi.

**Kadziko,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), (1) any small vessel in which snuff is kept. Dim. of Kiko and Muiko. Kadziko ka dumbuku.

**Kadzima,** *n.* (ka), a small dish of wari. Dim. of Dzima.
**Kadzimo,** *n.* (ka), a small stature. Dim. of Kimo.
**Kadzina,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Uina.
**Kadzinga,** *n.* (ka). Dim. of Kinga or Jinga.
**Kadzino.** Dim. of Dzino.
**Kadziri,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small body. Dim. of Muiri.
**Kadzisa, Kadziza,** *n.* (ka), a slight darkness. Dim. of Kiza or Giza.
**Kadzisu.** Dim. of Isu.
**Kadzisui,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a very small fish. Dim. of Sui.
**Kadzitu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). *See* Rundarunda. (1) A little man. Dim. of Mutu. Kadzitu ka mutu. Kadzitu na-ko ni katite hika!

**Kadzivo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). *See* Hombo.

**Kadzivu-udzungu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a virulent kind of boil.
**Kadziwe,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-) (= Nuidza), a small stone.
**Kadzo,** *adj.* (rel. to the ka class). *See* Kabindi. Good, pretty, nice.
**Kadzo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzo), a small horn (used for blowing). Dim. of Dzo.
**Kadzoho,** *n.* (ka). Kadzoho hika kanaaka. Kadzoho hikara kanagnala.
**Kadzoka,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzoka), a small hatchet. Dim. of Dzoka.

**Kadzombo,** *n.* (ka), a small vessel. Dim. of Chombo.
**Kadzomo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-).
**Kadzongo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzongo), a small back of a child. Dim. of Mongo.
**Kadzongonene,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzongonene), a seam; lit. a small back which is thick. Dim. of Dzongonene. Ku piga kadzongonene, To sew a small seam.
**Kadzovo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ludzovo.

**Kadzudzu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-).
**Kadzuga,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), (1) Dim. of Ndzuga.

**Kadzuha,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small bow. Dim. of Uha.
**Kadzuho,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzuho). *See* Mueha. A rivulet. Dim. of Muho.
**Kadzukue,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small rope or string. Dim. of Lukue.
**Kadzukue,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzukue). Dim. of Lukue.
**Kadzulo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small frog. Dim. of Chulo.
**Kadzulu,** *n.* (ka). Dim. of Dzulu.
**Kadzumba,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vidzumba), a small house or hut. Dim. of Niumba.

**Kadzunchi,** or **Kadzungi,** *n.*

**Kadzuni,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a very small bird. Dim. of Nnini.
**Kadzuri,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-).
**Kaere** (= Kari).
**Kaere,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small udder. Dim. of Ere.

**Kafuani** (Kidigo), *adv.* (= Haraka and Hiraka), quickly.
**Kafufu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ka class), narrow. Kadzidzi kafufu, A small, narrow creek.
**Kafufu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small thicket. Dim. of Fufu.
**Kafuhi,** *adj.* (rel. to the ka class), short. Yuna kadzimo kafuhi, ni kidzadzala.
**Kafuidzo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Lufuidzo. Reha ko kafuidzo, nika fuidzire mboga, kidzungu ni kidide.
**Kafuiho,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small and thin stick. Dim. of Pfuiho or Fuiho.
**Kafula,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Fula. Muhama unakafula kachache.

**Kakuro,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small dog. Dim. of Kuro.

**Kala,** *v.n.* *See* Zanche; Kosi; Mfaramfara; Mfaruka; Ufiasi; Funda; Kilongo; Kirenge. To be, to live, behave; (K) become, happen, exist, last, occur. Ku kala na musena, To have. Gnombe hino

  idzi kala muno. Dzongo na luvi akala kundi. Yudzikala muno (= yudzihenda uere), He stayed a long time.
  **Kari,** or **Keri.** *See* Denguri. Diekera dzulu. Merelu inafuma idzipua kare.
  **Karira,** *v.* *See* Mufumurisi; Fusira; Kulo. Kidzi mu karira kidzo (= Kidzi-mu faira). Karira machi, Breed, hatch. Gnombe hino idzi-ni-karira muno. Gnombe hi ka-i-ka-ni-karira. Duruma ndi-ko ni-dza-ko karira, be kula vatu na-va-mania.
**Kala,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), a crab. Kala yuna kala poani. Kala a poani. Kala hi bofuko.
**Kala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Nikala. A coal. Kala ra moho, Coal. Kala ra kufua, A dead coal.
**Kalakala,** *n.* *See* the pl. Makalakala. The sing. seems never to be used.
**Kalamu,** *adj.* (= Kaalamu). *See* Alamu. Broad. Kanoa kalamu. Mutu hiye yugomba kanoa kalamu, kafidza (Kid.). *See* Chalamu in Kir.
**Kalanga,** *v.a.* (= Kanga (Kaanga) in Kij.). *See* Ku fiasa; Kokote. To fry, to roast in a pot; (K.) crisp, sear. Ku kalanga madzere mafu ga ku vukusa luayani ela ku kanga ni madzere ma zima mohoni. Ku kalanga requires a pot, with the Wanyika a large potsherd generally answers the purpose; but Ku kanga is to broil immediately on the fire. Ku kalanga ichi. Aravai a-dzi-wesao-akaulaga kuku; be aka-m-katakata niama, aka-zi-kalanga hata zikidobera, zikiifua; be akabuma mafuha ga gnombe maidzi, basi zikasonona; akahegula, aka-buma luigani. Basi chamba yunaria na wari, hebu chamba yunanoa na uchi ni ku furahiwa sana. Lola yunaka langa kuku mzima be kuku mzima yukalanguadze? Vina-hu-masha sana.
  **Kalangira,** (1) *v.d.*, to fry to, for another.
  (2) *v. instr.*, to fry with. Nu-m-kalangira mulume niama.
  **Kalangirua,** *v.p.*, to have anything fried to or for any one. Anakalangirua niama; ni atu ario na mariadzi madzo, ku dzi andanisa, dza ano Muamkemba. Ahoho hia ari na ndzala, be adzikalangirua madzere, adzihafuna.
  **Kalangua,** *v.p.*, to be fried.
**Kalanga,** *n.* (ya). N'dzo uwire unga wa kalanga. Kalanga hi, ya madzere, or, ya muhama ni mbidzo. Yunawira unga wa kalanga. Kalanga ukidzangania na babayu, be ukibunda, basi vinahama sana-ni mdzuano.
**Kalansa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), interspace between plants only.
**Kalekale.** *See* Ku sema.
**Kalemba,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small comb of a cock. Dim. of Lemba.
**Kalifu** (Kij.), *v.a.* (= Ku refia sana in Kir. proper), to do violence, to molest. Kidzoacho ni ki? ukinoa uchi ka-u-komia ku-ku-kalifu. Nidzenoa uchi, udzi-ni-kalifu, sindanoa uchi, kaviri gisi hio.
**Kalima,** *n.* (= Rukudzu), diligence. (K.) Ku henda kalima, To bestir one's self.
**Kalo,** *n.* *See* Kala.
**Kalo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Makalo; Ukalo; Kare). Kulorangu ni menga, ka-ri-enerua atu airi.
**Kaloda** (?). *See* Ridira.
**Kalomo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). *See* Ku kokota. Dim. of Mulomo.
**Kalongo,** *n.* (ka). Dim. of Mulongo.
**Kalonsi,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small mulonsi.
**Kalubu** (Kij.), *n.* (= Kuro in Kir.), a dog. Only used in reviling language.

**Kamare,** *adv.*, (K.) never, in no wise. Ukihenda utu, henda utu kamare, ela ukihenda utu wa ku gesagesa, basi ka-u-hama; kituche hicho kina-ku-dzeka.

**Kamba** (Kir.), *n.* (za), strings or small ropes. Pl. of Lukamba. Kamba za milala; sing. Lukamba lua milala.
**K'amba,** *v.* *See* Humisa; Shononesera; Yongoya. To say; frequently used as a *conj.*, if. *See* Chamba. Contracted from Ku amba.
**Kambala** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kamba).
**Kambi,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). Mutu wa kambi.
**Kambo** (Kij.). In Kij., the word, when used in connection with Baba, Mama, Muana, denotes stepfather, stepmother, stepchild; but in Kir. the word is only used for an illegitimate child. Muana wa kambo (= Muana wa mbuya, muana wa dzakadzaka). In Kir., there exists no word expressive of such a relationship. The mother says of such, Niana a mulumanga, They are the children of my husband, and *vice versâ*. To be called a Muana wa kambo is felt as a great disgrace, even by the Wanyika. 'Enda hiko muana wa kambo-we, Go thy way, thou illegitimate child. Kalubu udzi-mu-ebula sana.

**Kamfindi.** *See* Kamvindi.

**Kamo.**

## [PDF Page 158 — Dictionary Page 145 (Kan — Kan)]

**Kanani,** *n.* (za), contradiction, contention, dispute; lit. mutual denial. From Ku nana. Kanani za mutu hiyu ni ningi. Atu adzihenda kanani akadiekerana mifunga. Nidzigomba utu hiu be atu adzi-ni-hendera kanani ankue sefio; be hukabisha hata nika-a-guisa ulongo. Atu anakanani rana kitu akaamba: kitu hicho ki-usiku, ki-ugala; yuya muya-wena ye akaamba: sevio; akahadza vingine; akahenda kanani.
**Kanda,** *v.a.* (in Kir. proper and Kidigo, Ku kandira). *See* Ranga; Kanga. To press on the members or parts of the body with the hand; to press on, as clay in plastering it; to daub. Adzomba ni ku kanda niumba.
  **Kandira,** *v.a.* *See* Loka. Nakandira vatu valumavo.
**Kanda,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), rind, husk, pod. Kanda ra dzere, A leaf of a cob of Indian corn. Nidzihewa nazi na makandage. Makanda ga ngorosho, The husks of cashew nuts. Makanda ga izu, The skin of bananas. Kanda ra kunde, The pod of a bean; pl. Makanda ga kunde. Luvande lua kanda, One side of a pod.
**Kanda,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Funsa. One side. Ku ika; or, Kudenga kanda, To put aside. Ku fidza kanda, To conceal. Chala cha kanda, The little finger.
**Kanda,** *verb. pref.* (indicating the future, and rel. to the ka class), it will.
**Kandkanda,** *n.* *See* Guta; Lembelembe. The brink. Kandakanda ya bahari. Kandakanda ya moho. Kandakanda ya dzaka. Ku ambira kandakanda, To caution.
**Kanju,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the fruit of the mukanju tree, cashew fruit.
**Kanga,** *v.a.*, to broil, to grill. Ku kanga niama, To grill meat. Small pieces are put on sticks and laid on the fire. *See* Wache. Trop., Maneno higa gadzi-ni-kanga, gadzi-ni-songa, sikamania utuwe.
  **Kansa,** *v.a.*, to warm; (K.) stupe, foment. Ku kansa nguo moho, To warm clothes at the fire.
  **Kansira,** *v.d.* Na-m-kansira gnania dzerere. Resp., Undakansadze, na momo kava.
**Kanga** (rel. to the ka class), it resembles.
**Kanga,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the guinea-fowl. Kanga wa madzini, The name of a species bird living on the seashore (in Kid., Musingi). Akiaka niumba ni ku-i-kanda ulongo; kuamba ni mutu, angari Muzungu, kua ku aka to.
**Kanga,** *n.* (ya, za), rust. The word is also used of the shafts of arrows when they are tarnished. Kifiu kidziguira kanga; lit. The knife has seized rust. Mifui yangu idziguira kanga, My arrows have become tarnished.
**Kangaja, Kangacha,** *n.* (ya, za). Dzana huansa kuri, ela rero ni kangaja. Kangaja and Gola chiramukoche mfaya akadicka, akahala miengero ku lasa dzi msala.
**Kangu,** *poss. pron.*, my, mine.
**Kanguangu,** *adj.* *See* Kanoa. Light, quick, easy.
**Kangurunga,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vingurunga). Dim. of Ngurunga.
**Kani,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Kanani), denial. From Ku kana, To deny. Eh! mutu hiye yuna kani ye! yudzidida kua mbiriri.
**Kaniama,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Niama. (1) A small animal.
(2) A small piece of meat.
**Kaniki,** *n.*, the name of a blue cloth, indigo-dyed.
**Kaniza** (?), *v.*, to make well, to repair.
**Kano,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a sinew.
