**Kano,** *n.* (za) (= Kono). *See* Kunsumana. Pl. of Lukano. *See* Kano (ra). Nidzipata kano, simania jamba sindala luvohe-na chamba kazi ndala-simania. Kuna kano sa niamani be hizo ka-si-hendua luvohe, sinariwatu. Kano sa mongoni na sa maguluni. Kano mbidzi. Kano pfu.
**Kano,** *dem. pron.* *See* Kaka. That.
**Kanoa,** *n.* (ra and ka). *See* Karama. The mouth. Kanoa ri, or, Kanoa kai, A bad mouth; *i.e.* Bad words, bad or foul language. Gnania yuna kanoa kanguangu; akiambirua neno, basi akiona mutu tu, ni ku sema.
**Kanofu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Munofu.
**Kanokano.** *See* Kuara.
**Kansa** (Kidigo), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Lukansa in Kir.), the leaf of a palm tree. Kansa ndizo uhalaso ku piga makuti. H'ende hukafute kansa, hudzehugule kolekole. Kansa mbidzi. Kansa pfu. *See* Kansu.
**Kansu,** *n.* (ya, za), a garment worn by the Wasuahili, resembling a long shirt. Adzomba hia akafuala kansu sika-a-agira.
**Kanundu,** *n.* (ka).
**Kao,** *poss. pron.*, their.
**Kara,** *dem. pron.* (= Kako). *See* Kaka. That.
**Kara,** *adj.*, equal.
**Kara,** *adv.* *See* Balu. It may be, perhaps. Kara kandakuenda? Kara k'endere be? Kara yudzikuenda be? Kara yudzifika, Perhaps he has arrived. Gnania msiku kandakuenda karaye? I dare say Mr. N. will not go after all; or, Mr. N. will not go, will he? Utu hiu kara unga hura, I think this is similar to that. Gnombe io nidza-yo-yona, kara inga yako (for ni-dza-yo-i-ona), The cow which I have seen is very like thine. Kitu hikino kara kinga dza chako (when you are uncertain); but, Kitu hikino kinga changu, ela secho-ni ku halana, because you are more certain about what is your own. Kitu hikino kara kinga hikino. In this instance and some others, Balu or Labuda may be put for Kara. Kitu hiki nidza-cho-ki-ona, kara kinga changu, again expressive of doubt. Kara ndefio-hangi sefio simania.
**Karada** (Kij.), **Karatha,** *n.*, borrowed money, a loan, credit. Nidzikuenda londa deni kua Chindua kaka-ni-amini; ela nduguye Murenge ndiye adzeyeingira karada, basi nikahewa. Nidzi-ku-ingirira karada uwe Kuhensi ku riva, be udzi-ni-buma uhalifuni.
**Karakara,** *n.*, equal; (K.) fitness, image.
**Karakara,** *adj.* *See* Mumiro; Elekania; Era. Lit. equal equal, very equal. Atu hia a karakara akalingana. Yu karakara na gnania musiku. Hiki na hicho vi karakara. Mifui hi na-i-esa nikate karakara. Muche akikala na mulume, sudi arumbame, kugomba naye karakara, ku-mu-udzira neno ri.
**Karakara,** *prep.*, according to.
**Karakara,** *adv.*, in the same manner, in the manner of.
**Karama** (Kij.), *n.*, a feast. Hudzekuenda Jomfu, hun'enda-ana-henda karama, basi suino Aravai hukahewa, kombe rehu ra wari, hukaria hata hukaukuha, huka-u-richa. Gnania yuna kanoa ri, yuna karama (= maneno mai); dzusi wa-m-lavisa muana wa mutu, kuamba: lumua ni nioka; be lola! dzusi na dzanana-rero yudzilumua ni nioka; mutu hiye yuna karama kanoa ni-mua-kue. ## [PDF Page 160 — Dictionary Page 147 (Kar — Kas)]

  dzai). Kuehu karama ni kanoa kai; mutu akigomba rira tu neno, be rikahendeka.

**Karamu** (Kij.) (= Karama). *See* Makombo. A feast.
**Kare,** *n.* *See* Ere. Ancient time, oldness. Ada za kare, Customs of ancient time. Niumba hi ni ya kare, This house is old. Nguo ya kare, Old clothes.
**Kare,** *adv.* *See* Mafuadzi; Fuererua; Imirira; Muroana; Mafiasi; Karekare. (1) Long ago, long since, formerly, already.
(2) Not soon, long after. Mutu hiye yu kare ku hamba. Hudzifika kare. Kare viomu. Kare may refer to the future as well as to the past, as is also the case with the word Mbere. Kuna kare ya mbereni hiko huendako. Mudzeria kare chunga? Have you already had luncheon? or, Have you eaten luncheon long ago? The following refers to the future: A kuhenda ye vidzo na we mu hende vidzo, be munda sikirana hata kare au. Kumba ndio maneno ya kare. Hiko kare gandakala dza ngano. Dza maneno ga nsimo. Opt. of Ku kala.
**Kari** (= Kaere; Koari). *See* Duka. Seldom used, Chari or Chere being more commonly used for the sake of euphony.
**Kari,** *verb. adj.* *See* Chari. Ni ngari ni-kere vavo. *See* Futa; Angari; Adzi.
**Kari,** *adj.*, sharp, sour. *See* Kobieka. Chungua hiri ni kari, ri nkuatu, This orange is sour as a cashew apple.
**Karia,** *v.a.* *See* Kathia. To boast.
**Karibu** (Kij.), *v.n.* *See* Umiria. To come near, to approach.
  **Karibisha,** *v.a.*, to cause to come near, to invite.
**Karima,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). *See* Kirima. A hill, a small mountain. Dim. of Murima.
**Karira.** *See* Kala.
**Kariri,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Uriri.
**Kariva** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Kaliba in Kij. and Kins.), to ferment, become acid. Uchi hiu ukariva, This toddy is acid, having fermented.
**Karonda,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-) (= Kironda), a small sore or wound. Dim. of Ronda.
**Karondo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Rondo.
**Karua,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small blossom. Dim. of Rua.
**Karufu,** *n.* (ka), a slight smell. Dim. of Rufu.
**Kasa, Kaza, Kala,** *v.a.* *See* Sisa; Kimirimiri; Fifira. (1) To tighten. Yudzifuala nguo, yudzi-dzi-kasa. Lukue hilu ni luofu ni lua kare, uki-lu-kaza, lundadoka. Nidzi-m-funga nidzi-m-kaza lukue. Nidzi-dzi-funga mukumbu nidzi-dzi-kaza.
(2) To seize severely. Said of sickness. Ukongo udzi-m-kasa. Meno gadzikaza muno ku luma. Muiri osi una-m-luma hangu kare, ela vino udzi-m-kaza, kaidima korokoro. Akikaza, yundapata vifio alondafio kuani kana haraka ya ku gusa.
  **Kasira, Kazira.** *See* Nkue. Nidzikue nda-mu-isa, nidzi-m-kasira hata yudzi-ni-riva. Mutu hiyu yudzi-ni-gazira muno, na-m-riva-seye akenguaye. Nidziamba nirime vadide-benidze, ela moyo yudzi-ni-kasira hata dzi-va-mala, says a lazy boy, who wants to go to play. Mu-kazire hata ahende kazi hio, amale.
  **Kasua, Kazua,** *v.p.*, to be tightened. Ku kazua ni ukongo, To be taken with sickness.
**Kasansu,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Sansu.
**Kasha,** *n.* (pl. Makasha), a box.
**Kasi, Kazi,** *n.* (ya, za; but the pl. Makazi is also used), labour, work, business, occupation. From Ku kaza. Kazi hizi and

  Makazi higa. Kazi yani (= in Kij., Kazi gani), What work, etc. Kana cho kazi, He has no business with it; *i.e.* He does not care about it.
**Kasi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Makasi), the shell of a large cocoa-nut, with the top cut off to hold toddy. Kirenge hikino ni musala hebu ni kasi? Resp., Nahu-vi-ese. Kasi ni ku hendua ra nazi ya tonga. Kasi ra luuso. Kasi regnie ra ku lola. Kasi komu rikadzupa makazi iyaye; ni mufuaha wa cha via homa ra gnombe? Hendani kasi kasi, rindatosha, musihende kirenge kibomu.
**Kasia, Kazia,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), (1) a small lake.
(2) An oar (= Kofi).
**Kasichana,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), (K.) smack. Dim. of Musichana. Kasichana kadzo.
**Kasidi** (Kij.), *adv.* (= Kir., Ku uchirira), intentionally, wilfully.
**Kasikasi** (also often pronounced **Kas'kasi** or **Kaz'kazi**), *n.* (ya, ka, and za). *See* Humbuka. The north-east monsoon. Muanzo wa kas'kasi hunafunga minazi, uchi uki humbuka hu-kahikahi ya kas'kasi.
**Kasiku,** *n.* (ka, pl. Visiku), a small piece. Dim. of Siku. Kasiku ka kamvindi.
**Kasima, Kazima,** *adj.* (rel. to the ka class). *See* Kabindi. Whole, entire, considerable.
**Kasinge,** *n.* (ka, pl. Visinge), a small round mat. Dim. of Singe.
**Kasiri** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to provoke to anger. Moyo udzi-ni-kasiri, nidzilonda ku rira vivi kua neno hiro, adzi-ro-ni-amba. Muana yudzihenda utu moyo udzi-ni-kasiri nidziambi ni-m-pige.
  **Kasirika** (Kij.), *v.n.* (= Ku dzukirua in Kir.), to be angry.
**Kasolandesi.** Gnania hangu dzana yudzihenda kasola ndesi, ku dzi fidza mfula.
**Kasuche,** *n.* (ka, pl. Visuche). Dim. of Suche.
**Kasumari,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small nail. Dim. of Musumari.
**Kasumba,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small needle. Dim. of Sumba.
**Kata,** *v.a.* *See* Sunguluka; Kisikane; Kuvisiku. (1) To cut off or asunder; but Ku dema is to cut down, to fell, to divide. Ku kata niama; ku kata lukansa; ku kata milala. Ku kata ngao, To cut, to divide a space with or by, a partition.
(2) To cut off by death. *See* Kakongo.
(3) To decide, to settle. Ku kata muengero. Ku kata kima, To determine, to fix the price of anything. Mukamba kana maneno ga ku kata, manenoge ni ga ku endereza. Mudzikata kondo, You have decided, finished, the strife.
  **Katakata,** *v. reit.* *See* Kalanga. To cut repeatedly, to chop.
  **Katika,** *v.n.* *See* Dumuka. To break. Kalumirue yudzihenda katika. *See* Kakongo.
  **Katira,** *v.d.* *See* Hasirika. To cut to, for.
  **Katirana,** *v. reit.*
  **Katirua,** *v.p.*
  **Katua,** *v.p.*, to be cut, to be decided. Maneno gadzikatua, The words have, *i.e.* the matter has, been decided.
**Katha** (Kij.). *See* Maleli.
**Kathia,** *v.a.* Gnania yuna zi kathia, wamba, niani mutu ana-fikeraye?
**Katiri,** *n.* *See* Kadiri. Measure.
**Kauli** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Linkua), a word. Ku lafia kauli, To testify.
**Kauma,** *prop. n.*, the calumba root.
**Kauri,** *n.*, cowry. Koho ya kauwara ku dzukirua hiraka.
**Kauwara** (Kig.).
**Kava.** *See* Kansira.

  Niki siwa na atu ela gnombe kava, be ni ndahendadze?
**Kava** (?). Hangu dzana na dita kava?
**Ka, va, ko,** *particles.*
**Ka va na.** Lit. Not there with, there is not.
**Kavande,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vivande), a small piece; (K.) slice. Dim. of Luvande. Kavande ka waraka, Slip of a letter.
**Kavansi,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small noose. Dim. of Vansi. Kavansi ka ku hegera vimbule.
**Kavayo,** *n.* (ka) (= Kabayo), (K.) talk, foolish talk. Mutu hiye yunanena, uki-mu-ona yu peho, ela akinoa uchi yuna kavayo, That man said he saw a spirit, but having drunk toddy, he talks foolishly.
**Kavedi,** *n.* (ka).
**Kavegnio,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small aperture. Dim. of Pegnio.
**Kavehe,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a very small ring. Dim. of Pehe.
**Kaveho,** *n.* (ka), (1) a slight, gentle breeze. Kaveho hiko ni kadzo, That little breeze is good, pleasant, agreeable.
(2) A little shade. Dim. of Luveho. Ningaoya hiva, ela kavana peho ya keri, kaveho ni kadide; ndakuenda mbere hata nione peho mbidzo.
**Ka-vi.** *See* Kaya.
  **Ka-vi-ko.**
  **Ka-vi-vo.**
**Kaviero,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small broom. Dim. of Luviero.
**Kavinda,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a small bag. Dim. of Pinda.
**Kavindi,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-), a necklace. Dim. of Vindi. Kavindi ka ushanga, A necklace of beads. Kavindi ka mukufu, A necklace of chain.
**Kavindo,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Luvindo.
**Kaviri,** *adv.*, again, also; lit. a second time.
**Ka vo.** He, or she, is not there.
**Kavoke,** *n.* (ka, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Luvohe. Kavohe ka uha wa tana.
**Kavu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Gamba. A basket.
**Kaya,** *n.* (ya, za; ra, ma; and ka, ra) (= Gaga). *See* Mumfiria. A retreat, place of retreat, a village fortified with jungle. Ku piga kaya (= Ku yayarika). A kaya must have (1) a mumfiria; (2) a moro; (3) a rungu. Mumfiria, na moro na rungu-ndivo mu-manika na-vo kuamba ni kaya. Kaya ka-va-ko-fungua lukuva to, ni kaya ka-vi-ko? Resp., Ni kaya kabomu; or, Ni kaya ka Mudzi muvia; or, Ni kaya ka Fimboni; or, Ni kaya ka Kjiembeni.
**Kayakaya,** *adv.*, entirely, thoroughly. Ku uma kayakaya kamare, To dry up entirely.
**Ke,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ka class), his, her, its.
**Ke,** *interj.*, indicating surprise. *See* Runga.
**Kedania,** *v.n.* Ndzo, huvonde, hukedanie. Ndzo, husage vamenga, hukedanie, hulole, andaye mala na mbere. Hukedanie ku aka niumba, hulole andaye mala na mbere. Atu hio anarima ku kedania, or, anakedania. Atu hara anakedania, mahihagao ni mabomu.
**Kefule.** *See* Kafule.
**Kehere,** *v.* Utu nikehere-o no hiu.
**Kehu,** *poss. pron.*
**Keke,** *n.* (ra), a drill, native borer. Keke ra wiha rina linkua ra ku endereza;—atu akisikira keke, basi akaramuka. Keke ra nioka ka-ri-enderesua ni fuhi. Mutu akilumua ni nioka, yunapiga keke, kuamba atu asikire, be huya amaniaye muhi wa nioka, adze, a-m-lagule. Muhoho yunaogesua firangi, be yunapiga keke. Mutu akipigua, naye ni ku piga keke.
**Kekerekekere,** or **Kikirikikiri,** *n.* and *adv.*, confused noise, jargon, gabble; in a rattling

  manner. Atu anafiererana kekerekekere. Unagomba kekerekekere mbona, sikasikira. Nasikira kekerekekere u ela semania a kombavio.
**Keleka** (Kig.), *v.a.* (= Ku kemba in Kir.), to strain. Ni-pa ndefu, nikeleke madzi.
**Kelele,** *n.*, an alarm, outcry.
**Keleti,** *v.n.*, to sit.
**Kelia,** *n.* (ra). *See* Yongoya. The name of a dance. Ku piga; or, Ku fuina kelia. Kelia hiro ridzikesua cho hata ba-kudzecha. Kelia hiro ringahama, kuamba vana mithiuka, ela kavari na mithiuka, adzifuina kivuvu, adzifumuka. Kupiga kelia uirani.
**Kema.** *See* Chema.
**Kemba,** *v.a.*, to strain. Said of water and palm-wine; but of the hui it is, Ku dzudza. Ku kemba uchi na ndifu.
  **Kembeka.** Nidzikemba higa madzi, ela ka-ga-ka kembeka to.
  **Kembera,** *v.d.* and *instr.* Ni-kemberani go madzi, nina shuhuli ingina mimi. Ndifu ya ku kembera madzi, or, uchi.
  **Kembula,** *v.a.* (in Kij., Dengua; Kins., Gompa). *See* Ku higa; Ku fuiga. To sop out, to pour out. Or Kebula. Nakembula madzi kisima ka-ki-reha.
**Kenda,** *v.*, for Ka enda, He, or she, goes not.
**Kenda,** *adj.*, nine.
**Kenga,** *v.a.* *See* Pishi. To deceive, to cheat, defraud. Nidzi-m-kenga, ela kakakubali.
  **Kengana,** *v. ref.*, to deceive one another. Atu hia anakengana usena.
  **Kengeka,** *v.n.* *See* Langasa. To be deceived. Mutu ni muerefu hiye, kakengeka kabisa, This man is clever, he is not to be deceived at all. Hiye ni bule-ni zuzu, kakomia ku kengeka, kakomia ku kubali maneno ga ku kengeka. Mutu hiye hata uki-m-bemba, kakubali, kakengeka.
  **Kengera,** (1) *v. rel.*, to deceive for. Udzi-m-kengerani, kumba ni ulongo?
  (2) To avoid, escape (?). Hudzi-m-kenkera, hata hudzi-m-guira hudzi-m-funga. Nidzi-i-kengera, hata nidzi-i-funga gnombe dziru. Kuku hiyu sika-m-zola, nidzi-m-kengera, hata nidzi-m-guira.
  **Kengerakengera,** *v. reit.*
  **Kengewa** (?).
  **Kengua,** *v.p.*, to be deceived or defrauded. Yukengua, kakakubali, yudzikahala.
**Kenge,** *n.* (ra). Obs.
**Kenu,** *poss. pron.* *See* Kadiri.
**Kere,** *adv.* (= Slangansira). *See* Ku; Rere; Futa; Mamu; Cheri; Kala. Vatu hivo vakere mutu, There is somebody in that place. Mahombo gakere lagani. Mukere-vi? Where are ye?
**Kerekere.**
**Kerekere,** *n.* (ya, za). Lomba luangu na lu henda kerekere.
**Kerekesa,** *v.a.* *See* Ringania; Sinda; Mkuadu; Divira; Dele; Udzungu; Kufia. (1) To cut even the bottom or top part of anything.
(2) To notch. *See* Msalaba. Nakerekesa nikate.
  **Kerekesera,** *v.d.* and *instr.* Ni-pa kifiu nikerekesere mufui wangu. Kifiu changu kidzihulua, be sina kifiu cha ku kerekesera mufui wangu.
  **Kerekesua,** *v.p.* Muvini hiu udzikerekesua to.
**Keregnense,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), a quail. The natives imitate its cry by the sound, Keregne! karegne!
**Keresa,** *v.a.* (= Chereza).
**Keresi** (Kig.), *v.n.* (= Ku sagala in Kir.), to sit.
**Keri,** *n.* (ya). *See* Golosa. Truth.
**Keri,** *adv.* *See* Darasira. Truly, really.
**Kesa.** *See* Chesa; Cha.

**Ki,** *a particle*, (1) this, prefixed to the following:—
* Kiki Hiki Kika Kikacho
* Kicho Hicho Kina Kidzacho
* Kina Hikino Kincha Kiricho
* Kira Hikira Kidzi
Yudzi ni funga yudzi ni kignia ki.
(2) Used in conjugation, if, when. Akidza, If he comes.
**Ki,** *a prefix to nouns*, (1) a particularizing particle, used to denote nouns of what is inanimate and diminutive; Kilongola, Kidia, Chotherua, etc., are exceptions. When followed by a vowel, *k* is changed into *ch*, and the *i* is dropped, and sometimes, when it is followed by a consonant, *k*, *d*, *ch*, are frequently interchanged for the sake of euphony.
(2) (= *ish* in English), pertaining to, language of.
(3) *dim. prefix* (= Ka).
**Ki, Kii,** *adj.* *See* Kalifu. Bad. Kicho unda-cho-ni-pa uwe, nahala, sina ki.
**Kia,** *n.* *See* Chia.
**Kiambo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viambo), a pig. Contracted into Chambo. Kiambo cha ku gotera dingo.
**Kiango** (Kid.), *n.* (pl. Vi-) (= Kotamiro in Kins.).
**Kiansa.**
**Kianso** (= Chanso cha usiku). *See* Kigolosi. Ku ansa kianso cha lusihu.
**Kiarabu,** *adj.*, Arabic.
**Kiasi, Kiazi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viasi). *See* Pima; Pingu; Gola; Muesa. (1) A load for two or three men? (Kadzeru). Kiasi cha atu airi, akahu, etc. Kiazi hicho yudzifika (= Kibindi, etc.).
(2) A root, the sweet potato.
**Kibaba,** *n.* *See* Mbaba. (1) A small measure, one-third of a pishi, holding about one pound of grain.
(2) Something very small. Gnania yuna moyo (wa) kibaba, akiona utu, kausa wala katieka moyo, ni ku fika na ku fiola tu. Gnania yunga dza gnania, yuna moyo kibaba. Yudzihenda moyo kibaba, ni kusa fumurira, ku londa kitu haraka, etc.
**Kibaba.**
**Kibadu,** *n.* *See* Kabadu.
**Kibahe,** *adj.* (= Kingi), great, large, considerable.
**Kibako,** *adv.* Only used in connection with Ku fuala nguo. Rarely used. Ku fuala nguo kibago (= Ku-si-dema), To wear one's cloth.
**Kibaladzanga** (Kid.), *n.*
**Kibambama,** or **Kibambame** (Kirive), *n.* (pl. Vi-). Kitunga nguo ku bambama?
**Kibambara.**
**Kibambaya,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small fragment, of calabashes only. Vibambaya via kirenge, The fragments of a calabash.
**Kibamfu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kabadu; Ku bamfula. A piece of anything. Mutu wadzonga kinu-n'enende nikadzole, vibamfu, or, vigome vikafio bodoka, nidze nibume mohoni ni chitire niungu.
**Kibanansi,** *n.*
**Kibanda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small bough. Dim. of Panda.
**Kibanda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small hut, a shed, such as is made in a plantation. Nidziaka kibanda cha mundani.
**Kibangala** (Kid.) (= Kibaria in Kir.). *See* Tembo. Dim. of Bangala.
**Kibansi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Bansi.
**Kibao,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small board or plank. Dim. of Lubao.
**Kibarabara** (Kij.), *n.*, (1) the name of a kind of fish.
(2) A babbler, a chatterer. U-kibarabara we.
**Kibari,** *n.* (cha), a small, distant relationship. Dim. of Mbari. Kibaridao ni kitembe, ni atu atembe. Kibari cha muhi.
**Kibaria,** *n.* (1) Kibaria cha ndzofu. (2)

## [PDF Page 165 — Dictionary Page 152 (Kib — Kib)]

  Kibaria kivudzu cha ku noerera. Also called Mueneza. (3) Kibaria kibomu cha ku noerera, cha kiasi. (4) Kibaria ngabe. (5) Kibaria muulaga ndzala. (6) Kibaria viiri musala. (7) Kibaria viiri kasi ma cha mbiri. (8) Kibaria viiri kasi ma cha via homa. (9) Kibaria viiri cha via homa ra gnombe.
**Kibato,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small spot, a speckle, of colour. Dim. of Bato. Vibato vibato via makuviu. Gnombe yangu ina vibato vibato, or, i-vibato vibato, My cow is very speckled; has speckles speckles; or, it is speckled speckled. Kibato cha munda, A small spot of a plantation; *i.e.* A very small plantation. Kana munda wa keri, ni kibato.
**Kibau,** *adj.* (= Kingi, which is more frequently used), much. Kitu hiki ni kibau.
**Kibawa, Kipawa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small ladle, made of a kivo cha nazi, the shell of a cocoa-nut. Dim. of Pawa.
**Kibedo, Kipeto** (Kij.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kifudza in Kir.), a packet.
**Kibekule,** *n.*, a small basin. Dim. of Bekule. Nguo ya kibekule? mua kibegu. Pishi ya mua kibekuli.
**Kibembefu** (= Kivuluda). Obs.
**Kibete,** *n.*, a small foot. Kuku wa kibete; pl. Kuku a vibete. Kibete kiki cha kuku, kikienenda, kihenda sororeka. Gnombe hi ni pfuhi, ni kibete.
**Kibicho,** *n.* (pl. Vi-).
**Kibiga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kikango in Kij.). *See* Uganga. (1) A small basin. Dim. of Luiga. Reha cho kibiga, hubumire mboga.
(2) A small earthenware vessel for roasting in. Kibiga kiingira mahoma mane.
(3) The raised edge of wire wound round the arm; it being formed into a small coil at one end. In Kik. it is called Chu. Kibiga cha dzango, hebu cha mukodo, kinga hako ra luiga. Dunga uhende kibiga.
(4) The name of a species of ant, as large as the dzalafu, red ants.
**Kibigatutu,** *n.* Prov., U-nga kibigatutu, kudzulka mafi. Gnania yunga kibigatutu, kadzuka mafi, *i.e.* Manenoge ni mangi, ka-ga-sira kanoani.
**Kibilingo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a banjo with one string, made of a small calabash or mauyu, by cutting off the top and bottom and covering the bottom with a piece of skin. A string, being run through it and fastened on the inside by a knot, is then tied to a small bow, so that it looks like a fiddle-stick, while the other part acts as a sounding-board. Ku piga kibilingo, To play the kibilingo. This was formerly a favourite amusement of boys whilst tending their sheep and goats. They called it their muansa, and the admission to it was to be paid for by a few cobs of Indian corn. It is now forsaken, as many other plays, in consequence of the increase of cattle and palm-wine.
**Kibiliwi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the name of a small kind of grasshopper. Dim. of Piliwi.
**Kibimba,** *n.* Dim. of Bimba. Kibimba wamba ni nche, or, ni cha nche. Ni kibansi kidide; ki-nga nioe, ela nioe ni mbomu.
**Kibimbinda,** *n.* (only used as predicate). *See* Kiharusi. One who is plump, short and thick. Mutu hiyu ni kibimbinda, ni mu fahi na muziho.
**Kibimo, Kipimo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) measure. From Ku pima. Nidzi-ku-rinda kipimo kizima.
(2) *See* Chisa. Moderation.

## [PDF Page 166 — Dictionary Page 153 (Kib — Kib)]

  S'ambe: ndo anoafio, yunoa na kipimo, ela rero yudzidundisua.
**Kibindi, Kipindi,** *n.* (cha) (= Pima). *See* Kua; Pima. A while, a small space of time. Kipindi hicho adzacho uka-yudzifika; lit. That while which he has started, he has arrived now (= By the time passed since he started, he must have arrived now). Nidzisa gala kipindi kisima ku-ku-rinda kukakudza, be nikaenenda. Dzana kipindi hicho wari yudziuka, Yesterday, about this time, he had started. Mu-rinde kipindi cha dzua kudzua, akikala ka-dza-kudza, basi uuye. Kula neno rina kipindiche (Kid.), Kula neno rina kiasiche (Kir.), Each word has its time; *i.e.* A matter should not be spoken of longer than is necessary. Hungakuenda hivo dzua ri-lua mudzana, basi hudzisa-gala hata dzua ridzivola; kipindi hicho, hata dzua ridzibodoka, hu-vavo; hunalola-kakundakudza mutu, basi hukauya. Kipindi hicho yu Makuba. Machero, kukiaja-liwa, kipindi hicho, or, pima hiso hundakala hudzifika.
**Kibindo.**
**Kibini** (Kij.), *n.* (cha), the real truth, in contradistinction to hearsay. Nidziona m'egnie na madzo gangu, si angue, ni kibini. Adzieona kibini ni ani? A. G. na muambamba akuenda ona Uguja ndio agomba-o kibini, kuani a kuenda geri. Ni dzie-mu vinda ndimi, na nidzie-mu-nida ordimi, It is I.
**Kibinikizo,** *n.*, a small cover.
**Kibiru,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kikorokoro in Kns.). In animals it is Nkuiru. Kibiru changu kina-ni-luma.
**Kibidza,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kidzamundi), a handful, of arrows only.
**Kibogo,** *n.*, the penis. Kibogo cha mulume (= Kigandegande cha mulume in Kid.).
**Kibolesa,** *n.* (pl. Vi-) (= Kiniumeniume). Gnania yuna kibolesa, yugomba kibolesa, manenoge ga-rero. Kare atu ere a-kigomba kibolesa muno, or, kibolesa kingi sana. Uwe wagomba maneno ga kibolesa nini? dza kuamba u-mukongo. Be ku-ni-usa kibolesa nini? This is said to one who you know has understood you, but asks again.
**Kibolobolo, Kipolopolo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (K.) pellet. Dim. of Polopolo.
**Kiboma** (Kid.), *n.* (= Muche; Mfiere). *See* Kihenso. Ache viboma a-vavo, ela ka-a-runga; yu mura tu mua muche mufiere, ndiye a-mu-hensaye.
**Kibombue** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kisombo and Mshedo in Kij., and Kibonkue in Kins.; Kishombo in Kir.), a mixture of beans, peas, etc., for food.
**Kibondonkue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), lit. something merely pounded. A dish made of unripe maere, merely pounded and boiled, not ground. Kibondonkue cha maere madzanga ga ku bokera ndzalani. When first dried over a fire and then pounded and sieved, it is called madasa.
**Kibongo,** *n.* (pl. Vi-), the brain, cranium.
**Kibonkue** (Kidigo), *n.* (cha) (= Kibondonkue in Kir.).
**Kibora,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a young cock. Dim. of Bora.
**Kibori,** *n.* Dim. of Bori. Pembe ya kibori.
**Kibuanabuana,** or **Kishombo,** *adj.* Una-dzi-ika, kibuanabuana, ku henda atu dza adumuao; be kuehu Ravai ka-ku-na dzumbe ra ku dzi ika kibuanabuana.
**Kibuelesa,** *n.*

## [PDF Page 167 — Dictionary Page 154 (Kib — Kid)]

  Kibolesa, ku dzomba kibuelesa. Gnania yunagomba kibuelesa.
**Kibuichi** (Kid.). Ku niala kibuichi.
**Kibula** (= Vuri). *See* Musa.
**Kibuli,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a pendant from the ear, consisting of a piece of brass, about the length of a finger and worked ornamentally. Vibuli via kunde, Pods of beans hanging, as they are immediately after the blossom is over. Kunde sidzihenda vibuli, The beans have made pods.
**Kibulu,** *n.* (cha), (K.) moth. Dim. of Bulu.
**Kibumba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Kibumba cha lusi (pl. niusi). Kibumba cha ukonche. Kibumba cha ufuha. Kibumba cha niuchi. Kibumba cha milala. Kibumba cha tumbaku.
**Kibumbafu,** *adj.*, nominal; (K.) clew, crewel, slug. Atu a kare maneno gao gari ga kibumbafu, or, ga kibolesa, because they said, N-dzoani, ndafiala mungina.
**Kibumbuana,** *n.* (only used as predicate, and subject to no change), roundness. Niumba sa Kikamba zi kibumbuana, The Wakamba huts are round; lit. are a roundness. Niungu nazo si kibumbuana, Pots also are round. Ichi ra kuku ri kibumbuana, The egg of a fowl is round. Machi ga kuku ga kibumbuana. Muvini hiu u kibumbuana, ela hura u mirima mirima, ka-u-ka dzongua to. Nazi hino i kibumbuana, ka-i-hendeka kaha, ni pfuhi, This cocoa-nut is round; it cannot be made into a kaha; it is too short. This is in contradistinction to Nire. Mikahe hio i-kibumbuana, These loaves are round. Vidziwe hivi vi-kibumbuana, These stones are round. Hunde hiri ni bumbuana. Fiza hiri ni bomu ni bumbuana.
**Kibumiro.**
**Kibungu.**
**Kibungufu,** *adj.* Kitu kino ka-ki-kadimira, ni kibungufu.
**Kibunguo,** *n.* Ku piga kibunguo, guamba, avole. Si pigue kibunguo.
**Kiburu,** *n.*, very large. Only used in connection with Gnombe. Kiburu cha gnombe (cha ndzao, cha ndewa bomu), An exceedingly large bullock.
**Kiburu** (Kidigo), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small calabash. Dim. of Buru.
**Kibusi, Kibuzi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small goat; (K.) a kid. Dim. of Mbuzi.
**Kichache,** *adj.* *See* Kinemi; Dzupisa; Kitembe. Few.
**Kichamanda.**
**Kiche,** *adj.* *See* Mafunganofungano; Mafundango. Small.
**Kichingo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Sosonga. A small skin, or hide. Dim. of Chingo.
**Kicho,** *pron.* (for the ki class) (= Hicho kichocho). *See* Ki.
**Kichogni,** *adj.*, pertaining to Chogni, the name of a town and tribe of Wanyika, one day's journey north of Rabai.
**Kichongochongo.** *See* Kitongotongo.
**Kichonguachongua,** *adv.* Gnania ni mudzai; yudzi-m-lola mutu kichongua, chongua, naye akaguirua ni muiri, akafua; be ndiye adzaye-m-loga.
**Kidaba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ludaba.
**Kidafu,** *n.* *See* Kidaka (K.). A small cocoa-nut, not fully ripe, but full of water. Dim. of Dafu.
**Kidagaya,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kidagna.** (Cha nazi = Kibando.)
**Kidahi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a twig. Dim. of Ludahi or Tahi. Lula ludahi nalo luna vidahi, vidahi nafio vina ndodo,

## [PDF Page 168 — Dictionary Page 155 (Kid — Kid)]

  ndo zi-ka-zo veza, or, sindikisa. Vaansavo kudanikana ni kidahi. Cha muhi (= kibanda)?
**Kidai** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kidahi in Kir.).
**Kidaida,** *adj.* *See* Mafu; Kidasi. Kitaita, pertaining to Taita.
**Kidaki,** *n.* (cha). Kidaki cha nazi.
**Kidako,** *n.* (ch. pl. Vi-; dza ya hako; pl. dza sa mahako), posteriors. Yusagala kidako, To sit, a common expression. Gnania yusegere kidako tu; atu anahamba—mutu akakuenda pata kitu, akauya, ela iye kana utu ahendao—yusegere kidako tu. The word also occurs in combination with Nche, in which it is the dim. of Mudako. *See* Nchi; Kitako.
**Kidala,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Ndala Bahasi vakarimua kidala.
**Kidale,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Punga.
**Kidama,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ndama.
**Kidamba,** *n.* Mutu hiye ni nui ni kidamba (= mudamba). *See* Ambaza.
**Kidambara, Kitambara,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (Kij., Kitamba). *See* Kidemu and Kidzansa. A small cloth. Nguo yangu idzitaruka, idzikala kitambara, ka-ki-fumika kaviri.
**Kidambi, Kitambi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a piece of cloth, about two yards in length. Kidambi ni cha Marikano, cha Basaradi, cha Sidara, cha Ngorio.
(2) *See* Thugnia. Thunia ra kidambi, ni rira-tu rikalaro ifuni.
**Kidambo, Kitambo** (Kij.), *n.* (cha) (= Kihambo ogu agou), a walk, *i.e.* the space which one walks. Kitambo hicho ni kure (= Kir., Vatu hivo ni kure), That's a long walk. Ni kidambo kisima navo (= Kir., Ni vatu vasima navo, hangu huaenenda kahufika kumba ni kure). Vatu hivo ni kidambo kisima.
**Kidamfira,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the chitterlings. Kidamfira ni mulomo wa ifu. Ifu rikihumbulua, rikilafiwa mafi, basi sira niamase sikikatua, sikigafiwa, basi kiihua kidamfira, ni niama ya ifu. Nidzienerua ni kidamfira tu, sibadire niama. Muana wenu yuchari mukongo, kavola? Is your son, or daughter, still sick? does he, or she, not recover? Resp., Muana wenu ni muana ye? ni kidamfira, kadzuka mafi (= Kadukana na ukongo).
**Kidana, Kitana,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a little bow made for a child to play with. Dim. of Tana. Muana lume akitimisa dziku dzano, babaye aka-mu-hendera kitana, aka-a-va afialusa, kuamba a-mu-upusire muana ndze na kira kidana.
**Kidanga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a bracelet, of flat workmanship. Kidanga kibambara, The kidanga is flat.
**Kidanidani,** *n.*, abroad. Machira ga kidanidani.
**Kidasi** (Kitaita), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a bag made of the fibres of the baobab. It is in such bags that people from Kathiaro sometimes bring beans to the Wanyika, whence the name has become known among them.
**Kidaso,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Ku dasa. Obs. Ku dasana kidaso. *See* Kuachula. Nidzi-ku-udzira kidaso.
**Kidedemeza, Kitetemeza,** *n.*, the unsteadiness of the hand in working. From Ku tetema, To tremble. Yuna kitetemeza.
**Kidedemo, Kitetemo,** *n.* (cha). *See* Surusa. Fever, ague. From Ku tetema, To tremble.
**Kideme,** *n.*, the large intestines.
**Kidemu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a small rag. Dim. of Demu.

## [PDF Page 169 — Dictionary Page 156 (Kid — Kid)]

  (2) The name of a kind of grass or plant.
**Kidenge,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small he-goat. Dim. of Ndenge.
**Kidengelesa,** *n.* (= Dao in Kij.). *See* Mfu; Kifumfu; Mkuena. A curvity, a curve. Atu adzifuina kidengeleza ku dengeleka lufu na uira.
**Kidengu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the wrist. Nalumua na kidengu (= Ulungo wa kigere).
**Kidengu** (Kij.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Masurui hivara kareari akiulaga atu ahalifu na kidengu.
**Kidesi.** Kidesi luanda pania.
**Kidia,** *n.* (cha). Kidia ngu. Nidziona kidia, ela Mulungu yudzierekesa hata nidzidia, yu-dzi-ni-lafia kidiani. Nidziona kidia vatite kuamba niulague, I had a very narrow escape. Nidziona kidia; kidia ni-dza-cho ona, ka-ki-dza onewa ni mutu, ela Mulungu yudzi-ni-difia; or, Kidia ni-dza-cho ona mimi, ka-ki-dza onua ni mutu mungine. Nidziona kidia, nidziamba nifui, ela Mulungu yudzi-ni-difia, yudzi-ni-lafia kidiani.
**Kidide, Kitite,** *adj.*, small.
**Kidignio.** *See* Pambo.
**Kidigo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Digo.
**Kidigo,** *adj.*, belonging to or being of the nature of the Adigo (Kij., Wadigo), the Wanyika tribes south of Mombas.
**Kidiki.** *See* Kibondonkue cha mugasija.
**Kidimu.** Kuku wa kidimu.
**Kidina,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Cha muhi), the stem of a tree. Muhi hiu una kidina kire. Muyu, kidinache ni kisiho, ni chalamu, ela si kire. Muhi hiu una kidina kisiho, This tree has a big stem.
**Kidindi,** *n.* (cha), wire of medium thickness, between the madzango and mukodo. Kidindi cha gnandu, Brass wire. Kidindi cha mukundua, Copper wire.
**Kidindirio,** *n.*
**Kidinge,** *n.*
**Kidio,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Chumba. Ku luma, mihi ya vidio. Yudzikochesa, kadzambue ku oka vidio, ndosa alumue ni chunu, yudziguirua ni vidio. Kuna Muganga wa vidio.
**Kidisa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Obs. The word denoted a big ring of metal which was worn round the neck. It has been superseded by the madzango, and, on account of its great weight, was gladly given up when brass wire found its way to their country. Kidisa chari urembo wa ache, ela hangu madzango gakudza, ka-vi-hama kaviri; vidziambua: ni mizigo dzingoni. Sudi mutu aalile dzango, ndo vihamafio. The *vi* and *fio* are here used in a general sense, not rel. to Dzango.
**Kiditi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a kind of small basket.
**Kidodi** (Kid.), *n.* *See* Dzakasa.
**Kidodo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small dry stick or twig. Dim. of Ludodo.
**Kidofu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Ahoha; Koma. Dim. of Tofu. Nchira ya kidofu, A straight way.
**Kidoko,** *n.* *See* Dioko.
**Kidolue,** *n.* (cha), a soft mass (1) of grain, when too much water has been put to it in the mortar while pounding. Also called Daki. (2) Of manure or mud, as it is in a kraal during rain. Mfula idzidana, kidolue nacho kidzifuhuka.
**Kidonga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kinando in Kik.). *See* Pinguvia. A calabash of the smallest size, used as a snuff-box, but especially for keeping the various powders used in charming and witchcraft. Vidonga via uganga. Kuna

## [PDF Page 170 — Dictionary Page 157 (Kid — Kid)]

  mudzungu ufialao vidonga, be kira tu kidonga kikafumua dza pingu, kikaziwa, kikakala ndani ya niukue; be ndio iihuayo nkoba.
**Kidonge,** *n.* *See* Hifio. A small lump, a pill. Kidonge cha wari, A lump of cooked grain. Kidonge cha kishombo.
**Kidono,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small spot or speck, a bit or piece of anything. Dim. of Dono. Vidono via mua, Small pieces of sugar-cane.
**Kidosho,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the name of a species of bird. Dim. of Ndosho.
**Kidosi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) the name of a species of bird. Kidosi ni kuria marua ga mudundo. Kina mudundo ariao. Kina mulomo mure, basi kikadunga ndifu, akafika ku-ri-ko uchi, kikanoa. Ndosa huambe Kidosi kiratu kinagema.
(2) The name of a dance or play; the kidosi being the subject of the song used on the occasion: Kidosi - mulalani kauka, The kidosi never leaves the mulala, a species of dwarf palm, which is its favourite resort. These words are continually repeated as long as the dance lasts—
*Rero ni kuri, atu andafuina kidosi;*
*H'endeni kaya, hukalole kidosi.*
Aravai akihenda uirawari, be ndo aimbavo kidosi; atu akafuina, akapiga kikobuekobue; ache akadzadzarika, alume aka-a-kuachisa.
**Kidubulu.** From Ku dubuluka.
**Kidude, Kitude,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), any little thing or instrument. Dim. of Mudude.
**Kidudu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) any small insect. Dim. of Dudu. Kidudu hicho, That insect. Kidudu hiki si-ki-mania ni kidudu chani, I do not know what insect this is. Nidziingirua ni kidudu dzidoni. In former times there also existed a Kiravo cha kidudu. It was still older than the Kiravo ka fisi, which preceded the msafula.
(2) Confusion, perplexity.
**Kidudusi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a pimple. Vidudusi via ukambi.
**Kiduene,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Duene.
**Kidugudugu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small tumour, a swelling from a sting.
**Kiduku,** *n.*, a mane (?).
**Kidukusa, Kidukuda,** *n.* (= Pumbu), hernia when small; lit. that which shakes. Gnania hangu dzana, yudzihenda kidukusa.
**Kidulusi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the name of a species of small animal, with a red skin. Yu-nga dali, ela kafula; ni kidune do.
**Kidumbakasi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kidzumbakasi.
**Kidumbusi.** Madzi ga kidumbusi (= Madzi ga kimbuija and Magombora mumo). Madzigadzikala kidumbusi. Tungudza ya kidumbusi.
**Kidumia.**
**Kidundu, Kitundu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a small hole. Dim. of Tundu.
(2) A small calabash.
(3) The forehead.
**Kidune,** *adj.*, red.
**Kidune,** *n.* Kidune cha ichi, The yolk of an egg.
**Kidunga,** *n.*, a basket.
**Kidunganguo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the name of a species of briar; lit. cloth-pricker. Kidungonguo kikimera kingi mundani, basi kinaumalasa munda.
**Kidungu,** *n.*, a small basket of plaited palm leaves. Dim. of Dungu. *See* Mudungu. Yudzi-ni-dania kidungu-yudzi-ni-kumbukisa. Ah! udzi-ni-dania kidungu, nidzimania basi.

## [PDF Page 171 — Dictionary Page 158 (Kid — Kid)]

**Kidunje,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the name of a species of small grasshopper, cricket. Ni kaniama kanga fuancho, ela fuancho ni bomu.
**Kiduro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the shoulder.
**Kiduruma,** *adj.*, pertaining to Duruma, one of the Wanyika tribes.
**Kidurume, Kiturume,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Turume. Kidurume kidzo - kidzikoma reale hivo ki-ri-vo.
**Kidza.** *See* Gano; Luga; Musiro; Kidubulu; Fuiha; Muhalakore; Nona; Funula; Madiriri; Mdzuano; Kirufu.
**Kidza,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a bundle, packet. Kidza cha niama, Long strips of meat twisted together and tied up, to be ready for sale, a practice forsaken by the Rabais, but still continued with the Durumas. Kidza cha maere. Miniore miiri ni kidza cha maere.
**Ki-dza-cho,** *particles* used in conjugation (rel. to the ki class, and implying the perf. tense), it is which, it has which; *i.e.* which is or has, etc. Kitu ki-dza-cho angamika.
**Kidzadza,** *n.* (cha) (= Kidada in Kij.), (1) entanglement, complication. Kidzadza cha mbono.
(2) Dim. of Ludzadza. Ku-m-funga kidza dza mutu adzeyevunsika mukono.
**Kidzadzala,** *n.* (cha) (= Muambamba), a dwarf. Obs.
**Kidzaga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ludzaga.
**Kidzagamba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kadzagamba. A little giant. Dim, of Ndzagamba. Kidzagamba cha pfuno; kidzagamba cha sa, etc.
**Kidzagodzago,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a place where the grass has been trodden down. Nidziona kidzagodzago cha sa, alala-vo (= kilalo).
**Kidzaka,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a grove.
**Kidzakudza,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kibumba?), bundle, bunch, packet. Dim. of Dzakudza. Kidzakudza cha pani. Kidzakudza cha milala. Kidzakudza cha gnongo.
**Kidzala** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kifuifui in Kir.; Kicha in Kij.), epilepsy, lunacy.
**Kidzambalasi,** *n.* (cha), kindness, regard, tenderness of feeling, delicacy. Gnania kana kidzambalasi; aonacho nikuria tu. Ela gnania yuna kidzambalasi, yuhendadzagula; uki-mu-ona akiria niama, be ni niama mbidzo.
**Kidzambi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the open cloth put round the body and tucked in at the bosom, according to the fashion of Suahili women. This costume is always adopted by Wanyika women during the first pregnancy, and in such cases of sickness as are ascribed to the pepo.
**Kidzambo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ludzambo.
**Kidzamundi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Dzamundi. Kidzamundi cha mifui.
**Kidzana,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a little child. Dim. of Muana. Kidzana kilume, A boy. Kidzana kiche, A girl. Kidzana cha gnania kikadania madzo-ni kierefu. Kidzana kikalacha cho. Kidzana 'lume kikalacha cho! Kidzana kiche kikalacha cho; cho for hicho, as ye for hiye. Kidzana gnonsi, A lamb. Kidzana mbuzi, A kid. Kidzana gnombe, A calf. Kidzana kuku, A chicken.
**Kidzanga,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class). *See* Chere. Young, raw, unripe; (K.) infant. Yugomba kidzanga, He speaks like a child.
**Kidzangadza,** *n.* *See* Yongoya.
**Kidzangala,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Muangala.

**Kidzanganio,** *n.* (= Kidzanganiro). *See* Muambalu.
**Kidzanganiro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Mudzungu. That which is mixed with something else. One vegetable mixed with another.
**Kidzango,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Bembere. A small basket when worn out. Dim. of Dzango. Ni kikavu kidza cho taruka.
**Kidzangua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Luankua. Kidzankua cha kahikahi.
**Kidzaniu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Kidzaniu ni cha muhi muvudzu. Kidzaniu ni kere na kivudzu, ela kigome ni kifuhi na kisiho.
**Kidzansa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a piece, strip. Nguo idzidaruka muno, idzihenda videmu-vidzikala vidzansa vidzansa.
**Kidzansalago,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kidzansu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kisansu), (K.) sprit, bough. Dim. of Dzansu.
**Kidzao,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a young or small bullock. Dim. of Ndzao.
**Kidzasi,** *n.*
**Kidzavukusi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (K.) sprit, sprout. Kidzavukusi hiki, ukikala kure, uki-ki-ona, wamba: ni mutu. Kidzavukusi hikira ki-nga mutu.
**Kidzaya,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small potsherd, or fragment of any broken vessel. Dim. of Luaya. Vidzaya via tuba. Pfuko idzifunsika dzikidziki, ka-i-na vidzaya.
**Kidzaye,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Mera. Kidzaye na rau amanikana varatu va ku fialua. Mutu hiye ni kidzaye; kafiarirue kidzaye, udzayewe wakudza ufiereni, ela wafialua mudzo. Muana hiku ni kidzaye. Ni vidzaye via niono hivi. Said of such beans as remain whole after pounding.
**Kidzedzefule** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kidzefu, 2).
**Kidzedzegula,** *n.*, the art of hopping on one leg. Ku piga kidzedzegula, To hop on one leg.
**Kidzedzo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Dzedzo. Kidzedzo cha ku dzongera mivini ya majembe.
**Kidzefu, 1,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class). *See* Dzefu. Thin, fine. Kivo kino ni kidzefu, ni chambamba.
**Kidzefu, 2** (Kid.), *n.* (in Kir., Dzedzefu), the hiccough.
**Kidzeka,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small round or oval mat.
**Kidzeko,** *n.* (cha), laughter. From Ku dzeka. Gnania yudzihafuna kidzeko e! Atu adzimania ku dzeka hata adziguirira mbafu; atu adzi-va-hafuna kidzeko e!
**Kidzendzendze,** *adv.*, outside. Only used of the roof of a cottage or hut.
**Kidzeo** (Kig.) (= Ugniete in Kir.).
**Kidzera** (Kid.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the beard.
**Kidzere,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a small cob of Indian corn. Dim. of Dzere.
(2) The marmot. Kidzere kitite. Vidzere ndio agubulao minazi.
**Kidzi,** *adj.* *See* Kiidzi.
**Kidzidzi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small creek or cove; (K.) tubercle. Dim. of Ludzidzi. Niama niru. Niama ya kidzidzi.
**Kidzidzoa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small head. Dim. of Kidzoa.
**Kidzifiu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small knife. Dim. of Kifiu.
**Kidzignie,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a chicken. Vidzignie via kuku; but, Makinda ga niuni.
**Kidzihi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a small tree. Dim. of Muhi.
(2) A small stool. Dim. of Kihi.
**Kidziko,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small spoon. Dim. of Kiko and Muiko.
**Kidzimbuiriri,** *adj.* *See* Eruka.
