  Downwards, slopingly, Only used of a hole or burrow. Uina hiu wenda kidzimbuiriri.
**Kidzimo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small image, stature. Dim. of Kimo. Gnania yuna kidzimo kifuhi, ni kidzadzala. Gnania is of short stature; he is a dwarf. Mutu mufuhi; or, Yuna kimo kifuhi.
**Kidzina,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Uina.
**Kidzindi,** *n.* (cha). Ku funga kidzindi.
**Kidzinga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Kinga (or Chinga).
**Kidzinga,** *n.* *See* Erefusa.
**Kidzinsira,** *n.* (cha). Gnania yuna kidzinsira muno.
**Kidziri,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small body. Dim. of Muiri.
**Kidzisui,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small fish. Dim. of Sui.
**Kidzivo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Kivo.
**Kidzivu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kimiro. A small boil. Dim. of Ivu. Kidzivu uzungu, A virulent kind of boil; lit. a boil of bitterness or pain.
**Kidziwe,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small stone; (K.) pebble. Dim. of Iwe. Vidziwe via ndarawe.
**Kidzo,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), good, fine, beautiful.
**Kidzo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small horn, used for blowing. Dim. of Dzo.
**Kidzoa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Wazimu; Maenensi; Raruka. The head. Ni-pa kidzoa cha kambi. Kidzoa cha uira. *See* Ririrua. Atu akifuina uira hangu mutu avofua hata hanga rikauka akifuina akichesa tu, basi akaamba: mutu hiye yuna kidzoa cha uira; atu adzi-mu-ihika muno, akidza uirani. Ku la kidzoa (= Ku la nkuma). *See* Mususi. Magn. Dzidzoa; dim., Kadzidzoa and Kidzidzoa.
**Kidzoe** (Kid.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kigua in Kir.). *See* Mfuha; Goboa. A species of corn allied to the millet. Muhama wa kidzoe.
**Kidzoka,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a hatchet.
**Kidzomba, Kijomba,** *adj.*, the Kinyika for Kisuahili.
**Kidzombo,** *n.*, a small vessel. Dim. of Chombo.
**Kidzongonene,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Dzongonene.
**Kidzonso,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kionso in Kid.). Kidzonso ni niasi zi-zi-zo via, zikazo sungulukua ni moho.
**Kidzonsoka,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small lizard. Dim. of Dzonsoka.
**Kidzopa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a few pieces of wood, collected, somewhat less than a muniahu. Nidzikuenda yeya kuni, nikapata kidzopa, ka-ki-ka-dimira muzigo, I went for firewood; I got a small bundle; I was not able to get a load.
**Kidzuchi,** *n. coll.* (cha), the name of a species of grass, used for thatching; similar to the mudzuchi.
**Kidzudzu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kishungi in Kij.), a tuft. Kidzudzu cha niere, A tuft of hair. Dim., Kadzudzu.
**Kidzuedzue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a sore in its commencement, a small sore. Karonda katite ndo kidzuedzue.
**Kidzufu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Fumba.
**Kidzuga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ndzuga.
**Kidzuho,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a rivulet. Dim. of Muho.
**Kidzukisi, Kidzukizi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kidunusi. From Ku dzukiza.
**Kidzukue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small rope or string. Dim. of Lukue.
**Kidzulo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small frog. Dim. of Chulo.
**Kidzulodzulo,** *n.* and *adv.* (= Luadzulo), evening; toward the close of day. It precedes Dzi-

*Footer: 160*

---

## [PDF Page 174 — Dictionary Page 161 (Kid — Kif)]

  loni, but the words are used promiscuously. Nadza kuako dzua ra kidzulodzulo. Nadza kidzulodzulo; or, Nadza machira ga dziloni, I come in the evening. Yukudza kidzulodzulo, He came in the evening. Yukudza dziloni.
**Kidzulujembe.** *See* Kobe.
**Kidzumba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (K.) a hut, cottage. Dim. of Niumba. Kidzumba cha Mulungu, The house of god; used of a small hut generally built outside a kaya, and to which much superstition is attached.
**Kidzumbakasi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kidumbakasi). Ndo vidzitu hivio.
**Kidzumbi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Yunadzumbi). *See* Dzumbi. Dim. of Dzumbi. Mongowe una kidzumbi; or merely, Yuna kidzumbi. Gnania kakagoloka karakara, yuna kidzumbi, akakoba.
**Kidzunda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Munda.
**Kidzunchi.** *See* Kidzungi.
**Kidzunga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Ludzunga.
**Kidzungi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Niumba; Mbayumbayu. A nest made of straw, etc. Kidzungi chaakua na niasi na vidzihi, A kidzungi is built with grass and little sticks. Kidzungi cha mifu, A nest of wasps.
**Kidzungu, 1,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small heap. Dim. of Dzungu. Kidzungu cha mihi, A small heap of trees. Kidzungu cha viniasi, A small heap of bundles of grass. *See* Kiniasi. N.B.—A heap of grass indiscriminately thrown together on a plantation is not called Kidzungu, but Iyi. Kidzungu cha mawe, A small heap of stones.
**Kidzungu, 2,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) *See* Gungu. A small pot. Dim. of Niungu. Prov., Kidzungu ka-ki-na muziro. Ku zula kidzungu. A kale kidzungu (= vamenga).
(2) *See* Mudzungu; Fua; Kirenge. A small gourd of that kind of which calabashes are made. Dim. of Dzungu.
**Kidzungula,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small hare. Dim. of Dzungula.
**Kidzupo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Aye-ki-gumba, kikibua, akaambua; undalafia dzere kuani, udzidieka kidzupo.
**Kidzuri,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a pole fixed in the middle of a round hut, and projecting a short distance from the top.
(2) A round top, in contradistinction to luanda. Niumba ya kidzuri, A round hut, with or without a pole projecting from the top.
(3) Top of a house in general. Kidzuri cha niumba, The top of a house. Nakuera dzulu kidzurini, I ascend to the top of a house.
**Kidzuvi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kichanga), a bracelet made of wire. Kidzuvi cha mukodo. Kidzuvi cha dzango.
**Kiere,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small udder. Dim. of Ere. Kiereche ni kitite. Niama ya kiere ni kilafiro cha mutu, na niama ya bache.
**Kiere,** *adj.*, pertaining to the udder.
**Kieruve.**
**Kifadzulo.**
**Kifalu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Pera), the guava.
**Kifialo, Kivialo,** *n.* (cha). *See* Fialo. Birth. Si Muravai kivialo, ni mumidzi, hebu ni mutu wa kiviarira, He is not a Rabai-man by birth; he is a settler, or he is a home-born slave. Muana hiye kasikira, ni kivialoche, simania kitako, or, simania akako hala.
**Kifiarira, Kiviarira,** *n.*, the state of being home-born, a slave; born to you. Mutu hiyu ni wa kiviarira, adzayevialua mumo, or, adzeyefialua, etc.;

*Footer: NIKA. | M | 161*

---

## [PDF Page 175 — Dictionary Page 162 (Kif — Kif)]

  *i.e.* alako ni musunie; pl. Si Aravai kivialo ni atu a kiviarira (= atu a kignombe in Kidigo). Kiviarira cha dzala, Pertaining to laying an egg (?).
**Kifiasi, Kiviasi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Ufiasi), nature. Mutu hiyu yuna kiviazi muno. Ni kiviazi che anae kasikira. Kiviazi che, ndo arifioanae kana akili. Kiviazi hikara kidzikala kinionge. Ni kifiazi chakue, It is her nature, by birth. Ni kiviazi che, mtumche hiye-anae kasikira, or, anae ni iafi. A mother says to her boy, Ku amba huamania undakala hivi, ungafugirua ni? Unga-sindikua. *See* Ku hala.
**Kifieramuhala** (Kidigo), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Goromue in Kir.). So kifiera muhala kino? (in Kir., Si, etc.).
**Kifiere,** *adj.* (= Kiuvade). *See* Mafu. Maneno ga kifiere. U-mufiere dze we, usiekula, ukaambira ahoho maneno ga kifiere? U-mufiere wani we? U-mufiere wa renge, usie hendeka kirenge. Dzusi ra kifiere.
**Kififiro,** *n.* *See* Kutusa; Fiahika.
**Kifignio,** *n.* (cha) (= Chamadzo). *See* Lukowe. Yudzi-mu-ambira utu haraka-kifignio cha madzo, or, lukove ku vesa.
**Kifimba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Nche). Gnania yuna kifimba dza nche (= yuna kibimba).
**Kifinikiro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a water-jar kept in the cottage. Dim. of Finikiro. *See* Pfuo. Kifinikiro cha ku ikira madzi.
**Kifiu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a knife. Derived from Ku fiula, To take off. Dim., Kadzifiu; magn., Dzifiu.
**Kifo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kimbirika; Kombala. Death. Mutu hiye kifoche ki-vivi yunahensa ku hamba muno. Atu hio vifoviao viari vimenga, dziku menga.
**Kifolongo,** *n.* *See* Koma.
**Kifoyeo,** or **Kifoyero.** Uki kala na muana mongoni be muana ni kifoyero; *e.g.* People will tell her. Hala vidzunga hivi-mu-hendere muana, arie.
**Kifu, Kivu,** *adj.*, dry. Viense vivu, Dry wisps of cocoa-nut leaves, etc.
**Kifu.**
**Kifua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Kifua cha. Mulungu ndo atu alombavo mfula.
**Kifua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a wooden tray smaller than the chano. Cha ku gandira.
**Kifuaulongo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kifudu** (Kig.), *n.* *See* Dula; Fumba; Pare; Dudumui. Half a cocoa-nut. Ku piga kifudu. Ku piga kifudu cha angura.
**Kifudza,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kivinda. A small quantity of corn in a bag, a bag of corn when nearly emptied. Dim. of Fudza. Ni kifudza chani kino? Resp., Ni cha muhama; or, Ni cha muvunga, What corn is that? Reply, It is a little millet; or, It is a little rice. Muhama wehu abe yehu wa-u-pima akigula reale, vakisala hiki kifudza be ndo huria cho.
**Kifudzu,** *n.* *See* Luvala; Fudzula. Ku fudzulua kifudzu.
**Kifudzulo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), lit. something plucked, *i.e.* food plucked in the field, eaten about noon, and consisting of anything that is just at hand; the regular meal being only prepared in the evening. The word is being superseded by Chunga.
**Kifuede,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), sciurus; (K.) squirrel.
**Kifufu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a piece of wood, reed, or a bit of grass

*Footer: 162*

---

## [PDF Page 176 — Dictionary Page 163 (Kif — Kif)]

  stuck in the ear-laps for enlarging the hole. The holes are made large enough to put a dollar in. Kifufu cha sikironi cha rua, cha niasi.
**Kifufu,** *adj.* (of the marua tree = Kivudzu), narrow. Kitu kino ni kifufu.
**Kifufu,** *adj.* and *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small thicket. Dim. of Fufu. Kifufu kira kinga mutu, kamba wachira na usiku, wamba: ni mutu, yuimire. Si mutu, ni kifufu.
**Kifugo,** *n.* (cha, pl. ). *See* Zumirua. Dim. of Fugo. Muganga wa kifugo, asumiraye.
**Kifuhi,** *adj.*, short.
**Kifuho** (also pronounced **Kifuo,** which seems more correct), *n.*, a side-digging, *i.e.* in digging after madali, one works in the direction of the burrow, and another by the side of it. Ku piga kifuho cha ku dzimba madali.
**Kifui.** Ku muta kifui.
**Kifuidifuidi,** *n.* (= Kibimbinda). *See* Nchamo. Short and low.
**Kifuifui,** *n.* (cha), epilepsy.
**Kifuisa,** *n.* Wari we kauna kifuisa.
**Kifuko,** *n.*, (1) a purse, a small bag. Vifuko via kifumba, kua milomo ku kala mifufu, or, kua dzingo ku kala pfupfu. Kambi anafunsa kifuko.
(2) A small water-jar.
**Kifulawe.** Dim. of Fulawe.
**Kifulo,** *n.* *See* Changodza, 6.
**Kifulofulo, Kivulovulo,** *n.* (pl. Vi-). Muana mbusi yunakoda mazia be yudzilaiwa ni kifulofulo.
**Kifuluda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kifulusi,** *n.* From Ku fuluka. Wari wa kifulusi. Rero udzihenda kifulusi, si wari, Ni wari omu, or, ufu. Wari ni kifulusi hiu; hata uka-u-fuluka na nguo, ka-u-guira nguo. Wari rero nidzi-u-henda ki fulusi, ka vari na madzi.
**Kifumanzi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small bell, worn as an ornament by girls and young women.
**Kifumba.** Vifuko vi-ri-fio na dzingo pudzu, hu-vi-iha vifuko via Kifumba. Pfuko zi-ri-zo na dzingo pfupfu, hu-zi-iha, pfuza kifumba.
**Kifumbulusa arima,** *n.*, the name of a species of lizard; lit. what startles cultivators, because it looks like a snake. It is also called Kiondosa akurima.
**Kifumfu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a round hollow or pit in a rock. Kifumfu cha iweni. Kifumfu ni kira tu, kikacho henda kidengelesa, ela ngurunga ni nialamu, kidza ni nire.
**Kifumi,** *n.* (cha). *See* Fuma. Noise. Dim. of Fumi. Kifumi cha atu angi ku gomba. Kifumi cha ku fumbukisa uira. Kifumi cha peho, cha madzi ga mf'ananiko, cha muamba, The noise of the wind, of the water, of the drum.
**Kifuna.** *See* Diba. Munda hio una kifuna. Niuchi anahola fula, 'enda buma kifuna mavalalani. Vatu hivo vana kifuna vanavua.
**Kifuname,** *n.*, a stand. From Ku funama. Una-ki-ika kifuname. kindamuagika.
**Kifundiro** (Kid.).
**Kifune,** *n.* (= Kifuna).
**Kifunefune,** *adv.*, on the face. Opposed to Kingaringari. Ku lala kifunefune, To lie on the face. Nidzila la kifunefune (= Atu hio adzilala kifunefune, not, vifunefune).
**Kifunga, Kivunga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). From Ku vunga.
**Kifunge,** or **Kifunche,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a sheaf. Kifunge cha muhama, A sheaf of mtama, millet.
**Kifungo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), anything

*Footer: 163*

---

## [PDF Page 177 — Dictionary Page 164 (Kif — Kig)]

  which fastens a button. Used also figuratively. Mumenga yu kifungoni. Airi a vifungoni; but you may as well say, Airi a kifungoni. Kifungo hiki, adzacho fungua, nikibomu. Kambi ari na kifungo sana machira higo.
**Kifungu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small collection of anything, a heap, a bundle. Dim. of Fungu. Kifungu cha atu, A small company or party of men, twenty or thirty. Kifungu cha mawe, A heap of stones. Kifungu cha niasi, A bundle of grass.
**Kifungudzore,** *n.*, the name of a constellation.
**Kifuo,** *n.* (cha). *See* Kiuho.
**Kifure,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small wooden basin. Dim. of Mufure.
**Kifuri, Kivuri,** *n.* (pl. Vi-?) (= Kifuri; Kifuri), a shadow.
**Kifurifuri,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kore. A shadow.
**Kifurungamadzi,** *n.* (= Kibanansi).
**Kifurungui,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a kind of basket or bag, with a wide bottom and narrow mouth, made by boys to conceal their little articles of food when they are out of doors. Arisa anadzukula chunga kifurunguini, The shepherd-boy carries his food in his basket.
**Kifurusaarima** (Kid.), *n.* (= Burusi in Kins.).
**Kifusi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Lufusi. Dim. of Lufusi.
**Kiga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Poja. The thigh, lap.
**Kigahe,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a kind of lizard. Dim. of Gahi.
**Kigalugalu,** *n.*, one who is changeable, fickle. From Ku galuka.
**Kigamba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small handful. Dim. of Gamba.
**Kiganda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), rind, skin. Dim. of Ganda.
**Kigande,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small lump of anything. Dim. of Gande. Kigande cha unga, A little lump of flour (when wet). Kigande cha kishombo.
**Kigandegande,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the penis. Kigandegande cha mulume (Kid.) (= Kibogo cha mulume, Kir.).
**Kiganga,** *adj.*, magical; relating to Uganga. Uira wa kiganga, A magic dance; or, A dance instituted by an mganga for a sick person supposed to be possessed by an evil spirit. Uira wa kiganga (= Uira wa aganga), wa ku dzangira muezi. Aganga anadzangira muezi, kuamba atu akarie viliwa via aganga.
**Kigango,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kigansi.** *See* Joho.
**Kigao,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Vigao via minazi vi-nga vichira via loma.
**Kigayu** (Kid.), *n.*, dryness. Dzi hi ina kigayu (= Nti hi ni yabisi in Kij.), This land is dry, hard.
**Kigedi** (Kik.), *adj.*, blue. Said of beads, and used of nothing else. Ushanga wa kigedi, Blue beads. In former times, when the Wanyika were ignorant of Kikamba, they were merely called Ushanga uiru.
**Kigema,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a boy who takes toddy from the palm tree. Dim. of Mgema.
**Kigere,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the wrist.
**Kigero** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kibiga in Kir.). *See* Fugo.
**Kigiri,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kichiri in Kins.; Kikiri(?), Chira(?); Ahade kuchira).
**Kigirikigiri.** Yukala kigirikigiri, kamanire (= Kagarakagara in Kij.), He knew not what to do.
**Kignia,** *v.a.* (= Ku dignia).
**Kigniafungo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the musk of the civet-cat. Adzomba ni ku buma kashani, ku nudzia nguo, i nuke to.
**Kigniando,** (1) *adv.*, in the side. Only used with words mean-

*Footer: 164*

---

## [PDF Page 178 — Dictionary Page 165 (Kig — Kig)]

  ing to shoot, to pierce, etc. Yudzifumagua kigniando, kandadia.
  (2) (= Kidzniando).
**Kignielesa.** Kuku hiyu yunaenenda kignielesa.
**Kignieresa,** *adj.*, long-faced. Mfula inagnia kignieresa. Mutu hiyu yunagomba kignieresa. Maneno ga kignieresa, Slow talk, as it were by drops (= maneno ga rero).
**Kignietesa.** Mvula i kignietesa (Kid.) (= Mfua i kisoea, Kij). Mvula inadzuisa dzi kidzniesi.
**Kigniesi,** *n.* (cha), awe, as peculiar to a place not inhabited. In Kid., a species of grasshopper (= Niense in Kij. and Kir.). Vanaguiza kigniesi (= Bananiama kimia in Kij., and Banazizira in Kins.). Kigniesi ni kura tu ku dzoa atu. Dzi ikikala hecheye, inaguiza kigneisi. Kaya mudzilaiwa, kamuna mutu korokoro, munaguisa kigniesi, nami nahenda kibanda mundani, nidzame.
**Kignio,** *n.* (= Chignio). *See* Nche.
**Kignioto,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Ku piga). Ku piga kignioto (= Ku fumbama). Atu hia adzipiga vignioto.
**Kigniugnuniu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the point of the elbow.
**Kigniundo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Cha musi), a charm made of roots.
**Kignogno,** *adj.*, only used with Ku gomba. Ku gomba kignogno, To speak through the nose.
**Kignognomfiro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small worm living in water.
**Kignognoro** (Kid.) (= Kignogno in Kir.). Kugomba kignognoro (= Ku nenea puani in Kij.), To speak through the nose.
**Kignombe** (Kid.), *adj.* (= Kifiarira in Kir.). *See* Kifiarira. Only used with Mutu or Atu; lit. of cattle, of the nature of cattle. *See* Gnombe. Mutu wa kignombe, A home-born slave. Si atu a kignombe fio? Are they not home-born slaves?
**Kigocho,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Mamu; Raso. From Ku goja. Nisegere kigojo tu, sidura ku enenda, kua urinsi nikiene nda n'amba: niama andakudza-adze, arie. Nisegere vava kigocho sidura ku enenda kuangu, kua yuya mukongo kufua kafua na ka vola-kavola, basi nisegere vava kigojo tu. Machira higo. Saidi avo pigana na atu a Kisiwani, ndivo Anika avoihua kuenda sagala kigocho; akahewa bosho ra nafaka, akiambua: ni chakuria chenu hiki.
**Kigoda** (Kid.), *n.* (in Kir., Kigota).
**Kigodi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Lugodi.
**Kigodi,** *n.* (= Munazi mkomu).
**Kigodo** (Kid.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kivongolo in Kir.), a bracelet.
**Kigodze,** *n.* (cha), something wound or tied around from top to bottom. Ku dzi funga kigodze kua mashaka, To wind one's cloth round the loins instead of carrying it in the usual way over the shoulders, which is done in distress. Kigodze cha tumbaku, A bundle of tobacco all wound round with milala—cord of plaited palm leaves.
**Kigofi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kilafiro; Kilaviro? Kigofi cha ugnaro.
**Kigofia,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small stick with a hook. Dim. of Lugofia.
**Kigogo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small piece of wood used as a seat. Kigogo cha ku uthira. Dim. of Gogo.
**Kigogodera** (Kid.), *n.*

*Footer: 165*

---

## [PDF Page 179 — Dictionary Page 166 (Kig — Kig)]

  Madzere higa ni vigogodera (= magumu in Kij.).
**Kigogorido** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kigniugnuniu in Kir.), the elbow.
**Kigogoto,** or **Kikokoto,** *n.*
**Kigolo** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kisinde in Kir.).
**Kigolosi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small round mat, placed under the millstone when grinding corn.
**Kigoloziro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Ku piga in Kig.).
**Kigoma,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Goma. Kigoma cha pala, cha sa, etc.
**Kigomba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Sagira. The stalk of the banana, when dried and reduced to powder, to mix with snuff. Mugoti wa isu ukianikua ukiochua ku sagirua tumbaku, basi ni ku ihua kigomba hebu muisu.
**Kigombe,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small cow. Dim. of Gnombe. Yuna vigombe tu, hata kumi ka-zi-dimira. Kigombe hiki ka-ki-kula.
**Kigome,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kibamfu), (1) splint, splinter, chip (of wood only).
(2) A small fort. Dim. of Ngome. Kigome cha Makuba.
**Kigongo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small stick; any little slip of wood.
**Kigongogo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Magongogo. Munda hio ka-u-rimika, ukazikua viombo, or, vigongogo. Mafo ndigo vigongogo.
**Kigongolo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Gongolo.
**Kigongoma,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Dononoka; Gungugu. The name of an insect (a little worm); it destroys Indian corn. Madzere gano gadzifunsua ni kigongoma. Dzere hiri rikariwa ni kigongoma.
**Kigonkue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kikonkue. This word has been superseded by the Kikamba word Kivedi.
**Kigonsi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small sheep. Dim. of Gnonsi.
**Kigopue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Dzimbuka. Dim. of Gopue. M'egnie kigopue cha milomo, hata uka-mu-ona yu mudzodze, ela ukidza lola hiratu tundu ya mulomo, basi ni ku ona yudzibanangika.
**Kigota,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) the stick by which a trap is fastened. Kigota cha muhambo.
(2) A knock with the knuckles. Yudzi-ni-piga kigota; or, Yudzi-ni-gota kigota.
(3) The bent sprout of a bean, when springing up. Kunde sidzidungia, sidziupusa vigota.
**Kigoti,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Mugoti.
**Kigova,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Chusa. A small piece of bark or rind. Dim. of Gova.
**Kigua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kidzoe in Kid.). *See* Mfuha; Goboa; Muhama. A kind of Guinea-corn, now very rare. Muhama hiu ni kigua. Muhama wa kigua ni hura tu, urio na mua muguawe una madzi dza mua wa manga. Muhama hiu una vigua. Kigua cha mfuha suchere ni dune dza wimbi.
**Kigube,** *n.* (= Kabeni in Kns.), a cob of Indian corn when beginning to form.
**Kiguchu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small leather bag. Kiguchu cha arisa.
**Kigugumisa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), stammering. Mutu hiye yuna kigugumisa; lit. That man is with stammering; That man stammers. Atu hio ana kigugumisa, These men stammer. Yunagomba kigugumisa, He speaks with stammering.
**Kigugusi, Kikukusi,** *n.* (cha). *See* Gugusa. The whirlwind.
**Kiguguta,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Girida. A husk of a cob of Indian corn when the grain

*Footer: 166*

---

## [PDF Page 180 — Dictionary Page 167 (Kig — Kih)]

  is plucked out. Madzere gadzivukusua, gadzila vigugutani.
**Kiguiriguiri,** *n.* and *adj.* (hiyu, pl. hivi), a strong-built man of the middle size. Kidzana kisiho kiguiriguiri, A bouncing child.
**Kigulu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Magulu), the leg, foot. Kigulu changu ka ki kolosera, naenenda. Nidzikuenda na kigulu ki; hata n'enda egnie kavo; be nidzisinda na ndzala hata nidziuya na ndzala zangu. Nidzikuala kigulu ki, nauya. Nidzikuala kigulu kidzo nienenderacho, basi akafururisa.
**Kigulue,** *adj.* *See* Isu.
**Kigumba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Divira; Wakamba; Midzare; Hutu. Mutu akikumia kigumba, basiyu-ki-iha gumba, akikumia muno, ni rigumba. Ni maneno ga ndumo, ga ku gnieta. Dim., Kagumba; magn., Gumba and Rigumba.
**Kigunda,** *n.* Dim. of Gunda.
**Kigundu,** *n.* (K.) Njoma.
**Kigungu,** *adj.* (= Charo). *See* Ndaro. Mutu huya akafua madzo, kaona ni kigungu. Mutu huya-unga-mu-ona, ni mudzofi wa madzo, kaona, yu kigungu. Lola! nafignia madzo n'enende kigungu, hata nifike hivara, A child in play. Nidziingira niumba, muna kiza, kamuoneka, ni kigungu. Halani moho, mukabuse niumbani, mukigungu; mubuse moho, mugnale. Rero hundalala kigungu, kavana kuni za ku asira moho.
**Kigunse,** *n.*
**Kiguo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small cloth. Dim. of Nguo.
**Kigurudumu,** *n.* Dim. of Gurudumu.
**Kiguruguru.** Nasi hi ni kiguruguru, ka-i-na madzi, ikahenda dzoye, inahama kuria na mugosija hebu ku gogoda, ela ka-i-hama mbeyu wala hui.
**Kiguso, Kiguzo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kingamia. Dim. of Nguzo.
**Kigutu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Doka. A small stump, not of trees, but of a broken instrument or a mutilated member of the body. Dim. of Gutu. Chala cha kigutu. Kifiu cha kigutu. Jembe ra kigutu. Mutu hiye akachoka chala yuna kigutu.
**Kihako,** *n.* Dim. of Hako. Yudzila kihako; or, Yudziduruka kihako (= Mfindo in Kid.).
**Kihanga,** *n.* *See* Kahangu.
**Kihari,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Roda). *See* Mulamba. Muhi una vihari via ku bula. Muhi hiu una viharivie u burira-vo; udzifika viharivie via ku busa makodza. Namania vihari via mfula. Aka mania vihari via muaka.
**Kiharusi,** *n.* (cha). *See* Nundu. The crick, a painful stiffness in the neck. Mutu hiye yuna kiharusi, or, yunaguirua ni ukongo wa kiharusi, muiriwe ukakala kibimbinda.
**Kihaso,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small quantity of medicine. Especially a small piece of the root of a tree, used as medicine, or bound up with a kiniundo. Dim. of Muhaso.
**Kihehemesa** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kidedemesa in Kir.).
**Kihendo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), lit. a deed, a custom, but only used of the established feasts, which so much distinguish the Wanyika from other nations and tribes around them, and which unite them more closely and stronger than anything else. Kihendo cha muansa. Kihendo cha Mfaya. Kihendo cha Kambi. Kihendo cha Govu.
**Kihengo,** *n.* *See* Kimo. Gnania yuna kimo cha ki-

*Footer: 167*

---

## [PDF Page 181 — Dictionary Page 168 (Kih — Kij)]

  hengo, wala si mure, wala si mufuhi.
**Kihensi, Kihenzi,** *n.*, an apprentice, a small worker. Dim. of Muhensi. Kihensi cha kasi, A doer of work,—said of a little boy.
**Kihenso,** *n.* (cha). *See* Henso. The one beloved. Rarely used. From Ku hensa. Muche, a-mu-hensaye, ni gnania musiku, ndiye kihenso che, hata akidzola kaniama, yu-mu-fidzira iye. Gnania ni musenangu hunahensania nayi yuna-ni-hensa wala ka-ni-fidza neno ri-ri-ro muakue ndani; mutu hiye ni kihenso-changu-hunahensania. Muana akaye-mu-ingisa moyoni, ni muana musiku ndiye kihenso che tua-mu-hensaye. Kibomache ndiye a-mu-hensaye ndiye kihenso che tu, ela suino kahuhensua-be hu ache nasui? nasui hu mifusi, say the wives of one husband with regard to their kiboma.
**Kihi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vihi), a very small stool, cut out of one piece of wood; any kind of stool, a chair—a chair as seen with the Mohammedans on the coast. But when a distinction is required, they will call the Mohammedan stool Kihi cha mkakasi, and the European chair Kihi cha ensi. Nalonda, kihi changu, rihisi yangu.
**Kihofu,** *n.*, fear. Yudzihenda ivu ra kihofuni.
**Kihoho,** *adj.* *See* Kagumba. Childlike, childish. Maneno ga kihoho ka-ga-na urungo (= ka-ga-hama).
**Kiholo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Pingi. The name of a species of rat.
**Kihombo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), of girls, of men (?). Dim. of Hombo.
**Kihude,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kidude).
**Kihuhufu,** or **Kihufuhufu** (?), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Ana aka kihuhufu; or, Kihuhuhufu dza adzomba.
**Kihui,** *n.* Kihui hicho kinaimba; yuna linkua ningi, or, malinkua mangi. Kihui ni muganga wa niuni. Wakenga Mudzomba, akimuaga muhamawe, akiamba ni mutu yunadza a-mu-huike musigo. Kumba ni niuni.
**Kihumbo,** *n.*, (1) not small, but a piece of it. Rel. to Uhumbo. Kihumbo uzungu.
(2) Oneness as to father and mother. Atu hia ni kihumbo adzila ndani menga. Ni ndugu yangu kihumbo tu.
**Kihunde,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kidude; Kihude), any little thing or instrument. Dim. of Luhunde.
**Kii** (contracted into Ki), *adj.*, bad.
**Kiifu, Kiivu** (generally contracted into Kifu), *adj.* (rel. to the ki class). *See* Uikane. Ripe, cooking, done. From Ku ifua.
**Kiikane,** *n.* (cha), agreement, for waiting for each other at a given place. Ndo kiikane chao a-cho-ikana. Kiikane ni kiikane; kandaenenda kuani, kakaikana fio?
**Kiike,** *n.* (cha). Prov., Kiike ni kiike, kimaniua ni m'egnie akayeika.
**Kiivi** (Kidigo), *adj.* (= Kifuhi in Kir.), short.
**Kiizi, Kiidzi,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), unripe, raw, fresh.
**Kijakasi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small slave-girl. Dim. of Jakazi.
**Kijego,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a tooth.
(2) A child who has not cut all his teeth. Muana hiyu ni kijego, kuona yudzimera meno ga dzulu; hebu akamera majego mbere, This child is a kijego; he has not cut his upper teeth, but he has two teeth.
**Kijogolo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a cockerel. Dim. of Jogolo.
**Kijomba,** *adj.* (= Kidzomba), Kisuahili.

*Footer: 168*

---

## [PDF Page 182 — Dictionary Page 169 (Kij — Kik)]

**Kijorojoro** (Kid.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Ku rima vijorojoro.
**Kika,** *n.* *See* Kuluka. A log of wood. Kisibidi changu kikasira ku hundua.
**Kika,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Muche?). Vika via ku vekedzera moho.
**Kika,** *v.a.* *See* Jika.
  **Kikisa,** *v.a.* *See* Jikisa.
**Ki-ka-cho,** *pron.* (pl. Vi-ka-fio-). *See* Kibamfu. That which is or has, implying the past tense.
**Kikafiri,** *adj.* and *adv.* *See* Gudiugudiu.
**Kikaha,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), lazy. Kidzana hiki ni kikaha, This youth is lazy.
**Kikaha,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Kaha. Kihaha cha ku noera madzi noerera?
**Kikahana,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small basket.
**Kikahe,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small loaf or cake of anything. Dim. of Mukahe. Mimi ndimi gnania, muana wa gnania; nidziambua, nidzihala kitu cha gnania; be na nikale nikahala keri, kikahe ni guira! na k'amba sikahala, ni ku henda singua, basi kikahe-enda shamba. Ku mu longosa kua? Kikahe. Ku mi longosa dzokani. Ku mi longosa tondzoni.
**Kikakaya,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a shell, the fragment of a shell. Only used of what is fragile; of fish it is Kombe. Kikakaya cha ichi, The shell of an egg, whether whole or only a fragment. Ni ichi rino hebu ni kikakaya? Kikakaya cha niono, The shell of a castor-oil berry. Kikakaya cha kobe, A fragment of the shell of a tortoise, the shell itself being called Lungo. Dim., Kakakaya.
**Kikalango,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a frying-pan. Ario na vikalango ni Adzomba na Adigo, kua ku kala na sui, ku chita na mugasija.
**Kikamba,** *adj.* *See* Mafu. Relating to Ukamba.
**Kikansa** (Kij. and Kir.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a trophy.
**Kikansi,** *n.* *See* Hukuha. Regard, pity, sympathy. Ai! yukuenda koniola madzere mabomu, kana kikansi; ela muana kana dambi yuno?
**Kikansu** (Kij.), *n.*, a small shirt or garment. Dim. of Kansu. The kansu is the outer garment worn by the Wasuahili and Arabs.
**Kikavu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small basket. Dim. of Kavu.
**Kikaya,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kigai.
**Kiki,** *adv.* *See* Kutuka; Pima. If it.
**Kikia,** *n.* (no pl.). Ku guira kikia. Yudzipigua ni mfula, yunadedema, yuna peho, yudziguira kikia, be yunaenenda kuao ku oha moho. Nidziona shoho airi, aka-dzi-guira kikia. Yuna utia, yudzi-dzi-guira kikia. Udzi-dzi-guira kikia, u-na-ni we? Resp., Ah, sina hata utu. The first says again, Una utu, ku na utu unga-dzi-guira kikia? Chaneye a-mu-usa muana wa nduguye; or, Una-ni we uki-dzi-guira kikia? una asa kuenu nika-ku-virike. Ku dzi dzuira kikia.
**Kikingiri, Kikuingiri,** and **Kigingiri,** *n.*, the name of a species of thorn.
**Kikiri,** *n.* (= Kigiri). *See* Mfaka.
**Kikirikikiri,** or **Gigirigigiri** (= Kekerekekere), noise, confused talk. Neno gao ni kikirikikiri, gana ni-gigiriaka ku nena.
**Kikisa,** *v.a.* *See* Kika.
**Kiko.** It is there.
**Kiko** (contracted from Kiiko), *n.* (cha, pl. Viko), that on or in which something is put. From Ku ika. (1) Kiko cha ku rira wari, A vessel in which to eat wari, cooked grain, rice, etc., generally the pot in which it was cooked.

*Footer: 169*

---

## [PDF Page 183 — Dictionary Page 170 (Kik — Kik)]

  (2) Kiko cha ku nudzira tumbaku, Any vessel in which snuff is kept, especially horns of sheep or goats. Viko viko.
  (3) Kiko cha Akiriama na Agala. The word seldom occurs without the particle Ni, in, being suffixed to it: Kikoni, and is then treated like a proper name.
**Kikoa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small thong. Dim. of Mukoa.
**Kikoba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Koba.
**Kikobe,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small tortoise. Dim. of Kobe.
**Kikobue.** Milomo ya kikobue ya ku kobokera?
**Kigobuekobue,** *n.* (pl. Vi-). *See* Mufumbulo; Kidosi.
**Kikocho.** *See* Kika; Cho. Relating to a Ki word, and the Ko implying the past tense. That which.
**Kikofia** (Kij.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kobiekera?), a small cap. Vadzikobuekera, vadzikala kikofia. Nidzi ri kamula hata ridzikala kikofia.
**Kikohokoho,** *n.* (= Kikuadulo), the whooping-cough. Yuna laga ra kikohokoho.
**Kikojo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a bladder. Kikoja cha gnombe, The bladder of an ox.
**Kikoko,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Dokola; Kironda; Firandzi. A scab. Dim. of Ukoko. Kironda kinavola, hangu dzana kidzihenda kikoko.
**Kikokoro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a fragment of the shell of a crab. Vikokoro via magando; vikovia lungo, etc.
**Kikokoto,** *n.* Yudzihala vigongo, yuenda pigira kikokoto; akagomba na kanoa kabomu: madzua mairi hebu mahahu uudze kitu hicho, ukisa udza, dziku ya-ne ndapiga kiravo, unda-ro-ri-ona ni rako m'egnie; us'ambe: sika-ku-ambira; or, Jembe rangu-uwe ukayehala be ri-udze, ukisa-ri-udza, ndakuenda abisa.
**Kikola,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small snail. Dim. of Kola.
**Kikola,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Heteresa. A party of men called together for expediting some work in behalf of one of them, as cultivating a piece of ground or building a hut. From Ku kola. Atu adzihenda vikola, ela kikola kibomu ki kua gnania.
**Kikolio,** *n.*
**Kikolo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). (1) *See* Sala. Kikolo hiki cha kuku ni kidaifu.
(2) (Kid.) (= Kisinde in Kir.), the vanda when finished by tapping.
**Kikolosa, Kikolosi, Kikohosi.** From Ku kolola.
**Kikombe,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a small shell. Dim. of Lukombe.
(2) A cup, a small basin. Kikombe cha ngulu. Kikombe cha mufui, One of the three rows of feathers of an arrow. Kikombe cha muhama, The eyes in cassava. *See* Kisengere. Muhama hiu una vikombe vingi.
**Kikomo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the forehead.
**Kikomolo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Komolo.
**Kikomu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), fully ripe, mature. From Ku komala or Ku koma.
**Kikonde,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Govi; Loama; Fioga; Gopola. The skin. Nidzihumbula kikonde, I have rent open the skin by knocking one's self, etc. Nidzi-dzi-chegnia kikonde, I have slightly cut the skin. Udzikidzi una kikonde kibomu, The udzikidzi has a thick fibrous skin. Muratu chingoni nipa kikonde, nioche. Nidzifumaga kikonde kivuvu, nidzihuga-mufui ka-u-kaingi-

*Footer: 170*

---

## [PDF Page 184 — Dictionary Page 171 (Kik — Kil)]

  ra ndani. Nguo hi ina kikonde (= ina lusi lusiho).
**Kikongo,** *n.*, sickness. Dim. of Ukongo. Gnania musiku wagandamisua ni kikongo cha dzua menga.
**Kikongo,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), sick, ill, bad.
**Kikongolo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a cocoa-nut tree when very high and slender, with the additional meaning of old. Dim. of Kongolo. Kikongolo ni cha kare hiki. Minazi hio ina vikongolo.
**Kikonkue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Dzagala.
**Kikoro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Koro, *q.v.* Kikoro cha matama.
**Kikorokoro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the staves of a cask in a bundle.
**Kikosi, Kikozi,** *n.* *See* Kosi; Chamba. Atu adziuka kikozi, adzikuenda thiana, adzikuenda ulaga atu. Na-huukeni kikozi, huende huka-a-fungire, hu-a-ulage.
**Kikuaba,** *n.* (Sumah in Arabic). *See* Kikuava. The smell of perspiration from the armpits. Yunanuka kikuaba.
**Kikuachile,** or **Kikuakile,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kikuada.**
**Kikuadulo** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Kikohokoho in Kir. proper). *See* Zimiamoyo. The whooping-cough. Ni ukongo wa ku kolola hata ukaahama. Yuguirua ni kikuadulo; or, Yuna laga ra kikuadulo.
**Kikuagulo,** *n.* (cha), the name of one of the miansa. Kikuagulo hicho kinarira. Atu anafuna kikuagulo.
**Kikuakuarushe.**
**Kikuala,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Lukuiri. (1) Weasel.
(2) The name of a species of bird with red feathers.
**Kikuankuara,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= in Kid., Kikuakuara).
**Ki-kuao.**
**Kikuaria,** *n.*, a kind of dance. Uira wa kikuaria upiguao na mifungu, A dance accompanied by stamping on the ground with bamboo canes.
**Kikuava,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), an armpit, a wing. Dim. of Kuava. Kikuava cha muhoho, The armpit of a child. Kikuava cha niuni mutite, The wing of a small bird.
**Kikuchi** (Kidigo), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kidzeka in Kir.), a small mat of a round or oval shape.
**Kikudu, Kikuchu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Mukoba. A bag made of leather.
**Kikuehu,** *adj.*, pertaining to ourselves, ours, our home.
**Kikuenu,** *adj.*, pertaining to yourselves, yours, your home.
**Kikuesa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a climber. Kikuesa cha ku kuerera minasini.
**Kikui.** Gnombe sa kikui.
**Kikuidia,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Lukuidia.
**Kikuko,** *n.* Kikuku ni kikuku.
**Kikulankove.**
**Kikuku** (Kij.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a bracelet, a small fowl.
**Kikulu,** *adj.* (= Kibomu), great, large. Kikulu ni ku ona me'gnie na madzo. *See* Angue.
**Kikumba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small fresh-water fish. Dim. of Kumba.
**Kikumbi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small bough of a palm tree. Dim. of Kumbi. Kikumbi cha munazi.
**Kikunse,** *n.*
**Kikunso,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small fold. Dim. of Mukunso.
**Kikuro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small dog. Dim. of Kuro.
**Kikuyu.**
**Kilagane,** *n.* (cha). *See* Ulagane. An agreement between two only. Prov., Kilagane ni kilagane, Dzimba kamala mbala, usiriche kudza, ku

*Footer: 171*

---

## [PDF Page 185 — Dictionary Page 172 (Kil — Kil)]

  galukua ni moyo mungine, The lion is said never to devour a whole mbala, but always to leave part of it.
**Kilagano,** *n.* *See* Malagano. A promise with respect to a small affair.
**Kilalo,** *n.* (= Ngono in Kij.). Bed-fellowship of a concubine in her turn. Nakuenda kua musenangu, nikihenda dziku mbiri, nikikala vilalo viiri, be nikiuya, I went to my friend, and spent two days and slept two nights, when I returned.
**Kilambam'iko,** *n.* (cha) (= Cha umiro), the uvula.
**Kilamo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), bee-stings.
**Kilamusakanoa,** *n.*, lit. the awaking or greeting of the mouth, breakfast.
**Kilangadzulo,** *n.* Kudzikala kilanga dzulo.
**Kilariro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Mukono. Lit. that to sleep with, *i.e.* the evening meal, which with the Wanyika is the principal meal of the day. *See* Kodzola. Ndzoni hurie kilariro.
**Kilasa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a ball made of grass by children, to play with. Ahoho ana-ki-dzuvirana. Ndzoni huka dzuve kilasa, Come, let us throw the ball. Nidzi-ku-funga umusunie wangu; or, Nidzi-ku-ika usunie.
**Kilaviro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kiere. (1) An extra portion of meat, in contradistinction to the Niama ya mudaro. Bora ana vilaviro viao, na bora soroko ana vilaviro viao.
(2) The skin of a goat, when taken by the mfaya from the kambi for the purpose of the ugnaro.
**Kileda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kafara in Kij.), a charm. Ku sindika vileda.
**Kilekile,** *n.* (ya). *See* Chulua. Kilekile hio-inarira.
**Kilele,** *n.*, noise.
**Kilemba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Mfongi. A small comb, a turban, summit, top. Dim. of Lemba. Kilemba cha kichogolo, The little comb of a young cock. Kilemba cha murima, The summit of a mountain. Kilemba cha muhi, The top of a tree (= kirere).
**Kilembo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Kilembo cha nazi.
**Kileo,** *n.* (= Urefi), the useless talk of one drunken.
**Kilido,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kiligo,** *n.* Aliguaye ndeye muegnie kiligo, ela aligaye ni muegnie maligo.
**Kilimo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kihari). *See* Mulamba; Lugare; Kara.
**Kilinga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Ngungu; Jia. A bracelet of iron, a ring, of colour, round the neck of animals; lit. that which goes round anything. Dim. of Mulinga. From Ku linga. Gnombe hi ina kilinga cha dzingo.
**Kilinge,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a charm, a spell, a sleight. From Ku linga. Ku-mu-piga mutu kilinge. Ku-dza-oniewa kilinge; kudzankue ku kala muganga. *See* Mulindi. Fanirua kilinge ni fitina.
**Kilingilo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Uhumbo wangu nidzi-u-lingila kigongoni ku ocha: be ni kilingilo changu, ni dza cho lingir ra uhumbo.
**Kilingo** (Kid.).
**Kilishankue** (Kichogni), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Dzange in Kir.).
**Kiliwa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kigonga. Via kiravo karamu.
**Kilo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a fish-hook.
**Kilolo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a looking-glass.
**Kilolua,** *n.* Gnania kana kilolua kidzo, akilolua ni ku uka. Muanangu ka-dza-pata kilolua, yu-

*Footer: 172*

## [PDF Page 186 — Dictionary Page 173 (Kil — Kim)]

  chari sirima. Of one who has never been asked in marriage, they merely say, Kana pamfu. But when at last she becomes settled, the word is no more used, but they say, Muanangu hangu dzana yudzipata mulume, yuhurire, ka uka ka viri, not, yudzipata kilolua.
**Kilomba,** *n.* (cha), animal fat when boiled, tallow.
**Kilome,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) the name of a species of bird, which during the hot season migrates. Ukiona vilomi vidzikudza, be muaka u vevi.
(2) The name of a kind of shrub, which, by its budding some time before the rain, indicates the approach of spring. Nidziona kilome, kidzimera, basi muaka u vevi.
**Kilondo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), subject-matter for a song.
**Kilonga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), bent, disposition, temper. Yudzihala kilonga cha kuche hebu cha ku lume. Yudzihala kilonga cha babaye mufiere, wari muzinzi.
**Kilongo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small row. Dim. of Lulongo.
**Kilongo.** *See* Ngama. From a root, Ku longa, or, ronga, which occurs in Kins., but not in Kir. nor Kij. Vatu hiva nidzimbavo ni vomu, vana kilongo, or, kalongo. Mudzanga wa Usambala ni kilongo kivuvu, na niunguye ka-i-funsika hiraka. Dzi ikikala ka-i-na kilongo, be ka-i-komia ku guirua ni dzua. Kinemiche kinakala muno, ka-ki-fuhuka haraka. Ka vilungoni muakue.
**Kilongola,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kirongora in Kins.), a leader, guide. Kilongola cha charo chehu niani? Gnania ndiye kilongola, ayelongola atu hata akifika hivo a-vo-kuenda.
**Kilosiro,** *n.*
**Kiluafuluafu,** *adv.*, sideways. Ku lala kiluafuluafu, To sleep on one's side. Ku bua kiluafuluafu, To fall sideways.
**Kiluavi.** Ni maneno ga kilua-vi?
**Kilube,** *n.* Mbawa hiu ni kilube.
**Kilulongo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small series or row; (K.) range, rank-and-file. Dim. of Lulongo. Kilulongo cha atu, cha gnombe, cha mihi, etc. Ku hunga niama kilulongo, To pass the blade of a mulala through pieces of meat, so as to make a row of them.
**Kilumakuiri,** *n.*, the name of a species of snake.
**Kilume,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), a male. Kidzana kilume, A boy.
**Kilunda,** *n.* Ni muhambo wa mfu.
**Kilungakuku,** *n.* (cha).
**Kilungo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Umia; Dieka; Amula. (1) A joint.
(2) Seasoning. Its fundamental meaning is that which joins or unites into one. Kilungo ni kula vatu va-ka-vo lunganiua. Muana Damu yuna vilungo vingi.
**Kilungu** (Kikamba), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (in proper Kiravai, Kifungu, which, like many other words, is being superseded by the Kikamba), a part, party. Kilungu kimenga kidzikudza, One party of a caravan arrived. Gnania yuna kilungu kidzo cha gnombe, Gnania has a nice little herd of cattle. Gnania naye hangu dzana yudzipata kilungu kidzo cha gnombe—from twenty to thirty—fungu ridze ra gnombe.
**Kima** (Kij.), *n.* (cha). *See* Baha; Fuhira. Value, price, amount. Hu-ambire kimache, i-fua dze?
**Kima,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, hia), a species of monkey.
**Kimagnii** (Kig.), *n.*
**Kimako,** *n.* (cha), a wonder. Ndzoni humake kimako; or,

  Ndzoni hulole kimako; lit. Come, and let us wonder at a wonder.
**Kimakoro,** *adv.*, angrily. Ku fungua kimakoro.
**Kimanga** (Kig.), *n.*, food made of a mixture of dzenga za madzere and kunde or podzo (= Kishombo and Mushubu in Kir.).
**Kimangari,** *adj.*, two-edged. Kifiu cha Kikamba ni kimangari (= kina maso kosikosi).
**Kimathaka,** *adj.*, belonging to or being of the nature of a Mumathaka. Maneno ga kimathaka, The language of the Amathaka.
**Kimaumba,** *n.*
**Kimba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vimba), (1) a corpse, but only of one who was slain; when dying naturally, it is Lufu.
(2) A carcase. *See* Gombo. Nidzi-m-fumaga niama kakabua hudzi-m-dua hata hukakuenda mu-ona kimbache, basi huka-m-dzinsa.
**Kimbere.** Adzilalama kimbere cha madzo.
**Kimbimbi,** *n.* (cha), (1) the name of a species of plant. Kimbimbi cha niazi.
(2) A goose-skin, the leaves of the plant, when first appearing, being marked in a similar way. Muiri una-mu-fumuka kimbimbi.
**Kimbira,** *v.n.*, to flee, to escape; to flee from. Atu hara anakimbira; kahumania akimbiriracho; kahi anakimbira pera, kahi anakimbira amaitha, kahumania.
  **Kimbirika,** *v.n.* Kula uenda-vo kifo ki-vavo; kula mudzi uenendao una mbira; be kufua ka-ku-kimbirika; kuani-ungaenenda, kifo kina-ku-duadua, hata Mulungu akihensa, basi kifo kika-ku-hala.
  **Kimbirira.** *See* Timbiriro. Mutu ni ku kimbira a ndi vo erekeratu, kana vatu a si vo kimbirira. Muakimbirira-vi? Suino kahukimbirire kuenda kaya, ela huakimbirira dzaka bomu. Be mino sina gnombe, si-ni, nikimbirirani na usiku? or, ni-kimbirire-ni. Ni muiri wangu muvuvu; andivokudza, andadua gnombe, be mino ndavegnia dzakani bosi.
  **Kimbisa, Kimbiza,** *v.a.* *See* Tumbulio. To make flee. Usiku hura tu; or ura tu; or merely, hura Amasai a-vokudza nari mundani nirere, basi vakidza asena aki-ni-ambira kuamba Amasai arere vevi, basi nikapika malo nik'enda-a-kimbiza muchangu na anangu.
  **Kimbisana, Kimbizana,** *v. reit.* Atu angine amania, akikimbizana, ela suino kahumanire hata chiramuko hunalola, amaitha hia, adzi-hu-ingirira. Der., Kimbidzua; Timbiriro.
  **Kimbisika, Kimbizika,** *v.n.* Gnania kakimbizika; nidzi-mu-amba: kimbira! ela yudzi-ni-tharau.
  **Kimbisira, Kimbizira,** *v.d.* Gnania yudzi-ni-kimbizira atu angu; yudzi-ni-difira atu angu kamare, yudzihenda to. Mulungu na iye ndiye adzie-a-difia.
  **Kimbisirua, Kimbizirua,** *v.p.* Ame gnania kuamba kakimbizirue anae, angare apata hasara sana.
  **Kimbisua,** or **Kimbidzua,** *v.p.*
**Kimbisua, Kimbidzua,** *n.* (= Maroba in Kins.), (1) Madzere ni ku vondua gakazakua sira tu.
(2) (Kir.), fresh-killed meat. Kimili yuria niama ya kimbidzua ya ku ulagua rero, ela ikalala, basi machero ka i-ria.
**Kimboye,** or more frequently **Kimboyo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the name of an esculent root, similar to the sweet potato,

  but only eaten in famine, or by hungry shepherd-boys. Kimboyo kimera mborerani. The kimboyo grows in light, sandy soil. The creeping plant which grows from it is called Murio.
**Kimbuicha,** or **Kimbuidzia,** *n.*, a word only used in connection with Madzi. Madzi ga kimbuicha, That state of the water in the sea, in which the ebb and flow is but slight.
**Kimbule,** *n.* *See* Kavansi.
**Kimburu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vimburu), a vulture, a bird of prey.
**Kimede,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the glow-worm. Kimede kignala ku ariza.
**Kimedemede,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kimede, but a somewhat smaller kind). Kimedemede kignala hiraka-haraka (ku signiasignia).
**Kimembe,** *n.* (cha). Kimembe cha moyo (= Kij., Chembe cha moyo), The merry thought.
**Kimememue** (Kid.), *n.* (= Chidui in Kins.).
**Kimemue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the habit of involuntary smiling and laughing. Gnania yuna kimemue yunahenza ku dzeka muno.
**Kimene,** *n.* (= Usafihi in Kij.), pride, seclusion, insolence. From Ku mena. Ela gnania si mugnieti ela! kana kimene! cha ku mena atu.
**Kimenga,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), one.
**Kimerera.** Muhambo hiu ni wa kimerera.
**Kimfamfani,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Pahasi in Kidigo).
**Kimfara,** *n.* (cha). *See* Kuchu. Baldness.
**Kimfedo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Shokodeka. (1) A turn, a winding. Used of burrows.
(2) A charm-stick; the name of some particular spells or charms; radically, something that turns aside or prevents mischief. (*a*) A charm buried in the doorway or in the centre of an enclosure for cattle, and therefore more generally called Pingu ya cha. (*b*) A charm-stick, at the top of which a creeping plant is wound round; used in travelling and war. The one for travelling is also called Pingu ya charo (ya ku enendera Daida), while that for war goes by the name Kimfedo cha Kaya; also Kimfedo cha ku ramukira viha. The kimfedo with which to set out for war is laid up in the rungu. In the old town (Vokera, or, Kaya bomu) it is kept in the niumba ya vizuka. *See* Kizuka.
**Kimfode,** *n.*
**Kimfudo** (Kid.), *n.* (cha), a storm.
**Kimfugnio,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vimf-), a comb made of wood by the people on the coast (rarely used by the Wanyika). Kimfugnio cha ku mfugnira niere.
**Kimfuimfui,** *adv.* (= Kisirisiri), secretly, privately. Ku fidza kitu kimfuimfui, To hide something privately.
**Kimia,** *n.* (cha, pl. ?), a net. Kimia kukikodzakodza basi akakiika vimenga basi akadzuva.
**Kimia,** *adv.* (?). Ku gniamala kimia. Yupiga kimia.
**Kimidzi,** *adj.* *See* Guafia. Neno ra kimidzi.
**Kim'irim'iri,** *n.* (cha). *See* Wiriwiri. Twilight. Used only of the evening. From Ku muirika. Kudzihenda kim'irim'iri, It has made twilight (It has become twilight). (1) Kudzizama. (2) Kudzihanda. (3) Kudzikala kim'irim'iri. (4) Usiku udzikaza; kunakala kiza. Kudzedzua, kudzihanda, ku kala kim'irim'iri. Ku chari, or, Kuchere) kim'irim'iri, ka ku dza-

**Kimiro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), an ulcer in the throat. Gnania ni mukongo, yuna kimiro, or, yudzihenda kimiro. (Ni kidzivu kidide umironi.)
**Kimo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Ku vera; Ku fira. Stature, height. Kiimo, from Ku ima. **Kimodzolo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a whitlow.
**Kimumunie,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a kind of small pumpkin, peculiar for the excrescences with which it is dotted over; a vegetable marrow.
**Kimvode,** *n.* (= Kifieri; Kivodo in Kik.), derision. Gnania yuna manenoga kimvode. Gnania yunagomba, ela kana kimvode. Gnania maneno yunago, ela kana kimvode.
**Kina** (rel. to the ki class), it has; lit. it with.
**Kina** (sometimes pronounced **China**), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Era. (1) Depth, in water only. From Ku ina. *See* Uina; Gnirigniri; Cha niambura.

**Kindiri,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the name of a creeping plant. Ni kadzihi katite, kahenda hambala dzi. S'endeni hivo, vana miya ya kindiri. Kindiri ni ku bumua mbalasini.
**Kinembe,** *n.* (= Nembe).
**Kinemi,** *n.* (cha). *See* Niarika; Kilongo. Kaku niarika, kinemi ni kichache; kura ndani ni kuvu, ukibuma mbeyu, ni ku ola.
**Kinena,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), that part of the belly under the short ribs, called the hypochondria; the middle of the hypochondria.
**Kinewa,** *n.*, the name of a muanza. Yukudza dziku mbidzo; rero kuna kinewa, yundaukuha uchi.
**Kinga,** *adv.* (= Kindzedza). *See* Nga. It resembles.
**Kinga,** *n.* and *v.* *See* Chinga.
  **Kingama.** *See* Chinga.
  **Kingamia.** *See* Chinga.
  **Kingamisa.** *See* Chinga.
  **Kingika.** *See* Chinga.
  **Kingira.** *See* Chinga.
**Kingade,** *n.* Hungaambirua huari hosi, be una-ni-usa kingade, or, kibolesa.

  **Kingamia,** *v.a.* (Kingania in Kikir.; in Kir. ?), to obstruct. Nalonda muhi, ni kingamie njira. Adzeyeika lukuni hilu, ni-ani ku kingamia nchira? Mukingiko unaikua

**Kingurunga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Ving-), a small rock. Dim. of Ngurunga.

**Kiniafungo,** *n.* (Kid. = Sabadi mitu; Kij. ?), a wood, forest.

**Kinialu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Lengara. Dim. of Lunialu. From Kuniala.

**Kinkindze** (?).

**Kinoauchi,** *n.* (cha, pl. ?), the name of a creeping plant (Lubugu).
**Kinofu,** *n.* Nidzihewa kaniama katite ka kinofu, be nidzeria vavo, kakadzukurika, I have been given a small piece of meat. and have eaten it on the spot: it was not worth while carrying it.

**Kinundu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small, crooked back. Dim. of Nundu. Mutu huya yuna kinundu, This man is crook-backed.

  Munazi hura una kinundu, wariwa ni changa.
**Kinungu,** *n.*, a small caravan, consisting of, say, ten to twenty men. A caravan of three hundred or four hundred men is called Nganiawa.
**Kio,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vio) (= Chio), a looking-glass.
**Kiokue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kiyokue. Dim. of Muyokue.
**Kiondosaakurima,** *n.* (= Kifumbulusaarima).
**Kionkua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kionso** (Kid.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kidzonso in Kir.; and Masiwemasiwe in Kins.), a spot of grass which escaped the general burning. Visere vionso vionso; Niasi zinasalia kudukudu in Kij.
**Kipi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vipi), a cock's spur. Vipi via jogolo. Via fuando.
**Kipingua** (Kid.), *n.* (= Pingua in Kir.; Kongoso, No. 1, in Kins.).
**Kira, Chira,** *v.*
**Kira,** *pron.* (= Hikira?).
  **Kitukira.**
**Kirana,** *n.* *See* Kithana.
**Kirangaona** (also pronounced **Kithangaona**). Niama hiyu ni wa kithangaona, musi murie. Kithangaona muacho ambirua ni koma, be mki-ki-mena, basi ndecho hiki, kidzihendeka. Gnania wagomba kirangaona, Gnania spoke a prediction, foretold something to come, by a revelation from the koma.
**Kirariro** (more commonly pronounced **Kilariro,** *q.v.*), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kilariro. Provisions.
**Kirasi, Kirazi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), yams.
**Kirahu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kiratu), a sandal.
**Kiratu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a shoe, a sandal.
**Kiravai,** *adj.* *See* Mafu.
**Kiravo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), an oath, connected with charms; an ordeal. (1) Kiravo cha ndogoe. (2) Kiravo cha bahasi, kakomia ku guira. (3) Kiravo cha msegeneko. (4) Kiravo cha fisi. The kiravo of the hyena, so called because the transgressor was supposed to howl like a hyena when going to die. Such a case being very rare, it was thought the oath was not much dreaded, and it was therefore superseded by the Musafuma. (5) Kiravo cha muansa wa ache. (6) Ku piga kiravo, To make an oath implying a curse. A solemn act, in which the human word is combined with a visible sign. Any one accused of a crime or any offence, and knowing himself innocent, may have recourse to it. The sign is that of breaking a pot (niungu), or merely a large potsherd (dzaya). *See* Dovola. Mutu akipiga niungu, wamba: Ndiwe niungu, u-chitaye vitu viosi, viakuria; or, Uwe niungu, udiwe mualamusi be nidzisingua udzai; na nikale naloga, or, be kiravo na-ki-ni-guire, na chamba silogere, ni ku henda singua, be uwe ukaye-ni-singa, kiravo na-ki-ku-one. Basi akapiga. Kunoa and Kuria kiravo. Ku risana? kiravo. Ku-m-pigira kiravo. Ku-m-risa kiravo.
**Kire,** *adj.*, long; Kimo, tall.
**Kirefu, Kirevu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) the chin.
(2) The wattles of a cock. Kirefu cha chogolo; dzulu ni lemba, The lappets of a cock; above is the comb. Kirefu cha ma dzafuni.
(3) Beard. In Kid., Kirefu means only chin, and the beard is called Kidzera. Kirefu cha dzulu mulomoni; or, Kirefu cha mulomo wa dzulu, The hair on the upper lip, moustaches. Kirefu cha dzini, The beard.

## [PDF Page 192 — Dictionary Page 179 (Kir — Kir)]

**Kirema,** *n.* (cha), a drawback. Ni kirema nidza cho hewa ni Mulungu; haya una-ni-iga-w'amba nafialua na cho? Kirema nidzihewa dzulu ya dzi, ela sifiarirue nacho; haya-una-ni-dzeka-dze we? Kuenu mbarini kakuna vionsue, u-ni-dzekaye we? Kisulutini ni kudzo, ela kiremache ni dzungu; na hiva ni vadzo, ela kiremache ni usiri.
**Kiremba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Lilia. Any cloth wound round the head in the form of a turban. Adzomba ndio apigao viremba kidzoani. A Mu-lungu yudzi-ni-pa kiremba; mukongo yudzivola kuamba nibade fungurangu; Mulungu yudziuchirira ku-ni-pa kiremba-kua huya m'kongo ku vola; be yu vosua ni Mulungu, says an mganga with regard to a patient, whose case he had considered hopeless. *See* Ganchagancha.
**Kiremesaaganga,** *n.*, a baffler. Gnania ni kiremesaaganga; lit. one who baffles the doctors, or charmers, *i.e.* one incurable.
**Kiremesafisi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the knee-pan; lit. what overpowers the hyena; what is too much too hard even for a hyena to eat. In Kij., Kilegesa mbua, What causes a dog to leave off. In Kij., Kiema mbidi.
**Kirenge,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) (= Kidoma in Kij.), a calabash, whether small or large. N.B.—The plant from which virenge calabashes grow is not, as one would suppose from the analogy, called Murenge, but Mudzungu.
(2) (= Dango in Kij.), a small pumpkin. Dim. of Renge. Murenge udzihenda vilembo, hata punde ukaamba vidzikala virenge vikikala vibomu, basi gadzikala marenge nago ka-ga-hendua virenge; and they are not made into calabashes, whence the Prov., U-mufiere wa renge kuhendeka kirenge, Kuani hata renge rikikala bomu dze-ka-ri-hendeka kirenge, Why, let the pumpkin become ever so great, it can never be made into a calabash. Vidzungu vikikomala, basi vi-kala virenge. Kirenge cha via homa ra gnombe.
**Kirere,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Luensa). *See* Mudzundu.
**Kiria.** *See* Kithia.
**Kiriama,** or **Kikiriama,** *n.* (= Bumira). *See* Mafu.
**Kiriango,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Msingi. A small door, a shutter, a window. Dim. of Muriango.
**Kiriangoe,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), lit. the crab-eater; the name of a species of animal which lives on crabs. Yunaria koe. Yu-nga kala. Gnania yunafua muno dza kiriangoe. Such is the superstition of the natives, that when they go crabbing, the name of this animal, and the name of the monkey, hyena, lion, swine, must not be used if they are to be successful in their employment.
**Ki-ri-cho,** *particles* used in conjugation.
**Kirima,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a hill.
(2) Top, plateau of a mountain, the eminence or prominent part of a mountain. Kirima cha Kathiaro kina murima mbomu, ela kirima cha. Kilibasi ni kirima, ka-ki-na murima mbomu.
**Kirimi,** *n.* (cha), an impediment in one's speech. Ku gomba na kirimi, gnania yugomba na kirimi. Ka ndiwe tha, for, Ka ndiwe ela.
**Kirimira,** *n.* (cha), the Pleiades. Kirimira kilume, Orion. In contradistinction to which

*Footer: 179*

---

## [PDF Page 193 — Dictionary Page 180 (Kir — Kir)]

  the Pleiades are called Kirimira kiche. Kirimira kilume ni lulongo lua niegniesi tahu. Mfumbi ndio u bodosao kirimira.
**Kirimo,** *n.*
**Kirimusha** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to entertain, to treat with hospitality. Ni shaha, dzina tu ela kana kitu cha ku kirimusha atu, He is a chief by name only, but has nothing with which to entertain people.
**Kirindi,** *n.*
**Kirindo,** *n.*, a ward, watch-guard.
**Kirinsi,** *n.* *See* Dzehui. Contradiction. Ku funa wa kirinsi. In contradistinction to Ku funa wa lugua and Ku dondola.
**Kirira,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Murira.
**Kiriri.**
**Kiriro,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Risa; Amula. Crying, lamentation, wailing. From Ku rira. Kudzi-fuewa hiva, atu anarira kiriro. The pl. is used when the crying is heard at a distance, indistinctly: Anariro viriro (!). Mbira kure na kiriro kure (Kid., Hanga kure na kiriro kure).
**Kiriwa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Vihendo. Dim. of Riwa.
**Kirobo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a kind of small basket; lit. a small quarter. Ni kikahana kitite, ki ngacho kibaba. Kirobo cha ku esera kilariro. Kirobo cha ku dzekesera. Ni kirobo to (= Ni kirobo geri = Ndecho geri).
**Kirogo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kidzaye; Kijedzo).
**Kironda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (in Kik., Kidau), a wound, a sore; ulcer, abscess. Dim., Karonda; magn., Donda.
**Kirondo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Rondo.
**Kiru,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viru), (1). *See* Gniri. Kiru cha kambi cha chiho.
(2) *See* Atili *aakao kiru*, or Mulili, pl. Alili and Ulili. Kiru cha mbega. This is very rare, and will only be worn when going to fight during a time of war.
**Kirua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the blossom of the murua tree. It is used as a perfume of the oil and grease with which the Wanyika rub themselves. Kirua cha ufumba, The blossom of the murua. Murua unafiala virua. Virua vinanuka ufumba.
**Kirudu, Kiruju,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Muruchu.
**Kirue,** *n. coll.* (cha), the blossom of beans, but only of the mukunde, not of the mubalasi. Mukunde wangu udzihenda kirue.
**Kirufu,** *n.* (cha), a slight smell. Dim. of Rufu. Rufu ni hirira rinukaro muno, ela rinukaro pundepunde, hebu ri siro nuka muno, basi ndicho kirufu; kidza, ukaamba ni karufu. Kirufu cha marua. Nidzisikira kirufu, kinanuka, ni chani cho? Hangi ni kirufu cha niama akafua, hangi ni kirufu chani, simania.
**Kirumbi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a magic wand of a caravan-leader. Many charms are appended to it. It is stuck up for the night in the camp. Should it fall down, it forebodes evil.
**Kirumbiri,** *n.* (cha).
**Kirumura,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (K.) a shrub.
**Kirungurira,** *n.* (cha) (= Kiungulia in Kij.), heartburn, flatulency.
**Kirunsa,** *n.* (cha), the cloth used for wrapping up a dead body. (K.) Ku enenda kirunsa, To condole. Kiyite, Condolence. Nguo ya kirunsa.
**Kirurumo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (Cha dziko in Kins.), a fine paid to the kambi or mfaya, *e.g.* for killing a man, or other great offences. From Ku ruruma.

*Footer: 180*

---

## [PDF Page 194 — Dictionary Page 181 (Kir — Kis)]

  Ku lafia gnombe ya kirurumo.
**Kirusi,** *n.* (cha) (= Kirufu). Marua higa gananuka kirusi ki.
**Kisa, Kiza,** *n.* (cha), darkness. Kiza cha usiku. Sinda upuka ndze, kuna kiza. Be kuna kiza chani, ko kadziza be ni kiza fio? Magn., Dziza; dim., Kadziza.
**Kisa,** *n.*, flare, blaze. Muhaso wa kisa. (Fulo, or Mukokola). Ku muta muerekera. (K.) Moho una kisa kisa, To flare.
**Kisaga,** *n.*, a small measure = vibaba vieri, two vibaba, half a pishi; lit. a small grinding.
**Kisahani,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small plate. Dim. of Sahani.
**Kisakisa, Kizakiza,** *n.* Madzoga. Kisakisa cha dziloni, above.
**Kisana, Kizana,** *n.* (cha). *See* Chisa. Very thin cloth.
**Kisansu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small branch. Dim. of Sansu.
**Kiseho,** *n.* This word will be the best for chapter, division. From Ku seha. Hukalala, hukadzinsa kiseho. Kiseho cha mbere. Uina hiu nidzi-u-dzimba kiseho kibomu, hangu nidzavoansa ku dzimba, ni kiseho kibomu. Mutu akipiga perembe, be akihenda kiseho cha kusa soha haraka, ndiye aambuaye yuna kiseho.
**Kiselasela,** *n.* (= Kiboleza). Rarely used.
**Kisemaabayo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a species of crab, similar to the koe, but smaller.
**Kisengere,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the skin in which the grain of Guinea-corn is enclosed, and which comes off on the masuche being beaten out. If it does not come off, it is called kikombe, and such grains are then pounded. Navonda visengere, I pound Guinea-corn still enclosed in its skin.
**Kisengesenge,** *n.* (cha), (1) (= Kiseho; Uina?), chapter, division.
(2) Ku uya kisengesenge (= Mfudura, Kins.).
**Kiserema,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Serema. Kiserema ni jembe rikiro rimirua-be rikasira.
**Kisha,** *adv.* (= Kij., Kushanda; Kuenda; Kidzanda; Kir.), then here, subsequently, after.
**Kishaka,** *n.*, a small forest, jungle. Prov., Niuma ni kishaka.
**Kishanda,** *n.* (cha) (= Kizianda).
**Kishombo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kibombue in Kid.; Kisombo in Kij.), food of sundry things compounded. Muchangu yudzibunda kishombo cha mugasija na nazi.
**Kishongo,** *n.* (cha). *See* Chongo; Kisongo cha moyo. (K.) Dishumour. Moyo udzihenda kishongo sikahensa. H'ende hukahambe vatu vasiku. Resp., A ningaenenda, ela sihensi moyo u kishongo, ka-u-ka-goloka to, or, ka-u-kaera; ka-u-kadzuka. Angaenenda moyo uere u kishongo (= Uere ka-u-kagoloka yuere kahensi rohoni muakue) hata akifika kure, basi moyo ukagoloka. Ningaenenda moyo uere u kishongo, ka-u-kagoloka, ela vino basi moyo udzigoloka. *See* Ongoresa; Esa.
**Kishonono,** *n.* (cha). *See* Kibicho; Usaha. Gonorrhœa. The common contagious kind in males is sadly common.
**Kisi** (Kij.), *v.a.* (= Ku gesa in Kir.), (1) to tack.
(2) To guess. Kitu hiki na-ki-kisi (= na-ki-gesa); nikiona na-ki wesa, ni-ki-dzukule.
**Kisi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Visi), (K.) nucleus, kernel. Kisi cha tembe ya madzere, or, muhama. Visi via chende, or, tsende.

## [PDF Page 195 — Dictionary Page 182 (Kis — Kis)]

**Kisia, Kizia,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small lake. Dim. of Zia.
**Kisianda,** *n.* Kisi ya nda (= Ku sia ndani).
**Kisibao,** *n.*, a vest. Mudzomba akafuala kisibao.
**Kisibidi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the name of an odoriferous shrub. Makodzage ni ufumba. Atu ni ku vunsa vidahi vie akadzomeka dzingoni; hebu akabuma dzasini irio na mafuha, aki-dzi-sara, aka-nuka to.
**Kisibidi,** *n.* Mboga za kisibidi, A sauce of kisibidi.
**Kisichana,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Musichana.
**Kisifu, Kizivu** (Kij.), *adj.*, ripe. Kitu hiki ni kisifu, ni kitu kiricho kamili, kisicho bunguani.
**Kisigo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Musigo.
**Kisiho,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), heavy; (K.) weighty, difficult.
**Kisihu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Lusihu.
**Kisikane,** *n.* (cha), the price at which grain is sold, fixed upon by the headmen of a town. The custom is now only met with in the northern towns, which are richer in grain, especially in Chogni. Kisikane ni murongo udzio katua ni mudzi. *See* Kidzansulago; Kisinde.
**Kisiki,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Cha muhi mdzua). *See* Kisinde. (1) A stump, Yudzi-ku-dzusa to, kamuna visiki.
(2) (Udaathi in Kik.), the rainbow. Kudzimuta kisiki. Kisiki kidzimuta muakani mfula indakala ningi. Kisiki kidzimuta udzerero wa dzua-be ni kisiki cha dzua, kakuna mfula ningi muaka wa rero. Kisiki kidzimuta vuri-vuri ra rero rindanona. Mvula idzimuta kisiki.
**Kisikisi,** *adj.*, quick. Ku uya kisikisi. Yudzienenda yudziuya kisikisi (= hiraka-hiraka).
**Kisiku,** *n.* (pl. Vi-), a small piece. Visiku via niama, Small pieces of meat. Visiku via kolekole, Small pieces of fish.
**Kisiku,** *adj.*, certain. Kitu kisiku, A certain thing. Kima kisiku, A certain price.
**Kisiku,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Musa. A piece. Kisiku cha dzango, A piece of brass wire. Kisiku cha mukodo. Nakata mua visiku visiku. Ni-pa kisiku kimenga, nirie. Of sugar-cane, Ku ria is used, not Ku hafuna. Na isu ni ku kata visiku visiku.
**Kizima,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Dzidzo. A well.
**Kizima,** *adj.* *See* Komo.
**Kizimba,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (K.) a cage. Kisimba cha ku hegera kuve, monso, etc.
**Kisimbamirara,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), an animal somewhat smaller than the lion, and white in colour.
**Kisimui.**
**Kizinda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Nidzibuma kisinda cha madzere navonda hata n'dzuse, be nihume kisinda cha viri. Nidzivonda visinda viiri hebu vihahu.
**Kisinda.** Kitu hiki kisinda kaki-kaidzala, or, kaka-ki-idzasa.
**Kisinde,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) (Kir.) (= Kigolo in Kid.), the stump of the vanda, when used up by the process of drawing toddy.
(2) *See* Lugua. The stump of a stalk, as of muhama. Visinde ni via muhama udzaodemua, not, kisiki.
(3) A ball made of grass and sand tied together, to play with. Ku dzuvana kisinde.
(4) *See* Dasa. Nidzisisndikirua kisinde mimi, nidzila la nacho. Gnania yudzilala na kisinde. Akaona haya dza adzeyeiya.

*Footer: 182*

## [PDF Page 196 — Dictionary Page 183 (Kis — Kis)]

  (5) (Kid.) (= Giniasi in Kir.), a bundle of dry grass for thatching.
**Kisindo,** or **Kishindo.** *See* Marura.
**Kisinge, Kisinde,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Singe.
**Kisingihi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the threshold, sill. Nokota kisingihi kuamba muriango usikururiedzi.
**Kisingiso,** *n.* (cha), pretence. From Ku singisa.
**Kisingo,** *n.* Njira ya kisingo (= Ya ku sunguluka).
**Kisira,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kisirisiri,** *n.*, a secret, mystery. Maneno ga kisirisiri. Yudzi-mu-va kitu kisirisiri, He has given him something secretly.
**Kisiru,** *adj.*, sharp, sour, bitter, fierce.
**Kisisi** (Kid.), *n.* (cha) (= Kikansu in Kir.). Kana kisisi. Kana joho.
**Kisisi, Kizizi,** *n.* Cha gnombe, (K.) stall. Gnombe hino ui dziru, ka-i-ndagamika, sudi mu-i-hendere kizizi.
**Kisisisi,** *n.*, sobbing. Mutu hiye yudzirira muno, yuna kisisisi. Muana hiyu yudzirira hata yudzihenda kisisisi. Muana hiyu akaansa kare kurira yudzihenda kisisisi.
**Kisiwa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kombora. An island.
**Kisiwani,** in (or to) the island, *i.e.* Mombas. This form of the word is always the one in which Mombas is spoken of or mentioned, but it is generally corrupted into Kisunai.
**Kis'mari,** *n.*, a task.
**Kiso,** *n.* (cha, pl. Viso) (= Mforonkue), the cellular nest of white ants. Kiso ni cha ludzoa.
**Kisoere,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kigocho. From Ku soerereka. Nisegere vava kisoere, siidima ku enenda. *See* Soere.
**Kisoloti,** *n.*, a piece of cloth, one-third of a doti.
**Kisonia,** *n.* (= Mboga).
**Kisosa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small bone. Dim. of Musosa.
**Kisuani.** Corrupted from Kisiwani.
**Kisuche,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Eleliua. Dim. of Suche.
**Kisuka, Kizuka,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Niumba ya muchena vizuka.
**Kisuki,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kisulasula** (Kid.), *n.* Anache hia anahenda kisulasula andaguirua ni kisungu.
**Kisumari,** *n.* (= Kis'mari).
**Kisumba,** *n.*, the name of a species of grass. Niasi sa kisumba.
**Kisumo,** *n.* Ku-m-piga kisumo (= Ku-m-suma). Gnania yunabigua kisumo, hata akiguirua ni muiri, akifua kua kisumo.
**Kisungu, Kizungu,** *n.* (cha) (= Ni ki zungu). *See* Sunsula. Giddiness. Mutu hiye yuna kizungu, kavuka madzi ga ku gera; akienenda na mudandando, basi akilola madzi gagerafio ni ku bua. Kidzoa kina ni sunguluka, nidzihenda kizungu. Nidzihenda kizungu, dzi inaenenda.
**Kisungu,** *adj.* (= Ni ki sungu), relating to the Asungu. Europeans.
**Kisunguluko,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Rarely used. Nchira hia, or, Hino inasunguluka, ina kisunguluko. Nchira hio ina visunguluko vingi, but more frequently they will say, Ina sunguluka muno.
**Kisungumuso,** *n.* (cha). *See* Sungumusa.
**Kisusi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kashusi in Kij.).
**Kisusu,** *n.*
**Kisusuri.**
**Kisusuri cha kanga,** (1) Makodzage gana vibato vieruve, vitite vitite dza kanga.
(2) The name of a species of plant. Muiriwe ni muiru, ela yuna vibato vieruve dza kanga; makaloge yukala minazini, or, makaloge yu-

*Footer: 183*

---

## [PDF Page 197 — Dictionary Page 184 (Kis — Kit)]

  hensa minazini. Kana haraka ya ku luma.
**Kisusuru,** *n.*, the name of a plant sometimes used in cooking. Ni kadzihi makodzage gaka dzambulua, gakabumua mbogani, basi zikafuidzua sikakala mbidzo.
**Kita** (also pronounced **Chita**), *v.a.* (= Ku dunga; Hu muta), to stick, to fix, to pierce, to transfix. Ku kita dzi fumo. Nidzi-ri-kita, or, Nidzi-ri-muta, vavo ndze. Ku kita, or, Ku jita gonga, To rest the head on the elbows (= Ku muta kita). Kid., Ku-m-kita mutu fumo (= Kir., Ku-m-dunga mutu fumo). Ku-m-kita nioka fumo (= Kir., Ku-m-dunga nioka fumo). Prov., Iyua yo ndio ikitayo.
**Kita,** *n.*, a thorn.
  **Kitakita,** *v. reit.*, to prick, to keep pricking. Said of pain. Ndani ina ni kitakita miya (= ini ni dungadunga), The belly it with me prick prick thorns; *i.e.* it keeps pricking me like thorns.
**Kitanda** (Kij.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a bedstead. Vitanda Aravai ahensa vio ni hivira vikavio ambua na chingo.
**Kitekilazo.**
**Kitembe,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class; pl. Vi-), little, scarce, scanty. Kitu kitembe (= Kitu kitate). Vitu vitembe, A few things.
**Kithama,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a forked post, on which the stalks of Guinea-corn are lodged during harvest. *See* Dzuri.
**Kithana,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Gumi). Kithana cha munga. Munga unalafia kilhana kingi. Kuna mihi ilafiayo vithana.
**Kithangaona** (Kik.), *n.* *See* Kirangaona. A sacrifice, a prediction. Kithangaona kidzi-m-kolosera m'egnie, The prediction was fulfilled on himself. Uchi hiu ni wa kithangaona, Toddy or palm-wine set apart for a sacrifice (= Kir., Uchi hiu na kasadoka vavo mudzini).
**Kithangu, Kirangu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kikomo), (1) the forehead.
(2) Lock. Gnania yuna kithangu kidzo na uso udzo, ak'enda dzuma ni ku rumiria. Mutu kiye yuna kithangu kidzo, aki uka tu, ni ku pata kitu. Yuna kithangu cha gnonzi.
**Kithembe,** *n.*
**Kithia,** *n.* Mbusi ya kithia (= Mboi ye Mulungu in Kikamba). Mbusi isio pembe.
**Kithugnia,** or **Kithunia,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a small piece of fat. Dim. of Thugnia.
(2) A white spot on the breast of an infant (spoken of as a complaint incidental to them, and which is cured by scarifying it). Muana yunalumua ni homboni, yuna kithugnia, m-dzodzeni.
**Kithuma** (Kik.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the half of the hide of a cow cut into an oval shape, used to carry loads in, and to lie on when travelling. Kithuma ni cha ku hambira.
**Kithumo,** *n.*, the name of a dance or play peculiar to the Agnaro. By others it is only performed on the occasion of a woman having a revelation from the koma (spirit). *See* Ku losa. Agnaro anafuina kithumo.
**Kitokoto,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kadzina katite), a small hole in the ground. Dim. of Tokoto. Ni niama wani yuno, ayefula kitokoto hiva?
**Kitongotongo,** *adv.* *See* Asira. Ku-ni-lola kitongotongo vio nini, nidzi-ku-henda dze?
**Kitu,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Mudabidabi; Dumania. A thing, something. Si muina kitu, etc.
**Kituma.** *See* Kithuma.
**Kitumbi** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kuva in Kir.; Kuba in Kij.), a tick.

## [PDF Page 198 — Dictionary Page 185 (Kiu — Kiv)]

**Kiusakowe** (Kid.), *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kikulangowe in Kir.; Dzambidzambi in Kins.).
**Kiuyekiuye,** *n.* Maneno ga kiuyekiuye.
**Kivala,** *n.* (cha) (= Kimfara). *See* Mfuadzi; Bora. (1) A bald head.
(2) A species of antelope. Dim. of Pala. Kivala ni muana pala.
**Kivalao,** *n.*
**Kivalo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-).
**Kivanda,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a small bough. Dim. of Panda. Kivanda cha muhi (= Kibanda cha muhi).
(2) Dim. of Vanda (ra munazi). Kivanda cha munazi.
(3) Reha kivanda; or, Lafia kivanda. Kivanda cha nguo (= Guruja mbiri).
**Kivande,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Luvande.
**Kivanga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), (1) a small cave. Dim. of Panga.
(2) A species of vulture, similar to the luvanga, but smaller. The luvanga catches fowls, but the kivanga only small birds. Dim. of Luvanga. Kivanga cha niuni.
**Kivango,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Pango. Kivango cha muhi; but, Kivanga cha iwe.
**Kivangua,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Gagamisa. A kind of trap for animals like antelopes. Kivangua cha ku hegera pala na funo.
**Kivansi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small noose. Dim. of Vansi.
**Kivarare,** *n.*, the name of a grass or plant.
**Kivedi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (Kik. for the Kir. word Kikongue). *See* Goma. An old woman. Gnombe hi idzikala kivedi. *See* Mukonkue. Ahoho a hikaraona mambo: aki-ku-ona, angue: u-kivedi; be ni-kivedi, nikadzinsa mfiala hebu dze? Ndo ahoho a hikara arivio; hata ukakala ukaviala mimba menga, aki-ku-ona, a-ku-iha kivedi.
**Kivegnio.** Dim. of Pegnio.
**Kiveho,** *n.* (cha). Dim. of Luveho; but Kaveho is more frequently used. Kiveho hiki ni kidzo.
**Kivesa,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). *See* Kibago; Enesa. Mihi ya kivesa. *See* Cheso. Atu adzimuta vivesa (via niumba mbiri-taku, etc.).
**Kivevero,** *n.* *See* Vevera.
**Kiveveya,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), light, as a feather, chaff, etc. Obs. Kitu hiki ni kiveveya kaki-merera; pl. Vitu hivi ni viveveya.
**Kivevo,** *n.* (= Kivevero).
**Kivi,** for **Kiivi** (Kid.), *adj.* (= Kifuhi in Kir.), short.
**Kivia,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class), new.
**Kiviakue,** his peculiarity. Uki-mu-ona-yunaria na mukono wa ku modzo, basi ndo mukonowe ahumerao, nda kiviakue.
**Kiviarira,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a home-born slave.
**Kividza,** *n.* (cha). Jogolo hiri rina kividza.
**Ki-vimenga,** *adv.* *See* Luvi. At one and the same time. Mfula yagnia ki-vimenga.
**Kivinda,** *n.*
**Kivindi,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a string (of beads, worn round the neck), a necklace. Kivindi cha ushanga. Kivindi cha dzingoni.
**Kivini,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), a small handle. Dim. of Muvini.
**Kivo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vivo) (= Kifuvu in Kij.), (1) the half of a cocoa-nut. Nidzikuna nazi nzima, vivo viiri.
(2) The crown of the head. Kivo cha kidzoa.
**Kivongolo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-) (= Kigodo in Kid.), a bracelet. Kivongolo cha hambo. Kivongolo cha dzango.
**Kivovolo,** *n.*

## [PDF Page 199 — Dictionary Page 186 (Kiv — Ko)]

**Kivudzu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class). *See* Pudzu. Thin, narrow.
**Kivukuse.** *See* Isu.
**Kivula,** *n.* *See* Umbuiga.
**Kivuluda** (Kig.), *n.* Kuku wa kivuluda. Kivuluda kiki.
**Kivumba, Kifumba,** *adj.*, belonging or relating to Fumba, a small territory in the neighbourhood of Wasin. The word only occurs in connection with water-jars of a particular shape. Pfugo sa kivumba, Water-jars with very narrow necks, such as are now only brought from India (the jars made in the country having no necks at all). It seems that originally necked jars only came from Vumba, while at the present date they are all brought from India.
**Kivumfu,** *n.*
**Kivumi,** *n.* (cha), dust, noise. Dim. of Vumi.
**Kivumivumi,** *n.* (cha, Niuche), the hum of bees.
**Kivunga,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), the hair of mourning. On the death of a relative they have their heads shaved. The hair which grows again is called Kivunga, and is not to be shaved. From Ku vunga. Muche yuika kivunga cha mumfera. Mulume naye yuika kivunga cha hahu cha mumfera. *See* Gochesa. Ku larika vivunga. Mfaya adieke, be alarike vivunga. Ku niolua kivunga.
**Kivuvu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class). *See* Kilongo. Naked, bare, empty.
**Kivuvu,** *adv.* *See* Kelia.
**Kiwarare,** *n.*, the name of a shrub.
**Kiwari** (Kid.), *n.* (cha), strife. Una kiwari nami hebudze? (Kisebabu cha kale in Kij.), An old strife.
**Kiwawa,** *adj.* *See* Ngigi. Thin, slender, from unripeness. Only used of calabashes. Kirenge ki-si-cho komala to, ni kiwawa, ka-ki-na ndzira.
**Kiwawai,** *n.*, the breaking forth of water from great saturation of the ground. Only used as predicate, and forming no pl. Dzi idzihumbuka kiwawai (= idzihumbuka madzo). *See* Di. Mfula idzegnia ningi, idzihumbula kiwawai.
**Kiwembe,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Mbusi idziupusa viwembe. Trop., Muhama udzihenda viwembe via sa.
**Kiw'eo, Kiwueo,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-), lit. something with. The curry or sauce eaten with the wari. Kiw'eo cha niuni. Kiw'eo cha kuku. Niama ya kiw'eo.
**Kiwewe,** *n.* (cha).
**Kiwiyiwiyi,** *n.*, the name of a species of bird. Kaaka muhi usio muiya, waaka miyani du, kuamba kidzungiche. Kis'ende halua ni mutu, ak'enda hala, adungue ni miya. Gnania akafuala kidzungi cha kiwiyiwiyi, akabuma ufumba, kinanuka to.
**Kiwue** (Kid.), *n.* (in Kij., Salsaliban?), a venereal disease similar to kishonono. These diseases are sadly common among the Wanyika, and there are many words for the different stages of the diseases. *See* Kibolesa and Kibumbafu.
**Kiyeseyese.** Gnania yuna gomba kiyeseyese. Atu a kare maneno gao gari ga kiyeseyese.
**Kiyokue,** *n.* (cha, pl. Vi-). Dim. of Muyokue.
**Kiyuya,** *adj.* (rel. to the ki class) (= Changu angu; Kipesi in Kij.). *See* Yuya. Light, not heavy, easy, not difficult. *See* Mafu. Kitu hiki ni kiyuya, ka-ki-merera.
**Kiyuye** (= Kiyuya).
**Ko,** *a particle* (the rel. to Ku), denoting direction as to place and time. *See* Sima; Dodola; Kundu; Kafindu; Lagana; Mbere; Niuma; Sansa; Yogoma; Rungu. There; to.

*Footer: 186*
