## [PDF Page 200 — Dictionary Page 187 (Ko — Kog)]

  Moyo wasa ko, be ndo wenda ko, Where to the heart thinks, there it goes. Moho u-dele ko kuenu ah unadzalonda moho hiku na moho una-u-richa kuko kuenu?
**Ko,** *poss. pron.* (a, rel. to the infin. Ku; b, rel. to the ka class), thy. Kurimako ku foroforo. Kugema ko ku foroforo.
**Koa,** *v.a.* *See* Andula. Ku koa babayu. Nakoa dafu, nirie lukoe. Dafu ra ku koa, in contradistinction to Dafu regnie. Der., Koa; Mukoa.
**Koa,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Regeza. Yudzi fungua mikono niuma na koa. Yudzi fungua koa mikono niuma yunafulumusua kuenda madzini.
**Koba, Kopa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Dim., Kakoba; Kikoba.
**Koba, Kopa,** (1) *v.n.* (= Ra nagasija). *See* Kidzumbi; Mfalume; Bemba. To bend, to incline. Isu rangu, ridzikopa, ralonda ku funsika, be nadema nguso, nika-ri-sike. Yunaenenda ku zama zama, yudzikonga, muiriwe ukaveheka. Yuna muiri wa ku kopa, or, akakopa muiri.
(2) (Kij.), *v.a.* (in Kir., Ku avaha, or, Ku hala deni), to borrow, to ask a loan. This word is said to be more frequently used now than their own. It has, however, often the additional signification of defrauding, from the too common practice of people not paying back. Nidzikopa kitu kua gnania. Yudzikopa reale kuangu; or, Yudzi-ni-kopa reale. Ku-dzi-kopa uchi kuku, etc. Der., Kobe; Lukove (pl. Kove); Jobo.
  **Kobesha,** *v.c.* (= Ku avasa in Kir.), to lend. U-ni-kobeshe reale.
  **Kobia,** *v.a.*
  **Kobieka,** *v.n.* *See* Kikofia.
  **Kobiekera,** *v.d.*
  **Koboka,** or **Kobuekera,** *v.n.* Der., Gopue; Tobo; Govi(?).
  **Kobola,** *v.a.* (= Ku koniola; Ku kaniula). *See* Kolola. Ku kobola tobo. Ku kobola uina.
**Kobe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a tortoise; lit. the curved one. From Ku koba. Dim., Kakobe and Kikobe; magn., Rikobe.
**Kobekera** (= Kikobue).
**Kobeziya,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Koboka.** *See* Koba.
**Kobola.** *See* Koba.
**Koda,** *v.a.*, to go (?).
  **Kodola.**
  **Kodesa, Kochesa.** *See* Koka.
**Kodo, Kocho.** Mvula inagnia kochokocho, ka-i-avusa. Nazi inasuka, inaamba: kochokocho; ndio nazi pfu.
**Kodza,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Lu kodza. A leaf, blade. Kodza ridzi, A green leaf. Kodza rivu, A dry leaf. Makodza maidzi, Green leaves. Makodza mavu, Dry leaves.
**Kodza, Koza,** *v. reit.* *See* Kamia.
**Kodzoka.** *See* Kongo; Gongika.
**Kodzola.**
**Koe,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), a species of crab, smaller than the kala. Koe hiyu. Koe hia. Koe yuhenda wimbi himura luindani.
**Koeleo,** *n.* *See* Pueleo.
**Kofi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Fumba), an open handful of grain, salt, etc. Yudzi-ni-pigira, or, Yudzi-ni-hegera, makofi mairi ga muvunga.
**Kofi,** *n.* (za), a box in the ear. Pl. of Lukofi. Ku piga kofi, To clap the hands. In Kij., Kofi means a box in the ear (= Ivi and Mbalahi in Kir.), but Kofi in Kir. means clapping of the hands.
**Kofia,** *n.*, a cap. Kofiae apigazo zinarira muno, zinaayuka masikironi.
**Kofui,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), limax.
**Kofula.**
**Koga,** *n.* (ya and ra), a mould. Chingo zidzihenda, or, iguira koga. Kavu idziguira koga.

## [PDF Page 201 — Dictionary Page 188 (Kog — Kol)]

**Kogo,** *n.* (ya, za), the occiput, the hinder part of the head. Kogo ya kidzoa. Miyokue idzi ahula idzi-upusa kogo.
**Kogo,** or **Koko,** *n.* (ya, za), the stone of fruit. Koko ya koma. Koko za gumo. Hubande zumo, hugafie kula mutu a hale kokoye koko za maembe, The stones of mangoes; but the stone of mzambarao is tembe.
**Koikoi** (= Korokoro).
**Koka,** *v.n.* *See* Ku chema. To crack, to make a sudden noise. Only used of what is breaking. Ukani! muhi una koka, ulonda ku bua, unahenda ka. Tahi hi inakoka, inagomoka ku bua. Niumba inafunsika, inakoka. Der., Koko; Lukoko; Ukoko; Kikoko.
  **Kochesa,** or **Kokesa** (the *k* being softened into *ch*), *v.a.* (= Doboa in Kij.; Kochesa in Kins.). *See* Muzizo; Kidio. To break, only used in a tropical sense; to infringe, to transgress. Ku kochesa muzizo, To infringe on a prohibition. Nidzi-ku-lagula, nidzi-ku-sikiha mudzi-o, be sudi vana mizizo; mkirinda mizizo, kavana mutu a ndayekudza hala kitucho; hata niama mudui kandavegnia mudzini muako; ela mki kochesa basi mudzibananga egnie.
  **Kokodeka,** *v.n.* (= Gogoda in Kij.). Mutu hiye yudzikala mufiere, kaidima ku enenda, yuhenda kokodeka. Ku dzedzera na mdada, ndo ku kokodeka.
  **Kokola,** *v.a.*, to refuse. Vatu va-ri-vo na mifusi mingi, ukaamba: nidzi-va-kokola, nidzifiera, hata nidzi-va-dzusa.
**Koko,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Imani, ni-mu-kuangurire koko, rarosala dzana.
**Koko,** *adv.* Muhoho yunaima koko. (1) Muhoho yunasagala. Vikidza koma, akaambua. (2) Muhoho yunafunsa mafuindi. (3) Muhoho yunahambala. (4) Muhoho yunaiua na mihi. (5) Muhoho yunaima koko; or, Yudziuma ku ima koko. (6) Muhoho yunasukula, it makes Suku-suku. (7) Muhoho yunaenenda. (8) Muhoho yudziuma ku enenda, yunapiga malo.
**Kokolewa** (Kij.), *v.p.* Mtanga unakokolewa na maji.
**Kokorakokora,** or **Kororakorora** (?).
**Kokorosha** (Kig.) (= Ku dodoma dodoma in Kins.).
**Kokota, Gogota** (= Kuku yudzi kokota ana; Engula). Mutu akilonda ku kalanga ichi, ni ku-ri-kokota kalomo, akalafia luho.
**Kola,** *v.n.* and *a.* *See* Ngulula; Mfumbi; Dzapiu; Dzongo. To choke, to be choked. Dzua nidzikola. Dzua ridzikoladzi, ka-ku-fiogeka. Dzi idzikola, mfula. Dzi idzikola dzua. Nanoa uchi hata nikole, basi ni-u-riche; or, Nanoa hata ndivokola ngufu sangu, basi nirite. Nidzeria kitu, kidzi-ni-kola, I have eaten a something, and it has choked me. Muiya wa sui udzi-ni-kola (= udzi-ni-kuama). Enche hiri rina kola dza muniu. Madzi gadzikola, ela ka-ga-dza ira. Moho nidzi-u-busa, udzikola (= udzikala moho kamiri). Muniu udzikola, usiongese kahiri. Kitu hiki kinazizima, ka-ki-kakola muniu. Nidzibuma muniu, ela ka-u-kakola. Sadaka idzikola. Komaze zika kola dza muniu.
  **Kaloka,** *v.n.* *See* Chegnie. Sansu ra nazi rikoloka, ridzebua. Chegnie kikikala kire, sansu ka ri komia ku koloka (= funsika).
  **Kolua,** *v.p.* *See* Dzohodzoho. Nidzikolua ni chiru, n'enda nikanoc madzi. Atu adzikolua ni ndzala, analonda chakuria. Atu adzikolua ni uchi,

*Footer: 188*

---

## [PDF Page 202 — Dictionary Page 189 (Kol — Kol)]

  adzi-u-richa. Gnania kakolua ni uchi, ni kunoa tu-yunamala homa zima, ela mimi nikinoa vibaria viiri hebu vihahu, basi udzi-ni-kola. Nakolua ni muiya wa sui.
  **Kolola,** *v.n.* *See* Fio. To cough, to gather. Niana adzaye kolola rino dzere. Ku kolola muhama when still unripe, but Kufunsa when ripe.
  **Kololua,** *v.p.* Dzana rere rika kololua, ela ri vavo; rero ridzikobolua, ridzienenda, Yesterday it was broken, but it was there; to-day it has been broken off, it is gone; ridzihalua, it has been taken.
  **Kolosa,** *v.a.* Kakolola-yuna-dzi-kolosa kasidi (= Yunapiga kolosi).
  **Kolosera,** *v.n.* and *a.* *See* Koma. To come true, to be fulfilled as a dream. Ku loha kuangu kudzikolosera. Nidzilo ha koma zangu zidzikolosera. Nidzilo ha usiku-vidzikolosera. Yudzikolosera mukuo wa babaye, ao kuira leu.
  **Korera.** *See* Bemba; Cherera.
  **Korerana.**
  **Korereka.**
  **Korerua,** *v.p.* *See* Lasima. Muiri udzi korerua ni moho, The body has been warmed by fire.
  **Kosa,** *v.a.*
  **Kosera.**
  **Koserua,** *v.p.*
  **Kosesa,** *v.*, to satiate.
  **Kesua.**
**Kola,** *n.* (ya, za), a very large snail. Lukombe kua kola. Nidzi-m-patika kola; or, unga wa kola. Nagogota lukombe lua kola, ni-m-lafie. Kola m'egnie, nipate lukombe lua ku engurira mafuha. Kombe za kola ndo ache asanazo miambo. Dim., Kakola and Kikola; magn., Rikola.
**Kolekole,** *n.* (wa).
**Kolia** (Kig.), *v.a.* Nidzi-m-kolia mufiu nidzi-m-dema (= fiula in Kir.). Yudzi-ni-kolia neno (= Yudzi-ri-avusa yudzi-ni-kofia neno). Kuna ku kolia kua maneno Kuna ku kolia kua mufiu. Der., Kolo; Kore; Kakalio; Koloa; Kololo; Kolosi: Koro.
**Kolo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Futika. Trunk, butt. (1) Kolo ra atu. *See* Lukolo. Kolorao yuere akiihua gnania musiku.
(2) Kolo ra muhi, The lower part of the trunk of a tree.
(3) Kolo ra lukuni. Kolo ra lurimi, The root of the tongue. *See* Lukuni. Kolo ra kuku. Atu anapiga mifungu, anadza kuria makolo. Dim., Kikolo.
**Koloa,** *n.* (Nondo in Kij.), a fabulous monster. Muezi udziguirua ni koloa (= Udziingira luhanduni, be ka-u-ala). Koloa richa muezi richa! Koloa richa muezi-richa! *See* Lumue.
**Kolokovue,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of crab, smaller than the kala. (1) Kolokovue ra poani, The kolokovue of the sea-shore. This is a little larger than the one on land. (2) Kolokovue ra ziani, or, ra ueruni, The land-crab.
**Kololo,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Luokue. A species of guinea-fowl, somewhat different in colour from the kanga, the specks being black and white, while those of the kanga are grey and white. There is also a difference in their voice.
**Kololo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), phlegm. Nidzikolola kololo; or, Nidzikolola nidzilafia kalolo.
**Koloma,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Nazi hi ni koloma, ni vevi na ku kala pfu; ni pfu ela ka-i-ka dimisa to, ichari koloma.
**Kolonde** (Kid.), *n.*
**Kolongo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Kolongo ra madzi.

## [PDF Page 203 — Dictionary Page 190 (Kol — Kom)]

**Kolosi,** or **Kolozi,** *n.*, a cough. Ku piga kolozi, To announce one's self by a short cough.
**Kolovondo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of tree. Misiye ikadororeka, ikamuta dzi.
**Koma, Goma,** *v.n.* *See* Toka. (1) To stop, to put an end to. W'enda koma vi? Udzirima hata udzigoma vi? Resp., Nidzirima hata nidzigoma mbabayuni.
(2) Goma hiwe, basi udzi-m-lavisa, The person spoken to will reply, Udzi-ni-asira ni we hata ukiamba nigome? Resp., Be ukigomesua unani-undahendadze? Si utu o, na ukome, No business that; and let it cease, let me have done with it. Der., Koma; Komo.
  **Komakoma,** *v. reit.* *See* Mulungu.
  **Komana, Gomana.** Hudzigomana vatu vasiku.
  **Kome, Gome.** Nidziona dziwe bomu, rikahenda gome; rinaogofia; uki-ri-lola, wamba: rindagomoka, ndosa riihue gome.
  **Komera,** *v.a.* Yudzikomera muriango, ka-u-sunduka. Siidima ku fugula ikafungua na komero. Der., Komero; Koma; Komo; Komolo; Mukoma; Mukomu.
  **Komesa, Gomesa,** *v.a.* Gnombe idzi-ni-komesa hikuno, ikimala, idzi-ni-udza kandahino. Narima hata ni komese hivara.
  **Komia.**
  **Komia, Gomia.** *See* Kilongo. Maneno higa gana-ni-gomia, siidima ku-ga-alamula hata rikigomba, ka-ga-erekeseka. Usiku wa Duruma ka-u-komia kucha. Kifiu ki-si-cho na mola, ka-ki-komia ku angamika.
  **Komiera.**
  **Komiera,** *v.a.* (= Komera). Yudzikomiera komero.
  **Komiero,** *n.* Nidzifunga niumba yangu na komiero, ela mutu yudzikudza-i-sundula; Niani? Usa, or, Upusa komiero usundule niumba. Muriangowe una komiero.
  **Komoka, Gomoka,** *v.n.* (= Bamfuka; Meguka). *See* Koka. Tahi sinagomoka ku bua.
  **Komola,** *v.a.*, to make a hole as with a chisel, to mortise. Muvini ni ku komola. Nakomola muvini wangu, nibume jembe, I perforate my handle that I may put the hoe into it. Nidzikomola muvini wangu hata nidzi-u-humbula, or, hata udzihumbuka. Kikomolo cha ku komborera! Ku komulua na komola. Not to be confounded with Gomola, To demolish. Der., Komolo.
  **Komolua.** Ku komolua na komolo.
  **Komorera,** *v. rel.*, to make a hole, etc., to, for, with. Uka-ni-komorere muvini wangu, nidze, nikotere jembe rangu. Ni-pa komolo ya ku komorera muvini wangu.
**Koma,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). *See* Yuyi. The name of a species of spider. Only such as spin webs.
**Koma,** *n.* (wa and ya, pl. *id.*, a and za). *See* Roda; Lubueka; Kola; Riveho; Mukoma. An evil spirit, supposed to be of some dead person. The chief idea of religion among the Wanyika seems to be to appease the koma. From Ku koma. Ku na koma atu kumi na vilolo. Kigulu kidziguirua ni koma. Chala changu kidziguirua ni koma. Koma sa dzaweye sidzi-m-guira kuamba akale muganga. Koma ya kuche na ya ku lume. Koma analosa, or, zinalosa. Komaye inakolosera mutu hiye; akiloha: mutu yudzefua, be yundafua keri. Gnania yuna koma, yudzilo sa; ko-

*Footer: 190*

---

## [PDF Page 204 — Dictionary Page 191 (Kom — Kon)]

  ma adziamba: ni usiku ni ugala; atu akapiga chamo. Nidzidzo la koma; huhende usiku, huhende ugala. Angue: Atu adzeria wari; nako ni kadonge ka koma adzako megurirua hivo njirani. Ni kitu chani hicho? ni kitu cha koma. Muna lufunsu muno. Ni dzere rani ro muhehera ro? Ko kadzere ka koma ndo muhehera ko?
**Komba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Ndzo, ni-ku-kamurire komba, ni-ku-nagnanise. Dzasi yangu ina makomba.
**Komba** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku dzuna in Kir.). Halani yo niungu, mukombe, basi mu-i-bume madzi, mu-i-dzukudze. Hala lo kibiga, ukombe. Hala-lo luvasi, ukombe. Ku komba minazo ka mutu.
  **Komberua,** *v.p.* Minasi yangu rero idzikomberua.
  **Kombola,** *v.a.*, to ransom, to redeem. Hala mufiu hiu, ukale na-o, machero nadza ni-u-kombole. Ku kombola kifoche.
  **Komborera.**
**Komba,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Kindi. A species of squirrel. Ndeye akobolaye minazi, akaria dzira. Komba yudzikobola kibariachangu. Komba huya yunadukanisa makue.
**Kombam'iko,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a species of beetle.
**Kombe,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lukombe. From Komba. Kombe za kola. Kombe za ngulu.
**Kombe,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (in Kid., Kombe ra kola; in Kir., Lukombe lua kola). *See* Karama. Dim., Kakombe; Kikombe.
**Kombesi,** *n.* (ra and ya), a ransom; (K.) lucifer. Mufuuhawe ni tondo.
**Kombo,** *adj.* From Ku komba. Muhi hiu u-kombo. Mihi hio i-kombo. Mutu hiyu yu-kombo. 'Atu hia a-kombo. Kitu hiki ki-kombo. Vitu hivi vi-kombo. Maneno higa ga-kombo.
  **Kombokombo.**
**Kombora** (Kij.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a canon-ball. Saidi avokudza piga Kisiwa, wakudza na misinga ya makombora. Msinga wa makombora ni mui ukibigua, be kombora rikibua dzi mutu akilonda kuenda-riguira-basi rika uduka. Nika-m-funusira dzedze za polopolo.
**Kome.**
**Komo,** *n.* (ya, za), a new piece put in the kino, mortar to repair it. Yudzibuma komo kinu kikacho humbulua ni ludzoa, kura tu hakoni. Kinu kikabumua komo, kidziuya kisima.
**Komolo,** *n.* (ya, za), a chisel. From Ku komola. Komolo ya ku komorera muvini, wa kidzoka, etc. Dim., Kakomolo; Kikomolo.
**Komu,** *adj.* (rel. to the infin. Ku). (1) Hard. From Ku kaomu. Kumania kuamba ni komu we, ka-ku-dzimpika.
(2) (rel. to the ra class), fully ripe, full-grown. From Ku koma, komala. Renge komu; pl. Marenge makomu. Der., Kombo.
**Konche,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the bark of a fibrous shrub or tree. The fibres are used to make string. Ku vuta unanasi, or, makonche.
**Konde,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Ngumi in Kij.), fist. Ku fimba konde, To close the hand, To clench the fist. Ku pigua makonde, To be struck by the fist. Atu ache anapigana makonde, ela alume anapigana mavi, hebu mbalahi. Ah! udzi-m-piga muyao konde, dza kuamba u muche! Kizo za konde.
**Kondo,** *n.*, strife, quarrel. Atu hia kondo yao ahehera-ni? Resp., Kondoyao ni ya kare angakala anainsana. Simania kondo zao.

*Footer: 191*

## [PDF Page 205 — Dictionary Page 192 (Kon — Kor)]

**Kondue,** *n.* (ra), slowness. Hiyu akienenda, yuna kondue, kasignia.
**Konga,** *v.n.* *See* Koba. To become old and feeble. Mutu hiyu yudzikonga (= yudzikala mufiere). Mutu iye yudzikonga; yukala mufiere hata yudzikonga. Der., Kongo; Tongo; Ukongo.
**Kongo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Ukongo; Dzupisha. A severe illness. Yudziguirua ni kongo ra kuafula. Yudziguirua ni ukongo, wa-mu-ansa kare, be vino ridzikala kongo, ka-ri-ndabonia, or, difia; or, Kandakodzoka.
**Kongo,** *adj.*, sick, bad. Jembe hiri ni kongo (= ni rofu), ka-ri-rira muangala. Gnombe kongo, A sick cow. Mbuzi kongo, A sick goat. Iyo gnombe ikikala ni kongo? ela inarisa hebudze? Is that cow sick? does she graze or not? Ndani ye ni kongo, His stomach is sick.
**Kongo,** *n.* (za). *See* Dzangira. Pl. of Ukongo. Yuna kongo za firangi. Kongo! andaye-ni-lola na dzidzo ri, na-afue.
**Kongolo,** *n.* (ya, za), a cocoa-nut tree when very high. Ni kongolo ya munazi hira, ikachira iyae yosi. Vana kongolo za minazi e! Ai! Munazi ni kongolo hiu, ka-u-kuereka, ni mure muno. Dim., Kakongolo; Kikongolo. N.B.—The diminutives in this instance have the additional meaning of oldness and decay.
**Kongoni,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Mia; Asrefu. The name of an animal. Kongoni ana malo sana, maguluge ni mavudzu. Ndzagamba ya kongoni ikapita goma ra gnombe.
**Kongosa,** *n.*
**Kongue,** *n.* (ya, za). From Ku konga. Kongue ni gnimbo sa uira wa pepo. Ku ongola kongue. Kongue si ya Mulungu, ni ya Musuka, ku-mu-iha na mukono, ku-m-kuignira madzo. Muganga yunaongola pepo, akisikira, afurahiwe, akuere kidzoani, afuine, aseme utu alondao.
**Konia** (Kig.), *v.a.* (= Ku isha). *See* Ku koba; Kenga.
**Koniola,** *v.a.* *See* Kikansi. To break off, to gather. Ku koniola madzere, To break off the ears of Indian corn.
  **Konioka.** Nafunsa lukuni, ludzikonioka.
  **Koniokera,** *v. rel.* *See* Mufu. Madzere gadziuma, gadzikala mafu hata gadzikoniokera.
**Konsi,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kofi. A closed handful.
**Konze,** or **Kondze** (contracted from Ko-ndze), *adv.* *See* Upusira. Out there.
**Kopoka,** *v.n.* Udzi-ni-fioga, hata kikonde kidzikopoka.
  **Kopokera,** *v.d.* and *instr.* (= Kopukira). Ndiye a ye ni koporera.
**Kopola,** *v.a.* *See* Kuada. Mutu uki-m-fioga uki-m-gaula udzi-m-kopola kikonde.
  **Kopolakopola.** Nazi gana kopolakopola hivi pia.
**Kore,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), retaliation. Kore ni mutu ayeulagua akarivua atu airi, muche na mulume, musichana na mudana; mumenga ni hiye nduguye ayeulagua; hiye wa viri ni kana kifurifuri cha huya ayeulagua. Na alafiwao si asunie, ni anafiale a lukolo luao lua vevi, lua iye ayeulaga mutu. Ni-ku-ve kore, ela husihehe. Muhi hiu ukahalua kore, udzikuenda mera kisiki ni mua muyawe, cha muhi mufu, ka-u-kamera m'egnie mudzangani.
**Koro,** *adv.*, quite, thoroughly, completely. Amasai akudza

*Footer: 192*

## [PDF Page 206 — Dictionary Page 193 (Kor — Kos)]

  hala gnombe sosi, koro, pia, or, korokoro, kasasire.
**Koro,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Madama. The cavity made by white ants for their nests. Makoro ga madama (= in Kij., Mashimo ya mtoa). Unaria muno dza koro—a proverbial expression, meant as a reproof for one who eats greedily (the koro being never filled with water, rain it never so much). Dim., Kakoro; Kikoro.
**Koro,** *n.* (za), anger, wrath. From Ku kola. Korose ni mbi. Gnania yuna koro, ela kana koro mbi, moyowe una mbasi.
**Korobesa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Goma. The male of a domestic animal when very old. Nidziona korobesa ra mbuzi; ra gnombe, etc.
**Korokodo** (?).
**Korokoro,** *adv.* *See* Makundi. Utterly.
**Korokoro,** *n.* (= Kolokolo in Kij.), a turkey.
**Koroma** (Kid.) (= Koloma in Kir.).
**Kororo.** Jembe ramba kokoro.
**Kosa,** *v.a.* *See* Kola.
**Kosa,** *v.n.* *See* Dzolosera; Karama. To err, to fail, to miss, to offend, to commit a fault or an error, wrong, trespass, mistake. Ku kosa mjira, To mistake the way; to lose one's way. Kaka-m-lenga to, yudzi-m-kosa. Mutu hiye yunaerekesa to, kakosa akidzanga. Der., Koso; Makosa; Mukosi.
  **Kosana,** or **Kosania,** *v. reit.* Hivo kare-mutu akikosania na muyawe, akadzoniola mufiu tu, akaambua ni mukosa mubomu, akariwa malu, mbusi airi.
  **Koseka,** *v.n.*, (K.) to be defective.
  **Kosera.** Gnania yunaerekesa maneno-ela rero yudzi-ni-kosera maneno. Hudzionana vevi na vevi, ela nidzi-m-kosera Mulunguwe. *See* Poniera in Kins.
  **Kosesa, Koseza.**
  **Kosezia,** *v.a.*, to make err, to cause to go wrong. Singakosa, ela gnania ndiye adzeye-ni-kosezia. Niamala, usi-m-koseze muyao maneno. Asi gombe mumidzi, yunda koseza maneno. Der., Koso; Makosa; Mukosi.
**Kosa,** *n.*, a mistake, an error. From Ku kosa. Una kosa. Ni'nende nikalafie kosa. Yudzikosa, basi hudzi-mu-ria kosa.
**Kosi, 1,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name of a species of bird. Yunga mlamba, madzoge ni madune do-do-do; akala angi, kundi dza dzongo. Kosi hia adzeria mababayu gangu.
**Kosi, Kozi, 2,** *n.* (ya, za), a watch-guard. Kudzikuesa kozi kare kavana utu. Yukuenda ku kuesa kozi. Nakuera kozini. Yukuenda kala kozi ya kulorera ueru, viha vindavo kudzira. Aravai akaika kozi yao, ku lola atu akidza, apige kululu, be atu aramuke. Rero kozi ni yakue; yukuenda kozini, or, yukuenda sagala kozi. Kozi idziikua hangu chiramuko. Kozi zikaikua kare, atu akuko. Muchena kozini. Atu ak'enda mundani sodi aike kozi. Hata niani ni ku ika kozi naye. Maniani kaenenda ku dzuma mundani azivo ika kozi.
**Kosi, Kozi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of large vulture. Kozi na ndzui karia kitu cha ku fua, ela mue na luvanga.
**Kosi,** *adj.* (rel. to ka and ku), all.
**Kosikosi,** *adv.* *See* Ludzengo. Every. Madzi gadziidzala muhoni kosikosi, kavana vatu va ku vukira. Kiluma kuiri kiluma kosikosi. Fumo rinaria kosikosi.
**Kosikosi,** *adj.*, two-edged. Mifiu yosi ya kuehu ina maso kosikosi.

## [PDF Page 207 — Dictionary Page 194 (Kos — Kua)]

**Koso,** *n.* (ra). Mutu akikosa koso tite, muambe munga-mu-ulagira mbuzi; haya mkihenda vio, kamu-dzi-angamiza vio, basi si ku reradzi hiko.
**Kota,** *v.a.* *See* Udauda. To knock, to stretch, to notch, to ascend. Nakota viguso via uriri. Ku kota luanda; ndo ku ansa ku rima, ukaricha niasi, sikaosera mumo. *See* Fumbula. Ku kota chingo, To stretch out a skin for drying. Ku kota mavalu, To cut notches into spars or rafters. *See* Valu. Nakota mavalu, niane niumba yangu. Ku kota murima, To ascend a mountain. Sudi muume kigulu, mu'endakota murima. Ku kota mutu gogoni, To put one into the stocks. Ku kotua pingu, To be struck into fetters. Yu fungua, yukotua gogo. Peho idzi-ni-kota. Lufundo ludzi-ni-kota pulani. Ku kota kululu (= Ku piga kululu). Ku-dzi-kota uchi. *See* Bu.
  **Kotua,** *v.p.* Gnania aka fungua kisiwani akagotua pingu na makatale.
  **Kotakota,** *v. reit.* (= Kokota), to keep knocking, to continue to knock. Yukotakota-ni ye? Whatever is he knocking at?
  **Kotera,** *v. rel.*, to knock into, to drive in by knocking. Nakotera jembe rangu; kifiuchangu, into a handle.
  **Koterera,** *v.d.* Nikavirike jembe kua gnania, a-ni-koterere.
**Kotoe,** *n.* (ya, za).
**Kotola,** *n.* (= Kikoko).
**Kotola,** *v.n.*, to be greedy.
**Kove,** *n.* (za), the eyelashes. Pl. of Lukove. Kove za dzulu, The upper eyelashes. Kove za dzini, The lower eyelashes.
**Ku,** (1) *a particle*, denoting the infin. to. Ku toha kuangu. When Kudza and Kuenda are followed by an infin., the *Ku* of the second infin. is not expressed. Ni kudza angirua, One is come to be possessed, bewitched. Na kudza loza, I came to bewitch.
(2) *pron.* (acc. of Uwe), thee. Hiku kukere kudzanga ukipiga pondiso hata dzulu umironi angue, munazi undafua.
**Kua,** *prep.*, by, at, on account of, after. Nila mundani kua gnania. Kua sababu, Because. Ku lala madzo madzo kua ukongo, To lie awake on account of sickness. Kulala madzo madzo kua ku luarisa mukongo, To lie awake to, in order to, nurse a sick person.
**Kua, Kukua,** *v.n.* *See* Pingi; Kue; Machira; Mbiriri. Ni rinda vava, hata kipindi cha dzua ku dzua; si-dza-kudza, basi ukue ukienenda. Nakua ni tenda, for Nikienda. Yunakua atenda. Hunakua hutenda. Anakua atenda. Kua utenda na mi nadza; pl. Kua mutenda na-mi nadza. Nakua nitenda, nika kua rinde mbere. Yunakua tenda, a-ku-fuhe magulu.
  **Kuakuala.**
  **Kuakuasa.**
  **Kuavia.**
**Kua,** *v.a.*
  **Kuika,** *v.n.*
  **Kuira,** *v. rel.* *See* Kolosera. To carry with.
**Kuachira,** *v.a.*, to catch with the mouth. Of birds of prey the word Niaka is used. Nidzikuachira madzere kanoa nahafuna.
  **Kuacha.**
  **Kuachirika,** *v.n.* Kuhega mangi, kuani-ka-vi-ndakuachirika.
  **Kuachisa,** *v.a.* *See* Kidosi.
  **Kuachisana,** *v. reit.*
**Kuachula,** *v.a.* *See* Wira; Kuatula? To give a private sign by a nudge.
  **Kuachulana,** *v. reit.*
  **Kuachurira,** *v.d.* Udzi-ni-kuachurira-ni?
**Kuada, Kuacha,** *v.a.* *See* Mfara;

## [PDF Page 208 — Dictionary Page 195 (Kua — Kua)]

  Kuada. To scratch. Ah dzitu hiri yudzi-ni-kuada mikombe vadzila miladzo yudzi-ni-kopola; yudzi-ni-kuada mikombe dza dzimba. Yuna-dzi-kuada (= Yuna-dzi-kuna viomu), He scratches himself violently.
**Kuada, Kuacha,** *n.* (ra, pl. Makuada, Makuacha), a hoof. Kuacha ra nsoya rikaguirana-ni menga. Niama a makuacha, Hoofed animals, in contradistinction to Niama a mafumba.
**Kua-dza.** *See* Dza.
**Kua-dze.**
**Kuadzika,** *v.a.*, to hang up.
  **Kuadzikika,** *v.n.*, to admit of hanging up.
  **Kuadzikira,** *v. rel.* Kavana vatu va ku kuadzikira.
**Kuafulo,** *n.*, something sudden. Ukongo wa kuafulo (= Ukongo wa fudi), A sudden illness.
**Kuafumira,** *v.a.* (= Dzagamira), to fall upon, to bounce upon in order to catch.
**Kuaju,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the fruit of the tamarind tree. Ku fuma kua kue; or, Ku fumakue ku foroforo.
**Kuako,** *pron.*, thee, thine, at thine, thy home.
**Kuakua,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the fruit of the mukuakua.
**Kua-kue,** *pron.*, his, at his home.
**Kuala,** *v.n.* and *a.*, to stumble; to stumble at or over. Udzikuala-ni? What did you stumble at? Resp., Nidzikuala kisiki, or, iwe, or, musi, etc. Mania usa-ni-kuala. Enenda to, usa-ni-kuala kuani kuna kisa.
  **Kualana.** Munakualana kamuenenda to!
  **Kuasa, Kuaza,** *v.a.*, to make stumble, to injure. Only used of the teeth. Muniu hiu unakuasa una midzanga. Wari hiu una midzanga unakuasa.
  **Kuasua, Kuazua,** *v.p.* Nidzhafuna wari nidzikuasua.
**Kuama,** *v.n.* (= Ku angama; Ku sikua), to stick fast; to lodge in, between, from being caught by anything. Muiya wa sui udzi-ni-kuama mumironi (= udzi-ni-kola). Yudzebua, ela yudzikuama (= yudzisekua), kakabuadzi.
**Kuamba,** *n.* *See* Ka; Kiwiyiwiyi; Muadza. War-music.
**Kuamba,** *conj.*, although, as if, notwithstanding. Kuamba si ludivio lua Yesus, hungari mumo kidiani, ela iye yudzihu lavia kidiani.
**Kuangu,** *pron.* and *adv.*, by me, to me; by mine, to mine.
**Kuangula, 1,** *n.* (ra), a cutaneous disease. Uvere wa kuangula, ka-u-vola haraka.
**Kuangula, 2,** *v.a.* *See* Dasa. (1) To take off. Only said of the upper crust of wari, etc.
(2) To scrape out.
  **Kuangurika,** *v.n.* Niungu hi ka-i-kuangurika ikaumalala, ka-i-na madzi makoko gakauma. *See* Pfuhupfu.
  **Kuangurira,** *v.d.* and *instr.* *See* Koko. Na fuidza mboga-be ni-kuangurira niunguyangu, nidze nichite niungu, ni ivuise wari na mapema.
  **Kuangurirua,** *v.p.*
**Kuani,** *adv. interr.*, why? by what?
**Kuaniula,** *v.a.* (= Ganiula in Kid.), to graze, to touch or rub slightly in passing.
**Kuansa.** *See* Gniere. Kigodi ni mulumbi wa kuansa na kuisha Kigodi,—name of a Duruma man. Muifi wa kuansa na kuisha (= Mugorofi?).
**Kuao,** *pron.*, their, at theirs.
**Kuara,** *n.* (ra), a bird of prey. Niama idzionda, idzikala kanokano, basi ka-i-rika-ni kuara. Hudzichita kuara ra gnombe ya ku henda niulula, wala ka-i-rika kabisa.

## [PDF Page 209 — Dictionary Page 196 (Kua — Kue)]

**Kuari.** *See* Ku.
**Kuari, Kuere.** Ku dasana kuari ku dzadziga kubomu muasikira atu aadira na usiku dzana? Resp., Huasikira ela kuari kudari kilanga zulo, usiku wari kauzakula. Angodira kuari kudari, etc.? Kuari kudzikala kidani kidani kuare ku rira ku bomu.
**Kuarika** (Kir.).
**Kuaru, Kuala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Bogo; Dzitu), a giant, generally followed by Mulume. Vadzichira mutu hiva-ni kuaru ra mulume, There passed a man here—a giant of a man. Vadzichira makuaru ga alume, Giants of men passed by here.
**Kuarura,** *v.a.* *See* Kuaniula.
  **Kuarusa.**
**Kuasa,** *v.a.* *See* Kuala.
**Kuava,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) armpit.
(2) A wing. Kuava ra kuku, The wing of a fowl.
**Kuavare,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a kind of bat, said to be white, while the nundu is black.
**Kuba,** *v.a.*, to push to a door. Nidzi-u-kuba muriango, ela sikafunga. Kuba nuimba.
  **Kubira,** *v.d.* Ndzo, uka-ni-kubire niumba, kuku asiingire basi hudze, huenende.
  **Kubuka** (= Kukoboka?). Kibaria kidzi kubuka kidzisongera dzini, kidzisororeka kua uchi ku merera.
  **Kubula,** *v.a.*
**Kubali** (Kij.), *v.n.* *See* Umba; Kumia; Kenga; Kengeka. To receive, to accept of, to consent. Nidzi-mu-ambira neno, ela kakakubali, yudzi-ni-tharau, be vio kadzi-ri-ona?
**Kubiru,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of red bird.
**Kubo.** Kubo ni mifusi ya lagani. Gnania akamera kubo.
**Kuda, Kucha.** *See* Cha.
  **Kudida, Kuchicha,** instead of **Kukicha.** *See* Kuki.
**Kude, Kuche.** *See* Che.
**Kudida, Kuchicha.** *See* Kukicha.
**Kudu, Kuchu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a carrion-bird, with a bald head. Vidzoa viao ni vieruve, ka-vi-na mifusi, vi-nga dza kimfara.
**Ku-dza,** *v.* *See* Dza. To come. The Ku is retained in many tenses, as in Ku enda. When Kudza is followed by an infin., the Ku of the second verb is not expressed. *See* Ku.
  **Ku-dza, Kutsa** (= Kusa). *See* Ririkana; Lurauko. Kudza ulaga atu, To come to kill people. Yunadza ni piga, He came to beat me. Akuenda ona, They went to see.
**Kudze.**
  **Kudze-cha.** *See* Cha; Fudzirua.
  **Kudze-dzua.** *See* Dzua. Kusinda hata kudzedzua; ku lala hata kudzecha.
  **Kudze-fua.** *See* Fua.
**Kudzi.** *See* Dzuka; Rungurungu; Ingu; Uvia. Kudzecha kudzignala. Kudzifewa, kudzifuewa; lit. To have died; *i.e.* To have had somebody dying.
**Kudzo.** *See* Kirema.
**Kudzua.** *See* Dzua. Mdzana kudzua, The whole day; but, Usiku kucha, The whole night.
**Kue,** *n.* (ra, pl. Makue). *See* Komba. A branch with leaves. Tahi zi-ri-zo na makodza, zinaihua makue. Kuna zira tu si-ka-sokua makodza.
**Kue** (= Kuakue). Kusaga kue ku foroforo.
**Kuede,** *n.* (ra). Only used in connection with muambo. Kuede ra muambo; *i.e.* An uncommonly large muambo, *i.e.* made of larger pieces of the kola than is usual.
**Kuegnie.** *See* Gniegniesa.
**Kuehu,** *pron.*, ours, at ours, our home. Contracted from Kua

## [PDF Page 210 — Dictionary Page 197 (Kue — Kuk)]

  yehu. Ache hio askudza kuehu rero, kuao ni ku dawa.
**Kuekueru,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a species of wild dove. Yunga jia, ela jia ni mbomu punde.
**Kueli** (Kij.), *n.* (= Keri in Kir.). *See* Nganasa. The truth.
**Kuembe,** *n.* *See* Puembe.
**Kuenche** (Kid.), *n.* (= Donda in Kir.; Soo in Kins.), a large wound.
**Kuenda.** *See* Enda.
**Kuensi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of bird.
**Kuenu** (Kij.), *pron.* (= Kuehu). Contracted from Kua yenu.
**Kuera,** *v.n.*, to ascend, to climb, to mount. Makuera dzula ya muhi.
  **Kuerana.**
  **Kueraka,** *v.n.* *See* Kongolo. Mufune na muare ka-i-kuereka, inaheresa, wala kana tahi sa vevi, si kura tukure, dzulu.
  **Kuerera.** *See* Kikuesa. Kavana vatu va ku kuerera; ka-ri-kuereka dziwe hiri.
  **Kuerua,** *v.p.*
  **Kuesa, Kueza,** *v.a.*, to elevate, to raise, to hoist, to put up; (K.) elevate. Ku kuesa vibaria munazini, To put.
  **Kueseka.**
  **Kuesera.** Ni-pani vibaria nika-m-kuezere miansoye. *See* Muanso.
  **Kuesua, Kuezua,** *v.p.*
**Kuere.**
**Kueruve.** Kudzikala kueruve dze-dze-dze, kakuna ingu (= kudzi dzuka).
**Kufia,** *v.a.*, to remove. Ku-dzi-kufia (= Ku avuka kanda, ku visa muyao). Dzi-kufie, nichire. Kitu hiki ki-hufie kanda, ki-nchirani.
**Kufu,** *adj.* *See* Kinemi.
**Ku-fua.** *See* Fua.
**Kuga,** *v.a.* Atu adzi-ni fierera, adzi-ni-kuga, kana asiro-niamba; nidzifiererua hata nidzikugua. Ku kuga ni ku hadza maneno mai, hata ga aibu ya kare akagomba.
  **Kugana,** *v. reit.*
**Ku-hahu.**
**Kuhu,** *n.* From Ku kuhala. Yudzifunga kuhu kafioka kaviri. Hangu dzana nidzi funga kuhu nidziricha ku fioka.
**Kui,** *adj.*, bad.
**Kui** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kigota in Kir.; Kodo in Kij.), a knock with the knuckles. Ku-m-piga muanache kui.
**Kuidia,** *n.* (ya). Pl. of Lukuidia.
**Kuignia,** *v.n.* (= Ku guna, except that this is applied to a lower, and Ku kuignia to a somewhat higher, more decided sound), to utter a groan or growl by way of disapprobation; to utter a slight grunt; (K.) growl, maunder.
  **Kuiguira,** *v. rel.*, to groan or growl at, for. Wakuignira-ni? What do you grumble for? Resp., Nidzi-ku-kuignia uwe; maneno go udza go gomba, si-ga-hensi, ndosa nikukuignia.
**Kuira.** *See* Kua, *v.a.*
**Ku-iri.** Maneno higa ga kuiri, ga ku hahu.
**Kuiru, Guiru,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a greedy desire, for meat only; for other food, Moyo is used. Mutu yuna kuiru hiyu, yunahensa niama muno, kula vadzinsua-vo gnombe karicha kuenda. Osi airi ana makuiru, ela ra hiyu ridzisidi; atu ana makuiru hio na niama. Nina kuiru, nahamirua ni niama.
**Kuisha** (Kij.), *adv.* *See* Kuansa. Then.
**Kuka,** *v.n.* *See* Dzua; Nche. To be sleepy, to nod, to doze. Nakuka, n'enda nikalala, I am sleepy, I go to lie down.
  **Kukacha.** *See* Cho.
  **Kukadzua.**
**Ku-ka-ko.** *See* Musa. Kura tu kure-ku-ka-ko koma koma Mulungu.

## [PDF Page 211 — Dictionary Page 198 (Kuk — Kul)]

**Kuki,** *adv.* *See* Dzudzira; Londera; Ala. When it; if it. From infin. part. Ku and the conditional part. Ki. Machero kukicha, To-morrow when it dawns. *See* Cha. Kukidzua, or, Kukicha, At sunset. *See* Ku dzua. Kula kukicha akarauka kuenda mundani.
**Kuko,** *adv.* (= Huko in Kij.). *See* Kosi; Lunialu; Chengeva; Luarisa; Hanga; Ku-simu; Nukirua; Ko; Ngilingili. Thither; (K.) there. Andafika kuko kua Akamba, ela hikuno Ravai kandafika; anda-ni-ona-vi?
**Kuku,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), a fowl. Kukue, His fowls. Kukuwe, His fowl. Chiramuko kukuni, kakudza bambahuka.
**Kuku,** *adv.* *See* Nugnunika; Pindilo; Sindikira. Hither. Machira higo Amasai a-vo-kudza, ndo Muzungu a-vokala kuku. Kuku hulako, Where we come from; but Kuko huendako, Where we are going to.
**Kukudika** (Kig.) (= Ku dzedera and Ku kutika in Kir.).
**Kukudu,** *adj.*, dried up. Nidziona mutu yunadzedzera be ni kukudu kukudu. Madzi gadziuma kukudu.
**Kukuhala,** *v.n.* Kitu kidza cho uma sana, ndicho uambacho kidzikukuhala. Madzere higa gadzikukuhala, ka-ga-hafunika. Mihanda ya niama idzianikua hata idziuma hata idzihenda kukuhala. Unakukuhala kua peho, hata ukaoha moho, muiri ukafuguka. Der., Kuhu.
**Kukumuka,** *v.n.*, to titter; (K.) cackle, wamble. Yunadzekera ndani kaupusa ndo ku kukumuka. Yunakukumuka, yulonda ku dzeka.
**Kukusia,** or **Kukuzia** (Kid.), *n.*, the name of a bird.
**Kukuta,** *v.a.*, to shake out. Ku kukuta mifui muriakani.
  **Kukutika,** *v.n.* (= Deteleka and Fiukafiuka). *See* Regarega. To stagger, to reel.
**Kukurukukuru,** *n.* and *adv.*, the habit of strolling about in idleness. Yuna kukurukukuru. Rarely used, the common expression being, Yunadangadanga, He or she is strolling or wandering about.
**Kula,** *n.* (ya, za), tweezers. Often suspended from the neck. The natives use them to pluck the eyelashes for the sake of beauty. A missionary's wife once asked a native why he plucked his eyelashes. He answered, pointing to her hair, "Your custom is to wear your hair like that, and it is my custom to pluck my eyelashes." The eyes look the reverse of pretty to our idea with the lashes plucked.—[ED.]
**Kula,** *adv.*, every. Kula m'menga, Every one. Kula vatu.
**Kula,** *v.n.* *See* Moro. (1) To grow.
(2) To pluck out. Only used of the eyelashes and the beard; of a hair of the head Ku futa is used. Ku kula kove, To pluck out the eyelashes. Una mikove, be kukulua? Thou hast large eyelashes, why are they not plucked? This is done for the sake of beauty. Ku kula kirefu, To pluck out the beard to prevent it growing. Der., Kulo; Kula; Kulukira; Mukululo.
**Kuluka** (Kidigo), *v.a.* (= Ku chakana in Kir., and Furunga), to stir in cooking, etc.
**Kulula,** *v.a.*, to rub off, to set a newly forged instrument; to wipe off, to carry off, as water does earth and sand. Nakulula kifiu changu, kidzila usanani hikara, I rub off, I set my knife, it has come from the smithy just now. Ku kulula mulala. Nadzaniula lukanolu-angu, nikulule, nisuke

## [PDF Page 212 — Dictionary Page 199 (Kul — Kum)]

  luvohe. Mudzanga udzikululua ni madzi.
  **Kulurira,** *v. rel.* N'enda nika-mu-ve gnania kifiu changu, a-ni-kulurire, ndiye akululaye to.
  **Kulusa,** *v.a.*, to wash off, to carry off, as running water does earth and sand. Madzi ni ku kulusa mudzanga (= kulula, when used in this connection).
  **Kulusira,** *v.d.* *See* Mukari. To make great to, to take or give the greater portion of anything. Mayo! udzi-m-kulusira muanao, ela suino udzi-huva katite katite.
**Kusa, Kuza,** *v.a.*, (1).
(2) *See* Moro. Trop., Muana hiyu yuna-ni-kuza moyo, ni muana arie na akili, akilagisua kazi, akahenda to, akadimiza.
**Kulo,** *n.* (pl. Ma-). Kuku yunalonda kulo kuansa. Kuku airi asegere makuloni, anadieka. Kuku yudziingira kuloni, yuna karira.
**Kulo,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the gnu (?).
**Kulu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya or ra class), great, large. Neno kulu, The chief word of Kikulu, Mukulu, Akulu, Mikulu, etc. (= Bomu). Raso kulu.
**Kulukira,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the road made by the traffic of cattle. Ni nchira ya ameitha na ya gnombe. Kulukira ra Mulungu, The cattle-way of heaven, *i.e.* the Milky Way. Ameitha avesa kare kuenda damfa gnombe, njira idzififira. Ikignala sana, basi ni ku ambua: Ameitha adzikuenda damfa gnombe.
**Kuluku.**
**Kulukulu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of bird.
**Kulukulusinge,** or **Kulukuzinge,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name of a species of worm. Kulukuluzinge ni adudu ahambalao, ana ndzorandzora, kama lunioga lua kanga; lit. Are worms which creep, they have spots like the feather of a guinea-fowl. Mihi ariayo muno, ni munafu na mahua na logadzi.
**Kulula,** *v.a.* *See* Kula.
**Kululu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kozi. Outcry, alarm, noise. Ku piga kululu, To make a noise. Yunapiga kululu yunarira. Una kululu muno, gomba porepore.
**Kulume.** *See* Lume.
**Kulungana** (?). Idzi-m-kulungana iki-m-gafika humo ndani.
**Kulungire,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Waka. The wood of the heart of the ebony tree, and of the muthungu. Moyo wa muvingo na wa muthungu ni ku ihua kulungire.
**Kulungu,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), (K.) deer, antelope.
**Kuluvira,** *v.a.* Na-mu-kuluvira iye yunda-ni-pa. Nidzi-m-kuluvira iye-yukuenda ni badira. Na-ki-kuluvira kitu hicho.
  **Kuluvirana,** *v. reit.* Atu hio anakuluvirana mumenga akidzoekua, ak'enda kua muyawe-ni ku hewa.
  **Kuluvirika,** *v.n.* Kakuluvirika mutu hiye.
  **Kuluvisa,** *v.a.* Mutu hiyu akakuluvisa moyowe, hata akichira munaria kitu vivi-iye ni ku chira tu na ku enenda; kana moyo hura wa ku londa. Kuna cha ku gurira, udzi kuluvisa nduguyo, be uka-ni-harira-ni we? singari nidzikuenda gusa kungine? Kuna kitu-una-m-kuluvisa mutu, be vidze vio?
  **Kuluvuka,** *v.n.* Ni hira miaso, ikisa ingira mura moyoni, ndo ku kuluvuka. Hamadi kakuluvu kire, yudziasa niuma, yudziuya.
**Kuma,** *v.n.*, to appear great.

## [PDF Page 213 — Dictionary Page 200 (Kum — Kum)]

  Gnania yudzifuala nguo bomu, be yudzikuma. Nguo idzi-mu-agira yudzikuma. Dzinare rikakuma. Der., Nkuma.
  **Kumia,** *v.a.* *See* Kigumba; Dzumbe. To make appear great, to magnify, to exaggerate. Yudzifuala nguo bomu, idzi-m-kumia (= ina-mu-ika mbomu). Gnania yunakumia maneno muno hata akigomba sikubali.
  **Kumisa, Kumiza,** *v.a.* *See* Lurero.
  **Kumiwa,** *v.p.*
**Kumba,** *conj.* *See* Mufu; Kidambo; Kofule. *See instances at* Bembere; Hadaya; Duria; Uchirira; Ririra (of Ria). Angakana kumba ndeye, Whilst he denied it, after all it was he. Kumba vidzo viko, After all, good is in store for me; I did not expect it. Kitu changu kidzihalua; namba niani? kumba ndeye, Something belonging to me has been taken; I say (= I ask) who is it? and find it is he or she. Ah! nahensua kumba; nidzireherua muganga, kudza-ni-lagula. *See* the prov. by Gandeganche.
**Kumba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a fresh-water fish. Makumba gakala madzi ga peho. Dim., Kakumba and Kikomba; magn., Rikumba.
**Kumba,** *v.a.*, to make fall, to throw down accidentally.
  **Kumbira,** *v.d.* Vidzi-ni-kumbira kirengechangu, uchi udzimuagika, be unda-ni-riva uchi wangu; sika-ku-huma, kuamba umuage.
  **Kumbuka.** Yudzi-m-kumbuka mutu wa kare, ayekala na mbasi, na choyo wari kana; mimi si-mu-onere.
  **Kumbukira,** *v.n.*, to remember.
  **Kumbukirua,** *v.p.*, to be remembered. Ndugu yehu ayegusua, waonewa, wa kumbukirua ni gnania.
  **Kumbukisa, Kumbukiza,** *v.a.*, to remind. Nari nidziniala, ela uwe udzi-ni-kumbukisa, na mime nidzi-kumbukira.
  **Kumbukisania,** *v. reit.*, to remember one another. Ana kumbukisania madeni.
  **Kumbukisua,** *v.p.*, to be remembered.
  **Kumbusha,** *v.a.*, to remind. Dzana na-ku-va kitu kuehu, ela uwe, chako ku-ni-pa? Resp., Na-we basi uhenda-ni-kumbusha (= una-ni-sumburira) ndiwe u-ni-reraye? Sa-ku-va-vio? be ni-riva kitu changu na-cho-ku-va. Der., Kumbi; Lukumbi; Kumbukumbu.
**Kumbaku,** *n.* (ya) (= Tumbaku). *See* Muisu. Tobacco.
**Kumbi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Lukansa; Mukoma. (1) The bough of a palm tree. From Ku kumba. Kumbi ra munazi. Dim, Kakumbi and Kikumbi; magn., Rikumbi.
(2) The husk of a cocoa-nut when stripped off. *See* Makanda. Kumbi ra nazi; pl. Makumbi ga nazi. Hala hiro kumbi, ukaharire moho. Fula, u-ni-pe go makumbi, nikabume mohoni, sina kuni.
**Kumbi,** *n.* (za), (1) the place of the eyebrows. Pl. of Lukumbi. From Ku kumba.
(2) The hair which forms the eyebrows. Kumbi sa madzo.
(3) The edges of the eyelids and the lower edges. *See* Lukumbi.
**Kumbikumbi,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), white ants when winged. Ni dzoa akikala anafuka. Ndo ariwao.
**Kumbukumbu,** *n.* (ya, za). Kumbukumbu viari-dze fio? Muansowe vidziansa dze? Kumbukumbuye idziansa dze? Hudzikala na kumbukumbu za ku sumurira.

**Kumbundua.** Ku kumbundua (= Ku pigua).
**Kumenga,** *adj.* Ku fumula na ku dzamula ni kumenga.
**Kumi,** *adj.*, ten.
**Kumi,** *n.* (ra). *See* Lumfia.
**Kumia,** *n.*, exaggeration. Neno ra ku kumia. Maneno ga ku kumia, The language of exaggeration.
**Kumisa, Kumiza,** *v.a.*, to count ten, to complete ten. Nidzidara hata nidzikumiza kumi (= nidzitimiza kumi). M'esi wa kumi ukikumisua yuere ka dza fiala.
**Kumo.**
**Kuna,** *v. aux.* *See* Wangu; Ala. Lit. to be with. Kunacha. Kunadzua. H'endeni ge! kunadzua. Kunahenda mamba kundu. Kunahenda rungurungu; or, Kunakala rungurungu. Rero kuna kusi. Kunadza atu, There are people coming. *See* Nugnunika Kunapigua gunda, There is a horn blown. Kunarira gunda, There is a horn sounding. Kuna-ni ko? What is the matter there? Ka kuna atu aahewa amuri za Mulungu, ela Maya hodi heche yao.
**Kuna,** *v.a.*, to scrape, to scratch. Ku kuna sui, To scrape fish. Na kuna sui mamba. Ku kuna nazi, To scrape a cocoa-nut. Ku kuna chingo, To scrape a skin, or hide, Ku usa mifuzi. Ku kuna miyokue. Ninawawiwa hivo mongoni, basi ni-kuna.
  **Kunika,** *v.n.* *See* Dzumbi. Sinauka mbada nazizenu, ka-zi-kunika.
  **Kunira,** *v.d.*
  **Kuniuka,** *v.n.*
  **Kuniula,** *v.a.* (= Gaula; Gopola). *See* Fioga. To scrape open, to graze, to strip off skin slightly. Gnombe iki-ku-fioga, ka-i-na abudi ku-ku-kuniula kikonde.
  **Kuniulua,** *v.p.* Ku kuniulua ni mawe.
**Kunche,** *n.* (ra), fog, mist; (K.) vapour, dew, haze. Kudzihenda kunche, There is a fog, or mist. Kunche ridzigota dzi yosi. Kunche rinaansa hata ridzigota. Kunche rinadana dzua ridziupuka. Rero kuna kunche, when much; but when little it is Murenge, Mumbi, and Guro.
**Kunda.** *See* Musa.
**Kundagnansi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Vunsa. The name of a species of snake; lit. the lover of converse, because it is said to draw near where people are talking together. Atu akikala anasumurira, be iye na ku songera vevi ku sikisandosa aihue kundagnanzi. U kundagnansi we, unasikisa gnansi, atu akisumurira. Kidigo, Kundagnansi we, ufunsa mambea (= Kir., Unasikisa luambo).
**Kundani,** *n.* (ya, za), a charm. Ku henda kundani.
**Kunde,** *n.* (za), beans. Pl. of Lukunde. Madzi ga kunde, Bean-water — a brown colour, and thus used like an adj. Mutu hiyu yu madzi ga kunde, si muiru muno, na mudune, si mudune muno; yugesi dza arie mudune, ela si mudune muno. Kunde mbala. Kunde mbala dzafuere ni ku riwa na maruage ni ku riwa.
**Kundi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a flock, a herd, a flight, a swarm, a cluster, a bunch. Kundi ra gnombe, A herd of cattle. Kundi ra mbuzi, A flock of goats. Kundi ra niuni, A flight of birds. Kundi ra niuchi, A swarm of bees. Yudzibuma kundi ra pehe sikironi muakue, He, or she, has put a whole bunch of rings in his, or her, ear. Dim., Kakundi.
**Kundika,** *v.a.* *See* Kururusi. To

## [PDF Page 215 — Dictionary Page 202 (Kun — Kun)]

  make into a bunch or cluster, to herd, to swarm, etc. Nidzeria kitu kidzi-ni-kundika, umironi ka-ki-hensi ku chira. Nidzimisa niama, idzi-ni-kundika. Mukahe unakundika.
**Kundu** (Kid.), *adj.* (= Mudune in Kir.), red. Yu-kundu ko (= Kir., Yu-mudune cho), He is quite red.
**Ku-ndze,** *adv.* *See* Ngosangosa. Then.
**Kunga,** *v.a.*, to gather, as rain. Mfula idzikunga; lit. The rain has gathered (= has come). Mfula inakunga-inadza. Mfula idzikunga-inalonda kugnia. Der., Lukungo; Mukungo, pl. Kungo.
  **Kungana.**
  **Kungua** (?), *v.p.* Ku kungua moho.
  **Kunguka.** Mufui udzikunguka (= udzigongoloka). Kisinde kidzikunguka (= kidziricha ku duena).
  **Kungukira.**
  **Kungula.** Minazi ka-i-kemua, ikarichua, or, ikakungulua.
  **Kungurira.** Minazi yangu idzefua lua mudzana, ela hivi na kungurira. Nidzigema lumenga, nidzikungurira, sikagema lua mudzana.
**Kungi,** *adj.* (rel. to the infin. Ku). *See* Dzupisa; Nkoera. Much.
**Kungina,** or **Kungine,** *adj.* *See* Dzua; Ngama. At one place or another.
**Kungo,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lukungo. Ahoho akikala naguira nioe, basi aamba, hudziguira kungo mbiri hebu tahu.
**Kungu, 1** (Kid. and Kij.), *n.* (Pungu in Kir.), the name of a species of bird.
**Kungu, 2,** *n.* (ya, za).
**Kungucha, Kimburu,** *v.a.* (= Ku himisa in Kij.), to urge, to *hasten*, to stimulate.
  **Kunguchana,** *v. reit.*, to urge or hasten each other. Kuamba kakakunguchana, kasiyao angori adzimala usiku, ela hifio adzimala na mdzana, dzua ri chariko.
  **Kunguchua,** *v.p.*, to be urged, hastened. Muana hiyu ni mukaha muno, hata akikunguchua ka henda kasi.
**Kunguma,** *n.* (ya, za), the fruit of the mukunguma.
**Kunguni,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), a bug.
**Kunguyu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the owl.
**Kuni,** *n.* (za), firewood. Pl. of Lukuni. Nidzikuenda yeya kuni, ni ka pigua ni niuni, nikakuenda dikisa ludahi ludzikomoka, ludzibua; be nikafunga nikatimiza hiha rangu ra kuni. Dim., Kakuni and Kikuni; magn., Chinga. N.B.—There exists no proper form for the magn. of Kuni, Chinga being used for it.
**Kunika.** *See* Kuna.
  **Kunira.** *See* Kuna.
  **Kuniuka.** *See* Kuna.
  **Kuniula.** *See* Kuna.
**Kuno.** *See* Hanga, *n.*; Malala; Makira; Sengera; Lasa. Kuno nikua kolo, kuno ni dza. *See* Lukuni.
**Kuno.**
**Kunoa.** *See* Noa. To drink.
**Kunsa, Kunza,** *v.a.* *See* Luveko; Vinda; Unga. To fold. Yudzi-dzi-kunza kua peho yupigua ni mfula yunadedema. Kimeri akakunza dzi, kavana mutu agombaye; osi bie anga dza asuniee, asunie-e, His slaves; the *e* is pron. poss.
  **Kunsakunsa, Kunzakunza,** *v. reit.* (= Ku ika vamenga), to put together, to gather. Ku yeya kuni. Nakunzakunza vikuni via vibamfu, or, via magome, I put firewood in bundles. Yudzi-vi-kunzakunza pia-yudzi-vi-hala.
  **Kunsika, Kunzika,** *v.n.*
  **Kunsira, Kunzira,** (K.) inwrap.

  Ku kunsira moho usaguira luandala, vitu vie vindadobera.
  **Kunsua, Kunzua,** *v.p.* Gnania akakunzua ni muchewe, kagomba kamare, ela mutu hiye kakafua e?
  **Kunsuka, Kunzuka,** *v.n.* I-kunsule yosi pia nguo i-kunsuke nilole.
  **Kunsula, Kunzula,** *v.a.* *See* Gumo. To unfold.
  **Kunsumana,** *v.n.* (= Ku umalala). Muiri udzi-ni-kunsumana, siwesa, Ukigolosa mukono, basi kano ka-zi-goloka to.
**Kunsa,** *n.* (ya, za). Fara, ra kunsa ni kasi. Kunsa chafio mara gnombe.
**Kunso,** *n.* (ra). Kunso hiri ulondaro ku-ni-kunsa, be karinda kufa.
**Kunsui,** *n.* (ya, za), the name of a bulbinous root eaten in famine. It is reduced to flour, soaked several times in water to extract the bitterness, and then made into soup or bread. The bitterness, if not properly extracted, causes dysentery, which may end fatally. The bulb also has the quality of destroying worms in wounds, and was found an excellent remedy for wounds in donkeys.
**Kunsuigala,** *n.*
**Kunukira,** *v.a.* The forms, Kunuka, etc., common to most verbs, do not exist. Yudzebua yudzikunukira (= Ku funamira moyo). Unakunukira-we unakuka.
**Kupula,** *v.a.*, to empty; (K.) effuse. Enda ukakupule dzalani. *See* Mifusi. Kupula dzuani! Empty it, pour it out, in the sun. Ku kupula madzi (= Ku muaga madzi), To pour out water. Mafuha kagadza, kupulua vatu (= kagadzalafiwa) gachari kirengeni. Yu kupula rua madzi.
**Kupuka,** *v.n.*, to come forth. Muiri wangu udzikupuka vidudusi kimbimbi, uvere firangi. Muangu mundani mudzikupuka p'ekue. P'ekue idzikupuka mundani ka-i-ndasira. Muhama wangu udzikupuka kavuni.
  **Kupukira,** *v.d.* Nidzi-m-kupukira (= nidzi-m-kopokera), nidzi-m-zola, hata nidzi-m-guira.
  **Kupukisira,** *v.d.*, to make turn, to drive to or towards. Yudzi-mu-kupukisira niuma, He has made him turn back to, towards those who were pursuing him behind. Hudzi-a-demera, huka-a-kupukisira kanda ya kuehu.
  **Kupukiza,** *v.a.*, to make come out, to turn out; trop., to cause to turn in a different direction, as one escaping, or assailants in battle. Ku kupukiza niuma (= Ku udza niuma), To make turn back. Demera, demera! u-mu-kupukise, auye niuma. Hudzi-a-demera, hudzi-a-kupukisa.
  **Kupukua,** *v.p.* Nidzikupukua ni uvere, firangi, ukambi, etc.
  **Kupurira.** Udzi-ni-kupurira unga wangu dzi. Udzi-ni-kupurira midzanga, or, madzi nini? Nidzi-kuhenda dze?
**Kupusa, Kupuza,** *v.a.*, to turn.
  **Kupuzira.**
**Kura.** *See* Hehera; Rogo; Fuguka; Mesa; Chignie; Kinemi.
  **Kuratu.** *See* Kuereka. Kuratu alala ko.
**Kura,** *v.a.* Gnania yudzifiola hata yudzikura. Yudzifiola, yudzihenda kura.
**Kura,** *adj.* (K.) solid, numb.
**Kure,** *adv.*, far.
  **Kurekure,** *adv.* *See* Manionioda; Daladala. Very far away. Ku mania kurekure.
**Ku-rere.** *See* Rere.
**Kuri,** *n.* (ya). *See* Gola. Kasi-

## [PDF Page 217 — Dictionary Page 204 (Kur — Kut)]

  kasi. The north-west monsoon.
**Kuri** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) one who is violent, overbearing, oppressive.
(2) In opposition to the word Muganga, it has the meaning of "arch" in its bad sense. Mutu hiye ni kuri, kunda-m-wesa. Atu hio ni makuri, ndio ariao atu. Muganga kuri, A chief magician or sorcerer. Though Muganga by itself always bears a good sense in the heathen mind, meaning a native doctor; when joined with Kuri, it implies a wicked, though superior, man.
**Kuria,** *v.a.*, to eat.
**Ku-ri-ko.** *See* Kidosi; Mudzovi.
**Kurisa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Chinchikiza in Kins. (?); Chindikisa; Kurisa?), to cause to eat, to lead to pasture.
**Kuro,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), a dog. Dzino ra kuro, An eye-tooth. The word is also used in contempt; they say, Atu adzikutana, hata wa kironda, hata kuro yu vavo, Men have assembled, even the one with a wound, with a bad leg, and even the dog is there. Dim., Kakuro; pl. Vikuro.
**Kuru,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Saruba), a species of antelope.
**Kuruda** (Kidigo), *v.a.*
  **Kurudika,** *v.n.* (= Dzedzera in Kir.), to halt, to limp.
**Kuruja** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (Hind.? Arab?), a score of bags, cloths, etc. Kuruja ya nguo (= Doti kumi na kumi = Yere ya nguo sa Lamale na mbaniani in Wanyika).
**Kururia,** *v.a.* (= Kulula kula). *See* Kisingihi.
  **Kururika,** *v.n.* Dzansu hiri ni bomu, ka-ri-kururika, ri-kateni vairi.
  **Kururira,** *v.d.* Gnania yunapiga cha be hukaihua kuenda ku-mu-kuru-*rira masansu*.
**Kururusi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), an extra large bullock. Kururusi ra gnombe. Ni ndzao idzayo kundika, or, idzayo idzala muiri sana.
**Kuruza,** *v.a.* (= Ku kulula), to scrape. Nidzi kuruza jembe.
**Kusa,** *v.a.* *See* Kula.
  **Kusania.** *See* Kula.
**Kusa** (Ku-dza). *See* Ririkana: Oneka. Kusa kudza. Kusa oneka, etc.
**Kusa,** *v.a.*, to touch.
**Kusi,** *n.* (ra), the south wind, the south-west monsoon. Kusi ridzilamuka-ra ku fusira muhama. Kakuna kusi rero-peho sihurire. Rero kuna kusi.
**Ku-si-ko,** *adv.*, to not where, *i.e.* there is not. Kusiko gnombe. Amasai kana ko kasi. Kariseni ko luandani, kusiko minda vevi, for Luanda, Ueru may be used in this instance.
**Kusiku,** *adj.* (rel. to the particle Ku), certain, some. Kutu kusiku, A certain place. *See* Makadi.
**Kuzimu,** *v.a.*, to place in the cold, the grave; hence to bury. Yudzefua, yudzizikua kuenda ku-zimu ko dzi; unda-mu-ona-vi kaviri naye yukuenda ku-simu. Niamala! hosi hundakuenda kuko kufua si kua mutu mumenga.
**Kuta,** *v.a.* *See* Vunga; Muniala; Mashuku; Londera. To shake off, to meet. Muhi hiu unakuta makodza, and merely, Muhi hiu udzi kuta. Mutu yunakuta muhama, A person shakes off Guinea-corn,—said of a little for immediate use; but in harvest-time it is Ku piga muhama. Hunakuta niama dzakani, a upuke. Ku kuta moho (= Ku busa moho), To blow the fire. Nidzeria wari hata udzi-ni-kuta (= nidziukuha). Ku kuta kidzeka. Nguo una-i-kuta fumbi. Hala nguo yangu, ni-kute fumbi. Ku-dze-kuta, To

## [PDF Page 218 — Dictionary Page 205 (Kut — Kwa)]

  take offence. Madzi gadzikuta hata kandakanda. Muana hiyu yuna-ni-kuta mashaka. Yukuenda kuta atu, adze, hunene maneno. Der., Kutu.
  **Kutakuta,** *v. reit.* Hudzi kutakuta ludzaya rero, madzere kamuna, gadzisira. Dzana muari rere nikikutakuta muriango mukisa amuka, muna usinsisi ui.
  **Kutana,** *v. reit.*, to assemble. Udzikutana na-ye i-vi? Udzi-mu-visa-vi?
  **Kutanira,** *v. rel.* Ndo adzovo kutanira, vavo, ku nena chuo hicho cha ku sola Akamba. Ndo utu a-dza-o kutanira kumba.
  **Kutia,** *v.a.* *See* Tia. To put, to place. Ku-dzi-kutia mashaka.
  **Kutika,** *v.n.* (= Bukudika or Vukuhika). Makodza ga muhi ni ku kutika, ku bua dzi. Maembe yadzi kutika, ga dele dzi. Manina gadzikntika, gadzifuhuka. Muhama wangu unakutika, osi udzi muagika dzi, but, Muvunga unavulurika.
  **Kutira.** N'ende, nika-ku-kutire atu, adze, uusue to. Muche yudzikuenda ku-ni-kutira utu. Ku-dze-kutira amba (= Ku-dzi-binikisa; or, Ku-dzi-finikira amba). Ku-dzi-kutira nguo (= Ku-dzi-finikira nguo).
**Kutuka,** *v.n.* *See* Dzumbi. Opp. to Hua. Udzidzukula-ni mo-mukobani? kuani-ukakutuka. Kivinda kikikala kivuvu, kikahua, ela kikibumua muhama, kikakutuka. Gnania ni mukongo, ndaniye ikakutuka; be ukongo uratu. Kaunda-m-difia.
  **Kutula,** *v.a.* Ku kutula kififiro. Yudzibuma kitu dzafu dele, yudzikutula madzafu, yunaria; madzafuge gadzikutuka. Gnania yuna-dzi-kutula fio (= ku-dzi-sifu), Gnania puffs himself up, he does. Kudzikutula; ku-dzi-ika shoha.
  **Kuturira,** *v.d.* Nidzikuenda kuakue, nidzi-m-lamusa, yudzilamusika, ela be yudzidzukirua, yudzi-ni-kuturira madzafu.
  **Kutusa,** *v.a.*, to drive out, to inflate. Yudzikutusa kififiro kidzikutuka. Nidzi-m-kutusa vevi niama hiye, kuamba nere nidzi-mu-ona, ninga-m-fumaga.
  **Kutusika,** *v.n.* Kififiro kidzihumbuka, be ka-ki-kutusika.
  **Kutusira,** *v.d.* Hala-u-ni-kutusire-kikutuke.
**Kutu,** *n.* (kua), place. Kutu kure, At a distance, a distant place. Kutu hiko, At that place, when not seen; go to that place. Huende kutu hiko. Kutu kusiku. *See* Fikirira; Loheka; Makadi. Amasai akisikira kutu kusiku kuna gnombe, basi ni ku henda charo ku pigana, ku-zi-hala.
**Kuva, 1,** *n.* (za), a fence. Pl. of Lukuva. Kuva za midzi.
**Kuva, 2,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Kuba in Kij.), a tick. Kuva si guirazo gnombe. Kuva ndizo zi-luma-zo mahombo ga gnombe gakafua, gakadza henda masia.
**Kuva, 3,** *n.* (ya, za), the fruit of the tree mukuva, eaten in time of famine. Kuva za muhi.
**Ku-via.** *See* Via. To beget, to bring forth.
**Kuviu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Ku-vo.** *See* Dzanche. Ku-vo, kuka darua.
**Kuwe,** or **Kuve,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a) (= Kuwe in Kij.). *See* Kisimba. An animal, said to burrow. Kana mujira muve. Yunga ndesi. The mfueresi is larger, has short legs and a large head.
**Kuyu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the fruit of the mukuyu.
**Kwanza,** *adj.* *See* Kuansa. First.

## [PDF Page 219 — Dictionary Page 206 (L — La)]

## L.

**L,** the twelfth letter of the alphabet, pronounced as in English.—[ED.]
**La, Laa,** *v.n.* *See* Vano; Golosa; Lukano. To go out, to come from, to come forth, to emanate, to issue. Madzi gana laa, The water goes out, the tide ebbs. U-lavi? Where do you come from? Na laa mundani, I come from the plantation. Madzosi gadzi-ni-laa. Mfukuhi sina-ui-laa; or, Nidzilaamfukuhi. Fig., Baha yangu idzilaa kitu ku ri ko yao ka-i-laire kitu. Mutu hiyu yudzi-ni-laa ndani. Hudzigafia kitu, basi gnania yudzilaa dzidzo-angue: adzagule kibomu. Ku laa nguma.
  **Lafia.** *See* Laiwa.
  **Lafia,** *v.a.* *See* Golosa. To take out, to hand out, to miscarry. *See* Romoria. Yudzilafia, She has miscarried. M-pigeni-mu-lafie ngufu, hu-m-funge vavo.
  **Lafika,** *v.n.* Kitu hiki kinalafika-ela kino ka-ki-lafika.
  **Lafira,** *v. rel.* *See* Oloha. Nidzikuenda londa kitu kuamba ni gule, ela yudzi-ni-lafira kitu ki, kakika-ni-fa. Yudzi-m-lafira muyawe dzansi (= Yudzi-m-pigira dzansi).
  **Lafirana,** *v. reit.* Analafirana mihumua akaaririane.
  **Lafirua,** *v.p.* Yudzilafirua dzansi ni gnania.
  **Lafiwa,** *v.p.* *See* Uganga. Vitu vidzafio lafiwa ni vingi. Ku lafiwa ndze uganga, To be taken out as to the art of healing; *i.e.* To be shown the herbs, roots, etc., used in medicine.
  **Laika,** *v.n.* Hudziamba hulae, ela ka-vi-laika, kudzifuewa.
  **Laira,** *v. rel.* *See* Muna ku-dzi-laira; Mudziva, with. To go out from, to, with. Munalaira-vi rero? Resp., Nalaa munda musiku. Uchi ni ungi udza-o-ni-laira rero kula nchira vo ndeo naihirua uchi.
  **Lairana,** *v.n.*, lit. to come out to with. Used of the water covering the food in a pot for boiling, and of a crack in a vessel going through to the other side. Nidzibuma madzi mbogani, gadzilairana (= gadzisiya mboga, or, madzere). Ubume madzi hata galairane. Kirenge kidziuduka kidzihendamuga, ela ka-u-ka lairana. Wino udzilairana kanda ya viri.
  **Laiwa,** *v.p.*, (1). *See* Kifulofulo; Muharara; Sosonga; Kigniesi. Gnania yudzi chegniua-yudzilaiwa ni miladzo, or, yudzila miladzo. Nidzilaiwa ni mfukuhi. Gnania ukigavia kitu, basi ni ku laiwa ni dzidzo; angue: ahale kibomu iye.
  (2) Machero kaku laiwa.
**Laula,** *v.a.* (= Kij., Aua), to trace, to see if seeds are springing up; (K.) to survey. Udzilaula mundani ni musima? Resp., Nidzilaula-ni muzima. Kulaula dzi uk'enda kua theri, ela iye aenendaye ku maniadzi, adze, apige wiha, be ndiye aambuaye: yukuenda thana dzi. *See* Thiana.
  **Laulana,** *v. reit.* Be mkisagala kuenu, musegere kamare kamu mania ku lamusa atu? Ge atu ni ku laulana, ukarmania muyao ni musima hebu ni mukongo. Be vino udzikudza kuhulamusa, si vidzo fio?
  **Laurira,** *v.d.* Na-m-laurira gnania mundawe.
  **Laurirua,** *v.p.* Nidzilagisa kuenda laurirua munda wangu.

*Footer: 206*

## [PDF Page 220 — Dictionary Page 207 (Lab — Lal)]

**Labuda** (Kij.), *adv.*, perhaps.
**Lacha,** *v.n.*, to leave, to abandon.
  **Lachira,** *v. rel.* Yudzilachira kasi.
  **Lachisa,** *v.c.* Wari, aki-m-kenga hata yudzi-m-lachiza. Yulacha basi, kalafia kaviri kitu. Muana hangu dzana yudzibara ndimua; babaye ndiye aye-m-lachiza, ku-m-funsia kula dziku. Ningakengua, ela gnania ndiye adzie-ni-lachiza.
**Ladia** (Kij.) (= Hala, Kir.).
**Lafia.** *See* La.
**Lafia,** *v.* *See* Lavia. To make swear.
**Lafuka.** *See* Lava.
  **Lafukisa.** *See* Lava.
**Laga,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kadi. (1) The chest, thorax. Nidzi-mu ona gnania, yuna muana lagani; or, Yudzi-mu-ika muana lagani, I have seen Gnania carrying a child in his arms; lit. on the chest. *See* Dzukula.
(2) Nidzihenda laga-nakolola.
**Laga,** *v.a.* *See* Munguana. (1) To take leave of.
(2) To agree for.
(3) To promise. Na hu lage mbatha ya ku uka, huenende, hukahambe. Mbatha a-yo-ni-laga, ka-i-dzafika. Unadzukula musigo wa gnania, udzihewa-ni? yudzi-ku-laga-ni? Resp., Yudzi-ni-laga kitu kisiku. Der., Ndagisua.
  **Lagana,** *v. reit.* *See* Mbatha. (1) To take leave of one another.
  (2) To agree, to make an agreement. Hudzilagana kitu kisiku, kuamba yundakudza a-ni-pe. Dzana hualagana na gnania kuamba n'ende kuakue; be ndiko n'endako.
  **Lagira.** Be u-ni-lagira ni we enenda du usi-ni-ambire.
  **Lagirua** (Kid.), *v.p.* *See* Vumbulukisa.
  **Lagisa,** *v.a.* *See* Uringo. To order, to give a charge; (K.) enjoin.
  **Lagisana** and **Lagisania,** *v. reit.*
  **Lagisira,** *v. rel.* U-m-lagisira-ni? Sina maneno ga ku lagisa.
  **Lagisua,** *v.p.* Gura tu adza-go-lagisua yudzi-ga-richa, akasa sema, akadua akili sa uchi tu.
  **Lagua,** *v.p.* Nidzilagua kitu kisiku, nindakudza nihewe.
**Lagula,** *v.a.*, (1) to doctor.
(2) To render invulnerable by charms. Ku lagula mutu mukongo. Ku lagula mutu kuamba asilogue, athime ayae. Ku lagula viera. *See* Huka.
  **Lagurika,** *v.n.*, (1) to admit of being doctored. Ukongo hura si ukongo wa ku difia-anabananga vitu viao ukongo hura ka-u-lagurika.
  (2) To prove well secured by charms. Gnania walagulua akilagurika yudzi solua ni Ameitha, ela yudzidia, kakaulagua. Atu akaamba ni hura uganga a-o-lagulua.
  **Lagulua,** *v.p.*, to be doctored, to be healed by charms. Ku lagulua ni Mulungu, To be healed by God.
  **Lagurira.** Muganga yudzi-ni-lagurira na mburuga, nidzionerua ni kiravo ni udzaini mufundoni koma, etc. Koma ya wawe, ya mameyo, etc.
  **Lagurirua,** *v.p.* Naenenda kua muganga-ni-kalagurirue a-ni-ambire ukongo u-m-lumisa-o.
**Laira.** *See* La.
**Laiwa.** *See* La.
**Laka,** *v.n.*, to be greedy, ravenous.
**Lakisa.** *See* Lacha.
**Lala,** *v.n.* *See* Madzomadzo; Moma. To lie, to rest horizontally. Kidzeka hiki kidzilala dzi hangu dzusi be ka-ki-ka riwa ni ludzoa hata? Na kinu una-ki-richa kilale vavo dzi, ka-ki-ndariwa ni ludzoa fio?

## [PDF Page 221 — Dictionary Page 208 (Lal — Lal)]

  Na kavu una-i-richa ilale vavo-dzi-indariwa ni ludzoa. N'enda nikalale; or, N'enda lala, I go to lie down. Nidzilala, ela sikavodzerua, nidzilala madzomadzo kua kunguni, I have lain down; or, I have been lying, but did not fall asleep; I have lain awake with the eyes open. Fig., Yuyu-lurimilue lunga ndzuga ka-lu-lala na ndzala, or, ka-lu-niamala.
  **Lalama,** *v.n.* and *a.* *See* Dada. To yield, to acknowledge guilt, to confess: the idea of the word being that of going down, letting one's self down. Alalamaye, moyowe ukasama, u-dzini, ela iye ambaye kalalama, moyowe u-dzulu aka-u-kuesa. Apigana hata anaona kanda-a-wesa, basi akilalama (imperf. tense). Adzipigana hata anaona kanda-a-wesa, be adzilalama (perf. tense). Yudzimigniua, yudzilalama, yudziamba: Ndzoni, mu-hu-da-nie. Gnania ni musinsi-wagnirua na mukasa mutu; wari akikana hata hivino yudziona, kondo ni niomu, yudzilalama. Neno hiri nidzi-ku-ambira uwe, ela sidade uka-ri-lalama, or, sidade uka-m-lalamira mutu.
  **Lalamira.** Gnania wa-ni-lalamira neno, kuamba ndeye adzayehenda hifio, aki-ni-kaga, kuamba nisilalamire mutu; be nidzi-ga-ona gadzikala mafioka.
  **Lalamirua,** *v.p.*, to be confessed to, to have a guilt confessed to one's self. Hualalamirua ni iye musena-o, hebu uwe ku-mu-ambirire we? Resp., Ah-chamba ndeye adzaye-mu-ambira, basi haya nindahe nda-dze-ni geri. Be ndo ku lalama, Well, this is to confess. Akalalamirua ndama ya gnombe, This relates to the kignole of the Wakamba.
  **Lalamisha,** *v.a.*, to make confess a guilt. Kangalalama, ela musenawe ndiye adzaye-mu-lalamisha. Yulalamishua, ela kalalama.
  **Lalana.**
  **Larika,** *v.n.* *See* Bochoreka; Madzula; Udulukiza. Ka-va-larika hiva kua dzungu ku kala angi, or, vana dzalafu. Ka-va-larika dzi, vana vibindo. Hiva ni vadzo-vanalarika.
  **Larikira,** *v. rel.*
  **Larira,** (1) *v. rel.* *See* Ekemesa; Lasema. Ku larira niama hebu aifi, To lie in ambush for animals or thieves, viz. watching,—the usual expression for a man sleeping on his plantation. Vika kala-dze? ngulue kudza ria munda, nawe u-mumo, udzikuenda lariravidze? *See* the answer by Iya. Chingo ya ku larira, A hide to lie on. A bullock's hide is one of the best beds in the Wanyika's estimation. *See* Mudzeka. Hivano ni vadzo, hata ukalala ka vana utu, ni ku-dzi larira.
  (2) *v.a.* Nina makasi mangi rero ni-si-go-ga-larira.
  **Larirana.** *See* Heteresua. Lola ahoho, adzilarirana magande.
  **Lasa, Laza,** *v.a.*, to make lie, to lay down, to put by. Kinu una-ki-laza vava dzi ka-ki-nda riwa ni ludzoa fio? N'enda nika-m-lase muana, hudze husumurire. Na laza uchi-nikiona thora nigule, I put by palm-wine; when I see a bargain, I will buy it with the palm-wine. Gnania yuna chiru muno, kalasa uchi. Fig., Ku laza lurimi na ndzala (Kid.); lit. To lay down the tongue with hunger, *i.e.* to keep silence. Gnania musiku kalasa lurimi na ndzala, He cannot keep silence. Sindalasa lurimi na ndzala, ninda gomba, I will not keep silence,

*Footer: 208*

---

## [PDF Page 222 — Dictionary Page 209 (Lal — Lan)]

  but I shall speak. Yuna-dzi-lasa, angue yurere, na kuno yu madzo, basi ahende lamusua; or, Yuna-dzi-lasa dza kuamba yurere, na kuno ku madzo, yudzi-dzi-lasa ku sikisa maneno.
  **Lasika,** *v.n.* Muana hiyu kalasika hecheye, sudi alale na mutu.
  **Lasira, Lazira,** *v.a.*, to put aside. Gnania musiku yuna-ni-ira, be na-m-lazira uchi, nidze, ni-m-rive. Na-m-lazira ndugu yangu uchi, ni-mu-avase.
  **Lasirua,** *v.p.*, to be put aside. Nidzilazirua uchi ni gnania, yudzikuenda ni pa, yudzi-ni-badira cha tahu, hebu cha kumi. Der., Kilariro; Malalo; Malele; Malazi.
**Lalikirua,** *v.p.* *See* Dzodza.
**Laliza** (Kig.), *v.a.*, to be hospitable to strangers. Ku wa liliza wegeni.
**Lalo,** *n.* (ra), a neighbourhood. Atu a laloni, People of the neighbourhood. Hu atu a lalo menga; kuani moho ukifua kuako, un'enda kua muyao ku hala moho.
**Lamba,** *v.a.*, to lick. Lamba usikise, chamba ki mdzuano. Prov., Mulamba niuchi, kalamba lumenga.
  **Lambika,** *v.n.* Ki-ri-cho uzungu, ka-ki-lambika lurimi lunadzodzota.
  **Lambua,** *v.p.*, to be licked. Niuchi hi ka-i-ka lambua lumenga, idzi kakaniua, idziriwa.
  **Lambualambua,** *v. reit.*, to be irritated, tickled. Said of the throat only, when accompanied by a cough. Umironi vanalambualambua.
**Lamfia,** or **Lamvia.** Mayo yuna-m-lamvia m'anawe uchi uidzi.
**Lamfiana, Lamviana,** *v. reit.* Ku lamfiana gnonsi.
**Lamuka,** *v.n.* *See* Kusi. To awake. Der., Chiramuko, Malamusi; Malamuso.
  **Lamukira,** *v. rel.* *See* Mbafu. Yudzilala, yudzilamukira mu'ndani kuenda rima; or, Yudzilala, yudzilamukira kuenda mundani.
  **Lamukirua,** *v.p.* Yudzilamukirua ni atu a-mu-isao.
  **Lamusa, Lamuza,** *v.a.*, (1) to awake, to arouse from sleep. Ku-m-lamusa mutu arereye ku vodzerua, or, arereye usinsisi.
  (2) To breakfast. Ku lamusa kanoa (= Ku fungula). Hangu chiramuko si-dza-lamusa kanoa; si-dza-fungula.
  (3) To greet. Ku-m-lamusa mutu nchirani hebu mudzini.
  **Lamuzana,** or **Lamuzania,** *v. reit.*, to greet one another.
  **Lamuzika,** *v.n.* Ni mukongo muno-kalamusika.
  **Lamusira,** *v.d.* Ni-lamusira gnania musiku; but more frequently they will say, Uk'enda uka-m-lamuse gnania musiku.
  **Lamusua,** *v.p.*, to be greeted. Udzilamusua ni gnania. Mudzilamusua ni ameyenu.
**Langa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), arrowroot. The plant grows abundantly, Unikani. Malanga ganariwa machira ga ndzalani.
**Langala,** *v.n.* *See* Midara. Madzi higano ganalangala; ka-ga-na vunsu. Nguo hi ka-i-ku dignia lusi, inalangala. Niumba inalangala; idzifumuka. *See* Pegnio. Kuna dziku kulangalako uka-vi-ona to virima. Der., Mulangasa.
**Langarisa,** or **Rangarisa,** *v.a.* Kirima hikira; lola to ku erekesa na muhi husa; ulangarise dzidzo, unda-ki-ona. Nidzirangarisa, hata nidzi-ki-ona.
**Langasa,** *v.a.* Gnania uki-m-lola, kadieka madzo, dzi-akalungasa madzo, yuna-ku-lola, ka vesa. Langasa madzo, ulole dzaha nguoni. Langasa madzo-m-lole

## [PDF Page 223 — Dictionary Page 210 (Lan — Lav)]

  to. Muana arie na uhongosi uka-mu-ambira: Dania madzo! hebu. Langasa madzoge, kudze cha, huenende. Muana hiye ni muerefu, akalangasa madzo, kakenkeka. Gnania ndiye adzaye-ni-langasa madzo, utu hiu nari si-u-mania.
  **Langasira,** *v. rel.* Nidziona mutu, sika-mu-mania, ela nidzi-m-langasira madzo hata nika-m-mania. Nidzichira vatu a-ni-vesa kare, ela mino nina-a-mania basi aka-ni-langasira madzo, hata aki-ni-kumbukira, aki-ni-mania.
  **Langasua,** *v.p.* Yudzilangasua madzo ni musenawe, ela wari bumbafu.
  **Langanzira,** *n.* (ra). Mutu yunafua langanzira rinagomba. Langanzira ka-ri-dza doka, yukere moyo.
**Lango,** *n.*, a large door.
**Lani** (Kij.), *v.a.* Yudzi-m-fierera, yudzi-m-lani foroforo, or, furufuru utu uambuao ka-u-dza laniwa mutu. Yudzisema aibuze zosi a-zo-henda.
**Lanika,** *v.n.* Muana akalanika hiyu, ni mkafiri; yuna moyo akiona kitu cha mutu, kafumurira.
  **Laniwa,** *v.p.*
**Larika.** *See* Lala.
  **Larira.** *See* Lala.
  **Lasa.** *See* Lala.
  **Lasira.** *See* Lala.
**Lasima** (Kij.), *n.* (ya). *See* Kumba; Dongea. Necessity, bail, surety. Muana yudzi-ni-buma lasimani, wapiga mbuzi-nkua, ikifua, nikidza sindikirua. Ku hala kitu cha mutu, ukapata lasima ya kudza ukiisua tu. Ndugu yangu yudzi-ni-tia lasima; deni hiri na-ri-riva, ela simania ra-ko-riwa, or, ra-ko-halua; na-dzi-rivira, be nindahendadze? Nidzikorerua jembe-rangu; yudzi-ni-buma lasima nisio-i-larira. Nidziingira lasima; chera cha mutu kidziangamika; basi ndayeya kingine, nirive.
**Lau,** *n.* *See* pl. Malau.
**Laula** (in Kig., Mundu muau and Mukongo). *See* La.
**Lava,** *v.n.* (in Kij., Lapa), (1) to be very hungry, well-nigh perishing with hunger. Madzere gadzilava. Gnania yudzilava, yudzefua kua ndzala. Gnombe inalava, inafua. Gnombe akisikira muladzo unanuka, be akakuenda vavo, akakuendava, nudzanudza, basi akalava. The natives say, Hata gnania, mino sikahala.
(2) (in Kij., Aba; Apa), to swear, to take an oath. Lava! kuamba kukahala. Yudzi-m-lava mameye; kakahala. Lomborera, kuamba si we, basi urie kikahe.
  **Lavalava,** *v.n.* Be unadza ukitafuta, unalavalava vio; u-la-vi we? Muana hiyu hata akakala na ndzala ya kufua, akidza, akadieka moyo hata u-mu-ve m'egnie, kadza kua ku lavalava.
  **Lavia,** *v.a.* (= Ku gnima in Kij., and Ku rasa in Kins.). Nidzichira kua gnania musiku, yunaria wari, yudzi-ni-lavia.
  **Lavira.**
  **Lavirana.**
  **Lavisa, Laviza,** *v.a.* *See* Karama. Dungua ni mufui! Demua ni jembe! Dungua ni kifiu! Dungua ni muiya! jegniua ni luhamba! Via na moho! Kuala kisiki! Guirua ni ndani! Lumua ni kidzoa! Lumua ni dzidzo! Aka-ku-lavisira. *See* Ruma.
**Lavi.** *See* Luavi.
  **Lavuka,** *v.n.* (= Lavukua in Kij.). Ah! mutu yudzilavuka ye yuna moyo ni mulave.
  **Lavukisa.** *See* Amula. Yudzigomba neno, yudzilavu-

## [PDF Page 224 — Dictionary Page 211 (Leg — Lik)]

  kisa; mutu hiye kafidza neno. Der., Ulave.
**Lego** (Kidigo), *n.* (ra) (= Kinembe in Kir.).
**Lela,** *v.n.*, to get loose, to slacken. Nidzifunga musigo, ka-u-kauma, udzilela (= udzidoroka). Hangu hudzi-voenenda dza ni kare, kahu-dza-oya, atu angine adzilela (= in Kig., Nsao idziu yekulela ingi, yeku kima = Kir., Nsao hino idzi-mu-iya muyawe, idzi-m-piga).
**Lelelele,** *n.* (= Kelele in Kij.), a noise. Kana lelelele.
**Leli,** *n.* (ya, no pl.). *See* Theri. Witness, testimony. Adzieona hura utu, ndiye agombaye leli. Leli ina iye ayeona, ela hara ashioona aamba ankue. Nidziambirua neno ra leli, or, maneno ga leli. Gnania hiye ndiye adziegomba leli; ndiye muegnie leli.
**Lema,** *n.* (ra, pl. Malema), a wickerwork used for fishing. Malema ni ga Adzomba, na Adigo nao ni ku henda.
**Lemba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the comb of a cock. Lemba ra jogolo. Lemba ra kanga. Dim., Kalemba; but not Kilemba.
**Lemba** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku kenga in Kir.). *See* Hofieka. To deceive.
**Lembelembe,** *adj.* and *adv.*, full to overflowing. Muho udziidzala-madzi ga lembelembe. Mamfula gadzikuta, hata kandakanda ga lembelembe. Uchi na o udzi-u-buma kirengeni lembelembe-udzumburire usamuagika, or, usimuagike. Uchi udziidzala lembelembe.
**Lenga,** *v.a.* *See* Chero; Kosa; Amuri; Malele. (1) To aim. Nidzi-m-lenga, nika-m-dzuva kigongo, nika-m-piga. Kukalenga dza vira ulengafio dziku sosi. Gnania uimowe aimao, basi niama kakira, ku-m-fumaga tu kua ku lenga. Musungu yunalenga ye. Mimi silenga ni mukosi.
(2) *See* Budzania. To speak to the point, to hit in speaking. Gnania kana lulaka lua ku aria, ela yunaidima ku lenga maneno.
**Lengalenga** (Kid.), *adj.* and *adv.* (= Lembelembe in Kir.), full to overflowing, brimful. Madzi ga lengalenga lengalenga, repeated as often as you like, in a high and singing voice. Uki u-lengalenga—
**Leu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Maleu). Kula mutu yuna leure. Ni-hendera leu, n'enende charoni.
**Leuka** (N.B.—This and the following word will be of great importance in religious instruction), *v.n.* *See* Rea. To become sober; trop., to become sober, right-minded. From Kurea, To be drunk. Ku leuka kunala ku rea ni. The word is expressive of the gradual change from a state of intoxication to that of soberness. Dzana warea, rero yudzileuka yunagomba maneno madzo ga akili urefi udzi-mu-la. Mutu hiye wari mgnieti, ela hangu dzana yudzihenda akili yunaleuka.
  **Leusa, Leuza,** *v.a.*, to make sober, to bring one to a sense of what is right and proper. Gnania wari kasikira wari mui-ela musenawe ndiye aye-m-leuza. Na-m-piga muana, ni-m-leuse, machero ariche, asihende dzambo hiri ni ri.
  **Leusua, Leuzua,** *v.p.*, to be brought right. Mutu hiye kangaleuka, ela waleusua ni gnania musiku.
**Lewalewa,** *v.n.* *See* Dorosa; Mufu. To dangle, to hang loose, to hang down. Gnania yudzichira na niama mukononi, inalewalewa. Nidzi-funga kitu muhini, kinalewalewa.
**Lika,** *v.a.*, to praise, to flatter. Mutu uhendalikua ni atu, ela uki-dzi-lika m'egnie, ka-vi-

*Footer: 211*

---

## [PDF Page 225 — Dictionary Page 212 (Lil — Lin)]

  hama. Yuna-dzi-lika bule, kana kitu.
  **Likana,** *v. reit.*, to praise one another. Atu analikana hio.
  **Likira,** *v. rel.* *See* Liga; Dokola. U-m-likira-ni naye, kua vivi ku-mu-ona rero yuhurire be ndo ku-m-lika? Kahama viratu unga-mu-ona.
**Lilia,** *v.a.* Ku-ni-wesa hata ukakala na maliso; wala kuni fikira kabisa, una mali irio dze we?
  **Liliana,** *v. reit.* Akamba ndio alilianao muno ndosa ahche kula dziku.
**Lilima,** *v.n.* (= Ku signia and Niakira), to go a running walk. Yudzililima hata yudzifika, yudziuya haraka.
**Limau,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Chungua), the bitter orange. In Kij., Limau means a citron, which in Kir. is called Kabu.
**Linda,** *v.a.* Yufunga niumba yudzi-i-linda (= Kamiria).
  **Lindana,** *v. reit.* Niumba idzifimbua, idzilindana, kavana tundu kaviri. Hiva vaira ku buma muhi, ka-va-kalindana, vana muagnia. Niumba idzilindana to, ka-i-na tundu (= idzilumana to). Menoge gakalindana, ela gangu gadaladala.
**Linga,** *v.a.*, to put or wind round, to wind into a ring, to coil. The more frequent word is Lingila. Ku linga mukumbu, chununi (= Ku-dzi-funga, etc.). Nalinga nguo yanyu kidzoani, ni ogerere, nivuke. Atu a kare ari akiamba: hunalinga mikaha hupigane mavi. Nidzilinga mbugu zangu. Linga lukueluangu. Der., Mulinga; Kilinga; Kilinge; Kilingilo; Kilingo.
  **Lingana,** *v.n.* *See* Ringania. To be like, to be equal. Vitu hivi vika, or, vina lingana (= vi-karakara). Ka-vi-kalingana hata, kuona kina ki-dzupa muyawe. Atu hia akarakara akalingana. Mbuzi hizi sika lingana. Mishigo hiyo ina, or, ika lingana, i-karakara.
  **Lingila,** *v.a.* *See* Mubawa; Thiaka. To wind round closely, tightly; to twine itself round, to wrap. *See* Mufo. Mutu yufunga gnombe be yudzilingila mukoa mukononi. Na mukumbu nao niku lingila chununi. Luvohe ni ku vinda uhani, lu-serelo uka-lu-lingila, or, uko-lu-dunga. Na lingila lubugu, lua ku fungira vanda. Nioka yudzi-ni-lingila kigulu. Nioka akikuera muhini, kakuera ku rungarara, yukuera dza ku amba, yuna-u-lingila. Na-m-funga gnombe muhini, lu kue na-lu-lingila muhini, nifunge.
  **Lingilana,** *v. reit.*, to entwine around each other. Niukue sidzilingilana (= sidzifungana).
  **Lingililia,** *v.a.*, to stimulate, to stir up, to instigate. The idea is that of being at one continually, winding one's self around him. Ku chinga and Kungucha. Atu ari asegere kabisa, ela gnania musiku ndiye aye kungucha atu, aki-a-lingililia hata akiuka. Ela kuamba si iye ku lingililia, hungari hu tari kuko. Kuna angine ana luhusa, be hu-a-lingililie, huenende kuehu. Atu hia kangaheha-ni gnania ndiye adzaye-a-lingililia hata adzipigana.
  **Lingilua,** *v.p.*, to be entwined or wound round each other. Nidzilingilua ni nioka kiguluni.
  **Lingira,** *v.d.* (of Ku linga). Hala lukueluangu, u-ni-lingire, n-lu-pige magumbi. Na-m-lingira lubugulue.
  **Lingirira,** *v.d.* and *rel.* (of Lingila). *See* Kilingilo. Rarely used.
**Linkua,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Mumiro. The voice. Linkua hiro ni ra gnania musiku. Linkua

## [PDF Page 226 — Dictionary Page 213 (Liw — Lol)]

  hiro ni ra baba, baba hiye yunagomba. Nidzimania linguare mutu iye agombaye. Na mania malinkuagao. Ku onia linkua, To show one's voice; *i.e.* To speak merely a few words for the guidance of others in deciding a case. Nidzi-a-onia lingua tu, ela sika uchirira ku nena halisi; maneno, higa nidzirichira afuaha, agombe ao, ela kuamba ni maneno mabomu, be ninganena. Gnombe hi irirayo namania ni gnombe dziku, linkuare nidzi-ri-sikira.
**Liwa,** *n.* (ra). *See* Luga. Muhaso wa pepo. Ku sarua liwa, ufumba wa pepo.
**Lo,** *rel. part.* to Lu. *See* Kidahi; Luuso; Komba; Lonso.
**Loa,** *n.* (pl. Vilua), a book, a ticket. Viziloa na mvula, The tickets were softened by the rain.
**Loa,** *v.n.*, to get soft, yielding, by wet; (K.) moist. Nguo idzitigua ni mfula, idziloa. Nguo idziingira madzini, idziloa. Kavu idziloa na mfula.
  **Loama,** or **Luama.** Usave hiu udzilafiwa haraka, ka-u-kaloama. Nidzifuika kikonde changu madzini, kuamba kiloame. Mianzo yangu hangu dzana inaloama; *i.e.* They have begun to flow.
  **Loamia,** *v.a.* Niusi sidzidzamuka, be ukaloamia na mahe, ukavongolola.
  **Loeka,** *v.a.* *See* Tende. To soak, to imbue. Chingo hi ni niomu, n'enda-i-laeka, iloame, nidze nigote-to. Usave hiu na-u-loeka, nifungire kivesa, hebu ni anire. Chingo idziloekua hata idziloama.
  **Loekera,** *v.d.* Enda uka-ni-loekere uloame (viz. usave). Na hega madzi, ni loekere ulongo, I fetch water to soften clay with.
  **Lofia,** *v.a.* *See* Mahemahe.
**Lofu** (Kidigo and Kidur.), *n.* (lua) (= Lufundo in Kir.). Kuna nuka lofu. Kitu hiki ka-ki-loreka, kinanuka lofu. Lofu lunukalo lunuka vi? (= Vatu va nuka vo lofu ni lua-vi?).
**Loga,** *v.a.* *See* Shumu. To bewitch.
  **Logana,** *v. ref.*, to bewitch one another.
  **Logeka,** *v.n.* Mutu hiye kalogeka, akalagulua akauma sana.
  **Logera,** *v.d.* Kare Munika akikala na undu na muyawe, akagomba na Mudzomba, aka-mu-va fungu aka-mu-amba: Ni-logera gnania, afue.
  **Logua,** *v.p.*, to be bewitched. Yudzilogua yunalumua. Yudzilogua yudzefua.
**Logadzi,** *n.* (lua), the name of a vegetable. (1) Logadzi lua kidzomba. (2) Logadzi lua kinika (= ujaka in Kij.).
**Loha** (Kij.), *n.* (ra), language, dialect. Loha ra kula kabila ya atu ana loharao. Chuo kidziandikua na loha ra Kiravai.
**Loha,** *v.n.*, to dream.
  **Loheka,** *v.n.* Kutu usiko ku fika, ku-ku-loha; ka-ku-loheka, ku-ku mania-ndosa.
  **Lohera.** Nidzi-ku-lohera koma mbi, ni-ku-funge luniasi luidzi hebu mulala muidzi, koma hio isagolosera.
  **Losa,** *v.a.* Gnania yuna koma, yudzilo sa. Gnania yudzilosa kunadza atu a vigofi.
**Loka** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Fika in Kir.), to arrive. From Loa.
**Lola, 1,** *v.a.*, to marry. N.B.—Muche ni ku lola, ela kua madzi ni ku lola. Ukasikira muche wa ku lola, be ni hiyu, ni muche m'egnie akili na m'egnie mukasi, asie ukaha; ndiye muche m'egnie mbaraka. Der., Ulosi.
