## [PDF Page 227 — Dictionary Page 214 (Lol — Lom)]

  **Lolana,** *v. reit.*, to intermarry. Atu hio analolana.
  **Lolua,** *v.p.*, to be married. Only used of the female. Muche yunalolua, ela, yudzilolua, muana wa gnania ndiye mudzedzangu, She has been married to the son of Gnania, who is my son-in-law.
  **Loreka,** *v.n.* (= Loreka). *See* Muso. Muche hiye ka uma kua mulume, kaloreka.
  **Lorera,** *v.d.* Ni-pa kitu nilorere, Give me something to marry with, *i.e.* some property. Mbuzi ndizo Mutaida alorera zo muche.
  **Lorerua,** *v.p.* Na-ku-riva hivi viangu, nikilorerua, nindaria na mi.
  **Losa, Loza,** *v.a.*, to betroth. Na loza m'anangu muche.
  **Losania, Lozania.** Atu ao akalozania.
  **Losua, Lozua,** *v.p.* Gnania yulosua muche ni babaye.
**Lola, 2,** *v.a.* *See* Zoesa. To look, to behold. Huya yuna-m-lola hiyu, ela hiyu ka-m-lola huya akafignia madzo. Wa-m-lola na madzo vivi tu? Kumania: muhi ukibua uekemere muyawe? Yudzigomba 'ye? yudzikuenda mu-lola na madzo tu, akauya; a wesa ku gomba naye? Yudzi-mu-isa kua haja. Der., Malola; Lore.
  **Lolana,** *v. reit.* *See* Galukirana. To look at each other, to look one towards another.
  **Loreka,** *v.n.* *See* Chenche. Ka-ku-loreka kanda hio, kuna muansa.
  **Lorera,** *v. rel.* *See* Kozi; Uringo. To look on, to look at. Mutu arindaye muyawe, basi yuna lorera njira. Sinda-mu-isa, na-m-lorera tu, kuamba yuna esima, nda-muona. Mutu hiye ni muaminifu, na-m-lorera, sindakuenda-mu-isa.
  **Lorerua,** *v.p.* Nidzidzoka ku lorerua, rero naenenda nikarive, nidane na deni. Yukuenda lorerua (= Yukuenda lagurirua, or, Yukuenda dzuvirua mburuga). Yunalorerua roho, ka-ri-dza toka (= Yunarindua roho).
  **Losa, Loza,** *v.a.* *See* Odi. To cause to look.
**Lolo,** *n. pr.* *See* Fifira.
**Loma,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma- and Wa-, hiku, pl. *id.*, a, hia) (in Kins., Nengo), the name of a species of animal (probably the badger)—it burrows in old ant-hills. When one is killed a lamentation is held over it, hoping that by so doing the meat will prove very fat. *See* Gadzo.
(2) An ant-eater. It is said to lay its tail on the ground for the ants to attack, and then aka vulula kanoani, to draw it into its mouth.
**Lomba,** *n.* (ra, lua, and pl. Niomba, sa, and Malomba; Lomba hilu and hiri). *See* Kerekere; Dzuva gnombe. Lomba ra ku gotera maonsa. Dim., Kalomba.
**Lomba,** *v.n.*, to pray. Ku lomba Mulungu, To pray to God. Ku lomba koma. Ku lomba mfula, To pray for rain. N'enda nikafove, ninda-m-lomba? ni Mulungu vohebu ui koma? be nda-m-lomba.
  **Lombekesa, Lombekeza,** *v.a.* *See* Rombeka.
  **Lombera,** *v.d.* *See* Haradora; Dai. Yudzi-m-lombera, ela Mulungu muniewe kakahensa. Nidzi lombera, Mulungu naye yudzi sikira, kuamba nashiononeka, yudzi-m-vosa hiye mutu mukongo, ku-ni-onera mbazi. Kava mutu alomberaye muyawe kuamba na apate mali, kava ndosa kulomberana ku si-kale-vo.
  **Lomberua,** *v.p.* *See* Lombola; Mulombosi. Yunalomberua, ela Mulungu muniewe ka-dza-henza.

## [PDF Page 228 — Dictionary Page 215 (Lom — Lua)]

  **Lombola** (= Jimbula). Ngoi yunalombola.
**Lomo,** *n.* Gnania yuna lomo (= mulomo mbomu).
**Lomu,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), hard. Contracted from Luomu.
**Londa,** *v.a.* *See* Odzania; Chinga. To desire, to want, to wish for; to be about. Gnania yudzikuenda londa atu, adze, agombe maneno (= Yudzikuenda kuta atu). Muana adzayekimbira, ndiye uendaye-mu-londa. N'enda nika-m-londe (= nika-m-yeye).
  **Londeka,** *v.n.* Mutu adzayekuenda hiko kua Muatunda, kalondeka kaviri.
  **Londera.** *See* Yesa; Uniama. Muana hiyu kasikira, yuna-hu-londera. Muana yunda-ni-londera hiyu; yunda-ni-kuta mashaka. Nikala kukicha ukaambua: muanao yudzihenda utu usiku, wa kudza riva. Machero n'enda nika-i-londere atu, i-dze i-riwe, i-sabanangika, To-morrow, I go, I desire people to come that it may be eaten, that it may not get spoiled. This refers to a sick cow.
  **Londerua,** *v.p.* *See* Kidanga.
  **Londua,** *v.p.*, to be desired.
**Longo,** *n.*, the name of a small territory in the Wadigo country.
**Longola,** *v.n.* and *a.*, to go in front, taking the lead. Atu adzichira vava, ela gnania ndiye adzie longola mbere (= ndiye adziedema lulongo, and, adziedema mbere). Ndiye ayelongola atu, akikala mbere iye. Mbuzi hira ni kilongola ku longola ayae. The word is identical in meaning with Dongoria, and they are used promiscuously, though Longola is more properly used of men, and Dongoria of animals. Der., Kilongola.
  **Longosa,** *v.a.*, to lead, to direct. Hunalonda mutu amaniaye njira, a-hu-longose, aka-hu-onie njira kutu hulondako kuenda. H'ende huka-ku-longose (H'ende, contracted from Huende). Ku longosa kikaheni. Ku longosa njira.
  **Longosania,** *v. reit.* Atu adziuka kuenda longosania.
  **Longosua,** *v.p.* *See* Vierera.
  **Longosesa** (Kig.).
**L'onio, Luonio,** *n.*, that which shows, a proof, a sign, an indication. From Ku lua, To show. Contracted from Luonio, and derived from Ku onia. Mutu hiye yudzilafia kifiucho, kuamba hureherue, humanie yuko, kafuere, basi hunamania yunadza, kuani, yudzilafia lonio. Ukiona manina vara tu kas'kasi ya m'isho, basi ndo l'onio lua muaka. Vula ndiro l'onio lua hira tembe. Dim., Kalonio. *See* Fula, *n.*
**L'onso,** *n.* (lua). L'onso hilu muhendalo ni lua-ni lo? munahenda l'onso kihoho, ela kamu atu asima fio? Muna l'onso muno.
**Lore,** *n.*, a fixed look, a stare. From Ku lola. Ku henda lore. To stare.
**Loreka.** *See* Lola.
**Lorera.** *See* Lola.
**Losa,** or **Loza.** *See* Lola.
**Losa.** *See* Loha. Madzi gana sisima gana losa.
**Losa,** or **Loza.** *See* Lola, 1.
  **Losana.** *See* Lola, 1.
  **Losania.** *See* Lola, 1.
**Losi,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), all whole. Contracted from Lu-osi.
**Loya,** *n.* (lua, pl. Nioya, sa).
**Lu,** *particle pron.* *See* Wawiwa; Afia. It, it is. Nidzi-lu-fiula lunaria (viz. luembe). *See* Kasa. Nidzi-lu-fiula ludziguira.
**Lua.** *See* Dzulo; Kungurira; Kibindi; Gema. Lua madzi; lua viri; lua lua haha; lua ne (luane); lua

## [PDF Page 229 — Dictionary Page 216 (Lua — Lua)]

  dzano; lua handahu, etc. Lua mudzana, At noon.
**Lua,** *n.* (lua), (1) Lua lua atu agnaro.
(2) Lua lua bora ayefua.
**Luafu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niafu) (= Kagniamigniami in Kins.), a nettle. Sichireni hivo, vana niafu.
**Luafu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Mbafu), (1) rib; (2) side. Nidzila la na luafu lumenga (= kandamenga), I have been lying on one side. Nidzila la na mbafu zosi mbiri, I have been lying on both sides. Mbafuzanga zina luma.
**Luago,** *n.* (lua), (1) (pl. Mago), the inner part of the thigh.
(2) (pl. Niago), pace. Vana dzalafu hiva, adzifumuka wamba, ugolose luago, or, ugolose kigulu, udzupe, asa ku luma.
**Luako,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the lua class), thy, thine.
**Luakue,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the lua class), his, her, hers, its.
**Luakue,** *adv.* *See* Megurira. (K.) Sundry. Kololo yurira luakue.
  **Luakueluakue,** *adv.*, (K.) divers, various, several, separately, dissimilar, manifold.
**Luala,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niala). *See* Dzago. A stone used for grinding corn. It is a flat stone, about two feet by one foot; the women kneel down and grind the corn with a small stone about the size of a small brick.
**Luala** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Duara in Kns.; Lumua in Kir.), to be ill, to be sick.
  **Luarisa, Luariza,** *v.a.*, to nurse. Yudzi-m-luarisa nduguye hata yudzivola. Yudzi-m-luarisa nduguye, hata yudzefua. Mimi na-mu-luarisa hata akivola, ela mino nalumua; akisakudza ni-lola ngari, hata nikivola; mutu hiye ela si mui? Wafuka kuko Ruruma, kuna nduguyao kuko, ni mukongo, yuna-m-luarisa.
  **Luasa, Luaza,** (1) *v.a.* (= Luarisa).
  (2) *v.c.*, to cause to ail, in the limited sense of a tumour or a cut turning to an ulcer. Nasagala vava, ninaluaza mukongo, ka-dza-oneka urungo (= ka-dza-henda baha). Wakudza kare, yu-vava, yuna-m-luaza nduguye. Ivu rikihumbulua, ka-ri-luaza, ela rikihumbuka regnie, basi ni ku henda kironda, ndo ri luaza vo. A wound thus raised is called domosi. Gnonzi hi nidzi-i-kata muchira, ela ka i ka i ka luaza idzi vola hiraka; mukono wangu ka-u-luaza.
**Lualamu,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class). *See* Muhawe; Alamu. Broad.
**Lua-lo,** *pron.* (implying the imperf. tense, and rel. to the lu class). *See* Dzoniola. That which. Luvande lua-lo ikua hiva, lu-vi? The piece which was put here, where is it?
**Luama,** *v.n.* (= Loama). *See* Dzimbika; Omu.
**Luambe,** *n.* (lua) (Kij., Wombe). *See* Fusira; Wawisa. The dust of millet. Luambe ni fumbi ra muhama, Luambe is dust of millet. Luambe lua niazi, The dust of cocoa-nuts. Ondo rina luambe, rinawawa.
**Luambo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niambo), backbiting. Hangi niki-mu-ambira, yunda-ni-amba: nidzi-mu-amba vi-akashagomba, ela aki-mu-ona mutu mungina, akahendi gnansi, aka-mu-ambira hiye mutu mungina, basi ndo luambo. Sinda-ku-amba luambo, na-ku-ambira uso na madzo: u-mui, I will not backbite thee; I tell thee to thy face thou art bad.
**Luana,** *v.a.*, to emasculate, to geld. Seldom practised among the Wanyika.
**Luana,** *v.n.*, to differ. Atu analuana, anahenda kanani, maneno ka-ga-dza goloka ndo

## [PDF Page 230 — Dictionary Page 217 (Lua — Lub)]

  usikiravo lonso Atu analuana, kula mumenga yufuhira kuake. Maneno ganatuana.
  **Luanira,** *v. rel.* (= Ku hehera). Hunaluanira kitu kimenga. Analuanira muche mumenga.
**Luanda,** *n.* (lua). *See* Afia; Kusiko. Lit. something extended, something of length. (1) An open tract of land. From Ku anda.
(2) A fresh piece of ground taken under cultivation. Opposed to Fue. Vatu vasivodzaka ni luanda. Luanda hilu ludziguirua mani, atu analonda ku rima minda. Na laa munda muvia wa luandani; or merely, Na laa luandani. Dim., Kadzanda.
(3) Length. Only used of a hut, in contradistinction to Kidzuri. Niumba ya luanda, A hut of length; *i.e.* built lengthwise, oval.
**Luandala,** *n.* (lua). *See* Kunsira. Ku-si-korimua ni dzansala, ela ku-ka-korimua ni luandala.
**Luangu,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the lu class), my, mine.
**Luangua,** *n.* (lua) (Wangua in Kij.), a level tract of white sand, which is covered with water at high tide, but bare at low tide. From Ku anga.
**Luani,** *pron.* (rel. to the lu class). *See* Luyeyo. What.
**Luania,** *n.* (lua) (= Pengo; Kij., Wangu), a cave. U-ni-dzonge luania, u-ni-kote na pengo. Ndio nimbo ya kare. Gnania yuna luania lua Mulungu, kadzongerue.
**Luansa,** *n.* (lua), any small piece of metal used for cauterizing or tattooing. Luansa ni kisiku cha mukodo hebu cha chuma cha ku-m-dzomera mutu akilumua ni misiva.
**Luao,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the lu class), their, theirs. Lukolo luao.
**Luao,** *adj.*, separate, by themselves.
**Luare,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niare). *See* Kithuma. One-half of the hide of a cow. Used to lie on.
**Luario,** *n.* (pl. Maario? Kidigo?).
**Luarisa.** *See* Luala.
**Luasa.** *See* Luala.
**Luasu,** *adj.* and *adv.* *See* Sasira; Chinga. Open, openly; obvious, obviously. Kuika luasu, Explain, show.
**Luavi,** *adv.* (= Kiluavi). *See* Yulavi. Where. Kua gnania ni luavi. Yu kerevi, Where is he? Na londa niumba ya gnania, i lua vi. Na londa niumba ya musenangu, gnania i-lua-vi.
**Luaya.** *See* Finiangika; Danikana. Magn., Dzaya.
**Luayo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niayo). *See* Ala. (1) The sole of the foot. From Ku aya.
(2) A footstep, footprint. Prov., Kava mutu agulave gnombe luayo. Luayo hilu nidzi-lu-mania, ni lua gnania musiku. Gnania yuna luayo lua uchi.
**Lubadu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Patu) (= Ubadu in Kij.), a tray of copper imported from India. The Wanyika sometimes borrow them from Suahili friends, to use them as a kind of gong to accompany the drum, when a dance is being performed for expelling an evil spirit from a sick person. Padu ni sa Azomba; ndiso sibiguaso kuamba mutu yunavungua; sinapigua vurisa ngoma.
**Lubafu, Lubavu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Mbafu, Mbavu) (= Luafu), a rib, the side.
**Lubalula,** *n.* (lua).
**Lubangu,** *n.*
**Lubao,** *n.* (lua, pl. Mbao, za), a board, a plank. Dim., Kabao and Kibao.
**Lubele,** *n.* (lua).
**Lubombombo,** *n.* (lua).
**Lubomu,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), large, great. Luvande lubomu, A large piece.
**Lubueka,** *n.* (lua, pl. Pueka), the

*Footer: 217*

---

## [PDF Page 231 — Dictionary Page 218 (Lub — Lud)]

  name of a species of bird used for sacrifices. Gnania yudzilosa, koma idziamba: Mukasole lubueka, mu-lu-guire, mudze na-lo lua moyo, atu adze, ahendere sadaka. Lubueka ni ku guirua lusima, lukakudza henderua sadaka ya viha hebu ya makongo.
**Lubugu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Mbugu), a creeper used for binding. Dim., Kalubugu.
**Lubuidia,** *n.* *See* Lukuidia.
**Luchari.** *See* Luhosi.
**Luche.**
**Lucheche,** *n.* (lua, pl. Tsheche), a slice. Ku checha lucheche lua nazi, To cut off a slice of a cocoa-nut round about the brim of the shell.
**Luchegnio, Lutegnio,** *n.* ( ), a state or tendency to cut. From Ku chegnia. Maneno ga luchegnio, Offensive language. Uchi hiu afu muno, uki-u-noa una luchegnio.
**Luchemi,** *n.* (lua, no pl.). *See* Chenche. Moho hiu una luchemi ka-u-sengerereka vevi, una-ku-dzoma na luchemi.
**Luchere,** *n.* (lua, pl. Tshere). *See* Cheche; Chera. A slice. Luchere lua manazi lua koba. Luchere lua nazi, A piece of a cocoa-nut.
**Luchigo, Lukigo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Tigo, Tshigo), a hedge. Ku piga luchigo, To make a hedge. Sometimes made to keep the cattle from getting into a plantation. Luchigo lua ku mera, A hedge which grows. Dim., Kachigo.
**Lucho,** *n.* *See* Luho.
**Luchocho.** Nchocho za muhogo.
**Ludaba, Lutaba,** *n.* (lua, pl. Taba), made of the golovolo ra mugomba. Ludaba lua tumbaku. Ludaba lua kironda. Dim., Kadaba and Kidaba; magn., Daba, Dava, and Ridaba (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Ludago,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ndago), a *rush*. (1) Ludago zia. (2) Ludago luanda. (3) Ludago munda.
**Ludahi, Lutahi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Tahi) (= Kij.; Udawi, not Utawi, which becomes Udzai in Kir.), a dry bough. Nidziamba ni ludahi luifu, kumba ni panda mbidzi. Dim., Kidahi and Kadahi; magn., Ridahi (pl. Midahi and Madahi).
**Ludai** (Kid.), *n.* (pl. Tai) (= Ludahi in Kir.).
**Ludara,** *n.* (lua, pl. Tara), a bier; a rude kind of litter for carrying a disabled person or a corpse. Mutu akizikua, basi ludara ni ku demua, luka hendua viambo, na kuamba viambo vidzienera, be ni ku demuademua, lukadzuvua, When a man is to be buried, a bier is made of sticks cut for the purpose. When the bier is done with, the sticks are cut up and thrown away. *See* Chambo.
**Ludea,** or **Luthea,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ndea, or Nthea), the jawbone. The word is becoming obsolete, being superseded by the Kig. word Ngambu.
**Ludi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ti and Vidi), a string of beads. Ludi lua ushanga; pl. Vidi via ushanga; or, Ti sa ushanga. Ushanga huno u-dze? What are those beads? *i.e.* How many strings? Resp., Ni ti mirongo miiri, They are twenty strings.
**Ludi, Luchi,** *adj.*, luscious. Mdzuano ukisidi, be ndo luchi; lit. Sweetness, if it exceeds, that which is luscious. Uchi hiu u-luchi, ni uidzi muno.
**Ludide, Lutite,** *adj.*, small, little.
**Ludingo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ndingo), a strip of skin, used for binding up the heads of arrows when poisoned.
**Ludodo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ndodo). *See* Kidahi. A dry twig, any thin piece of wood when dry. Ndodo ni sa muhi mufu. Dim., Kidodo (pl. Vi-).

*Footer: 218*

---

## [PDF Page 232 — Dictionary Page 219 (Lud — Lue)]

**Ludude,** *n.* (lua). *See* Lugua.
**Luduo,** *n.* (lua), the propensity of a child to follow after its mother or father. From Ku dua. Muana alondaye ku-m-dua babaye hebu mameye kula vatu aendavo, be ndiye aambuaye yuna luduo.
**Ludzadza,** *n.* (lua, pl. Dzudza, za) (= Utata in Kij.), a hurdle fence fixed in the sea to catch fish. Ludzadza lua kamba, lua ku fuira kamba.
**Ludzaga,** *n.* (lua, pl. Dzaga), (1) a sort of enclosed platform, or rack, erected in native huts over the place they make their fire, and which serves as their granary. Dim., Kadzaga and Kidzaga; magn., Ridzaga.
(2) One of the sticks laid lengthwise on the frame of what forms their bedstead. Ludzaga lua ku handika uririni, Sticks, generally the boughs of a cocoa-nut tree, are used to make a bedstead.
(3) In Kidigo, the word means a Kinyika bedstead (= Uriri in Kir.).
**Lu-dza-lo.** *See* Fumagirua.
**Ludzambo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Dzambo). *See* Mishombo. A cloth gathered up and bound round the waist. Only used of women. Yudzi-dzi-funga ludzambo ku-dzi-dzundika tu, ku piga mishombo. Yudzi-dzi-funga ludzambo yudzi-fuererua ni mulumewe. Gnombe hira ina ludzambo. Dim., Kadzambo and Kidzambo.
**Ludzanga,** *n.* (lua) (Utanga in Kij.). *See* Ngama. Fine sand. Mdzanga mdzefu, or, muyuya.
**Lu-dza-vo.**
**Ludze.** *See* Ludzi.
**Ludzengo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Dzengo). *See* Dzomera. Rero huenda rima ludzengo-kosikosi, raso kulu na raso ra dzini, kula atu arime kandayao.
**Ludzere,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niere, za), (1) a single hair of the head only.
(2) A plait of hair. Nidzisuka ludzere lumenga, I have formed one plait; pl. Niere mbiri, tahu, etc., Two, three plaits, etc. Dim., Kidzere, pl. Vidzere, Little hairs.
**Ludzi,** *pron.* used in declining verbs (indicating the perf. tense, and rel. to the lu class). Before monosyllables and enclitic verbs the *i* is changed into *e*. Ludahi ludzifunsika ludzebua, It has, it is.
**Ludzidzi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Dzidzi) (= Luangua), a creek, a cove. Ludzidzi ni mukono wa bahari, hikura u-ka-ko vesera, kuenda luankuani lua bara. Dim., Kadzidzi and Kidzidzi.
**Ludzimbo,** *n.* Muana hiyu ni kidzaye, ni ludzimbo, yunadzimba. Gnonsi hi ni ludzimbo.
**Ludzo,** *adj.* *See* Maki; Lulaka. Good. Lusi ludzo, Good thread.
**Ludzoa,** *n. coll.* (hiyu, hia). *See* Dzoa.
**Lu-dzo-vo** (= Lu-dza-vo).
**Ludzovo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Dzovo), a ladle exclusively used for toddy. Ludzovo, lua ku dzovera uchi, ni ku hendua lua nazi tide. Dim., Kadzovo.
**Ludzua,** *n.* (lua), the sun when hottest, as he is before the rains in spring and in autumn, in the Kas'kasi muisho, and the time called Lukarikare. Ludzua lua mfula lunaala muno, mfula i vevi. Si ludzua lo.
**Ludzunga,** *n.* From Ku dzunga. Muche hiyu yuna ludzunga. Yuna ridzunga, kahi yundafiala ana airi, yudzichisa ridzunga mberembere. Dim., Kadzunga and Kidzunga; magn., Ridzunga.
**Ludzungo.**
**Lue,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the lu class), his, her, its. Lurimi

*Footer: 219*

---

## [PDF Page 233 — Dictionary Page 220 (Lue — Luf)]

  lue, His, her, its tongue. *See* Dzua.
**Luegnie,** *adj.*
**Luehu,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the lu class), our, ours.
**Lueka,** *v.a.* *See* Loeka. To soak.
**Lueluelue,** *n.* *See* Madzimadzi.
**Luembe,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niembe). *See* Rika. A razor,—a rare instrument among the Wanyika: they shave their heads with a common knife. Dim., Kadzembe and Kidzembe; magn., Dzembe.
**Luena,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niena), a very thin waist. Yuchenchereka mua luena.
**Luengu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niengu) (in Kij. and Kig., Wengu), the spleen.
**Luensa,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niensa), a cup. Muhama udzilafia luensa. Madzere gadzilafia niensa. Luensa lua munazi.
**Luenu,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the lu class), your, yours.
**Luera,** *n.* (lua, no pl.). *See* Dimula. The mane. Luera lua tia, The mane of a giraffe, sometimes worn by men as an ornament across the breast. *See* Muagalo.
**Luerere,** *n.* (lua), the name of a disease.
**Lueruve,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), white. Luho ni lueruve.
**Lufidzo,** *n.* *See* Lufuidzo.
**Lufiho,** *n.* *See* Lufuiho.
**Lufiusa,** *n.* (lua, no pl.), the stick, or spring, of a trap which is intended to go off on being touched. From Ku fiusa.
**Lufu,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class). *See* Fu. Dried up, hard. Lukuni lufu, A dry, hard piece of wood. Lukano lufu.
**Lufu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niufu), a corpse.
**Lufugulufugu,** *n.* and *adj.* (only used as predicate or in the gen.), tepid, lukewarm. Madzi ga lufugulufugu, Tepid water. Madzi higano gadzikola lufugulufugu. Madzi *higa gadzikola* muno, be hega madzi ga peho, ubigirire, gakale lufugulufugu.
**Lufuhi,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), short.
**Lufui,** *n.* (only used in the gen.). Muriango wa mbugu; ndio muriango wa lufui.
**Lufuidzo,** *n.* (lua). *See* Mkuluko. A forked stick, used for stirring in cooking. Lufuidzo lua ku fuidzira mboga sa kunde. Lufuidzo lua ku fuidzira wari; mahuhu gafunsikefunsike, hebu wari usihende mahuhu. Dim., Kafuidzo.
**Lufuiho,** *n.* (lua, pl. Pfuiho and Fuiho). *See* Ingisa. A thin, long stick. Yudzi-m-piga lufuiho, kana menga; but, Yudzi-m-piga pfuiho, kana ningi. Lufuiho lua ku dzungira mbuzi.
**Lufuje,** *n.* *See* Megula.
**Lufula,** *n.* (lua, no pl.). *See* Fula. Niuchi onadzukula, or, anahala lufula.
**Lufulo,** *n.* (lua, no pl.). *See* Musinsi. A ditch, a hollow made in the ground. From Ku fula. Ku dzimba lufulo. Lufulo lua kivesa. Lufulo lua ku chitira vitu via sadaka.
**Lufumulo,** *n.* (lua). *See* Umba. Destructiveness.
**Lufundo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Pfundo), a swing. Lufundo lua ku desera, hebu lua ku dugnagnira. Ahoho adzifunga pfundo za ku desera, h'endani muka-sikate.
**Lufundo,** *n.* (lua).
**Lufunsu,** *n.* (lua) (= Wenga). Muana hiyu yuna lufunsu, kakomia ku rira. Muana hiyu hangu dzana yudzihenda lufunsu. Kuna ku lumua na lufunsu-kura ku vayavaya; opposed too Ku lumua kua ku fumurira. Ku kala na lufunsu (= Ku-dzi-hehemesa in Kid.).
**Lufusa,** *n.* (lua, no pl.).

*Footer: 220*

---

## [PDF Page 234 — Dictionary Page 221 (Luf — Luh)]

  Lufusa lua gnombe (= Kid., Lumuaji lua gnombe). Madali ga lufusa.
**Lufusi, Lufuzi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Mifusi, Mifuzi). *See* Kubo. The hair of animals and of the human body.
**Lufusi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Mifusi), a particle of dust or dirt. Nidziingirua ni lufusi, or, kifusi dzidzoni, ndzo, u-ni-fifire. Dim., Kifusi.
**Luga,** *n.* (lua), memory, especially a good memory. Gnania yuna luga, kam'ala maneno. Gnania yuna luga, kakomia ku mania maneno ga atu. Muana yuna luga yuyu, hata neno a-ro-sikira kare, ka-ri-niala. In Kid. it also means quickness of apprehension. Si luga lo-wasikira dziku menga na ku mania; muana hiyu yuna luga (= Kir., Yuna masikiro manguangu). Gnania yuna masikiro manku-angu-kidza yuna luga, N. has quick ears, and, in addition, a good memory. Sina luga mino, sikomia ku niala; *i.e.* My memory is very bad.
**Lugeregere,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ngeregere), the sakreet of Egypt,—an expression of joy used by women after childbirth. Ku piga lugeregere. Atu ache akifiera dziku ya kuri, anapiga ngeregere.
**Lugesigesi,** *n.* (= Luchesichesi; Lukesikesi). Nasikira lugesigesi.
**Luginga,** *n.* (lua, pl. Nginga).
**Lugnialu.** *See* Lunialu.
**Lugnongo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Gnongo, za), the ridge of the leaf of a mulala. Gnongoche, Female gnongo. Gnongo ndume, Male gnongo. Lugnongo ni lua mulala, ela luhuahu ni lua Munazi, and, lua mugumo.
**Lugodi,** *n.*
**Lugofia,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ngofia), a long stick with a hook. Hikara ache an'enda kuni na madzoka. Dim., Kigofia.
**Lugua,** *n. coll.*, lit. a stalk or straw-field, stubble,—a term applied to a plantation after reaping, when nothing but the stalks or straws remain. The word refers to the Wanyika mode of reaping, only the ears being cut off. Of Guinea-corn, muhama, the word is never used, because that is cut down near the ground. Lugua ni lua wimbi, lua muvunga, lua maere. Ku dzaira lugua, To glean. N'enda nikadzaire kunde sa lugua, podzo za lugua. Muhama ka-u-na lugua, ni visinde. Maere ga lugua wimbi wa; of muhama, visinde.
**Lugue.** *See* Lukue.
**Lugululo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ngululo, *q.v.*).
**Luguma,** *n.* (lua, pl. Nguma), a wound caused by a blow. Yudzi-m-piga yudzi-mu-ahula luguma. Luguma ni lua kigongo hebu iwe, ela si lua chera.
**Lugunsu** (Kidigo), *n.* Yudzidzapa na vava lugunsu (= Kir., Yudzichira na vava chiramuko kukuni).
**Luguso.** *See* Lukuso.
**Luhadzi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Tadzi), a cloth thrown over the head; (K.) wimple.
**Luhago,** *n.* (lua, no pl.), the name of an odoriferous plant. The women extract the juice by pounding it and mixing it with water, which they press out over a new cloth until it is impregnated. Luhago ni ufumba wa ache, lunanuka to.
**Luhalo,** *n.* (lua). Gnania yuna luhalo; anae osi bia aka-m-hala abeyao sura. Muana hiya aka-m-hala mameye sura halisi wamba ndiye mtumche hiye yuna luhalo.
**Luhamba,** *n.* (lua, pl. Pamba).
**Luhandu,** *n.* (lua). *See* Koloa. Lit. a spreading, something spread over so as to cover.

*Footer: 221*

---

## [PDF Page 235 — Dictionary Page 222 (Luh — Luk)]

  From Ku handa. (1) Luhandu lua masia, Cream. *See* Mudindi.
  (2) Luhandu lua kola, The lid of a snail.
  (3) Luhandu lua madzo, A film over the eyes. Madzoge gana luhandu; ka-ga-ona to. Dim., Kahandu.
**Luho,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niuho). *See* Musibi. Glair; the juice of fruit when somewhat consistent and slimy. Luho lua ichi (= Cheruve cha ichi), The white of an egg. Luho lua dzaje; luho lua mafo. Dakuma hiri ri mdzuano, rina luho.
**Luhopo,** *n.* (lua). From Ku hopa. Narima luhoponi, ni niale muvunga.
**Luhosi,** *n.* (lua, no pl.), the vertex. Gnania yunapigua kigongo cha luhosi, yunapigua luhosini, na ku bua, akazimia moyo, akamuagirua madzi, akafufuka. Ni muana mudzanga, luhosi luchari pigapiga.
**Luhuaha,** *n.* (lua, pl. Tuaha). *See* Lugnongo. The ridge of a palm leaf. Muhoho ni ku pigua na luhuaha. Ludzadza lunasukua lua tuaha.
**Luhula** (Kid.), *n.* (= Wanamo in Kir., and Pura in Kins., and Muvua wa nsuki in Kig.).
**Luhunde,** *n.* (lua, pl. Tunde), a thing, a trifle. Dim., Kihunde.
**Luhusa,** *n.* (= Uere). *See* Dovola. Slowness, tardiness. Kuhenda luhusa.
**Lui,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), bad. Lukue lui, A bad string. Lufundo lui, etc.
**Luidzi,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), fresh, raw, green.
**Luidzo,** *n.* (lua), infection. Gnania yuna luidzo, uki-mu-ona yuna ivu, basi nawe ni kuenda henda ivu.
**Luifu,** *adj.* *See* Ludahi. Ripe. Lukuni hilu ni luifu.
**Luiga,** *n.* (lua, pl. Mbiga), a basin made of clay in the country and unglazed, those imported are called bakuli, a pan. Dim., Kabiga and Kibiga.
**Luigo,** *n.* (lua). From Ku iga. Gnania yuna luigo, yunaiga muyawe utu ahendao.
**Luiko,** *n.* (lua), (1) (= Kiko and Muiko, which words are more frequently used than Luiko), a spoon. Luiko lua ku ririra.
(2) Gnania yuna luiko; yunaika kitu muno, kitu cha muaka dzusi ki-mumo, cha muaka dzana ki-mumo.
**Luina,** *n.* (lua, no pl.). Kifua hiki kina luina.
**Luinda,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ninda), (1) Luinda lua koe. Koe hia ana wimbi wa nindani.
(2) Ku piga luinda. Abaniani karicha kupiga luinda.
**Luiro,** *n.* (lua) (= Malo). *See* Ramuka. Ku usa luiro; or, Ku piga luiro.
**Luje,** *n.* Pumbuye ina luje (= ni nire).
**Lu-ka,** *particles*, used in conjugation.
**Lukadza.** Lukanda lua ndani ndo luambualo: nagua lukadza. Ndzugu na mabawa ndo gaguiwago lukadza.
**Lu-ka-lo,** *particles*, used in conjugation.
**Lukamba,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kamba), a rope made of milala.
**Lukancha,** *n.* (lua).
**Lukanda,** *n.* (lua, no pl.). *See* Lukadza.
**Lukandakanda** (= Maandanda), only used with Doma or Funsaya. Nidzi-m-doma, or, Nidzi-m-funsaya, lukandakanda, or, maandanda, I grazed him with an arrow, shooting.
**Lukano,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kano). *See* Gano (pl. Makano). Vein, sinew, tendon. Lukano lua muladzo, A blood-vessel. Lu-

*Footer: 222*

---

## [PDF Page 236 — Dictionary Page 223 (Luk — Luk)]

  kano luegnie, The lukano itself, or the proper lukano; *i.e.* A sinew or tendon. Lukano lua mongoni mua gnombe ni lure, ni luvudzu, mongoni mua gnombe kuna kano mbiri, lumenga lunala luvohe. Nadzaniula lukanoluangu, ni kulule, nisuke luvohe. Lukano luidzi. Lukano lufu. Gnania yuna lukano, A person has a disease of the veins or sinews (= Mshipa in Kij.).
**Lukansa,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kansa). *See* Mumondo. (1) A single leaf of the branch of a palm tree, lukodza lumenga. The pl. Makansa is especially used in Kidigo.
(2) The whole branch from where the leaves begin, lukansa luzima. Nidziona kumbi ridzebua, be n'endadema lukansa; or, Kumbi ridzebua, n'enda, nikalole chamba muna (in with) lukansa ludzo, nideme, nika suke.
(3) The platted branch, lukansa lua ku suka.
**Lukarekare,** *n.* (lua), the time between mdzuo and furi. Lukarekare kana mfula; nidzua vuvu-wau; hata mfula ya furi ya ku dza bua. Lukarekare na kas'kasi; hio kana tundo wala kana kilimo, kuani-kavana mvula. Dzua hiri ni ra lukarekare.
**Lukere.**
**Lukesikesi,** *n.* (lua). Nina laga, nasikira lukesikesi umironi.
**Lukindia,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kindia, za). Lukindia ni lukansa lua luensa, lua ku fungira vanda.
**Lukodi,** *n.* (lua, no pl.), the nape.
**Lukodza,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kodza), a leaf, smaller and thinner than the kodza, a small leaf. *See* Kodza ra. Kodza ni sira tu niamlamba, pudzu.
**Lukoe,** *n. coll.* (lua). *See* Mudzungu. The name of a kind of vegetable.
**Lukoe,** *n.* (lua), the soft kernel of a cocoa-nut, when the nut is half-ripe, called dafu.
**Lukofi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kofi), a clap with the hands.
**Lukoka,** *n.*, a grass growing around a heap of stones.
**Lukoko,** *n.* (lua). *See* Ukoko. The crust on porridge of grain or flour, when still soft. Nidzibinikisa wari, unaansakuhenda lukoko, ka-u-dza ifua.
**Lukokoko** (?). Dzusi na henda lukokoko.
**Lukolo,** *n.* (lua). *See* Fuererana; Kolo. Kindred; (K.) lineage, kinsman, relative. Lukolo adzi-ni-kana, ka-ni-hensi. *See* Kana.
**Lukombe,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kombe), a dish, a cup, a shell. (1) The shell of fish when bivalvular. Lukombe lua ngulu. N.B.—As an exception, the word is also used of a large snail called kola; but other shells go by different names; as ngudu, ndogoe, mueri.
(2) Claw. Lukombe lua niama wa mafumba, na lukombe lua niuni.
(3) Nail of a finger or toe. Lukombe lua chala. Dim., Kakombe and Kikombe; magn., Kombe.
**Lukongo** (Kid. and Kidigo), *n.* (lua) (= Lulongo), a row.
**Lukosi, Lukozi,** *n.* (lua). Madzi higa gana lukozi ni vidude vi nga mihambo ya koma. Mawe gadzihenda lukozi; ka-va-fiogeka, vanaheresa kua lukosi.
**Lukove,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kove), (1) a single hair of the eyelashes. From Ku koba.
(2) In the following instances the word seems to stand for eyelid, though my informant does not admit this application of the word, and says they have no name for the eyelid itself. Lukove na ku vesa, In the twinkling of an eye. Utu hiu-lukove na

*Footer: 223*

---

## [PDF Page 237 — Dictionary Page 224 (Luk — Lul)]

  ku vesa-udzichira. Yudzihenda utu haraka; lukove ku vesa, or, kifignio cha madzo. Kove za dzulu, The upper eyelashes. Kove sa dzini, The under eyelashes. Lukove ni lufusi lumea dea!
**Lukovohi** (Kig.), *n.*, the umbilical cord.
**Lukua** (?). *See* Nga.
**Lukuare,** *n.* (lua), lewdness, lasciviousness, lustfulness. Yuna lukuare; kaogova adzedza, wala ana, wala ndugu.
**Lukuchu** (Kid.), *n.* (= Rukudzu in Kir.).
**Lukue,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niuke, za), anything platted or twisted like a cord, a rope, a string. Lusukua lo hebu luvalasua lo ni lukue hata lukakala ni luvudzu. Lukue ni lua urihi, uriro, ukonche, udzikidzi. Dim., Kadzukue and Kidzukue; magn., Dzukue.
**Lukuidia,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kuidia, za, or Luhuaha). N.B.—Sometimes you fancy you hear Puidia; it is a very strange sound. Kuidia sa munazi. Kare-ahoho ari akihenda kuidia, akainsira mabansi, ela hangu dzana vikarichika. Dim., Kakuidia and Kikuidia.
**Lukuiri,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kuiri), the name of a species of animal. Yunga kikuala, ela kikuala ni kitite.
**Lukulu,** *adj.* *See* Dzua, Nos. 9, 10.
**Lukumbi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kumbi). *See* Kumbi. (1) The eyebrow, the hair being called kumbi, which it is the Wanyika custom to shave. From Ku kumba.
(2) The edge of the eyelid. Lukumbi lua dzidzo.
(3) The lower edge of the eye. Kuna lukumbi lumeralo kumbi; na lukumbi lumeralo kove, There is a lukumbi on which grow the *eyebrows*; and a lukumbi on *which grow* the eyelashes.
**Lukunde,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kunde). *See* Makanda. A kind of bean. The sing. can only be used of beans still in the pod, but a single bean is, Tembe ya kunde, A grain of a pod.
**Lukungo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kungo), something gathered up, a set of things filed or strung, or stuck upon a stick. From Ku kunga. Lukungo lua nioe, A string of grasshoppers, which are caught and taken home by boys for food. Lukungo lua niama mbifu, Pieces of boiled meat stuck upon a stick. Lukungo lua makumba, A string of sweet-water fish.
**Lukuni,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kuni), a single piece of firewood. Lukuni ka-lu-bumua dza, lubumua kolo. Lukuni hilu-kua-dza ni lua-vi? or, Kua kolo ni lua-vi? Dim., Kikuni.
**Lukuso, Lukuzo,** *n.* (lua). *See* Enensia. From Kuza. hiyu yuna lukuso, karikisa Mbuzi i na lukuzo. Kuku haraka. Muana we sodi a kule, mutu adononoke, basi ndo akaviala mungina; basi hiye muana akaye fiarerua, aka-mu-ereka mfuahawe.
**Lukuva,** *n.* (lua, pl. Kuva).
**Lulaka,** *n.* *See* Lenga. A loud and clear voice. Ku lafia lulaka (= ku lavukisa). Mutu hiye yuna lulaka, yunasikirika kure. Gnania yuna lulaka, akigomba, manenoge gasikirika kure. Kugomba viomu ukalafia lulaka nikasikira unani? *See* Pore. Gnania yuna lulaka ludzo, hata akagomba kure punde, be unasikira to adzofioamba; kagomba bekerebekere.
**Lula,** *dem. pron.* *See* Kidahi.
**Lulo.** *See* Fuirua.
**Lulolongo,** or **Lulongo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ndongo) (= Muthia). *See* Lungana. A row, a line. Atu adzidema lulolongo, ku enenda. Adzidema ndongo

*Footer: 224*

## [PDF Page 238 — Dictionary Page 225 (Lul — Lum)]

  mbiri, hebu tahu. Gnombe sidema lulongo (= in Kid., Sinalongosana lulongo). Gnombe sira sidema lulongo; ka-si-ka enenda wamba, sidzidema lulongo. Adema ndongo mbiri, They cut two rows or lines; *i.e.* They formed themselves into two lines.
**Lulu,** *dem. pron.* (rel. to the lu class) (= Hilu). Luhu; Luno; Lulo; Lula. Like a pearl. Lungo lulu, or, hilu.
**Luma,** *v.a.* *See* Pfungo; Ukongo. (1) To bite, to sting, to give pain. Nioka ni ku yunaluma, A serpent bites. Niuchi ni ku luma, A bee stings. Kuro yunaluma, The dog bites. Kironda kinaluma, A wound gives pain. Kidzoa kina-ni-luma, My head aches. Ndani ina-ni-luma; lit. Within me is pain; My belly aches, gives me pain. Ku luma meno.
(2) To shut one's teeth (*see* Pengo); to gnash kaa koro, one's teeth (*see* Gnasa; Kakata).
  **Lumana,** *v. reit.* (= Lindana; Kij., Gasana), (1) to bite one another.
  (2) Niama mguisi akiheha, ni ku lumana. Kivesa kikafungua, kikalumana. Menoge gakalumana; ka-ga-na miania (= lindana).
  **Lumia,** *v.a.*
  **Lumika,** *v.a.*, to cup. Udze-u-ni-lumike, Come and cup me. Cupping is very common, and is practised in a very barbarous manner.
  **Lumikika,** *v.n.*, (1) to admit of cupping. Vatu varivo musosa, ka-va-lumikika.
  (2) To prove well cupped. Nidzi-m-lumika, ela miladzo ka-i-kahensa kudza kakalumikika to.
  **Lumikira,** *v.d.* and *instr.* Ndzo, uka-ni-lumikire muanangu. Pembe ya ku lumikira.
  **Lumikisa,** *v.* Udzihenda dzukula ku lumikisa nawe!
  **Lumira,** *v.* *See* Siika; Dorosa. Nidzikuala nidzilumira. Yudzebua yudzilumira. Gnania yunalumira na kironda, Gnania is suffering from a wound.
  **Lumirua,** *v.p.*
  **Lumisa,** *v.a.*, to hurt, to grieve. Yudzi-m-piga hata yudzi-m-lumisa. Neno hiri rina-m-lumisa moyoni, moyo udzihenda dzoho.
  **Lumua,** *v.p.* *See* Nionga; Ufiusi. (1) To be bitten or stung.
  (2) To be pained, to be in pain, to suffer. Mukongo yunalumua. Yunalumua nini? What does he suffer from? lit. What is he pained by? Yunalumua ni ndani. Yunalumua ni muiri osi.
  **Lumualumua,** *v.* *See* Runda. To be sickly.
**Lumba,** (1) *v.a.*, to descry. Gnania yunalumba keri, ela ni Mulongo. Basi ku lumba udzi-vi-henda kondo we?
(2) *v.n.*, to debate. Gnania yunalumba to, akilumba, malauge yunaerekesa. Yukudzahenda-ni naye kaidima ku lumba?
  **Lumbana,** *v.n.* Mutu hiye ni mulumbi, kundawesa ku lumbana na-ye. Hunalumbana malau.
  **Lumbanira.** Hudzilumba mwezi. Hudzilumba dzahazi kura tu baharini, dzahazi hirira-rinagnala. Nidzilumba mutu kura tu kure. Udzi-m-lumba vi? Resp., Nidzi-m-lumba kura tu yunaderemuka dzomvu.
  **Lumbira.** Muezi hudzi-u-lumbira vava. Muezi hudzi-u-lumbira nchirani. Muezi hiu ni wa hahu, hudzao-u-lumbira vava; but, Muezi hiu ni wa hahu, udzao-hu-lumbira vava, is also used. Hangu huakudza, hudzimala miezi miiri kamiri, udzao-hu-lumbira hikara, ni wa hahu,

## [PDF Page 239 — Dictionary Page 226 (Lum — Lun)]

  or, hiu hu-ri-o na-o ni wa hahu. Muezi hiu hua-u-lumbira njirani.
  **Lumbirua,** *v.p.* Nafungua Kisiwani, hata muezi udzi-ni-lumbirua kuko, and, udzi-ni-lumbira kuko. Hudzilumbirua ni muezi hu vava Unguja.
  **Lumbua,** *v.p.* M'esi wa ku lumbua (= M'ezi wa ku andama in Kij.). M'esi ungalumbua, muari mudziuka kare, hebu muari muchari kuko? Resp., Huari hudziuka kare m'esi hiu wa-hu-lumbirua nchirani. M'esi udzilumbua rero.
  **Lumbuka** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Rumbuka in Kir., and Limbuka in Kij.). *See* Ku limbua; Ku davula; Uthaka. Lit. to finish waiting; hence, to enjoy the firstfruits.
  **Lumbukisa.** Yudzi ni uza, na mi ka mu lumbukiza.
  **Lumbusa, Lumbuza** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Rumbusa in Kir.). Yudzi-hu-lumbuza vitu via muaka, or, vitu via furi.
  **Lumbusania,** *v. reit.* Atu hio niku lumbusania-iye aifuisaye kitu mbere, basi ni kuenda-mu-lumbusa muyawe.
  **Lumbusua,** *v.p.*
  **Lumfia,** *v.a.* Ni madzi ga ku lumfia mwezi. Ni mamfula ga ku lumfia mwezi. Kumi hiri ndo ra ku lumfia mwezi; or, Kumi hiri ni ra ku lumba mwezi.
**Lumbua** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Gniere in Kir.). Gnombe za lumbua.
**Lumbui,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Ndiye niama a-dzi-galusaye muiri. Gnania yudzigaluka muiri dza lumbui ni ukongo wa safura, ndo ugalusao muiri.
**Lume,** *n.* and *adj.* *See* Muhua. Male, masculine. Mukono wa ku lume; lit. The male *hand* = the right hand. Muana lume, for, Mulume, A male child, a boy, a male offspring. *See* Kidana.
**Lumenga,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), one. Lukodza lumenga.
**Lumenga,** *adv.*, once. Nidzigema lumenga.
**Lumfindu,** *n.*, (1) (= Luhandu).
(2) Trop., deception, illusion. Madzo gangu gadzihenda lumfindu, ka-ga-ona. Madzoge gana lumfindu, kaona to. Yudzi-hu-sara lumfindu; or, Yudzi-hu-piga lumfindu angue: yunalafia chombo; lit. He daubed a film upon us; *i.e.* He deceived us, saying, He is taking out a vessel. *See* Mulindi.
**Lumfo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Mfo). *See* Fidio. Uganga wa lumvo.
**Lumfui,** *n.* (lua, pl. Mfui). *See* Uaki. One gray hair.
**Lumiri,** *n.* *See* Lumuiri.
**Lumodzo,** *n.* (pl. Vimodzo), a left-handed person. Yuna lumodzo, He is left-handed. Gnania akirima, yurima na ku modzo; kuani yuna lumodzo. Osi airi ana vimodzo.
**Lumuaji** (Kid.), *n.* (lua). Lumuaji lua gnombe.
**Lumue,** *n.*, the name of a dance, performed when the moon is seized by the Koloa. The custom is, however, nearly abandoned, only the young people keeping it up. Ku fuina lumue.
**Lumuiri,** *n.* (lua). *See* Muirika. One or two palm leaves kindled for giving a hasty light in the cottage. Lumuiri lua lukanzu, ku-m-m'irikira mutu akichakana.
**Luna,** *pron.* (rel. to the lu class), it with, with it. Nidzi-lu-fiula-lunaniola, viz. Luembe, I have sharpened, stroked, it, it shaves, viz. a razor.
**Lu-nda,** *pron.* *See* Wawiwa. It will.
**Lu-nga,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class). *See* Nga; Lala. It is like.

## [PDF Page 240 — Dictionary Page 227 (Lun — Luo)]

**Lunga,** *v.a.* (1). *See* Sagira; Muvilivili; Unga. To season, to salt.
(2) (Kid.) (in Kir., Ku dua), to follow, to go after.
  **Lungana** (Kidigo and Kid.), *v. reit.* (= Duana in Kir.). *See* Sunganira. Atu hara 'enda-vi, adzio lungana lulongo? Where are those men going who follow each other in a line?
  **Lungania,** *v.a.*, to join by tying together. Lukue ludzitoka, be na-lu-lungania. Madzere gangu na-ga-lungania mukoa.
  **Lunganika,** *v.n.* Yudzilungania mulala-udzilunganika. Udzidzuvuka-ka-u-kalunganika to.
  **Lunganira,** *v.d.* Gnania yudzi-ni-lunganira milala.
  **Lunganirua,** *v.p.*
  **Lunganisa,** *v.a.* (= Lungania).
  **Lungika,** *v.n.* Wari hiu udzilungika to. Mboga idzilungua-to, idzilungika.
  **Lungira,** *v. rel.* and *dat.*, to season with. Kavana cha ku lungira, There is nothing to season with. Ni-pa vidzuniu nikalungire, Give me a little salt to season with. Kuamba una muniu uka-ni-hegere vidembe, nidze nilungire mbogatables with it. Naenda, or, N'enda, umanie mboga zangu, zikiifua, u-ni-lungire. Ni-pa mafuha nikalungire tumbaku yangu.
  **Lungirua,** *v.p.*, to be seasoned, to have one kind of food seasoned by another. Nidzilungirua ni gnania.
  **Lungua,** *v.p.*, to be seasoned.
  **Lungukiza,** *v.a.* (= Ku udzikiza). *See* Hongosa. To reply, to join in speech, implying willingness, readiness; when in anger, Udzikisa must be used. Nidzigomba naye, ka-ka-ni-lungukiza. Yudzi-ni-uza neno, be na-mi ka-mu-lungukiza.
  **Lungukisana,** or **Lungukizania,** *v. reit.* Wamba vari na kondo vo? hudzi henda lungukizania tu-basi iye na ku dzama.
  **Lunsa, Lunza** (Kid.), *v.a.*, to lay together. Ku lunsa milala.
  **Lunsania** (Kid.) (= Lungania in Kir.; Runsisa and Runsidza in Kins.). Ku lunzania madzere, To lay Indian corn together.
**Lungi,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), much.
**Lungina,** or **Lungine,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), another.
**Lungo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niungo), something shallow, a winnowing-basket, very shallow. Lungo lulu, or, hilu ni luehu, This lungo is ours. Lungo lua kobe, The shell of a tortoise. Lungo lua kala. Lungo lua koe. Lungo lua kolokovue. Niungo zira hendua za mongo wa mulala, wa mudzapu, na wa mukindu. Those made of the mukendu palm are considered the most durable. Dim., Kadzungo and Kidzungo; magn., Dzungo.
**Lunialu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Minialu). Lunialu hilu ludzirehua ni peho; kunadzomua, dzanzala kuko kure. Kavana ndere ya muhaso; mbadikeni minialu.
**Lunialu,** or **Lugnialu** (Kig.), *n.* (pl. Mignialu), dung, manure. From Ku niala, To dry up.
**Luniania** (Kid.), *n.* (lua).
**Luniasi,** *n.*, a kind of grass. Luniasi lui, A bad, *i.e.* poisonous, grass or herb. Mbuzi idzeria luniasi lui, idzihuluka.
**Lunioga,** *n.* (lua, pl. Nioga), a feather.
**Luno.**
**Luo,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the lu

## [PDF Page 241 — Dictionary Page 228 (Luo — Luv)]

  class), thy. Luvandeluo, Thy piece.
**Luofu,** *adj.* *See* Kasa.
**Luonio.** *See* L'onio.
**Lupfu** (?). Ku ona lupfu.
**Lurauko,** *n.* Gnania yuna luraukoe, yudzikudza-ni-lamusa tiramuko kukuni, kudza danadana to, Gnania rises early indeed, he came to awake me at cock-crow, before daybreak; lit. when not dawning well or properly (Kudza = Kusa).
**Lure,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), long. Lufuiho lure.
**Lurero,** *n.* (lua). *See* Fugira. A percentage given out of the profits for breeding goats, sheep, fowls, etc. Yudzikumisa, yunahewa lurero. Nidzifuza kuku wa mutu, be yudzifiala, nidzihewa lurero. Luero ni lua mbuzi na kuku, ela gnombe ka-i-na lurero. Murisa wa gnombe ni ku hewa reale hebu mbuzi, ela kahewa lurero lua gnombe yegnie.
**Lu-ri-lo,** *particles* used in conjugation (implying the perf. tense, and rel. to the lu class), that which.
**Lurimi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Ndimi), the tongue. Fig., talkativeness. Gnania yuna lurimi; lurimilue ka-lu-lala na ndzala; yunasema muno. Lurimilue luna uere.
**Lurindi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Gnindi). Lurindi lua ku vekedzera moho.
**Lusemo,** *n.* (lua). *See* Dadalika. The propensity of telling tales. From Ku sema.
**Lusi, Luzi,** *n.* (lua, pl. Niuzi), thread, sewing-cotton. Niuzi za dzere, The hairy tuft which grows on cobs of Indian corn.
**Lusiho,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), heavy. Lukue lusiho.
**Lusihu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Dzihu), a narrow strip of platting, which is worked into mats, baskets, *and bags*.
**Lusikiro,** *n.* (lua), obedience. Muana hiyu yuna lusikiro, lua ku-m-sikira babaye hebu mameye; kula mameye a-mu-ambira fio basi naye yunaguira ira-tu vi fio.
**Lusiku,** *adj.*
**Lusima, Luzimo,** *adj.*, whole, entire, sound. Lukolo luzima, The whole kindred. Lukansa luzima, A whole branch of a cocoa-nut.
**Lusinga,** *n.* (lua, pl. Dzinga). *See* Usinga; Mulili.
**Lusisi,** or **Lusiso,** *n.* Gnania yuna lusisi, yuenenda akisisa; yunahensa gnansi muno. Iye kana lusisi, akinenda ni ku signia tu.
**Lusonia,** *n.* (lua, pl. Dzonia) (= in Kij., Upenu and Kipenu), the eaves of a hut or cottage. Lusonia lua niumba. Dzonia sa niumba.
**Lusuania** (Kid.), *n.* (= Lusonia).
**Lusumbulo,** *n.* (lua), the propensity of reminding others of past favours. From Ku sumbula. Gnania yuna lusumbulo muno, aki-ku-va kitu, basi udziguira zani, yunda-ku-sumburira.
**Luthua** (Kig.) (= Ndele).
**Luuso,** *n.* (lua). Una luuso muno. Gnania naye yuna luuso fio be ni luuso luani lo? Ni luuso luani hilo?
**Luvaha.** *See* Luhuaha.
**Luvala,** *n.* (lua, pl. Pala, za). Ku niola luvala, in contradistinction to Ku niola tengere. Yudzipigua luvala (= Yudziniolua luvala; but the latter expression is becoming obsolete).
**Luvande,** *n.* (lua, pl. Pande). *See* Dzapukira; Kanda, *n.* A piece, a tract of land. Luvande lua nguo, lua niama, etc., A piece of cloth, of meat, etc. Aravai ana luvandeluao lua dzi, na Aduruma ana luvandeluao. Dim., Kavande and Kivande; magn., Rivande.

## [PDF Page 242 — Dictionary Page 229 (Luv — Maa)]

**Luvanga,** *n.* (lua, pl. Panga), (1) a cave, a den. Mifiu ya Kidzomba hunaiha panga.
(2) The name of a species of vulture.
**Luvani,** *n.* (lua, pl. Pani). Magn., Rivani, pl. Mivani.
**Luvasi** (Kidigo), *n.* (lua) (= Kibawa in Kir.).
**Luvayo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Paya) (= Bayo), idle talk. From Ku vaya. The word also occurs in the dim. form, Kavayo. Yuna maneno mangi yuna luvayo, He has too many words; he has, or uses, idle talk. Mutu hiye manenoge ni luvayo luvuvu lua ku dzesia atu. Muna luvayo muno, kamu niamala!
**Luveho,** *n.* (lua, pl. Peho), a moderate wind. Luveho luvudzu luambamba. Dim., Kaveho and Kiveho, also Kabeho and Kibeho; magn., Riveho and Ribeho.
**Luveko,** *n.* (lua), the propensity or habit of bellowing or scolding. Kuro hiyu yuna luveko muno. Mutu yuna luveko 'ye! yudzivekera anae, hata nalola ana adzidzi, kunsa kua oga.
**Luveve,** *n.* (lua, pl. Miveve). From Ku veva. Luveve ni choa cha muvunga, ki sicho na tembe, ni gova vuvu. Muvunga wangu ukafira, ni miveve mivuvu.
**Luveveya,** *adj.* *See* Veva. Light, as a feather, chaff, etc. Lunioga ni luveveya, kua kura ku veva.
**Luvi.**
**Luvi,** *n.* (lua and wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name of a species of bird, fond of muhama. Luvi ni afuaha adzongo akala kundi anauruka kivimenga.
**Luvia,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), new.
**Luvia,** *adv.* *See* Remesana. Once more.
**Luviero,** *n.* (lua, pl. Piero). Luviero lua ku vierera. Luviero lua chedi, and, lua lukolo. Dim., Kaviero; magn., Riviero.
**Lu-vi-lo,** *particles* and *prons.*
**Luvi-lo.**
**Luvindo,** *n.* (lua, pl. Pindo). *See* Dzundula. The corner of a garment. Luvindo lua nguo. Dim., Kavindo.
**Luvohe,** *n.* (lua, pl. Pohe), a bowstring. Dim., Kavohe; magn., Rivohe.
**Luvudzu,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class), thin. Lukano luvudzu.
**Luvundo,** *n.* (lua), smell of corruption. Vana luvunde lui, vakafua niama, hebu vanuka-ni?
**Luvunga,** *n.* (lua, pl. Punga, za), the blossom of the cocoa-nut, the cocoa-nut in its first stage of growth.
**Luvuvu,** *adj.* (rel. to the lu class). Ludzaga ni luvuvu.
**Luvuyi,** or **Luvuyu,** *n.* (lua, pl. Puyi or Puyu), (1) a fibre. Of plants only.
(2) A single hair. Luvuyu lua niere. Luvuyu lua ukonche, unanazi, umbuiga, etc.
**Luyeyo,** *n.* (lua). Muana yuna luyeyo hiyu! Uenende hangu chiramuko, usimanie ku uya, kudza londa chunga, ela usinde kuko hata udze dziloni, be ni luyeyo luani lo? Undakala mukaha muana hiwe, or, muana uwe.

## M.

**M,** the thirteenth letter of the alphabet, often used as a prefix to other words.—[ED.]
**Ma,** within. As a prefix to a verb, it expresses the idea that what is indicated in the verb is contained in the object spoken of.
**Maalamu,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class). *See* Alamu. Broad. Makasha higa ni maalamu, These boxes are broad.
**Maalamu,** *n.* (= Walamu, Ualumu), width, breadth.
**Maalamuzi,** *n.* (ga). *See* Golokera.

*Footer: 229*

---

## [PDF Page 243 — Dictionary Page 230 (Maa — Mab)]

  Judgment. Mualamuzi yudzialamula maneno, maneno adza go alamula be ni maalamuzi.
**Maana** (Kij.), *n.*, meaning, interpretation. Rarely used in Kir.; their own word being Ukomo.
**Maandanda,** *adv.* *See* Thumba. Coming in slight contact with. From Ku anda (= Lukandakanda). Only used in connection with the words Ku fumaga and Ku doma. Nidzi-m-fumaga maandanda, or, lukandakanda, I have shot it so as merely to graze it, *e.g.* an animal. When a person is spoken of, the *m*, of course, must be translated by "him" or "her."
**Maango,** *n.* (sing. Ango). Maango gano gadzafio fungua si gangu, niumba idzifugulua (= mafungo).
**Maario** (Kidigo), *n.* (ga, pl. of Luario).
** Maasali** (?) (= Ga maneno).
**Maaso,** *n.*, thoughts.
**Mabadano, Mapatano,** *n.*, anything obtained; hence, an agreement. From Ku pata, To obtain.
**Mabahe,** *adj.*, a good many, pretty many. Ela ukahenda mabawa o m'bawa? But has that bean plant produced any beans? Resp., Ah ga-mo ga kahenda, ni mabahe. Kana madzere ga keri, ela ni mabahe. Ninga-ku-ambira maneno, ela ni mabahe, na-mi nina haraka, n'enenda, be ndakudza ni-ku-ambire dziku ingine.
**Mababangao** (Kid.), *n.* (= Madu ya ngoma).
**Mabamaba,** *n.* (ga). *See* Mbawa. Spots, such as are near together. N.B.—This word has no sing. form; to express this, Bato or Dono or one of the diminutives is used. Gnombe hino ina mabamaba, This cow has spots; is spotted. Gnombe *hino i* mabamaba, This cow is spotted. Gnombe hiza zina mabamaba, or, zi mabamaba, These cattle have spots, or They are spotted. Niuni hiyu yuna mabamaba, or, yu mabamaba. Kitu hiki kina mabamaba, or, ki mabamaba. Nidziona nguo ina mabamaba, or, i mabamaba. Lunioga lua kanga lu mabamaba; but, kanga yu mabamaba. Dzui yuna mabamaba, or, maramara.
**Mabaramabara,** *n.* (ga) (= Mabamaba), streaks, lines of colour.
**Mabaro** and **Mabaso,** *n.* (ga), familiarities, the art of making familiar and common, or getting accustomed to. Unga sikira akihukana atu, be ni mabaro ga babaye na mameye, ka-m-kanira, When you hear him abusing people, know it is the familiarity with his father and mother; they deny him nothing.
**Mabato,** *n.* (ga, sing. Bato), spots of colour different from the rest, and larger than the mabamaba. Mabatomabato, Various or many spots. Daradasi idziduenerua ni wino, idzihenda mabatomabato. Mabato gadze go? What spots are they? Resp., Ina mabato m'iru na m'eruve.
**Mabawa,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Bawa) (= Mbawa), a species of broad bean.
**Mabawale** (Kid.), *n.* (= Mabaw'a in Kir. and Kij.), a kind of wild beast.
**Mabawasi,** *n.*
**Mabawasi,** *n.* (ga) (= Mbalanga in Kij.), a painless cutaneous disease. It appears in the hands and feet, and the skin becomes white.
**Mabema, Mapema,** *n.* (ga). *See* Kuankurika; Haya; Dzuesa; Shuhuli; Huari. Early, at an early hour. Yukudza na mapema, dzua rinalewalewa. Ku chari mapema, It is still early. Mudziifuisa wari ma-

*Footer: 230*

---

## [PDF Page 244 — Dictionary Page 231 (Mab — Mad)]

  pema higa, or, na-mapema higa. Enenda kuenu mapema, kuchari gnala, ka-ku-dzankue ku handa, kukakala usiku.
**Mabendeleano** (Kij.). Adzigomba mabendeleano, kakaalamula keri. Mayo yudzi-ni-amba; n'ende mapema kuehu ni s'ende usiku.
**Mabengo.** *See* Bengo.
**Maberoa,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Beroa, ra), the guava.
**Mabesi, Mapesi** (Kij.), *adj.*, light, quick. Masikiro mapesi, Quick ears.
**Mabila,** *n.* *See* Dzaladzala.
**Mabishi,** *n. pl.* (ga). *See* Duku; Ubishi. Acts of contumacy.
**Mabisua,** *n.* (ga).
**Mabomu,** *adj.*, great, large.
**Mabu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Ibu), a species of fly, somewhat smaller than the house-fly. The country is said to have been full of them formerly, and, as they lived in the grass, were especially tormenting to the grazing cattle, so that they would soon return home. Now it is rarely seen.
**Mabulu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Bulu), worms.
**Mabusa,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Busa, ra) (= Madzavukusi), a sprout, a bud; (K.) sprig. Kisiki hiki kidzimera mabusa. Muhi hura udzihenda mabusa. Mabusa ni ga mahi, kisiki, udzaodemua.
**Mache,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class). *See* Magonche; Masu. Female.
**Machego,** *n.* *See* Majego. Teeth.
**Machelekano.**
**Machelema,** *n.* (= Chege in Kij.).
**Macheresa.** Muesi wa macheresa.
**Machero,** *adv.* *See* Mbeko; Dia; Muelo; Dzanganikana. (1) To-morrow.
(2) In the future.
**Mada, Maja,** *n.* (ga), lightning; (K.) fulguration. Maja gana meka.
**Madafe** (Kig.), *n.* (= Niara in Kij.), booty, plunder, hostages.
**Madafu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dafu), the cocoa-nut when partly ripe and full of water.
**Madaha** (Kij.), *n.*, sacrifices, graceful behaviour, words anointed with oil. A-dzi-dunsaye muiri-we, ni ku ambua: yuna madaha. Ni utu wa ku pendeza. Gnania yuna mafualo madzo-ga madaha. Gnania yunarima porepore ku ika niazi to na madaha. Yunafimba niumba to na madaha. Gnania yunagomba maneno madzo, wamba: gakasarua mafuha; yugomba na madaha. Gnania yunaenenda to na madaha.
**Madama,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dama).
**Madamada,** *n.* (*adj.*?)(ga), partly dry.
**Madanga,** *n.*
**Madano,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dano).
**Madara,** *n.*, (K.) palsical. From Ku dara or Ku dala. Muiri udzi-ni-piga madara, Being startled. Gnania ni mukongo muno, muiri una-m-piga madara yunadedema.
**Madaradio,** *n.* (ga). Gnania yuna madaradio mai kitu kichache iye ni ku henda kaze n'ima punde yukudza isa punde yukudza isa, or, ni susususu tu kudza isa be atu ka avaha?
**Madaro,** *n.* (ga). Madaro ga Kitaita, akigusa pembeye, ni mangi, kula kitu adare, kula kitu adare. Mutaita akigusa pembeye, be sudi uume, kuani, yunda-ku-darira madaro ga kula kitu, akibuma mumo pembeni.
**Madasa,** *n.* *See* Kibondonkue.
**Mademi,** *n.*, a cut, new wound. Dana ya mademi, Medicine for cuts, etc.
**Madeso,** *n.*
**Madete,** *n.* Ku ji piga madete.
**Madeuso** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Ndumo in Kir.). Neno ra madeuso.
**Madi, Maji,** *n.* (pl. of Idi, Iji).
**Madide, Matite,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class), small.

*Footer: 231*

---

## [PDF Page 245 — Dictionary Page 232 (Mad — Mad)]

**Madidimizo,** *n.* (ga), distant thunder. Rarely used. Mfula inadidimisa madidimisa ganasikirika kure mfula hio i kure.
**Madidimuko,** *n.* (ga). Amasai avokudza kudamfa gnombe na ku ulaga atu, gari madidimuko gani go! Madidimuko higo gari mabomu atu a-godidimuku; hangu urumengu ku diekua, kahu-dza-ona mbulagua dza hino.
**Madiki,** *n.* Masia gadzikala madiki ga naifua. Masia gadziifua ga dzikala madiki.
**Madiko,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Diko) (= Madiko ni ga niere), (K.) tufts of hair.
**Madiriri,** *n.* (ga) (= Udiriri). Kare kuari na madiriri ga udzai, mutu akakuenda loga mutu, kidza, mutu akakuenda mignia mutu kua udzai. Be ni madiriri gani gano, mudza-go-henda, mundakala adiriri. *See* Mudiriri.
**Madobesa,** *n.* (ga).
**Madofia,** *n.* (ga), mud. Rero kuna madofia; mfula idzegnia ningi, To-day there is mud; rain has fallen much. Dzi ya ludzanga ka-i-na madofia. Vana madofia, ka-va-enendeka, ela dzi ya ngama na dzulu na dzi i-ri-o na kilongo.
**Madongo,** *n.* (ga), matter, from the eyes only. From Ku donga in Kij. Gnania yunala madongo; or, Madzoge gadzihenda madongo.
**Madono.** *See* Dono.
**Madoro.** *See* Doroka.
**Madu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Idu, ra, *q.v.*).
**Madudumiso,** *n.* (ga) (= Madidimiso).
**Madudusi,** *n.* (ga). *See* Choga. From Ku duduka. Gnania yudzi kupukua ni madudusi muiri osi.
**Maduene,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Duene).
**Madugudugu,** *n.* (ga). *See* Mukuamba; Kimumunie. Small protuberances, or excrescences. Dim., Vidugudugu.
**Madulusi,** *n.* (ga) (= Mabishi).
**Madumaini, Matumania** (Kij.), *n.* (ga), trust, confidence, firmness of mind. Mimi na gnania huna matumaini ga ku tuma'niana. Mutu hiye moyowe una matumaini, hata uka-m-fidina, kakubali.
**Madumanio,** *n.* (ga) (= Madumaini).
**Madune,** *adj.*, red.
**Madungo,** *n.* *See* Marero. From Ku dunga. Gnania ni mukongo, yuna Mulungu, yulonda madungoge, urembowe, afuikue, basi mutu hiye yundavola.
**Madza** (Kidigo). Ku aka niumba sa madza (= Kir., Ku guira musena).
**Madzacha** (Kigiriama), *n.* (= Chiramuko in Kir.), morning. Yudzachira haha madzacha (= Kir., Yudzichira vava chiramuko).
**Madzafu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dzafu), cheeks.
**Madzaje, Madzache,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dzaje) (= Madonga in Kir.), the fruit of a tree.
**Madzanga,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class). *See* Mamfula; Dzafu.
**Madzango,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dzango, ra). *See* Kidindi; Mukodo. Wire of the thickest kind imported. Madzango ga gnandu, Brass wire. Madzango ga mukundua, Copper wire.
**Madzano.** *See* Gola.
**Madzansu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dzansu), branches.
**Madzadzigo,** *n.* (ga). *See* Dasana. Hangu dzana ahoho adziguira madzadzigo ga Kikamba, ga ku wana na ndada; ela Aravai akare ari akifundana mavi.
**Madzedzebe,** *n.* (ga). *See* Sherehe. Foolishness, stupidity. Una madzedzebe mangi uwe. Muanagnombe kana madzedzebe mangi (= in comparison with a goat).
**Madzere,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dzere),

*Footer: 232*

---

## [PDF Page 246 — Dictionary Page 233 (Mad — Maf)]

  Indian corn. Madzere ga arisa. *See* Dzerere.
**Madzevuso,** *n.* (ga). From Ku dzevula. Madzevuso ga mabusa.
**Madzi,** *n.* (ga), water. Madzi ga peho, Rain-water. Madzi ga muniu, Salt water. Madzi ga kunde, Dirty water. *See* Kunde. Trop., Moyo wa madzi, A heart of water; *i.e.* timidity, cowardice. Yuna moyo wa madzi (= Ni mutu muoga). Dim., Vidzi.
**Madzifundi,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Dalamu. Lit. one who teaches himself; *i.e.* a learner of an art or trade, an apprentice. Musana hiyu ni madzifundi, ka-dza-mania, to; Yuna-dzi-fundaka dzankue ku mania.
**Madzimadzi,** *adj.*, wet, damp. Nguo hi i-madzimadzi, idziloama. Mboga hizi zi-madzimadzi muno, zi-lueluelue. Kavu yangu i-madzimadzi, n'enda, nika-i-anike, ifuhuke.
**Madzinsi,** *n.* (ga), meat taken as wages for slaughtering an animal. Hunahala madzinsigehu (= Mafungu ga ku dzinsa).
**Madzo,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class), good. Maneno madzo, Good words.
**Madzo,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dzidzo). *See* Dzorua; Kua; Haya; Midzidzo. The eyes.
**Madzomadzo,** *adv.* (= Kimato in Kij.), awake, not being asleep. Ku lala madzomadzo (= Kusa pata usinsisi), To lie awake. Ku lala madzomadzo, kua urinsi, To lie awake on account of watching a plantation.
**Madzodzo,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dzodzo), heads of Guinea-corn, which have fallen to the ground, or such as are not thickly set with grains. Kuna madzodzo ga bua go-dzi. Kuna madzodzo, gaimire go, ela ka-ga-ka buma tembe muno, or, ka-ga-ka fuika tembe gakalonda ku-fira; tembese ni daladala. Mukadzagule madzodzo mundani, mudze, mukute, muhende kilariro.
**Madzomo.** *See* Bengo.
**Madzongi,** *n.* (ga). Madzongi higano ga-nga ga gnania fulani; ndo madzongi-ge garivio. Nidziona madzongige adzongavio.
**Madzosi,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dzosi). Madzosiga peho.
**Madzuchi,** *n.* (ga) (in Kid., honeycomb; Mavalala in Kir.). Magn. of Uchi. Vana madzuchi mangi. Lusinga luna madzuchi mangi hilu.
**Madzukuriko,** *n.*, loads, carryings. Madzukuriko mairi, Two carryings—what may be carried in twice.
**Madzula,** *n.* (ga) (= Mianso). *See* Ku dzula. Minazi ichari madzula ka-i-dza henda muengero. Uchi wa madzula ni uchi ukiansa ku humbuka. Madzula gadziingira hangu dzana, atu anarea. Muezi hiu ni wa madzula, muezi wa machero, uchi ukiingira wa madzula, atu andalarika kuri. Idzikala kas'kasi madzula, atu anaukuha uchi hangu dzana.
**Madzumbuso,** *n.* Ana madzumbuso madzo atu hia, anahensa ageni.
**Madzuzi.** Pl. of Dzusi.
**Maenensi,** *n.* (ga), gait. Gnania yunaenenda to, maenenzige ni madzo. Gnania yuna maenenzi mai, akienenda yuenenda vidzoa vidzoa, kakadulisa muiri. Gnania maenensige ga haraka haraka, ela gnania, maenenzige niga pore.
**Maere,** *n.* (ga, sing. Ere), a kind of grain, red millet.
**Maerefu,** *n.* *See* M'erefu.
**Mafi, Mavi,** *n.* (ga), excrements, dross of iron. Mafi ga chuma, Dross of iron (= in Kid., Chomoe). Kabafi kachache.
**Mafiasi,** *n.*, birth, confinement.

*Footer: 233*

---

## [PDF Page 247 — Dictionary Page 234 (Maf — Maf)]

**Mafiererano,** *n.* (ga). Adzifiererana usiku to hata kudzecha mafiererano mangi tu.
**Mafierero,** *n.* (ga), scoldings. Yudzi-ni-fierera mafierero mai.
**Mafiga,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Figa). *See* Ririra; Meko. Kitchen.
**Mafingo,** *n. pl.* (ga) (= Mokofora; Kagafingo). Mafingo ni misi ya uganga, ya ku sikiha mudzi. Ku zika mafingo. Mudzi wa gnania ka-u-endeka na u siku, ukahendua mafingo, u sikihiwa. Muganga aki-ga-zika mafingo, akalomborera.
**Mafioka.** *See* Lalamira. From Ku fioka.
**Mafiolo,** *n.* (ga) (= Domeka). From Ku fiola.
**Mafiorerano,** *n.* (ga) (= Mafiererano).
**Mafiorero,** *n.* (ga) (= Mafierero), scoldings.
**Mafiosi,** *n.* (ga). From Ku fiola or Ku fiosa, What is cutting? Mafiosi ni maneno ga ukolo. Yudzigomba maneno ga mafiosi. Yudzifiola mafiosi mavuvu.
**Mafiru,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Firu, ra), the fruit of the tree called mufiru.
**Mafiuri,** *n.* (ga). *See* Malola. A slight squint. From Ku fiula. Madzoge gana mafiuri.
**Mafo,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Fo). *See* Kigongogo. (1) The fruit of a creeper called mufo.
(2) Small pieces of certain roots used in witchcraft in former times, but no more occurring now. They were buried near the abode of a man whom the sorcerer intended to injure, and by treading on the spot the desired effect would take place.
**Mafu,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class). *See* Makumbi. Dead, dried up, hard, difficult; matured, becoming. Madzi mafu (*see* Kimbuicha), Dead waters; *i.e.* that state of the water when the difference between high and low water is very small. Madzera mafu, Indian corn dried up. Adzomba ni ku amba: maneno ga kiravai ni mafu, hebu ni momu, ela ga kiriama ni mayuya, mangu-angu maolofu; na maneno ga kitaita nago ni mafu, ela kikamba ni cholofu, hebu kiyuya. Muana hiye yuna maneno mafu, kana oga wa ku nena, akadania madzo sana, yunagomba maneno ga kifiere halisi.
**Mafua,** *n.* (pl. of Fua).
**Mafuadzi,** *n.* (ga), mortality. Mafuadzi ga kare; kare atu ari akifua-adzikomala, ela hangu dzana mafuadzi ga hikara-afua akere ahoho, ka dza-komala to.
**Mafualo,** *n.* (ga). *See* Madaha. Gnania yuna mafualo madzo.
**Mafubefube** (Kid.), *n.* (ga, drizzling rain. Ni mafubefube tu, ela mvula ka-i-gnia, It drizzles only, but the rain does not come.
**Mafuemfuere,** *n.*, a feeling of heaviness, exhaustion, lassitude. Dzana wasinda chi kunoa uchi, akalala nao, basi vira kaidima kua mafuemfuere ga uchi. Mutu hiyu akachesa uira, kakalala usiku, be vira yuna mafuemfuere ga usinsisi.
**Mafufufu,** *n.* (ga) (= Mafubefube). Rero kuna mafufufu ga mfula, ni maduene matite kama kunde, To-day there is drizzle of rain, the drops are small as a fog. Mvula idzifika mundani? Resp., Idzifika mahemahe, idzihenda mafufufu tu, ela ka-i-kagnia bomu. Mafufufu gadzihenda fu-gakachira.
**Mafuha,** *n.* (ga). *See* Sagira. Oil, fat. Mafuha maidzi, Butter. Mafuha ga chu chita; or, Mafuha maifu, Ghee. Mafuha ga niama, or, ga kilo-

*Footer: 234*

---

## [PDF Page 248 — Dictionary Page 235 (Maf — Mag)]

  mba, Fat. Mafuha ga misosani.
**Mafui,** *n.* Ku muta mafui.
**Mafuindi.**
**Mafukuefukue.**
**Mafulo,** *n.* (ga). *See* Shukushula. A sour taste in the mouth on waking; lit. what wants to be drawn out and to be removed. From Ku fula, To draw out. Ni-pa uchi, ninoe, niuse mafulo.
**Mafumba.**
**Mafumfumafumfu** (Kid.), *n.* (ga), cloudy weather. Kunafania mafumfumafumfu (= Kins., Kuachida mipfupfu).
**Mafundango,** *n.* Mimbaye idzi-m-henda mafundango, basi kana kasi a wesayo, vilungo vina-m-gniognoniera. Gnania akienenda, ka signia; yuenenda kiche, yuna mafundango. Mutu akiika muiri muno, ndo ahenda-vo mafundango.
**Mafundo,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Fundo), knots, joints in a tree or cane. Mafundoge ga vevi kafuhusa m'ana.
**Mafundukui,** *n. pl.* (ga). Yudzilafia mafundukui ga pembe; *sc.* gnombe.
**Mafune,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Fune). Dzana nadzoka muno, muiri udzihenda mafune; rero na oya.
**Mafunganofungano,** *n.* (ga), entanglements. Rarely used. Maneno higo ga-nga mafunganofungano, ka-ga-na geri, wala ka-ga-manikana; hiyu yuna-m-singa, muyawe, naye yuna-m-singa muyawe-ni maneno ga dzungamisi, ga kiche.
**Mafungo,** *n.* (ga) (= Maango). Mafungo higa si gangu, mafungo-gangu na-ga-mania. Mafungo-gangu nidza-ga-funga sego, gadzifungua mafungo mangine. Mayo adzo fio funga sego, yudzifungirua mafungo mangine.
**Mafungu,** *n.* (ga). *See* Baha. An allowance, a portion, wages. Ku ria mafungu. Si mafunguge ariago kula dziku; yuria doti; ela wa-ni-uchirira mimi tu.
**Mafuno, Mavuno,** *n.* (ga). *See* Funa, Wau. Reapings.
**Mafunsigo,** *n.*, breaking, destruction.
**Mafutulo,** *n.* (ga). *See* Futurira. Rarely used.
**Magabu.** Kuku wa baba yudieka m'iyani, ni magabu (?).
**Magalagala,** *n.*
**Magande,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Gande). *See* Larirana. Magande ga atu (= atu dele).
**Magani,** *n.*
**Maganiko,** *n.* (ga). Hudzionana varatu maganikoni. Nidzi-mu-ona varatu maganiko ga nchira.
**Magari,** *n.* (ga) (= Niali in Kij.), messes of cooked grain, rice, Indian corn, etc. Magn. of Wari.
**Magaro,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Garo).
**Magau.** Midafu ni wisua wa mbere kua gara magauge. Magauga luhago ga magova.
**Mageiroa** (Kid.) (Maka in Kins.). Yudzi-ni-guira mageiroa (= Kir., Yudzi-ni-guira ndea, or, dzia).
**Mageso,** *n.*, temptation.
**Magirisi** (Kij. and Kiriama).
**Magniognioda,** *n.* (ga) (= Manionioda), drizzling rain. Kakuna mvula ya geri, ni magniognioda, hata ku lofia muiri ka-ga-lofia.
**Magnugnua,** or **Maniuniua** (= Mafufufu).
**Mago,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Luago). *See* Musekeneko; Sajika. The inner part of the thigh. Yudzihenda ivu ra magoni. Yudzienenda ku dania mago.
**Magofia,** *n.* (ga), bandy legs. Mutu hiyu yuna magofia. Maguluge gakalonda ku henda

*Footer: 235*

---

## [PDF Page 249 — Dictionary Page 236 (Mag — Mah)]

  magofia. Yuna-go (magofia) ela si mangi.
**Magomberamumo.** *See* Kidumbusi.
**Magonche.**
  **Magonchemache.**
  **Magonchemudzi.**
**Magongogo,** *n.* (ga). *See* Kigongogo.
**Magova,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Gova).
**Magovi,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Govi). Magova ni ga mihi. Magovi ni ga nafaka. Makanda ni ga tundo.
**Maguaju,** *n.* *See* Makuaju. The tamarind fruit.
**Maguguta,** *n. pl.*, cobs of Indian corn with only the leaves taken off; but Kiguguta is a cob of which the grains are plucked off. Madzere ga maguguta (= Madzere ga ku vavula, in contradistinction to Madzere ga makanda). N.B.—The sing. (Guguta) is not used; but they say, Dzere ra ku vavula, A cob of Indian corn with the leaves taken off.
**Magulu,** *n.* (ga, pl of Kigulu), the legs. Magulu ga dzua. Dzua rikiombola, rina magulu hata rikidana na dzi, basi gaka-angamika. Wau-di-hata kukidzua, rikizama, basi gakaoneka kahiri; ndo hu-amba-go ni magulu ga dzua. Rero magulu ga dzua ka-ga-ka oneka, gadzifidzua ni maingu.
**Magumbi,** *n.*, skein, hank. Magumbi ni ga lukue; but, Makumbi ni ga nazi. Ku piga magumbi.
**Maha,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Uha), a bow.
**Mahaba** (Kij.), *n.*, love, affection, between husband and wife. Mtumche hiye yuna mahaba, ni kura ku-m-dunsa mulume. Atu hio anahensania, kandadana; hiye muche yuna mahaba, na mulume naye yuna mahaba. Ku-u-na mahaba hio.
**Mahako,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Hako), the *fundament*, the seat; the bottom part of anything; foundation.
**Mahana,** *n.* (ga). *See* Doka, or Dosa; Choga. Sinda-ku-fidza, na-ku-ambira: ni mahana higa, gadzikala kare.
**Mahandiko,** *n.* (ga). Neno ra mahandiko rikaonewa rina uere; be hangu dzana siihua tandiko.
**Mahanga,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Hanga).
**Mahe,** *n.* (ga), saliva. Ku dzuva mahe. Mahe ga ku dzuva na ga ku fuluka madzo ni gavi-go? Resp., Madzo ni ga ku fuluka.
**Maheho,** *n.* (ga) (= Kondo), strife, quarrel. From Ku heha. Rarely used. The word in common use is Kondo. Atu hio kana theri muao niumbani ni maheho tu; kasumurira gnansi; ukisikira anagomba, basi anafiererana; muao niumbani ni maheho tu.
**Maheje,** *n.* (ga) (= Mugazija).
**Mahemahe.** Mfula idzihenda mahemahe ga ku lofia mutu. Mfula idzihenda mahemahe madzo-ga ku gesa madzi.
**Mahende,** *n.* (ga) (= Ukongowa).
**Mahendo,** *n.* (ga) (= Uchi wa hendo). *See* Udzengo; Ubora. Mahendo ni vira-tu vitu. Vitu hivi viosi atu alafia-fio ni mahendo ga ku henda kihendo.
**Mahensi, Mahenzi,** *n.* (ga), pleasure, will, love. From Ku henza.
**Mahombo,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Hombo).
**Mahua,** *n.* *See* Kulukulu; Tinge, or, Mavua (?).
**Mahuhu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Huhu). *See* Fuka; Lufuidzo. Lumps.
**Mahukano,** *n.* (ga). Yudzi-ni-hukana mahukano mai.
**Mahukuhu,** *n. pl.* (ga) (= Mafundukui). *See* Kiwembe.
**Mahumbo.** *See* Hindirika.
**Mahumbui,** *n.* (ga), glandular swellings, the mumps. Ma-

*Footer: 236*

---

## [PDF Page 250 — Dictionary Page 237 (Mah — Mak)]

  humbui ni ukongo wa madza funi. Kolo ra sikiro.
**Mahumiko,** *n.* (ga). Rarely used.
**Mahunda,** *n.* (ga). Ku lafia mahunda. Mahunda ga mfaya.
**Mai,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class), bad, wicked.
**Mai,** *n.* *See* Asira.
**Maidzi,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class), fresh, raw, green.
**Maifu,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class), ripe. Madzere maifu. Masia maifu.
**Maimbi,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Imbi), waves, billows.
**Maingu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Ingu), clouds. Rero kuna maingu ga mfula, To-day there are clouds of rain, passing showers.
**Mainsi,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Insi), flies.
**Maisa,** *n.* Ku risa maisa, To tend (cattle) by turn.
**Maishi** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Uaki. Life, lifetime. From Ku ishi, To live. Kuku kana maishi mangi. Kitu hiki kina maishi, ela kino ka-ki-na maishi. Niumba hi indahenda maishi kuani, ina mihi midzo.
**Majabali** (Kij.), *n. pl.* (ga). Maingu gadzihenda majabali chamba dzua rinabodoka.
**Majego,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Jego), the grinders.
**Majiba** (Kid.), *n.* (ga, pl. of Jiba) (= Maisa in Kir.), turn. Sambi ni jiba-ro, Now it is thy turn.
**Majira,** *n.* (ga). *See* Wau. Time. Majira higano adzekua nika. Hangu avo enenda, majira gaga, adzifika Ukambani. Dzana wa uka majira ga tiramuko. Dzusi majira higo wari, or, yuere yudziuka kare. Majira hukiajaliwa majira higo, hundakala hudzifika.
**Maka,** *v.n.*, to wonder, to sympathize. Una maka kiche, or, kihoho. Gnania yuna moyo mui wa ku ulaga yudzi-mu-ona muyawe kaidima, ela iye aka-m-chira, akaenenda, karurukua ni ku maka kabisa.
  **Makira,** *v. rel.* *See* Dai. To wonder at, to pity. U-makira-ni? ni utu ubomu wa ku makua-o? U-makira-ni? ku-dza ona utu uka-o-pita uno udza-o-hendeka? Yudzi-m-makira muyawe (= yudzi-mu-onera mbazi). Mutu yudziguirua ni ndani; basi gnania ndiye adzie-m-makira, aki-m-dzedzesa, aki-m-fisa kuakue. Mulungu na gnania, ndiye adzie-m-makira, kuamba si iye, angapigua angaulagua.
  **Makirana,** *v. reit.*, to pity one another. Atu hio anapatana anamakirana, kuamba atu osi anga dza ao, basi vingari vidzo.
  **Makirua,** *v.p.*, to be pitied.
  **Makua,** *v.p.*
  **Masha,** *v. caus.*, to astonish, to excite wonder, to excite pity. Neno hiri rina masha. Utu hiu una masha. Ukongo hio una masha. Huaona utu wa ku masha.
**Maitha,** *n.* *See* Mumaitha.
**Makabaila, Makabaila** (Kij.), *n.* Rarely used. Hangudzana ndio adzaokala makabaila, hebu masorodani, kamania mutu; akiona mutu asie kitu, be akaamba: ana kasi yani hara?
**Makabu.**
**Makadi,** *n.* (ga), time. Makadi higo, ana hia ari ka-dza fialua. Makadi higo huari hukari kutu kusiku, or, huere hukere kutu kusiku.
**Makadzombo,** *n.*
**Makafara** (Kij.), *n.* (pl. of Kafara), sacrifices to avert calamity.
**Makafiri** (Kij.), *n. pl.*, infidels, unbelievers in the false prophet Mohammed. Makafiri anafunsa kihi changu. Ni hira milungu. *See* Mulungu, 3; also called, Asonga niele.
**Makalakala,** *n.* (ga). *See* Peho, 2.

## [PDF Page 251 — Dictionary Page 238 (Mak — Mak)]

  The palate. Nidzevia makalakala. Nalumua ni makalakala.
**Makalo,** *n.* (ga). *See* Fiula. Room, space. Uka-ni-sukuma-we! or, Una-ni-sukuma! Resp., Be kuno kuna makalo? Niumba hino ni fufu, ka-i-na makalo, ka hundaenerua.
**Makanda, Maganda,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Kanda, Ganda). Makanda ga nazi, The husks of cocoa-nuts, when on; when off they are called Makumbi. Makanda ga madzere, The leaves of the cobs of Indian corn, when on; when off they are called Madzaragadza. Mgazija una makanda ga ndze na ga ndani. Makanda ga ndze ganagaulua na ku dzuvua. Madzere ga makanda; in contradistinction to Madzere ga maguguta.
**Makandakanda** (ga mimba) (= in Kij., Makanda ga mimba), the skin over the stomach. Malumua ni makandakanda ga mimba; or merely, Makanda ga mimba.
**Makani** (Kidigo) (= Kani in Kir.).
**Makansa.** *See* Lukansa. Kidigo, Nadzenga niumba ya makansa; Kir., Naaka niumba ya kansa. Nadzukula makansa ga ku dzomera dzalafu, hebu ga ku muirikira.
**Makari,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class), sharp, fierce. Gnania yudzukirua; yudzigomba maneno makari, Gnania is angry; he has spoken sharp words.
**Makari,** *n.*, fierceness, vehemence, violence. Mvula ya makari na-i-fiuke; mvula ya peho na-i-dze, The rain of vehemence, and be it off; the rain of softness, gentleness, and may it come. Said in prayer.
**Makasi.** *See* Muizi; Larira.
**Maki,** *n.*, thickness, stoutness, largeness. Muhi hiu una maki sana. Nguo hi ina *lusi*, ludzo, lusiho, ina maki.
**Makinda.**
**Makoba.**
**Makobero.** Mbalazi hisi ni makobero, *i.e.* ka-si-dzankue ku komala, cheteha kunde.
**Makodza.** Makodza maidzi. Makodza mafu.
**Makodzo,** *n.* (ga), urine.
**Makoko.** *See* Ukoko.
**Makolo.**
**Makololo,** *n.* (ga), phlegm. From Ku kolola.
**Makombo** (Kij.), *n.* (= Masasa in Kir.). *See* Karamu. The remainder of food. The word is only used in connection with the pepo.
**Makomo,** *n.* *See* Uaki.
**Makomu.** Yunamadzo makomu, yu muerefu.
**Makonde,** *n.*, (K.) fist, cuff.
**Makongo,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Kongo). *See* Dzupisa; Chinga. Diseases.
**Makoro.**
**Makosa,** *n.*, offence, fault, error.
**Makuacha,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Kuacha), a hoof.
**Makubuli** (Kij.) (= Masosa; Makombo).
**Makudi.** *See* Kansa.
**Makue,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Kue, *q.v.*).
**Makulu.** *See* Mamfula.
**Makumba,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Kumba). *See* Furunga.
**Makumbi,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Kumbi), (1) boughs. Makumbi ga munazi, The boughs of a cocoa-nut tree.
(2) Husks. Makumbi ga nazi, The husks of cocoa-nuts when stript off. *See* Makanda. Nazi ikifulua, ikisira, basi makandage gaihua makumbi. Makumbi ga madafu ni maidzi, ela ga nasipfu ni mafu.
**Makurima,** *n.* (ga) (= Mirimire), special ways of cultivating the ground. Mutu hiye yuna makurimage, hebu yuna ndimuaye, akirima ku dzimba

*Footer: 238*
