## [PDF Page 252 — Dictionary Page 239 (Mak — Mal)]

  dzi sana; yuna makurima madzo.
**Makutano,** *n.* (ga), meetings, assemblies. Rero kuna makutano ga afiere, kahumania a-ri-ro na-ro, To-day there is a meeting of the elders, but we do not know what it is for. N.B.—The pron. Ri and its rel. Ro refer to Dzambo or Neno being understood.
**Mala,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Chala) (= Viala), finger. Malagangu (= Vialaviangu), My fingers.
**Mala** (properly **Maala**), *n.* (ga, pl. of Ala), kicks. Ku piga mala, To kick.
**Mala,** *v.a.*, to finish, to make an end of, to spend. Rimani haraka, mu-va, or, musise, male, huenende. Nidzimala miezi miiri Ukambani, I have spent two months in Ukambani. N.B.—Ku henda is also used in the same sense. Der., Molo.
  **Malana,** *v. reit.* Atu hio analogana, andamalana.
  **Malua,** *v.p.* Madzigangu-gadzimalua niani?
  **Marika,** *v.n.*
  **Marikisa,** *v.a.*, to complete. Rimani haraka, hu-va-mari-kise na-mabema.
  **Marikisika,** *v.n.* *See* Doka. Madzi gadziuma, gadzimari kisika. Mutu yudzefua. Yudzimarikisika.
  **Marikisira,** *v.d.* Ni-pa, ni-ku-marikisire. Yudzi-ni-marikisira kavu yangu.
  **Marikisirua,** *v.p.*, to have anything finished by another. Yudzimarikisirua ni gnania, He has had it finished by Gnania.
  **Marikisua,** *v.p.* Fuere rindamarikisua rero.
  **Marira,** *v.d.* *See* Huahuira. Una-ni-marira vitu viangu. Nagula muniu mungi, ela atu adzi-ni-foya, hata adzi-nimarira.
  **Marirua,** *v.p.* Yudzifoyua-akilafia; yudzifoyua akilafia hata yudzimarirua.
**Malada,** *n.* (pl. of Yalada). From Mayalada.
**Malagano,** *n.* (ga). Malagano gehu hua-go-la-gana, ni rero.
**Malaika,** *n.*, angels, babies.
**Malalo,** *n.* (ga), sleep, rest, a sleeping-place. Hudzipata malolo kare hurere; or, Hudziguira malalo kare hurere, kahundauka. H'endeni husole malaloni na mapema. Malalogangu ni hiva (= ninda-lala hiva). Ka mu va malalo riulume.
**Malamu** (for **Maalamu**), *adj.* *See* Mare.
**Malamu,** *n.* (= Walamu), width, breadth. Nguo hi ina vana, ina malamu.
**Malamusi,** *n.* (ga). *See* Maalamusi.
**Malamusi,** or **Malamuso,** *n.* (ga), greetings. Rarely used. Malamusoge ni madzo mutu hiye.
**Malau** (Kidigo), *n.* (ga, pl. of Lau) (= Mioro in Kir., which, however, is less frequently used than Malau). *See* Ndarira; Moro. Trials, judicial debates. Hudzipiga malau-nika-m-chila (Kidigo) (= nika-m-thima in Kir.). Ka piga malau (= Ku aria mioro). Hudziihirua malau; hu'enda malauni, hu'enda for huaenda. Rero kuna malau.
**Malaumalau.**
**Male,** *n.* Shuka la male doti la, or, za male. Kau sahaursa yale mawaso.
**Malele,** *n.* From Ku lala. Amasai akudza-hu-guira malele, kuamba huamania, kahunga-dzi-fidzi? ela kahumanire, adzi-hu-guira malele. Nari simania-ni-malele, hata gnania akidza, udiye adzaye-ni-difia. Anae osi ere malele, kamanire kuamba ana-

*Footer: 239*

---

## [PDF Page 253 — Dictionary Page 240 (Mal — Mam)]

  dza, or, andakudza. Mutu hiyu yu-malele, kamania neno ri-ndaro kudza. Umalele, kulenga we, kumania kuna katha na katha. Usegere malele tu, kumania kuamba kondo inadza.
**Malengi,** *n.* (= Yunalengi maneno).
**Maleu,** *n.*
**Mali,** *n.* (ya and za). *See* Lilia. Wealth, property. Kakala mutu ni kufua aka uya, be nika uya nika-m-dikiza na mali yangu, ki i ngari kondo vio-ya ku ulagana, ela ukifua ndzifua. One at enmity with his brother will try to disinherit him when dying. He says, Hata nikafua nduga yangu na si ridi kitu changu korokoro. The relatives try to reconcile them, saying, Asifua na chala; but often without success. They reply, Afuaye ka laga ufua, yudzi-fua na shetani mui. Nafua mali yangu inadza ihalue ni gnania aridi ahi; kakala mutu ni ku uya moyo kahiri, be ningakudza mu ona yuna mali yangu kai ngkala kondo vio? Ela ukifua ndzifua. Gnania yunadzahala mui yangu aridi ahi, be kuamba ni moyo, anga-i-pata ye?
**Maliko,** *n.* (ga). *See* Kiliko.
**Malimau,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Limau), lemons.
**Malinkua.**
**Malo,** *n.*, a run, a race. Ku piga malo, To run.
**Malomalo.** U-malomalo fio unani? Resp., Kudzifewa ni gnania musiku. H'enda malomalo, nirie, nienende.
**Malola,** *n.* Gnania yuna malola, aki-ku-lola, wamba; yunalola kanda, na kuno yuna-ku-lola uwe. Yuna malola; or, Yuna madzo ga malola; or, Madzoge gana malola.
**Maloli,** *n.* (ga). Rarely used. Ndo maloli ge alolafio atu-ku-a-hurisira madzo.
**Malozi,** *n.* (ga). *See* Ulozi. Almonds. Huenda virika uchi wa malozi.
**Malu,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). Kimoche kina pita gnombe na pembe-se ndiso si henduaso magunda.
**Malu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kosania; Andika; Demera. A fine, a mulct of expiation. The word is always construed with Ku ria, To eat. Malu hino nidza-yo riwa, be adziavaha-na mbari yao akiguirua na muche wehu, na sino huenda-a-ria malu dza iyo, adza yo-hu-ria. Ndo muafio hu-ria, nasui huna-mu-ria malu iyo. Hudzihuenda ria gnombe ya malu.
**Malume,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class), male. Masu malume.
**Malumifu,** *n.* (ga). Rarely used.
**Mamanira,** *v.a.* *See* Denguri. To overpower by numbers, to throng, to crowd upon. From Ku mamania in Kig.
**Mamba** (Maamba), *n.* (ga, pl. of Amba). Aravai a mbere ari aki-dzi-binikisa mamba.
**Mamba,** *n.* (ga), scales of fish. Yunakuna sui mamba. Nakuna sui wangu mamba, ni-ga-use.
**Mamba,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the crocodile.
**Mambakundu,** *n.* (ga), the morning red. Mambakundu higara gadzihendeka, kunacha. Kunahenda mambakundu.
**Mambamba** (for **Maambamba**), *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class), thin, fine.
**Mambea** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Ulongo in Kir., and Luambo). *See* Kundagnansi. A lie, slander.
**Mambo,** *n.* (ga). *See* Kivedi. Ni mambo gani higa? Mambo gano ga-dze? Mambo ni mabomu higa. Mambo ga Mulungu ni mangi.
**Mameye.** *See* Mayo.

## [PDF Page 254 — Dictionary Page 241 (Mam — Man)]

  Mamaye atu (= Make wana in Kins.).
**Mamfamfa,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Mfamfa, *q.v.*).
**Mamfula,** or **Mamvula,** *n.* *See* Lumfia; Lembelembe. Madzi ga mamvula, Spring-tide. (1) Mamvula madzanga. (2) Mamvula makulu, Kuna mamvula ga kumi ra ku ansa. Kuna mamvula ga kumi ra kahi. Kuna mamvula ga kumi ra ku isa.
**Mamira,** *n.*, the discharge from the nose. Ku mika mamira.
**Mamu,** *n.* (ya). *See* Raso. A lavia mamu, ngoja mua Mbawa mua gulu. Kare atu a vo kala akere kaya, ari akiika mamu; angine akala mindani, angine aka sagala mamu kaya, sabubu ya ku rinda kaya.
**Mana.** *See* Muana. A son, a child.
**Mananazi,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Nanasi), a pine-apple.
**Mane,** *adj.* (rel. to the pl. Ma-), four.
**Manemane,** *n.*, myrrh.
**Manonde** (Kid.) (= Madali in Kir.).
**Manene** (Kid. and Kig.), *adj.* (= Mabomu in Kir.), great.
**Maneno,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Neno), words, speech, language.
**Manga** (Kidigo and Kig.), *n.* (wa, hiu) (in Kir., Mugasija), the cassada root. Mua wa manga, in contradistinction to Mua wa muhama and Mua wa madzere. Pilipili manga, Black pepper.
**Mangeche** (Kid.), *n.* Ku piga mangeche.
**Mangera,** *n.*, the name of a species of bird with a long neck.
**Mangi,** *adj.*, many, much. Hu-u sirire muho asidze reha madzi mangi akahu hosa ela muho ka-u-siririka. Gnania yuna lumira malumifu mangi sana.
**Mangisi,** *n.* Jogolo wa mangisi; pl. Majogolo ga mangisi. Mifusiye na misusu ye ka-i-mera haraka.
**Mango,** *n.* *See* Maango.
**Manguangu,** *adj.* *See* Mafugondoefia. Quick, easy, not difficult. Masikiro manguangu, Quick ears, of quick apprehension.
**Mangue.** From Ku nga or Ku manga. Mutu aki ingira mangueni ya mfaya basi ni ku riwa gnombe.
**Mani,** *n.* *See* Vagira; Luanda. Semen, a germ, sprout. Vitu vikafio nialua, vichari mani, ka-vi-dzafiala. Gnania yuna muhama, ela uchari mani, ka-u-dzakala muhama, Gnania has muhama, but it is still in the blade, it has not yet become real muhama. Ka-ga-dza kala madzere gacharimani, It has not yet become Indian corn; it is still in the blade. N'enda nikafoye Mulungu, nikaguire mani. *See* Aluka. Yudziguira mani vatu vairi.
**Mania,** *v.a.* *See* Fiolo; Rindi. To know, to mind. Hivo mbere kare akamba ainsi ndio aokudza mania dzi yehu; akanya kuao, akambira ayao, basi nao akakudza na madzoka, kudzakula ushanga na mukodo; hata akimania pembe ndizo zirizo na kima, basi akahenda akidzi na pembe. Ku mania mania, To know well. Ku mania mutu yuno yufula akiomdika? (= Yugomba akigundiza kaka ri-upusa rosi). Der., Kimagnei.
  **Maniana,** *v. reit.*, to know each other.
  **Manika,** *v.n.*, to be known.
  **Manikana,** *v. ref.*, to be known by one another. Mutu hiye yuna manikana, or, yuna maniwa.
  **Manira,** *v.* *See* Vi, 2. Nari si-m-mania, ela nidzi-m-manira kua utu usiku.

## [PDF Page 255 — Dictionary Page 242 (Man — Mar)]

  **Manirira,** *v.* *See* Mukono; Muadza.
  **Manirirua,** *v.p.* Hikara adzi manirirua, kahewa kitu kaviri.
  **Manisa,** *v.a.*, to make acquainted with. Vatu hivo, si-va-manire, ela gnania musiku ndiye aye-ni-virika, nik'enda-vamania, be ndiye aye-ni-manisa, I did not know that place, but N. N. it is who took me, and I went to know it; it is he, you see, who made me knew it.
  **Manisana,** *v. reit.*, to be made acquainted with one another.
  **Manisika,** *v.n.* Vatu hivo ka-va-manisika, kuani-ka-va-fikika; ela vafikika-vo be ndo va manisua-vo.
  **Manisua,** *v.p.* Yuere ka-va-mania hiva, ela yudzimanisua ni gnania fulani, ndiye adzaye m-fisa. Abe Gunja akamanisua Lunguja ni Asungu.
  **Maniua,** *v.p.* Unamaniua o? Is it known hat? (*sc.* Utu).
  **Maniwa,** *v.p.*, to be known.
**Manina,** *n.* (ga). Kuna manina ga umande na ga mvula. Udzi-ni-dukanisira manina.
**Manioha** (Kid.), *n.* (ga) (= Manionioda in Kir. and Kij.).
**Manionioda,** or **Magniognioda,** *n.* (ga), heat-drops, rain in large drops, but at a distance from one another. From Ku nioda (nioda). Mvula idzihenda manionioda inadzudzua, maduene ge ni mabomu, ela ga kurekure, The rain comes in large drops, but they are distant. Dzana huari na manionioda ga mvula, ela rero be ndo mvula yegnie.
**Manire.** Manire kusa kala vo; Mulungu wa-ni-usa kasidi; kuamba nari vavo, ningaulagua na-mi. *Manire* Mulungu nikasa kala vo; ela kondo hio ka-i-ngasira.
**Maniuniua, Magnugnua,** *n.* (ga).
**Mankue,** *n.* (ya, za). Nankue ni vatu mfaya arindanavo; mutu akivegnia, ni ku riwa gnombe.
**Mano, Maano,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Ano).
**Manoadzi,** *n.* (ga), moderate drinking, as distinct from Urefi. Atu hia uchi ananoa ela manaadzigao, or, unaadziwao kana lonso.
**Manognona.** *See* Pfu.
**Manona.** Rero hunaafuna manona.
**Mansa,** *n.* (ga), a trace of blood from man or animal wounded in fighting or hunting. From Ku hansa. Mutu hebu niama afumaguaye, ndiye aambuaye; yunahausa mansa. Nidzi-m-fumaga niama, be yuu'enda akihansa; nidzi-m-dua mansa hata nika-m-pata; or, Nidzi-m-dua mansa, gadziangamika.
**Maolofu,** *adj.* *See* Mafu.
**Maonsa,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Onsa). Ahoho ndio ahendao mifui ya maonsa.
**Mapema.** *See* Mabema.
**Marai** (Kij.), *n.* (ga) (= Urai and the verb Ku rai), artifices, tricks. Yudzihenda marai hata yudzipata kitu kibomu.
**Maramara** (Kitaita, but beginning to be received in the Kir.), *v.a.* (= Ku yeya and Ku dzuma in Kir.).
**Maramara,** *n. pl.* (ga), spots somewhat smaller than the mabamaba. Wadzadziga toveni, muiri-o u-maramara. Dzui yuna maramara, or, mabamaba.
**Mare,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class). *See* Era and Esa. Long, deep. Niumba hi ina mare, ela ka-i-na malamu.
**Mare,** *n.*, length. Kana mare kakomia ku dzukirua.
**Mare** (Kid.), *n.* (ga) (= Ndumo in Kir.), joking, a joke. Prov., Kakuna mare ga umiro (=

## [PDF Page 256 — Dictionary Page 243 (Mar — Mas)]

  Kij., Hakuna msaha wa shinga).
**Marefi,** *n.* *See* Dzupisa.
**Marenge,** *n.* *See* Fua.
**Marengerenge.** *See* Mufumbulo.
**Marero** (Kid.) (= Madungo in Kir.).
**Mar'fuku, Marashufu** (Kij.), *n.*, anything double.
**Mariadzi,** *n.* (ga). *See* Kalanga; Golokira. Mtumche hiyu mariadzige ka-sira, yuna mukonomui.
**Mariapamba,** *n.*, a cocoa-nut grown on a branch from which toddy has been drawn; lit. bill-hook eatings (luhamba), what has escaped the cutting of the bill-hook, as generally no nuts will grow from a tapped branch. Nazi hi ni mariapamba; pl. Nazi hizi ni mariapamba. Ni kama masasa ga luhamba, It is the remnant of the bill-hook. Such a nut is always kept for seed, the tree being thought particularly good.
**Maridawa** (Kij.). Kitu hiki ninacho maridawa, kuangu ka-ki-koseka. Gnania yuna mali maridiwa (= Kadirike, yunaukuza ndaniye). Gnania musiku kuakue ni mu-ndzala, hebu yuna-fio viakuria? Resp., Ah Mulungu bariki, yuna-fio maridawa, s'ambe ni mutu mudabidabi.
**Marika,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Rika).
**Marika,** *v.n.* *See* Mala.
  **Marira,** *v.d.* *See* Mala.
  **Mar'kisa,** *v.a.* *See* Mala.
  **Mar'kisika,** *v.n.* *See* Mala.
**Marikano,** *n.*, cotton cloth from America.
**Marinsi,** *n.* (ga). Nidzifikia machira ga marinsi, or, urinsi.
**Mario,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name of a species of large birds. Also pronounced Mathio. They are rarely seen except in flights.
**Mariso,** *n.* (ga), pasture, pasturage.
**Marondo,** *n. pl.* (ga, sing. Rondo), the legs of animals from the middle joint downward, the shanks.
**Marora,** *n.* (ga), (K.) wares, commerce.
**Marua,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Rua), blossoms.
**Marukuruku,** *n.* (ga) (= Fundo), knobs in trees.
**Marunga,** *n.* (ga). Ku limira marunga.
**Maruru,** *n.* (= Kibaba), haste. Sina maruru, I am in no hurry. Kuna morua we kuna kishindo we. Unafika na ku fiola, si ku usa to kuansa? be una maruru. Ah! yuna maruru mai hiyu! utu utite ye ni ku henda ubomu. Gnania ni mulumbi, ela yuna maruru, kadieka moyo.
**Masa,** *n.* (ga), remainder. Especially used of that portion of toddy which remains and belongs to the toddy-drawer after paying the muengero to the owner of the cocoa-nut trees. From Ku sala.
**Masansu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Sansu).
**Masasa,** *n.* (ga), remainder, of food only. Viakuria viosa visalavio viihua masasa.
**Mashaha.**
**Masia, Mazia,** *n.* (ga), milk. Masia maidzi, New milk. Masia maifu, Milk coagulated; lit. ripe. Masia ga kusuka, What is reserved, retained in the udder. Ni masia. Dim., Visia, A little milk.
**Masia,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Sia).
**Masiho,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class). *See* Maso. Heavy, blunt, thick.
**Masika,** *n.* (ga). Masika ni vevi na ndzala; ganaihua masika kua vitu ku kala hapa. Masika mabomu.
**Masikiro,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Sikiro). *See* Mankuangu. The ears. Kana masikiro kasikira; or, Akafua masikiro, kasikira, He or she is deaf. N.B.—There is neither adj. nor noun in this language meaning deaf

*Footer: 243*

## [PDF Page 257 — Dictionary Page 244 (Mas — Mau)]

  or deafness, and the only way to express it is the above.
**Masiku, Maziku** (pl. of Ziku). *See* Ansansu.
**Masikua,** *n.* (ga) (= Mdongoa, or Masiaki in Kij.), things used at a burial. From Ku sika. Niama ya masikua, An animal for a burial.
**Masimiadzange** (= Mvula za masimiadzange).
**Masirimio,** *n.* (ga). Masirimio higo a-ni-sirimia-go, ka-ga-dza sirimiwa mutu. Una-m-sirimia muyao dza kuamba, kafiarirue, be ni masirimio gani gano, uki-m-sirimia muyao fio? Wamba wadzolua hebudze? ni musunieo? says a mother to a naughty, spoilt child.
**Masirimo,** *n.* (ga), troubles. Gnania yu masirimoni (= Yu mashakani). Si masirimo gara a-ri-go na-go? Yuna masirimo mangi tu.
**Maso,** *n.* (ga). *See* Uso. Edge. Maso ga kifiu. Kifiu hiki kina maso masiho, ka-ki-ria; ela kino kina maso mambamba, kinaria sana, ni luembe.
**Masu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Isu). Masu mache. Masu malume.
**Masuche,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Suche). *See* Lusuche. Masuche ga muvunga. Masuche ga muhama. Masuche ga maere. Masuche ga wimbi.
**Masumbulo,** *n.*
**Masumfio,** *n.* (ga). Rarely used.
**Masumuriro,** *n.* (ga).
**Masunga,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Sunga). Minazi yangu ina masunga n'enda bambahula.
**Masha,** *v. caus.* *See* Maka.
**Mashaka,** *n.* (ga). *See* Oya. Trouble. Ku kuta mashaka. Kahu-dza-pata mashaka kama higa hu-dza-go-pata rero.
**Mashauri** (Kij.), *n.* (ga, pl. of Shauri), advice, plans. Na hu fanie mashauri; hugule gnombe, huhende mboga sa muaka muvia. Ku fania; or, Ku *henda* mashauri.
**Mashihara** (Kij.), *n.* Una-ni-hendera mashihara; wamba: sinda-ku-piga.
**Mashindano,** *n.* (ga), contention, the effort to conquer each other. Muna henda mashindano; kamumania nika ka-i-hendua mashindano.
**Mashombo** (= Mishombo), plains. From Kishombo.
**Mashuku,** *n.* (ga). *See* Muta. (K.) Dash. Wakutua ni mashuku.
**Masu.**
**Matembe,** *adj.* (= Machache), few, little. Mawe matembe, A few stones. Majira matembe, A short time, a little while. Maneno matembe, A few words.
**Mathe,** *n.* (ga) (= Mare in Kir.). *See* Henda.
**Mathora,** *n.* (ga), (K.) wares.
**Matu,** *n.* Gnania ni matu gani ku-ri-ko ndzofu?—an expression of contempt.
**Matumbui** (= Makumbui in Kid.?).
**Mau,** *n.* (ya and ra), (K.) chalk. Ulongo ueruve ndio mau. Agnaro akignara; be aka-dzi-piga ulongo wa riani, kuansa hata mfungahe wa ndani ukisira; basi mfungaha wanse akahala ulongo wa mau, aka-dzi-pigano.
**Maujudi** (?), *n.* (= Maarufu kia). *See* Pishi.
**Maumbi,** *n.* (ga), the workmanship of a potter; one's way of forming earthen vessels. From Ku umba. Maumbige ni higano, niungu-ze ndivio aumbavio.
**Maumbire,** *n.* (ga), creation. Maumbire higa ga Mulungu-a-go umbadzi na viumbe be kamumania; Mulungu ni mbomu-mui?
**Maungo,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Ungo), the fruit of the muungo, a creeping plant. Ganga mafo.
**Maurumauru,** *n.*, the name of a species of insect, similar to the earwig, but larger.

## [PDF Page 258 — Dictionary Page 245 (Mau — Mba)]

**Mauziro,** or **Maudziro,** *n.*
**Mava,** *n.* (ga), wings. For the sing. Mfamfa, Mvamva, is used.
**Mavalala,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Valala, ra) (in Kid. = Madzodzo).
**Mavalu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Valu, *q.v.*), spars or poles. Mavalu ni mihi ya ku anira niumba, Mavulu are trees with which to build houses.
**Mavavika,** *n.* (ga), vomitings.
**Mavesi,** *n.* (ga).
**Mavi,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Ivi).
**Mavia,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class). *See* Uvia. New.
**Mavindi,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Vindi, ra). Mavindi ga ushanga. Mavindi ga mkufu. Nioka yudzipiga mavindi, The serpent has coiled itself round.
**Mavuvu,** *adj.* (rel. to the pl. Ma-), bare, mere, empty.
**Mavudzu,** *adj.* *See* Daladala. Thin. Masuche mavudza, Thin heads of Guinea-corn.
**Mawasa,** *n.* (ga), a small shower of rain. Mvula idzihenda mawasa, si mvula ya keri. Mvula idzegnia hapa, idzimuaga mawasa.
**Mawe,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Iwe), a stone.
**Mawu, Mahu,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Iwu, Ihu), a tumour.
**Maye,** *n.*, a mother. Only used in exclamations, the same as Mayo-we, Thou mother.
**Mayo,** *n.* *See* Dzea. Mother. The word presents some irregularities when the poss. pron. is added. They first say, Mayo wangu, My mother; but Mameyo, Thy mother; and Mameye, His or her mother. The two latter forms point to Mama in Kij. The prons. my and our are, however, rarely used in connection with parents. For the pl. of the poss. pron. (our, your, their), the word Ame is used: Ameyenu, Ameyae, Your mother, Their mother. *See* Ame. Mayo mufiere. Mayo muhoho.
**Mayuya,** *adj.* *See* Riyuya; Mafu. Light, easy.
**Mbaba,** or **Mubaba,** *adj.* *See* Kibaba. Opp. to the Moyo musinde.
(1) Gnania yuna moyo mbaba; but more frequently they say, Yuna moyo kibaba (= Kana moyo wa ku fumurira; kakomia ku dzukirua), Gnania has a hasty temper. (2) Yuna moyo mbaba, yunahensa ku foya muno.
**Mbada.** *See* Yegnie. Kala hiyu yuna mbada (= akanona sana). Ku uka mbada. Kala akinona muno, ni ku uka mbada. Nazi na-yo ni ku uka mbada.
**Mbafu, Mbavu,** *n.* (za, pl. of Lubafu, or Luafu). *See* Kiseho. The sides, the ribs. Nenda na umforo, ukalale mbavu mbiri ku lamukira ndze.
**Mbagazi, Mpagazi** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a bearer, one who carries a load on a journey. Na-we unalonda ku-ni-ika mpagazi-o? And you also will make me your bearer? Resp., Be ku mpagazi, una kasi yani?
**Mbahasi,** *n.* *See* Isu. Streaks? Mugomba mbahasi, A banana tree with red rinds.
**Mbahe,** *adj.* A., Gnania yuna gnombe ningi. B., Si ningi muno, ela ni mbahe.
**Mbai** (Kigiriama) (= Luakue in Kir., and Mbale in Kij.).
**Mbala,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a, Ni mbala). *See* Kilagane, the prov. Mbala yufiala maraso mairi, raso ra mulume ni kulungu, raso ra muana muche ni mbala. Kulungu wadamfua ni mbala, be nawe wadamfua ni muche, ndo uira wa sayo. Kava na kulungu muche, wala kavana mbala mulume.
**Mbala,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Sugu in Kij., and Mbara or Psambara in Kins.). *See* Ni-mbala. Callousness, hardness. Mutu

## [PDF Page 259 — Dictionary Page 246 (Mba — Mbe)]

  mukongo hebu mucharo ahambaye ndiye aohaye moho muno, akahenda mbala.
**Mbalahi,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Ivi; Kij., Kofi), a slap, a box with the open hand. Ku piga mbalahi. Ka-m-pige gnombe mbalahi, u-dzi-guse m'egnie, the Adigo.
**Mbalazi,** *n.* (ya, za), a species of pea, growing on a shrub called mubalazi.
**Mbali** (Kij.), *adv.* (= Luakue in Kir.), different, at variance with. Ni mbali go ugomba go, What you say is different.
  **Mbalimbali,** *adv.* (= Luakueluakue in Kir.), various, variously.
**Mbambara,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kidoda (Kij.). The name of a species of acacia; its boughs spread out like an umbrella—whence the name, the wide one, Bambara.
**Mbambu,** *n.* (ya, za). Mbambu ni vigongo via bambara via muamba wa mulala, hebu vikumbi via munazi, vikafungua dza dandara, hebu dza ludzadza, mukono usi diekuke. Yufungua mbambu.
**Mbanangi, Mbananzi,** or **Mbananzi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-) (Kibananzi is also used = Kifurunga madzi), a destroyer.
**Mbanga,** *n.* (za), a kind of illness. Ukongo wa mbanga sila misosani; mutu ni ku kokotua ni misosa, na ku onda, magulu gakakala hapahapa dza hapa ra mufia. Virondavie vienda vikirisa muiri, dza firangi gnandu.
**Mbao,** *n.* (za, pl. of Lubao), boards. Dalu ra mbao, in contradistinction to A dalu ra muhi mumenga.
**Mbara,** *n.* (= Mbatha).
**Mbaraka** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za). *See* Lala, 1; Haraka. Blessing. Mulungu yudzi-ni-bumira mbaraka mundani. Muche hiye yuna mbaraka.
**Mbarara,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Ngurunga.
**Mbari,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Nundu. Kindred. Mbari hira ni fugo menga, ka-i-na kure. Mbari ya ku lume. Mbari ya ku che. Mutu hiye akahala mbariyao, ya udzai, ya uifi, etc. Dim., Kibari.
**Mbasi, Mbazi,** *n.* (za), pity, mercy, compassion. Ku guisa mbazi, To excite pity.
**Mbatha,** *n.* (ya) (= Inda in Kij.). *See* Laga. A day specified, an appointed time. Ku larika mbatha. Ku lagana mbatha. Nidzihenda mbatha na gnania kuenda vatu vasiku, be mbatha yehu ka-i-dzafika. Nia-mbira mbatha nidze rini, Tell me a time when I may come. Nidzikuenda isa mudeni, kadza-ni-riva, yudzi-ni-pa mbatha, I have gone to ask a debtor for payment; he has not paid me yet, but has given me a day, an appointed time.
  **Mbathambatha.** Yudzi-ku-sara mbathambatha (= vichache vichache), mafuha ka-ga-kaenera to.
**Mbawa,** *n.* *See* Mubawa. The name of a plant.
**Mbawa,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). Prov., Ukongo u-m-guira mbawa. Mbawa ni muviriwe dzimba. Vana arie mueruve, vana arie mabamaba, vana arie ngululo ngululo; yuna rangi ningi. Mbawa a-miiri miiri, mibahu, ela uiru ndo ungi, The mbawa are of two and three bodies (*i.e.* colours), but black is the prevailing one. Angine akuenda umira, angine akakuta.
**Mbayumbayu,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Mufundo. A species of swallow. Mbayumbayu kaaka vidzungi, aaka niumba sa ulongo.
**Mbede** (Kik.), *n.* and *adj.* (pl. *id.*). From Ku veda, To cover. Atu hio ni mbede.
**Mbega,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Chiho. A species of monkey;

## [PDF Page 260 — Dictionary Page 247 (Mbe — Mbo)]

  (K.) guresa, with white hands.
**Mbeko,** *n.* (ya, za), a store, anything laid up or provided for future use; provision? From Ku weka, Kij. and Kir. Ku ika mbeko. Kitu kino sinda-ki-humira, na kikale, ni mbeko ya machero. Nguo hiso na-si-kale, ni mbeko, nikifua, ni ufua wa muana'ngu, na nikikala ni chari moyo, be ni mbeko. Naniala minazi, ni mbeko ya machero, hata nikifua, muana ngu yundaridi ufua.
**Mbele,** *n.* (ya, za). Mbele za kola (= Pembe za kola).
**Mbengeo** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za). Mbengeo ya muado.
**Mbere,** *adv.* and *prep.* *See* Ngombo; Kedania; Chinga; Hivara; Mimba; Uka; Dongoria. Before, as to time and space, further on. Muana wa mbere, A firstborn child. Hiko mbere huendako; lit. There before we go to; *i.e.* in future. Hivo mbere hulako; lit. There before we come from; *i.e.* in past time. Kare hu-lako na mbere huenda-ko.
**Mberia** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Mbayumbayu in Kir.).
**Mberoa,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the guava tree.
**Mbewa,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), a jackal. Mbewa ni mutune yuveka dza kuro; mchirawe u-bambara.
**Mbeyu,** *n.*
**Mbi,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), bad. Koro mbi, Bad (fierce) anger. Yuna ndani mbi, or, niomu; lit. He has a bad or hard belly; *i.e.* he is pitiless, hard-hearted.
**Mbidzi,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), fresh, unripe, raw, green. Niama mbidzi, Raw meat. Niungu mbidzi, A raw (*i.e.* unbaked) pot. Kaidima ku aka, yuaka niumba mbidzi.
**Mbidzo,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), good.
**Mbidzui,** *n.* Ku piga mbidzui, To dive.
**Mbifu, Mbivu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), ripe. Kansa mbivu. Tahi hino ni mbivu.
**Mbiga,** *n.* (za, pl. of Luiga), earthenware, unglazed native basins.
**Mbilikimo,** *n.* (wa; no pl. in Kir., but in Kij. Wa-). The word is used in Kir., but their own proper name for them is Vidumbakasi or Vidzumbakasi (sing. Kid- and Kidz-). Muana hiyu kakula, yunga mbilikimo.
**Mbimbi.** *See* Meneka.
**Mbingu** (wa), the heavens, God, the name of an evil spirit, supposed to cause sickness. The word is especially used in the northern part of the Rabai territory, called Ruruma, while in the southern part he is more generally called Mulungu. Mutu yudziguirua ni mbingu, The man is seized with the evil spirit.
**Mbira,** *n.* (ya, za, pl. the same), a grave, graves. From Ku bira in Kins., To sink.
**Mbiri,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), two.
**Mbirio** (Kik.), *n.*, the place where a cow is put in the charge of another. Nidziika gnombe mbirioni (in Kir. proper, Nidzikuenda fidza gnombe; or, Nidziika gnombe kua gnania).
**Mbiriri,** *n.* *See* Kani; Humili; Oniua; Dida. Mutu hiye-ak'enda akikuangue ku rima, hata dzua rikaala ka uka ngueni hata asise yuna mbiriri.
**Mboe,** *n.* (ya, za), trophy. Ya, or, Mudzomba sio mboe-ni ya mke na marinda.
**Mbofu, Mbovu** (Kij.), *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), bad. Ndaniye ni mbofu, ka-i-komia ku-m-luma (= in Kir. proper,

## [PDF Page 261 — Dictionary Page 248 (Mbo — Mbu)]

  Ndaniye ni kongo), His or her stomach is bad, weak, etc., almost any food making it ache.
**Mboga,** *n.* (za). *See* Zirizo. Vegetables, any sauce made of vegetables to eat with the wari.
**Mbogo,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name given to the niahi (buffalo) while being hunted, from the superstitious dread that, if it is called by its proper name, no success will attend the hunting. Prov., Mbogo, mania mrambo! ndo niani aambavio. Buffalo, mind the trap! says the monkey. Sense: Mind what you are going to do. The proverb is taken from the fact that no niani have ever been caught in an open trap, though they are caught in the trap called riwa, wherefore it is said of them, that the one which goes before and first sees a trap, warns the one coming next to beware of it, and so on to the last. N.B.—Mrambo is Kij., and stands for Muhambo.
**Mbohoja,** *n.* (= Lubugu), the name of a species of creeper.
**Mbolo,** *n.* (wa), membranum virile.
**Mbomu,** or **Mubomu,** *adj.* (rel. to the Mu- and Wa- class, with the preformative Mu- or M'-), great, large.
**Mbona,** *v.a.* (= Ku ona). *See* Pore; Nundu; Fifira; Kekerekekere; Enesa. To see. Una-ni-mbona fio? be na-ku-amba: utu hiu uriche. Udzi-ni-mbona na dzidzoro, nikihala?
**Mbonga.**
**Mboni,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Uiru. The apple of the eye, the eyeball. Mboni ya dzidzo; pl. Mboni za madzo. Nidzi lavia madzo.
**Mbono,** *n.* (ya, za), the castor-oil berry. Mubono, pl. Mi-, is the *fruit of the* castor-oil shrub.
**Mborera.** Munda muolofu, in contradistinction to Mugangando. Vatu hiva vana ludzanga, ni mborera. Vatu hiva-mudzanga we ni mborera. U-munda wa mborera we! ka-u-komia ku kola mfula, na kidza: ka-u-komia ku kola dzua; nawe ku komia ka vokera neno, uambuaro ni ku hikisa tu, ku kania; ni moyo uriodze o, urievio?
**Mbosa,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the wild bee. Mbosa nao ni ku henda uchi, ela ka-u-hama dza hura uchi wa niuchi, uchiwe una kadzungu.
**Mbotherua,** *n.* *See* Choderua. The falling in with a something previously wished for; lit. the being present with. From Ku therua (?). Kitu hiki nidzi-ki-pata kua mbotherua, sikamania kuamba nda-ki-ona. Ni kitu ulonda cho, be kika-ku-kudzira.
**Mbu** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Kama in Kir., but the Kij. word is fast superseding the Kir.), red ochre.
**Mbua** (Kij.), *n.*, a dog. In Kir., only used in scolding and abuse, instead of their own word, Kuro.
**Mbuangu,** *adj.*
**Mbuda,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a) (= Parara in Kij.). *See* Dzudzurira. The name of a species of bird. In building its nest, the opening is always on the opposite side from whence the monsoon blows.
**Mbuda** (Kik.), *n.* (wa), a robbing attack. From Ku vuda, To rob. Hudzionana na mbuda. Aendi ndio ahendao mbuda, ku vuda atu.
**Mbuehe,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a species of bird.
**Mbuchirire,** *n.*, intention, design, purpose. From Uchirira.
**Mbue,** *n.*
**Mbugu,** *n.* (za, pl. of Lubugu).

## [PDF Page 262 — Dictionary Page 249 (Mbu — Meg)]

  Mbugu za mrobo. Mbugu za mufimfira.
**Mbukisi,** *n.* (ya). *See* Zani.
**Mbulagua,** *n.* (ya). *See* Madidimuko. Slaughter. From Ku ulaga. Mbulagua hino kahu-dza-i-ona; atu hio ni aulagi sana.
**Mbulu,** *n.* (ya, za). Mbulu ya chuma ifuhiruayo mikufu.
**Mbulu,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Fulula. A species of large lizard. Mbulu ni kuria maji ga kuku. Kuna masikiro we-u mbulu? Prov., Maneno madzo galafia mbulu pangoni.
**Mbuludenge, Mbuluchenge,** *n.* (= Mbulu, but somewhat smaller and distinguished by a glossy skin, whence its name). Ni muvudzu punde. Muiriwe una chenche, unagnalagnala, ndosa aihue mbuluchenge.
**Mbulukambuluka,** *adj.*, light-headed, thoughtless. Muana hiyu kasikira-yu-mbulu, kambuluka, kadulisa akili.
**Mbumaniumba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Ab-). *See* Ingirirana. A brother-in-law.
**Mburudia,** *n.* (ya, za), the red pods produced by the tree called muburudia. Mburudia ni lundo sa muburudia.
**Mburuka,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Lagurira. The fruit of the muburuga, used for divination.
**Mbuya,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Mahawa in Kij.), a lover, a mistress. Yuna mbuya airi, or, mbiri. Muana wa mbuya (in Kid., Muana mbuya, without the gen. particle), An illegitimate child (= Muana wa kambo). Mtumche huya tu, ni mbuya ya gnania. Mulume huya ni mbuya ya amegnania.
**Mbuyu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Muuyu. (1) The seeds of the fruit of the baobab. Mbuyu ni tembe za uyu.
(2) The shell made into a vessel for milking, and, especially on the coast, for tapping cocoa-nut trees, and drawing water. Nakota uyu, nihende mbuyu.
**Mbuzi,** *n.* (ya and wa, pl. *id.*, a and za), (1) a goat. Dim., Kabuzi and Kibuzi; magn., Buzi and Ribuzi.
(2) An instrument used for scooping cocoa-nuts. A blade with a number of teeth is fixed into a board. The natives sit on the board and hold a half cocoa-nut in their hands, and scoop or rasp out the kernel. Mbuzi wa ku kunira nazi.
**Mdume, Mtume** (Kij.), *n.*, the name given by the Wasuahili to Mohammed, and, owing to the frequent intercourse between them and the Wanyika, known also, to some extent, to the latter.
**Mdumua, Mtumua** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. Wa-) (= Musunie in Kir.). *See* Muhumiki. A slave.
**Mduku.** *See* Muduku.
**Mdzuano.** *See* Mudzuano.
**Mdz'usa.** *See* Mudz'usa.
**Meda** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Meka in Kir.), to lighten, to flash. Mfula inameda (= Kir., Mvula inameka; Kij., Inafania umeme).
**Mega,** *v.a.* (= Megnia in Kij.), to eat greedily. Ku mega wari. Megani wari mu-u-sase to usayaya.
  **Megeka,** *v.n.* Wari hiu umoho ka-u-megeka, This mess of rice is hot; it cannot be eaten greedily.
  **Megera,** *v.d.* Ima! ni-ku hegere wari. M-megereni wakue, mu-ikire.
  **Megerana,** *v. reit.* Ahoho hia anamegerana wari.
  **Megula,** *v.a.* Ku megula wari wa peho, or, dzima ya peho. Ku megula wari udzao pigua ni lufuje.
  **Meguka,** *v.n.* (= Ku bamfuka). Vadzimegulua hiva, be udzimeguka wegnio? Luiga ludzimeguka, ndzara idziuka.

  Niungu idzebua, ela ka-i-ka funsika, idzihenda megeuka.
  **Megurira,** *v.d.* *See* Gande; Koma. Kuka ukuha-atu ari angi, be sagala ni-ku-megurire wari, udzaoikua luakue.
  **Megulua,** *v.p.*
**M'egnie.** *See* Muegnie.
  **M'egniewe.** *See* Muegniewe.

**Meitha,** *n.* *See* Mumaitha.

  **Mekameka.** Dzua rina mekameka. Mufiu unamekameka.
  **Mekera,** *v. rel.* Macha ga mekera-vi? or, Gamekera kanda ya lua-vi? Resp., Ganamekera udzerero wa dzua; or, Ganamekera hiko kanda ya Usambalani, etc.
**Mema,** *v.a.* *See* Venula. Ku mema m'iya. Ku mema mibele ya niungo.

  **Memera,** *v. rel.* Ni-pa kifiu, nika-m-memere gnania m'iya.
  **Memena,** *v.a.* Ku memena muhi ni ku u kata visikuvisiku.
  **Memenera.** Ndzo, u-ni-memenere, hukidzanga, hundagafia kuni.
  **Memerera** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Remerera in Kir.). Redupl. of Merera.
**Mena** (Kig.), *v.a.* *See* Fumulafumula. To slight, deride, sneer at, defy.
  **Menana,** *v. reit.*, to slight one another. Atu hio akamenana, hata akionana, katamusania; simania akavio menanira.
  **Menanira,** *v. rel.*
  **Meneka,** *v.n.* Gnania yuna videmu kana ufualo udzo, be akameneka. Mutu hiye si-m-mene kua nguoye ku kala mbimbi, ukakuenda vakue unaguirua ni haya, kuakue yuna vitu sanana moyo mudzo, kana muyawe-kameneka mutu hiye.
  **Menera,** *v. rel.* Ndo atu a-m-meneravo, kuria atu malu asivokosa utu wa geri. Yudzi-ni-mena ku-ni-mbona (= ku-ni-ona) akadzuva mahe, be yu-ni-menerani? Ninanuka vironda hebu dzi?
  **Menua,** *v.p.*, to be slighted, to be despised.
**M'ende,** *v.* Contracted from Muende, Go ye!
**Menga,** *adj.*, one.
**Meno,** *n.* (ga, pl. of Dzino), (1) teeth. Meno ga mbere, The front teeth. Meno ga majego, The grinders. Meno ga kuro, The eye-teeth.
(2) Links.
  **Menomeno,** *n.* Lukue hilu lu-menomeno, ka-lu-ka fuihiwa to. Lukue hilu kakafuiha to, meno ganaonekana.
**Mera,** *v.n.* *See* Hungo; Hombo; Mumera; Kubo; Choga. To spring up, to grow. Naniala vikimera; ela basi vikifuka, kuani mfula yere chache. Muana hiyu yudzimera ga dzulu, mena being understood; naasindikue, ni kidzaye. Muana hiyu kumania ni mui we? Resp., Ni mui dzoa wa mera ga dzulu ge. Gnania yudzimera kirefu; lit. Gnania has grown a beard; *i.e.* has got a beard.
  **Merera.** *See* Fundula.
  **Mererua,** *v.p.* *See* Tumbo.
  **Mesa, Meza,** *v.a.* *See* Mumera; Ingu. (1) Mvula idzoyognia; mutu akavanda; ina meza.
  (2) Gnania musiku yudzimesa muaka hiu. Gnania yunarima akimesa; yunadzuma akipata; be kura ku-dzi-vungusa ku fuala videmu, nini?

## [PDF Page 264 — Dictionary Page 251 (Mer — Mfa)]

**M'erefu, M'erevu,** *n.* (ga), cunnings, devices; (K.) pertness. Contracted from Maerevu. Mutu hiyu ni muerefu; m'erefuge ni mangi, kake-ngeka. Gnania ni mukobi; m'erefuge ni mai ga ku kenga atu tu, m'erefuge ni ga ugniagnanii.
**M'eri,** *n.* *See* Mueri.
**M'eruve,** *adj.* (rel. to the Ma- class), white. Contracted from Maeruve.
**M'eruve,** *n.* (ga), white (things); *i.e.* what is clearly known, matters of course. Maneno higa ni m'eruve gangu, gakadzuka, na-ga-mania. Utu hiu, or, Neno hiri ni m'eruvegangu, This affair, to me, is a matter of course. Na-ga-mania; ni m'eruve gaugu, ukiavaha, kuriva.
**M'esi,** *n.* *See* Muesi.
**M'eso,** *n.* *See* Mueso.
**Meto,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Tibitibi in Kij.). *See* Mfara. The seed of a plant with an agreeable smell. The fruit of the muluchiluchi, or mumeto. Meto ni tune to, ela vano kilemboni ni viru.
**Mfaka,** *v.a.*, to bribe. Kikiri ni ku-a-va atu angi, ela ku mfaka ni mutu mumenga. Gnania ni mulongo, ela yudzimfaka kura tu kua mualamusi.
**Mfalume** (Kij.), *n.* (= Muerefu and Mukobi; Mugniognania in Kir. proper), one who is violent, oppressive. Gnania ni mfalume, akahala kitucho, be sodi uume ku muisa, kariva mutu. Ah! mfalume yukudza, ka richa ku gniagnanira. Gnania yudzigandamirua ni mfalume yunda-m-koba, yunda-m-koba, Gnania has been stuck to by a violent man, has come in contact with him. Ah! mfalume yudzikudza, yundagniagnanira, yundagniagnanira.
**Mfamfa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mamfamfa or Mava), a wing. Mfamfa ra kuku, The wing of a fowl. Kuku yudzibinikisa anae mamfamfa. Chogolo akiihika, yunapiga mamfamfa. Mamfamfa ga sui, The fins of fish; sing. Mfamfa ra sui.
  **Mfamfuka,** *v.n.* Yudzimfamfuka niasiniasi hata yudzikuenda guira njira, or, hata yudziupuka njirani.
**Mfana,** *v.a.* (Ku vana in Kig.), to cut off the tips of the ears of goats, a practice supposed to improve the beauty of the goats. Mbuzi hizi nizi-zi-mfana masikiro, ni kana urembo, asikale dza niama wa dzakani.
**Mfaniuka,** *v.n.* (= Ku bamfuka and Ku meguka). *See* Vadza. To break out, as a fragment from earthenware and calabashes. Niungu ni ku mfaniuka.
**Mf'ananiko,** *n.* *See* Muvuananiko; Kifumi.
**Mfanga,** *n.*, ill luck. Mutu hiyu yuna mfanga kula ak'enda vatu yutungua ni muiya; atu akapigana, ye sudi apigue aahulue luguma. Adzihenda uganga wa ku lafiwa mfanga. *See* Uyiwa. Yudzi-m-fumagira mfanga, kakauchirira (= zani), He shot him by ill luck, by accident; he did not intend it.
**Mfano,** *n.* *See* Mumfano. A ticket.
**Mfara,** *v.a.*, to scratch. Yudzi-dzi-kuna, yudzi-dzi-mfara kombe, vadzila miladzo. Yudzi-ni-mfara, He or she has scratched me. Yudzi-ni-mfara kombe. Nidzi-ku-mfara.
  **Mfarana,** *v. reit.*, to scratch one another. Adzi mfarana kombe, ndo kondo ya ache.
  **Mfarua,** *v.p.*, to be scratched.
**Mfaruka,** *v.n.* (= Baruka in Kins.; and Mfamfuka in Kij.). *See* Dai. Gnombe idzimfaruka, ka-i-lala chaani, wala ka-i-dua ayae; ka-i-mania kuao, idzimfaruka. Gnombe yudzimfa-

*Footer: 251*

---

## [PDF Page 265 — Dictionary Page 252 (Mfa — Mfi)]

  ruka, yukimbira ku fungua. Paka wangu hangu dzana akamfaruka, ka-va-kala hiva vangu; yudzikala paka muitu. Unamfaruka dza gnombe hebu dze? undakala mudabimdabi, kundahenda akili.
  **Mfarukira,** *v.d.* Ku mfarukira muyao vio nini? Dza kuamba ni mumeitha undakala mui we. Ni ku-m-piga punde kua punde, kua ufiarirua.
  **Mfarura,** *v.a.* Kio mfarura kombe.
  **Mfarusa,** *v.a.* Udzi-i-mfarusa gnombe (= udzi-i-lachisa); u-i-gniase, i-gniale, be undakudza, u-i-funge, ela hiku udzi-mfarusa. Kuku yudzivonioka, udzi-mfarusa; m-bembe, m-dieke moyo, kuani yudzilacha. Ukinoa uchi na niama ka u ku mfarusa.
**Mfara,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mamfara). *See* Kimfara. Baldhead; lit. a scratch, a place laid bare. Only used in reviling language. Huusire ro mfara; lit. Take from us that bald head; go away, etc.
**Mfaramfara,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mamfaramfara), a species of lizard, somewhat larger than the gahe. Muiri-we u-mikirimikiri, unachegniachegnia, ndosa aihue mfaramfara. Yukala muhini; akikala yunakimbira, be nawe u-dzulu ya muhi, aka-ku-kuera muirini ku chira; basi ndo a-ku-mfaramfara-vo kombe.
**Mfare,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Furuma. The name of a species of squirrel.
**Mfarika,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Mudamba; Ndama. A virgin, a young female animal before she has become a mother. Mfarika ya gnombe, A heifer. Mfarika ya gnonsi, Kid. (= Kir., Muadi wa gnonsi). Mfarika ya mbuzi, A young she-*goat before bearing*.
**Mfaya,** *n.* *See* Kangaja.
**Mfengo,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Luania and Pengo, which are artificial gaps), a gap in the teeth. Dzino riki uka regnie, ni ku henda mfengo.
**Mfera,** *n.* *See* Mumfera, which is the more correct pronunciation.
**Mf'eresi,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Mfueresi.
**Mfiala,** *n.* (ya). *See* Kivedi. Yudzinsa mfiala, mafundoge gadzisira gosi; or, Yudzidzinsa mfiala, yudziricha ufiasi; pl. Ache hia adzidzinsa mfiala.
**Mfiela,** *v.* (= Thioma in Kig.). Gnania yunagomba maneno ga Kikamba, ela yuna mfiela, ka-ga-mania to. Kakadimisa kiravai, yunamfiela. Nidzigomba maneno gangu, ela gnania musiku yudzi-ni-mfiela, or, yudzi-ga-mfiela, ka-ga-kahensa, mutu huya aka-ni-mena, ni neno ra muyao-ku-ri-hensi. Neno hiri rikamfiela vatite, This word is a little different. Yugomba maneno, ela yudzimfiela. Neno hiro adza-ro-gomba, ridzimfiela vatite, ka-ri-kagoloka geri ni.
**Mfignio,** *n.* (ya). *See* Muthungu. The name of a disease peculiar to children. Muana yudziguirua ni mfignio. Mfignio idziifua, m-dzodzeni, The mfignio is ripe; scarify ye him, or her. The blood which flows is said to be quite black. Nasira muhaso, muana yunadzodzua mfignio. Muana hiyu ka-dza-la mfignio. Muiri ni ku dzadzuka na madzo ni ga kindikindi, The skin turns white and the eyes are swollen.
**Mfimbo,** *n.* (ya, za), a rat's nest. Niumba ya pania.
**Mfindo, Mvindo** (Kid.), *n.* (= Nkoko in Kir.; Kihako in Kir.).
**Mfisa, Mfiza,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) *See* Ndoredore. From Ku fiza.

## [PDF Page 266 — Dictionary Page 253 (Mfo — Mfu)]

  Ichi hiri ni mfiza. Machi higa ni mfiza; or, Machi gano ni mfiza.
  (2) Kuna mfisa ya madzere ga ku kalanga.
**Mfo** (= Fo). Ku enenda-mfo-na ku richa muchewe (vidzoa vidzi-mu-uyira).
**Mfo,** *n.* (za, pl. of Lumfo).
**Mfoda, Mvoda,** *v.a.* *See* Ku voda. To confute, to disprove. Yudzi-ni-mvoda geri; gakue gadzikuenda karakara, ela gangu gadzikala makosa. Nidzigomba, nidzi mvoda. Yudzigomba, yudzi-a-mvoda osi, a dzaodeda, adziguirua ni haya.
  **Mfodua,** *v.p.* *See* Elemea. Atu ere akishindana, ela gnania yudzi mfodua.
**Mfongi,** *n.* (ya, za). Vana mfongi ya muhi, kura-tu, kilembani. Vana mfongi sa mavalu hivo. Vana mfongi sa pfuiho hivo. Mfongi za mileli, The longest tail-feathers.
**Mforonkue,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Uina walamu), a hole in the ground; of animals that burrow, when uncommonly wide.
**Mfu,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the river-horse, hippopotamus. Luayolue ni kama hako ra kinu, kidengelesa kibomu. Niamaye ka-i-gniererua, ni insi, wala ka-i-ingira mabulu, wala ka-i-ola; na mdzusi-we ka-u-funda. Kikondeche atu anabuma kisukini, angue: ni muhaso wa mafuha. Ku piga mfu mbirani.
**Mfua.** From Ku fua. Wari mfua ni wari usio ifua to.
**Mfuadzi,** *n.* (hiyu, wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name of a species of ant. Ni adune to, They are quite red. Madzere ga madzinani gadziriwa ni mfuadzi, atu akaamba: ni koma, yudzidzukirua, yunalonda ku henderua kivalao.
**Mfuaha,** *n.* *See* Mufuaha.
**Mfuaho,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Mfadu in Kij. A huge basket for keeping grain. No longer in use. Dim., Kafuaho and Kifuaho.
**Mfuamfua,** *n.* and *adj.* *See* Kalakonche. The blending of colours with each other. Mbuzi hira i-mfuamfua. Gnombe hino i-mfuamfua; or, Muiriwe u-mfuamfua.
**Mfueresi,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), an animal larger than the kuve, with short legs and a big head. Yunadundumira niasini, na uina ni ni ku ingira; kaidima ku dzimba m'egnie. Mfueresi yuna pula ya ku sikira kungu ya atu.
**Mfufi,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a species of snake, of a shining black colour and with very red eyes, said to be exceedingly venomous. Kaoneka muno; madzoge ni madune to-dza moho. Muiriwe una range niru, be yuna ngenge sa ku gnala; yunaogofia sana. When seen it is considered a vioni to say, Mbere kundakudza utu, Something serious or unlucky will take place; and the frightened person brings an offering to the koma, ku piga mfua, or goes to consult a muganga, ku logurirua.
**Mfugnia,** *v.a.*, (1) to comb. Ndzo, nidze-ni-ku-mfugnie nierezo.
(2) Trop., to tell one a secret. Ndzo, ni-ku-mfugnie maneno na-go-sikira, ni maneno ga faraga, ga siri.
  **Mfugnira,** *v. rel.* *See* Kimfugnio.
**Mfuha,** *n.* (ya, za), the stalk of millet. Muhama wa mfuha, Red Guinea-corn, the stalks of which are sweet. Mfuha hino. Tembize ni tune; masuchege gana kifumba, mugua we ni miwa ya vigua. Mfuha kana maonsa mare, onsare rikisama kana kilo, ku veheka.

## [PDF Page 267 — Dictionary Page 254 (Mfu — Mia)]

**Mfui,** *n.* (za, pl. of Lumfui), grey hairs.
**Mfuje,** *n.*
**Mfukudza,** *n.* (za). Nidzevia na mfukudza za moho.
**Mfukuhi,** *n.* (za), sweat. Niumba hira ina mfukuhi, ela hino inasisima, ina peho.
**Mfula, Mvula,** *n.* (ya), rain.
**Mfulani,** *n.* (wa), youth.
**Mfuma,** *n.* Kid., Gnania musiku yufaka niama, mufui upiga mfuma. Kir., Yudzi-m-piga mfuma, mufui udziupuka kanda ya viri, ukuenda oha dzua-ei! mutu yunafuha-ye!
**Mfumbi, Mvumbi,** *n.* *See* Kirimira. Drenching rain. From Ku fumba. Mvula hi ni ya mfumbi, ka-i-dana (Kid.). Mvula ya mvumbi, ndio i-kola-yodzi.
**Mfumi,** *n.*, the noise made by anything rushing by. From Ku fuma. Mufui hiu udzila na mfumi. Ah gnania yunachira hivano, yunachira na mfumi, kahu-mania arironaro. Mue yudzichira na mfumi, yudzihala kuku.
**Mfuna** (Kid. and Kidigo), *v.n.* (= Ukuha in Kir.). *See* Dzafulo. To be satisfied.
**Mfungu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Fahi; Fundo; Nai. A joint, a knot. Mfungu za. Mfungu ni vara-tu, vameravo kodza. Mfunguni ni vomu ka-va-gogodeka.
**Mfuno,** *n.* (wa), plenty, satiety.
**Mfuo,** *n.* (ya, za). Mfuo ni vatu ntu aampikavo ludzadza. Mfuo hio ina risira.
**Mfura,** *v.a.*, (1) to scratch so as to leave marks behind; to scratch out from a bag, etc.
(2) Trop., to take advantage of. Ku mfura kivinda, To scratch out grain from a bag. Nidzi-mu-mfura mutu hiye nidzi-mu-mfura muvunga, I have scratched that man, I *have scratched* him his rice; *i.e.* I got it under the price, the owner having been in want of money; I took advantage of him. Yudzi-m-fiola, yudzi-mfura, die-yudzienenda (*i.e.* Yudzi-ga-mfura 'ndani muakue, ku-ga-lafia gosi). Adzichira atu-adzimfurika, pronounced with a high and singing voice. Ai! ela gnania kana mbusi ningi ela-zidzifmurika, ku chira.
(3) To scold, to revile.
  **Mfurika,** *v.n.*
**M'ganga, Muganga,** *n.*, medicine-man.
**M'gniagnani,** or **Mugniagnani,** *n.* (Kij., Mgurure). *See* Muvingo. The name of a tree something like ebony.
**Mguadu.** *See* Mkuadu.
**Mgue.** *See* Mkue.
**Mguena.** *See* Mkuena.
**Mgugunda** (Kid.) (= Mufimba in Kir.). Maneno higo nidzi-ga-richa mgugunda, simania nchirase.
**Mguisi, Mguizi,** *adj.*, seizing of prey. From Ku guira. Only used in connection with Niama. Niama mguizi, A beast of prey; pl. *id.* (hiyu, hia). Niuni mguizi, A bird of prey, but this is rarely used.
**Mi.**
**Mi** (Mii), *adj.*, bad.
**Mia,** *adv.* *See* Kimia. Yugniemere mia. Yudziniamala mia kakagomba.
**Mialamu,** *adj.* (rel. to the pl. form Mi-), broad, wide.
**Miamiamia.** Yudziniamala— The word may be repeated as often as you like.
**Miansa.** Bora wa mianza ya ache.
**Mianzo.**
**Miario,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Muario), judicial discussions. Ni maneno ga ku aririana. Rero hudzisinda na miario di. Vana miario mingi hivo.
**Miaso, Miazo,** *n.* (pl. ya), thought. Sodi uhende miazo moyoni

## [PDF Page 268 — Dictionary Page 255 (Mia — Mig)]

  muako, nda unda-vo mania, ela ukisa kala na miaso moyoni, basi, haya kundakosa vio?
**Miayu,** *n.*, a yawn. Ku piga miayu, To yawn.
**Mibomu,** *adj.* (pl. Laarge). Muadza una miya mibomu.
**Michewa** (Kid.).
**Midafu,** *n.* (pl. ya), chaff, from the first pounding. Ni wishoa wa mbere kua gara magauge. Mutu muche akivonda madzere, akihegula ku veta, be hura tu wishoa wa mbere, ndio uihuao midafu, ni magofi ga dzulu.
**Midalemidale,** *adj.*, doubtful. Ya kere midalemidale.
**Midara.** *See* Madara. From Ku dara (?). Nguo hi i-midaramidara (= i-langalalangala; i-hanukahanuka) ka-i-ka dignia, or, ka-i-ka digniua luzi. Ku fuma midaramidara (= kurekure).
**Midodo,** *n.* (pl. ya). *See* Mifufu. Njira ya midodo. Njira hio ina midodomidodo; yavesa kare ku chirirua.
**Miduare** (Kij.), *n.* (ya) (Kir., Ayuka), echo.
**Midza,** *n. pl.* (ya, sing. Mudza), fringes.
**Midzango,** *n. pl.* (ya). *See* Nguruma. Midzango inarira, yunandzala.
**Midzani.** *See* Kadzongonene.
**Midzano.**
**Midze,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Mudzo). Vitu via ku niala ndivio viambuavio vidzimera, vidzilafia midze.
**Midzere.** Midzere misiho.
**Midzidzo,** *n. pl.* (pl. of Dzidzo). *See* Dumbula; Fignira. An eye.
**Midzoga,** *n. pl.* (ya) (= Vioga), mushrooms. Magn. of Choga.
**Midzoka,** *n. pl.* (ya), a large serpent. Magn. of Nioka.
**Midzunsu,** *n. pl.* (ya), understanding. The word is only used in the negative. Kana midzunsu (= Kana akili); but of one who is intelligent, Yuna midzunsu is not used, but only, Yuna akili.
**Miemia,** *v.a.*, to smile. Yudzimiemia milomo, yulonda ku dzoka, He or she has curled his lips; he wants to laugh.
**Mifu,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). Mifu hiyu; pl. Mifu hia. Mifu yudzi-ni-suhira. Mifu gnombe abomu. Mifu kigonsi atite.
**Mifufu, Mivuvu,** *n. pl.* *See* Fufu. Mifufu jembe.
**Mifuhi,** *adj.* (rel. to the pl. Mi-), short.
**Mifungahe.**
**Mifuo,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Mufuo), bellows.
**Mifusi, Mifuzi,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Lufusi). *See* Kuchu. The hair of animals and of the human body; the hair of the head is Niere; the down of birds, Niama kaambua ana niere, ni mifuzi tu.
**Mifusi,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Lufusi), sweepings. Muriangoni vadziidzala mifusi, i-fiereni, mu-i-dzome, hebu mu-i-dzuve dzalani.
**Migeriudzungu,** *n.* *See* Fumbirua. A sourish smell from the stomach. Nidziheruka migeriudzungu.
**Migirijimbo,** *n.*
**Migirimigiri,** *n.* (ya). Muiriwe udzikala migirimigiri kua fuiho a-dza-zo pigua; vatu va-dza-vo pigua vakafutuka.
**Mignia,** *v.a.* *See* Lalama; Madiriri. To hug. Yudzi-m-dieka, yuna-m-mignia vavodzi.
  **Migniana,** *v. reit.* *See* Gofiana. To wrestle. Ima humigniane, nami ni-dzi-kombole.
  **Mignira,** *v. rel.* Hudzimigniana, nidzi-m-dieka, basi na-mu-mignira vavo dzi. Yudzi-ni-dieka, yuna-ni-niguira vavo dzi.
  **Mignirua,** *v.p.*

## [PDF Page 269 — Dictionary Page 256 (Mig — Mim)]

  Yunamignirua vavo dzi.
**Mignialu** (Kig.), *n.*, dung, manure.
**Mignieri,** *n.* Ku dzuva mignieri.
**Mignio,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a) (Kij., Tungu ufundo), the name of a species of large black ant, the enemy of the termites, which it attacks and kills in regular bodies, as is shown in the following description: Mignio hia adziramuka, adzikuenda piga viha, adzirumiria. Mignio ak'enda dzuma, akikala adzisikira ludzoa ananuka, basi ni ku ima, akadindiria vamenga ku rindana, hata osi akikala vamenga; akalafia mithia, akademera hara ludzoa hata akagota; akapiga nchemi; hara ario niuma na-o akaramuka, basi akaulaga ludzoa, akaulaga akiika vimba; akahenda mizigo; na hara adzio lumua ni ludzoa, na-o aka-a-dzukula, hata adzio-ulagua korokoro, akadzukulua; basi ndo akaenenda, akauya mudzini kuao.
**Migniu,** or **Migniuka.**
**Miiri,** *adj.* (rel. to the pl. form Mi-), two.
**Miiri,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Muiri). *See* Korera; Chererua.
**Miivi** (Kidigo), *adj.* (= Mifuhi in Kir.), short.
**Mika,** *v.a.*, to discharge mucus from the nose. Ku mika mamira, To wipe one's nose; lit. the discharge from the nose.
  **Mikira.** Yudzi-ni-mikira mamira, yudzi-ni-mena. Sika-ku-ona Shaha-ni kana zani.
  **Mikirua,** *v.p.* Yudzi mikirua mamira ni gnania.
**Mikindui,** *n.*, pleasure, joy. Kupiga mikinduiku furahiwa (= ku dzadzarika).
**Mikirimikiri.** *See* Mforamfora.
**Miko,** *n.* *See* Muiko.
**Mikojo** (Kid.), *n.* (= Shahawa in Kij., and Mukodzo in Kir.), (*obscene*), semen.
**Mikoma.** Nikapiga mikoma yangu nika-i-guiza be n'enda jindale.
**Mikombe,** *n. pl.* (ya). *See* Kuada.
**Mikuludzulo,** *n.* Gnania yunagomba mikuludzulo-be yurere.
**Miladzo,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Muladzo).
**Miliki** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to rule, reign.
  **Milikiwa,** *v.p.* *See* Angindo.
**Milinga.**
**Milomo,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Mulomo), (1) the lips.
(2) Trop., words, speech (= Maneno). Milomo mingine, Other words.
**Milosi,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Mulosi), whistles. Ku piga milosi, To whistle.
**Mimba,** *n.* (ya, za), the embryo, the fœtus, protuberance, pregnancy, a child, a young one. Mimba ya mugumo. Mugumo hiu ka-u-dza komala, ka-u-dza henda mimba. Gnombe hizi sina mimba, ela mimba zao ka zi-dza komala. Mimba zao sidzikomala, sindaviala hikara. Mimba ya mbere, generally abbreviated into Mimba mbere (= Muana wa mbere), The first young one; the first child, or young one,—used of animals and men. Muana hiyu ni mimba mbere ya gnania, ndiye ayeahula dzansu. N.B.—The natives often say merely, Imbambere, such is the tendency of every language towards abbreviation. Dim., Kibimba and Kabimba; magn., Bimba.
**Mimenga,** *adj.* *See* Mumiro.
**Mimfi,** *n.* (= Mufumbiso). Dzana naria kishombo, be nidzilamuka na mimfi, hata uvolue sikawesa kuria.
**Mimfo,** *n.* (ya).
**Mimi,** *pers. pron.*, I, me.
**Mimina** (Kij.), *v.a.* (= Kakania in Kir.), to empty. In Kir., especially used of the clearing of a boil or ulcer by pressing it. *See* Kamula. Ku

*Footer: 256*

## [PDF Page 270 — Dictionary Page 257 (Min — Mis)]

  mimina ufira, To free from matter.
  **Miminika,** *v.n.* (= Kakanika in Kir.). Udzimiminika ufira hata ridzavola moyo.
**Mina,** *n.* (pl. of Uina).
**Minane,** *adj.*, four.
**Mine,** *adj.*, four.
**Minga,** *adj.* (rel. to the pl. form Mi-). *See* Nga. They resemble.
**Mingavi,** *adv.*, how many.
**Mingi,** *adj.* (rel. to the pl. Mi-), many.
**M'ingo,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, ya) (= Muguisho, which is more frequently used), brim. M'ingo is contracted from Muingo, pl. Miingo, and derived from Ku inga. Ku dieka m'ingo.
**Minialu,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Lunialu), soot. Minula ya mosi ka ludzago ni.
**Miniamaminiama.** *See* Fuidza.
**Minini** (Kid.), *n.*, sense. Kuna minini (= Kuna akili we).
**Miniolo,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Muniolo).
**Mino.**
**Miokue,** *n.* *See* Miyokue.
**Miono,** *n.* (ya), snoring. Ku piga miono, To snore.
**Mioro,** *n.* (ya) (= Miario). *See* Niacha. Ku gomba mioro (= Kik., Ku dzila). Husihende mioro ya Kidigo; ka-hu-na yo kasi.
**Mire,** *adj.* (rel. to the pl. form Mi-), long.
**Miri,** *n.* *See* Miiri.
**M'irika.** *See* Muirika.
**Mirimire,** *n.* (ya) (= Makurima), one's way of cultivating the ground. From Ka rimira. Ndo mirimireye arimafio.
**M'irim'iri,** or **Muirimuiri,** *n.* *See* Biribiri. The quivering of the atmosphere about the horizon, from extreme heat, preceding the rainy season. Dzua ramba m'irim'iri.
**Mirimiro,** *n.* (ya), environs. Gnombe zi mirimironi mua atu. Muthiani mumenga wa longosa atu mirimironi, akaulagua sana.
**Miromironi, Mimironi,** *n.* (ya). *See* Muiro.
**Mirongo,** *adj.*, teens, tens. Mirongo miere, Twenty. Mutu hiye kana mirongo.
**M'iru,** *adj.*, (1) (rel. to the Ma- class), black. Contracted from Mairu. Mabato m'iru, Black spots.
(2) Contracted from Miiru.
**Misa, Miza,** *v.a.*, to swallow. Kuna sui amizaye sui angine.
  **Misika, Mizika,** *v.n.* *See* Sama. To admit of being swallowed.
**Misho,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Muisho, *q.v.*).
**Mishombo,** *n. pl.* (ya, the sing. is not in use), a cloth gathered up and bound round the waist, the two ends hanging down in front. Only used of men. Ku funga mishombo. Nguo yangu na-dzi-funga mishombo. Atu hia adzi-dzi-funga mishombo, be ni mfaya anadieka. Kambi akipiga rima, aka-dzi-funga mishombo sana.
**Misima,** *adj.*
**Misindo,** *n. pl.* (ya). *See* Fuka. Atu adzipiga misindo. Nidzisikira misiond atu anachira.
**Misisi,** *n. pl.* (ya), soot, smut. Misisi ni ya niungu.
**Misiso, Mizizo,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Musiso) (= Miiko in Kij.), large spoons. Kana mizizo.
**Misiwa,** *n. pl.* (ya) (= Musivo; Mshiba, Kij.; Lukano). Nalumua ni misiwa (ya) kanda menga. Nidzidzoka misiwa, inaluma. Yunalumua ni misiwa kosikosi.
**Mis'mari,** or **Misumari** (Kij.), *n.* (pl. of M'sumari, or Musumari), (1) a nail. Misumari i-la kua Adzomba, ela kuehu Nika-kakuna. Dim., Kasumari and Kisumari.
(2) Lancewood, which grows in East Africa, and is used for rafters, handles of tools, etc.; but its value is not known by the natives.
**Misumo, Mizumo,** *n.*

## [PDF Page 271 — Dictionary Page 258 (Mis — Mom)]

  Ka fua mizumo.
**Misungu, Mizungu,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Musungu, 1, *q.v.*).
**Miukiro,** *n.* (ya).
**Miumbirue,** *n.* (ya), what one was formed or created with. From Ku umba. Only used of bad qualities. *See* Akili. Mutu hiyu ndo miumbirueye a-fio-umbua, or, a-yo-umbua, ni Mulungu; hata muka-mu-ambira, kandasikira.
**Miwa,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Mua, *q.v.*).
**Miya,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Muiya, *q.v.*).
**Miyokue,** *n.* (ya, pl. of Muyokue), sweet potatoes.
**Miyuyu.**
**Mkafiri,** *n.* *See* Lanika. An infidel, an unbeliever.
**Mkambe,** *n.* *See* Mukambe.
**Mkango** (Kid.), *n.* (1) Madzere ga mkango, Hard Indian corn.
(2) An old maiden.
**Mkatha.** *See* Isu.
**Mkilekile,** *n.* (= Sudi sherti in Kij.), necessity.
**Mkuadio,** *n.* *See* Mukuadio.
**Mkuadu,** or **Nkuadu.** Ku sikira mkuadu. Nidzeria kitu nikasikira mkuadu kanoani. Kitu hiki ki-mkuadu, ka-ki-rika.
**Mkue,** or **Nkue,** *n.* (ya, za). Rero nidzirima mkue tahu mundani muangu.
**Mkuena,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), (1) a species of large crocodile, the alligator?, which is supposed to have emigrated. Mkuena yu nga mamba, ela ni mbomu ye, He resembles the mamba, but he is great; *i.e.* greater than the mamba. Niayose akienenda, hiko kua kombe, ku lola niuma, ela hikuno kua jimbe ndo ku lolako mbere. Kare kuari na mkuena, wasagala kifuani; basi atu akiokerera, mkuena akafuha madzi, akahenda kidengelesa, madzi gakafuha mutu kuenda varatu varivo *mkuena*, basi mkuena aka-m-guira. Mkuena akirira, muakawe ni ku nona sana.
(2) The name of a muansa.
**Mkulu, Mukulu** (?), *n.*, the name of a tree.
**Mkunguni, Mukunguni** (?), *n.*, a tree, the wood of which is useful for pestles.
**M'meitha.** *See* Mumaitha.
**Mo.** *See* Muno; Dziko; Kutuka; Fuluka; Mabahe. Kuamba unaomo ndereni muako, basi buma, unoe. Mo-bindoni u-dzukula-ni?
**M'odia,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miodia). Obs. A quiver consisting of bamboo cane. It has been superseded by the thiaka, or riaka, which is made of leather.
**Modzi,** *adj.*, one.
**Modzo.**
**Moho,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mioho). *See* Dzoho. Fire. Madzi ga moho, Hot water; water of fire. Dzua ri moho, The sun is burning hot.
  **Mohomoho,** used as *adj.* *See* Dovola. Warm, fresh.
**Mohola,** *v.a.*, an agricultural term. Hunamohola fue, huniale madzere.
**Mokolo.** *See* Salama.
**Mola,** *n.* (wa, no pl.) (= Alama), a mark. Mbuzi hiyu kaangamika-ina molawe, inamanikana. Mbuzi hizi sosi zina mola. Kifiu changu hicho kina mola, ka-ki-angamika. Vifiu via kizungu viosi vina mola, All European knives have a mark. Kitu hicho kina molawe, This thing has its mark.
**M'olofu,** *adj.* *See* Furika. Soft. Contracted from Maolofu.
**M'oloho,** *n.* *See* Muoloho.
**Moma,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mioma); the name of a species of serpent when full grown; when still young it is called bafie. It is about three or four feet long, but as big as one's arm. Muchirawe u gutu ka-u-na dza. Aki-ku-luma-udzunguwe ni ungi-yuna visania meno.

## [PDF Page 272 — Dictionary Page 259 (Mom — Mor)]

**Moma, Mooma.** Muniu una yaya, ela uzungu unamoma ukipigua ni mfula, hebu ukilala pehoni; ni ku hoka, basi ukamooma. Mifui yangu idzipigua ni mfula, idzimooma uzungu.
  **Momoka,** *v.n.* (= Ku enderera), to spread, to eat further. Said of a wound.
**Momu,** *adj.*, (1) (rel. to the Mo-, Mu-, and U- class). *See* Omeka; Omu. Hard. Contracted from Muomu. Gnania yuna moyo momu, hata aki-mu-ona muyawe yu mashakani ka maka kabisa. Muhi hiu ni momu, ka-u-demeka, nidzihenda gogota.
(2) (rel. to the pl. preform. Ma-). *See* Mafu; Girida. Hard, difficult. Contracted from Maomu.
**Mondo,** *n.* Obs.
**M'ongo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miongo). *See* Bashana. The back. Contracted from Muongo. Yudzi-ni-pa m'ongo; lit. He gave me his back; he has turned his back upon me. M'ongo wa kifiu, The back of a knife. M'ana wa m'ongoni. M'ongo wa fisi. Si vibanda, ni miongo ya fisi, A slight shed raised on one side only, to shelter from rain; lit. the back of a hyena. Shi vibanda, ni miongo ya fisi. Be kamuhenda ngari mongo wa fisi, muka-dzi-fidza mfula, ukaona vatu va ku busa moho? Dim., Kadzongo.
**M'ongolo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miongolo), (1) the copal tree. Contracted from Muongolo.
(2) The copal itself, which more correctly is called wongolo. Contracted from Uongolo. Kithanache ndicho uongolo (wongolo) hebu m'ongolo.
**Monso,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mionso), a species of wild cat.
**More,** *n.* (wa), (1) a drug which, when taken, is said to make one furious, and resolved to do anything, like the ndarama of the Waniasa. Muhaso wa more, or, mori.
(2) Madness, fury. Mutu hiyu yudzeguirua ni more, hu-m-funge, hata ku-m-kania kakanika.
**Mori** (Kid.) (= More).
**M'oria,** for **Muoria,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mioria) (= Mugosa in Kij.). *See* Oria; Ugosa. The name of a species of tree. Its bark, being very fibrous, is frequently used, in building native huts, for binding the sticks to their places.
**M'oro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mioro). *See* Kaya; Ihana; Endereza; Malau. (1) A speech, an oration. From Ku aria. Ndio moro hio wa ku nena; atu osi pia adzihamirua ni maneno ga gnania adzo-go-gomba; yudzegomba m'oro mudzo. Huende huka arie mioro. Ku aria m'oro, or, mioro (= Ku piga malau). Prov., M'oro mudzo ka-u-lavia dzua; lit. A good speech does not bring out the sun; *i.e.* it brings a matter soon to a conclusion, before the sun is risen high.
(2) The place in a town (kaya). M'oro ni vatu, atu asagalavo ku aria mioro. Ka-va-fiogua ni ache; ela dziku ya sayo ndo ache na ahoho afikavo moroni. Dziku hio ndo arivo na ruhusa ya ku ingira moroni. If a woman or child enters the place at any other time, the husband or father will be fined. The Wanyika say, Mucheo, etc., yudzifioga m'oro, be una malu, mbuzi na makolo mairi. The Wanyika have standing forms of address at the beginning and ending of their speeches. For those for the beginning, *see* Simila. The speaker then addresses himself to one in particular, whom he mentions by name, and

*Footer: 259*

## [PDF Page 273 — Dictionary Page 260 (Mor — Mua)]

  who keeps responding to what he says, while all the rest are listening in silence. The words, Kula Abegnania! Become great, live, father of Gnania! Resp., Hosi nahu kule! And may we live, both of us! mark the conclusion of a speech. Ndo Aravai avesavio maneno. Ukisikira yunakusa muyawe, basi yudzimala ku nena.
**M'oro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mioro), the dewlap. M'oro wa gnombe; pl. Mioro ya gnombe.
**Mosi, Moshi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miosi), smoke. Vana mioshi luakueluakue. Kanda hino na kanda hira.
  **Moshimoshi,** *n.* and *adj.* Rero ku moshimoshi, kuna murenge.
**Mosi,** ye all. Contracted from Muosi.
**Mosini.**
**M'oyo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mioyo). *See* Choyo. (1) The heart, the inner part of anything. Mioyo ya kirenge. Moyo wa ivu. *See* Funsia; Mimina. Dim., Kadzoye; magn., Dzoyo.
(2) The mind, soul. Utu hiu nidzi-u-henza muangu moyoni, m'egniewe nidzi-u-henda, wala sikuambua ni mutu. Mioyoyenu i-dze? Yuna mioyo miiri, He is double-minded. Ka ri moyoni jembe.
(3) A violent longing, a greedy desire after food. *See* Kuiru; Kotola. Ela muana hiyu yuna moyo; ndo ukafiri. Muana hiyu ni mui kua moyo; yuna-dzi-omeka makoncheharaka haraka, dza kuamba yunakimbira.
(4) Life; and in this sense also used as an *adj.* Gnania ni mukongo sana, yunarindua moyo (ni vevi na kufua). Utu hiu uhendao ka-u-nda-ku-ika moyo. Yukere moyo; or, Yuchari moyo, He or she is still *alive*. Mudzai sana ni ku zikua wa moyo, A great sorcerer is buried alive.
**Mrambo** (Kid.), *n.* (= Muhambo), a large trap. Prov., Mbogo, mania mrambo! Buffalo, mind the trap!
**Mrandu** (Kid.), *n.* *See* Randu. A debtor. Prov., Ka-ku-na mbira ya mrandu, There is no grave of a debtor; *i.e.* a creditor will never kill his debtor, it is in his own interest to keep him alive; I need not care much about payment.
**Msafula.** *See* Musafula.
**Msaha** (Kij.), *n.* (= Ndumo in Kir.), (1) tools for digging a grave.
(2) Derision.
**Mshiba** (Kij.), *n.* (= Lukano in Kir.), one who is satisfied.
**Mtamta,** *v.n.* *See* Muta.
**Mtumche,** *n.* (wa). *See* Era. Contracted from Mutumuche. Luhalo maririro and Mahaba, A woman.
**Mu,** *prep.*, in, used in composition; *e.g.* Muna, Mumo, Muga, Mudza, Himu, Himuno. Mukala poho muratu kipini, From there comes out a butterfly from the chrysalis.
**Mu.** *See* Za; Muka; Muki; Mudzi, etc.
**Mu,** *pers. pron. acc.*, him, her, or it. Mu-mu-ve, Give ye him or her.
**Mua.** *See* Kibakule. Pango ni mua muhi.
**Mua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miwa). *See* Kigua; Mvuha. The sugar-cane. Mua wa manga.
**Muababa,** *n.* (= Mbaba).
**Muachi,** *n.* (wa), a ewe. Muachi wa gnonzi (= Kid., Mfarika wa gnonzi).
**Muado,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miado). *See* Waniachi.
**Muadza,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Muadawada in Kij.), the name of a species of euphorbia. Its pricks are larger than those of the mufumakua. Ndo uhenduao viense via ku enendera na usiku wa kisa, una-

## [PDF Page 274 — Dictionary Page 261 (Mua — Mua)]

  aka to. Mutu akidema muadza, yufignia madzo, be okodema; una-u-dema ku-dzi-manirira, kuamba masiage gasi-ku-ingire madzoni. Masiage gaki-ku-ingira madzoni, ganaakaka muno; undakala mukongo hata vatu ngari dziku tahu, kundaona. Prov., Fignia madzo, udeme muadza.
**Muadzaka** (Kidigo), *n.*
**Muadzere** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kidzere in Kir.), the marmot.
**Muafuka.**
**Muafuka,** *v.n.*, to feast. Nidzimuafua, idzimuafuka, I entertain; he feasts. Ulongo hiu unamufuka, ni ui. Kirenge changu kidzimuafuka, My calabash has split — a small piece has broken out from want of an ngada (= vokavuda). Kavu yangu idzimuafuka.
  **Muafula,** *v.a.*, to entertain, to feast; (K.) to junket. Yudzi-m-muafula kitu, yukuenda ria. Yudzi-ni-muafula. Ku muafula niama na meno; but, Ku gniekula na mukono.
  **Mnafurika,** *v.n.* Ka-i-muafurika, ni niomu, sudi ni kate na kifiu.
**Muafumuafu.** *See* Gotola.
**Muaga,** *v.a.* *See* Umera. To spill, to scatter, to shed. Ku muaga madzosi, To shed tears. Mvula idzimuaga teramuka tu.
  **Muagamuaga,** *v. reit.* *See* Dengeva; Mukono. To squander.
  **Muagika,** *v.n.* (= Mukokolo). *See* Kutika. To be spilt. Gnombe zidzimuagika ueruni, ye, ye, ye, ye.
  **Muagikana,** *v.n.* Atu adzimuagikana luandani-angi tu.
  **Muagira,** *v. rel.* (= Ku muagira wimbi). Muagirani mudzusi, hurie wari. Enenda, uka-m-muagire madzi, aoge. Hega madzi, ukamuagire minazi. Gnania yudzi-hu-muagira midzanga.
  **Muagirana,** *v. reit.* *See* Bodza.
  **Muagirua,** *v.p.*
  **Muagua,** *v.p.*
**Muagalo,** *adv.*, across the breast. From Ku agala in Kid. Muche ni ku buma muagalo mavindi ga ushanga. Luera lua tia nikubumua muagalo.
**Muagnia,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miagnia). *See* Lindana.
**Muahi,** *adj.* *See* Muhinio; Wariko. Pertaining to circumcision. Kironda cha muahi, The wound made by circumcision before it is healed.
**Muahuladzansu,** *n.* (wa), the firstborn child. Muana wa mbere.
**Muaka,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Udzerero; Luiko. Year, spring.
**Muakaka,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a species of small lizard.
**Muaki,** *n.* *See* Uaki.
**Muako** (= Muakue). *See* Kota.
**Muakule.** *See* Hafunua. Yufungua muakule (= yupigua mbalahi).
**Mualambe,** *n.* (= Murungu), the name of a tree.
**Mualamo** (?). Muezi mualamo.
**Mualamu,** *adj.* *See* Kidubulu. Broad, wide. Muriango mualamu, A wide door.
**Mualamusi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Aalamusi). *See* Golosera. A judge. Gnania si mualamusi, waalamula muvunga na tafi; kaalamula keri, waalamula viakuria.
**Mualango,** *n.*, reckoning, account. From Ku langa.
**Mualubugu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of snake.
**Mualukisua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Alukisa, *v.a.* A cocoa-nut tree which yields toddy all the year round. Munazi urio na uchi hata muakani wambua 'nimualukisua, kuani, ka-u-dzererua; *i.e.* ka-u-richua ku gemua, udi we una-u-alukisa.

## [PDF Page 275 — Dictionary Page 262 (Mua — Mua)]

**Muamba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) a reef in the sea. From Ku amba. Kuna muamba ufumao baharini. Muamba unafuma (= unaruruma), mfula ni vevi na kudza.
(2) Nausa miamba, nihende pani za lungo, The thorn or prickle of a mulala. Muamba wa mulala; pl. Miamba ya milala.
**Muambalo.** *See* Ku ambala; Ku hambala.
**Muambalu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Mudzungu. The name of a kind of vegetable. Kidzanganio cha mudzunga ni muambalu, mudzunga ukaricha uzungu.
**Muambamba,** *adj.*, thin. Moyo muambamba; lit. A thin heart, a weak heart.
**Muambaniama,** *n. coll.* (wa, hiu). *See* Dzadza. The name of a species of weed.
**Muambeyu,** *n.* (wa).
**Muambo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Utundu, Kij.), pieces of the shell of a large snail (kola), rounded and strung; worn round the waist by women to support their garments. Muche ni ku zikua na muambo, ela kazikua na wakue, A woman is buried with a muambo, but not with her own. It is first the niece by a brother, or, in absence of her, by a sister or other female relative, who gives up her muambo for the burial, and receives that of the deceased. Miambo ni ku hendua ya kombe sa kola, Miambo are made of the shells of the kola.
**Muam'cheche,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of cricket similar to the bansi, caught, roasted, and eaten by children.
**Muamdasafundo.**
**Muaminifu** (Kij.), *adj.* *See* Lorera.
**Muamkere,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mnakaka).
**Muamkiriama,** *n.*
**Muam'lele,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miamileli). *See* Muleli. The name of a species of bird, remarkable for its tail-feathers, whence its name.
**Muamuagisa,** *v.a.* Ku muamuagisa ushanga.
**Muana,** *n.* (wa, pl. Ana). *See* Lolua; Niani; Zana. A child, a son, a daughter; a young animal, a young bird. Ara ana a gnania akalolua? Are the daughters of Gnania married? Muana angu, My child. Anangu, My children. Mdamu, A child of Adam, a human being. Muana Ravai, A native of Ravai. Muana Duruma, A native of Duruma. Muana Dzomba, A native of the coast (= Muravai, Muduruma, Mudzomba). Muana mbuzi, A kid. Muana gnombe, A calf. Ana Kuku, Chickens. Dim., Kadzana or Kidzana; magn., Dzana.
**Muanababa,** *n.* (pl. Anababa), a cousin on the father's side.
**Muanachane,** *n.* (pl. Anachane), a cousin on the mother's side.
**Muanache** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. Anache). *See* Kui; Lamula. Either a boy or a girl.
**Muanachetu** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Musichana in Kir. and Kid.), a girl, a young woman.
**Muanachuoni,** *n.*, a son of the book, a learned man, a schoolmaster. Mudzomba hiyu ni muana-chuoni.
**Muanadamu,** *n.* (pl. Anadamu). *See* Usira; Umba.
**Muanadzi** (pl. Anadzi) (= Muanafiale). Si mugeni, ni muanadzi; or, Si mumidzi, ni muanadzi. Prov., Muanadzi kafunsadzi.
**Muanafiale,** *n.* (pl. Anafiale). *See* Kore. A native, when free-born. Opp. to Muana wa kifiarira, and to Museonie.
**Muanafundi,** *n.*, an apprentice.
**Muanamadzi,** *n.*, a son of the water, a sailor.
