## [PDF Page 276 — Dictionary Page 263 (Mua — Mua)]

**Muana-mira-nchira,** *n.* (= Mira, and by itself does not exist in Kir.), the name of a species of thorny and creeping plant. Vikodzavie ni vitite, kama luhuaha; vikalangua muthea. Vidzihivie agangani ku buma pinguni.
**Muanamuari,** *n.*, a virgin.
**Muanamuche,** *n.*, a daughter, a young female animal.
**Muanamulume,** *n.*, a son, a young male animal.
**Muanandzi** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a young tree.
**Muananjira.**
**Muana wa dzidzo,** *n.*, (K.) eyeball.
**Muando,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Muando ni mudzi wa asunie avuvu; mutu, muegnie asunie angi aka-a-oniadzi ku rima, na kuaka niumba vatu vamenga.
**Muandzala,** *n.* (wa), the cholera. Muanso wangu udzihumbuka hangu dzana.
**Muanemuane,** *adv.* (= Barara in Kins.). Atu hia a-muanemuane kapatana mashauri. Aravai ere a-muanemuane mindani, ela hikara adzikuenda sagala vamenga kayani. Lukolo hilu kasikirana-a-muanemuane. Muhama hiu ubume pinda menga, usikale muanemuane. Via hivi yudzi-vi-richa muanemuane, kakabuma vamenga.
**Muanga,** *n.* (wa), (1) (= Changa, Mudalasa), a break in the weather. Kudzihenda muanga, mfula ka-i-nda-ni-piga, inda-ni-fisa kuangu.
(2) (pl. Mi-), the name of a species of tree, which, when decayed, yields a powder, called gogo, used as a perfume.
**Muangaluanda** (Kid.).
**Muangala,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a kind of bell. Niungu hi inarira muangala, ni nsima. Jembe hiri rinarira muangala, ni sima. Dim., Kidzangala; magn., Dzangala.
**Muangamisamasia.**
**Muangamsuhu** (Kid.).
**Muangani,** *n. coll.* (wa) (= Mkabilishamsha in Kij.), the name of a vegetable. Mboga sa muangani huna-si-dzangania na mudzunga.
**Muango,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Ndundu), a rise, an elevation. Muango hura. Ndundu hira.
**Muangu,** *pron.*, in of me, mine.
**Muanguangu,** *adj.* (= Mudzangu), quick. Mutu muanguangu kua kasi, A quick man at work.
**Muani** (Kidigo). *See* Fieta. Muani hiyu muanga, yunaanga.
**Muania,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Muania wa iwe. Muania we kikuku.
**Muanika,** *n.* (= Ndada in Kik.; Mondo in Kij.), a fabulous monster.
**Muano,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Muano wa niumba. Ku kuesa muano. Muano mure. Muano mufuhi.
**Muansa,** *n.* (wa, pl. Ma-). Kalondini bora akuesaye mikono akalamuse muansa!
**Muanso,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Fuguka; Dangazda. (1) (abstract) Beginning. From Ku ansa.
(2) (concrete) A fresh vanda when beginning to be tapped.
**Muao,** *pron.* *See* Fuma; Maheho; Ndimo. Lit. in of them, theirs.
**Muarabu.**
**Muaranda,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the membrane which covers the heart, the pericardium.
**Muaranda** (?).
**Muare,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of tree. Muare na Mufune ka-i-kuereka, inaheresa, wala kana tahi sa vevi, zi-kura-tu kure dzulu. Ndo ndzui na kosi aakavo vidzungi viao.
**Muari,** *n.* (wa, pl. Aari). *See* Ndarira. An orator. The word is becoming obsolete,

*Footer: 263*

---

## [PDF Page 277 — Dictionary Page 264 (Mua — Mub)]

  being superseded by Mulumbi. Atu hia ni aari.
**Muario,** *n.* *See* the pl. Miario; the sing. is rarely used.
**Muaro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Dzuva (gnombe). A small pointed stick, used in the play Ku dzuva gnombe.
**Muasi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Aasi). *See* Uaki. (1) A builder, one who distinguishes himself in building, doing it nicer and better than others—as every one builds his own hut. Aidimaye ku aka. Mutu hiye ni muasi, yunaaka to. Achogni na Agiriama ni aasi muno; agnietera mihi ni mingi, The people of Chogni and Giriama are great builders; they are wanton with their trees, because they are many.
(2) One who is of a hasty temper. Mutu hiye ni muasi, yunaaka dza moho kua hura usiru.
**Muatika,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of plant, the leaves of which are very bitter.
**Muaye,** *n.*, a spendthrift; any one who is careless with his property. From Ku aya. Gnania musiku ni muaye, vitu vie ka-vi-ika, vikarumbama, or, ka-vi-richa.
**Mubabayu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Mubahe,** *adj.*, pretty large. Gnania yuna munda mubomu. Resp., Ah! yuna munda, ni mubahe, ela si mbomu muno.
**Mubalazi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a shrub producing a kind of pea. *See* Mbalazi. Mubalazi mukuluhi.
**Mubamba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the branch of a mulala.
**Mubambakofi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Mudzani. The name of a species of tree, the African teak.
**Mubambara** (= Mualamu).
**Mubanansi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-).
**Mubawa,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the *name of a* plant producing the mabawa, a kind of bean. Mubawa wa kilube. Mibawa i-nialua kolo ra muhi, basi ikimera ikahambala, ikali ngila muhi kuenda dzulu.
**Mubesi, Mupesi** (Kij.), *adj.*, light, not heavy, quick.
**Mubie,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Mulala. A name given to the mulala when in an advanced state, but before bearing fruit.
**Mubishi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Abishi). *See* Dukudika. One who is obstinate, wayward, peevish, contentious. From Ku bisha. Mutu hiye ni mubishi.
**Mubobo, Mupopo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), Areca catechu.
**Mubohoya,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of creeping plant (lubugu), used for binding the vanda, and in building huts.
**Mubomu,** *adj.*, great, large. When speaking of largeness of body with regard to a person, the word Musiho is added; as, Mutu hiye ni mubomu, be musiho.
**Mubono,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the castor-oil shrub. It grows wild in abundance Unikani.
**Mubonokoma,** *n.*, the name of a wild shrub; so called from a slight resemblance to the castor-oil shrub, but being useless to man. *See* Koma.
**Mubukusa,** *n.* (= Mbukusa), the name of a tree.
**Mubumbafu, Mupumbavu,** *adj.*, foolish, stupid. Muhi mupumbavu, A knotty, hard working tree.
**Mubundukui,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of small tree.
**Mubungufu, Mupunguvu** (Kij.), *adj.*, one who is wanting in something. Mutu hiye kana akili, ni mupunguvu akilize ni punguvu. Mutu hiye kana muiri wa geri, ni mupunguvu (= muambamba).
**Muburudia,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the

*Footer: 264*

---

## [PDF Page 278 — Dictionary Page 265 (Mub — Mud)]

  name of a species of tree. Ndo udzonguao ngoma.
**Muburuga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of creeping plant. Tundose ni mburuga.
**Muchache,** *adj.*, little. Muhama muchache (= mutembe).
**Muchaka,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a thorn. The fruit is called taka.
**Muchari.** *See* Madiki.
**Mucharo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Acharo), a traveller.
**Muche,** *adj.*, female.
**Muche,** *n.* (pl. Ache), a woman. Muchangu, for Muche wangu, My wife.
**Muchea,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a wrinkle. Only used of infants. Michea ni ya muana mudzanga.
**Muchena,** *n.* (pl. Achena). *See* Kosi; Rumbusa. Muchena kitu hiki ka-vo. Muchena lumfo.
**Muchetu** (Kid. and Kidigo), *n.* (wa, pl. Achetu), a term given to elderly women, mothers and grandmothers. W'enda-vi we muchetu? Resp., Nenda, hiku kua muchetu, ni mukongo. N.B.—The word admits of no pron. poss. Sometimes the word Muche is still added, though it seems rather redundant; *e.g.* Muchetu muche huya yudzihenda utu. Muchetu hiya ni muche wa gnania.
**Muchia,** *n.* (wa, pl. Achia), one who is poor, destitute. Prov., Kid., Cha m'chia ka k'enda, for, ka-ki-enda, mbere, there may be an allusion to the word Muchira, Tail. In Kir., Ra munionge ka r'enda, for, ka-ri-enda mbere; or, Kitu cha munionge ka k'enda mbere.
**Muchinchiko,** *n.* *See* Mukingiko.
**Muchira** and **Mukira,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the tail.
**Muda.** *See* Mutha.
**Mudabidabi,** *n.* *See* Mfaruka; Maridawa; Husa. Uki-mu-ona muana yukala hivio, basi ni mudabidabi, si muana kitu, yudzifira.
**Mudada,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a large walking-stick. *See* Enenda; Ndada. Ni mufiere yunadzedzera na mudada.
**Mudadzi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a small tree, the leaves of which are applied to scalds. The Wadigo use them as a vegetable.
**Mudako, Mutako,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), posterior.
**Mudakombe, Mdakombe,** *n.*, the name of a tree.
**Mudakuma,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mtomoko in Kij.), the wild custard-apple tree. The fruit, Dakuma, pl. Maduma. Makodzage gana ngigi (= ni maziho).
**Mudalamuaka,** *n.*, the name of a plant or tree.
**Mudalasa,** *n.* (wa), clear weather. Rero kudzihenda mudalasa (= mudzari). Hangu dzana kudzihenda mudalasa.
**Mudamba,** or **Mtamba** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Kidomba. (1) A trap. Mutamba ni mutu akengaye atu, arie muivi, musinsi, etc. Mtu mtamba hiyu!
(2) Mutamba wa gnombe; pl. Midamba ya gnombe, A heifer (= Mfarika in Kir.). Yudzikala mutamba wa madzi ndani. Dim., Kadamba and Kidamba.
**Mudamu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Adamu), a human being. Corrupted from Muana damu; and this again has been corrupted from Muana wa Adamu, A child of Adam. Kifurifuri ndiye mudamu.
**Mudana,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a youth (corresponding with Musichana in females). Na mu sia ni muhoho, vino yudzikala mudana. Haya muchewe yuna ana airi, yudzikala abe mutu, be ni mudana wani kahiri vo? Gnania yudzidemua tengere,

*Footer: 265*

---

## [PDF Page 279 — Dictionary Page 266 (Mud — Mud)]

  yudzisiga niere, yudzikula kowe, yudzi-sara mafuha, be akichira hiva, unamania, vanachira mudana.
**Mudanche** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a pair of scales. The Wanyika only know them from the Wasuahili on the coast. Nidziona Mudzomba akipima pembe na mudanje.
**Mudandando,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a tree laid across a river, and fastened, to serve for fording. Mudandando ni mihi i funguayo, atu akadandanda akifuka muho. Note: If there was a bridge in the country, it would be called by this name.
**Mudanganifu** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Kabisa. A deceiver.
**Mudangidangi,** *n.* (pl. A-). Muche hiye kahurira va alume-uki-m-lola basi punde auke, akamute kua mulume yuya; auke, aende kua mulume mungine, mtumche hiye ni mudangidangi, kakala va mulume.
**Mudaro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kilaviro. Mudaro wangu mu-veni gnania, a-ni-dzukurire. Mudarowe gnania; mu-ni-pe mimi, nda-m-virikira.
**Mudebe,** *n.*, faintness from starving. From Ku deba, To sway. Yudzifunga mudebe kua ndzala. Hosi airi hudzifunga mudebe. The word seems only to be used in connection with Ku funga.
**Mudelema,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Mudembe,** *n.* Muhama hiu una afia, una midembe mibomu.
**Mudeni,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a debtor. Nin'enda kua mudeni wangu, nika-mu-ise. Mudeni ni iye airuaye.
**Mudide, Mutite,** *adj.*, small.
**Mudicho** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mucho in Kir.).
**Mudimu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the lemon tree. Ndio ufialao *ndimu*.
**Mudindi, Mutindi,** *n.* Mudindi wa masia ni masia maidzi, ga-ansa-go ku kamana, ela kadzankue ku henda luhandu; kikala kutu kua peho. Mutu hiye yu vuvu ra mudindi.
**Mudirima,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Mukundua. An armlet.
**Mudiriri, Mutiriri,** *n.* From Ku tiririka in Kij. Ela ku-mutiriri vino we? Ela muana si mutiriri hiyu?
**Mudo.** *See* Handika.
**Mudoki,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Wakigani; Muanabere in Kins.). Yudzihenda ivu mudokini, or, ra mudoki.
**Mudokozi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). From Ku dokoza. Gnania ndiye mudokozi, adzie-ni-ansa.
**Mudondolo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Ndio ufialao tondolo.
**Mudude,** *n.* *See* Omola. (K.) Fellow. Mudude wa mulala.
**Mududu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Adudu). *See* Kulukulusinge. (1) An insect. Dim., Kadudu and Kidudu; magn., Dudu.
(2) An internal ulcer. Yuna mududu wa ndani (= ivu ra ndani). Gnania yudzihenda mududu wa ndani, yudzionsua ni mududu.
**Mudui,** *n.* (wa, pl. Adui). *See* Kochesa. An enemy. Mudui wa wiha, An enemy at war.
**Muduku,** *n.* (pl. A-). *See* Duku. One good for nothing. Especially used of one who seldom hits in shooting (= Mukosi). Uwe undakala muduku ayao, rikaso, anagema, anarima, anaaka niumba, ela uwe kuna uwesa-ro, be u-muduku, You will be a good-for-nothing; your companions in age take down toddy; they cultivate the field; they build huts; but you have nothing that you are able for, etc. Mutu ni muduku hiyu! Uka hivo uimoni, usa-hu-difira niama. Muduku ni mutu, akosaye

*Footer: 266*

---

## [PDF Page 280 — Dictionary Page 267 (Mud — Mud)]

  niama uimoni veve (= mukosi). Mutu hiye msi-mu-ike-uimoni, yunda-hu-difira niama ni muduku muno; in Kid., Musuhu yudzi-u-dema sana yuna mduku wa dzunda yuna mduku wa idzoa.
  **Mudukuso,** *n.*
**Mudula, Mulula,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a shrub. Its fruit is the tulua.
**Mudula.**
**Mudumani, Mtumani** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. ), a surety. Mutumani ndiwe, kuani ndiwe udzayepiga daraka.
**Mudumia,** *n.* (wa, pl. Ad-), an old man. Originally Kig. *See* Mufiere; Mugonkue.
**Mudumua, Mtumwa** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Kibuanabuana; Mukimbisi; Zinza. A stave.
**Mudumudu,** *adv.* (= Tembetembe). Udzi-ni-riva mudumudu, Thou hast paid me in driblets. Kusa dimisirua ndo mudumudu.
**Mudundo, Mutundo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kidosi; Mukuva. A tree; the wood is soft. Muhalakore ni mutundo wa vidosi.
**Mudune,** *adj.*
**Mudungi,** *n.* (pl. Ad-) (= Mualili in Kig.), a putter-on of brass wire, etc.
**Mudungu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Wanamo. (1) The name of a species of small tree. Dim., Kadungu and Kidungu.
(2) The name of the gum which comes from it (in Kij. = Hancha). Used as a perfume in mixing it with butter. *See* Mbono, oil; Kadungu.
**Mudungudza,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Tungudza. The name of the plant which bears the love-apple.
**Mudurasi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Durasi.
**Mudza, M'dza** (= Dza). Kutua ni muhi. Kid. prov., Mudza mkulu karia mameye. Mudza niuma.
**Mudza,** *n.* (wa, pl. Midza). *See* Dzongonene. (1) The corner of a cloth. Ku valaza midza, Adana ndio ahendao midza, nguo zao za dzulu. Nalafia niusi za nguo, nihende midza. Navalasa nguo yangu midza.
(2) A fringe.
**Mudzadza,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a small tree or shrub. Mudzadza wegnie. Mudzadza gudu. Makodzage ganahalua, gakabumua luigani; ukabuma madzi, ukafuga na mikono, basi uka-mu-okesa mutu kidzoani, kidzoa kike-m-luma.
**Mudzafudzo.** *See* Isu.
**Mudzafue** (Kid.). Ni mani ya mkunde.
**Mudzai,** *n.* (pl. Adzai), a sorcerer.
**Mudzala,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Fukisa. A stalk of sorghum, Guinea-corn, after the head has been cut off. Midzala ya muhama ni migua idzayo fiolua masuche.
**Mudzalakaso,** *n.* (wa) (= Kij., Mtara), a small, frequent noise. From Ku dzalakasa. Ku sikira o mudzalakaso we? Sikisa, undasikira mudzalakaso.
**Mudzambano.** Uira wa dzambo.
**Mudzana,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a day, noon. Vatu hivo ni kure-ni vatu va midzana mihahu hebu mine ndo ukafika.
**Mudzanga,** *adj.* *See* Dzua, No. 3; Wari; Kimo. Young, fresh, new. Muezi mudzanga, New moon. (K.) Muhoho mudzanga, Babe, infant.
**Mudzanga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), sand.
**Mudzango,** *n.*, a palm. Angine ana midzango mi, ka fumbirua. Midzango inarira ndani.
**Mudzangu,** *adj.* (pl. A-) (= Muanakuangu). *See* Mulamba. My child. (K.) Mutu mudzangu, Diligent.
**Mudzani,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Kithana; Chamudzani), the

*Footer: 267*

---

## [PDF Page 281 — Dictionary Page 268 (Mud — Mud)]

  name of a tree. Mudzani, mubambakofi na mukuva, ndio mihi idzongua-yo vinu.
**Mudzapu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a palm tree.
**Mudzare.** *See* Divira. Kigumba cha mudzare.
**Mudzari,** *n.* (wa). Mvula idzegnia, be rero kudzihenda mudzari. Mvula i-si-vognia, ka-u-hadzua mudzari.
**Mudze,** *n.* (wa, pl. Midze). *See* Ongokerua. (1) Germ.
(2) *n. coll.* Ku lafia midze, To germinate, to sprout. Madzere gadzilafia midze. Muhama udzilafia midze. Nazi zidzilafia midze.
**Mudzedza,** *n.* (pl. A-). *See* Lolua. A man's father-in-law, mother-in-law, or son-in-law. This word is used only of the husband's relations; the wife's father-in-law is Abefiala, and Amefiala is the wife's mother-in-law. Mudze dzangu (for Mudzedza wangu), My father-in-law. Mudze dzangu mulume, A father-in-law. Mudze dzangu muche, A mother-in-law. Aravai akare ere akiogova adzedza muno; aki-mu-ona nchirani, akamu avukira kure.
**Mudzedzembe,** *n.* (1) (Kid.) (= Luera in Kir.). *See* Dimula. Mane.
(2) (Kir.). Obs. Yudzi-dzi-gutula hata yudzila mudzedzembe; but now they say, Yudzi-dzi-gutula, yudzihenda nundu. *See* Nundu.
**Mudzefu,** *adj.* (= Mudzigni; Muyuya). Mudzanga mudzefu hebu muyuyu (= ludzanga).
**Mudzeka,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mkeka in Kij.), a fine mat, such as are made by the people on the coast. Atu ache a kidzomba anasuka midzeka, ela Aravai kasuka; kalarira midzeka, alarira chingo. Viao ni vidzeka via ku sagira, na majamvi ga ku hendera ngao.
**Mudzele,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) (Kik.), a leather apron, decorated with beads, and worn by Wakamba females. Asichana a Kikamba ndio afumao midzele ya mithanga, ela akihalua ni alume, hura muthanga aka-u-gusa, akafuala mudzele wa ushanga. Dim., Kadzele.
(2) (Kir.), a border of beads round a woman's dress. Nabuma nguo yangu mudzele. Alonda ku buma midzele. *See* Marinda.
**Mudzembesi,** *n.* (pl. A-). Neno hiri rinahadzua ku zia aibu; vakala vo atu uogovao, kuamba: mutu hiye ni muzinzi, wamba: ni mudzembesi.
**Mudzengalungo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Lubugu. The name of a creeper.
**Mudzere,** *n. coll.* (wa), grain, corn. Madzere ga mudzere, Indian corn of grain picked out of the cobs. Mudzere wa muhama, Millet threshed out. Mudzere wa muvunga, Threshed rice. Mudzere wa ku vonda, Corn stripped of the husk or bran by pounding.
**Mudzerere,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a small tree.
**Mudzeria,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree.
**Mudzi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Midzi), (1) any place of abode.
(2) The people of a place or their representatives, the elders. Mudzi ari vavo. (In Kid., the pl. Adzi is used.) Vana muuyu wa viedi, ndivo atu avokala akikutana midzimidzi.
(3) Mudzi wa mbira, The place in a grave into which the corpse is laid. It is dug a little deeper, with ledges left on both sides, over which sticks are laid to prevent the

*Footer: 268*

---

## [PDF Page 282 — Dictionary Page 269 (Mud — Mud)]

  earth from falling immediately on the corpse.
**Mudzi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Midzi), a town, village, hamlet.
**Mudzigni,** *adj.*, fine. Vatu hiva vana mudzanga mudzefu mudzigni.
**Mudziki** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Mudzikidzi in Kir.).
**Mudzikidzi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Udzikidzi. The name of a palm. Mudzikidzi unga mukindu na mukuagna. Makumbi-ge ni mavudzu dza mudzapu. Of its bough (kumbi) winnowing-baskets (lungo) are made.
**Mudziva,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a basket of a middle size, larger than the kikahana, but smaller than the kavu. Mudziva wa kavu ni kavu tite. Mudziva ndo ulairuao mundani; lit. The mudziva it is which is taken to the plantation (*i.e.* the basket used when going to the plantation).
**Mudzo,** *adj.*, good, handsome, fair, beautiful.
**Mudzoare,** *n.* (wa). Ku lava mudzoare (= Ku irika kua ndzala, or, kua chiru). Kahuari na mudzoare wa ndzala, ela wa chiru. Ku guirua ni mudzoare.
**Mudzofi,** *n.* Mudzofi wa akili. Mudzofi wa haja. Mudzofi wa madzo. Mutu hiye ni mudzafi, kana kitu.
**Mudzofudzu.**
**Mudzolokana,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Mudzomba,** *n.* (pl. Adzomba) (= Mujomba, pl. Ajomba), the Kinyika name of the Msuahili, pl. Wasuahili, natives of the coast.
**Mudzore,** *n.* (pl. Adzore).
**Mudzovi,** *n.* (pl. A-). Mudzovi hiyu yunadzova uchi to.
**Mudzuano, Mdzuano** (sometimes pronounced Mdzano), *adj.* and *n.*, sweet, sweetness. Kitu hiki ki mdzuano, ki luchi muno. Uchi wa niuchi u mdzuano, kidza - u - luchi. Mdzuano hiu nao ni mungi muno.
**Mudzuchi,** *n. coll.* (wa), the name of a species of grass used for thatching. Mudzuchi, hidzuchi, muvunga, muriakulo-ndiso niasi sifimbiruao niumba.
**Mudzudza** (Kig.) (= Muze in Kir.).
**Mudzufu,** *n.* *See* Haja; Risa.
**Mudzukulu,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a grandchild.
**Mudzukumuhi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) the name of a tree.
(2) Dregs of wine.
**Mudzukusi,** *n.* (pl. A-), a bearer.
**Mudzulameno** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Muhangulamafi in Kir.), the name of a tree; lit. the teeth-cleaner.
**Mudzumbano,** *n.* (wa), the name of a dance, common among young people.
**Mudzumbe,** *n.* (wa). Kironda hiki ni mudzumbe wa firangi.
**Mudzumi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). Mudzumi wangu a-ni-dzumiraye ni mulumewe. Gnania ni mudzumi.
**Mudzumo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), what may be claimed and appropriated by any one. Mudzumo ni kitu ki-si-cho nialua mundani, kitu cha niasini, hebu cha dzakani, ndicho ki-ihuacho mudzumo; ni kitu ki-si-cho m'egnie. Midzumo ya dzakani, Wild fruits. Midzumo ya poani, All that is found on the coast by fishing, crabbing, etc.
**Mudzundu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree. Makodzage-ga-si-go dzankue ku fumula gara tu ga kirereni-ndo ahoho adoniolago, akahafuna, akadzikidza magansani, gakakala madune; be akaamba: Lola, magansagangu gadzikala madune to, dza mudzomba. Akaerekeza ni urimbo.

*Footer: 269*

---

## [PDF Page 283 — Dictionary Page 270 (Mud — Mue)]

**Mudzunga,** *n. coll.* (wa). Manige ga uzungu, ela ni ku hendua mboga, atu akarira na wari. Ukichitua, sodi uhokohe to, uifui.
**Mudzungu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kidonga. The name given to a European. Mudzungu ndio ufialao virenge, ela murenge unafiala marenge. Mboga sa Mudzungu ukahunda na munafu, hebu muambalu, hebu dzalakushe, hebu lukoe, basi ukadzanga-nira na hura Mudzungu, ukachita, ukasa kala uzungu muno kua hikira kidzanganiro. Mudzungu wa peko vidzunguvie vinariwa. Mudzungu wa uzungu-vidzunguvie ka-vi-rika, vi uzungu.
**Mudzungurisi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Mudzuo,** *n.* (wa). Mudzuo ni mufuaha wa muaka. Mudzuo wa mbere.
**Mudzuri,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mshumbi in Kij. and Mdanda in Kins.), the heaped-up part of food or grain put into vessels. Yudzievula dzima dele na mudzuri-yudzievula mudzuri mbomu. Dzima hi ka-i-ka idzala, ka-i-na mudzuri. Dzima sosi zi-dza-zo kudza zina midzuri.
**Mudz'usa, Mdz'usa** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Bora in Kir. and Kij.), a cockerel. Na-mu-va mdzusa wa kuku. Yunaansa ku-dzi-usa, ndosa aihue mdz'usa. Yuna-dzi-usa vara-dzi-ni ku-ra ku kula.
**Mudzuzi,** or **Mdzuzi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Prov., Mdzuzi wa moho udadua na lurimi, Slow and sure.
**Mue.**
**Mue,** *n.* (wa, pl. ), a hawk. *See* Mue; Luvanga; Ndzui. Mue kana ki; a-ndi-cho chona tu, ni ku hala, yu-nga fisi, naye kana musiro, for, a-ndi-cho-ki-ona, He will which it *see* (= whatever he sees).
**Muegnia,** *n.* (= Kidinkuiri).
**Muegnie** (gen. contracted into M'eguio), *pers. pron.* (pl. 'Egnie, for Aegnie). *See* Dubani; Guisua; Muando. One's self. Prov., Muegnie kifiu ndiye adzinsaye niama.
**Muegniewe, M'egniewe,** often pronounced quickly, as Muniewe (pl. Egniee). *See* Avahira; Futu; Kanira; Hensia. Mimi m'egniewe, I myself; pl. Suisui egniee. Uwe m'egniewe, Thou thyself; pl. Muimui egniee. Iye m'egniewe, He himself, She herself; pl. Ao egniee.
**Mueha** (M'eha), *n.* (wa, pl. Mieha), the name of a district in the Rabai territory. A long and hollow space of ground, generally the bed of a torrent. Mieha ya muvunga (= Fumbi in Kij.). *See* Chete. Mueha ni vatu va kadzuho (= kadzuho ka ansa vo). Dim., Kadzeha; magn., Dzeha.
**Muehu.**
**Muelo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Chemesa. Mutu yuna muelo 'ye, yuna gnieta hiyu; yunadzera hiyu. Machero undahenda muelo, uulage kahiri, ni kura ku gnieta na ku dzira.
**Muembe,** *n.* (wa, pl. Niembe), the mango tree.
**Muenchero.** *See* Muengero.
**Muenehu,** *n.* (pl. 'Enehu, for Aenchu).
**Muenendo,** *n.* (wa) (= Maenenzi), gait.
**Muenenzi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a good walker. Gnania ni muenensi sana, kadzoka hiraka. Muana ni muenensi hiyu, akikala nika ni mulume to, akadania vilungo fio.
**Mueneza,** *n.* Kibaria cha mueneza.
**Muengere,** *n.* (wa), the name of a species of creeper (lubugu), the leaves of which are glutinous, and, being pounded, are used for stopping up cracks in pots, as also for softening the ground when it

*Footer: 270*

---

## [PDF Page 284 — Dictionary Page 271 (Mue — Muf)]

  is too hard for digging, in which case the leaves are beaten into the hole intended to be dug. The root is also used as a medicine for a complaint called dudu.
**Muengero,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Madzula; Masa. That quantity of toddy the drawer has to give to the owner of the trees, according to the agreement; the rest, called masa, being his wages. Atu akemeruao-ndio ario na miengero. Derived from Ku enga, engera, Something taken off for another.
**Muenu,** *pron.*, lit. in of you, yours.
**Mueramuera, Mueremera,** *n.*, the name of a tree.
**Muerefu,** *adj.* *See* Fuha. Clever, skilful, shrewd.
**Muerekera,** *n.* (wa).
**Mueri,** *n.* (wa) (= Kiwandzoa in Kij.; Pande in Kins.), shell. Ku saga mueri.
**Mueruve,** *adj.*, white.
**Muesa,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miesa). Ni kadzihi katite. Makodzage huna-ga-buma maereni. Muesa, muesa! galuka ere; na ere, ere! galuka muesa! Akafuika kiasi cha kumi angue: ndo maere ganda-vo-henda tembe sana, gadzuke dza hura tu muesa.
**Muesi, Muezi,** *n.* (wa), (1), the moon; lit. the measurer of time. From Ku esa. Muezi muzanga, New moon. Muezi mugomu, Full moon. Muezi wa ku zira, Last quarter.
(2) (pl. Miezi), a month. Muezi udzi lumbua. Muezi udzila choani. Muezi ugogomoka. Govu ra muezi. *See* Mudzovi.
**Mueye** (Kid.) (= Muaye in Kir.).
**Mufaranga,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). Ana kuku akirikisua, anaihua afaranga: akila ufarangani, muche akaihua muso, mulume akaihua bora.
**Mufiakadzi** (Kidigo), *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a busybody, a talebearer, a sower of discord.
**Mufialusa, Muvialuza,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a midwife.
**Mufiasi, Muviasi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Fuisa. Avialuza angasagala, arinda muviasi, afiale, be, a-m-vialuze.
**Mufidina, Mufitina,** *nom. adj.* (pl. A-), one who instigates strife. More frequently the word is used without the preformative Mu-. *See* Fidina.
**Mufiere,** *adj.*, senior, elder, surpassing another in age.
**Mufiere,** *n.*, an elder. Afiere, The elders. The Afiere are the governing body of the tribe. Formerly the word also designated a very old man in particular, as Mukonkue did a very old woman; but in this sense the word has been superseded by Mudumia, borrowed from the Kig.
**Mufignio.**
**Mufimba.** Maneno higa nidzi-ga-richa mufimba, ka-ga-kadoka. Maneno higo gadzigombua, ela gadzirichua mufimba.
**Mufimba.**
**Mufimfira,** *n.* (wa). *See* Lubugu. The name of a creeping plant, used for binding the vanda.
**Mufinansi** (Kij.), *n.* (in Kir., Muumbi and Muumfi), a potter.
**Mufiringo,** *n.* Chembe hiri ka-ri-na mufiringo, musana ka-ri-firingirelo.
**Mufiru,** *n.* (wa).
**Mufiu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mifiu), a sword. From Ku fiula, The taker-off. Dim., Kadzifiu, A very small knife; and Kifiu, A common knife.
**Mufiumeno.**
**Mufo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mifo), the name of a species of creeper. Mufo ni lubugu, luhenda hambala, lukalingila muhi. Mufo ndo uhendao mafo.
**Mufo** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mifo) (=

*Footer: 271*

---

## [PDF Page 285 — Dictionary Page 272 (Muf — Muf)]

  Mufuananiko in Kir.), a torrent. Mufo udziingira. Mufo hi oka-u-chisa kamoe kamoe. Mufo unachira fo.
**Mufu,** *adj.* Muhama hiu ni mufu, maonsa gadzikoniokera, masuche ganalewalewa. Muhi hiu nidziamba ni mufu, kumba ni muidzi.
**Mufuadzi,** *n.* and *adj.* (wa, pl. A-) (= Merhem in Kij.), one who is deceased, late, defunct. Mufuadzi baba, My late father. Mufuadzi gnania kuamba yuko, maneno gano a nga-ga-fanisa, kudzafua iye, dzi idzi-banangika. Afuadzi gnania.
**Mufuaha,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Linkua; Luvi; Mudzuo. (1) A younger brother or sister.
(2) A junior, an inferior, a successor. Afuaha angu.
**Mufudu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree. Its fruit is called fudu or pfudu. (1) Mufudunga, contracted from Mufudu unga, The flower mufudu, the wood of which burns, even when green, like that of the mukuakua. (2) Mufudu madzi, The wood of which is sappy.
**Mufufi,** *n.* (pl. Afufi), a fisher. From Ku fua. Like the word Mugena, it is sometimes used in scolding. Enda hiko mufufi we! Thus saying, you have greatly despised a person. Udzi-m-mena sana—ni vi sana.
**Mufufu.**
**Mufugi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a breeder, a rearer. Mufugi wa gnombe, A rearer of cattle.
**Mufugo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Fugirana; Nionia.
**Mufugudira,** *n.* (wa), closeness, oppressiveness of heat; as peculiar to a confined space. Derived from Ku fuguda. Usiku wa rero sikaona usinsisi kua mufugudira. Kuna dzua ka-vi-neneka, be kudzi-*henda* mufugudira.
**Mufuhi,** *adj.*, short.
**Mufuhufu,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-) (= Ufuhufu). Muana ni mufuhufu ye akavindua dya uha.
**Mufui,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mifui), an arrow. Mufui wa peho, A cold, *i.e.* unpoisoned arrow, in contradistinction to a Mufui wa uzungu. Dim., Kadzifui.
**Mufui,** *adj.* Mutu ni mufui hiyu! akafua sana, hata maneno ka-ga-mania, wabumbusua ni ukongo. Gnania ni mufui; yudzigomba maneno ga ku fua. Neno adzaro gomba, ka-ri-hama, ela hiro ra keri ndiro kama ri dzaro buma tembe.
**Mufuiko,** *n.* (wa). Mufuiko ni makodza ache afuikirago madzi pfukoni, kuamba gasimuagike.
**Mufuko,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a bag, of cloth only. Magn., Rifuko.
**Mufulana,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Chari; Chere. A young man or a young woman. Yudari mufulana, ka-dza-kala mufiere. Muche hiye s'ambe ni mufiere, yuchari mufulana. Atu hara unga-a-ona akifuina uira, usiambe ni adana, ni afulana, ela ni ku hensa uira tu.
**Mufumakua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Muadza), the name of a species of euphorbia. Vidziyavie ni vitite, vifuhi.
**Mufumbiso,** *n.* (wa). Dzana naria kitu nikifumbirua, hata rero mufumbiso ni-chari nao.
**Mufumbulo,** *n.* (wa), the name of a dance, not now practised. Uira wa mufumbulo wari ukifuinua hangani. Atu ari akifuifia mufumbulo, akacheza cho, akapiga kikobuekobue hata mukono ukahumbuka miladzo hebu akahenda marengerenge.
**Mufumo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree. Ndo udzonguao malomba ga maonsa na tana, ni ahoho.

*Footer: 272*

## [PDF Page 286 — Dictionary Page 273 (Muf — Muf)]

**Mufumulandola,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Fukisa.
**Mufumurisi,** *adj.* and *n.* *See* Husa. Forbearing, enduring, persevering. Yuna moyo mufumurisi (= musabidi, *see* Duria). Mutu hiye ni mufumurisi. Kuku hiyu ni mufumurisi, akikarira, kauka machini harakaharaka.
**Mufundo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a grudge. Babaye yuna mufundo, ndo udzaoguira muana. Muana yunaguirua ni mufundo wa babaye, hebu mameye.
**Mufune,** *n.* (= Dza mboyamboya?). *See* Uyiwa. Yuna mifundo mingi.
**Mufunga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kanani. Ku ika mufunga. Kuamba kuhensi ku lafia uchi, wamba: nda-ku-kenga, basi na-ku-va mufiu wangu mufunga.
**Mufungahe,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Mau. A hebdomad. It is observed only in connection with certain usages and customs. (1) In childbirth. Muana akivialua, yuna mufungahe wa niumbani, na mfungahe wa ndze, ndo mameye akala mundani, Mother and child remain for seven days in the house, and for another seven days she may come out, but does not go to any distance. The husband also considers himself bound during the fortnight to abstain from women; if he is guilty, he does vokodza mihaso. This custom for the women applies to the Wasuahili; the Wanyika women are often seen at hard work before the babe is a week old.
(2) In circumcision. Ana akiarikua, ana mifungahe miiri, ya ku sagala, wa ndani na wa ndze; ikisira, basi akaenenda.
**Mufungiso,** *n.* (wa). Kuna mufungiso wa maidzi-ka-ga-chirika. Kuna mufungiso wa mvula, atu akasa wesa ku upuka ndze.
**Mufungo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a heavy stick; one of the four heavy sticks got ready by every new kambi, to be used during the time of their initiation in gathering their fines, after which they are laid up in the rungu.
**Mufungu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kolo; Thiaka. The bamboo cane. It does not grow in the Kinyika country, but is occasionally brought from Usambara. The cane was formerly used for quivers, which are now made of leather. They now only use bamboo in dancing, as a kind of rude musical instrument, stamping them on the ground. Mufungu wa babayu, wa muono. Mufungu ndio upigiruao sayo. Dim., Kafungu.
**Mufunguo,** or **Mufungulo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a key. Nidzigula mufungulo wa ku fugurira, or, sundurira kasha.
**Mufunguriri,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Mufunguriri wa uriri. Mufunguriri wa ludzaga.
**Mufunsakuni.**
**Mufuo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mfuo in Kij.), a sandy beach.
**Mufuo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Mufuo ukahenda fu-fu-fu, peho ikaingira. Ku fuguda mifuo.
**Mufure, Muvure,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) a wooden bowl. Aravai a kare, mpiga sao sari mifure, ela hikara basi ni mpiga za ulongo, za ku henda umbua.
(2) The name of a tree; it makes excellent timber and planks. Mufure wa mufure; wa mumbu; wa muvula, A basin made of the mufure tree, etc. Mufure unawaka.
**Mufuri,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Kifurifuri). *See* Gumo. Shade, an umbrella. (1) Muhi hiu una mufuri mudzo, *i.e.* pehoye ni mbidzo, inazizima. (2)

*Footer: NIKA. | T | 273*

## [PDF Page 287 — Dictionary Page 274 (Muf — Mug)]

  Mufuri wa kuehu ni gumo, An umbrella with us is the leaf of the deleb palm.
**Mufusi,** *n.* (= Mufugi). Abe Mkamba ndiye ayekala mfusi wa gnombe, or, wari mfugi wa gnombe. *See* Ufugi; Ufusi.
**Muga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miga). *See* Lairana. A crack. Muga huno ukalairana, kirenge kinafudza. Ni dzuga ro, wamba ni muga? That is a large crack; do you say it is a small one? (a common or ordinary one). Dim., Kadzuga; magn., Dzuga.
**Mugafii,** *n.* Gnania ni mugafii, yudziga via niama, yudzienesa atu osi, adziokala vavo.
**Mugagana** (Kid.), *n.* (= Muga in Kir.; Ufa, pl. Niufa, in Kij.), a rent, a crack, a chap.
**Mugagando** (Kid.).
**Mugagasi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-).
**Mugala,** *n.*, a native of the Galla country.
**Mugamamu,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-) (= Salamala), a clever workman, carpenter, etc.; one who is master of his business. Yuna madzo mutu hiye, ni mugamamu, yudzonga to.
**Mugandi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree, very good for planting, as it grows readily. Mugandi ka-u-mera-dzi, ukakula, ukakala mbomu; sudi umere pangoni ya muhi muyawe, hebu kisiki cha muvingo.
**Muganga,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Mganga. The medicine-man, the sorcerer, a witch-doctor.
**Mugangando,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mugagando in Kid.), an agricultural term.
**Muganganga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the highest beam of a native cottage which supports the roof.
**Mugasija** (some also pronounce **Mungasija**), *n. coll.* (wa). *See* Dzoyo; Mifufujembe. The cassava root. The pl. Mi- is rarely used. Hala mugasija kaidima ku gnola. Twice in the year the root becomes waxy, in consequence of the rains and heat. Dim., Kagasija and Kigasija; others, Kangasija and Kingasija.
**Mugema,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), one who draws toddy, which with the Wanyika is the business of all young men. Nevertheless, the word is sometimes used in contempt. Enda hiko mugema we! He replies, Kuani ku-ni-iha mugema? Why do you call me a mugema? Answer, Be ku gema vio? Mugema, Sina kazi? kaziyangu ni ku gema tu? denguri hiro be si-ri-henzi.
**Mugeni,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a stranger. Mu-anseni mugeni. Niama ya mbere ikahewa m'egnie kaya, ya viri ikahewa mugeni.
**Mugeri,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), one who speaks the truth, one who is truthful.
**Mugesi** (Kid.) (= Muzosi in Kir.). Mugesi hiyu yunagera uchi to.
**Mugina,** *n.* (wa). Niasi sidzimera, sidzihenda mugina.
**Mugnambo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree, the fruit of which are the gnambo.
**Mugnaro.** *See* Ugnaro.
**Mugniagnanii,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a defrauder.
**Mugnialu** (Kig.), *n.*, dung, manure.
**Mugniefu,** *n.* (wa) (= Peho in Kir.), (1) (Kidigo), wind.
(2) (Kir.) (= Peho sa kucha; Umende), the coolness of the morning. Mugniefu wa manina.
**Mugnierere.** Atu akauya mugnierere.
**Mugnieti,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Kimene. One who is naughty, wilful, a mischief-maker.
**Mugnieto,** *n.* (wa), naughtiness, wantonness. Manenoge gana mugnieto.

*Footer: 274*

## [PDF Page 288 — Dictionary Page 275 (Mug — Muh)]

**Mugninua,** *n.* (wa, pl. ?), the name of a shrub or plant.
**Mugniore,** *n.* *See* Muniore.
**Mugnogno,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of an insect somewhat larger than the mulonsi.
**Mugnuiri.**
**Mugoma,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the tusk of a female elephant. Migoma ya pembe ni sa ndzofu ache, magoma. Dim., Kagoma.
**Mugomba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) the banana tree.
(2) A roll of tobacco. Nidzihenda migomba yangu ya tumbaku, nagusa. Enda! uka-m-futire mugomba, uka-m-virikire, a-fungire kironda.
**Mugombi,** or **Mugomvi,** *n.*, a quarrelsome person. Gnania ni mugomvi sana, yunaerekesa maneno, ukafungua na maneno, iye yuna-ku-fugula.
**Mugongohi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the bridge of the nose. Mugongohi wa pula. Mugongohi wa lukodza.
**Mugonkue.** *See* Mukonkue.
**Mugono,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a wickerwork cage used for fishing. Mugono unga malema ga kidzomba. Mugono wa ku vuira makumba.
**Mugorofii,** *n.* Ku ansua ni mugorofii.
**Mugoti,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Za; Muisu. Stalk. Mugoti wa isu, wa nanasi. Mugoti wa ludago. Mugoti wa mulanga; or, Mugoti wa langa. Dim., Kagoti and Kigoti.
**Mugovu,** *n.*
**Mugua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Lugua). *See* Haja; Kigua. A stalk. Mugua wa muhama, maere, madzere.
**Mugugu,** *n.*, the name of a species of grass. Niasi za mugugu si-muhoni, sikanona sana.
**Muguisho,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the tail of a giraffe or a zebra when used by a muganga. Kare wari ukiihua m'ingo. Formerly it was called m'ingo. M'ingo is the real Kir. word and still in use, though not so frequent.
**Mugumba,** *n.* (pl. Agumba) (= Tasa, but this is more generally used for animals). *See* Fuisa. One who is barren.
**Mugumi,** or **Mugumiro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a groan. Ku piga mugumi, To groan. Yu piga migumi, yuasani? hebu yudzihendua-dze?
**Mugumo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Mugumo ukihenda mimba, basi unakomala.
**Mugungundu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the backbone, or spine.
**Muguoguo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Musimu. The name of a fibrous plant. Hemp (?). It does not grow in Rabai, but in the more northern parts of the Wanyika country.
**Muguto,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Muhadaya** (= Mufiosi?).
**Muhakiso,** *n.* (wa). Dziku dziku ni muhakiso.
**Muhala.** *See* Goromue.
**Muhalakore,** *n.* (wa, pl. ), a mistletoe. Una makodzage, kidza ni ku henda marua, ukafiala tundo, sikariwa ni vidosi.
**Muhali,** *n.* (wa). Dzovani uchi, huguire kibaria kibaria, basi hu-m-rinde muhali. Muhali wa muche.
**Muhalifu** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a transgressor.
**Muhama,** *n.* (wa) (= Mtama in Kij.), Holcus sorghum, white millet. Dim., Vihama.
**Muhambo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a trap. Muhambo wa koma, a cobweb.
**Muhamfi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a traveller.
**Muhamfua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of acacia, with red blossoms.
**Muhanda,** *n.*, (1) (wa, pl. A-), one who is cleanly in his habits. Mutu huya ni muhanda, yuna-dzi-dunsa, kahensi dzama.
(2) (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mta-

*Footer: 275*

---

## [PDF Page 289 — Dictionary Page 276 (Muh — Muh)]

  nda in Kij.), a strip of meat. Mihanda ya niama.
**Muhango,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of tree. Ndio ufialao muhango.
**Muhangula.** *See* Ku hangula.
**Muhangulamafi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mudzulameno in Kid.), the name of a species of tree.
**Muharara** (Kij.), *adj.*, weak-minded. Muana hiyu yuna moyo muharara-wa ku dzoa haya. Mutu asie moyo musubidi arie na moyo muharara akiona atu anagafia niama, akalaiwa ni dzidzo, kuamba apate ningi iye.
**Muhasidi** (Kij.), *n.* Muhasidi ni mutu asiehensa ku ona kitu cha mutu kidzo.
**Muhaso,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Muhawe.** *See* Debe. Lukodzalue ni lualamu kama makodza ga mukungu.
**Muhehera,** *n.* (wa), a fowl which is going to breed for the first time, a pullet.
**Muhema.** *See* Dzange; Mgagando. Muhema ni munda muvia, uansao ku rima hikara. In Kir., the word is being superseded by Luanda.
**Muhembo,** *n.* *See* Thatha.
**Muhengulamafi,** *n.*, the name of a species of tree.
**Muhensi, Muhenzi, 1,** *n.*, a maker, a doer, a mechanic. From Ku henda. Rarely used. Gnania ni muhensi wa kasi sana, ni mukurima. Ni muhenzi wa kazi, I am a lover, a doer, of work.
**Muhensi, Muhenzi, 2,** *n.*, a lover. From Ku hensa. Wari muhensi wa uchi sana, He was a great lover of toddy.
**Muhepe,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of small tree or shrub, used for perfuming.
**Muhi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mihi), (1) a tree. Dim., Kadzihi and Kidzihi; Magn., Dzihi, pl. Ma-.
(2) The name of a disease, somewhat resembling cancer, but eating the flesh from the bones, and spreading over the body; whence its name. They distinguish between two kinds: (*a*) Muhi wa tafuna, This is considered less dangerous, and soon yields to proper treatment. (*b*) Muhi wa mbanga.
(3) A drug. *See* Vavisa.
**Muhidaji, Muhitaji** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Gurira. Lit. a wanter, one desirous to buy, etc.; hence a beggar.
**Muhinio,** *n.* (wa), circumcision. Muhinio udzifika, hundakuenda virika ahoho ahinue.
**Muho,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miho), a river.
**Muhoho,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Hasirika; Mafuadzi. A child, junior.
**Muhoi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Ma-), the name of a tree.
**Muhombo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Muhondo.**
**Muhongolo,** *n.* (pl. Mi-), the copal tree. Uhongolo, Copal.
**Muhoto,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Muhoto ni muhambo wa pania, uhenduao wa kivo.
**Muhua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Ahua) (in Kij., Mjomba), the son or daughter of a brother's sister, a nephew, a niece, but in this restricted sense. For the children of a brother there is no special name; he merely calls them ana as well as his own. Mutu yunagusa muhuawe hebu mudzukulu we wa kuche, ela wa ku lume kagusa; akigusa wa ku lume, ni kana mutu adzeye avaha deni; kuao kuche akakutana, akakudza guira muhuao wa kuche, nao akakuenda gusa.
**Muhuiko,** *n.*
**Muhula,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Muhumba, Mumba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of soft wood. Sheep slaughtered for sacrifices must be laid on branches of this and the mukone tree. Its leaves and roots also are used in the per-

*Footer: 276*

---

## [PDF Page 290 — Dictionary Page 277 (Muh — Mui)]

  formance of their ceremonies, and as charms.
**Muhumiki,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a servant. Kagula mtumua muzungu-kana musunie; ela atu akala o nave ni ahumiki. aka-a-va feidayao hebu mafungugao.
**Muhumisi,** *n.* Rarely used. Nidzi-m-huma gnania musiku, kuamba a-ni-usire muchi, chamba muche akahensa, basi adze, a-ni-ambire nikalole.
**Muhumua.** Gnania yudzilafiwa muhumua wa malu.
**Muhunde** (= Mudude).
**Muhuye** (Kij.), *n.* Sina muhuye.
**Mui,** *adj.* *See* Mera. Evil.
**Muida.** *See* Muino (= Mbatha?).
**Muidio,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (in Kig., Muguva). *See* Lumba. An awl. Dim., Kadzidio.
**Muidzi,** *adj.*, (1) unripe, green, raw.
(2) Immature, imperfect, useless. Muhi hiu ni muidzi, This tree is green. Mutu hiyu ni muidzi, kakaifua, ni mukaha, ni kudza wesa makasi.
  **Muidzimuidzi,** *adj.*, greenish, somewhat unripe, raw.
**Muidzio** (Kig. ?).
**Muifii,** *n.*
**Muifu, Muivu,** *adj.*, ripe. Muhama hiu ni muivu.
**Muigni** (Kij.). *See* Mulungu; Sema. An owner, a possessor; hence God. *See* Dzi. Atu adzidubu kare, ana-ku-amba: Muigni ku sema: Muigni-nda ku lalama. Yudzi-m-piga hata yudziamba: muigni. Asunie-Angindo hiko kareari akiamba: muigni. They said, Muigni baba to a free man, and Muigni mama to a free woman. Akilamusa atu anguana, ela hangu dzana alamusa vivi kinika, akiamba: baba na mayo. Kuro akidukanisa muchira, basi yuna-ku-amba: muigni. In Kig., a woman will say to her offended husband, Muigni ! bai, mulum'angu, ni dza richa, na kosa; si nda ku kosa, kaviri, ni dza mania na henda vi; basi nta richa. Muigni meho.
**Muiko,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miiko, Miko), a spoon. From Ku ika, To put. Dim., Kadziko, Kiko, and Kidziko; magn., Dziko.
**Muimbo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Suhira.
**Muimui,** *pron.*, you, ye.
**Mui-mui.**
**Muingo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miingo, Mingo) (= Muguisho). Muingo wa ku vungira Mulungu. Gnania yupigua muingo-ni mudzai.
**Muino,** *pron.* (= Muimui), you (ye). Muino muna-ni mui-mulonda-ni mui; va ukeni, muenende.
**Muinsi,** *n.* (pl. Ainsi). *See* Mukala. A hunter. Rarely used. Akamba aoansa kudza Udzoroni, ari ainsi.
**Muiri,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miiri?). *See* Mbawa. The body. Miiri miiri, Two bodies; *i.e.* colours. Used of such animals as have half of their body one colour, and the other half another. Miiri mingi idzikutana. Ku henda muiri, To become stout. Ku guirua ni muiri, To become unwell; lit. To be seized by the body. Ku-m-richira muana muiri. *See* Hensia. Ku foya na miiri ya atu. Foya na moyoo, usifoye na miiri ya atu, kuenda ukiamba atu luambo.
**Muirika,** *v.a.* Kuani ku-ni-muirika. Una-ni-muirika, udzi-ni-mena. Ku m'irika niuni. Hufunge viense, huka m'irike niuni, or, mafuancho. Der., Kim'irim'iri; Lumuiri.
  **Muirikira,** *v. rel.* *See* Makansa; Lumuiri; Mahepe; Keregnense. Chense cha ku muirikira dzoa, niuni, etc.

*Footer: 277*

## [PDF Page 291 — Dictionary Page 278 (Mui — Muk)]

**Muiro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the trunk of an elephant. Muiro ndo adzumirao, The trunk is that he forages with.
**Muiru,** *adj.*, black.
**Muisho,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miisho, Misho), the end, termination. Muisho wa mambo higa kahumania gandafiokala. Muisho wa mambo higa gandadukia utu usiku, or, gandakala utu usiku. Mambo higa misho ye gandaisha mai. Mishoye indaisha utu usiku; sing. Muishowe undaisha utu usiku. Mambo higa-muishoni gandakala madzo.
**Muisu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Kigomba). Mugoti wa isu, uki-u-anika, ukiuma, unaihua muisu; ndio usagiruao kumbaku ya ku nudza; ni kilungo cha kumbaku.
**Muivi** (Kidigo), *adj.* (= Mufuhi in Kir.). *See* Ivi. Short.
**Muiya,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miiya, contracted to Miya). *See* Kuaniula; Mufumakua. A thorn; lit. a stealer. From Ku iya, To steal. Prov., Huo ni muiya wa ku-dzi-tunga m'egnie, ka-u-luma. That's a thorn for pricking yourself with, for the purpose—it does not sting; *i.e.* You have brought this upon yourself. Nidzi-tungua ni muiya, be si mu-iya-o, ni ridziya (pl. Midziya); lit. I have been pricked by a thorn, but not by a common thorn; it is a very large thorn. Dim., Kadziya and Kidziya; magn., Dziya and Ridziya.
**Mujakasi, Mujakazi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Ajakasi), a bond-slave, a slave-girl.
**Mujomba,** *n.* (pl. Ajomba) (= Mugomba), an Msuahili, a native of the coast.
**Mujume** (Kij.). *See* Mudzanga. Saramala hiyu ni mujume, yunamania to.
**Muka.**
**Mukabu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Mukabu muitu.
**Mukadi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kadi.
**Mukaha,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) a cloth wound round the arm for the purpose of fighting, the left arm being used as a shield. This was done in the play Ku pigana mavi.
(2) One who is lazy. Gnania ni mukaha wa ku rima.
**Mukahe,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), anything shaped like a loaf or cake. Mukahe wa tumbaku, A cake of tobacco. Dim., Kakahe and Kikahe.
**Mukakasi** (= Kihiche).
**Mukala,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a hunter. Mukala yunainsa; pl. Akala anainsa.
**Mukamba, 1,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a piece of cotton cloth in which the women carry their babies. The babies are tied on the back. Mukamba wa muana; or, Mukamba wa ku erekera muana (= Mueleko in Kij.). Mukamba mameye Kamba.
**Mukamba, 2,** *n.* (pl. Akamba), a native of Ukamba. The Wasuahili on the coast formerly called them Warumangao.
**Mukambe,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) Na piga mukambe ueru wangu, niniale, kuani ueru udzienera. Yudzipiga mukambewe mundani hata yudzi-u-mala. Atu hara ana piga mikambe (= anafumbula).
(2) Mukambe wa tero. Mutu hiye yudzipiga tero, nasikira mukambe ukirira.
**Mukanju,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the cashew tree. Ndio ufialao kanju (pl. Makanju), kanju naro rikafiala ngorosho.
**Mukari,** *adj.*, fierce, savage, ravenous, greedy. Gnania ni mukari, yuna choyo na uchi. He! mutu mukari yuya! yuna choyo'ye, kafuga, niama mbidzo yuria m'egnie, ka-a-va muche na ana, ni ku-dzi-ku-lusira kuria he! cheye tu.

*Footer: 278*

## [PDF Page 292 — Dictionary Page 279 (Muk — Muk)]

**Mukasa,** *n.* (pl. Akasa). Mukasa Chindua. Mukasa muezi, Venus.
**Mukashomba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a coward. Mutu hiye ni muoga muno ni mukashomba.
**Mukasi,** *n.* (pl. Akasi), a worker.
**Mukatale,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (K.) rack, pillory. Gogo ra mukatale. *See* Golua.
**Mukebe** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a mug, a tin. The natives call the tins in which the preserved meats, etc., are taken to their country. Mikebe. Dim., Kakebe.
**Mukere,** *adv.* Mukere vi? Where are you?
**Muki.**
**Mukimbizi,** *n.* (pl. A-). Mudumua hiye si mukimbizi, wahendakimbizua ni muyawe.
**Mukinda,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a young cocoa-nut tree.
**Mukindo** (?). Mukindo wa nguo.
**Mukindu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Mudzikidzi. The name of a species of palm tree, the leaves of which the Mohammedans on the coast make their finest mats of. Of the bough itself the Wanyika make winnowing-baskets. *See* Lungo.
**Mukingiko, Muchinchiko,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kingamia. Something laid across. Nidzibuma mikingiko ya uriri.
**Mukingiri,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of tree (acacia?). Mukingiri una moyo momu dza muvingo; ndo muhi uhensuao ku hendua kivesa, unawaka. Dim., Kikingiri.
**Mukoa,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a thong. Mukoa wa chingo. Mukoa wa madzere, The leaves of the cobs of Indian corn, when tied together for hanging them up. Dim., Kakoa and Kikoa; magn., Rikoa.
**Mukoba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a basket-bag, hung over the shoulder, made of milala. Mukoba ni wa mulala. Dim., Kakoba and Kikoba; magn., Koba and Rikoba.
**Mukobi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Akobi). *See* Hadaya.
**Mukodo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), wire thinner than the madzango and kidindi. Mukodo mueruve wa gnandu, White wire, of brass. Mukodo mudune wa mukundua, Red wire, of copper. Of iron, *see* Mulinga. Mikodo idzibanangua ni madzango, ka-i-na kima kaviri.
**Mukodze,** *n.* (wa) (= Muvuye). *See* Ridira; Ngufu. Strength. Only used negatively. Sina mukodze. Kana mukodze, hata muche yuna-m-dieka. Lagare ni rofu, kana mukodze.
**Mukodzo,** *n.* (wa), semen.
**Mukodzolo,** *n.* (wa). Gnania ni mukongo wa mukodzolo.
**Mukoi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Akoi), a cousin the son or daughter of your mother's brother. Mukoi ni muana wa avu, na avu ni mayo nduguye. *See* Muhua.
**Mukoko,** *n.*
**Mukokola,** *n.* (wa), froth left behind by rain water. Mukokola wa mvula.
**Mukokolo,** *n. coll.* (wa). Kuangu mundani kudzimera mukokolo, or, kudzi muagika mukokolo hata ikarimua. Ka-i-nda sira.
**Mukolo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Akolo). *See* Rifukuefukue. One who is dirty in his habits. Opp. to Muhanda.
**Mukoma,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Koma). *See* Mulala. The departed spirit. Yudziguirua ni mukoma wani? Yuguirua ni mukoma wa dzaweye, wa avuye, wa mameye, etc. Yuguirua ni mukoma wa dzaweye wa waweye-wa kuche-wa ku lume. Sigombe hivio; unda-mu-unurira mikoma; *i.e.* Koma andakuenda-m-sirimia

*Footer: 279*

---

## [PDF Page 293 — Dictionary Page 280 (Muk — Muk)]

  kua mufundo wa babaye, Do not say so, else you will bring upon him the departed spirits; *i.e.* they will go and trouble him on account of the ill will of his father. This is said to a father whose son went travelling against his wish. *See* Radi. Ku piga mukoma wa dzi. Ku piga mukoma wa dzulu, ni ku kata makumpige. Ku dzula mukoma. Ku kuesa mukoma (= Ku buma vibaria).
**Mukombola,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Alula.
**Mukomu,** *adj.*, full. Muezi mukomu, Full moon.
**Mukondo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Ifuisa. A track, a narrow path. Atu adzichira hiva, adziavuka niazini, mikondo hino.
**Mukone,** *n.* *See* Mahumba. Lufuiho lua mukone.
**Mukongo,** *n.*, a sick person, sickness.
**Mukongo,** *adj.*, sick. Hangu avo lumua hata hivino guchare mukongo.
**Mukongosa,** *n.* (wa), the name of a creeping plant.
**Mukonkue,** *n.*, an aged or feeble person.
**Mukono,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Maririro. The arm, the hand. Gnania yuna mukono wa ku lavia-akikala na kitu, ka-ki-muumira. Gnania yuna mukono mui; nazihende akisimika luiga. Mutumche hiye yuna mukono mudzo; akiria kituche, kina waka, karia ku muagamuaga, yuna manirira to kilariroche, That woman has a good hand; when she uses anything it lasts long, she does not squander, she minds her store well. Mukono wa tundu, A hand with a hole,—said of a woman whose store of grain, etc., goes quickly. Mukono ukadzume, urehere kanoa. *See* Muansa. *Mukono* wa bahari, An arm of the sea. *See* Ludzidzi. Bahari ikareha mukono, ukakudza vatu vasiku.
**Mukosa,** *n.* (wa, pl. Akosa). *See* Kosania. Hiyu ni mukosawehu, hu-mu-rie-malu.
**Mukosi,** *n.* (pl. Akosi). *See* Lenga.
**Mukuadio,** *n.* (in Kig. = Mukuado). From Ku kuadia. Ndzao inadua mukuadio; but of sheep and goats they say, Ndenge, turume idzidua ache.
**Mukuafi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Akuafi). *See* Dzua.
**Mukuagna,** *n.*
**Mukuaho,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Mukuaju,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the tamarind tree.
**Mukuakua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree; its fruit is called makuakua. Kunise hata sikikala mbidzi, mi ku aka-ka-u-na madzi himuya muirini ukafuhuka.
**Mukuakua,** *adj.* (pl. Akuakua) (= Tatai in Kij., and Mtanta in Kins.), one who is passionate, violent, daring, easily inflamed, like the tree mukuakua. Mutu hiye ni mukuakua, ni mutu mubishi, musiru-ahendaye kondo muno. Muana ni mukuakua hiyu punde yudziheha na ayae punde yudziheha na ayae, kaogova utu.
**Mukuamba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Fukisa. The name of a small tree. Tundose ni puamba. (1) Mukuamba wegnie ni momu, ndio udemuao pfuiho sa ku vagarira niumba; pfuiho se sina madugudugu. (2) Mukuamba dzore ni muolofu, una vidugudugu, ela ka-u-hama.
**Mukuaruso,** *n.* (pl. Mi-), a scratch. Yuna makuaruso yudzi kuaruswa ni miya.
**Mukue,** *n.* *See* Agora.
**Mukuehu,** *n.* (pl. A-), lit. one of with us, one of the same place. Mutu hiyu ni mukuehu; pl. Atu hia ni akuehu.

*Footer: 280*

---

## [PDF Page 294 — Dictionary Page 281 (Muk — Muk)]

**Mukufu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a chain. Chains are made by the Wakamba of iron, copper, and brass, and form a principal ornament for young men. The Wasuahili, to some extent, imitate them, for petty trading.
**Mukuili,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Lulongo), a row. Vadzichira mukuili wa atu. Atu ario lulongo. Mikuili miiri, Two rows.
**Mukuinio,** or **Muknignio,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Ku piga mukuinio, To grumble (= Ku kuignia, or Kuinia).
**Mukuku,** *adj.* and *adv.* (N.B.—This is one of the few words which undergo no change, neither in singular and plural, nor with regard to the classes of nouns and adjectives.) *See* Songona. Close, dense. Muhama hiu u-mukuku, wanialua mungi, ndosa usihende masuche mabomu (= gagaga dzikiridzikiri). Mihi hio i-mukuku. Minazi hi yanialua mukuku. Niazi hiva zi mukuku. Niereze zi mukuku.
**Mukulu,** *adj.*, large, great. Muhi ni mukulu hiu (= mubomu). Mu atu akulu mui, be namba: n'enda kuano (for kua ano) baba, ngari hunapata wisua, hungakuenda hendira ahoho chakuria. Prov., Mudza m'kulu karia mameye (Kid.).
**Mukulu,** *n.*, an elder brother or sister. Mukulu wangu; pl. Akuluangu. Mukulu wehu, Our eldest brother or sister.
**Mukuluanire** (Kid.), *n.*, the eldest brother. Maneno gano kahunda-ga-gomba vadzovo mukuluanire vadzovo (= vasivo in Kir.).
**Mukulufundi,** *n.*, great teacher. This is a word coined and applied to a missionary.—[ED.]
**Mukuluhi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a mubalazi shrub left of the preceding year. Hunaria mbalazi za mukuluhi, wa muaka dzana. The beans of such a shrub are to be had earlier than those of a new shrub.
**Mukuluko** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (in Kir., Muiko wa ku chakana wari; Mtiko in Kins.), a rough wooden spoon used in cooking.
**Mukululo,** *n.* (wa), the force or rush of running water, the carrying off. From Ku kulula. Madzi gano gana mukululo, kaga lasa kala, The water runs out forcibly; it leaves no crabs,—said of a spring tide. Madzi ga mukululo, Water that is running with force, ready to take you along with it. Kadzuho kana riguvu hika, kana mukululo, kana shukushula.
**Mukumbu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a girdle. Na-dzi-funga mukumbu.
**Mukunazi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree.
**Mukunde,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the bean plant. Mukunde mbala, Streaked like the mbala, an animal. Mukunde wegnie, The common red bean of one colour.
**Mukundu,** *n.*, something red.
**Mukundua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kidisa. Copper. Mukodo wa mukundua (= masoka maekundu in Kij.), Copper wire. Dzango ra mukundua, Copper wire, somewhat bigger. Mudirima wa mukundua, An arm-ring of copper.
**Mukunga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), an eel.
**Mukungo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Mudzuri. A seam, border, brim. From Ku kunga. Mukungo wa nguo, The seam of a cloth. Mukungo wa luiga. Mukungo wa kavu. Madzi gadziidzala hata mukungoni, The water fills the vessel to the brim.
**Mukungu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree. Lukodza lua mukungu ndilo Abaniani aevuriralo wari.

*Footer: 281*

---

## [PDF Page 295 — Dictionary Page 282 (Muk — Mul)]

**Mukunguma,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree. It is also good for planting, but not so much as the mugandi. The fruit is called kunguma.
**Mukunso, Mukunzo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Fopala. A fold, a double, a crease, a wrinkle. From Ku kunsa. Mutu yudzinona yudzihenda mikunso mikunso. Dim., Kakunso and Kikunso.
**Mukuo.** *See* Kolosera. Mukuo ni wa ka kuira musigo.
**Mukurima,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Kadzunda; Funda; Dukana. A cultivator of the ground. This being the business of all Wanyika, the word is applied to one who excels therein by diligence; it is, however, little in use. From Ku rima.
**Mukusi** (Kid.), *n.* (= Muegnie lumfo), one who has received the lumfo.
**Mukuva,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree, the fruit of which is called kuva; used to make mortars. *See* Mudzani. Ndo mudundo huriao ndzalani, viz. tundoze.
**Mukuyu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree; the fruit is called kuyu (pl. Ma-). Ahoho akihenda mifui ya maonsa, akuenda sara masia ga mukuyu, varatu kidzoa cha onsa, lomba rikaguirana na onsa ndi ka ri dzonioka kahiri. Makodzage ni malamu. Ku piga mifui mukuyu, To apply the sap of the mukuyu to arrows, when fixing the lomba into the onsa.
**Mula, Mulaa,** *n.* (pl. Ala), the name of a dispersed tribe, remnants of which are found in various countries. They live exclusively by hunting; they are not murderous as the Gallas and Masai. In Kij. they are called Wamataka. Mawali ga Kisiwani ari kagu-*la Mula*, angue: ni kabilayao.
**Mulachu,** *adj.*, intelligent.
**Muladzo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), blood. Generally the pl. (Miladzo) is used.
**Mulagusi,** *n.* Rarely used. Gnania ni muganga yunaonai-ni mulagusi, ukilagurirua ni mutu hiye, be aki-ku-ambira utu, ni wa geri; muganga hiye ni mulagusi, yunaona.
**Mulala,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Mulala ukidza kula, niku ihua mukoma. Mikoma yosi-kuansa ni milala, ikikula, basi ukaiha mibie, hata ikichira mibie, ikifiala makoma, basi idzikala mikoma.
**Mulalamucheche.** Mulalamucheche ka-u-komia ku doka.
**Mulalapire, Mlalapiri,** *n.*, the name of a plant.
**Mulamba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Dzota. Mulamba ni mufiere wa niuni, ndiye asolaye mue na kosi, akifiala vevi na mudzi, basi kuku adzikala rahani; ni mudzangu wa ku uruka. Yunamania vilimo, or, vihari vio kucha kukikala kunacha, basi ni ku rira dza chogolo aihikavio.
**Mulambo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mugoba). *See* Muruchu; Milambo. A sort of basket.
**Mulamu,** *n.* (pl. Alamu), a brother- and sister-in-law, with the exception of a wife and the sister of her husband, who call each other wifi. *See* Wifi.
**Mulamuso.**
**Mulanga** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Lufuiho in Kir.), (1) a switch or thin stick. Mulanga wa ku dzungira gnombe.
(2) (= Langa).
**Mulangafu,** *adj.*, clever, sharp. Mutu hiyu ni mulangafu wa madzo muerefu, This man is sharp with his eyes.
**Mulangasa,** *n.* (wa). *See* Gnarira. Light. From Ku langasa.
**Mulangu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Guru.

## [PDF Page 296 — Dictionary Page 283 (Mul — Mul)]

**Mulave,** *adj.* Mutu hiye ni mulave, yunalavalava, wamba yula ndzalani; akiona kitu chakuria, iye ni ku sagala kuria tu, asieambua. Ana hia ni alave.
**Mulaviso,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a curse, an imprecation. From Ku lavisa.
**Mulawa** (Kidigo) (= Mulanga in Kid.).
**Mulelengua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Muleli,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the tail-feather. Mileli ya jogolo, Tail-feathers of a cock.
**Mulengi.**
**Mulili,** *n.* (wa, pl. Alili) (= Aakao kiru).
**Mulimau,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Muchunkua (Kij.). A lemon.
**Mulindi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the pencil-shell. The muganga, hiding one in his mouth, makes it appear as coming out of the wound of a person he has been sucking. People formerly would also drive one into an old decaying cocoa-nut tree for preserving it.
**Mulinga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Linga. Iron wire, made by the Wakamba. Formerly worn as an ornament by both Wakamba and Wanyika females, who almost covered their arms in winding it round them; whence the name. Dim., Kilinga.
**Mulo, Muulo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (in Kig., Muo). *See* Chulo. A pointed stick used for digging holes in the ground. By the Wakamba, in the interior, sticks are used for cultivating the ground. Der. from Ku, ua, Kij. and Kig. Something to undo, turn up the ground with. Reha mulo, nidzimbire gopue, nisimike nguso; or, hudzimbire masandzu. Magn., Dzulo; dim., Kadzulo and Kidzulo.
**Mulodo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the shin-bone. Gnania yuna milodo, —an expression for Magula mare.
**Mulolo** (Kid.), *adj.* (= Mborera in Kir.), soft, light. Said of the soil. Munda hiu ni mululo, or, muyuya.
**Mulombosi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Ngoi. Obs. Ni mutu alombolaye uira.
**Mulomo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Ansa; Kidosi. (1) Mouth, lip, beak, bill. Mulomo wa dzulu, The upper lip. Mulomo wa dzini, The under lip. Mulomo wa niuni, The bill of a bird. Mulomo wa mutu, The mouth of a man. Dim., Kalomo; magn., Domo, Lomo, and Romo.
(2) *See* Ivu; Kidubulu. An aperture.
**Mulongo,** *n.* (pl. A-). *See* Oloha; Amba. A liar.
**Mulongohi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a mast.
**Mulonsi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Bunsi in Kij.), the name of a species of insect. Dim., Kalonsi.
**Mulosi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mlusu in Kins.), a whistle. Yupiga mulosi yudzi-ni-iha na mulosi. Nidzi-ku-iha na mulosi, kukasikira, I have whistled to you, but you did not hear.
**Muluchiluchi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a parasitic plant, which bears the meto. Makodzage ga luchi muno; ga-nga ga mudadzi kua utite. Ukiduna makodzage, ni ku ererua ni moyo kua hali ya luchi.
**Mulumbi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Maruru; Lumbana; Ku lumba; Ndarira. One who is eloquent. Mulumbi ni mutu arie na hadzidzi ya maneno ga kare. Gnania ni mulumbi, akikola iye vova, ka-va-na neno ri-nda-ro banangika.
**Mulume,** *adj.*, male, masculine, manly, brave. Muana mulume, A male child, a son.
**Mulume,** *n.* *See* Yoboyowe. A man, a husband. Muluma-

*Footer: 283*

## [PDF Page 297 — Dictionary Page 284 (Mul — Mul)]

  ngu (for, Mulume wangu), My husband. Alumini (*see* Amiui), often used in addressing people without regard to sex.
**Mulundi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mulodo) (in Kij., Mvundi), the shin. The pl. is often used for Magulu mare, Long legs. Hai! yuna miluudi! Hai! long shanks!
**Mulungisi** (Kidigo), *n.* (wa) (= Mufuaha in Kir.). From Ku lunga. Mulungisiwe ni hiyu (= Mfuahawe ni hiyu).
**Mulungu, 1,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Dalalia; Dzoreka; Kukako. (1) Heaven. Kuratu ku-nga-ko dza ku amba: kuka sika sika mulungu, Yonder where, so to say, heaven ends. Baba wakuenda kuko kure, ku-ka-ko komakoma mulungu, ku-si-ko oneka; ndo baba a-ko-kuenda, Our father went yonder, far, where heaven ends, where he was not visible, there it was that father went.
(2) *See* Luani; Zani; Salama; Kosera; Umba; Wceeka; Niuni. The Supreme Power; the Deity; the Being believed to watch over and to govern the universe, without whose permission nothing happens; the smallest accidents being referred to the Mulungu. Kula uendavo Mulungu yuvo; be vira tu ukigomba, yuna-ku-sikira; hata ukaingira uinani, ku-dzi-fidza, Mulungu yuna-ku-ona. For a sick person: E Mulungu we! na muigni na-ku-amba. Mu-difie mutu hiyu ukongo hiu. Huna-ku-lomba uwe Mulungu, na-we hu lombere; ufugurire mutu hiyu, avole. Yuna Mulungu we, and Mulungu yudzi-m-rinda. When going to cultivate a new piece of ground: Uwe Mulungu! na-ku-lomba, nawe u-ni-lombere. Ninarima munda hiu, basi upate vitu; na mino m'egniewe nipate afia; be koma! Narima munda hiu; nafaka i-ole mundani, kua ku kala ningi; nikidzuma, nipate. Then he spits slightly on his hoe, aka-ri-dzuvira mahe, and says, Jembe na-ri-hege tove. When going on a journey: Ewe Mulungu dzulu! koma zi-dzi. N'enda charoni; basi uwe Mulungu u-ni-rinde; nik'enda dzuma, nipate, nirumirie; nidze kuehu muokolo. Basi akahasa. Ni ku dzumbula madzi, akafusira via-via, misigoye. Niama hiye nidzi-m-kosa vevi, Mulungu we yu-chari-m-rinda. Ela gnania kana Mulungu mudzo'ye? Hudzikuenda hosini kuenda insa, iye akadzola pembe ya ndzofu; Mulungu yudzi-mu-hensa, God still preserves the animal that I have just missed. But gnania, he not with God, good he? We have gone both to go hunting, he found (picked up) a tooth of an elephant. God he has loved him. Eh-Mulungu! ku-ni-pa we? nikienenda nika, nikakuenda dzola pembe njirani, nikauya, nikakudza gusa, nikapata mali. Mulungu yu-dzulu, koma zi dzi, God is above, the komas are on earth. The latter are supposed to be nearer to them, but still dependent on the Mulungu, wherefore in prayer they address him first and afterwards the komas. For rain: 'Ewe Mulungu we! huve mfula, hu-mashakani, hunasirima; nasui hu-anao; basi hu-ve ingu ra mvula, atu apate viakuria, hukifoya uwe Mulungu, u-Abeyehu. Kula unda vio amba, Mulungu yu-na-ku-sikira, yudzi-ku-lagisa iye(?). Muana yunalagisua ni Mulungu ku nena yunafundua ni Mulungu muegnie ku go-

*Footer: 284*

## [PDF Page 298 — Dictionary Page 285 (Mul — Mum)]

  mba. Ukihenda vi, Mulungu yuna-ku-ona, yunda-ku-riva vi vivio, viratu uka vio henda muyao. Uki-mu-ulaga mutu, unamania ni vi, hata ukakimbira, undaduiwa hata uulague na-we; kuani-'da ukadzi-fidza, Mulungu yuna-ku-ona, yunda-ku-ika luasu, uoneke. These ideas may have been derived from their intercourse with the Mohammedans.
  (3) *See* Madungo; Makafiri. An evil spirit supposed to cause sickness; also called Mbingu, pl. Milungu. Yudziguirua ni Mulungu, ku-mu-ona a-fuina fio? Yudziingirua ni Mulungu wa Kisambala. Yudziingirua ni Mulungu wa Kibondeni. Yudziingirua ni Mulungu wa Kimbugu. Yudziingirua ni Mulungu wa Kikuafi. This impious use of the word is only of recent date, and is said to have originated with the Wadigo and Wadusuma. Abe Gunja said, Ni Shetani ndiye a-dzi-galusaye hivio.
**Mulungu, 2,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree.
**Mulungusi,** *n.*
**Muma** (Kig.) (= Kiravo and Dzoga in Kir.). *See* Kimavio.
**Mumafi,** *n.* (= Mufo).
**Mumaitha,** or **Mumeitha** (Kij.), *n.* (pl. A-), a robber. Amaitha ni atu ualagao atu, dza Agala, Akuafi. *See* Ladzurika.
**Mumande,** *n.* *See* Umande. The morning wind, land breeze.
**Mumathaka.** *See* Mula.
**Mumbi** (= Guro). Rero kudzihenda mumbi.
**Mumbu** (for **Muumbu**), *n.* (wa, pl. Miumbu). *See* Mufure. The name of a tree. Mumbu ni ku henda tongo ukarira ukalafia vithana, basi hiko ndani vithanavie vikakala dza hura uongolo, ukabundua ufumba, atu akasora nguo, angene akabuma mafuhani, aka-dzi-sora.
**Mumemue,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a creeper, pieces of which, when kept in the house, are said to have the efficacy of turning anger into laughter! *See* Kimemue. Mumemue u-nga dza lubugu, makodzage ni malamu; kua ndze ni kuiru, kua ndani ni ku dune.
**Mumenga,** *adj.*, one.
**Mumera,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a sprout, a shoot. Mumera wa muaka wa rero ukamera to, mvula yagnia bomu. Kuenu mudzi meza? Resp., Ah hudzi meza, mumera u-dele mundani, ukamera to. Mimera ya minda hi ikamera to.
**Mumeto.** *See* Muluchiluchi, which is the more common name for the creeping plant which produces the meto.
**Mumfano,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mimfano). *See* Cho; Mfano. Shape, form, characteristic. Kula gnombe za Mukamba ana mumfanowao, Every cow of the Ukamba has its characteristic. Kula muhi una mumfanowe kua higara makodza. Mimfano ya mihi ni mingi.
**Mumfera,** *n.* (wa). *See* Muvera; Shukuru. Gratitude, a sense of obligation, gratification. From the Kins. Ku mfera. Gnania yudzi-ni-hendera mumfera, yudzi-ni-pa uchi, yudzi-ni-ulagira kuku, na wari udzihenda na muvunga yudzi-ni-hendera mumfera ubomu, kua utu hura na-o-mu-hendera. Mutu hiye wa-ni-hendera utu udzo, niki-m-hendera mumfira hata rero. Gnania yudzi-ni-pa kitu cha bule, ninaye mumfera ndani muangu. Nidzeria kitu hata nidziukuha, nidzi-ki-onera mumfera. Hudzeria kitu, hudziukuha, huna mumfera naye. Ndo mumferao hiu, kudza-ni-buma gogo! *said* Abe Gunja to his uncle,

## [PDF Page 299 — Dictionary Page 286 (Mum — Mun)]

  who put his feet in the stocks when he had become insane. The uncle had taken much property from his father, when Abe Gunja was left an orphan. Mutu hiye ni mui, kahewa kitu kari kana mumfera; uki-mu-va kitu-mutu hiye-basi udzidzuva dzakani.
**Mumfindi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mimfindi) (= Mumvindi), the backbone. Used of sharks only. Mumfindi wa kolekole. Mumfindi wa papa. Dim., Kamfindi (Kamvindi).
**Mumfiria,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mimfiria). *See* Tumbulio. The gate of a kaya. Mumfiria ni wa makaya ga Anika.
**Mumfuno,** *n.* (wa). Muaka wa rero una mumfuno (= Nioha, viakuria vi-dele). Kakuna mumfuno wa keri; atu apata vitu habahaba, or, vichache vichache.
**Mumidzi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Amidzi). *See* Gofia; Kula. A settler. Atu hio ni amidzi, ahenda kudza. Si Murvavai halisi, ni mumidzi.
**Mumiro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kuama. Atu hio mimiroyao ni mimenga; akiimba, ukaamba: ni huya muyawe kua hira linkua kuenda karakara.
**Mumo,** *adv.* *See* Guika; Larira; Madaro; Divira; Dzulo; Dzahasi; Chunga, 2. In, within. Udzi-ki-buma-vi? Resp., Nidzi-ki-buma mumo, mukobani, or, kavuni. Jembe ki-mumo. Nidzikuenda dzaira mumo luguani. Nidzikuenda kaya chiramuko, nidzisinda mumo di. Mumo kua mumo.
**Mumondo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Amondo). Mumondo ni mutu asiedza-nkue ku thura; kasagala kihini wala lukansani; yusa-galadzi, mudzangani wegnie. Amondo ni arisa a magovu. Mumondo nkua, wa gnania.
**Mumunia,** or **Mumugnia,** *v.a.*
  **Mumunika,** *v.n.* Niungu inamumunika, ni mbidzi. Muniu udzimumunika (= udziyaya). Nidzibuma muniu hikara, ka-u-dza mumunika. Kitu hiki kidziola kidzimumunika bugubugu.
**Mumvindi.**
**Muna,** *pron.*, 2nd pers. pl., (1) you with = you have.
(2) *See* Kigniesi; Ku lukansa. In with.
**Muna,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mina) (= Munani minani). *See* Kina.
**Muna,** *n.* (wa). Nidzigutua ni muhi pulani, hata nidzila muna. Kuna muna wa ku-dzi-laira tu, ela kukagutua.
**Munada** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), auction, of slaves only? Yudzibumua munadani; or, Yudzinadua.
**Munafu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a vegetable.
**Munago,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Munanasi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the pine-apple plant.
**Munandi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). Munandi ni mutu arie niuma ya dzumbe muviriwe. Kimeri yuna munandiwe, ndiye Mbereko.
**Munazi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the cocoa-nut tree. Munazi hiu ni wa kas'kasi ela si wa muaka; *i.e.* it yields toddy in the dry season only. The natives say one tree will now yield three vibaba per day, about three pints, while formerly one yielded twice as much, or at least four pints. Munazi wangu unadzeresa musala dele, and another, kasi dele.
**Munda,** *n.* (wa, pl. Minda), a plantation, any piece of ground under cultivation. Dim., Kadzunda; magn., Dzunda, pl. Midzunda.
**Munda, Munta,** (1) 2nd pers. pl. of the fut. tense, you will.
(2) (rel. to Mumo). *See* Gundisa. In there will.
**Mundu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miundu), a

## [PDF Page 300 — Dictionary Page 287 (Mun — Mun)]

  hook or hatchet. Mundu ni wa ku demera mbugu sa vidzaka. Aravai a mbere ari na miundu sana, ela hikara ana vidzoka tu.
**Mtnemo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Farasi.
**Munena** (Kidigo) (= Kinena in Kir.). Ku guira munena (= Ku kuachisa in Kir.).
**Munene** (Kij. and Kig.), *adj.* (in Kir. proper = Mubomu and Musiho), big, bulky, large, great.
**Muneno,** *n.* (wa), edge, brink. Wa-ki-ika munenoni; ku mania kindabua? You put it on the edge; do you not know it will fall down?
**Munga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Minga). *See* Kithana; Munga, pl. Miunga. Munga unala madzosi una tongo.
**Mungasija,** *n.* (= Mugasija).
**Mungero,** *n.*
**Mungi,** *adj.* *See* Oheka. Much.
**Mungina,** or **Mungine,** *adj.* (pl. Angine). Other.
**Mungo, Muungo,** *n.* (wa), the name of a creeping plant lubugu. Its fruit is called maungo.
**Mungu** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Golosera. God.
**Mungu,** *n. coll.* (wa and a, pl. Miungu). *See* Chaje. Rarely used. Mungu anavula muhama; or, Mungu a vulaye muhama na kirenge. Mungu udziingira muhamani, and also Muhama udziingira mungu. Muhama udziingirua ni mungu lola hio miungu idzayo vetua. Kirenge kidzihumbulua ni mungu.
**Munguana** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. A'nguana), a free man. Gnania ni munguana, dzana wa-ni-laga kuamba: machero ndzo, udze, uhale kitu kisiku, n'endaa ka-ni-pa. Yudzi-ni-pa kitu, nidzeria; mutu hiye ni munguana sana, simania kitu nindacho-mu-va, naye ahende mumfera.
**Mungudi, Munguji,** *n.* (wa, pl. Angudi, Anguji). Munguji ni bora ra kiche ra muansa; akavima muansa ku kuesa mikono.
**Mungufu,** *n.* and *adj.* (pl. Angufa). Gnania ni mungufu, ela si shaha; huya akayepita ayae mali-wambua ni shaha. Sira sa ku midzniana na atu, be hunaamba: gnania yuna ngufu. Mihi mingufu.
**Munguji.** *See* Mungudi.
**Mungumi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mingumi) (= Mgumi in Kij.), the whale.
**Munia,** *v.n.*
  **Munika** (= Bugudika).
**Muniahu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a small bundle of wood, somewhat larger than the kidzopa. Muniahu wa kuni.
**Muniakalele.**
**Muniala,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a small tree. Unakuta makodza dza, muburudia. Mutu akiona muniala udzibusa makodza, akamania, muaka udzibua.
**Muniale,** *adj.*, forgetful. Only used in connection with Moyo. Moyowangu ni muniale-sikomia ku niala vivi. Gnania yuna moya muniale.
**Munialu.** *See* Lunialu.
**Muniambo** (Kig.), *n.*, a lion. The word is only used in superstitious dread, while the proper word both in Kig. and Kir. is Dzimba. Atu aenendao nika, kahadza dzimba, aamba muniambo, ankue: akihadza dzimba, basi andaonana naye.
**Muniau** (Kidigo), *n.* (pl. Mi-) (= Paka), a rat.
**Muniefu,** *n.* *See* Mugniefu.
**Muniewe.** *See* Muegniewe; Lomberua.
**Muniolo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Kuna miniolo ikalayo dzi midzangani. Kuna miniolo mingine ikakala ndani mua mutu.
**Munionge,** *n.* (pl. A-), one who is weak, infirm in body.

**Munionge,** *adj.*, poor, miserable.
**Muniore,** or **Mugniore,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kidza. (1) Muniore wa maere.
(2) A small bundle. Nidzipiga muniore niasi sari chache, sikatimisa kiniasi, I have formed a small bundle or wisp; there was so little grass, I did not complete a load. Nidzifunga muniore wa milala, ka-i-kadimira musigo.
**Muniosi,** *n.*, a shaver, of the head only. From Niola.
**Muniu,** *n.* (wa), salt.
**Muniulufu,** *adj.*, tough. From Ka niuluka. Muhi hiu si muifu, ni muniulufu, uchari muidzimuidzi.
**Muno,** *prep.* *See* Mumo. In, within. Ukabuma-ni muno? (= Ukabuma-ni mo?).
**Muno,** *adv.* (= Sana), much, greatly.
**Munoadzi,** *n.* *See* Manoadzi. A moderate drinker. Munoadzi wa uchi (= Muhensi wa uchi). Gnania ni munoadzi, ela unoadziwe kana urefi. Gnania ni munoadzi, ela kakomia ku rea, kaidima uchi.
**Munofu,** *n.* (wa), meat without bone. Niama ya munofu, isio musosa wala kanokano. Munofu muvuvu hiu. Dim., Kanofu; Kinofu.

**Munsa** (= Ni kana ufumfu). Muana yudziguirua ni munsa.
**Munsaka** (Kidigo) (= Muthaka in Kir.).
**Muodia,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a quiver made of bamboo (not now used, being superseded by the muriaka, made of leather).
**Muofu,** or **Muovu.**
**Muoga,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), lit. a fearer, one who is afraid.
**Muokolo,** *adj.* *See* Mulungu.
**Muokosi,** *n.*, a deliverer, saviour.
**Muolofu,** *adj.* *See* Nemuka, Soft, flexible. Mutu hiye yuna moyo muolofu.
  **Muoloho.**
**Muomu,** *adj.*, (K.) severe.
**Muona,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Muondo,** *n. coll.* (wa), the name of a grass. It is called muondo when young and small, but when full-grown and large, ondo. It may be used for thatching, but as it soon decays it is only taken in an emergency; whence the saying, Yudzifimba na muondo dza gungu, He has thatched his hut with muondo, as a widow. Muondo ka-u-komia ku ola.
**Muongo.**
**Muongolo,** *n.* *See* M'ongolo.
**Muono** (Kid.), *n.* (pl. Miono) (= Kij., Msono), (1) snoring. In Kir. the pl. only (Miomo) is used for snoring.
(2) (Kir.) (= Mubono).
**Mura,** *adv.* *See* Yegnie; Msingi; Anamira; Durura. In there.
**Murandu,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a debtor. The word is becoming obsolete, being superseded by Mudeni. It is derived from Ku randa (in Kns.), Ku landa (in Kig.). Nin'enda kua murandu wangu, nika-mu-ise.
**Muranga,** *n.* (Kij., Mtada?), a tree, the wood of which is used for torches.
**Muranse,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Muthanse).
**Muranse** (= Kiremge).
**Muranzi, Muranzi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Mufungu. (1) The bough of a bamboo. Kiko cha muransi. Dzu muranzi. Mianza ya buhazi (= Kiravo cha bahazi).
(2) A telescope.
**Murao,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a lunt, or match. Adzomba anachira bundukuisao sinafuka murao.
**Murao,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Lubugu). Murao ni muhi wa tosa. Nalonda murao nibume tosani.
**Mura-tu,** *adv.* *See* Kikonde. In there only.
**Murauko,** *n.* *See* Dzua. Dzua rifika murauko wa gno-
