## [PDF Page 302 — Dictionary Page 289 (Mur — Mur)]

  mbe. Yukudza chiramuko, dzua rari murauko wa gnombe.
**Muravai,** *n.* (pl. Aravai), the name given to a native of the Rabai or Ravai tribe.
**Mur'dudu,** or **Murututu,** *n.* (wa), blue vitriol.
**Mure,** *adj.*, long, tall.
**Murefi, Murevi,** *n.* (pl. A-), a drunkard.
**Murego,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Muthego).
**Murembe,** *n.* Mufui wa murembe; pl. Mifui ya mirembe.
**Murenge,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Fua. (1) The pumpkin plant; its fruit is called marenge.
(2) (= Guro), thin vapour, a slight mist in the morning; the state of being hazy or cloudy at day-time. Rero kuna murenge, kunadzuva-dzuva mahe dza kunche. Rero kuna murenge, ka-ku-na dzua. Rero ku mosimosi, kuna murenge.
**Murere,** *n.* (wa). Ushanga wa murere, A long string of beads.
**Murerenkua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a thorn tree. Miyaye inga dza kilo, be ni mifuhi-ela vikakobieka dza kilo. Fuiho sa murerenkua.
**Muresi,** *n.* (pl. A-). *See* Rera. Mtumche hiye ni muresi-hata ana a nduguye ni ku rera 'ye. Yuna moyo mudzo. Mtumche hiye si muresi, ni mui korokoro; yurera muanawe, ela karera muana wa mutu.
**Muriadzi.**
**Muriaka,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Muthiaka).
**Muriakulo,** *n.*, the name of a grass which the kulo eats.
**Muriamuno,** *n.*, the name of a play, formerly practised by children.
**Muriango,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) a door. Dim., Kiriango; magn., Riango.
(2) Family. Muriango wa Chindua.
**Muriapania,** *n.*, the name of a grass.
**Muriap'embe,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree; (K.) voracious.
**Muridza,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Murihi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree. Its bark (urihi) is used for binding in building, and for ropes of traps. *See* Ugosa.
**Murima,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kibumbuana; Kirima. (1) A mountain; (K.) mainland. Dim., Karima; Kirima.
(2) Ana hiri ridzipigua musasa, ridzidzuka, ridziusua mirima.
**Murindiro,** *n.* (wa), a rite, ceremony. Rero ni murindiro wa juma, or, wa muezi, To-day is the ceremony of the great day, of the moon. Kare-mirindiro yere mingi, Formerly ceremonial observances were many.
**Murinsi,** *n.* (pl. A-).
**Murio,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a creeping plant, with a root called kimboyo, similar to the sweet potato. This is one of the few instances in Kinyika of a plant having a different name from its production. Murio ndo uvialao kimboyo, The murio it is which bears the kimboyo.
**Murira,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a line; the trace left by drawing anything along the ground. Ku piga mirira, To make lines in the sand in counting anything.
**Muriro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Muniandege; in Kij., Guchere). *See* Kosi; Uriro. The name of a tree. Tundose ni ndiro. Muriro na musikaha ndio i-valasua yo lukue lua ku hungira ushanga.
**Murisa,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a shepherd, a herdman.
**Murisi,** *n.* (pl. A-). Gnania ni murisi yunarira to, akirira yunaguisa mbasi. Mutu akifua akikala kana mbari ningi, be ndo aambu-

*Footer: NIKA. | U | 289*

## [PDF Page 303 — Dictionary Page 290 (Mur — Mus)]

  avo; kana murisi, hebu: kana arisi.
**Muroana,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). Mutu hiye unga-mu-ona na kofiasi, na kansuse, na panga se na najambiage-sambe ni mudzomba kifialo, ni muroana, wakanda silimu. Viha vidzebua via aroana, ka vi-nda sira haraka; hata vindavasira ni kare. Viha via aroana. Duruma and Ravai, etc.
**Murobo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a creeping plant, used in binding the vanda, and also in building.
**Muroi,** *n.*
**Muronda,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a small tree. Makodzage ni ku badika vironda, ndosa uihue muronda.
**Murongo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kisikane. A decade. Kana mirongo ya ku timisa (= Kana akili).
**Murua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Urini). *See* Dzofia; Kirua. The name of a small tree, the blossoms of which, being very fragrant, were formerly mixed with the ricinus oil, with which the Wanyika anointed themselves. With the increase of cattle it came into disuse, butter being much preferred to it, as being so much cleaner. Murua ndo udemuao miroi, atu akioka madzi ku piga sayo.
**Muruche,** *n.* (wa), the smell of roast meat. Ni harufu ya niama ikiochua. Nasikira muruche-una-nuka, kunaachua kuku hiko. Mtumche hiye yunanuka muruche mudzo (= yunanuka ufumba). Mudzichita vitu, ela vinalafia muruche, ka vi-nda ifua. Such is the case with Mgasija-masumaidzi; Marenge; Mababayu; and Miyokue.
**Murudu,** or **Muruji** (Kid. and Kidigo), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). Mkuba mbomu (= Hundu in Kir.; Chungu).
**Murugudira,** *n.* (wa) (= Mufugudira), heat. Niumba hi ina murugudira (= tugumira in Kins.). Niumbani muna murugudira.
**Murungu,** *n.* (= Muthungu), a tree.
**Murungudira,** *n.* (pl. *id.*).
**Muruo,** *n.* (wa). From Ku rua.
**Mururuku** (Kig.), *n.* (Mdakombe in Kij.; and Mkunguni), a tree.
**Musa,** *n.* (wa, pl. Misa). *See* Roda. A meteor. Musa ukila ulairo wa dzua, uk'enda udzerero wa dzua, basi udzikuenda dzuva makongo na mai gosi bia ya dzi; ela ukila udzerero wa dzua, be uk'enda ulairo wa dzua, basi ankue; w'enda hala makongo. Ukidikania urumengu, uk'enda kanda ya kibula, na-vio ankue; ni vidzo; ela ukila kibula, uk'endamuakani, basi kundakudza utu. Ukavo kuenda kisiku kisima cha urumengu hata ukasimira, basi ukabua baharini, ku-ka-ko sikasika mulungu.
**Musabidi** (Kij.), *adj.* Yuna moyo musabidi-wa ku fumurira (= Mufumurisi in Kir.).
**Musadiki** (= Musabidi).
**Musafii** (Kij.), properly **Msafihi,** *n.*, a proud person. Ela gnania si msafii iye! utu hio adzaohenda, be ni utu wa ku hendua o? (Kid.).
**Musafiri** (Kij.), *n.* (= Muhamfi in Kir.), a sailor, a traveller.
**Musafula,** *n.* (wa). *See* Dulua. (1) Kimvo cha musafula. *See* Safura; Dzafulo. Yudziguirua ni kiravo cha musafula. Gnania ni mukongo, yudziguirua ni musafula, si ukongo wa Mulungu. Mualamusi ni musafula. *See* Molande.
(2) (pl. Asafula).
**Musagasi,** *n.* (pl. A-). Ela gnania ni musagasi. hebu yundaenenda kahiri? Muche

## [PDF Page 304 — Dictionary Page 291 (Mus — Mus)]

  ulolaye, ela ni musagasi hebu ni ku dzi lorera tu-yundaenenda? Resp., Ah-ni musagasi akisagala, yundasagala, na akienenda, nindalola mungina; ela muche hiye nidzi-m-hensa na mayo wangu, sindaricha ku-m-lola.
**Musaha** (Kij.), *n.* (wa) (= Ndumo). Neno hiri ridziingira sana.
**Musala,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kasi. The name of a calabash of a particular size, a measure. Munaziwangu unadzeresa musala dele.
**Musalaba,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (K.) a cross. Musalaba ni makumbi ga mulala gafunguago vamenga-mutu akafumira hako ra kavu; misalaba ikagandamisa hira hako, kuamba risibana ngike rigoloke.
**Musambakuji,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of acacia. Miyaye ni mire.
**Musambaraho, Muzambaraho,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree; the timber resembles elm.
**Musana,** *n.* (pl. A-), a blacksmith. Musana hiye ni salamala sana, wa ku piga majembe tu.
**Musangu,** *n.* *See* Vima.
**Musasa,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree. Makodzaga musasa gana miya-ganachegnia; ganadzusa mifui. Ni rehera musasa, nidzusire, or, nisasire maanogangu. Gnania ni muhanda mifuiye ni midzo aka-i-piga musasa, inagnala. Dzana nareherua mifui, kuamba ni-m-pigire musasa.
**Musave,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Ugoza. The name of a tree. Its bark, when used for binding, is called usave.
**Muse** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. Wase, or Ase in Kir.).
**Musede,** or **Museje,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the staff of a charmer or native doctor, decorated with rings and beads. To become a member the novice must give a feast to his new colleagues. Formerly the word also meant the staff of an old person, which is now called m'dada. Museje ni wa muganga.
**Musego,** *n.* (= Segasega). Ku dzagamira ku fuina musego.
**Musekeneko.** Kiravo cha musekeneko. Yudziguirua ni kiravo cha musekeneko; yudzihenda vironda via mago.
**Musena,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a friend, a companion. Musenangu, for Musenawangu, My friend.
**Musense** (Kig.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mukoma mubie in Kir.; Kidigo, Kugemamusense).
**Muserembue,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Muchewa; in Kns., Manankuea). Muserembue wa dzere; pl. Miserembue ya madzere.
**Musesero,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a line drawn on the ground with the foot, for cutting a small ditch, into which the sticks of a new hut are to be fixed.
**Mushaha,** *n.*
**Mushishui,** *n.*, the name of a tree.
**Mushombo** (Kidigo), *n.* (wa) (= Kishombo and Mushubu in Kir.).
**Mushubu,** *n.* (wa) (= Kishombo; Musunie). From Ku suena? or soena?
**Mushururu,** *nom. adj.* (pl. Ashururu), one who is tardy. Mutu hiye ni mushururu, kandakudza haraka.
**Musi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Misi). *See* Muthungu. A root.
**Musiba, Musipa,** *n.* (wa). *See* Lugano. Musiba wa mulodzo, Blood-vessel.
**Musibi, Mushipi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) a fishing-line. Mushipi wa ku fuira sui, ni lugue lua ukonche.
(2) The name of a creeping plant, the root of which has a fibrous bark used for making string. Dende sa musibi ndani mune luho.

## [PDF Page 305 — Dictionary Page 292 (Mus — Mus)]

**Musibidi,** *adj.*, (1) (= Musabidi). Yuna moyo musibidi; kana moyo muharara, wa ku dzoa haya.
(2) Ni musibidi moyo mutu hiye.
**Musichana,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a girl, a young woman; corresponding to Mudana in males.
**Musidadi,** *adj.* (Kij., Mustati), clever, expert. Gnania ni musitati sana wa ku okerera.
**Musifu** (Kij.). Muhi hiu ni musifu; pl. Mihi hio ni misifu, ni miomu; ndo mihi ya ku akira niumba.
**Musigo,** or **Muzigo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a load, a burden.
**Musiho,** or **Muziho,** *adj.* *See* Muvudzu. Heavy, thick.
**Musihu** (Kid.), *n.* (wa) (= Kins., Msidu; Dzaka in Kir.), a forest.
**Musika,** *n.* (no pl., and only used as predicate), something unfinished, an unfinished state. From Ku sika. Wari hiu nidzi-u-richa musika-sika-u-mala. Nidzifuma kavu, ela sika-i-mala, nidzi-i-richa musika. Neno hiri-'dzi-ri-richa musika, sika-ri-mala. Yudzigomba, ela yudzi-ri-richa musika. *See* Gundisa; Maneno. Nidzirima, sikasisa, nidziricha musika. Hudzirima, ela kahuka udulukisa, hudziricha musika. Ngue zao adzi si richa musika, kaka sisa.
**Musikaha,** *n.* (wa). *See* Muriro.
**Musikihira,** *n.* (wa), the hair which grows round about the tengere. The tuft of hair left when the other part of the head is shaved. From Ku sikiha.
**Musikisi,** *adj.* Prov., Muana musikisi yuria chakue na cha mayawe. Akahewa kira kitu a-dza-choihirua.
**Musiku,** *adj.* *See* Laira. Pertaining to some one. Gnania musiku. Mutu musiku, A *certain* man or woman.
**Musima, Muzima,** *adj.* Nidzilaula munda, ela si muzima, mgasija ukagnolua, na mababayu gakahundua, na isu rikademua.
**Musimbiki,** *n.*, the name formerly given to the blue cloth now called kaniki. Probably it was first imported to this coast from Mozambique, of which Musimbiki is a different pronunciation. Nguo ya musimbiki.
**Musimu, Muzimu,** *adj.* *See* Diba. Ku-m-sirimia vino nini; or, Kusa-m-riva kituche nini, na-ye ni muchia musimu? Mimi ni muchia muzimu, hata kudza ku-ni-voka kitu changu nini?
**Musimu,** *n.* Musimu wa pembe. Muduruma-akiguira pembe, basi ni msimuwe, kula alondacho ni ku ki-pata.
**Musinde,** *adj.* Gnania yuna moyo musinde, wa ku fumurira (opp. to, moyo mbaba).
**Musindo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Mshindo in Kij.), a loud and sudden noise. Ku piga musindo, To make a loud and sudden noise. Musindo ni wa muche akivonda. Musindo ni wa mutu akichira vatu va riravo dindindi. Musindo ni wa musinga na wa bundukui, The report of a cannon or of a gun. Bundukui rinaayuka. Nasikira misindo-mutu yunadira.
**Musinga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kombora. A cannon. Ku piga misinga.
**Musingi** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= in Kir., Kanga wa madzini), the name of a bird.
**Musingo, Muzingo,** *n.* (wa) (= Muruche), the smell of meat. Said to be obsolete; but in Kid. it means the same as Muombe in Kins.
**Musinsi,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), something rubbed off. From Ku

## [PDF Page 306 — Dictionary Page 293 (Mus — Mus)]

  singa. Na piga musinsi, madzi gasiingire niumbani.
**Musinsi, Muzinzi,** *n.* (pl. A-). *See* Mudomba. From Ku zinga.
**Musira,** *n.* *See* Ku ona; Sira (Kid.). A mystery, secret.
**Musiro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Mue. Anything avoided or abstained from. Kana niama asirayo, kula niama yosi yunaria-ni kidzungu, kakina musiro. U-kidzungu, kuna musiro we-udzee ame sa atu, kidza udzee ana be u-kidzungu we, kuna musiro kana musiro (= lipondeponde in Kins.).
**Musiru,** *adj.* *See* Lungudza.
**Musiruaufua,** *n.* (pl. A-), an heir; lit. one to whom has been left something by death. From Ku siira and Ufua. Mutu musiruaufua (= Ndiye ayesiruaufua).
**Musisi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). Gnania ni musisi sana, akiupuka iye, mutu ni ku sikua to. Gnania na gnania ni asisi-akidza vatu vasikua vo mutu, karicha ku zika o. Ndio aerekezao ku ahula mudzi to, wa mbira; wala kana ukaha wa ku dzimba mbira.
**Musisima,** *n.*
**Musiso, Muzizo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-) (= Siso? wa mkue? Sifo?). *See* Kochesa. Vatu hiva vana musiso; ka-va-vondua na usiku. Muganga wakudza lagula mudzi, basi akisikiha, akigomba misiso, akiamba. Vasiupuke moho na usiku; vasiupuke madzi, na usiku; vasifunsue lukuni na usiku; vasidzangue lukuni na usiku; vasivondue na usiku; basi akisisa misiso hio, be dzusi mutu akikochesa musiso, ndo niama kudza guira mpusi.
**Muso,** *n.* *See* Mufaranga.
**Muso,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miso) (= Mahunda). Muche huya kaloreka, yuna mali ningi; yudzilolua na miso mihandahu.
**Musoa.** Wari rero ni musua, ka-u-megeka.
**Musora.** Nguo ya musora muiru.
**Musosa,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a bone.
**Musuaki,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a small fibrous tree, sticks of which are used by the Wasuahili as tooth-brushes by first chewing the ends into shreds and then rubbing the teeth. The Wanyika only use the roots of it, the inner bark of which they scrape into their toddy and drink it for a cough.
**Musuhu** (Kid.), *n.* (wa, pl. ) (= Dzaka in Kir.), a forest.
**Musuka,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Musuka, Muzuka,** *n.*
**Musumari** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a nail.
**Musunduladzansu,** *n.* (= Muahuladzansu).
**Musunga, Muzunga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the foreskin.
**Musungu, Muzungu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Shakashaka. (1) A thought, an idea, a purpose. Ana muzunguwao ndani. Muzungu wa ndani; pl. Mizungu ya ndani. Muzungu hio na-u-kome: Ku hala kitu nidzacho muikira babayo, uka-ki-hala, uka-ki-ria. Nere nikiasa heche yangumu-zungu moyoni muangu hata nikapata neno siku; be nikaamba: na-ri-henda riro, ri-ni-fae, ama risi-ni-fae; be nidzi-ri-henda, riki-ni-fa; hata hangu dzana ndo kitu niduacho.
(2) (= Mirongo). Kana misungu, or, mciongo mutu hiye; yuna mania kuria tu, hata akikala yu vuvu, kadzi mania, or, kadzi dara yunamania ndaniye tu kuukuha. Kana mizungu ya ku amba: Hivi ni vuvu nadzagula kidemu-ni ku danga danga tu.

## [PDF Page 307 — Dictionary Page 294 (Mus — Mut)]

**Musunie,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a slave.
**Musunsua,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Mususi,** *n.* (pl. A-), a platter. Ni mutu asukaye kavu hebu pinda. Hikara kavana mususi kuehu akayela kidzoa (= akayela nguma).
**Mususi,** *n.* (pl. A-). Muganga hiye ni mususi, yunasusa ku gnola viombo vika vio sikua.
**Mususu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the tail, of birds only.
**Mususu, Muzuzu,** *adj.*, silly, stupid.
**Mususu, Muzuzu,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), a fool.
**Muta,** (1) *v.a.* *See* Dzoniorera; Henda; Hege; Nguso; Kita. To fix, to hold up. Ku muta kivesa. Ku muta viguso via ludzaga. Ku muta luiga (= Ku simika). To fix a basin into the ground. Ku muta chense, To hold up a wisp over a fire, to catch. Muta lumuiri, u-ni-muirikire.
(2) *v.n.*, to stand still, to stop. Nidzidzimbira nguso, nidzimuta. Ku muta gonga, To rest the head on the elbows. Ku muta mafuindi, To kneel. U-asa ni we-udza ye muta gonga, or, udzie muta gonga? What are you thinking of, resting your head on your elbows? Resp., Ah-ni mambo ga mashuku ga urumengu. Naenenda, nikamute hivo poani, be niuye. N'enda nikakome hivo kua gnania, ni mute vavo, niuye, sindachira kuenda mbere.
  **Mutamuta** (often pronounced without the *u*, Ku m'tam'ta), *v. reit.*, (1) (Kir.), to stop repeatedly, only used of one wandering about. Kula vatu pia umutemute ukauye, hata ukote dzi yosi-ela kudangadanga muno we! go magulugo ganawawa ukisagala vamenga hebudze? Naona mutu ak'enda muta vatu vasiku, akauya, akakuenda muta vatu vangine, akauya; kula vatu yudzi mutamuta, yulonda-ni, yuyeya-ni?
  (2) (Kid.) (= Chuchumia in Kij., and Sintama in Kins.), to halt, to limp.
  **Mutikisa, Mutikiza,** *v.a.* (= Ku chisa). Muganganga hiu ni mufuhi-ela ni mudzo, na-u-mutikisa, sinda-u-richa.
  **Mutikisua,** *v.p.* Muhi hiu ukamutikisua.
  **Mutira,** *v.d.* Huari huki-mu-mutira gnania kivesa.
  **Mutua,** *v.p.*, to be fixed. Kivesa hiki kidzimutua to.
**Mutembe,** *adj.* and *n.* (pl. Atembe, when of persons, in some cases also of animals; Mitembe when of things) (= Muchache). *See* Mudembe. Small, a little. Muhamu mutembe, A little sorghum (Guinea-corn). Muhama wangu ni mutembe, My Guinea-corn is little. Mugasijawehu ni mutembe.
**Mutembue,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the top leaf of the mulala and of the mugumo (= luensa in a cocoa-nut tree). Mutembue wa mulala ni dza isio dzankue ku bambahuka. Mutembue wa mugumo ndo Aravai ahendao mufuri.
**Mutha,** *n.* (wa) (= Mta in Kij.), a district or part of a town, a township. A-veni Anika mutha. *See* Kidzidzi. Adzomba akidikisa gnombe enaulagua, basi ndo afiosao, akimala, akahewa mutha. Aravai akikala anaria lusinga, be Adzomba akichira na vavo basi ni ku hewa mutha we wari.
**Muthaka,** *n.* Gnania wari muthaka, ela vino hangu dzana akalola muche, aka-m-hala.
**Muthalimu,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-), one who is false, dishonest, unrighteous; an intriguer, a

## [PDF Page 308 — Dictionary Page 295 (Mut — Muv)]

  cheat. Mutu huya ni muthalimu; or Kir. proper, Yuna fitina. Hungapatana, ela mutu-huya ni muthalimu-yudzi-hu-fitina.
**Muthana,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Vioni; Niuni. (1) An omen, generally an ill omen.
(2) Luck. The word principally refers to the first meeting with an odd number of persons, when setting out on a journey, though it also includes the omen obtained by observing birds. *See* Ku era, niuni. Nidzipigua ni muthana nauya. Muthana wa uchi ku u na utu. Nidzikuenda na muthana mudzo, or, mui; lit. I went with a good or bad omen; *i.e.* I was lucky or unlucky.
**Muthanga,** *n. coll.* (wa; the pl. Mi- is, however, also in use, and is optional). *See* Kanga; Mudzele. Iron and brass beads, as made by the Wakamba. Ku hungira muthanga.
**Muthanse,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of tree. The root is odoriferous.
**Muthaya** (Kig.). Muthaya wa madzi.
**Muthea** (Kik.), *n.* (wa). *See* Muanamiranchira. A charm, consisting of a kind of powder.
**Muthego,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Mutheko,** *n.* (wa). Lukungo lumeralo meno, ndo mutheko.
**Muthia,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mithia). *See* Mignio; Doroseka. A partition in a hut, a line, a stripe. Ku lafia muthia. Atu ademerao, ndo muthia. Atu adzipigana viha, be akalavia mithia ku-a-demera hara tu adzao, muka sunguluka ku-a-ika kahikahi.
**Muthiaka,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Thiaka (ra). A quiver. Note: This form of the word is not so much in use as Thiaka or Riaka.
**Muthiani,** *n.* (pl. Athiani; irregular pl. Ndiani). From Ku thiana. A spy.
**Muthiuka,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kelia.
**Muthuamuthua,** *adj.*, impudent (asie haja); lit. without behaviour, badly behaved,
**Muthungu, Murungu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-). *See* Kulungire. The name of a thorny tree. Its fruit is called ndungu. Ana adide anadzodzua mfignio, akasarua musi wa muthungu. The wood of the muthungu is used for perfuming.
**Muthuri,** *n.* From Ku thura.
**Mutu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Atu). *See* Kota; Dovola. (1) A human being, a person, somebody. Mutu muche, A female, a woman. Mutu mulume, A male, a man. Mutu wa ku dungua milomo. Dim., Kadzitu.
(2) The pupil of the eye. Kuna mutu dzidzoni; or, Kuna mutu kahikahi ya dzidzo. Muana ka-dza-henda mutu dzidzoni, ka-dza-ona.
**Muulagakuku,** *n.*
**Muulagi,** *n.* (wa, pl. A-). *See* Mbuladzua.
**Muulo,** *n.* *See* Mulo. A killer.
**Muumbadzi.**
**Muumbi,** or **Muumbu.** *See* Mumbu.
**Muumfi,** *n.* (pl. Aumbi, or Aumfi), a potter. Adzomba a-mu-iha mufinansi. Muumfi hiyu akaumba niungu to.
**Muundu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Aundu). *See* Hai. An envier, antagonist, an enemy. Mua Mkemba yuna aundue; or, Mua Mkemba, He has his enemies.
**Muunguana** (Kij.), *n.* (pl. Aunguana), a free man.
**Muuso,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-).
**Muuyu,** or **Muyu,** *n.* (wa, pl. Miuyu), the baobab.
**Muvaka,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a boundary, limit. Ku vaka muvaka, To set a boundary.
**Muvakajembe,** *n.*, hoe-boundary; *i.e.* where the hoe is brought

## [PDF Page 309 — Dictionary Page 296 (Muv — Muw)]

  in contact with the field of a neighbour; in contradistinction to where uncultivated land bounds the plantation. Hudzivakana muvakajembe. *See* Vakana.
**Muvala** (= Nazi). Nazi ya muvala; pl. Nazi sa muvala. Muvala hiu una mudze.
**Muvande,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree, Ka-i-na tundo. Adzidzanga mivande ya kuni.
**Muvara** (Kig.), *adj.* (= Mkali in Kij.).
**Muvera** (Kig.), *n.* (= Mumfera in Kir.), gratification, attraction. Ni muvera wani umuhehao? What attraction brings him here?
**Muvesero,** *n.* (wa). Muveserowe gavesa-ga. The ga refers to Maneno, which is understood.
**Muveveya,** *adj.*, light as a feather, chaff, etc. From Ku veva. Miveve ya muvunga ni miveveya. Mulomo wa volovondo na wa p'embe ni miveveya.
**Muvevera.**
**Muvia,** *adj.*, new.
**Muvidza,** *n.*
**Muvilivili,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the red pepper shrub. Tundoze ni pilipili, or, pil'pili. Muvilivili wa nika, urio muhaso. Magova na vibamfuvie ni muhaso wa laga, vilungua na-uchi hebu madzi, mutu akanoa na muridza. Na lunga muvilivili na uchi.
**Muvindo.**
**Muvingo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the ebony tree.
**Muvini,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), a handle.
**Muviri.** Mbawa ni muviriwe dzimba.
**Muvisa,** *n.* and *adj.* *See* Mfisa.
**Muvolognondo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) the name of a tree of soft wood. Its bark is used to intoxicate fish in sweet water. The natives first beat the bark, and then throw it into the water, and stir it. Dumbaku ya muvolognondo.
(2) Tobacco, the leaves of which resemble the leaves of this tree.
**Muvovo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a tree of very soft and light wood.
**Muvuananiko,** *n.* *See* Fururira; Fururisa. Muvuananiko ka-u-chisa muhoni madzi ni mangi. Muvuananiko udziukuta hata kandakanda. Yudzihalua ni muvuananiko. Muvuananiko unavuma.
**Muvudzu,** *adj.* (= Muambamba), thin, slender. From Pudzu. Mutu muvudzu, A thin man. Muhi muvudzu, A slender tree. Umiro muvudzu, A thin, *i.e.* high-sounding, voice; in contradistinction to Umiro musiho.
**Muvunga,** *n.* (wa), (1) rice.
(2) The name of a grass, used for thatching.
**Muvuvu,** *adj.* (pl. A- when rel. to persons, and Mi- when rel. to things). *See* Muando. Bare, mere.
**Muvuye,** *n.* (= Mukodze). Kakabinikisa-to niungu, idzilafia muvuye; mugasija udzifua hiu, ka-u-kaifua. Only used negatively: Muhi hiu ukayuya, ka-u-na muvuye, kusa merera udo ku dzoa muvuye. Kitu hiki ka-ki-na muvuye (= ka-ki-merera, ni kiyuya). Nguo hi ikayuya, ka-i-merera, ka-i-na muvuye. Gnania kana muvuye (= kana ngufu). Musiko hiu ka-u-na muvuye (= ni muyuya, ka-u-merera).
**Muwale,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), the name of a species of palm in Usambara.
**Muwaye,** *n.* (pl. Awaye). Mutu hiyu ni muwaye, kaika kitu, kituche ni ku muagamuaga, maliye ka-i-kala; kuna mbeko wala kana akiba.

**Muya,** *n.* (wa, pl. Aya).
**Muyesi,** *n.* (= Mudzembesi). *See* Yeya.

## N.

**N,** the fourteenth letter of the alphabet, pronounced as in English.—[ED.]
**Na,** (1) *conj.*, with, and, by. (*a*) It is used in composition with the personal pronouns, in the conjugations: Ni-na, U-na, Yu-na, Hu-na, Mu-na, A-na. The particles which represent the various classes of nouns are used in the same way. Anajira na njira-kadza kuku, They pass along the way; they do not come hither. *See* Remiria. Na usiku, In the night. Na-ni, With what. *See* Rima, 2. Yudzizikua na gnombe; lit. He was buried with a cow; *i.e.* a cow was killed at a funeral entertainment. Manire na Mulungu kusu-kalavo a-ni-rinde rero na machero. Nari nidzingira menoni kare, ela Mulungu ndiye adzaye, ni difia. (*b*) It is often prefixed in a way which, at first, seems redundant, but, in fact, imparting a peculiar emphasis to a sentence. Na-mi, And I, And me; Na-we, And thou, And thee; Na-ye, And he, And she, And him, And her; Na-sui, And we, And us; Na-mui, And you; Nao, And they, And them. *See* Hadi; Kore; Fiuka; Mera; Chari; Mukono; Funsa; Nundu. This use of the particle is constant in prayers.
(2) 1st pers. sing. in the conjugation of the verbs, implying the pres. as well as the imperf. tenses. *See* Mishombo; Mukumbu. Na piga rero, I strike (pres.). Na piga dzana, I was striking (imperf.).
(1) Na-ga, And they; Na-go, And they, with them.
(2) Na-i, And it; Na-yo, And it, with it. This when referring to Mi- also implies the pl.
(3) Na-ki, And it; Na-cho, And it, with it.
(4) Na-lu, And it; Na-lo, And it, with it.
(5) Na-ri, And it; Na-ro, And it, with it.
(6) Na-si, And they; Na-zo, And they, with them.
(7) Na-u, And it; Na-o, And it, with it.
(8) Na-vi, And they; Na-vio, And they, with them.
(9) Na-va, And it; Na-vo, And it, with it. This only relates to place where, there.
(10) Na-ku, And it; Na-ko, And it, with it.
(11) Na-ka, And it; Na-ko, And it, with it.
(12) Na-mu, And in, there; Na-mo, And in, there.
Ninga niria na cho mimi, It is if I myself had it.
**Nabunabu,** *adv.*, out of sight. From Na and Bu, which *see*. It is only used in connection with Ku binikisa, To cover, with vessels only, and never to cover with a cloth.

**N'ano.** From Ni, or Na ano. N'ano baba ni baba zangu. N'ano baba zangu hara.

**Nasi, Nazi,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) a cocoa-nut. Nazi fu; or, Nazi pfu, A dry, or hard, *i.e.* fully ripe cocoa-nut.
(2) The kernels of stone-fruits. Nazi ya koko ya koma ka-i-gogodeka. Nazi ya koko ya gumo, ka-i-riwa; ukaria, unavavika.

**Nathiri** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Hadi), a vow. Ku ika nathiri, To make a vow. Nathiri a-yo ika, ka-dza-usa; pl. Nathiri a-zo-ika, ka-dza-usa.
**Nauli,** *n.*, fare, freight.
**Nausi,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). Pembe sa nausi ndizo sihenduazo palapanda.
**Na-vo** (= Avo; Uvo, etc.; Enda, fut.; Lomba).
**Nchakama** (Kigiriama), *n.* (ya, za) (= Mufunga). Ku ika nchakama.
**Nchama,** *n.* (ya, za), private consultation. Ku uka nchama, To go aside for private consultation.

**Nche,** *n. encl.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), a word which conveys no distinct meaning by itself, but only in the three following combinations: (1) Nche mure, the centipede; lit. the long nche. (2) Nche kifimba, the scorpion-spider; lit. the belly-nche. Udzunguwe ni uchache, Its poison is little, even less than of the centipede; both are said to bite only in self-defence. (3) Nche kidako, or Nche kigonsi, a scorpion; lit. the sheeptail-nche or sheep-nche. Udzunguwe ni ungi. Yuluma na mulomo, basi akareha kira kignio, aka-va-muagira madzi varatu adzovoluma, basi uka akakewa sana, Hata niuchi ndo ahendavio, Its poison is much; he bites with the mouth, then he brings that tail, and there spits a fluid, even there where he has bitten, then you are made to burn much. Aki-ku-luma chiramuko, basi ni ku akaka hata kukadzua, ukalala naye hata kukacha, vakidzota, vakiricha, hata ukomo dza huratu avo-ku-luma, basi vakaricha kamare ku luma. When one says, Nidzilumua ni nche, he will be directly asked, Ni nche wani adzeye-ku-luma?
**Nchelele,** *n.* (= Chongo, or Tongo). *See* Ngelele.
**Nchemi,** *n.* (za), a shout, a yell, an outcry. From Ku chema. Ku piga nchemi, To shout, to yell. Ku rira na nchemi, To cry aloud, to shriek.
**Nchia-manga,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a pigeon, a dove.
**Nchini,** *n.*, (K.) the vagina.
**Nchira, Njira,** *n.* (ya, za), a way.
**Nchogoma,** *n.* (ya, za).
**Nda,** *n.* *See* Remeria; Cha. Hunger, famine.
**Ndada,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Mdada; Madzadzigo. (1) A walking-stick. Dim., Kadada.
(2) Orion's belt.
**Ndagisua,** *n.*, commission. From Ku lagisa. Prov., Ndagisua si urinsi, urinsi ni m'egnie, vioonewa kare.
**Ndago,** *n. pl.* (za, sing. Ludago) (= Dongo?). *See* Fukisa.
**Ndala,** *n.* (= Kidala).
**Ndale** (Kig.), *n.* (ya, za). *See* Muthanga. Beads from Gnandu. Mudzele wa ndale.
**Ndalo,** *n.* (ya, za). Ndalo ni sa uinani, ela mfimbo ni dzulu ya niumba, niasini.
**Ndalu,** *n.*, the name of a snake.
**Ndama** (Kidigo), *n.* (ya, za, hiyu, hia) (= Mfarika in Kir.), a heifer. Dim., Kadama.
**Ndama** (?). Maneno go ga ndama usi-mu ambire muche.
**Ndani,** *prep.* *See* Gnarira; Ingira, Within; (K.) inside, inwardly, into, interior.
**Ndani,** *n.* (ya, za), the inside, belly, womb. Yuna ndani niomu na moyo momu. Yuna ndani mbi. Yudzi-ni-la ndani, I have done with him or her.
**Ndarawe,** *n.* (ya, za). Vidziwe via ndarawe. Ndarawe ya vidziwe.
**Ndarira,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Simo in Kij.). Maneno ga ndarira. Ku dzuva ndarira. Nidzi-m-dzuvira ndarira, ela ka-ga-mania. Mutu aambuaye ni muari hebu mulumbi, ndiye a maniaye maneno higo ga ndarira muno; ndiye amaniaye ku dania malau. Munga ambavio, mudzuva ndarira za ku-ni-amba mimi hebu dze? Resp., Si uwe hecheyo, ache osi ario na Mkuavi; be kamuna ada, muakenga atu tu.
**Ndata,** *n.*, a walking-stick.
**Ndaundau,** *adj.* and *adv.*, ready to start off or to run away. From Ku rauka. Adziima ndaundau, adzikimbira. Ku sagala, u-imire tu, u-ndaundau, unazolua hebudze? Gnombe hi i-ndaundau, or, i-tungitusigi indakimbiao.

  kueli. Nidziona mutu, ndzagamba ya mulume, yunaogofia. Ndzagamba ya ndzovu; ya niahi, etc., A giant of an elephant, of a buffalo, etc. Dim., Kadzagamba and Kidzagamba, especially used of smaller animals.

Kirenge hiki cha komala, kina ndzira, This calabash, meaning the rind, is fully ripe; it is solid. Pfuko hi ka-i-na, ndzira, inaveva, This jar has no substance; it is very light.
**Ndzo,** *v. imper.*, come.
  **Ndzoni,** *pl.*, come ye.
**Ndzora,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Ora; Ludzambo; Kilinga. Ornamental carvings, streaks or lines of various colours, in animals. Kirenge hiki kikahendua ndzora. Kula chugkina ndzorase. Mbuzi hira ina ndzora za malu, That goat has the streaks of a malu.
  **Ndzorandzora.** *See* Foro; Kulukulusinge. Gnombe hi ina ndzorandzora. Foro yuna ndzorandzora.
**N'dzo-vio, Ni-dzo-vio.** Viniasi vine, n'dzo-vio dzukula, ela n'dza-vio richa ni paki ya viniasi viiri.
**Ndzovu,** *n.*, an elephant.
**Ndzuga,** *n.* (ya, za). Dim., Kadzuga; magn., Ridzuga.
**Ndzugu,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Ndu in Kij.). Lukadza lua ndzugu (Kid.). Ku fuka ndzugu.
**Ndzui,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). *See* Kozi. Ndzui hata ana mbuzi ni ku guira, hata za. Yuna kombe nire.
**Ndzumbi** (Kid.) (= Fuzi in Kir.).
**Ndzusi,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia) (= Chagabu in Kid.), the name of a wild cat.
**Ne.** Ne enende, for Ni enende. *See* Muta; Sika.
**Ne,** *adj. encl.* *See* Kadiri. Four. Used in this simple form with words of the ya class; with other words the usual preformatives are prefixed: Ane, Mane, Mine, Vine. *See* Ine. Niumbane, Four houses. Gnombene, Four cows. Atu ane, Four persons. Vifiu vine, Four knives.
**Neko,** *n.* (ya, za). Na alafie dzango ra neko, basi ahale muchewe (ni dzango ra pima mbiri).
**Nema, Neema,** *n.* (ya) (= Diba; Mbaraka; Kifuna), grace, mercy. Muaka wa rero kuna nema. Gnania yuna nema, uk'enda vakue muriangoni, basi vanahama, vana sisima to.

## [PDF Page 316 — Dictionary Page 303 (Nem — Nga)]

**Nemba,** *n.*, a tribal mark.
**Nembe.**
**Nemuka,** *v.n.* (= Yongoheka in Kid.). Mutu arie na muiri muolofu, wa ku idima ku fuina sana-akikala yunadui-kaduika muiri-ndiye aambuaye; yuna nemuka.
**Nena,** *v.n.* *See* Kavayo; Moro; Neno. To say, to speak. Der., Neno (pl. Ma-).
  **Neneka,** *v.n.* *See* Fumi; Mufugudira. Ka-vi-neneka.
  **Nenera,** *v.d.* Wari aka-ni-zira, ka-ni-nenera, ela, hangu dzana, aki-ni-ona, ni ku-ni-lamusa, akanena nami. Wari aka-ni-zira, ela hangu dzana yuna-ni-nenera.
  **Nenerana,** *v. reit.* Atu hio kanenerana, aheha.
  **Nenesana,** or **Nenesania,** *v. reit.*, to dispute, to quarrel.
**N'enda** (for **Naenda**), I go.
**N'ende** (for **Niende**), may I go, or let me go.
**Nene,** *adj.*, big, thick, fat. Dzi nene.
**Nene,** *n.* *See* Koma. Numbness. Kigulu kidzihenda nene (= Kidzefua gansi), My leg or foot is asleep. Gulu ridzefua nene.
**Neno,** *n.* (ra. pl. Ma-), a word, a sentence, a speech. Gnania yudzenena neno hata yudzimala pia, or, pie. Mutu hiye yudzi-ni-piga neno, karindala ndani, baha kuamba yudzi-ni-hu kuna ku riko neno hiro adza-ro-ni-amba.
**Nere** (= Nari), I was. From Niere. Angafika, nere vavo, or, nere-vo.
**Neruve.** *See* Nieruve.
**Nga,** *v.a.* *See* Resa; Ririra (ria); Sia. To resemble, to be like. Ni-nga. U-nga. Yu-nga. Hu-nga. Mu-nga. A-nga. I-nga, zi-nga; ki-nga, vi-nga; ri-nga, ga-nga; lu-nga. Kala a-nga-ye kiniegere. Gnombe hio, or, io, ni-dza-yo-ona, i-nga gnombe yangu. Kasha hiri ri-nga hirira. Gnania a-nga dza ku la charoni, mameye yuere yudzefua kare, in Kig., Fulani, ali-pa kuja ku toka safarini, mamaye alikua anakuisha kuva, A person when he came from his journey found his mother was dead. Anga enenda yuari kahensi, or, yuere kahensi. Yuyu musenao angahenda akidza vava, yuna-m-londa yuyu mucheo. Angahenda-yunaonewa, He was seen when he did it; lit. He is like doing, he is seen. Nikure? ungafika dzua riluavi? Is it far? where was the sun when you arrived? Ningafika, or, Ningavofika, dzua ridi na vidzoa, When I arrived the sun was vertical. *See* Bagisua; Chererua; Hadi; Kara; Kunsa; Balu; Se-ye; Onia; Mufiasi; Yeyerua.
**Nga** (= Nda? Kid.). *See* Resa. Contracted from Ni ga. Madzere nga lukuani.
**Ngada,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Vadza.
**Ngai,** *n.* (= Ngumbu). The latter is more generally used.
**Ngala,** *n.* (ya, za). Ngala ya dzere.
**Ngama,** *n.*, white clay, marl. Munda wa gnania una kilongo, u-nga munda wa ngama, madzerege ni masiho. Kunzine ni ngama, kungine ni luzanga.
**Ngamba** (Kid.), *n.* (= Ndere in Kir.).
**Ngambu** (Kik.), *n.* (ya, za) (Luthea in Kir.), the jawbone. Yudzi-m-guira mua ngambu, He seized him by the jawbone.
**Ngamira,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a camel.
**Nganasa,** *adj.* (= Hodari), strong, bold, brave. Lukuva hilo ludzifungu anganasa to. Opposed to Foroforo. Hei! adzipiga nganasa ya kueli.

## [PDF Page 317 — Dictionary Page 304 (Nga — Ngi)]

  Lukuva lusiku ludzi fungua nganasa to.
**Ngano,** *n.* (ya, za), a riddle, a fable. Ku ana ngano. Ngano za ku imba, A riddle, to sing.
**Ngao,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) a shield.
(2) *See* Kata. A screen, partition. Nuhala jamfi, nifunge hiva, ni kate ngao.
**Ngariba,** *n.* (= Ngariba in Kij.). *See* Ngao. A circumciser.
**Ngare,** *n.* (za) (= Nimbo), (1) Pl. of Lugare. Ku piga ngare. Mutu hiyuyuna ngare ningi dza kihui.
(2) Yuna ngare ningi (= Manenoge ka-ga-sira kanoa-ni-muakue).
**Ngarengare,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the beckoning crab. It is smaller than the gandoniumue. Gnania yuna mbusi ningi, zidzimuagika luandani dza ngarengare.
**Ngari,** *n.* and *adv.* Naokerera, nahenda ngari. Ku okerera ugari.
**Ngari,** *adv.* *See* Bamfula; Hanga; Bu; Gunchagancha; Rimu, 2; Surusira; Ngosangosa; Muadza; Niongo. May, whether, about. Gnombe na-zo-gula, hata anao, ngari zinatimira kumi na dzano, ela si-si-noere masiagnere nikaoniua tu, ela ka-vi-ere viangu. Ni-pa vidembe ngari, nika lungire rero tu. Na-mu-va ngari reale mbiri.
**Ngazi, Ngazi** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za), (1) the frame of a door. Used by the Wanyika only of the gates of their kayas.
(2) Any forked tree used for a post. Masimika nguso, ni nsiho, i-nga ngazi.
**Ngawa** (Kij.), *adv.* (= Ngari in Kir.), what though.
**Nge,** *n.* *See* Nche.
**Ngeido** (Kid.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Ovolue in Kir.? Kishunda in Kij.), remainder of food, a small basket or vessel in which the remainder of food or other things is kept.
**Ngelele,** or **Nchelele,** *n.*, a one-eyed person. Gnania yuna ngelele (= yuna tongo), He or she is one-eyed.
**Ngemi,** *n.* (= Nchemi). Ana piga ngemizao.
**Ngemua,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Ugema). *See* Funsia. Ngemua yani ino, ngemua ya foroforo. Ni kura tu ku funsiua, ndo ku mania ngemua.
**Ngenge,** *n.* (za), glittering. Mufiu una ngenge, unagnala. Nidziona nioka; yuna ngenge. Ngenge ni za mufiu na za nioka, ela za dzua ni chenge.
**Ngeregere,** *n.* Pl. of Lugeregere.
**Ngero,** *n.* (= Kigere), the wrist. Nidzibuma mukono uina wa koe hata ngeroni, nika-m-guira, nika-m-lavia.
**Ngeru,** or **Njeru** (Kid.).
**Ngeu,** *n.* (ya, za).
**Ngi,** *adv.*, thoroughly, well.
**Ngi,** *adj.*, in composition with prefixes, Mangi, Mingi, etc., many, much.
**Ngigi,** *n.* (= Uziho). *See* Mudakuma; Dzikidziki. Thickness, compactness, solidity in substance, density. Kirenge hiki kina ngigi, ela kino ni chambamba, ni kiwawa. Sikirore rina ngigi, ka-ri-dza-niuka.
**Ngilengile** (Kid.) (= Sonde in Kins.).
**Ngilingili,** *n.* (ya, za), obstinacy. Nidzi-ku-kania, kukasikira, nidzi-ku-kania kahiri, kuka sikira-wamba: nahenda ngilingili tu. Ngilingiliyo kuambirika hebudze; ni yani yo ngilingili uhendayo? Ku henda ngilingili. Ni ngilingili-kuenda kuko tu, kuenda hendani?
**Nginga,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luginga. Nginga ndizo zifumiruazo toa cha mufiu.
**Ngi-ngi-ngi,** *interj.*, very. May be

## [PDF Page 318 — Dictionary Page 305 (Ngi — Ngu)]

  repeated many times. Jembe ri na ngi-ngi-ngi ni tegnie.
**Ngira.** *See* Inga.
  **Ngirisira.** *See* Inga.
  **Ngiza.** *See* Inga.
**Ngoba,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Nkoba.
**Ngodia,** *n.* (ya, za), the name of a dance, performed by the young. Uira wa ngodia unafuinua ni ahoho.
**Ngoera,** better **Nkoera,** *n.*
**Ngogomue,** *n.* (ya, za), an improvisator. Ngogomue ni muhi ku guirana na muyawe, be ukisumfiua ni peho, ukaheresa, vikakala dza luala na dzago; ni muhi ku girida muyawe.
**Ngoi,** *n.* (in Kig., Ngui), a leader in singing, who composes the words as he sings. Ngoi hiye akiupuka uirani, basi yuna hurisa uira. Ngoi hiye yuimba uira wa kare, kaidima ku dusa uvia.
**Ngolangola,** *v.n.*, to speak kindly to one who has been offended, to pacify. Si dzukirua ndugu yangu; hala hikino, uongese.
  **Ngosangosa,** *v.a.*, to soothe, to pacify, to flatter, especially to soothe children. Na-mu-ngosangosa muana, yunarira. Mu-hale muana, uende, uka-mu-ngosenyose ku ndze, ngari yunaniamala.
**Ngolodi,** *n.* (ya, za). Ngolodi za madzere (= Midzere mibomu).
**Ngolo.**
**Ngologolo,** *n.* (1) (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a species of ant. Ngologolo akadzupa dzalafu punde, a-nga pirua. Kaviri a-nga mignio, ela mignio ni are, are, ela-o ni afuhi.
(2) (ya, za), the stone of the fruit of the mugumo.
**Ngoma,** *n.* (ya, za), a drum. By way of synecdoche, it often means the dancing accompanied by the drum. *See* Ihika.
**Ngombo,** *n.* (ya, za). Na hufungane ngombo, hulole andeye-i-dosa na mbere. Hudzifungana ngombo; mimi yangu, nidzi-i-dosa, 'ye-yakue-yudzilala nayo; kakafumaga niuni.
**Ngome,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Ku goma. A fort, castle.
**Ngori,** *n.*, the name of a song used at the war-dance called Ndaro. Dziku ya ngori; ya ku uyiwa. Huenda ngorini, hukisa kuenda, hundariwa makolo. *See* Rereodzo. Ngore ho hularire chonkua.
**Ngorio,** *n.* (= Gurugufe in Kins.).
**Ngoro** (Kid. and Kidigo), *n.* (ya, za) (= Koro in Kir.), anger, wrath. Ku-dzi-tia ngoro ya gnigni. Yu tia ngoro ya gnigni.
**Ngorodo,** *n.*
**Ngoromoro.** Kombayuna.
**Ngorongoro.** Yugomba maneno ga ngorongore, kingindo. Angindo agomba ngorongoro, ka-ga-sikirika; Ataita agomba dekeredekere; Akamba amba, ndiendiendie.
**Ngorosho.**
**Ngosangosa.** *See* Ngolangola.
**Ngozi,** or **Ngodzi** (= Muravai).
**Ngu,** *pron.*, used in composition with the prefixes Angu, Changu, Yangu, Sangu, etc., mine, my.
**Ngudu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Pepo. The cowrie-shell. The Wakamba buy the ngudu for ornamenting calabashes and the skin in which women carry their children, called Ngoi in Kig. Ame ngudu; lit. The mother of the cowrie; a shell of the same shape and colour, but much larger. N.B.—Of Ngudu, the word Lukombe (pl. Kombe) is never used.
**Ngufu, Nguvu,** *n.* (za). *See* Gurika. Strength, might, power, force. Mutu hiyu yuna nguvu, ka-ku-sika.
**Ngui** (Kid.) (= Ngoi in Kir.).
**Ngula,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia) (= Barare).

## [PDF Page 319 — Dictionary Page 306 (Ngu — Ni)]

**Ngula,** *v.a.* *See* Enga.
  **Ngulula.** *See* Enga.
**Ngulu** (Kid.), (1). Mutu hiye yuna ngulu (= yuna gnieta in Kir.).
(2) A bivalvular shell-fish(?). N.B.—The word is only used in connection with Lukombe, and never by itself. Lukombe lua ngulu-ndilo Aravai a kare a-lo-kuangurira niungu; lit. The shell of the ngulu. It is the one with which the Rabais of former times scraped their pots. Now they only use a kivo or a kibamfu cha lukuni. Kombe za ngulu zikala poani.
**Ngulue,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the wild hog.
**Ngululo.**
**Ngululo,** *n.* (za). *See* Mbawa. Streaks. Pl. of Lugululo.
**Nguma,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luguma. Yudziahulua nguma mbiri.
**Nguma,** *n.* (ya), popularity. Ku la nguma, To become famous (= Ku ligua ni atu). Na sikira ngumayo, be nidziamba; nami n'enda nika-ku-lamuse, ni-ku-one, nami nikienenda kuehu, nikasumurire. Ngumaye ikafika kure.
**Ngumbau,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a hero. Gnania ni ngumbau, kalola niuma kabisa-ni mulume tu. Atu hio ni ngumbau.
**Ngumbo** (Kidigo?), *n.*, the name of a tool used in carpentry. Ngumbo ni chombo cha ku dzongera kinu.
**Ngumbu,** *n.* (ya, za), the name of a disease incidental to young cattle. Gnombe hi ka-dza-la ngumbu, sinda-i-hala. Ngumbu ndizo ziulagazo ana gnombe. Muana gnombe hiyu ka-dza-la ngumbu.
**Ngundu,** *n.*, the name of a red cloth, used for girdles. Mukumbu wa ngundu.
**Ngungu,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), (K.) the raven. Muiriwe osi pia ni muiru, ela yuna kilinga cha dzingo cheruve.
**Ngungu.**
**Nguo,** *n.* (ya, za), cloth, in general. Nguo ya dzulu. Dim., Kaguo and Kiguo.
**Nguruma,** *v.n.*, to rumble. Midzango ina-ni-nguruma (= Ndani yangu ina-ni-nguruma). Dzimba yuna nguruma. Der., Kingurumo.
**Ngurunga,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Yo wa in Kig.). *See* Kifumfu; Mbarara. A large rock. Dim., Kangurunga and Kingurunga.
**Nguso, Nguzo,** *n.* (ya, za), a post. Nguzo ya chuma. Mutu hiye yudzi-ni-pa kitu cha bure; Mulungu na a-mu-simike dza nguzo ya chuma, maguluge gamute dza nguso ya chuma; akidzuma naabade; kuani yuna moyo wa mbasi za ku-a-va atu vionsue. Dim., Kiguzo.
**Nguyu,** *n.* (ya, za), the ankle-bone. Nguyu ya ndani. Nguyu ya nse.
**Ni,** (1) the particle which indicates the 1st pers. sing. as used in the conjugations of the verbs; *e.g.* Ni-na; Ni-ka; Ni-dzi; Ni-nda; Ni-ki. The Ni, when connected with Na, is generally omitted or contracted, and sometimes in composition with Ka, Dzi, and Nda, but never with Ki.
(2) *pron.*, the objective case of Mimi: Me, To me; Ni-pa, Give me.
(3) It is used adverbially in connecting nouns with adjectives, and also with the verbs when preceded by the infinitive particle Ku. N.B.—The verbal particle Ni connects an adjective with its noun or pronoun, without any regard to the various classes of nouns. Gnombe ni ku gura, A cow scrapes the ground; Kuro ni ku gura, A dog scratches the ground; but Yunagura, The cow or the dog is scratching now. Dzui ni ku niada.

## [PDF Page 320 — Dictionary Page 307 (Nia — Nia)]

  (4) *prep.*, in, and, in a few instances, to.
  (5) *adv. of place*, in, by, to, among. Mu-tiani. Ku-m-funga gnombe muhini, To tie a cow to a tree.
  (6) *adv. inter.*, what. Abbreviated from Nini. It is always in this sense put at the end of a word or sentence. *See* Riaria; Laga; Larira; Adi; Risiki.
**Nia** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), (K.) conscience. Yudzitia nia moyoni, yudzi-ki-henza. Nidzi-ki-henza na nia yangu, moyoni.
**Nia,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the ostrich. Nia ndiye babaye niuni, ndiye buana wao, The ostrich is indeed the father of birds, yea, their buana.
**Niada, Niata,** *v.n.* (in Kid., Gniaba; Kins., Wenda; Gniagnamira in Kij.; *i.q.* in Kir.), to be robbed (?). Dzui ni ku niada, be anganiada, yuniadira ira tumbuzi. Lumbui na-ro ni ku niada. Mutu aki fuererua kayani, akikala yunala, kuenda mundani, basi niku niada. Be anga mada, Well, as to his going stealthily, it is for.
**Niada, Niacha,** *n.* (pl. *id.*), a clever person. Ni mutu muerefu zana. Mutu hiye ni niacha; hata mkikala na mioro miziho ya ku aririana, be-ye ni ku-vi-dandaula pia; ni niacha muno. Atu hio ni niacha.
**Niafariri** (Kid.), *n.*, the name of a species of small black ant.
**Niafu, Niavu,** *n.* (za), stinging-nettles. Pl. of Luafu, Luavu.
**Niago,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luago.
**Niaha,** *v.a.* (= Hega).
  **Niahira,** *v.d.* Nidzi-m-niahira kamba, kuenda henda mboga.
  **Niahirua,** *v.p.* Nidziniahirua kamba ni amegnania, kuamba nidze nihende mudzusi ngari.
  **Niahua,** *v.p.* Kamba adziniahua, si 'da osi.
**Niahi,** *n.*, a buffalo.
**Niaka,** *v.a.* *See* Gniaka. To catch, as a ball.
**Niakula** (Kid.).
**Niala,** *v.a.*, (1) to plant.
(2) To forget.
(3) To dry up, as a wound when healing, and to wither as grass. Nidziambua: nihale madzere, nikaniole, be nidziniala. Kuniala ni ku andika ku uma (= Ku anza ku uma). Der., Lunialu; Kinialu; Muniale.
  **Nialua,** *v.p.* (1) *See* Tarare. To be planted. Hiva vadzinialua, Here it has been planted.
  (2) To be forgotten.
  **Niarika,** *v.n.* *See* Kinemi. (1) To admit of planting. Mvula idzegnia, kunaniarika hebudze? Resp., Kuna niarika-inamesa, kineme ni kibomu. Mvula ni chache, kakuniarika.
  (2) To admit of being forgotten. Neno hiri ka-ri-niarika; more frequently, however, the people will say, Neno hiri ka-ri-angamika, atu anda-ri-mania hata kare ka-dze. Utu hio wamba: hundania la we? Kahundaniala, ka-u-niarika.
  **Niarira,** *v.d.*, to plant to or for another. Gnania ni mukongo, h'endeni, huka-m-niarire ueruwe, usamera, mifusi, kaku-dza-nialua. Uk'enda kuangu mundani, ni-niarira mbeyuyangu.
  **Niarirua,** *v.p.*, to have one's field planted by another. Yudzinirarirua ni nduguze.
  **Niasa,** *v.a.*, (1) to strew, to spread. Ku niasa milala.
  (2) *See* Mfarusa. To make forget. Gnania yudzi-ni-niasa kitu changu, by keeping it a long time. Muivi yudzi-ni-niasa, hata ku mania rero

## [PDF Page 321 — Dictionary Page 308 (Nia — Nia)]

  si-vo, iye yukudza iya, yudzimania sivo hangi. Niama yuno yudzi-ni-niasa, hangu navolarira kadza, hata ku mania nidzidzoka, yudzikudzaria.
**Nialamu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class). *See* Kifumfu. Wide, broad. Niumba udzi-i-henda nialame. Kavu hino ni nialamu. Njira hi ni nialamu.
**Niama,** *n.* (1) (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a wild animal, a beast. Niama mguisi, A beast of prey. Dim., Kaniama and Kiniama; magn., Riniama.
(2) (ya, za), flesh, meat. Niama sa ufiere. Niama niru. *See* Kidzidzi. The fleshy part of the thigh, fillet. Dim., Ka- and Ki-, as above.
**Niamala, Gniamala,** *v.n.* *See* Era; Esa. To be silent. Ka-mu-niamase muyao, aniamale; mutu yudzefua kare, yunarira hata rini?
  **Niamarika, Gniamarika,** *v.n.* Maneno higa ka-ga-niamarika, hundakuenda hukamu-use.
  **Niamarira, Gniamarira,** *v.d.*, to be silent to any one. Yudzigomba, nidzi-m-niamarira mia.
  **Niamasa, Gniamaza,** *v.a.*, to make silent, to silence, to still. Mutu akifuererua ni nduguye, be yunarira sana, basi ukakuenda-m-niamaza. Nidzi-m-niamaza, ela kaniamala, yuchari rira wifio. Muhoho akirira, mameye ni ku-m-niamasa na hombo. Na mutu afiolaye, muyawe ni ku-m-niamaza.
  **Niamasika,** *v.n.*, rarely used. Kaniamazika, basi arire.
  **Niamasua,** *v.p.*
**Niambamba,** *adj.* (= Dzefu). *See* Rambamba. Thin.
**Niambo,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Wambo. From Ku amba, No. 1. Kudzinsa niambo za chingoni.
**Niambu,** *n.* (ya). (1) *See* Ndundu. The other side of a river or bay. From Ku ambua. Ukivuka muho hio, basi undafika niambu ya viri. Dim., Kadzambu, used with reference to Kadzuho.
(2) (za) (= Niambo).
**Niambura,** *n.* *See* Chumba.
**Niamuru** (Kidigo), *n.* Udzeria niamuru, ukala musunie wangu. Nidzeria niamuru, basi ni-musunieo.
**Niani,** *interrog. pron.* *See* Ani; Nani; Nanio? Who? who is it? Hata uwe udarua niani u maniwa niani we? Una kitu chani we? muna kazi yani mui adude? or, mui a hunde? Yulolua niani? To whom was she married? Resp., Yunalolua ni muana wa gnania, She was married to the son of Gnania.
**Niani,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name of a large monkey. Prov., Niani anadzekona nkoko (= Dzuku za niani).
**Nianiasa,** *v.a.*, to annoy, to molest. Uo uhuahui-we wa amegnania, ndio udzo-o-m-nianiasa muanangu chakuria, hata muanangu kakaukuha, yuna ndzala kua-o uhuahui.
**Niansiye.**
**Niara** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Damfa. Booty. Nidzipata niara.
**Niaraka** (Kij.), *n.* (za), (K.) letters. Pl. of Waraka. Adzomba adzilafia niaraka.
**Niasa,** *v.a.* *See* Niala.
**Niasa,** *v.a.* Ku-ni-niasa, dza ku amba ni-muanao, nini?
  **Niasua,** *v.p.*
**Niasi,** *n.*, grass, herbage.
  **Niasiniasi,** *adj.*, lit. of grass, illegitimate. Muana wa niasiniasi, or, wa dzakadzaka, or, wa kayakaya, or, wa mbuya, An illegitimate child. Kamanikana babaye.
**Niauka,** *v.n.* *See* Runda. To contract, to shrink up, to shrivel, to wither, to wrinkle. Madzere madzanga, ukivuku-

*Footer: 308*

---

## [PDF Page 322 — Dictionary Page 309 (Nia — Nin)]

  sa, ukianika dzuani, be wamba: na-ga-anika, ganiauke, be nivonde. Mutu akionda kua ndzala hebu kua ukongo, ndo aambuavo: yudziniauka. Mudumia hebu kivedi ni ku niauka muiri kua ufiere, An old man or an old woman, he or she is wrinkled in body by old age.
  **Niausa,** *v.*, to cause to wither or wrinkle. Madzere higa ni madzanga, ka-ga-vondeka, be na-ga-niausa, gafuhuke, ndivo gandavo vondeka. Na muhama mudzanga una-u-niausa, uume.
**Niayo,** *n.* (za), footsteps. Pl. of Luayo.
**Nibuni,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). Nibuni! muaga! nidzole tembe.
**Nidze,** 1st pers. sing. of the perf. tense; used before monosyllabic and enclitic verbs. *See* Fua. Not to be confounded with Nidze, from Kudza, To come.
**Nidzi,** 1st pers. sing. of the perf. tense; the common form, used before polysyllabic verbs.
**Niefula, Gniefula, Nievula** (Kid.) (in Kir., Muafula).
**Niegere,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia) (= Kiniegere).
**Niegnie,** *n.* (= Chindesi?), dirt, filth. Muana hiyu yuna niegnie (= dzama), hata ku oka kaoka; yuna guiza niegnie.
**Niegnieza,** *v.a.* (= Gniegnieza), to tickle.
**Niegniezi,** *n.* (ya, za), a star; lit. the twinkler. Niegniezi hiyiya (Kid.). Niegniezi hizira.
**Niekuka.** *See* Gniekuka.
**Niembe,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luembe.
**Niemere.** *See* Niamala.
**Niemere,** *n.*, silence. Hungajira-yuvavo, yuniemere mia, kagomba, While we passed, he was there, he was quite silent, he speaks not. Suino huari niemere, ela uwe unadza una-va-henda lonso, be uka, uenende! U niemere kimia, Thou keepest silence. Ari akigomba, ela aniemere, or, adziniamala.
**Niena,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luena.
**Niengu,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luengu.
**Niensa,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luensa.
**Niense, 1,** *n.* Niense, za muniense, ndizo Wadigo ahendazo tende za maguluni.
**Niense, 2,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), (1) the name of a species of cricket, somewhat smaller than the fuancho; the grasshopper. Yunga nsige, ela nsige ni mure, kidzoache ni chalamu.
(2) *See* Udauda. The singing in the ear. Sikiro rangu rinarira niense (= rinaambirisa). Yudzi-ni-piga mbalahi ya niense.
**Niere,** *n.* (za), hair. Pl. of Ludzere.
**Nieruve,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), white. Gnombe nieruve, A white cow, or white cattle. (The sing. or pl. can only be indicated by using a dem. or poss. pron., or by adding a numerical word.)
**Nika, Nyika,** *n.* (ya), wilderness, the name of the country near Mombas, occupied by about twelve tribes called Wanyika, people of the wilderness. Their language is Kinyika.
**Nimbo,** or **Gnimbo,** *n.* *See* Ongora. A song. Ku imba muhurisa.
**Niminisa,** *v.a.* Ku niminisa ngoma.
  **Niminisika,** *v.n.* Ngoma hi inaniminisika, ela hino ni bomu, si-i-dima ku-i-niminisa.
  **Niminisira,** *v.d.* Ndzo, u-ni-niminisire ngoma, mimi nikote.
  **Niminisua,** *v.p.*
**Ni-na,** prefix of a verb 1st pers. sing.; lit. I with, I have.
**Ni-nda** (= N'enda lasa). *See* Gumo; Nda; Siwa.
**Nine** (Kidigo) (= Mameye in Kir.,

*Footer: 309*

---

## [PDF Page 323 — Dictionary Page 310 (Nin — Nio)]

  and Moyo in Kig.), his mother. Prov., Mgema kasika nine (= Kir., Mugema kasika mameye). *See* Nsimo (and Prov.).
**Nin'enda** (for Ninaenda), 1st pers. sing. pres. ind. of Ku enda, I go.
**Ni-nga.** *See* Nga; Dumania; Ningari; Ni-ngere; Nga; Niumba; Gnombe; Mbuzi.
**Ninga,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of dove, somewhat larger than the jia, said to carry a little stick in its claws to stand on when coming to drink water. *See* the fable about it under the word Pingi.
**Ningavi,** *adv. interrog.* *See* Esa. How many?
**Ningi,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), much, many. Niumba ningi, Many houses. Mudzi hiu ka-u-na niumba ningi, ni tembe.
**Nini,** *adv. interrog.*, what? Often contracted to Ni.
**Niodanioda,** *v.a.* Der., Manionioda.
**Nioe,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). *See* Kungo. The name of a species of grasshopper. Nioe ni mdzuano muno, ku sidi vibansi viosi, ana mafuha, a-nga kamba.
**Nioga,** *n.* (za). *See* Nderi. Feathers. Pl. of Lunioga.
**Niognonio,** *n.* (ya), languidness. From Ku gniognoniera.
**Nioha,** *n.* (ya).
**Nioi.** *See* Nioe.
**Nioka,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a serpent, snake. Nioka masia. Nioka mfufi. Nioka mukufu, The chain-snake. Kua muiriwe-u-nga mukufu wa chuma. Nioka mgema (= Ukukui in Kij.). Nioka mgema yunalamba uchi wa muanso, kibangala ki-si-vo dzangue ku fungirua. Nioka mukoko; pl. Nioka mikoko, The red mangrove - snake. Yuihua nioka mukoko kua ku kala mudune dza mikoko. Yuoneka tupani; akionewa, ankue: ni koma, ukakuenda piga mfua. Dim., Kadzoka; magn., Dzoka and Ridzoka.
**Niola,** *v.a.*, to shave.
  **Niolana,** *v. reit.*, to shave each other. Atu hia ananiolana.
  **Niolua,** *v.p.*, to be shaved.
  **Niorera,** *v. inst.*, to shave with. Luembe lua ku niorera, A razor to shave with.
**Niolofu, Niolovu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), soft. Niama ni niolovu, Meat is soft.
**Niomu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class). *See* Uumfi; Waka. Hard, severe. Mihi hio ni niomu, These trees are hard. Kondo ni niomu, The quarrel is severe. Kasi niomu, Hard work. Musungu yuna kazi niomu; kahu-i-wesa, The European has hard work; we are not able to do it. Yuna ndani niomu, or, mbi; lit. He has a hard inside; *i.e.* He is cruel, hard-hearted. Dzi idzikala niomu, The earth has become hard.
**Niondo,** *n.* (ya, za), nipple.
**Nionga,** *n.* (ya), journey. Nionga ina-ni-luma. Yunalumua ni nionga.
**Nionge,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), weak, slight, poor, of no account. Kazi nionge, A small or poor business. Munionge, Kinionge, etc.
**Niongo,** *n.* (ya), (1) bile.
(2) The word is sometimes used instead of Chumvi, Sea-water, from the superstition that, in boiling it for salt, more salt will be yielded if the real name is concealed. From Ku nona. Nidzikuenda hega niongo (*i.e.* Chumvi), nidze, nichite, nipate vidembe ngari via ku lungira.
**Nionio** (= Nikuererua). Nionio e, nidzidzola kifiu. Nionio e, nidzidzola pehe, etc.
**Nioniosa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Kij., Nianiasa; Kins., Sunsa; in Kir.,

*Footer: 310*

---

## [PDF Page 324 — Dictionary Page 311 (Nio — Niu)]

  Ku shononesa), to tease a child.
  **Nioniosera,** *v.d.*, to cause to tease. Ku nioniosera muanangu vio nini?
**Niono,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Mbono), the castor-oil berry, seed. Mafuha ga niono, Castor-oil.
**Niotola.** *See* Gniotola.
  **Niotoka.** *See* Gniotola.
**Nioya,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Loya.
**Nire,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class). *See* Lukano; Kifumfu. Long. Kombe nire, Long.
**Niri,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a bird.
**Nirie,** *pron.* (composed of Ni-ri-ye). *See* Dumania. I who.
**Niru,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), black. Gnombe niru.
**Ni-sa, Ni-za.** *See* Za.
**Niuchi,** *n.*, a kind of beer.
**Niufu,** *n.* (za), the dead. Pl. of Lufu.
**Niuhe.** Niama za ku duena niuhe.
**Niuho,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luho.
**Niukaniuka,** *v.a.* (= Ku sukuma; Ku kururia; Ku mignia), to carry. Yudzi-mu-va muana niama bomu, yunahenda-i-niukaniuka, ka-i-wesa. Yudzi-ni-niukaniuka.
  **Niukana,** *v. reit.* Atu ananiukana.
  **Niukula,** *v.a.* *See* Gniukula.
**Niukue,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lukue.
**Niulula,** *v.a.* (in Kid., to lift = Niamura in Kins.). *See* Kuara. Yudzi-mu-niulula muana dzafu. Der., Muniulutu.
  **Niuluka,** *v.n.*, to be tough, to be clammy. Muhi uniulukao, uki-u-funsa, ka-u-funsika. Ulongo hiu unaniuluka. Muhi hiu udziniuluka makodza, unafua. Milalayangu ka-i-ka uma to, idzihenda niuluka, be n'enda nika-i-umise na moho. Kava utu yu na niuluko.
  **Niulurira,** *v.d.* Mameye yudzi-m-niulurira hombo, ni kiravo kikulu.
**Niuma,** *adj.* *See* Soena; Soenera; Sia. (K.) Backwards, behind. Kala niuma yangu, Be, or get, behind me. Kua niuma, Behind.
  **Niumase,** *adv.* *See* Titimuka; Thiaka. Afterwards; lit. their behinds; but the poss. pron. pl. Ze stands here in a general sense, without referring to the class of words it represents in other instances. Kua niuma hu-la-ko, kua mbere hu-enda-ko.
**Niumba,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Mbayumbayu. Lit. a building. From Ku umba. (1) The word is applied to the meanest hut of the natives as well as to the best houses of the Arabs on the coast. Dim., Kadzumba and Kidzumba.
(2) A nest when made of clay. Niumba ya mbayumbayu. Niumba ya mulonsi. *See* Kidzungi; Chumba.
**Niumbu,** *n.* (ya, za), the fruit of the mumbu.
**Niumbue** (Kid.), *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia) (= Tia), the giraffe. In Kid. both words are used, in Kir. only the latter.
**Niundo,** *n.* (ya, za), a hammer. Kakosa niundo mbiri za ku ansirua ni nduguye.
**Niungo,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lungo.
**Niungu,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) (in Kid. = Pfugo in Kir., and Mdungi in Kij.), an earthenware pot. Ku chita niungu ya wari. *See* Futu. Dim., Kadzungu and Kidzungu; magn., Dzungu (pl. Mi-).
(2) Locust. Ku piga niungu. *See* Kiravo.
**Niuni,** *n.*, a bird. Nidzipigua ni niuni mudzo; (1) lit. I have been struck by a good bird, *i.e.* I have had a good omen from birds (*see* Ku era niuni); (2) generally, I have been fortunate, lucky. Nidzipigua ni niuni mui, (1) I have had a bad omen from birds; (2) generally, I have been unfor-

*Footer: 311*

---

## [PDF Page 325 — Dictionary Page 312 (Niu — Noa)]

  tunate, unlucky. Note: In observing birds, seeking an omen, the Kig. word Ku theja is more frequently used. When they say, Nidzikuenda na niuni mui, or, mudzo, the expression is merely figurative, and does not imply the actual observing of birds, but meaning, I have been unlucky or lucky (= Nidzikuenda na muthana mui, or, mudzo). Even the word Mulungu is often used in the same sense. Dim., Kadzuni.
**Niunira,** or **Gnignira,** *v.a.*, to strew, to sprinkle. Muhaso wa unga ni ku niunira. Ku niunira m'dzuzi (= ku muagiza). Niunirani mdzuzi, hurie wari.
**Niuniua,** *v.n.* (= Umande mdzefu; Dzudzua; Umande mbomu).
**Niusi, Niuzi,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luzi.
**Niuya,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), light, not heavy. Nguo niuya. Nguo hi ni niuya. Nioga ni niuya, or, ni veveya. Kuna kavu niuya, ikayo yuya. Kavu hi ni niuya.
**Nivini,** or **Nivinini** (also **Niyoni**), expressions used when the proper name of a thing is not recollected at the moment.
**N'ka,** instead of **Nika.** *See* Chererua.
**Nkathio.** Mutu yuna nkathio hiyu, yuna-dzi-kathia muno. Na-we una nkathio muno; utu utite ukathie, ukale ubomu, be una nkathio muno.
**Nkoba** (Ngoba?). Nkoba ni ya Muganga. Mutu akenda charo, akaruma aka lavisira. Mudai a uke njirani, kisiki na mika na vi uke njirani, niama musiru a uke kanda.
**Nkoera,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Ngoera?), mistletoe. Nkoera kungi inamera mukomani hebu mudza nini.
**Nkoko.** Yudzi vavika nkoko niongo.
**Nkore.**
**Nkolokolo,** *n.*
**Nkua.** Udzisundula muriango nkua-wa Abe Gunja. Yudzibananga mali-nkua-ya mutu musiku. Yudzipiga gnombe-nkua. Ni yani Ni yaani? Resp., Ni ya gnania. Yudziulaga kuku-nkua, wa gnania musiku. Yudzipiga muana nkua, wa gnania musiku. Mumondo-nkua, wa gnania.
**Nkuadu,** *n.* *See* Mkuadu.
**Nkue,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Mkue). *See* Ombosa; Mbiriri. Father-in-law or mother-in-law.
**Nkue,** or **Ngue,** *n.* (ya, za). Mu-kasire, hata asise io nkue, or hio nkue. Vatu hivo ni nkue mbidzo (= ni kutu kure).
**N'na.** Contracted from Ni-na, *q.v.*
**Noa,** *v.n.*, to drink. Der., Manoadzi; Munoadzi; Unoadzi.
  **Noeka,** *v.n.*, to be drinkable. Musua hiu ka-u-noeka, u-moho; uvose, u-vole, be hupate kunoa to.
  **Noera.** *See* Bumira.
  **Noerera.** Vibaria viangu uka-ni-noerere uwe, mimi sindakudza. Nanoerera dzulu, sidzangue ku kuera na kibaria, I am drinking it above, I do not yet ascend with the calabash. The toddy which at first flows from a newly tapped tree is so little that the tapper drinks it on the tree. Kavana kibaria cha ku noerera uchi, hala udzumburire, little, or, uanamire, much.
  **Noesa, Nosa,** *v.a.*, to make drink, to water, to irrigate. Hudzi-m-noesa mui, ela kakanoa, kavana chumbe. Ni mukongo sana, kaidima ku guira m'egnie, hu-mu-noese. N'enda, nikanoese minasi yangu, nika-yo-niala.
  **Noesera,** *v.d.* Enda, uka-m-noesere, m'egniewe kavo.
  **Noeserua,** *v.p.*

*Footer: 312*

---

## [PDF Page 326 — Dictionary Page 313 (Nog — Nsi)]

  **Noesua,** *v.p.* Minasiyo idzinoesua kare, anao adzi-ku-noesera.
  **Noewa,** *v.p.* *See* Hungue.
**Nognona,** *v.n.*, to whisper. Kuku ananognona. Ku gomba porepore ndo ku nognona. Sikasikira adzovio gomba, adzinognona vara-tu.
  **Nognonera,** *v.d.*, to whisper to. Yudzi-m-nognonera muyawe maneno (= Yudzi-m-nognonesa maneno).
  **Nognonerana,** *v. reit.* Lola! kuku ananognonerana, anaroda ageni andakudza.
  **Nognoneza,** *v.a.*, to whisper. Gnania yudzi-ku-amba-dze? Resp., Kaka-ni-amba utu. Ela sidzi-mu-ona, aki-ku-nognonesa e? Resp., Yudzi-ni-amba geri: machero huende kutu kusiku. Ah-nidzi-mu-ona adi.
  **Nognonezana,** *v. reit.*, to whisper to each other. Atu hara ana.
  **Nognonezera,** *v.d.* Nidzi-mu-ona gnania aki-ku-iha, aka-ku-nognonesera, yudzi-ku-amba dze?
**Nognona,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Koloma). *See* Guuika. Lit. a whispering one, a cocoa-nut not quite ripe. Nazi hi ni nognona, inasuka kurekure.
**Nola,** *v.a.*, to sharpen. Der., Nolo.
  **Nolua,** *v.p.*, to be sharpened.
  **Noreka.** Nidzinola, kidzinoreka, kinaria.
  **Norera,** *v.d.* and *instr.* Nolo ri luavi? ninorere kidzoka changu.
  **Norerua,** *v.p.*
**Nolo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Manolo), any stone used for sharpening instruments.
**Nona,** *v.n.*, to be fat.
  **Nionia,** *v.a.*, to fatten. Dzi hio inanionia gnombe. Gnania yuna mukono wa ku nionia mufugo. Muana hiyu udzi-m-nionia m'egnie, ku-m-kanire, udzi-m-rijira muiri.
  **Nonera,** *v. rel.* Gnombe hi yudzinona, hata yudzinonera dzi. Makumio ga maneno.
**Nona,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a bird. Yun'enda dzi ku dzudzurira, kauruka ku bua muhini, yubuadzitu; yuna malo sana, kidza ui muerefu. Yuihua nona kua ku nona. Anae u-a-guire udzanga, ka-dza-sisimala, akisisimala kaguirika kaviri.
**Nongo,** *n.* (ya, za), dirt. Nongo za chanda.
**Nsambaraho.** *See* Ndzambaraho.
**Nsao,** *n.*, a bullock.
**Nsara,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Meguka.
**Nsiche,** or **Nsige,** *n.*, a locust.
**Nsiho,** *adj.*, heavy; (K.) villous. Niere nsiho. Niukue nsiho, Heavy ropes; sing. Lukue lusiho. Kavu nsiho, A heavy basket; pl. *id.* Nguo nsiho, A heavy cloth; pl. *id.*
**Nsima, Nzima,** *adj.*, whole, sound, well. Dzi nzima, The whole land. Nazi nzima, A whole cocoa-nut, in contradistinction to Kivo. Kunsa nzima, A sound measure, *i.e.* the vessel. Niungu nzima, A sound pot.
**Nsmo,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) (= in Kins., Ndzumo; Kij., Watoto), a saying, a name, *especially* a nickname. Nsimo ndio simo kua kidzomba. Ndivo nsimo hio yavokudza.
(2) (= Ndumo in Kir.; in Kid. and Kidigo it means a jest, a sport). Kid., Anache ana nsimo zao za ku sisika na vivo, wana simozao za ku tesa na vifuvu via nazi. Ku fumba nsimo. Ni nsimo sani so u henda so? Maneno ga nsimo neno ra fimbo. Nsimo za kare simia?
**Nsinga,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Kilingo in Kid. and Kidango in Kij.), lit. that which goes round. From Ku singa. A ring made in binding the vanda. Yudzifunga vanda to, nzinga ni mbidzo. Yudzifunga nsinga mbiri, tahu, etc.

## [PDF Page 327 — Dictionary Page 314 (Nsi — Nun)]

**Nsingo,** *n.* (ya), to go round about, the place behind anything. From Ku singa. Of persons, Niuma must be used. Yudzikuenda nsingo ya niumba, He has gone behind the house, or cottage. Sunguluka vo nsingo, Go there behind. Yusunguluka nsingo ya muhi, aka-dzi-fidza. Nsingo ya kasha, Behind the box.
**Nsinsikiro,** *n.*, (K.) intimation. Maneno ga nsinsikiro (= Maneno ga ku elekania, ga ku dzesia atu - kama ndumo). Nsinsikiro sa akili.
**Nsoya,** *n.*
**Nsumirua,** *n.* (= Ganga). Muganga wa nsumirua.
**Nsusua,** *n.* Machero kuna nsusua.
**Nuka,** *v.n.* *See* Wari; Rufu; Lofu; Nuna; Numfa. To smell. Prov., Aivi ka nuka, Thieves don't smell.
  **Nudza,** *v.a.*, (1) to smell. Nidzinu dza niama hi, ka-i-dza ola, ina nuka to. Nudza tumbaku hi, u-i-sikise jamba ni mbidzo, nigule.
  (2) To take snuff. Ku nudza tumbaku. Sina tumbaku ya ku nudza, jamba unayo, ni-pe, ninudze.
  **Nudzia,** *v.a.* *See* Kigniafungo. To make smell, to scent.
  **Nudzika,** *v.n.* Tumbaku hino ni mbidzo, inanudzika, ela hino ni mbi, ka-i-nudzika.
  **Nudzira,** *v.d.* Nidzi-ku-nudzira, nidziona ni mbidzo, guladu, sihende fingi moyoni.
  **Nudzua,** *v.p.* Tumbaku yangu idzinudzua ni atu angine, hata kiko ni kivuvu hiki.
  **Nukira.**
  **Nukirua,** *v.p.* Nanukiruani ufumba, simania kuko u-nuka-ko. Nanukirua ni utu, simania kuko u-la-ko.
**Numfa,** *v.a.* Ku numfa niama.
**Nuna** (Kidigo), *v.n.* and *a.* (= Ku amba luambo in Kir.), to backbite.
**Nugnunika,** *v.n.*, to murmur, to grumble. Nidzisikira atu, ananugnunika, kunadza atu, hebu ni atu ajirao njirani? Resp., Anadza kuku; or, Anadza vava hu-ri-vo.
  **Nugnunikira,** *v.d.* and *rel.*, to murmur, to grumble to and for. Maneno higo si-ga-hensi, ku-ni-nugnunikira atu. Sihende uki-ni-nugnunikira atu, ukikala kuhensi, basi gomba: "Sihensi sindahenda," ela kura ku nugnunika, u-ni-nugnunikira-ni?
**Nundu,** *n.* (ya, za), (K.) exuberance, protuberance. Ah! nawe una nunchu vio dza ya gnombe! Udzihenda nundu dza ya muniau! Gnania yuna nundu dza ya paka. Gnania yudzihenda kiharusi hata yudzihenda nundu. Dim., Kinundu.
**Nundu,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a bat. Kana a-ri-ko, ni nundu. Ak'enda, kua niuni, wambua: Mava una-go, unauruka, be mbana una meno; be ku mbari yehu we, He is not there; he has a protuberance; if he goes to birds, he is told, "Wings thou hast, with them thou fliest, but how is it with thy teeth? Well, thou art not of our kindred." Basi akauya, akakuenda kua niama a-ri-o na meno, ela kana mava; nao aka-mu-amba: Meno una-go, unahafuna, be mbona una mava, unauruka; be ku mbari yehu. Basi kua achena mava akisolua, na kua achena meno na-ko akisolua. Basi ni ku vevaveva tu, ku angalala njirani; yu-kahikahi; ndosa aihue nundu. Ah-we muana! undakala-dze we? undakala dza 'ye nundu. Unga nundu we, kusagala vamenga; kuna u-ri-vo, u-nundu.

**Nungu,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the hedgehog.
**Nusu** (Kij.), *n.* and *adv.*, half.

## O.

**O,** the fifteenth letter of the alphabet, uniformly pronounced as *oo* in "foot."—[ED.]
**O,** *rel. particle* to the pl. A- and the sing U-. *See* Musafihi; Derasega; Koma; Gota; Ngologo-o; Ela-o; A-na-o; Muana-o; etc. Ao, They.
**Oa** (Kidigo), *v.a.*, to take shelter. Ku oa mvula (= Kir., Ku-dzi-fidza mvula; in Kid., Ku zama mvula), To take shelter from rain.
**Oboza,** *v.a.*, an agricultural term, to abut on, to meet, to join a piece of ground previously cultivated. Yudzirima hata yudzi-ni-oboza.
  **Obozana,** *v. reit.*, to abut one on another. Adzirima hata adziobozana.
**Ocha,** *v.a.* (= Ku oka in Kij.), to broil, to roast.
  **Ochera,** (1) *v.d.* Hala niama yangu, u-ni-ochere.
  (2) Ku ochera muhi. Na ochera muhi, ubue, ni-u-hende kuni. Naochera muhi, ufue-usahenda peho mundani.
  **Ocherua,** *v.p.* Nidziocherua niama ni gnania.
  **Ochua,** *v.p.* *See* Gansa. To be broiled, to be roasted.
**Odi.** Ku dieka odi. Uso uki-u-losa-dzi, u-segere, basi udzidieka odi. Udzidieka odi, una-ni?
**Odola,** *v.a.*
**Odzania,** *v.a.* (in Kig., Odza = Dzola), to put together. Ku odzania via (= ku-vi-ika to vamenga). Naodzania misigo yangu, nienende. Na-mu-ona akiodzania via-vie; kumba yudzidzama. Mutu hiye na-mu-isa; ela nidzidzoka ku-m-londa; si-mu-odzania; nik'enda ka-vo tu. Gnania ni muerevu wa ku vaana; yuna madzo ga ku ona mifiu hata Mukamba ka-mu-odzania.
  **Odzanika,** *v.n.* Kaodzanika; kaoneka muiriwe.
**Oga,** *n.* (wa), fear, timidity, apprehension. Ogawe a-ri-o-na-o, be yu nga mimi, kuani nami ni muoga.
  **Ogofia, Ogovia,** *v.a.*, to frighten.
  **Ogova,** *v.a.*, to fear, to dread.
  **Ogovana,** *v. reit.*
  **Ogovewa,** *v.p.*, to be feared.
**Ogola,** *v.a.* and *v.n.*, to turn round. Ku ogola kidzoa. Mu-ogole muyao pfugo, i-kombokombo. Njira ikaogola, ikauya na hiva.
  **Ogoka,** *v.n.*, to turn. Dzua ridziogoka. Njira idziogoka.
  **Ogorera,** *v. rel.* Ku ogorera mbere. Ku ogorera niuma.
**Oha,** *v.a.* *See* Mfuma. (K.) To bask. Ku oha dzua. Ku oha moho.
  **Oheka,** *v.n.* Moho hiu ka-u-oheka, unadzoma, ni mungi. Dzua rinaaka dza moho muiri unaakaka, dzua hiri ka-ri-oheka.
**Oka, 1,** *v.n.*, to bathe. Kavana madzi ga ku oka, ni machache, ka-ga-nda hu-dzusa. Madzi gana, uki-ga-oka, ganawawisa.
  **Okeka,** *v.n.* *See* Udugu. Kifua hicho kina mamba, ka-va-okeka.
  **Okerera,** *v.n.*, to swim.
  **Okeresa,** *v.a.*
  **Okesa,** *v.a.*, to bathe. Ku okesa kironda, To bathe a wound or sore.
  **Okeseka,** *v.n.* Muhoho hiyu kaokeseka kua oga, sodi u-m-guire.
  **Okesua,** *v.p.* Firangise ka-zi-dza okesua.
**Oka, 2,** *v.n.* (= Gokomoka in

## [PDF Page 329 — Dictionary Page 316 (Oka — Omu)]

  Kij.), to retch, to vomit. Yunaoka-yulonda ku vavika. Nidzeria kitu, moyo udzi-ni-erera, nidzioka, ela sika vavika.
**Oka, 3,** *v.* (Kij.) (= Ocha in Kir.), to broil, to roast.
**Okola,** *v.a.*, to save, to rescue, to deliver. Gnania ndiye adzaye-ni-okola, na kuamba si iye, ni-nga fua. Gnania yudzi-ni-okola utu ubomu, nari ninairua, nikilonda madeni ku avaha, sikabada, hata u'enda kua gnania musiku, ndiye adzie-ni-okola; nidzikuenda riva, basi moyo udzi-ni-bua (= udzi-ni-hurira).
  **Okoka,** *v.n.* *See* Afiwa; Afu; Hehera. Niungu zangu, na-zo-umba, na-zi-dzoma, sikiokoka, kava menga ikayo banangika. Mutu ayelongosua kuenda kikaheni, kiravo kikisa-m-guira, ndiye aambuaye: yudziokoka.
  **Okolia.** Ku dzi okolia.
**Ola,** *v.n.*, to corrupt, to get putrid. Niama hio idziola, basi inanuka. Der., Olovu.
  **Osa, Oza,** *v.n.*, to decay. Niama hio idziosa ni muansa i-chari mbidzo mbidzo.
  **Osera, Ozera,** *v. rel.* *See* Gota; Kota? To decay to or in anything.
**Oloha,** *v.n.* *See* Bu. To point to, in scoffing. Yudzi-ni-oloha na lurimi; or, Yudzi-ni-lafira lurimi, kuamba niambue ni mulongo. Der., Muoloho.
  **Olohana,** *v. reit.*, to point at each other in scoffing. Atu hio adzifiererana, adziolohana, hata adziasa ku pigana mikutulo.
  **Olohera,** *v.d.* Nidzi-mu-olohera na chala, hata yudziona. Aalamula mabendeleano udzioloherua na lurimi.
**Olovu,** *adj.*, soft, mild. Der., Cholovu; Muolovu.
**Ombola,** *v.n.*, to come forth. Dzua ridziombola, The sun has risen.
  **Omborera,** *v.d.* Hudzikuenda, ela kaka-hu-ona, hata huka-a-omborera hivi vevi, uso na madzo.
  **Omborerana,** *v. reit.* Atu adziomborerana vatu vasiku, akapigana.
  **Omborerua,** *v.p.* Nidzi omborerua ni mugeni.
  **Omboza,** *v.c.*, to let or cause to come forth. Ku omboza dzua.
**Ombosa, Omboza,** *v.a.* (= Lafia), to make go out. Nidziomboza peho kififironi, idzila bia. Hudzirima nkue hata hudzi-i-omboza (= hata hudzi-i-upusa; hata hudzi-i-sisa).
**Omeka,** *v.a.* *See* Moyo; Kande. To stuff up, to fill up, to stuff into; (K.) cram. Madzi ganaira, hala dzafue, uomeke. Ku omeka niono, ni ku hala niono u-dza-zo bunda, ukabuma niunguni, ku chita mafuha. Gnania akaomeka vitu via kare na kare, vi-vavo. Ni m'omu huya! Ni maneno ga ku-m-shirika. The word is sometimes used in contempt for Ku ria and Ku buma.
**Omola,** *v.a.* Nidziomola mababayu, hata ndani yangu dele. Yudziomola wari vava, hata akaukuha, ndo akaenenda-ni mudude kuria iye hiye!
**Omoka,** *v.n.* (= Komoka; Bamfuka; Banduka; Ganduka), to tumble to pieces. Niungu hi ni mbidzi, idziomoka, or, idzikomoka. Niumba ya Musungu yaomoka vatu vamenga (= yakomoka). Nidziumba niungu, nidziika, idziomoka; ulongo hiu ni ui.
  **Omokera,** *v. rel.* Niunguyangu idziomoka, idzi-ni-omokera magansani muangu.
**Omu,** *adj.* (rel. to the U- class). *See* Kifuluzi. Dry, hard. Uchi hiu u-chari omu, ka-u-

## [PDF Page 330 — Dictionary Page 317 (Omu — Ond)]

  dza luama, or, ka-u-dza kala uolofu. Der., Ch'omu; M'omu; Niomu.
**Omu,** *n.* and *adj.* Mutu hiye yuna omu wa moyo (= yuna umiria). N.B.—The word is irregular in both of its uses as adjective and noun, in not receiving the usual *u*, which, with words beginning with a vowel, becomes *w*.
**Ona,** *v.a.* *See* Cho; Kisinde; Mulagusi. To see. In the neg. of the imperf., Wene is used beside the regular form Onere; *e.g.* Udzavokuenda ku-mu-wene (= ku-mu-onere)? When you went, did you not see him or her? Udzikuenda, udzi-mu-ona? Resp., Si-mu-wene, or, si-mu-onere. Ku ona haya, To be ashamed. Ku ona usinisi, To get sleep.
  **Onana.** Udziona-ni we? What have you seen?
  **Oneka,** *v.n.* *See* Nioka; Dubani. To be visible. Muezi unala hata dzungu yunaoneka, The moon shines so brightly that even a dzungu, a very small ant, can be seen.
  **Onekana.**
  **Onera.** Na-m-lasira uchi musenangu, dziku io ni-mu-onere ngari kadzama. Uchi hiu nidzi-ku-onera, humira kasi so. Yudzi-ni-onera huruma hebu mbazi.
  **Onerera.** Nidzi-mu-onerera, be sika-m-zola, angakudzaria. Adzi-hu-onerera, be akakimbirari.
  **Onerua,** *v.p.*
  **Onewa,** *v.p.* *See* Kidia; Nga. To be seen.
  **Onia,** *v.a.*, to make see, to show, to warn. Nidzi-mu-onia, kaona. Ngua hi idzifumua midaramidara, inaonia. A-ngahewa ulongo, nere, nidzimania kare; gnania ndiye adzaye-ni-onia na lurimi; ndiye aduiwe.
  **Oniesa,** *v.c.*
  **Oniua,** *v.p.*, to be shown, warned. Mutu akioniua ni ku ona, ela mbiriri ka-zi-hama.
  **Onua,** *v.p.* *See* Kidia.
**Onda,** *v.a.* (in Kij., *v.n.*, to taste = Ku dada in Kir.), to let taste, to try. Only used of medicine. The word has been introduced by the Aganga, who, in treating patients whose sickness is ascribed to the pepo, invariably speak in Kisuahili of the coast. Na-mu-onda muhaso (= Na-mu-gesa muhaso). Yudziondua muhaso (= Yudzigesua muhaso), He was trying a medicine.
**Onda,** *v.n.* *See* Niauka. To become lean. Kuonda kua makazi.
**Ondoka,** *v.n.* (= Kutuka in Kij.), to start, to move suddenly, to be frightened. In Kij., Ku ondoka means to get up, to leave one's place (= Ku uka in Kir.).
  **Ondosa,** *v.a.* (= Fumbulusa), to startle.
**Onsa, Onza,** *v.a.* *See* Dangadza, No. 5. Machero n'nadza nionse miansoyangu na kibaria. Muhambo uka-o-hega, basi ni ku onsa.
  **Onsera,** *v.d.* Nahega muhambo wangu hiva, be munda-ni-onsera, niama akiguirua, mufugule, niinike kahiri.
  **Onserera,** *v.a.*
  **Onsia, Onzia,** *v.a.* *See* Peho, 2. To make thin. Mashaka ari-go na-go gadzi-mu-onzia. Ndzala idzi-ni-onzia, Hunger has made me thin. Ukongo udzi-mu-onzia. Gnania yuna-dzi-onzia, kuamba asiambirue ahende kazi. Yuna-dzi-onsia kua ukaha, kuamba asihende makazi. Yudzi-dzi-onzia kua hali ya haya, He has humbled himself by reason of shame

## [PDF Page 331 — Dictionary Page 318 (Ond — Ono)]

  for a benefit received. *See* Haya.
  **Onsokaonsoka** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Ku dononoka).
  **Onsola,** *v.a.* Yuere, or, wari muchia, or, mutia, ela hangu dzana yuna-dzi-onsola, yunaukusha ndaniye. *See* Ufufi. Gnania wari mukongo, ela hangu dzana yuna-dzi-onsola, nidzi-mu-ona ak'enda mundani kuenda rima.
**Ondo,** *n.* (ra). *See* Luambe. The name of a species of high grass. Vatu hivo vana ondo, bomu, ka-va-rimika. Der., Chonsue; Chonda; Muondo.
**Onga,** *v.a.* *See* Ongera (Kins.). To reel, stagger, from the force of the wind, to increase. Maansa ku onga mbeyu.
  **Ongera.**
  **Ongereza.** Kilariro ni kitembe, be enda ukahege muhama, uongereze.
  **Ongerezeka** (= Ongeseka). Atu hara ere atembe, vino adziongereseka, adzikala angi.
  **Ongesa,** *v.a.*, to increase, to multiply. Kuamba kava cha ku ongeza, basi nahala hiki kichache.
  **Ongezeka,** *v.n.* *See* Dzulo.
  **Ongezera,** *v.d.* Rarely used. Yudzi hewa vitembe, be yunadza kua nduguye, ndiye adzaye-mu-ongesera (= adzaye-mu-ongesa).
  **Ongezerua,** *v.p.* Muniu-we uere mutembe, ela yudziongezerua, or, yudziongezua.
  **Ongezua,** *v.p.* Gnania ndiye adzayehenzua yudziongezua, ela mino kaka-ni-ongeza.
**Ongo,** *n.* (wa), the brains. Kuahula kidzoa, ongo ukala (= Kid., Uka furika).
**Ongola** (to be distinguished from Ku ngolangola), *v.a.* *See* Kongue. To lull, rock. Mu-hale muana, enenda naye ndze, uka-mu-ongole. Mu-ereke muana, uka-mu-ongole ko-ndze.
  **Ongoka,** *v.n.* Hudzi-a-niadira niama, aka-hu-onerera, be aka ongoka, akakimbira. Yudzidzoma niungu, sidziongoka, ka-zi-ka funsika, ulongowe ni udzo. Nidzihenda utu hiu, udzi-ongoka.
  **Ongokera,** *v.d.*, to grow up. Utuwangu udzi-ni-ongokera. Alume ndio ao-mu-ongokera, The sons, they grew up to her.
  **Ongokerua,** *v.p.* Gnania-muaka wa rero yudziongokerua ni mudze, yudzibada kilariro.
**Ongolo.** *See* Uongolo.
**Ongora,** *v.a.*, to lead in singing. Ngoi yuna ongora hiye! Ku ongora ni kuimba nimbo za muzuka.
  **Ongoreza,** *v.a.* (= Ngolangola), to soothe with kind words, to persuade, to wheedle. Yuere kahenzi ku enenda, basi nidzi-m-ongoreza mimi, hata yudzihenza. Navokudza nere sihenzi, ela gnania ndiye aye-ni-ongoreza, or, ngolangola, hata nikihenza.
  **Ongorezua,** *v.p.*
**Ongosa, Ongosha,** *v.a.* (= Ku henda to). Nidzifuma kivinda, 'dzi-ki-ongosa. Nidzihenda utu, nidziongosha. Der., Chonga; Chongua; Mongo.
  **Ongoseka,** *v.n.* Utu hiu ka-u-ndaongoseka.
  **Ongosera, Ongoshera,** *v.d.* Mufiere yudzi-ni-ongosera nenorangu. Muhondo nina kazi yangu, be uchi wangu ka-u-nda-timira, be namba: dziku hio u-ni-badire uchi, nidze, u-ni-avase, hebu unadeni? Resp., Na-hu ujaliwe tu, dziku hio, ukidza, nda-ku-ongosera.
  **Ongozerua,** *v.p.*, to have a thing well settled. Yudziongo serua nenore.
**Ononga** (Kigiriama), *v.a.* (= Bananga in Kir.).
