  **Onongeka,** *v.n.* (= Banangika).
**Onsa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). From Ku onda. Onsa ndiro m'isho wa makodza, ndo ri-ri-ro na suche.
**Onsa,** *v.a.* *See* Onda.
  **Onsera.** *See* Onda.
  **Onserera.** *See* Onda.
  **Onsia.** *See* Onda.
  **Onsola.** *See* Onda.
**Ora,** *v.a.*, (1)
(2) Moyo udzi-ni-ora vi, kuamba nikabige mutu, moyo mungine ukakania. Yudziorua orua muiri osi, wahendua ndzorandzora. Nidzihenda koro kuamba nikahehe na mutu, be kahiri moyo uka-ni-ora, nika-dzi-uda; basi nikaricha nikasa kuenda.
  **Orua,** *v.p.* Nidziorua ni moyo, n'enda nikahende utu usiku. Nidziorua ni moyo.
**Ora,** *v.a.*, (K.) appointed. Ni orewe o, yunaguisa mbazi. Ni orewakue muakawe rero. Ah! ni ore wangu, nindahenda-dze? Ndo Mulungu adzofio-ni-pa, ku fuererua ni atu gisigisi yunashononeka. Ni ore wangu hio, nidzi-u-ona mimi.
**Oria** (for **Uoria**), *n.* (wa) (= Ugoza in Kij.), the fibrous bark of the m'uoriam'oria. Oria wa ku fungira mihi. Oria wa ku vagarira niumba.
**Oromocha** (Kid.), *v.n.*
**Osa,** *v.n.* *See* Ola.
**Osi,** *adj.*, all.
**Ovoloe.** *See* Uvolue.
**Oya,** *v.n.*, to rest. Yudzefua, yudzikuenda oya mashaka, ka-nda-ga-ona kahiri. Naoya; nidzidzoka, I rest, for I am tired. Naoya, nidieke vilungo. Niuchi anaoya.
  **Oyera,** *v. rel.*, to rest at. H'endeni hukaoyere mbere, Let us go and rest further on.
  **Oyesa, Oyeza,** *v.c.* *See* Erikera. To cause to rest, to relieve.
  **Oyesana, Oyezana,** *v. reit.*, to relieve, to assist one another, to let one another rest.
  **Oyesua, Oyezua,** *v.p.*, to be made to rest. Yudzioyezua ni nduguye.

## P.

**P,** the sixteenth letter of the alphabet, often represented by *b*; but the pronunciation is quite English.—[ED.]
**Pa,** *v.a.* (1st pers. sing. imp. of the verb Ku va, To give). Ni pa, Give me. Va becomes Pa in this case only. Ni-pa mukono, Give me your hand; but, Yudzi-mu-va mukono, He gave him his hand. Ka-ka-ni-pa, He has not given me. Yudzi-ni-pa, He has given me. U-mu-ve, or merely, Mu-ve, Give him or her. Ni-ku-ve, hebu nisi-ku-ve? Shall I give thee or not? Hu-ve, Give us; or, U-hu-ve, Mayest thou give us. Yudzi-hu-va, He or she has given us. Azungu aokudza adzi-mu-va mikahe hebu dze? Kaka-hu-va. N'a-ve, for, Ni-a-ve, Shall I give them? A-ve, Give them. Nidzi-a-va, I have given them.
**Padu,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lupadu.
**Padza,** *n.*, twins. Ana padza, She has twins. Ana hio adzifialua padza. Ana padza-akiokoka osi-ankue: babe yao, or, abe yao, yundafua, hebu ameyao yundafua kuani anadzimba adziookoka osi.
**Pafu, Pavu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Fulo. The lungs. Pavu ni hira irio hovuhovu.
**Pagadza,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Pagacha in Kij.), a basket.
**Pagna** (= Puagna).
**Pahasi** (Kidigo), *n.* (in Kij., Pabasi (K., Papasi); in Kir., Kimfamfani), the name of an insect, the bite of which is said to cause a fever.

## [PDF Page 333 — Dictionary Page 320 (Pak — Peh)]

**Paka,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a cat. Paka muitu, Wild cat.
**Pala,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luvala. Adzipigua pala. Adziniolua pala. Mvala pala.
**Pala,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the gazelle. Dim., Kivala.
**Palahi** (= Kongolo).
**Palala** (Kid.), *n.* (= Mbuda in Kir.; Panara in Kij.), a bird. It makes a noise with its wings, but does not sing.
**Palamamba,** *n.*, the name of a fish.
**Palamanche,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Kolonche in Kid.; Chengere in Kins.), a sauce or curry made of peas and beans of all sorts. Mboga za podzo na kunde na mbalazi-ndizo sihendazo palamanche.
**Palapanda,** *n.* (ya, za), the horn of the nausi, when used for blowing. It is smaller than the gunda. In former times the Gniere were not allowed even to touch these instruments, while now they may be used by any one.
**Palo,** *n.* (ya, za). Niama hiyu yuna palo muno.
**Pamba,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luhamba.
**Pambo,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a species of ants. Pambo ni adune to; ana vidignio.
**Pamfu,** *n.* *See* Kilolua. Mutu hiye yuna pamfu na ageni. Musichana huya kana pamfu. Bahadi ya wa nme.
**Panche** (Kid.), *n.* (= Pandiso in Kir.; in Kij., Pandio). *See* Panche in Kins. Notches cut in a palm tree, in which the feet are placed in climbing.
**Panda.** *See* Banda.
**Panda,** *n.* (ya, za), a bough. Panda mbidza, A green bough; green boughs. Panda mbifu; or, Panda pfu, A ripe or dry bough, or boughs. *See* Ludahi. Dim., Kibanda.
**Pande,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luvande.
**Pandiso,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Ku. Ku piga pandiso.
**Pandue,** *n.* (ya, za). Mutu muche hiyu yuna pandue bomu panduese sinarira muno.
**Panga,** *n.* (ya, za). Sing. Panga (ya iwe); pl. Panga (za mawe). Dim., Kapanga or Kavanga, and Kibanga or Kivanga; magn., Rivanga (pl. Mivanga).
**Panga,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luvanga. (1) A sword.
(2) A vulture.
**Pango,** *n.* (ya, za), a hole in a tree or in a tooth, a cave. Pango ni mua muhi na mua dzino. Sing. Pango ya muhi; pl. Pango za mihi. Dzino rangu ridzihenda pango. Dim., Kapango and Kipango; magn., Ripango or Rivango (pl. Mi-).
**Pani,** *n.* (za) (Kig., Pangule). *See* Pinda; Kavu; Gnongo. Pl. of Luvani.
**Pania,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a rat.
**Pansa,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). *See* Muleli; Kidzudzu. The name of a bird.
**Papa,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a). *See* Kolekole. A shark.
**Papadzi,** *n.* Menoge gakaerekana, gana papadzi.
**Pare.** *See* Kifudu.
**Pau,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class). *See* Abau. A good many. Obs. Mudzi hiu una niumba pau, This village has many huts. Paulosi avolingilua ni nioka mukononi aka-m-dimfa mohoni.
**Payo,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luvayo.
**Pegniegnio** (Kid.), *n.* (= Kibenge in Kij.).
**Pegnio,** *n.* (ya, za), a crevice, a loophole, an aperture. From Ku vegnia. Pegnio inalangala. Naricha kasidi pegnio ya ku lafira mosi, vatu va magaruba mairi. Niumba ina pegnio, inafumuka. Dim., Kavegnio and Kivegnio; magn., Vegnio and Rivegnio.
**Pehe,** *n.* (ya, za), a ring. Dim., Kavehe; magn., Rivehe (pl.

## [PDF Page 334 — Dictionary Page 321 (Peh — Pep)]

  Mi-). These are being left off; Vibuli and Mikufu are preferred.
**Peho,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) wind. Pl. of Luveho (also used as a sing., as the following instances will show). Peho za muaka. Peho za furi. Peho za muaka sidzigaluka. Peho sikari, or, Sichari za muaka. Rero peho inafuma sana kuna kusi. Peho bomu idzilamuka, ya kas'kasi. Peho hi nayo idzisidi. Peho dzana yafuma hata ikignola mihi. Peho ya dzana yayofuma, mua-i-sikira hebudze? Hua-i-sikira yajira peho bomu sana.
(2) *See* Mufui; Dangamuka; Chari. Coolness, cold. Trop., quietness, weakness, want of quickness and energy, spiritlessness. Peho ya muaka inaonsia atu. Niumba hino inasisima, ina peho. *See* Mfukuhi. Madzosi ga peho, Cold, *i.e.* silent tears. *See* Rira. Ku piga peho, To cool; trop., To get rest. Wari udzi piga peho, hurie. Musua hiu u-moho muno, huricheni punde, u-pige peho, usa-hu-dzoma makalakala. Mutu hiye wari akisirimia atu, be vino yudzefua, atu anda piga peho. *See* Mufua; Kavayo. Gnania yu-peho, kana kondo na mutu, Gnania is of a cool, quiet nature; he has no strife with anybody. Mutu hiyu yu-peho, kakadangamuka vilungo, yu-nga dza arie mukongo, This man is cold, spiritless; he is not sprightly as to his limbs, he resembles one who is sick. Mihi hira-tu-pehose ni mbidzo. Ndzoni hukasagale hivara peho ya muhi; muhi hura una peho mbidzo. Peho ya ku oya. Kuna peho ya maingu, gadzisia dzua.
(3) Shade, a sheltered place. Yudzihenda ivu ra pehoni, He has got a boil in the shade; *i.e.* on the thigh, as being shaded by one's cloth. Mikono midzano na peho (?) (= kasiku), Black muamba. Hu kale peho mmenga (?).
**Pekedze,** *n.* (ya, za), a small awl used in making arrows. From ku vekedza. Pekedze ni kadzidio ka ku vekedzera mifui.
**P'ekue,** *n.* *See* Puekue.
**Pembe,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) horn, tusk. Pembe za ndzofu, Tusks of elephants, which are distinguished as follows: (*a*) Bori, of the young male; (*b*) Ndzao, of the full-grown male; (*c*) Mugoma, of the female.
(2) *See* Puembe. A bird.
**Pengere,** *n.* Euphem. for Thaka (= Kugnio). N'enda pengere.
**Pengo,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Kig., Thegnia). *See* Luania; Ulume. A notch, a gap, the notch made by filing the teeth to sharp points. Ku kotua pengo. Kare atu ari akikotua pengo na ku dzodzua kiduro. Ukikala na pengo, hata ukilava, ukikala udziluma meno, kuidima ku hansula kanoa, basi ni ku bumua musua na pengoni ukafufuka.
**Peno,** *n.* (ya, za).
**Pepo,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kongue. An evil spirit. Pepo ni Mudzomba, udiye alondaye kikuku na hirisi i-ka-yo andikua na daradasi. Ela mulungu ni Munika yulonda urembo wa ushanga, na Mukuafi yulonda mukufu muiru na ngudu. Isilamu wa? Kisuahili? Pepo ya kidzomba yu sindikua baharini poani. Pepo mue yusindikua hiko kanda ya nika. Pepo ya muganga ku ongola kongue, Spirit of the muganga to take away sickness. A ka sarua hiva ufumba wa pepo ku dondua marinda makafiri. Asonga ni ela anafimza kihi changu muganga be kamu a sola? pl.

## [PDF Page 335 — Dictionary Page 322 (Per — Pin)]

  Ana chenguri mbi. Munemo wangu wa farasi wangu mu ni dagire wa ku rinda kihi changu—white fowl—rehisi yangu. Pepo ya mulume kanena!
**Pera,** *n.* (pl. Ma-), the guava. Madzere ga pera-za muaka (?).
**Perembe,** *n.* (ya, za), a kind of flute, made of the stalk of muhama.
**Pesa,** *n.* *See* Puesa. A fish.
**Pewo** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Pepo in Kir.).
**Pfihipfihi,** *n.* (= Budznaro).
**Pfu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class) (= Fu). *See* Komu; Koloma. Dry, hard, dead. Nazi pfu za muvala. Ni-rehera nazi pfu; si-ni-rehere nazi za manognona. Mbalazi sikala pfu, sinavururika, sinaarika. Pfuko ni pfu madzi kamuna gadzisira.
**Pfudu,** *n.* (= Mufudu).
**Pfuhi,** *adj.* *See* Kibele; Kibumbuana. Short.
**Pfuhupfu.** Niungu hi ka-i-kuangurika, ni pfuhupfu.
**Pfuigo,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Figo), the kidneys. Pfuigo yangu ina-ni-luma. Gnania yunalumua ni pfuigo.
**Pfuiho,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lufuiho.
**Pfuko,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Fuko). *See* Kagania. A bag.
**Pfumfu,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Fungu in Kij.), a portion, a part. Pfumfu sa baharini. Pfumfu za madzo (= Kij., Kogo za mato; Midzidzo mibomu in Kir.), Protruding eyes.
**Pfungo,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a) (= Fungo), the civet-cat. Pfungo akifumagua, ni ku luma mufui, aka-u-durura. Una usinsisi, unga dza wa pfungo. Yudzi kolosera niama ya pfungo, a-yo-ria.
**Pfuno,** *n.* *See* Funo.
**Pfupfu** (also pronounced **Fufu**), *adj.* (= Pudzu). *See* Kifumba. Narrow. Yudziaka niumba pfupfu, ka-i-i-na makolo. Nafaka pia.
**Pfupfu,** *adj.*, very dry.
**Pfuto,** *n.* (ya, za), some dry grass plucked off, used to catch fire. From Ku futa. Pfuto za niasi, za ku busira moho.
**Pia,** *adj. encl.*, new; (K.) all, whole, entire, total. Nguo pia, A new cloth. Mbira pia, A fresh grave. Mfaya pia.
**Pia.** *See* Bia.
**Pidza.** *See* Piza.
**Piero,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lufiero.
**Piga.** *See* Biga.
**Piliwi,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a kind of grasshopper. Piliwi ndio arisa a nioe, ni asunie a nioe. Dim., Kibiliwe.
**Pil'pili,** *n.*, red pepper. Pil'pili manga, Black pepper.
**Pima,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Azango; Dikisa. A fathom, a measure, a weight. Pima sisi yudzifika (= Kiasi kiki yudzifika and Kibindi hiki yufika (Kid.), and Kara yudzifika). Rero pima hizi yudzifika Kisiwani. Dzana pima hizo wari yudziuka. Machero-huki ajaliwa-pima hizo-hundakala hudziingira Taita. Yudzi ni pima nguvu (migniana).
**Pinda,** *n.* (ya, za), a large bag, made of milala. Dim., Kavinda; magn., Vinda and Rivinda.
**Pindi,** *n.*, a winding, a wriggling, a turn. Nidzi-m-vesa pindi sana bomu. Pindi hio yudzifika kure. Dim., Kapindi and Kipindi.
**Pindilo,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) the binding round arrows made by boys of the stalks of Guinea-corn, serving to fasten the lomba; also the binding round the ends of a bow. From Ku vinda. Pindilo ni za mifui ya maonsa, ya kihoho, ela mifui ya kifiere i-fungua na makano. Nafunga uhawangu pindilo, ni vinde.
(2) *See* Vendula. The grass bent down. Lolani pindilo-

*Footer: 322*

## [PDF Page 336 — Dictionary Page 323 (Pin — Pis)]

  silola-vi? Njira hi-pindilo silola mbere kuko huendako. Prov., Arie mbere ndiye ausuaye pindilo.
**Pindo,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luvindo. Atu hia akafuala nguo, pindozao akavesera ku lume, or, ku modzo.
**Pindui,** *n.*, the act of turning head over heels, a somersault. Ku piga pindui, To turn head over heels. Pindui ni ku muta kidzoa-dzi, ukabedukira kanda ya viri, A pindui is to fix your head on the ground, and then to turn over to the other side. Aravai a kare-mulume akifua, akizikua, hata akimala, basi alume akiuka mbirani-hara ache akakuenda, akapiga pindui; muchewe iye akayefua, na nduguse ache, na anae ache; ela hikara vika richua.
**Pingi,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the shrewmouse. Pingi na kuku na ninga niama hio ahahu adziambua: Uwe pingi! sidikanie njira, ukidikania njira, fua! Na-we kuku, ukinoa mdzi, sudi ulole dzulu mulunguni; na uwe ninga, na-we sikuedze dzi mudza ngani, ukikua dzi, na-we udzefua; basi ninga akifumagua na onsa, akikua dzi, kadia kaviri; naye ninga hata akilonda kunoa madzi, sudi adze na kidodo kivu, basi kidodo kikuse dzi, ela iye akale dzuluye, asikuse dzi; ndo ahendafio, The shrewmouse and the fowl and the ninga—those three animals have been told: thou pingi must not cross a path, for if thou crossest a path, thou wilt die! And thou, fowl, if thou drinkest water, be sure thou lookest above towards heaven; and thou ninga, light not on the ground, for if thou lightest on the ground, thou diest; well, the ninga, if he is shot with arrow, and falls to the ground, he recovers not again; and the ninga, even if he wants to drink water, he must be sure to come with a dry stick, then the stick may touch the ground, but he must be above it, he may not touch the ground. Thus it is that they do. Pingi akiona njira, basi ni ku uya niuma, ela chamba temoye idzifika ya kufua, basi ni ku dzupa njira, kana menga, akafua vavo. Mulomowe ni mure, dza wa dzange na wa kiholo.
**Pingu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kotua; Kidanga. (1) Fetters. From Ku pinga. Ku kotua pingu, To be put into fetters. This always refers to the people on the coast, the Wanyika having no such instrument, but only the gogo, which is of wood. Magn., Vingu; Rivingu.
(2) A charm. Pinguyo i-chire! Pingu ndio kihi cha pepo.
**Pingua,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kipingua. From Ku binga.
**Pirua,** *n.*, ants.
**Pishi,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) (Kij.), a measure, a roughly made bowl, which contains about five pounds of grain. There is no standard. The term Muana paromu is also given to the wanting measures. (*a*) Kuna pishi yegnie, bomu. (*b*) Kuna pishi ya maujudi, ndio abimirayo ku kenga atu. (*c*) Kuna pishi ya mua kibekule ndio tide muno.
(2) (Kid.). Ku dzinsa pishi.
**Pisho, Bisho,** *n.* (only used with Mbi, quickly pronounced Pishombi, as one word), refractoriness, stubbornness, contrariety, unluckiness. From Ku bisha. Muana yuna pishombi hiyu! Charo hicho kina pishombi, ka-ki-hama, This journey is unlucky; it won't do. *E.g.* change when a man,

*Footer: 323*

---

## [PDF Page 337 — Dictionary Page 324 (Piz — Pug)]

  on setting out, repeatedly met with bad omens, which induced him to return. *See* Muthana.
**Piza,** or **Pidza,** *n.* (ya, za), tips of thorns from the muthungu tree, tied round the lomba, to secure a better chance of hitting. A practice of boys only when shooting after birds.
**Poa,** *n.* (ya), the coast. Ni poa. Poa hira. Poani. *See* Kala. On, to the coast.
**Podzo,** *n.* (ya, za), a kind of peas or vetches.
**Pogo,** *n.* (ya, za), a bend. Muhi hiu una pogo ukavogoka.
  **Pogopogo.** Muhi hiu una pogopogo.
**Pohe,** *n.* (za), bow-strings. Pl. of Luvohe.
**Poho,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a butterfly.
**Pola,** *n.* *See* Ku vula. Mildew. Only used in connection with Ku fua. To die of cold or damp = to lose its virtue. Tumbaku ikiingira peho, basi ni ku fua pola, Tobacco, when it becomes damp, loses its flavour. Udzungu wa mufui udzefua pola kua peho, The poison of an arrow has lost its virtue by damp.
**Polokania,** *n.* (= Mfuma). Ku piga polokania, ni mufui ku upuka kanda ya viri. Nidzi-m-fumaga niama, mufui udzipiga polokania. Gnania yunafuha 'ye-yudzifumaga niama, yudzi-m-piga polokania.
**Polopolo,** *n.* (ya, za); in Kichaga, a musket (= Kundukui in Kir.). Yupigua polopolo. Adzomba apiga atu na polopolo, hata ukakala kure, ni ku-ku-piga.
**Pombe,** *n.* *See* Dumbu; Udzoro. Beer, made in various ways, sometimes from millet, sometimes from bananas, when it must be more like cider. Ku dzudza pombe.
**Pombolo,** *n.*, (1) (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the dolphin.
(2) (ya, za). Pombolo yangu idzi fomoka.
**Pondo,** *n.* (ya, za), a punting-pole. Pondo za ku pigira dalu.
**Ponolo,** *n.* (ya, za). Ponolo ni mihi ya ku vonorera makonche.
**Popo,** *n.* (ya, za), betel-nut. Popo ni za mubobo.
**Pore,** *adv.* *See* Wanguangu. (K.) Afterwards, order, regularity. Mbona unagomba pore, kulafia lulaka nikasikira? Mutu hiye, mariadzi ge ga pore. Mutu hiye, mariadzi ge ga haraka haraka ni mukafiri.
  **Porepore,** *adv.* *See* Nognona; Chignie. Slowly, gently.
**Puagna,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name of an animal. It lives in the cavities of rocks. The name is onomatop. from its cry: Kua-kua.
**Puamba,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Mukuamba).
**Puare,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia) (= Kuali in Kins.).
**Puasa,** *n.* (only used as predicate), seldomness, rareness. N.B.—The word is always pronounced in a high singing tone, the voice resting on the first *a*. Neno hiro ni ra puasa, ka-ri-gombua muno (= dubani). Kitu hicho ka-ki-oneka, ni puasa. Kitu hicho nidzi-ki-ona kua puasa.
**Puedza.** *See* Puesa.
**Pueka,** *n.* Pl. of Lubueka.
**Puekue,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kupuka. Weeds, tares. Pueke dzanga.
**Pueleo,** *n.* (ya, za), tongs, pincers. Musana yunaguira chuma na pueleo.
**Puembe,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), a bird, the toucan.
**Puesa, Pueza,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). Pueza yuna mijira minane.
**Pugu,** *n.* (ya, za), the hollow of a tree, the inside of which is

*Footer: 324*

---

## [PDF Page 338 — Dictionary Page 325 (Pui — Puz)]

  decayed. Muhi hiu una pugu.
**Puirua** (Kid.) (= Kinkowe in Kins.).
**Pujikombe,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a bird.
**Puku,** *n.* *See* Pania.
**Pukupuku,** *n.* (za), (1) crumbs. Pukupuku sa wari. Mudzeria wari, mudziricha pukupuku; mudzirichira-ni so pukupuku?
(2) Bricks. Pukupuku za madfali.
**Pula,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) the nose. From Ku fula.
(2) *See* Mdzudza. The eye of a yam, from which it germinates.
**Pula.** *See* Bula.
**Pulapula,** *n.* Gnania yuna pulapula muno. Ei! mtu yuna pulapula huya, yunafiola muno!
**Pulumuko,** *n.* (ya, za), a ravine; (K.) vale, valley. Pulumuko hi ni nire, This ravine is deep. Dim., Kabulumuko or Kavulumuko; magn., Rivulumuko (ra).
**Pumbu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Luje; Lukano.
**Pumsika.** *See* Bumsika.
**Pumu,** *n.* (ya). Yudiekua ni pumu. Pumuye idzi-m-dieka kawesa; ni mukongo wa pumu.
**Pumuzi,** *n.* (ya), breath. Naoya, pumuzi idzi-ni-kuera. Naoya, nidieke pumuzi.
**Punda,** *n.* *See* Dorosa.
**Punde,** *adv.* *See* Hensekesa; Rindikisa; Tindi; Rasi; Husa; Peho. After, afterwards. Bomu punde.
  **Pundepunde,** *adv.* *See* Kiruvu. Somewhat less.
**Punga,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luvunga.
  **Pungapunga,** *n.* (ya, za), a small unripe cocoa-nut in its first stage of growth. Nidzigema, pungapunga sidzebua. (1) Pungapunga. (2) Kidagna. (3) Kidale. (4) Dafu. (5) Koloma. (6) Nazi. (7) Muvala.
**Pungire,** *n.*, a swoon, consternation. Ku fua pungire. Gnania yudzipigua, yudziburua, hata yudzefua pungire. Nidzefua pungire kua oga.
**Pungu,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a bird; (K.) Cuntas vulture. Pungu yuria nioka na makobe na miakaka na madzonsoka, na mamfaramfara na puku, etc. Pungu ni mbomu dza kosi.
**Pungua,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Karamua? in Kij.), a decrease. From Ku vunga. Mu-hendere pungua (= mu-vunge), ndivo andavo hurira; ana damaa.
**Pungufu** (Kij.), *adj.*, defective. Akilize ni pungufu (= chacha in Kir.).
**Pungulu** (Kid., = Kidzere; Kitite).
**Pupu,** *n.* (ya, za), a kind of bean, somewhat smaller than the mabawa. Pupu singa mabawa, ela zo ni tide. Muhiwe ni mububu (= Dzi ya Kidui (in Ukambani) ina pupu ningi). In Kig. they are called Mbumbu. Si-henza kutu ku-si-ko mvula ningi dza Ukambani; siki nialua kuehu, ni ku nona muno, sikahambala, be ka-si-fiala muno, ni ku fua, They like a place where there is not much rain, as Ukambani. If planted with us, they will become too gross, and will not bear much.
**Puyi,** or **Puyu,** *n.* (za), fibres. Pl. of Luvuyi or Luyuyu. Puyi za ukonde. Puyi za makumbi ga nazi.
**Puze, Pudze,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class). *See* Kifumba. Thin, narrow. Njira pudzu; but, Muhi muvudzu. Pembe pudzu, A thin horn, also pl. thin horns; thin tusks, of female elephants. Der., Kivudzu, Muvudzu, etc.

## [PDF Page 339 — Dictionary Page 326 (R — Ran)]

## R.

**R,** the seventeenth letter, pronounced as in English.—[ED.]
**Ra,** (1) *gen. part.*, of.
(2) *See* Goma. Sign of the imperf. tense.
**Rada** (?). Ku fua rada.
**Radi, Rathi** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), readiness, willingness. Yudzikuenda kua radi moyo ni muakue.
**Radi,** *adj.*, ready, willing. The particles are prefixed for the various persons; *e.g.*: Sing., 1st pers., Ni rathi, I am ready; 2nd, U-rathi, Thou art ready; 3rd, Yu-rathi, He is ready. Pl., 1st pers., Hu-rathi, We are ready; 2nd, Mu-rathi, You are ready; 3rd, A-rathi, They are ready. Ni-rathi, ukale rathi nawe. Muanangu yudzi kuenda hamba, ela mimi si rathi, yudzi henda ni thima, yudzienenda. *See* Mukoma.
  **Radira, Rathira,** *v.d.* (in Kig., Ku thauja). *See* Dzua, Nos. 5, 6; Usiri. To be ready to; *i.e.* to go to meet. Nikasikira, ndugu yangu yudzikudza, yu Kisiwani, be na-m-rathira.
  **Radirua, Rathirua,** *v.p.*
**Raha** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), rest, ease.
**Rahani** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Mfunga in Kir.), a pawn, a pledge. Nidziika rahani ya mufiu, nidzihala uchi kudza humira.
**Rahisi** (Kij.), *adj.* (= Rahasa), cheap.
**Rai** (Kij.), *v.a.* *See* Marai; Urai. To put morsels of food in a person's mouth as a mark of affection; (K.) guile.
**Raiwa,** *v.p.*, to be duped.
**Raka** (Kid. and Kidigo), *n.* (ra) (= Lingua in Kir.), voice. Kula mutu yuna rakare, Every person has his own peculiar voice.
**Rako.** Prov., Ukikala kuvo, na rako ka-ri-vo. *See* Dzanche.
**Rakue.**
**Ralamu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), broad, wide. Contracted from Ri-alamu. Jembe ralamu, A wide hoe. Kasha hiri ni ralamu, This box is broad.
**Rambamba,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), thin. Contracted from Ri-ambamba. Jembe rangu ni rambamba, My hoe is thin. Kasha hi ni rambamba kaina ndzira mbao ze ni niambamba nidzefu.
**Rambo,** *n.* Dim., Karambo,
**Ramu,** *interj.* *See* Karama. Up! The root is preserved in the Kins. Lama or Rama. Atu anapiga ramuramu, andainsa.
**Ramuka,** *v.n.* *See* Isa; Keke; Kozi. To start, to set out, especially for war. Ku ramuka wiha; or, Ku ramuka wihani, To start for a battle. Ndo atu adzioramuka luiro (= malo) si wa ramukeni. Der., Chiramuko.
  **Ramukira,** *v. rel.* *See* Kimfedo. To start, to set out to, for, with. Atu adziramukira kutu kusiku rero.
  **Ramusha.** Dzimba yunaramusha anae.
**Randu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Deni). *See* Murandu. A debt. The word is getting obsolete, being superseded by Deni. Hikura, neno ra deni ndiro ri dzarokala ranguangu. Yuna randu rangu, ka-dza-ni-riva. Marandu-go ni mangi; hata ukagusua niere-zo, ka-zi-riva. Marandu u-ri-go-na-go; be undakala-dze we?
**Ranga,** *v.a.* (= Ranga in Kins.). The word is getting obsolete, being superseded by Ku kanda. Ku-m-ranga mutu aka yefiala na madzi ga moho na mavuha. Hala mavuha, mu-range muana, yuna-dzi-golola.

*Footer: 326*

---

## [PDF Page 340 — Dictionary Page 327 (Ran — Rea)]

  **Rangala,** or **Langala.**
  **Rangarisa,** *v.a.* (= Langarisa).
  **Rangasa,** or **Langasa.**
  **Rangasira,** or **Langasira.**
  **Rangua,** *v.p.* Yurangua na mavuha yuna nagnanika (Kid.).
  **Rangandzira,** *n.* (= Langandzira).
**Rangi** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), colour, paint. Rangiye ni nieruve.
**Rangi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Marangi) (in Kig., Iangi; pl. Mangi), a kind of reed. Marangi ka-ga-mera dzi ya Ravai, gamera Ukambani tu, muho wa Athi na muho wa thua. Ganalondua ku humirua mifui.
**Rangu,** *poss. pron.* *See* Rimbiko. Mine.
**Ranguangu,** *adj.* (contracted from Ri anguangu, and rel. to the ra class). *See* Gondoefia. Easy, not difficult. Neno ranguangu; pl. Maneno manguangu. Yudzi-ni-ambira neno ranguangu.
**Ra-ni.** *See* Pingu. Una randu ra-ni we?
**Rara,** *v.n.* (Kij., Lala), to lie down.
**Raramira** (?) (= Derera).
**Ra-ri,** *particles* used in conjugation (rel. to the ra class). *See* Fua; Galukira; Murauko. Contracted from Ri-ari. It was.
**Rarika,** or **Larika,** *v.a.*, to appoint. From Ku lala (?). Ku rarika dziku, To appoint a day. Ku rarika mbeyu.
  **Rarikira,** *v.d.*, to invite, inform, for another. N'enda nika-m-rarikire mbatha, atu arive.
**Ra-ro,** *particles* implying the imperf. tense (rel. to the ra class). *See* Koko; Kokotera; Gogotera (?). It which.
**Raruka,** *v.n.* From Ku lala (?). Niama hiyu yuraruka (Kid.); Kir., Niama hiyu yudziraruka (= yudzimfaruka). Gnania yudziraruka ni kidzoa kina-m-luma. Gnania yudziraruka ni vidzoa, yudziguirua ni vidzoa, yudzivavayuka. He! yudzirarukua, or, yudziukua.
  **Rarukua,** *v.p.*, to become mad.
**Rasi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of vulture. Ri-nga kosi, ela rina punde, ni bomu punde.
**Raso,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Mbala; Ludzengo. Huere hukihenda maraso mairi: raso kulu na raso ra dzini. Raso kulu akakala mamu, raso ra dzini akala; machero raso kulu akala, raso ra dzini akakala mamu. Kulu razini.
**Rau.** Obs. Muvunga wa rau (= mungi). Muhama wa rau, or, mua rau. Gnania yudzifuna vitu via rau.
**Rau** (= Madzere; Marau; Minosi; Miarau). *See* Kidzaye. Muana hiyu ni rau.
**Rauka, Laula,** *v.n.* *See* Bambauka; Iya. To rise early. From Ku lala.
  **Raukira.** Yudzilala, yudziraukira mundani. Machero ni-raukira uka-ni-rorere niuni; nami n'endakoma vatu vasiku, be ninadza.
  **Raukirua,** *v.p.* Gnania yudziraukirua chiramuko kukuni kudza isua.
  **Rausa,** *v.a.*, to rouse early. N'enda, nikalale, machero mu-ni-rause.
  **Rausira.** *See* Futa. Der., Lurauko; Murauko.
**Re,** *adj. encl.*, long. Der., Mure (pl. Are); Kire (pl. Vire); Rire (pl. Mare), etc.
**Re,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ra class), its. Gaure, Its bark or rind.
**Rea,** *v.n.* *See* Tukumira; Hokoha. To be astonished (= in Kig., Lea, To refuse; Kij., To be drunk). Murea uchi ni ku leuka, ela murea mali kaleuka. How true! Der., Refu; Rero; Murefi; Resa.
  **Refia,** *v.a.*, to intoxicate. Mutu hiye ndiye adzeye-ni-refia,

*Footer: 327*

## [PDF Page 341 — Dictionary Page 328 (Rea — Rem)]

  yudzi-ni-dundisa uchi. Mali idzi-m-refia.
  **Refiua,** *v.p.*, to be intoxicated. Kuna ku refiua ni uchi kuua ku refiua ni mali.
**Rera,** *v.n.* (1) *See* Theri. To subside, yield, repose. Niungu idziira hata idzirera (= idzifualala). Kid., Chungu kirera (= Kins., Kali yadodobua).
(2) To rear, to bring up. Ku rera muana, To bring up a child. Kuku hiyu ni muresi, yunarera ana a muyawe. Ku reradzi. *See* Koso. Mufiere hiye yuna maneno madzo, yunareradzi yuna moyo wa mbazi.
  **Rereka,** *v.n.* Muana hiwe! unarerua, ela kurereka; mbuzi mbi unaifia murisa.
  **Rerera,** *v.d.* Much'angu, for, muche wangu, yuna-m-rerera nduguye muana we.
**Resa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku enderesa in Kir.). Gnania musiku manenoge n'ga ku resa yugomba ku resa. Gnania kuimbakue yuimba ku resa. Mukamba kana maneno ga ku kata, manenoge ni ga ku resa. Leuka; Leusa.
**Reale,** *n.* (ya, za), a dollar.
**Redza** (Kidigo), *v.n.* (Ynadza in Kir.), to come. Niredza, I come. Yuredza, He comes.
**Refu,** *adj.*, long.
**Rega,** *v.n.*
**Regarega,** *v.n.*, to waver. Nina dzino rinaregarega, rilonda ku uka. Yudzenoa uchi yudzirea, yuhenda regarega, yunakukutika. Mu-rereni vivi ni ku regarega akakudza kala mutu yuyu. Muana hiye warichua mutite ni mameye akiregarega, hukiamba yundafua hata yudzikala mulume na midziye.
**Regera,** *v.n.*, to slacken, to yield. Dzichita mudzunga, hata udziregera to ku ifua.
  **Regesa, Regeza,** *v.a.* *See* Umia; Unula. To relax, to loosen. Ku regeza uha (= Ku dorosa uha). Nidzi-m-regesa koa-sidziregera. Yudziregesa maneno, kakagomba ubizi.
  **Regesera,** *v.d.* Nidzi-m-regesera muiri hata iye akauchirira dza kuamba ni kondo, mimi nika-m-guira, nika-m-piga chafu.
**Reguaregua,** *v.p.* Ku reguaregua ni moyo ku regua ni moyo, To feel sick, nauseous.
**Regnie.** *See* Dafu.
**Reha,** *v.a.*, to bring. Ku reha habari, To bring news.
  **Rehana,** *v. reit.*, to assemble. Mudzikutana hiko, mudzirehana hiva kudza hendera atu lonso; lit. You have assembled there and brought each other here, in order to make a noise,—said to children.
  **Rehera,** *v.d.*, to bring to, to take to.
  **Reherana,** *v. ref.*
  **Reherera** (?). Nizi ku reherera tu.
  **Reherua,** *v.p.* *See* Lonio.
**Rehema** (Arab.), *n.*, mercy. Munda hio una mbaraka, una rehema.
**Rema** (Kidigo), *v.a.* (= Kir., Kahala), to refuse. Kid., Mvula yakuenda rema. Kir., Mvula idzirema, ka-i-hensi kugnia. Mvula idzegnia kanda ya Kisimani, ela kuehu mundani idzirema, ka-i-ka fika, or, idziremesa, ka-i-ka-fika.
  **Remekera.** Yukuenda remekera kuko (= Kawilia in Kij.). Maneno higo garemekera (Kid.). Muhi huno ka-u-surika, uremekera vava (Kid.). Yusagala kuko hata yudziremekera.
**Remera** (= Kigiriama and Kir., Merera).
  **Remeria.** Niama hiyu yunaremeria ku

## [PDF Page 342 — Dictionary Page 329 (Rem — Ria)]

  jira na vava, ndakudza ni-mu-hege.
  **Remerua** (= Mererua in Kir.). *See* Tumbo.
  **Remesa,** *v.a.* *See* Vovola. To resist, to refuse. Nidzi-mu-amba: h'enende kuehu, yudziremesa, or, yudzirema.
  **Remesana,** *v. reit.* Atu hio adziaririana hata adziremesana, machero gan'enda, gan'enda, for, ganaenda—maneno is understood—ansua luvia ku nenua kahiri.
  **Remesua,** *v.p.* Nidzidala hata nidziremesua.
**Remba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Vibani vitite!). Aravai a mbere angine ere akifuala maremba.
**Remereme.** Ku remesa remereme, To refuse absolutely. Yudziremesa remereme (= Kakahensa korokoro).
**Remua** (Kid.), *v.p.* (= Dzoka in Kir.). *See* Vokeka. To be tired.
**Rengarenga,** *v.a.*
**Renge,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Duka.
**Rengerenge,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Rera.** *See* Rea.
  **Rereka.** *See* Rea.
  **Rerera.** *See* Rea.
**Rere** (= Rari).
**Rere,** *v.* *See* Lamusa; Larira. Yurere ela yu kere madzo. Arere vamenga; Arere uriri umenga, or, lalana. Yurere, ela ka-dza-vodzerua, yurere madzomadzo. Yurere hebu yukere madzo? Resp., Yurere usinsisi. Urere? Resp., Nikere madzo. In the following instances, however, it implies sleep: Yuere karere, yuere madzo, He was not asleep, he was awake. Yuna-dzi-lasa, angue yurere, na kuno yu madzo. *See* Lasa. This refers to one who feigns himself fast asleep for the purpose of watching to see what people would do if he were.
**Rerere** (Kid.). *See* Fumbulusira.
**Reri,** *n.* (ra). *See* Theri. Safety, peace.
**Rero,** *adv.* *See* Kibolesa; Kigniera. To-day. Dza rero be machero ni juma, ndo avokudza mutu hiyo. Muaka wa rero, This year.
**Reruve,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), white.
**Resa,** *n.* (ra), the name of a creeping plant.
**Ri,** *adv.*, where. Ki richo; Ga ri go, etc. Here. Ni ri vio; U ri vio. Si ri ko simania gnombe si ri ko, I do not know where the cows are.
**Ri,** *pron.* (for the ra class). *See* Dzua; Mfiela. It. As such it enters into composition with the various other syllables which help to form the pronouns, as well as with those employed in the conjugations; *e.g.* Hiri, hirino, hirira; Rino, rira, riri, riro; Rina, rinda, ringa, rika, riki, ridzi. When no tense is to be indicated, it is put before the verb by itself singly.
**Ri,** *particle* prefixed to those adjectives which refer to nouns of the ra class. When the adjective begins with a vowel, the *i* is dropped; *e.g.* R'ambamba, for, Riambamba; R'afu, for, Riafu. Kasha ridzikala rofu; rina tundu, rina muga; si-r'ensi, for, si-ri-henzi. Jembe rino ni rofu; u-ri-manirire to; usa-ri-mar'kisa. Niungu rikala dzaya hebu bembere.
**Ri,** *particle* prefixed to a noun to form a magn., as Ki or Ka to form a dim. Kahana, A basket. Rikahana, A large basket. Kikahana, A small basket.
**Ri,** or **Rii,** *adj.*, bad. Contracted from Rii. Dzina ri, A bad name.
**Ria,** *v.a.* *See* Hata; Mukari; Mukono; Mafungu; Lasima. To eat, to consume, to spend,

*Footer: 329*

## [PDF Page 343 — Dictionary Page 330 (Ria — Rid)]

  to use. Ku ria deni, To incur a debt. Ku ria ufua (= Ku hala ufua). Kifiu hiki ka-ki-ria. Ku ria dzi, To eat the land; *i.e.* to enjoy it. *See* Dzakala. I-ria i-ria ge! haraka we, uenende, u tue mbuzi! Mudzomba hiye yudzi-ni-ria feida ningi.
  **Rika,** *v.n.*, to be eatable.
  **Ririka.** Ku ririka daraka. *See* Daraka.
  **Ririra,** *v. rel.*, to eat with, to, for, at. Muiko wa ku ririra, A spoon to eat with. Mdzusi wa ku ririra wari, Curry or sauce to eat with the rice or other cooked grain. Ku ririra dzi tu, To eat to the ground only. *See* Rima. Hangu dzana ka-ni-hendera gnansi, wala kadzeka nami dza vira mbere; nik'enda, akadzikirua tu; be kumba angadzikirua yuna-ni-ririra uifu, angue: nina muchewe. Mtumche hiyu ni dia, niamaze yurizira mafigani (Kid.).
  **Ririrana.** Ku ririrana ufua.
  **Risa,** *v.c.*, to feed, to lead to pasture. Mayo yuna-m-risa m'ana wari, A mother has fed her child with wari. Murisa yunarisa gnombe, The herdman has pastured the cows. Gnombe na mbuzi ni ku risa niazi. *See* Fuguka. Muganga ni ku risa atu kiravo. Mutu ni ku-m-risa muyawe banga, ku-mu-afuisa ufumfu, ku-m-niamasa kiriro, asiririkane, asiase muno. Nalasa uchi, nika-m-rise Abe gnania hanga. N'enda nika-m-rise Ame gnania hanga. Wari huno nidzi-ku-risa hanga.
  **Risana,** *v. reit.* Ku risana mahanga. Ku risana kiravo.
  **Risika,** *v.n.* Ka-va-risika hiva, kavana niazi za geri.
  **Risira,** *v. rel.* (= Ku voeera). *See* Mfuo. To cause to eat. Mdzusi hiu ni mudzo, unarisira wari. Nidzikuenda mrisira gnania rero. Ku risira tundu ga sikironi, To cause to eat a hole in the ear.
  **Riwa,** *v.p.* *See* Choga.
**Riaka** (= Thiaka).
**Riango.** Riango ya Kisiwani. Riango ya ngomeni. Riangoni.
**Riani** (= Ulongo wa?).
**Riaria,** *v.n.* (= Ungusa in Kins.; Marisimarisi in Kij.), to look about. Mutu hiye yunariaria, yudziona-ni?
**Ribomu,** *adj.*, great.
**Ribumbuana.**
**Richa,** *v.a.*, to leave; (K.) to part.
  **Richana,** *v. ref.*, to leave with another.
  **Richika,** *v.n.*, to be left.
  **Richira,** *v.d.*, to leave to, for. Sinda-ku-richira ufua we, baba mufiere, hecheyo, nahugafie. Mudzirichira ni zo pukupuku? What did you leave these crumbs for? or, Mudzirichirani richira ani? Whom, etc.? Vidzere a ki ni richira fudzula? Kalada sina mukodze muiri ni uvio.
  **Richirana,** *v. reit.*
  **Richirira,** *v.d.*, to leave to, for. Udzi-m-richirira-ni kuenda nacho? Resp., Be kadzi dzukurira chakuriavio?
  **Richirua,** *v.p.*
  **Richisa, Rikisa, Richiza,** *v.c.*, to cause to leave, to wean. Mayo ni ku-m-richiza muana. Gnombe yangu idzirichisa, ina mimba, My cow has become dry; she is in calf. Wari yunarima, ela gnania yukudza-m-rikisa kazi.
  **Richisua,** *v.p.*
  **Richua,** *v.p.*
**Riche,** *adj.*, a large (female). Vuri, or, Furi riche. Furi rilume.
**Ridahi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma- and Mi-), a large bough. Magn. of Ludahi.
**Ridambi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma- and Mi-). Magn. of Kidambi. Gnania akafuala ridambi ri-

## [PDF Page 344 — Dictionary Page 331 (Rid — Rim)]

  bomu, rinagororeka-dzi, or, rinasororeka-dzi.
**Ridi, Rithi** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to inherit. Ku rithi ufua (in Kir., Ku ria; or, Ku hala ufua).
**Rididi.** Dzua ridididi na vidzoa.
**Ridze** and **Ridzi.**
**Ridzi** (contracted from Ri idzi), *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), fresh, unripe, raw. Papayu ridzi.
**Ridzo,** *adj.* *See* Era. Dzina ridzo.
**Ridzungi,** *n.* (ra). Magn. of Dzungi. Nidziona ridzungi ra ndzui-tute.
**Ridzungu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mi-), a large heap. Magn. of Dzungu.
**Rierie** (= Riaria). Mutu hiye yunarierie muno.
**Rifia.**
**Rifu.**
**Rifu** (contracted from Riifu), **Rivu,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), ripe. Papayu rifu, A ripe papau.
**Rifua,** *n.* (pl. Ma-), a piece of a broken pot put on the lid of another pot in which the wari is being cooked, as a girdle to hold a heap of live coals to finish cooking the wari, rice, or other grain.
**Rifuhi,** *adj.*
**Rifukuefukue,** *n.*, a sloven, a slattern. Gnania rifukuefukue, kafuala nguo to; ni mutu mukolo, asie-dzi-dunsa.
**Rifumfu,** *n.* (ra). Rifumfu ra iweni.
**Rigano** (Kigiriama or Kigala), *n.* (ra and wa, hiri and hiyu, pl. Ma-), an interpreter. Rigano ni mutu amaniaye maneno ga kigala sana, vimfode viosi.
**Rihisi,** *n.*
**Ri-ka.** *See* Kalakonche; Hombo.
**Rika,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Sagala. (K.) Peer, equal, fellow. Gnania na gnania ni mutu na rikare; or, Gnania na gnania ni marika. Mutu hiyu ni rika rangu. Mimi na hiyu hu rika menga, huagnara vamanga. Hia ni rika menga, hebu luembe lumenga. Atu hia ni marika, ela hiyu ndiye ayeona dzua na mbere. Ni Kironda cha rika, ka-ki-vola, mutu ni ku fua nache.
**Rikahana,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mi-), a large basket. Magn. of Kikahana (Kahana; Mudziva; Kavu).
**Ri-ki,** *particles*, (1) prefixed to verbs, Ri, it, and Ki, if.
(2) implying a part., when.
**Rikisa, Richisa** (= Vokesa). *See* Richa.
**Rikumba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mi-). Magn. of Kumba. Gnania yudziguira rikumba ribomu hecheye munavosera. But more frequently they will say, Kumba bomu.
**Rilume,** *adj.* *See* Riche. A large male. Vuri, or, Furiri lume.
**Rima,** *v.a.* *See* Fuma; Mishombo. To cultivate the ground. Ku piga rima. Gnania akirima rimare ni kuririra dzi tu, kagula ngari kadzitu akaika, ukafua unasikirua, ela urime rima ukiririra dzi tu hata ukafua usikua na-ni? Rima ra muaka, or, ra furi ridziuka. Der., Rimo; Makurimo; Mukurima; Ndimua.
  **Rimika,** *v.n.* Ka-va-rimika hiva, vana tove (hebu ni vomu).
  **Rimira,** *v.d.* and *instr.* *See* Burugira. Gnania yunarimira runga kua gnania musiku. Urimira-ni we? unarimira kunsa, hebu uchi, hebu ni ku-mu-afuisa tu? Ku rimira pekue. Rima rosi u-rima-ro, unarimira kuria tu.
**Rima,** *n.* (ra) (= Rima; Kilimo; Rimira; Mirimire; Mirimiro).
**Rima,** *n.* (ra) (= Kilimo).
**Rimba,** *n.* (ra). Yudzihenda rimba kidzoani-ringalukosi. Niereze ka-zi-nioreka-sina rimba.
**Rimbiko,** *n.* (ra). Rimbiko ni rakue, ndiye adza-

## [PDF Page 345 — Dictionary Page 332 (Rin — Rir)]

  yekudza mbere. Narindira madzi, rimbiko ni rangu.
**Ri-na,** with it.
**Rina,** *v.a.* (= Thina).
**Rinda,** *v.a.* *See* Kochesa; Mfua. To wait, to keep, to watch, to keep from. N.B.—With regard to a plantation, Rinda only can be used, but with regard to persons, both Rinda and Rindisa, as also Rindikisa, may be employed promiscuously. Hudzidzoka ku-m-rinda, hunaria, We are tired of waiting for him; we eat. Hangu chiramuko ari vavo ku-ni-rinda, or, ku-ni-rindikisa.
  **Rindana,** *v. reit.*, to wait for each other.
  **Rindika,** *v.n.* Kandarindika mutu hiye-yundahenda uere, kandakudza hiraka-h'enendeni, hu-mu-fuhe magulu.
  **Rindikisa,** *v.a.* (= Rinda). Na hu-m-rindikise punde, akisa kudza, hundaenenda.
  **Rindikisika,** *v.n.* Be yunarindikisika 'ye-hudzidzoka, h'enendeni.
  **Rindikisua,** *v.p.* (= Rindua).
  **Rindira,** *v. rel.* *See* Rimbiko. Na-m-rindira gnania niuni. Narindira muiri wangu misiso, na-yo-sisua kuamba nisirie kitu hiki. Na-m-rindira mulum'angu, for, mulume wangu akakuenda hamba.
  **Rindirua,** *v.p.*
  **Rindisa,** *v.a.* (= Rindisira? Si rindisirire for Rindisire). Hunadzadziga, hurindise wari, We play, waiting for our meal. Mkievurirua wari, be m'anangu akikala kavo, akaamba: mu-ni-rindise, or, mu-ni-rindikise, or, mu-ni-rinde. When the wari is laden out for you, and my child is absent, he will say, "Wait for me."
  **Rindisana,** *v. reit.*, to wait one for another. Hunarindisana, hudze-hurie wari.
  **Rindisua,** *v.p.*
  **Rindua,** *v.p.* Yunarindua roho (= Yunalorerua roho). Udzirindua hangu chiramuko, Thou hast been waited for since this morning.
**Rindi** (Kidigo), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), (1) a hollow, a pit, as long as it remains open. Mania usaingira rindini (= Kir., Mania usaingira gopueni). Kudzimba rindi.
(2) (= Samia ra minazi in Kir.), a grove of cocoa-nut trees.
**Ri-nga.** *See* Kalakonche.
**Ringa,** *v.* *See* Gnara. To triumph. (1) Atu akiuya vihani, akafuina ndaro, hata akimala basi akaringa. (2) Atu ak'enda uyiwa, kuenda lafiwa mfanga, basi akidza, akafuina ndaro, akimala basi akaringa. Ukipata-i-ringe.
**Ringania,** *v.a.*, to make even, also to make straight, as the boundary-line in cultivating a fresh piece of ground, by cutting right through with an axe or hatchet, as ku kerekesa is done with a knife. From Ku linga. Naringania mihi ya wala. Na muhi mubomu atu ni ku ringania kinga (= ku memena).
  **Ringaniua,** *v.p.* Muhu hiu ukaringaniua to, dza uka-o-ringaniua na muflumeno.
**Ringi,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class) (= Hiri), much. Dzua ni ringi.
**Rini,** *adv.*, when.
**Rino,** *dem. pron.* (= Hirino; Hiro?), this. Kaha rino ri dza ro ikua vano ri dze? Resp., Ri kala bembere, or, ni bembere.
**Rira,** *dem. pron.* (= Hirira). *See* Hofiera; Karama. That, yonder.
**Rira,** *v.n.* (= Ku rira na viligo), to sound, to utter a voice, to cry, to weep. Kunarira nyoma hiko. Kifumanzi ki-

## [PDF Page 346 — Dictionary Page 333 (Rir — Riv)]

  narira. Gnonsi sinarira, The sheep cry. Niuni ni ku rira. *See* Ku imba. Muhoho yunarira, The child cries. Dzimba yunarira, The lion roars. Mutu yudzefua, atu anarira, Somebody is dead; people are crying. Kuna ku rira kua miaso, madzosi gakala ga peho. Ku rira kua Aravai, a riravio. *See* Maririro.
  **Ririkana,** *v.a.* and *n.* (= Ku-m-ririra uifu), (K.) envy. *See* Risa. Kura kusa-m-ririkana-be ndo kudza-m-loha. Yuririkana mboga tu ku usa lusinga.
  **Ririra,** *v. rel.*, to cry for, to weep for, to bewail. Mutu yudzefua, n'enda vavo, nikamuage madzosi, ku-m-ririra. Gnania yuna-ni-ririra choyo, kuamba ndimi nikayehala kituche. Dzangasimiyo yuna-ku-ririra, yulonda uuye, yuna-ku-asa sana. S'ambe: yudzipigua, ni ku-dzi-ririra tu yuna lufunsu. Mahanga ni ku ririra. Mudzusi ni ku ririra.
  **Ririrua,** *v.p.* Mutu yudzefua, yunaririrua, Somebody is dead; he or she is bewailed. Mutu hiyu yudziririrua kiriro, yuna kidzoa cha uira.
  **Risa,** or **Riza,** *v.a.* Naona mutu yudzifungua-w'enda akipigua-ei! utu hio ni ui-unariza, madzosi gadzi-ni-la. Gnania yuna maneno ga ku dzi riza; uk'enda kuakue ku-m-foya kitu, wamba: sina huadzufu hudzimala na sui ela yunacho, yugomba ku dzi riza tu, or, yuna-dzi-riza ulongo. Gnania akirira, yunarira to, akadondola kula utu; ukalola, nawe yuna-ku-risa.
**Rira-tu.**
**Rire,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), long, deep. Gopue rire.
**Riri,** *dem. pron.* (rel. to the ra class). *See* Fo; Hanga, *n.* This. There is a fine difference between Riri and Hiri, the former bearing more the sense of the same, but both words are promiscuously used. Kasha riri, or, hiri ri-nga riro, na-ro-r'ona dzana (r'ona, for, riona).
**Ririra,** *v.* (1) *See* Ria. To eat with.
(2) *See* Rira. To cry for.
**Ri-ri-ro,** *particles* (rel. to the ra class. The first Ri is the pron. for the ra class, the second Ri is verbal, and the Ro is rel. to the first Ri). *See* Kolo; Onsa. Lit. it is which = that which is.
**Riro.** *See* Funsachala; Musungu. The same, that same. Kula andi-ro-amba, ndiro atu akao-na riro; kula neno agomba-ro, atu akaona riro mtume. Be ona riro neno us'ambe unakuta mashaka, wa-ga-henza m'egnie.
**Riru,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), black.
**Risa.** *See* Rira.
  **Risira.** *See* Rira.
**Risa,** or **Riza.**
**Risasi** (Kij.), *n.* (= Hambo in Kir.), lead. Peho yutaka pingu ifuikue risasi.
**Risiho,** *adj.* *See* Rivohe.
**Risiki** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Hanga. The necessaries of life in general, victuals, provisions. Udzihenda uere, suino hudzeria chunga kare, hudzimala, be undaria ni we? Resp., A-si risiki yangu, kuria ka ku sira.
**Riva,** *v.a.*, to pay.
  **Rivana,** *v. ref.*, to pay one another.
  **Rivika.** Madenige ka-ga-rivika gakasira nimangi.
  **Rivira.** *See* Hambira. Ah-u-ni-rivireni? nacho kidzifunsika kare, be basi.
  **Rivirana.**
  **Rivisa,** *v.a.* Yudzi-ni-piga-nami nidzi-m-piga, nidzi-dzi-rivisa.
  **Rivua,** *v.p.*

## [PDF Page 347 — Dictionary Page 334 (Riv — Ron)]

**Riveho,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mi-), a storm; lit. a great wind. Magn. of Peho. Kudzilamuka riveho rero, ridzichira na atu kidza, be ni atu a mulunguni, anadzembera dziyao. The natives also say, Mvula idzichira na koma usika analaula dzi; lit. The rain has passed with departed spirits, to-night they look over the country.
**Rivia,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), new.
**Rivudzu.**
**Riwa,** *v.p.* *See* Ria; Ku ria.
**Riwa,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a kind of trap. Riwa ra ku hegera niuni hebu tumbiri ni muhambo wa ku guira niama wa moyo, A trap for catching animals alive. Ni mihi ifungua dandara kama ludzadza. Dim., Kiriwa.
**Riyuya,** *adj.*, light, not heavy. Kasha hiri ni riyuya; pl. Makasha higa ni mayuya.
**Ro,** *particle* (rel to the pron. Ri, or to any word of this class, which, if not expressed, is implied). *See* Sumfia; Upukika; Gumo; Mfara; Sumfia; Muga; Demu. That. A ri ro, Naro, etc.
**Robo** (Arab.), *n.*, a quarter in general, a quarter-dollar. Katha, or, Kasa robo; lit. lest a quarter = three quarters.
**Roda,** *v.n.* *See* Nognonerana. To forebode. Muhi hiu unaroda muaka, This tree forebodes spring by budding before the rain has set in. The mubambakofi, muburudia, and the muniala are known to bud before the rain. Kunsui na-yo inaroda muaka. Hura tu musa wari ukiroda higo mai gagokudza. Koma idziroda utu undao kudza, chamba ni viha, chamba ni ndzala, kahumania (= koma idzilosa).
  **Rodua,** *v.p.* *See* Vioni. Utu hiu udzirodua ni koma.
**Rofu** (contracted from Ri ofu), *adj.* (rel. to the ra class). *See* Ri; Mukodze; Kongo. Bad, spoiled.
**Rogo,** *n.* (= Kijego), a child who has not cut all his teeth. Muana hiyu ni rogo. Ni muana afialuaye mudzo, ela hikuno niuma akakudzakala mui, akaingira urogo kua kura ku mera meno ga dzulu, hebu kua utu ungine ui ui. Ni rogo ra ndze.
**Roho** (Arab.), *n.* (ya). *See* Lorerua; Dzoreka. Spirit, life. This word must be used to express the Holy Spirit. Roho ya mutu, The soul or life of a man. Roho ya niama, The life of an animal. Kitu Muzungu a-si-chomania, ni ku buma roho, Mulungu ka-a-funurire hivo, ela utu osi pia wa-a-funurira. Roho iki uya vakue.
**Rolofu,** *adj.* *See* Vukusika.
**Rombe,** *n.* (ra). *See* Lomba. Alluvium, rubbish. Visima vidzisiriua ni rombe. Vatu vakikala na gopue, madzi kadichira, gakasirirua ni rombe, At a place where there is a hollow and the water passes, it gets covered with rubbish.
  **Rombeka,** *v.a.*, to cover with rubbish.
**Romo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the prow of a vessel. Romo ra dalu, The prow of a canoe.
**Romoria,** *v.a.*, to miscarry. Only used when the fœtus is in an advanced state; when taking place early, Ku lafia is used. Mbuzi hino idziromoria.
  **Romoriua,** *v.p.* Muana kakakomala, yudziromoriua.
**Romu** (contracted from Ri-omu), *adj.* (rel. to the ra class), hard. Iwe ni romu, A stone is hard.
**Rondo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Dim., Karondo and Kirondo; magn., Rirondo, pl. Mirondo (ya nia). Magulu ga kuku.

## [PDF Page 348 — Dictionary Page 335 (Ron — Run)]

**Rongaronga,** *v.a.* (= Ngolangola).
  **Rongera** (Kichogni), *v.n.* (= Thura in Kir., when the lumfo is put on; Rongesa in Kisambola; Gombera in Kir.).
  **Rongovia** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to belie. Yudzi-ni-rongovia (= Yudzi-ni-gombera maneno ga foroforo, ka-vi-ka-ni-hamira).
**Rora,** *n.* (= Thora). *See* Fudia; Fuhira; Gurika. (K.) Bargain, commerce, trade. Atu anapiga rora.
  **Roraromu.**
**Roreka.** *See* Lola; Loreka; Lorera; Lorerua; Raukira.
**Rorera.** *See* Lola; Loreka; Lorera; Lorerua; Raukira.
**Rorerua.** *See* Lola; Loreka; Lorera; Lorerua; Raukira.
**Rosi,** *adj.* *See* Dzomola. All, whole.
**Rovolognondo,** *n.*
**Rua,** *n.* (ra, pl. Marua), blossom. Rua ridzifumula. Dim., Karua, but Kirua is the blossom of a particular tree called murua.
**Rua,** *v.n.* *See* Gada. Ku rua ni ku laiwa ni miladzo mingi. Mutu hiyu yudzi-dzi-dema kifiu, yunarua miladzo. Der., Muruo.
**Rude, Ruche,** *n.* (ra), steam. Ruche ni ga madzi ga moho.
**Rufu,** *n.* (ra) (= Harufu, Kij.). *See* Kirufu. Scent, odour, smell. Rufu ra marua, Smell of blossoms. Kunanuka rufu. Rufure rinanuka vi. Dim., Karufu and Kirufu.
**Rugurugu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Fundo. A club.
**Ruhusa** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Moro. Promise, leave.
**Rukudzu,** *n.* (ra), diligence, assiduity. Yuna rukudzu mutu hiye! ra ku henda kazi.
**Ruma** (Kidigo), *v.a.* Daro ni ku ruma nika na pingu, kuamba aduiaukenjirani, Endani mukarume njira. Ku ruma nika; in Kir. proper, Ku hukanira nika (= Ku lavisira and Ku kotera).
  **Rumaria,** *v.a.*, to see one off. Muana-o muche, akihalua, ni ku-m-rumaria. Ku rumaria charo.
  **Rumiria,** *v.n.* *See* Mignio; Mulungu. To return with goods from a journey. Rumiria ni ku pata.
**Rumbama,** *v.n.* (= Ku tuama in Kij.). *See* Karakara; Muaye. To settle,—said of mud in water. Madzi higa gakahurira, gakarumbama. Mutu aye kala mui, hata akiricha hura ui, basi wambua: yudzirumbama. Mutu hiye yuere akisirimia atu, ela hangu dzana yudzirumbama. Angari yudzihenda sani bomu, ela gnania ndiye adzie-m-kania, hata yudzirumbama. Gnania hangu dzana, yudzirumbama; kauka kaviri kua mulumewe, yudzihurira. Dzi idzirumbama, idziingira nema, ka-ku-na ndzala wala kakuna viha.
  **Rumbika.** Ku rumbika mbuzi.
  **Rumbuka.** Rero nidzirumbuka vitu via muaka-vivia.
  **Rumbusa,** *v.a.* (= in Kid., Lumbusa). Yudzi-ni-asa, yudzi-ni-rehera kitu ki-la-cho kure. Yudzi-ni-rumbusa. Gnania yudzi-kudza-hu-rumbusa madzere.
  **Rumbusua,** *v.p.* Hudzikudza rumbusua madzere ni achena Mehani.
**Runda,** *v.n.* (= Bumba ku pidua niyule mdogo). Gnania yudzirunda muiri, kua sumasi hebu ukongo. Muana hiyu akarunda muiri kua ku lumualumua, yudzivokua nguvu ni mufuahawe. Vitu via mundani vidzirunda kua dzua, vidziniauka.
  **Rundarunda,** *v. reit.* Kadzitu hika kakarundarunda.
**Runga,** *n.*, to remain behind in growth. (K.) Ku rimiru runga durisa.

## [PDF Page 349 — Dictionary Page 336 (Run — Sad)]

**Runga,** *v.a.* *See* Kiboma. To call one away from another. Midzigomba naye, kaka-ni-runga yudzi-ni-niamarira. Nidziamba: ni avasa; kaka-ni-runga. Be kahenzi dzua. Gnania yudzijira na vava, ela kaka-ni-runga. Ke ndiwe musena! ko ku jira ukasa-ni-runga, nini? na-ku-henda-dze?
  **Rungana,** *v. reit.* Lukolo hilo karungana.
**Rungarara,** *v.n.* (= Goloka; in Kns., Rungama). *See* Golola; Lingila. To be straight. Mutu hiyu yudzirungarara, muiri ukagoloka to.
  **Rungura,** *v.n.* Niama hino idzevia, idzirungura. Dzere ridzevia hata ridzirungura.
  **Runguza,** *v.a.* Ku unguza ni ku kuenda sola niuni. Enda ukarunguse, chamba niuni adzebua, u-a-sole.
  **Runguzira.**
**Runga.**
**Rungu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (in Kig., Ndzoma), a club, made of heavy wood.
**Rungurungu,** *n.* and *adj.*, cloudy, overcast. Dzi i-rungurungu (= i-foroforo). Rero kurungurungu, To-day it is cloudy, overcast. Kudzikala rungurungu; dzua ka-ri-ala, na mvula ka-i-gnia.
**Runia,** *n.* *See* Thunia.
**Rura.** *See* Thura.
  **Ruria.** *See* Thura.
**Rura,** *n.*, to feast.
**Rurukua,** *v.p.* *See* Gniekererua; Makira. Nidzirurukua ni utu, ni kama ku ririkana. Nidzirurukua, nidzimania, ni utu usiku. Nidzirurukua ni kazi yangu, n'enda, nika-i-hende. Moyo uka-ku-kumbukisa; but Ku orua ni moyo, is to be struck with a new thought.
**Ruruma,** *v.n.* (= Ku fuma). Dzimba yunarurumo (= Yunapiga kingurumo yunafuma), The lion growls; but of roaring, Ku rira is used. Muansa unaruruma. Mvula inaruruma (= inadudumisa). Muamba unaruruma mvula i vevi (= Muamba unafuma). Der., Kirurumo.

## S.

**S,** the eighteenth letter; here confused with *z*, but the pronunciation must not be confused.—[ED.]
**Sa,** *a particle* used in conjugation. Ela sa-mu-ambira, mki-ni-sarau; be munga-ga-ona rini-go?
**Sa.** Gnombe ana-zi-kata za migoti ya makodza ga miono, As to the cows, they cut them out of the stalks of the leaves of the castor-oil shrub. *See* Dzuva. The accusative construction is also used to express the same meaning; *e.g.* Angine ana-zi-kata migoti ya ndago.
**Sa,** *interj.*, used to *intensify* an expression. Ndo sa, come sa! Asabadu (= Asibade). Aka sa bo da. *See* Ora; Runga. Ikisa kikisa kulu vuka.
**Sa,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia). *See* Kiwembe. (K.) Chamois.
**Sa, Saa** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Kibimo; Bemba. Time, an hour, a clock, a watch.
**Sababu** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), reason, cause. Sababu nini hata aki-heha?
**Sabidi, Zabidi** (Kij.), *v.a.* (= Musabidi; Musibidi), to take civet from the civet-cat. Ku sabidi moyo.
**Sadaka,** *n.* (ya, za), a sacrifice, a sacrificial offering, a feast.
**Sadiki** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to believe.
**Sadikira** (corrupted of Stakia, Kij.), *v.a.*, to accuse, impeach. Gnania yudzi-ni-sadikira, kuamba niriwe malu; but more

*Footer: 336*

---

## [PDF Page 350 — Dictionary Page 337 (Saf — Sal)]

  frequently, Yudzi-ni-fitina, etc., is said.
**Safari** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), a journey, a voyage; the departure for a journey or voyage. Safari ya ku hamba idzifika. Safari ka-i-dza fika.
**Safiri,** *v.n.* (= in Kir., Ku hamba), to travel.
**Safura,** *n.* *See* Lumbui. An illness. Gnania yunalumua, ni mukongo wa safura; or, Gnania yudziguirua ni safura.
**Saga,** *v.a.*, to grind.
  **Sagika,** *v.n.*, to grind. Muhama hiu una sagika to. Madzere gano gadzikolua, ganasagika to.
  **Sagira,** *v. rel.*, to grind to, for, another; to grind with. Yudzi-ni-sagira muhama wangu. Luala lua ka sagira. Yudzipanda misosa, mafuhage akasagira tumbaku, ga ku lunga. Nidziocha kigomba, ni sagire tumbaku.
  **Sagirana,** *v. reit.*, to grind one for another.
  **Sagirua,** *v.p.* *See* Muisu. To be ground.
  **Sagua,** *v.p.*
**Sagala,** *v.n.* *See* Wau. To sit, to stay. Sagalani, ni-mu-ve chakuria. Yusagala muno, kaasa niuma; yuna kidzoa-ni muniewe? He or she stays long, she not thinks backwards, of those left at home; is she with head? (= is she crazy?). Mutu hiye yudzisagala sana (= yudzikala sana, kana rikare kahiri; marikage gadzisira, yusere iye). Gnombe hi idzisagala sana, ni ya kare na kare, ka-i-na rikare.
  **Sagarika,** *v.n.* Hiva ka-va-sagarika.
  **Sagarira,** *v. rel.* Kidzeka cha ku sagarira.
  **Sagaza,** *v.c.* *See* Chero. To make a child sit, to make stay, to detain. Ku mu sagaza muana. Nidzi-a-sagaza mimi, kuamba a-ni-rinde, ela angari adzienenda, It is I who have detained them, that they might wait for me, else they would have been gone now.
  **Sagazira,** *v. rel.*, to detain for. Yudzi-ni sagazira dzima ya wari. Yudzi-ni-sagasira cha tahu cha uchi, akamba (= akaamba): dzova ukinoa.
**Sahani** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za), a plate, a large round dish.
**Sahare,** *n.* (ya, za), the name of a kind of cloth imported from Sahare, in Arabia, a town in the neighbourhood of Muscat.
**Sahau, Sehau** (Kij.), *v.a.* (= Niala in Kir.). *See* Dondola. To forget.
**Saidi, Zaidi** (Kij.), *adv.* *See* Unurisa. More. Zaidi ya, More of, more than. Often used as an adj., greater. Used in comparisons, it is always with Ya. Kitu hiki ni kibomu zaidi ya hikira, This thing is great, more than that; *i.e.* greater than that; in Kir. proper, Kitu hiki ni kibomu ku-ri-ko hikira, This thing is greater that that is.
**Sajika** (Kidigo), *v.n.*, to carry, to nurse. Ku-m-sajika muana magoni, To take a child on the lap (= in Kir., Ku-m-dzukula muana).
**Sako, Zako,** *poss. pron.*, thy, thine.
**Sakue, Zakue,** *poss. pron.*, his or hers.
**Sala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the palm-cabbage; the top part of palm trees, which in time of famine is cut off, boiled, and eaten. Ku piga sala ra munazi, To take off the top part of a cocoa-nut tree. Sala ni dza ya munazi, kikolo cha luensa. Kuehu Ravai munazi ka-u-pigua sala; no dambi, baha mutu ku gusa muanawe. Apigaye sala ra munazi ni kana akata ye hombo ra muche. Muche akiulagua vihani, kakatua hombo, ni vi sana.

## [PDF Page 351 — Dictionary Page 338 (Sal — Sam)]

**Sala,** *v.n.*, to remain.
  **Sarira,** *v. rel.*, to remain to or for. Nidziriva kadzama, uchi udzi-ni-sarira. Mafuhagangu gadzi-ni-sarira, sika-ga-mala.
  **Sarirua,** *v.p.*, to be left. Nidzisarirua ni uchi wa rau (= uchi ungi).
  **Sasa,** *v.a.*, to cause to remain. Hudzeria, hudzisasa.
  **Sasira,** *v. rel.* Udzi sasirani? contracted from Udzi sasira ani? For whom have you left, it to remain? Nidzi-mu-ambira uso na madzo luasu luasu, sika-m-fidza, sika-m-sasira neno menga.
  **Sasirana.**
  **Sasirua,** *v.p.* Atu adziiya madzere gangu, nidzisasirua aini ya kavu menga tu.
  **Sasua,** *v.p.*, to be left as a remainder. Ndo wari udza-o-sasua, dzima ya alume.
**Salafu,** *n.* *See* Dzalafu. Black ants, very fierce.
**Salama** (Kij.), *n.*, peace, well-being. Enda na salama (= Kir., Enda na umforo), Go in peace. Adzikuenda, adziuya salama (= Kir., Adzikuenda adziuya mokolo), They went, and returned safely. Nidzikuenda foya nguvu mbirani, basi enendani na salama, ahendeni hofu; foyani Mulungu, muhambe, Mulungu ndiye mbomu.
**Salamala** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Musana. A mechanic, a carpenter.
**Salamiza** (?), **Salamisha,** *v.*, to make peace, to reconcile.
**Sama,** or **Zama,** *v.n.*, (1) (Kir.). *See* Sam'; Samu. To gather, collect. Madzi gadzigera, gadzisama gopueni. Madzi gadzisama njira njira, The water has collected on the road. Madzi gadzisama vi gopue vi gopue, The water has gathered in little pits.
(2) (Kid.) (= Dzama in Kns.), to stick. Niama idzi-ni-sama menoni (= Kir., Niama idzi-ni-ingira menoni). Muiya udzi-ni-sama, ka-u-misika (= Kir., Muiya wa sui udzi-ni-kuama, or, udzi-ni-kola).
**Sama, Zama,** *v.n.* *See* Dzua. To stoop, to lower. Kazama ku rima, He does not stoop to cultivate the ground, *i.e.* he refuses to cultivate. Ku zama mvula (= Ku-dzi-fidza mvula), To take shelter from rain. *See* Dz'amba. Nidzi zama mvula kolo ra muhi (= Nidzi-dzi-fidza mvula kolo ra muhi). Mvula ikignia, atu ni ku zama nuhini, or, ni ku zi fidza niumbani. Napiga nguo yangu mavuha izame izikale nieruve. *See* Dama.
  **Samasama, Zamasama,** *v. reit.* *See* Koba; Chignie. Mutu akiniadira niuni ni ku zamazama.
  **Samia, Zamia,** *v.a.* (= Chignie), to make go down. Ku zamia vanda. Yudzifuala nguo bomu, idzi-m-zamia, He has put on a large cloth, it has made him go down; he is almost lost in it. *See* Urusa.
  **Samira, Zamira,** *v. rel.*, to stoop, to bend towards.
**Samani, Zamani** (Kij.), *n.* (za). *See* Kaganira. Time, times. Zamani za kare zere mbidzo, ela za hikara ka-zi-hama; lit. Times of old they were good, but of now they are not of use.
**S'ambe** (for **Siambe**). *See* Kipimo; Ririra.
**Sambi** (Kid.), *adv.* (= Hikara in Kir.), now, presently, just now.
**Samia,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Chunga in Kij.). *See* Era. Husks. Samia ra minazi.
**Samu,** *n.* (= Kauli in Kij.?). Gnania kandakudza, ela yudzilavia samu kuamba: katoaheni, or, kahendeni hio utu, etc. Shetani yudzilafia samu. A-ni-pa samu.

## [PDF Page 352 — Dictionary Page 339 (San — Sas)]

**Sana, Zana,** *v.a.* *See* Kola. To forge as a smith, to manufacture. Ku sana majembe, vifiu, etc. Ku sana miambo.
  **Sanira,** *v. rel.*
  **Sanirua,** *v.p.*
  **Sanua,** *v.p.*
**Sana** (Kij.), *adv.*, well, greatly, much, very, very much.
**Sanamu,** *n.*, an idol.
**Sanga,** *v.n.*, to be perplexed.
  **Sanganira,** *v. rel.* (= Sunganira). Hudzi sanganira kaha menga, kahukorerue (= kahuka-kolua, or, kahuka usa chiru) (= Kij., Haja ku tu isha kia). Adzi-ni-sanganira ku-ni-fierera (hebu ku-ni-piga).
  **Sangaza,** *v.a.*, to perplex.
**Sangu, Zangu,** *poss. pron.*, mine, my.
**Sangu,** *n.*
**Sani, Zani,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Mikira; Gorereka; Guisa; Umba; Mfanga. An accident. Atu hio kadza kuehu, akidza mumenga, ni zani ukiona kitu hicho ni kama zani. Ku guira zani. Ku-m-guisa zani. Gnania yudziguira zani: yudzi dzuva kigongo, akakuenda piga muana wa mutu; si ku ujirira, ni zani; ni zani ya Mulungu. Ela mutu akiheha na mutu kasidi, aki-m-lumisa, ndio zani ya ku ujirira. Mutu hiye yudzi ni guiza zani. Uki-mu-ulaga mutu kua zani, unariva kore menga tu; ni kama mbukisi ya Mulungu, ndiye adzie ujirira ku-m-buma zani, asiro-ri-larira, If you kill a man by accident, you pay only one kore. Zani izi ku guira uwe (= Kij., Muaku lazemu wewe).
**Sansa** (Kij.), *n.* (ya). *See* Bafuta. The name of a kind of calico. Gnombe hi ikanona mathunia dze dze dze dze sansa. Si ku nona ko-ni sunsa.
**Sansu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (1). *See* Vanda; Chense. The fruit-branch in palm trees, in a state when the twigs on which are the flower-buds have burst from the sheath. Sansu rikaguira (= ridzifiala nazi ningi).
(2) A branch of any tree when cut down. Tahi za muhi, zikitemua, zikibua, basi ni masansu. Tema tahi sira, hupate masansu.
**Sao, Zao,** *poss. pron.*, their, theirs.
**Sara,** *v.a.* *See* Vuga; Madaha. To smear, to rub over with oil, to anoint, to grease.
  **Sarana,** *v. reit.* Adzisarana mafuha (ni hikura mongoni).
  **Sarasara,** *v. reit.*, (1). *See* Kunsumana. To oil each other.
  (2) Gnombe hi ka-i-ka nona muno, ela ikasarasara, ni ku nona kutate.
**Sarau** (Kij.), *v.a.* *See* Tharau.
**Sare,** *n.* *See* Kumia; Duza. Dzina ra sare ni dzina ra ku-dzi-lamfira m'egnie. Dzina ra sare ni kama ra ku dzola.
**Sari** (contracted from Si ari), I was not. Sari-vo, I was not there.
**Sari,** or **Zari** (contracted from Zi ari) (= Sere). *See* Muniore. They were. Zari-ko, ela zikasira. There were, but they are finished (*sc.* Mboga, Vegetables).
**Sarira.** *See* Sala.
**Saruba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Sasa.** *See* Sala.
  **Sasira.** *See* Sala.
**Sasa,** *v.a.* *See* Msingi. (1) To rub, to make smooth.
(2) To crowd, to fill up as a river, to close up as clouds.
(3) Trop., to press with words. (*a*) Ku sasa ano. (*b*) Yudzonga ano yudzi ri sasa. (*c*) Atu adzisasa muhalani, hada adzi idzala dele. (*d*) Madzi gadzisasa hata kandakanda, yanaria niazi. (*e*) Mvula idzikunga, idzisasa dzi yosi. (*f*) Magari gadzi-

## [PDF Page 353 — Dictionary Page 340 (Sas — Ser)]

  sasa hangani, or, lusingani. (*g*) Mutu hiye ni mukobi, akidza kuako, yuna-ku-sasa hata uka-mu-va m'egniewe radi. (*h*) Yudzi-ni-sasa hata nidzi-mu-va-kitu. (*i*) Yudzisasua hata yudzila fia.
  **Sasika,** *v.n.* Ano hiri richari ira musasa ka ri dzankue ku sasika to richari siho.
**Sa-so.** *See* Tarare.
**Sauti** (Kij.), *n.* (ya) (= Linkua in Kir.), voice, sound.
**Sawadi, Zawadi** (Kij.), *n.*, a present, a keepsake.
**Sayo,** *n.* (ra). *See* Mbala; Moro; Ingirira. Ku piga sayo ra boso.
**Se,** *adj.* *See* Zee. Aged; used as *n.*, with a prefix. Muzee wazee kihendo cha zee, etc. Kikobue kobue bomo mufumbulo.
**Se, Ze,** *poss. pron.* *See* Ze-nda; Zi-nda; Sesera. His, hers.
**Se.** Niye si.
**Sebabu** (Kij.), *n.* (ya) (= Sababu). *See* Gundisa.
**Se-cho,** *sing. neg. part.* *See* Kara. It is not so, no.
**Sega** (Kidigo), *v.a.* (= Ku soesa in Kir.; (K.) in Kis. D. = Ku pansa, or, Ku ji pania nguo), to tuck up one's cloth.
  **Segasega,** *v. reit.* Atu anasegasega musego.
**Segere,** *v.n.* (= Segerere; Hakahu segererere; Hu sagorirare). *See* Odi; Kulo; Kisoere; Malele.
**Segnie,** or **Zegnie.**
**Se-go.**
**Seha,** *v.a.*, to press upon. Una-ni-seha ge! Der., Kiseho.
  **Sehana,** *v. reit.* (= Fiehana in Kid.), to throng.
**Sehau** (Kij.). *See* Sahau.
**Sehu,** or **Zehu,** *poss. pron.*, our, ours.
**Se-ko.**
**Selaha** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Chera, pl. Viera in Kir.), a weapon of war.
**Se-lo.**
**Sema,** *v.a.*, (1) (Kij.) (= Kugomba in Kir.). *See* Kongue; Shudia. To say.
(2) To tell, to state, to make known, to betray. Ku sema utu wa mbere. *See* Losa. Ninda-ku-va kitu kisiku, ela si-ni-seme, nikariwa malu, na muigni na-ku-amba.
  **Semana,** *v. reit.*, to talk, to converse.
  **Semera,** *v.d.*, to tell of, to make known, to betray to any one. Be u-singisira nduguyo, dza kuamba uhukane atu, be ukipigua, uka-m-semere nduguyo? Nidzi-m-semera gnania neno hiro.
  **Semua,** *v.p.* Der., Lusemo.
**S'enda** (for **S'ienda**), *v.*, 1st pers. sing. pres. indic. neg. of Ku unda. *See* Durisa. I go not. Not to be confounded with Sinda, I shall not, as used in the conjugations.
**Sengera,** *v.n.* *See* Akalo. To draw near, to approach. Sengera kuno vevi, ni-ku-ambire utu.
  **Sengerera,** *v. rel.*
  **Sengererana,** *v. reit.* Atu hara ari kure na kure, adzisengererana, hata adzifikirana vevi, aimire vamenga.
  **Sengerereka,** *v.n.* *See* Luchemi. Nisengere-vi? na-ko ka-ku-sengerereka, nidzigota kivesani, kavana makalo.
  **Sengesa,** *v.a.* (= Songesa).
  **Sengesera,** *v. rel.* Hala musigowe-mu-sengesere mbere.
  **Sengeserua,** *v.p.*
  **Sengesua,** *v.p.*
**Senu,** *poss. pron.*, yours, you.
**S'enzi** (contracted from **Sihenzi**), 1st pers. sing. pres. indic. neg. of the verb Ku henza. I much dislike, I do not like. S'enzi mino.
**Se-o,** *poss. pron.*, they, theirs.
**Sere** (rel. to the pl. Sa-, Si-) (= Zari), they were.
**Sere,** *v.n.* *See* Lingila; Sagula. To remain.

## [PDF Page 354 — Dictionary Page 341 (Ser — Shi)]

**Serema,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a worn-out hoe. Maserema higa mahahu ni mabomu, ganala jembe. Jembe ka-ri-dzambusua, ni ku dzangania na maserema ayae, basi rikakuenda sanua jembe rivia.
**Seremba.**
**Se-ro.**
**Sesera,** (1) *v.n.*, to feel one's way with the foot.
(2) *v.a.*, to draw a line on the ground with the foot. Enendani to, ku sesera, vana mawe, musakuala, Go carefully, feeling your way—there are stones—lest ye stumble,—said to people going out in the dark. Signia, huenende! sienende dza kuamba unasesera. Ku sesera musesero, To drag a lame leg (in Kir.). Der., Musesero.
**Se-so.**
**Se-vio,** *pl. neg. part.* *See* Kanani. These things are not so, no.
**Se-ye.** *See* Vatite; Kasira. Na kuamba se-ye, ni-ngari nidzefua, or, ni-ngere nidzefua.
**Se-yo.** *See* Hivio; Duruma.
**Shaha,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Mushaha). *See* Nderi. Chindua, or, Jindua, ndiye shaharehu. In Kid., a chief by title, and title of honour given to anybody by way of courtesy; but Sheha, a rich man (= Muigni vitu = Dzambe). In Kir., there is no such distinction. Ah! sika ku ona shaha, ni ni kana sani.
**Shahidi,** or **Shaidi** (the latter pronunciation is more frequent) (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za; pl. also Mashaidi; but Shudia seems more commonly used than either of these words), a witness. Gnania ka-vo; ndiye shaidi (hebu: cho therua).
**Shaka,** *n.*, (K.) duck.
**Shakashaka.** Atu hara ana shakashaka, ana musungu ndani (= in Kij., Watu wale washikashika nkue-wana shauri).
**Shakira,** *v. rel.* (= Kij., Kushaka; in Kid., Ku dzaka), to wrap up with or in, *i.e.* bows and arrows in a skin, skins having been used formerly instead of the present quivers. Obs. Kid., Gnombe ya kuansa ni ya ku shakira maha, when the kirurumo is being paid. Kir, Nashakira uhawangu thiaka, kuamba mifui isiingire peho, uzungu uka moma.
  **Shakula,** *v.a.*, to unwrap bows and arrows.
**Shala** (Kij.), *v.n.* (= Dzali), to pray. Adzomba ni ku shala.
**Shamba** (Kij.), *n.* *See* Kikahe. A plantation, a garden.
**Shambi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a species of animal. Shambi ndiye m'egnie magunda.
**Shanda** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Kirunsa in Kir.).
**Sharia** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), law.
**Shauri** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za), advice, counsel, consideration.
**Sheda, Sheta** (Kid. and Kij.), *v.a.* (= Seha in Kir.).
  **Shedana,** *v. reit.* (= Sehana in Kir.).
**Sheha.** *See* Shaha.
**Shehena** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), a load, a cargo; (K.) a burden. Madzi gadziidzala shehena. Madzi gadzi kuta, ga shehena, ka-ga-chisa.
**Sherehe** (Kij.). Kuehu hu shereheni, ka-ku-na madzedzebe mangi (= kahudaradiwa muno).
**Sheria** (Kij.) *See* Sharia.
**Shetani,** *n.*, Satan.
**Shibiri** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), (K.) span.
**Shida** (Kij.), *adv.*, scarce, rare.
**Shida** (in Kij., Ku shoda (E. shota); in Kins., Ku siora), to set fire to, to set on fire. Udzi-ni-shida kinga cha moho. Kid., Luanda nta-lu-shita kinga cha moho. *Id.*, Mayiyi gangu ntafunga viguga, ka-ga-shide moho (Ma-

## [PDF Page 355 — Dictionary Page 342 (Shi — Sho)]

  yiyi = Kir., Maiyi, pl. of Iyi). Nashita niasi sivie, I set fire to the grass, that it may be burnt.
  **Shidira,** *v. rel.* Chenze cha ku shidira moho.
  **Shidua,** *v.p.*, to be set on fire.
**Shinda,** *v.a.*, to overcome, to conquer, to defeat, to vanquish. Adzi-m-shinda nguvu (= Adzi-m-thima in Kir. proper).
  **Shindana,** *v.n.* *See* Weseka. To dispute, to compete, to bet.
  **Shindua,** *v.p.*, to be overcome, to be conquered.
**Shirika** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), a share, partnership. Kitu cha shirika kuidima ku humira hecheyo. Na-hukale shirika, hugule gnombe hio. Hudzigula kitu shirika.
**Shirika, Shiriki,** *v.a.* (= Ku sirika), to taunt.
  **Shirikana,** *v. reit.*, to taunt each other.
**Shoda,** *v.a.* *See* Sindira. (K.) In Kij., to pierce or thrust at one. Nguso hi nidzi-i-shoda midzanga, idziuma; be ndzoni, mu-ni-afuise, hu-i-sule.
  **Shodashoda.**
**Shokoda,** *v.a.* (= Chokola), to poke, to poke into. Vatu usi-vo-fikira.
  **Shokodeka,** *v.n.* Uina wa kimvedo hebu wa pogopogo ka-u-shokodeka, ela uina ukaorungarara, hebu ukaogoloka, ndio ushokodekao.
  **Shokodera,** *v. rel.* Nadema lufuiho, nika shokodere niama, yudziingira uinani.
**Shoma,** *v.a.* (= Soma in Kij.), to read.
**Shombera,** *v.a.* (= Kid., Sombera), to climb a tree by clasping it. In contradistinction to Ku chancha. Of a tree with boughs or a cocoa-nut tree with steps—pandizo—Ku kuera is used.
  **Shombereka,** *v.n.*, capable of being climbed, having boughs. Ka-u-shombereka muhi hiu, unaheresa.
  **Shombeza, Sombeza,** *v.a.*
  **Shombezua,** *v.p.*
**Shonde,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a cake of semi-dried cow's dung, in some parts used as fuel. In Kid., Mutu huya hu mashonde.
**Shongashonga** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Songasonga in Kij.). Nioka yudzi-dzi-shongashonga, yudzihenda kaha.
**Shongola,** *v.a.*, to strangle.
  **Shongolana,** *v. reit.*, to strangle one another. Ku dzi shongola. Niukue sidzifungana, be-mbuzi sinalonda ku shongolana.
  **Shongoloka,** *v.n.*, to have, to present, many turns or windings. Lubugu hilu ludzishongoloka. Utu hiu una-ni-shongoloka moyoni muangu, or, una-ni-shongolola.
  **Shongolokana,** *v.n.* (= Ku vongolokana), to wind with, *i.e.* round, anything.
  **Shongolola** (= Lingila). Ndani ina-ni-shongolola (= Ku luma porepore).
**Shonona,** *v.n.* *See* Kalanga. To boil gently. Wari unashonona, The rice bubbles.
**Shononeka,** *v.n.* *See* Lombera; Ore. To be grieved. Moyo uka-m-shononeka, He was grieved at heart.
  **Shononekera,** *v. rel.* Yupigua hiko ni mulumewe, akakudza aka-ni-shononekera vava, nika-m-niamasa.
  **Shononesa,** *v.a.* (= Nioniosa; Ondosa; Sonionia), (K.) groan.
  **Shononesera.** Ku-ni-shononesera m'anangu vio, nini? Si hende uki-ni-shononesera muanangu hivio! k'amba ku-mu-henzi, mu-riche, yuntalolua ni mulume mungine, ela usi-ni-ulagire muanangu.
**Shoshomeka,** *v.a.*, to push into, to thrust into, so that a thing is concealed. Ku shoshomeka kifiu., etc., niasini, hebu mudzangani.

## [PDF Page 356 — Dictionary Page 343 (Shu — Sia)]

**Shudia** (Kij.), *v.a.* *See* Hongosa. To bear witness to. N.B.—This is the meaning the word ought to have according to its origin from the Kij. Ku shuhudia; but Abe Gunja affirms that in Kir. it is used in a different meaning, *sc.* to answer, to reply, and only in the neg., like the word Ku runga. The fact is that such words as are borrowed from the Kij. are often imperfectly known to the Wanyika, and therefore liable to misapplication. In their own language they use Ku kanira when testimony is given to say that one is not guilty, and Ku-m-sema to say that he is guilty. Nidzi-mu-usa, ela kaka ni-shudia (= Kaka-ni-udzira), I have asked him, but he answered me not.
**Shudia,** *n.* (wa and ya) (in Kir. proper = Chotherua), a witness. Ndiye shudiawehu, or, yehu, It is he who is our witness. This word is more frequently used as a noun than as a verb. Atu ao ndo shudia anamania, or, ndio.
**Shudu** (Kij.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Kir. proper, Fuanda), the refuse of semsem when the oil is pressed out, an oil-cake. The cake is sometimes eaten.
**Shuhuku** (Kij.), *n.* (ya).
**Shuhuli** (Kij.), *n.* (pl. Ma-). *See* Kembera; Huari. Business, occupation. Hungari huakudza na mapema, ela huari na shuhuli.
**Shuku** (Kij.), *v.a.* *See* Mashuku. To suspect one. Nidziguirua ni dzambo, rina-ni-shuku (= Kir., rina-ni-lumiso).
  **Shukira,** *v.n.*, to.
  **Shukirua,** *v.p.* Nidzi-shukirua ni dzambo, ni-si-ro-ri-larira, ni kama sani.
**Shukuru,** *v.*, to thank.
**Shukuru** (Kij.), *n.*, thanks.
**Shukushula,** *v.a.* Nashukushula madzi kanoani nilafie mafulo mai. Utu hio ushukushule, udzuve. Madzi gano gana shukushula, galonda ku-ni-dieka.
**Shuli** (Kij.), *n.* (in Kir. proper, Wangundu), the name of a kind of red cloth. Mukumbu wa shuli.
**Shumu** (Kij.), *n.*, poison. Yudzi-m-loga; yudzi-m-bumira kitu uchini, kitu ki ulagacho hiraka, kama shumu.
**Si,** *neg. part.* (Zi in Kid.), not. Prefixed to a verb, it forms a neg. Nahenza, I like. Sihenzi, I do not like.
**Si, Zi,** *pron. pl.* (rel. to nouns which are the same in the pl. as in the sing.; sing. I, in the gen. ya, pl. za) (= Dzopola; Dzikiriruana). *See* Lulolongo; Mulungu; Tungudza; Kuereka; Dimuka. Where it precedes the word Enda, the vowel *i* is dropped; as, Mbuzi z'enda kure, The goats they go far off; but, Mbuzi zi nta kuenda kure, The goats they will go far off; or, Mbuzi zinta-enenda kure. The former, Z'enda, is the present; the latter, Zi nta, the future tense.
**Sia,** *v.a.* *See* Mudana; Fusa. To leave, to leave behind. Muana udzi-m-sia nani? With whom have you left the child? (= Muana udzi-m-siirani?). Resp., Nidzi-m-sia na gnania; or, Nidzi-m-siira gnania. Mimi ni-nga-m-sia, yuchari dueda. Kua niuma watoka roho, yudzefua, As, or when, I left him. Ku sia ngao. Gnania yunasia niumbaye ngao. Muche akiveta muhama, akimala luambe, basi akasia vira visengere. Madzi gadzisia mboga. Nidzi-u-sia wari una hokoha.
  **Siana,** *v. reit.*, to leave one another behind.
  **Siika,** *v.n.*

## [PDF Page 357 — Dictionary Page 344 (Sia — Sia)]

  Muanangu kasiika, yundarira muno, alumire mbavu.
  **Siira,** *v. rel.* *See* Singe. To leave to, to leave with. Udzi-m-siirani (contracted from Udzi-m-siira ani)? With whom have you left him or her? *Sc.* Muana. Muana udzi-m-siira chunga chani? Kifiucho udzi-ki-siirani? Uhao udzi-u-siirani (for, udzi-u-siira ani)?
  **Siirua,** *v.p.* *See* Bi; Uthiki. To have a thing left to one's self by another. Muanawe yudzisiirua ufua. The word must follow after Sisira, at the end of the group. Ana aku siwa (= Kins., Wana wa masie). Muana wa ku siwa korokoro ni iye akayefuererua ni babaye na mameye. Muana hiyu babaye wafua, ela aknfiwa na mameye. Ana hia akasiwa tia.
**Sika,** *v.a.* Nadema nguso nikasike isurangu. Niumba ilondayo ku bua ni ku sika. Ku sika muriango, To leave a door ajar. Nidzikuenda vatu nidzisika vavo, nidziuya. Nidzikuenda sika vo sokoni, nikauya, I only went to the market and returned. Nidziamba, n'enende kua gnania musiku, be nikasika njirani, nikauya (= nikasisa njirani), I said, or I thought, I would go to Mr. or Mrs. So-and-so, but I stopped short on the road and returned. *See* Goma. Der., Masika; Musika; Siku (Musiku, etc.).
**Sikira,** (1) Nalonda muhi, nikasikire isurangu.
(2) *v.n.* *See* Lugesigesi; Weka. To be sensible of, to perceive; to feel; to hear; to understand; to attend, to obey, to mind.
  **Sikirana,** *v. reit.* *See* Patanisika; Sikiza. (1) To hear, to understand one another.
  (2) To agree with one another, to be in concord, etc. Der., Lusikiro; Sikiro.
  **Sikirika,** *v.n.* *See* Lulaka. To be audible. Manenoge akigomba, yugomba haraka haraka ka-ga-sikirika to.
  **Sikirua,** *v.p.*, to be heard. Anasikirua agomba-vio.
  **Sikisana,** *v. reit.*
  **Sikisika,** *v.n.* Nidzikuenda-a-sikiza agomba-vio, kasikisika, adzi-ni-fiola.
  **Sikiza,** *v.a.* *See* Lamba; Weka; Patanisha. To listen, to hearken. Be usikizani vo? va-uke! Gnania yudzikuenda-a-sikiza, nao adzisikirana.
  **Sikizua,** *v.p.*
**Sira,** (1) *v.n.* *See* Usichana. To leave off, to cease, to be finished. Kukuangu adzisira, My fowls are finished. Kifiu changu kidzisira, My knife is finished. Nguo ye izimusirisa; lit. His cloth ceases him (= is worn out). Vitu vidzi sira, The things are finished.
(2) *v.a.* (= Sugua in Kij.), to make go off from anything by rubbing. Nidzi-ki-sira kifiu, ela ka-ki-dza-dzuka. Nasira kifiu changu, kina kanga.
  **Sirana,** *v. ref.*, to avoid each other.
  **Sirika,** *v.a.*, to taunt with (K.). Ni ku-m-sirika muyawe tu, ela kagombere neno hiro. Maneno higo-una-ni-sirika. Be ku-ni-sirika vio nini?
  **Sirikana.** Atu hio maneno gao ni gaku sirikana.
  **Sirikisa,** *v.a.* (= Sikiza!).
  **Sirima,** *v.a.*, to trouble (K.).
  **Sirimia,** *v.a.*
  **Sirimiana,** *v. reit.*
  **Sirimiwa,** *v.p.*
  **Sirira.** Nidzibuma nguzo, ela si-dza-i-sirira. Ndzoni, musirire madzina.
  **Sirirua,** *v.p.* *See* Debe. Nidzibuma milala madzini,
