## [PDF Page 358 — Dictionary Page 345 (Sia — Sia)]

  ka-i-ka sirirua, or, idzi sirirua. Ubume, hata isirirue, be ndivo inda vo loama.
  **Sirisa.** Hala muengere, usirise hio niungu mugani, uike dzikoni, huchite niungu.
  **Sirisha,** *v.c.*, to cause to abstain.
  **Sirua,** *v.p.*
  **Sisa,** *v.a.* (= Timiza). *See* Mala; Ombosa; Musika; Mbiriri. To stop, to put a stop to. Ku sisa njirani (= Ku sika njirani), To stop short on the way. Gnania yudzirima, yudzisisa; be nasui nakukase ku rima, husise, huenende; kudzedzua. Nkuezao adzi-zi-richa musika haka sisa.
  **Sisika** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Dzadzika in Kir.), to play. Nsimo za ku sisika na vivo.
  **Sisikania,** *v.a.*
  **Sisira.** Ndzo, u-ni-sisire niere zangu. Nidzi sisira niere.
  **Sisirua,** *v.p.*
  **Siwa,** *v.p.*, to be left behind. Redupl. of Sika (?). Gnombe sikisira, nikisiwa na atu, be nindahenda dze? Niumba hio ikasiwa ngao.
**Sia, Siia,** or **Zia, Ziia,** *v.a.* *See* Mudzembesi; Lairana. To stop a gap, to obstruct, to hinder. Naika masansu hiva, nizie njira. Uriri una-u-zia na ngao, na njira una-u-zia na masansu. Nidzikata ngao ya ku zia uriri. Nidzizia uriri na jamvi, nidzihenda bazia. Maingu ni ku zia dzua.
  **Siana, Ziana,** *v.* Tundu za mazikiroge sidziziana, sidzefua.
  **Siasia, Ziazia,** *v. reit.*, to try to screen, to continue screening. Ku dzi ziazia na madzavu kusi.
**Sika, Zika,** *v.a.*, to bury.
  **Sikika, Zikika,** *v.n.* Amasai adziulaga atu angi, kasikika, The Masai killed many men, but they did not bury them.
  **Sikira, Zikira,** *v. rel.*, to bury with. Nalonda deni ya nguo, u-ni-pe, nikazikire muanangu, I want the loan of a cloth; give it me, that I may bury my child in it.
  **Sikirua, Zikirua,** *v.p.* *See* Rima, 2. To be buried. Ku zikirua mafo.
  **Sikua, Zikua,** *v.p.* *See* Rima, 2.
**Sira, Zira,** *v.a.* (1) *See* Mufundo. Kitu hiki zi-ki-ria, nika-ki-zira. Sina kitu ni ziracho-sina muziro. Gnania aka-ni-zira, kahenzi ku-ni-ona, The man has sent me away; he does not want to see me. Yuzira mutu ku dukusa mulomo (= Kid., Muzira ku ona). Yuno yuzira? ku ona kitu tu-na ku sagala kuria. Mutu ni ku-m-zira. Kuku ni ku-m-zira.
(2) This is, perhaps, better taken as a separate word. The idea, however, is still the same—to make go off, fixed to a more special and concrete object. To singe, to scorch. Ku zirazira, *v. reit.* *See* Golola. Ku zira kuku ni ku dzoma mifuziye. Hunazira mbuzi mifuzi, hu-i-dzinse.
  **Sirana, Zirana,** *v. reit.* *See* Taka. Atu hio akazirana, kahenzi ku onana.
  **Sirua, Zirua,** *v.p.*
**Sisa, Ziza,** *v.a.* (= Sia). *See* Gaga; Musiso; Pitikiza. To stop, stop up a road, a gap, etc.; (K.) hinder. Naziza njira, atu asijire na-vo. Atu adzi-ni-ziza, or, adzi-ni-zia, si-mu-ona hiye mutu. Maingu gadziziza dzua. Ame gnania, hangu dzana akaziza m'anawe mohombo.
  **Sisira, Zisira,** *v. rel.* Muzizo wa ku zizira mudzi, hebu cha.
  **Sisua, Zisua,** *v.p.* Hivo ka-va-na njira, ikazizua (= ikaziwa). M'ana we ame gnania akazizua mahombo, kaamua. Angakudza, ela yudzizizua ni m'anawe, ni

## [PDF Page 359 — Dictionary Page 346 (Sia — Sik)]

  mukongo. Na-mi hivara mbere nazizua, nikiambua: nisirie kidzoa ta niama, osi ulako usikako, ela be.
  **Siwa,** *v.p.* *See* Ufulana. Der., Masikua; Muzizi; Muzizo; Bazia.
**Sia, Zia,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kiere. A reservoir, what reserves, retains, a lake; lit. that which is stopped or arrested in its progress, ceasing to flow. Ndzo huzie madzi, gahende zia; lit. Come and let us stop the water, let it make a stopping,—a play of children. Dim., Kasia and Kisia.
**Siara** (Kij.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a burying-place. N'enda, nikapige mfua masiarani (= mbirani).
**Si-cho,** *neg. sing.*, it is not so, no.
**Sida,** *v.n.*, to be blunt, obtuse; to be hard, as wood resisting the axe, etc. Kifiu kino kidzi sida, n'enda nika-ki-nola, kirie. Muhi hiu ni momu, unasida, kidzoka ka-ki-ingira. Ndifu sinazida, ka-si-heresa.
**Sidara,** *n.* (= Seder in Arab.), the name of a kind of coloured cloth.
**Sidiri** (Kij.), *v.a.* (= Zika in Kir.), to bury. Hun'enda huka sidiri mutu, yudzefua.
**Sidza,** *n.*, great grief.
**Si-dza-nkue.** *See* Ankue.
**Si-dza-zo.** *See* Mudzuri.
**Sidzi.** *See* Nognonesa.
**Sidzi.** *See* Mimba.
**Sifu** (Arab.), *v.a.* *See* Kutula. To commend, to praise.
**Sifu,** *n.*, anything grand or splendid. Kitu kisifu.
**Sifua,** *n.* (= Nguma in Kir.), praise, fame. Mutu hiye yuna sifua yuna nguma.
**Siga,** *v.a.* *See* Mudana.
  **Sigida,** *v.a.*, to press about a sore place. Si-va-sigide muno, undakala dza kuamba una-dzi-kuna.
  **Sigidika,** *v.n.* (= Shononeka), to be pressed in the mind; to be depressed, sorrowful; (K.) to pity, to sigh. Si sigidike hivio, ukalonda ku guirua ni munga. Moyo wangu una-ni-sigidika.
  **Sigika,** *v.n.* Niereze sidziima, sidzisigika to.
  **Sigira,** *v. rel.*, to rub into, with. Ni-pani mafuha nisigire nierezangu, Give me some oil, that I may rub it into my hair.
**Signia,** *v.n.*, to go at a quick pace.
**Sihi** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to beg one humbly, to entreat.
  **Sihika,** *v.n.* Nidzi-m-sihi, ela Kasihika, basi nika-m-richa (in Kir. proper, Nidzi-m-kania, ela kakasikira, or, kakahensa, etc.).
**Siho, Ziho,** *adj.*, heavy, thick. Root-word of Kiziho, Muziho, etc.
**Sika,** *v.n.* (= Verera). *See* Verera. To support. Mutu hiyu yuna ngufu, ka-ku-sika. Njira idzisika hiva (= idzigoma and idzikoma). Mutu hiye ka-ku-sika korokoro, yuna ngufu sana. Gnombe hio ina ngufu, ka-i-ku-sika. Nidzienenda na njira hino hata idzisika. Nikasika njirani na isu ni ku sika!
  **Sikasika** (= Ku komakoma; also Kitu for Ka-ki-nuka). *See* Mulungu. Nkue ka-i-sika (!), hikara, hukaenenda.
**Si-ka.**
**Sikari,** *n.* Askari, A soldier.
**Si-ka-so.** *See* Kue.
**Siki,** *n.* (ra), vinegar. Hivo mbere Aravai ere akihenda siki ra ndimu, A mixture of unga wa muhama, pilipili, kilungakuku, muniu zira za uchi, and ndimu or makabu, pounded together. Sometimes called pilipili.
**Si-ki.** *See* Sansu.
**Sikiha,** *v.a.* *See* Musiso; Kochesa.

  **Silimusira.**
  **Silimusirua,** *v.p.* Aye silimusirua kisiwani.
  **Silimusua,** *v.p.*
**Sima, Zima,** *adj.* (rel. to the ra class). *See* Muangala. Sound, whole, entire. Samia zima, The whole grove of cocoa-nut trees. *See* Era. Yuna ila zima. Hiva kivindani muna fudza zima. Jembe zima, A sound hoe.
**Sima,** or **Zima,** *v.n.*, to be well; lit. whole. Ko u-la-ko ni ku sima? Resp., Ni ku zima. Ku zima-ko mundani? Is all right in the plantation? Resp., Ah-ni ku zima; kahumania kuku mudzini, It's all right; we do not know how it is here at home. Resp., Ah-na-ko ni ku zima, And there all is right, too. Ndo vidzo.
**Simia, Zimia,** *v.a.* *See* Fualala. To extinguish. Ku zimia moho. Ku zimia tumbaku. Ku zimia moyo. Gnania yudzi zimia moyo, kidza-yudzifufuka. Muana akolole hata alonde ku zimia moyo, be ni ukongo wani uno? This is said of the kikuadulo.
  **Simika, Zimika,** *v.n.*, to go out. Moho udzizimika, The fire has gone out.
  **Simira, Zimira,** (1) *v. rel.* *See* Dokomera. Rehani madzi, ni-zimire tumbaku yangu, sina mafuha-be na-ri-zimia na madzi. Ni-pa mafuha, nikazimire tumbaku yangu.
  (2) *v.n.* *See* Musa. To disappear. Yudzienenda hata yudzizimira, si-mu-ona kahiri. Nidzeria kitu kino, ela chayu ka-ki-ka zimira.
  **Simirika, Zimirika,** *v.n.* *See* Bakasa. Linkuare ka-ri-zimirika. Kifiu changu kidziangamika, ela kina mola, ka-ki-zimirika, or, ka-ki-zimira.
  **Simisa, Zimiza,** *v.a.* Kanoa kangu kana chayu, be ni-pa kitu kino, nirie nizimize.
**Simula** (Kid. and Kidigo), *v.a.* (in Kir., Ku pisania). Ku simula uchi uidzi na ufu (= suntisa in Kns.).
**Simunga,** *v.n.* Mutu hiye yudzi-ni-simunga na-m-vesa kare, sika-m-mania, ela iye ndiye adzaye-ni-kumbukira. Kitu hiki kidzi-ni-simunga, ku kala ndecho-ku kala secho-simania.
**Simama** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to stand.
  **Simamira,** *v. rel.*, to stand to, to superintend. Ka simamire ahoho, arime. Ka simamire atu, apige muhama. Kasimamire atu, ahende kazi.
  **Simika,** *v.a.* *See* Nguso; Fukula. To erect, to stand up anything. Ku simika nguso, To erect a post.
  **Simikira,** *v. rel.*, (K.) uphold.
**Simikiro** (Kid.), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Finikiro in Kir.). *See* Fugo.
**Simila,** *v.a.* *See* Hai. A word used to announce one's arrival, to ask others to clear the way. Similani kambi! Resp., Hai! Similani mudzi! Resp., Hai! Similani bora e! Resp., Hai! Similani bora soroko! Resp., Hai! Niani mutu hiyu asie simila? (= asie piga hodi).

  Yudzi simisa kambi, yudzi simisa mudzi, basi yudzilumba.

**Simba,** *n.*, a lion.
**Simia,** *v.a.*, to extinguish.
**Simu, Zimu,** *adj.*, invisible. Said of one buried. Yudzizikua, yu ku zimu. Nidziona gopue, rikakuenda ndani ku zimu.

**Sina,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the lower part of a stem or stalk, corresponding to the kolo in trees, and the sinde in grass. N.B.—Kolo and Sina are sometimes used promiscuously. Sina ra dzere, ra muhama (= Kolo ra dzere, etc.). Masina mairi ga mugasija.
**Sinda,** *adj.* *See* Anamira. Uchi-u-sinda. Madzere ga sinda. Kitu ki-amba-cho ki sinda; or, Kitu ki-kala-cho sinda.
**Sinda,** *v.a.*, to spend a day. Nidzisinda vavo di hata kudzedzua. Sinda rero na machero, muhondo udze. Rero hunda sinda na-ni, h'endeni hukaavahe uchi, hudze, husindire. Ka-va-nda sinda mutu hiva rero, h'enendeni mundani, ndiko ku-ri-ko na chunga, There will not be any one spend the day here to-day; let us go to the plantation—that is where the luncheon is.
**Sindika,** (1) *v.n.* *See* Ndzira. To be shut, closed up.
(2) *v.a.* *See* Kafara; Hala. To close, to shut; to make an end of, to despatch, to kill. N.B.—In this latter sense, the word is used of children only, who are considered evil; but killing in war, etc., is Ku ulaga. *See* Rogo; Kidzaye. Ku sindika uina, To close up a hole. Ku sindika niumba, To shut the house. Atu adzikuenda sindika muana mui (rogo, kidzaye, etc.).
  **Sindikana,** *v. reit.*
  **Sindikika,** *v.n.* to bind. Kavana lukue lua ku funga niumba, ikasindikika; lit. There is no rope with which to fasten the house, so as to have it shut.
  **Sindikira,** *v. rel.* Una-ni-sindikira niumba, nami ni kuku ndze? Resp., Ah-sikamania kuamba u-ndze.
  **Sindikirua,** *v.p.* *See* Kisinde.
  **Sindikisa,** *v.a.* *See* Teti; Kidahi. To conclude, to be the end of.
  **Sindikua,** *v.p.* *See* Mera; Pepo; Fuanda.
**Sindira,** (1) *v. rel.*, (K.) thrust. Cha ku sindira hudzipata, ela cha ku larira kahuntapata.
(2) *v.a.*, to press into. Na shoda pinda yangu, ni sindire muhama. Ku sindira bundukui.
  **Sindirika,** *v.n.* (= Shindilia in Kij.), to press. Madzere higa ka-ga-sindirika, ka-ga-sindiririka.
  **Sindirira,** *v. rel.* Nalonda muhi wa ku sindirira muvunga wangu.
  **Sindiririka.**
  **Sinsia,** *v.* Ku mu sinsia mutu ti.
  **Sinsira,** *v.n.* Yunasinsira (= yunakuka). Nidzi-m-lagisa utu, kaka-u-henda, yudzisinsira. Der., Sinde; Kisinde.
**Sinda** (comp. of the neg. particle Si, implying the 1st pers. sing. when standing before a verb and Ku enda, To go, the *e* being dropped), I shall not.
**Si-nda** (rel. to the pl. za). *See* Mimba. They will.

**Sindano, Shindano** (Kij.), *n.*, a needle.

**Si-nga** (rel. to the ya and za class), they resemble.
**Singa,** *v.a.* (= Sugua in Kij.). *See* Kanira. (1) To rub off, to polish. Ku singa nongo. Ku singa uzungu mufuini. Ku singa muyao uivi, udzai, etc. Utu wa ku thani ndo uambuao udzi-m-singa muyao, ela utu udza-o-ona na dzidzoro. Usi-m-singe muyao neno hiri-kagombere.
(2) *v.a.*, (K.) to lay at one's door, to commit adultery.
  **Singana,** *v. reit.* H'ende, hukaoke husingane. Adzisingana uivi.
  **Singira,** *v. rel.* Ndzo-u-ni-singire mifui yangu uzungu.
  **Singirua,** *v.p.*
  **Singisa, Zingisa,** *v.a.* (= Singa in its second meaning). Said to have become obsolete, Singa being used instead. Udzi-ni singisa uivi, nami sikaiya.
  **Singisana, Zingisana** (= Singana; Zingana).
  **Singua,** *v.p.* Gnania yudzisingua uivi. Der., Kisingiso; Musinsi.
**Singa, Zinga,** (K.) fornicate. Der., Kisingo; Musinsi; Usinsi; Singe; Nsenga; Nsingo.
  **Singira, Zingira,** *v.a.*, to surround. Niama hio-kuamba hu-angi, hungari hudzi-a-zingira, ela huari achache.
  **Singirana, Zingirana,** *v. reit.* Atu hio ana singirana (Euphemistically, anaingirirana niumba).
  **Singisira, Zingisira.** *See* Sema. Kuka-ni-hukana kua ngufuzo, una-m-singisira nduguyo.
**Sinsa, Zinza,** *v.a.*, to offer for sale. N'enda nikasinse nafakayangu uchi. Adzomba ni kudza kuehu na adumuao, akakudza a sinsa. Ku sinsa roho. Prov., Musinsa mikono niuma, kafungua. Mutu mulume ni ku-m-sinsa muyawe usinsi, na muche naye ni ku-m-sinsa muyawe usinsi. Muche hiye usienende naye-yunda-ku-sinsa kua alume-be s'ensi (for, sihensi) naa-dzi-sinse m'egnie, ela asidze hala muanangu, akakuenda-m-sinsa, warning of a mother to her daughter.
  **Sinsira, Zinzira,** *v. rel.* Na-m-sinsira gnania mbuziye, yulonda reale.
  **Sinsua, Zinzua,** *v.p.*
**Singe, Sinche,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a round mat. Singe ra ku siira ngao. Dim., Kasinge and Kisinge; magn., Risinge.

**Sinia** (?). Ana kudza ku' ziza, Witch-song.

  **Sirimia.** Udzisirimia kifiuchangu hata kikifua, ka-ki-ria.

**Soesa,** *v.a.* *See* Dema. To tuck up one's garment at the waist, to give more liberty to the legs in climbing a tree, etc. Ku soesa muambo.

  **Soesera,** *v. rel.* Yudzisoesera niuma.

**Soha,** *v.n.* *See* Kiseho. To breathe. Mosi udzi-ni-futisa, sikaidima ku soha.
  **Soheka,** *v.n.* Unasoheka, udzisolua ni ani? Gnania yudzipiga malo, yudzoka, a-ngafika hivo yunasoheka.
  **Sohera,** *v. rel.* Be una-ni-sohera vevi nawe! una-ni-sohera usoni! Ka-vi-ka sohera.

  **Solana,** *v. reit.*
  **Soreka,** *v.n.* Kuku hiyu yuna malo, kasoreka mutu mumenga uka-m-guira haraka.
  **Sorera,** *v. rel.* Ni-sorera madzere gangu, u-ni-rehere. Mu-ni-sorere madzere gangu, mu-ni-rehere. When spoken to a person, it is the language of respect. Iha hara ahoho, adze, a-ni-sorere kuka, a-m-guire.
**Soma** (Kij.), *v.a.* (in Kir., Ku fioma), to read.
**Sombera** (Kid.), *v. rel.* (= Paraga in Kij., and Sedera in Kins.), to climb a tree.
  **Sombesa** (Kid.), *v.a.*

**Somo,** *n.* (ya, za), a friend, a brother. Somo ni muana wa chaneyo, na wa babayo mufiere hebu babayo muhoho.
**Songa,** (1) *v.n.* *See* Kanga; Dimira. To be at hand, to be about; (K.) to wind, entoil. Mvula inasonga-inadza. Muaka unasonga, unaifuisa wau mvula ni vevi na kudza.
(2) *v.a.*, to choke as to growth; trop., to set on, to urge, to instigate. Niasi sina songa vitu; sudi urimire pekue, uulage niasi, basi vitu vindaviala. Ku songa jaro, To set a journey on foot. Ku songa kondo, To instigate a strife or quarrel. Ao songa kondo hi ni gnania ora gnania basi kondo iki bua, atu akipigana.
  **Songana.** Muhama ukinialua mukuku, basi ni ku songana, ukaviala visuche vitite, ela uki gnorera, ndivo u viala vo masuche mabomu. Maneno gano gano songana; kula mutu yugomba ku fuhira kuakue; ela mumenga yundahewa ulongo.
  **Songera,** *v.* (= Sengera), to draw near.

**Stala** (Kij.).

**Suino** (= Suisui?).
**Suisui,** *pers. pron.*, we, us.
**Suka,** *v.a.* *See* Ku gnoda; Kochokocho; Lukansa. (1) To shake. Ku suka masia kirenge ni, kuamba galae mafuha, To shake milk in a calabash, to churn butter.
(2) To plait. Ku suka niere, To plait the hair.
(3) To weave. Ku suka midza, To make or weave fringes.
  **Sukana,** *v. ref.* Anasukana niere, They plait each other's hair.
  **Sukanika,** *v.n.*, to feel grief; (K.) to be sorry. Na-mu-ona muana akipigua ni mameye, be moyo udzi-ni-sukanika, I saw a child being beaten by his mother; indeed, my heart was grieved.
  **Sukanikira,** *v.n.*, to sympathize.
  **Sukasuka,** *v.* *See* Udumani. (K.) To shake, to shake well, thoroughly. Muana akikala kahenzi ku enenda, hebu kahenzi ku uka, be una-m-guira, uka-m-sukasuka.
  **Sukika,** *v.n.* Rarely used. Lusihu hilu ludzi sukika to; but more frequently Ludzi sukua to is used.
  **Sukira,** *v.d.*
  **Sukirua,** *v.p.* Nalafia milala yangu, kuamba nisukirue lusihu, be nindafuma m'egnie.
  **Sukuka,** *v.n.*, to get dislodged. Nidzi-m-sukula dzino, ridzi sukuka. Ah rero yudzi sukuka 'ye Shaha!—said of one who seldom goes anywhere.
  **Sukula,** *v.a.* and *n.* *See* Koko. To dislodge, to disunite. Ku sukula dzino, To dislodge a tooth, to extract it. Ku sukula lukombe. Ku sukula nazi; or, Nazi ya ku sukula, To dislodge or lift out a piece of a cocoa-nut from the shell. Muanawe ka-dza-enenda, ela yuna sukula, Her child does not yet walk well, or properly, but it toddles.
  **Sukuma,** *v.a.* *See* Fieta; Batula; Kafara. To push, to propel, to punt.
  **Sukumana,** *v. reit.* *See* Hofiano. To push one another.
  **Sukumisa, Sukumiza.** Yudzi-ni-sukumisa maneno mai. Ku sukumiza uganga.
  **Sukurika,** *v.n.* Menoge ni momu, ka-ga-sukurika haraka, ela gangu ka-ga-kakomia ku sukurika.
  **Sukurira,** *v.d.*
  **Sukurirua,** *v.p.* Nidzisisukurirua nazi ni musenangu.
  **Sukusula,** *v.a.* Rare.
**Sukari,** *n.*, sugar.
**Sukua,** *v.p.*, to be plaited. Yudzi sukua niere (= yudzignodua). Lusihu hilu ludzisukua to.
**Sukumo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a push; (K.) jolt. Yudzi-m-sukuma sukumo ra geri, aka-m-dieka.
**Sula,** *v.a.* (= Gnola). *See* Shoda; Kidzungu. Ku sula kidzungu. Der., Kisuka; Musuka; Mususi; Mususu; Susu; Nsusua.
  **Suka,** *v.n.* Wari yudzi-dzi-fidza, vino yudzisuka (= yudzisumbuka).
  **Sulula,** *v.a.*, to season. Ku sulula niungu (in Kij., Ku sua tungu; Kins., Ku sirura mbia). Ku sulula niumba, To season a house, by sleeping in it for the first time.
  **Sulurira,** *v.d.*
  **Sulusa,** or **Surusa,** *v.a.*, to swing, to whirl round as a sling. Ku sulusa tero.
  **Surika,** *v.n.* Ka-u-surika mugasija hiu, rehani jembe, huhende dzimba.
  **Surira,** *v.d.* Na-m-surira mugasija, nika-mu-ve.
  **Suruka,** *v.n.* Mboga idzisuruka. Dzere ridzi suruka, ka-ri-dzankue ku ivua to. Madzere gangu gadzisuruka, gaira kumi

## [PDF Page 367 — Dictionary Page 354 (Sul — Sum)]

  menga tu na ku kala mafu ga ku funsa. Na muiri wa mutu ni ku suruka kua ukongo, kua charo, kua makazi, etc.
  **Surusa,** *v.a.* Nidzi-u-surusa, ka-u-ka ivua (viz. Mugasija). Muiri udzi-ku-suruka, unani we? Resp., Nari nakitetemo hangu madzusi, ndo kikacho-ni-surusa muiri.
  **Surusira,** *v.d.* Ima! ni-ku-surusire madzere, upate ngari mairi, uenende ukihafuna.
  **Surusua,** *v.p.* Nidzisisurusua ni moho wa luchemi, nidze via.
  **Susa,** *v.a.* *See* Mususi. Muganga ni ku susa viombo vidzavio sikua ni mudzai. Ku susa kitu kikacho iyua.
  **Susira,** *v.d.* Ndzo uka-ni-susire via viangu, vidzavioiyua-uki-vi-ona nda-ku-va mafunga.
  **Susirua,** *v.p.* Gnania yudzikuenda susirua vituvie ori muganga.
  **Susua.**
  **Susua,** *v.a.* Mutu hiye na-mu-isa, kahenzi ku-ni-riva, nik'enda-ni ku-ni-susua tu.
  **Sususa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (in Kns., Ku sususa), to soothe, to pacify a child.
**Sulia** (Kij.), *v.*, (K.) impede, embar. Guira o muhi, u-u-sulie, ni funge. Nidziamba nihewe kitu kisiku, ela gnania yudzi-ki-sulia. Nguso inasulia muganganga. Nidzilon da kifiuchangu, ye aka-ki-sulia. Nidziamba nijire na njira, be gnania aka-ni-sulia. Ku-dzi-sulia.
  **Suliana,** *v. reit.*
**Suluhia,** (Kij.). *See* Herera, *v.n.*; Sulumu. Ka-dza-suluhia to (= Ka-dza mania to); *sc.* his work or business kazi. Mbuzi hiyu ka-dza-suluhia, sudi mu-i-tunze to, isnangamika. The root Sula and the intermediate formations do not exist in Kir.
  **Sulumira,** *v.n.* Yudzijira kare, yudzisulumira, kaoneka kaviri.
  **Sulumira,** *v.a.* Uki sulumire (= sulumize).
  **Sulumiza,** *v.a.*, to wash down. Ni-pani madzi, ninoe, ni sulumize kitu nidza-cho-ria. In Kid., Ku-m-sulumiza gnombe mufiu. M-sulumize sana-gnombe ni musiru hiye. Kir., Niama hiye nidzi-m-doma mufui, nidzi-m-sulumiza, ka uka ye. Nidzi tungua ni muiya, udzi-ni-sulumiza, siidima ku enenda kabisa.
**Suma,** *v.a.* and *n.* *See* Ganga. To say, to tell, to speak. Ku suma ni ku amba: hu suma o! Nidzi-mu-ambira utu, yudzi-ni-suma, yudzi-ni-kuignia. Mutu akitendua, atu akidzeka osi, be ana-m-suma, hu suma o. Ku suma muansa. Ku suma uira dzakani. Gnania yudzigomba maneno, yudzisumua. Kig., Ku sumo muezi kongo andie ni lola vi nafue (= Ku sumua; or, Ku lumbua muezi, Kir.).
  **Sumira,** *v. rel.*
  **Sumirua,** *v.p.* H'endeni ukasumirue kua muganga wa kifugo. Uganga wa ku sumirua.
  **Sumurira,** *v.n.*, to converse.
  **Sumurirana,** *v. reit.*, to talk with each other, to converse. Der., Kisumo; Nsumirua.
**Sumari** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za, and ra, pl. Ma-) (= Bugno in Kir.), a corn-pipe. Sumari ihendua yu mugua wa muhama, The sumari is made of a stalk of Guinea-corn. It is smaller than the perembe.
**Sumasi,** *n.* (ya). *See* Runda. Sorrow, grief, dejection.
**Sumba,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Sindano in Kij.), a needle. Dim., Kasumba.

## [PDF Page 368 — Dictionary Page 355 (Sum — Sun)]

**Sumba,** *v.n.*, to shake; (K.) pulse, totter. Moyo una-ni-sumba ukikala unadzukirua.
  **Sumbasumba,** *v. reit.* *See* Cho.
  **Sumbira,** *v. rel.* Gnania ni mukongo, ela nduguye yuna-m-sumbira. Yuntahenda thimua ni Mulungu tu.
  **Sumbuka,** *v.n.* (= Sirima).
  **Sumbula,** *v.a.*, to trouble, to tease. Ku sumbula atu.
  **Sumbulana,** *v. reit.*
  **Sumburira,** *v. rel.* *See* Kumbusha. To upbraid, to remind of past favours, to taunt, to throw in one's teeth. Mutu hiye yuna-m-sumburira muyawe kitu a-cho-muva.
  **Sumburirana,** *v. reit.*
**Sumbuka,** *v.n.*, to be vexed, troubled. Kitu changu chaangamika, vino kidzisumbuka na gnania. Kiravo hua-cho-pigirua, kidzisumbuka.
  **Sumbula,** *v.a.*, to find out; (K.) contrive, devise. Mulungu na gnania ndiye ayekuenda-ki-sumbula ndiye aye-ki-ona. N'enda ku sumbula, I go to find it out.
  **Sumburira,** *v.d.* *See* Chisa.
  **Sumfia, Sumvia,** *v.a.* *See* Umba. To shake, to toss, to disquiet, to stir. Ku sumfia dzi. Gnania yulonda ku sumfia dzi, ela dzi ka-i-sumba, yuna-dzi-sumfia m'egnie; a-henda-ro atu kahenzi, na ku idima ku-m-kania, kaidima. To exercise (= Ku dzembeza magulu, etc.).
  **Sumfiua,** *v.p.* *See* Ngogomue.
**Sumurira.**
**Sunduka,** *v.n.* Mukokola ka-u-ndasunduka mundani (= ka-u-ndasira).
  **Sundurika,** *v.n.* Ka-i-sundurika. Ka-ri-sundurika-kasha, ka-ri-na mufungulo.
  **Sundurira,** *v.d.* *See* Mufungulo. Ndzo-u-ni-sundurire niumba, siidima ku sundula.
  **Sundula,** *v.a.* (= Ahula). Ku sundula dzansu (= Ku ahula dzansu). The latter expression is the more usual.
**Sunga,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Masunga; Musunga. Foreskin, uncircumcision.
**Sunga,** *v.*
  **Sungamiza,** *v.a.*
  **Sungamizania,** *v. reit.* Vatu hivo vana maneno ga dzungamizi, atu anasungamizania.
  **Sungamisua,** *v.p.* Der., Dzungamizi.
  **Sungania** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Lingilia in Kir.; Kij., Dangania; Kins., Songeresa; Kir., Jinga, etc.), to instigate one another.
  **Sunganira,** *v. rel.* (= Sanganira; in Kid., Hulungane). Ni-rinda, husunganire njira, huduane. Gnombe sinaheherana, sinasunganira muyawe. Aravai adzi-hu-sunganira Adzomba ehu, kondo ikafuka muho.
  **Sunganirana,** *v. reit.*
  **Sunganirua,** *v.p.* *See* Denguri. Yudzisisunganirua ni atu ahahu hebu ane, akapigua hata akaviogua.
  **Sungira** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Dundisa in Kir.; in Kins., Sunga), to urge upon.
**Sungula** (Kid.) (= Laula). Ku sungula munda (= Ku runguza munda in Kir.).
**Sunguluka,** *v.n.* *See* Kisungu. To go about, to walk about. Njira hio, or, hino inasunguluka muno, na hudueni hino muho ya ku kata, ndo hunda-vofika haraka.
  **Sunguluza,** *v.a.*, to force about. Nina makasi mangi, gana-ni-sunguluza kidzoa.
  **Sunguluzua,** *v.p.*, to be forced about.
**Sungumuza,** *v.a.* Abe Gunja yudzi pata kisungumuso, be suino suino hunda-dzi-sungumuza nani-hendeni hukalonde uchi, hunoe.
  **Sungumuzana,** *v. reit.*
  **Sungumuzania,** *v.a.*

  **Sungumuzua,** *v.p.*
**Sunsula.** Ahoho hia anahenda sunsula, andaguirua ni kisungu. Sunsula niumba ya muganga.
**Sunuka,** *v.n.* Muhi udzisunuka. Niumba yangu idzikala ya kare, inasunuka, inalonda ku bua.
  **Sunurika,** *v.n.*
  **Sunurira,** *v.d.*
  **Sunula,** *v.a.*, to lift out. Ku sunula kisiki cha muvingo. Ku sunula iwe, nguso.
**Sura** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za, and ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Luhalo. A likeness, a picture, an image. Mutu hiye kana sura, ni mui. Surare ri-nga ra gnania; or, Suraye i-nga ya gnania. Surare akahala gnania fulani kuko kuehu.
**Suredi,** *n.*, the name of a kind of cloth and brass wire imported from Surat, in India.
**Surudi** (Kij.), *n.* (= Sudi), necessity. Kua surudi, *adv.*, necessarily. Surudi nienende rero, nikahale uchi wangu, nikisa kuenda rero, sinta-u-pata, ntahewa mbatha ingine. Surudi u-ni-pe, You must give it me.
**Suruka.**
**Surusa** (= Sula).
**Susa.**
  **Susua.**
  **Susuna** (?).
**S'use** (= Si use). *See* Mufundo.
**Susi,** *n.*, wind.
**Susu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Obs. It was a kind of screen, made of sticks, closely strung together, and hung up over the fireplace.
**Susu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Mususu; Bule?). *See* Kengeka. (K.) Hanger? Mutu huya ni susu; pl. Atu hio ni masusu.
**Susula,** *v.a.* Muho hiu ka-u-fukika, madzi ganasusula.
**Susurika,** *v.n.* Nidzidzoka ku susurika, sina-muaka nisiokuenda.
**Susurika** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Sukasuka in Kij.), to continue, to shake, to waver. Yu kere ku susurika, ka-dza-pata nguvu (= Kij., Akali akisukasuka, haja pata nguvu), The mind wavers; he does not get strength.
  **Susurikira,** *v.d.*
  **Susurisha.**
  **Susususu.**
  **Sususa** (Kid.), *n.* (= Ku sususa in Kns.). *See* Dzudzurira. (K.) Hanger?

## T.

**T,** the nineteenth letter, pronounced generally as in English, but in some words the pronunciation is softer. It should not be confused with *d*.—[ED.]
**Ta.** *See* Andika.
**Taba,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lutaba.
**Tabia** (Kig.), *n.* (ya), bias, natural disposition, temper, character. Yudzihala tabia ya mbari yao ya uivi, za udzai, etc. Mutu hiye uiviwe hio ni tabiaye hecheye, kuao mbarini kakuna.
**Tafi,** *n.*, the name of a fish.
**Tafuna,** *v.a.*, to chew.
**Tafuna,** *n.*, lit. something that is chewing, feeding.
**Tafuta.** *See* Dafuta. Used only with Muhi.
**Tahayari.** *See* Dahayari.
**Tahi,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lutahi. Panda mbivu, or, Panda pfu ndizo riishazo tahi.
**Tahu,** *adj.*, three. Gnombe tahu, Three cows. Gnonzi tahu, Three sheep. Mbavu tahu, Three ribs. Dziku tahu, Three dogs.
**Tai** (Kid.), *n.* (= Tahi in Kir.). Pl. of Lutai.
**Taka,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Lamfiana. (1) Taka si-nga tembe za ndzugu.
(2) Muana yudzifuhuka mahe

*Footer: 356*

---

## [PDF Page 370 — Dictionary Page 357 (Tak — Ted)]

  kanoani, be ni mukongo, akaambua: yudziguirua ni taka; mameye ni chaneye akikala akasirana, be ndo muana aguiruavo ni taka. Kana mahe; ni taka hisi. This is removed by the ceremony of Ku lamfiana gnonsi. Muhi wa taka (= Mutaka); its leaves being used to remove the sickness. *See* Lamfiana.
**Tako,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Tera in Kins.), the buttocks, the butt end of a gun. Tako ya mufui, The handle of a sword; pl. Tako za mifui, Handles of swords. Anorangu nidzi-ni-dzonga, ela si-dza-ri-piga tako.
**Tala,** *n.* (= Ta in Kij.), the name of a fish.
**Talago,** *n.* (ya, za). Talago za fiala.
**Tama.** *See* Dama.
**Tama** (Kij.), *n.*, sweepings, rubbish. Tama muana na iye (?).
**Tamani, Thamani** (Kij.), *n.* (ya) (= Kima in Kir.). *See* Baha. Price. Thora hiri rinagurika, rina thamani mbidzo. Thamani ye i-dze? Hu-ambire tamani ye.
**Tambale** (Kij.). Dzi hio ni tambale, ka-i-na mirima, wala ka-i-na mawe, ka-ku-na utu u-ku-ogoviao, ka-i-na ndzala, wala ka-i-na viha, uk'enda waenenda raha.
**Tambasi,** *n.* (wa) (in Kid. and Kij., *id.*), rheumatism. From Ku hambala. Tambasi wangu una-ni hambala muiri osi, kadzankue ku henda ivu.
**Tambo,** *n.* (ya, pl. za), (1) a kind of string.
(2) A giant.
**Tambotambo.**
**Tamfa,** *v.a.*, to plunder.
**Tana,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Zano. A small bow for boys. Tana ya ku insira niuni na ya ku fumagira madali. Dim., Kidana.
**Tana,** *v.n.*, to separate.
**Tandadu,** *n.* (ya, za).
**Tandahu,** *adj.*, six. Niumba tandahu, Six houses. Reale tandahu, Six dollars. Mbuzi tandahu, Six goats. Gnombe tandahu, Six cows.
**Tandala,** *n.* *See* Eremerana. Ku sagala tandala.
**Tandiko,** *n.* (za). *See* Mahandiko. From Ku handika. Tandiko ni kitu chosi u-nda-cho handika ku larira, ikakala kansa hebu kidzeka, hebu chingo. Kare atu ari aki-i-iha malalo hebu mahandiko.
**Tando,** *n.* (ya, za), a spider's web. Enda hiko mduniua we! una tando, una kigopue cha milomo.
**Tanga.** *See* Danga.
**Tangaizi, Tangawizi,** *n.* (ya), ginger.
**Tangulia,** *v.n.*, to precede.
**Tania,** *v.a.*
**Tanzi,** *n.* (ya, pl. za) (= Mihasi ya), a noose of string or wire, used to catch animals, fish, etc.
**Tara,** *n.* (za), tremblings, shakings. Pl. of Lutara.
**Tarare,** *n.* (= Purumukua in Kns.), a plant sprung up from seed accidentally scattered. Dzere hiri ni ra tarare. Madzere gogo ka-ga-niarirue, gakamera g'egnie kua tembe yayobodoka; pl. Tembe sasobodoka, majira garatu ga ku funsa madzere. Muhama hiu ni wa tarare.
**Tasa,** *n.* and *adj.*, a barren woman or barren animal.
**Tatama,** *v.n.* (= Ku muta mafuindi), to kneel.
**Tate,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), little. The root-word of Kitate; Mutate, etc. Mvula tate.
**Tayari.** *See* Dayari.
**Tazi,** or **Tadzi,** *n.* (ya). Pl. of Luhadzi.
**Te,** *adj.* and *n. encl.*, female.
**Tede,** *n.* (za). *See* Kipunguo. Properly in Kij., the grain of sorghum in the unripe

*Footer: 357*

---

## [PDF Page 371 — Dictionary Page 358 (Ted — Tha)]

  state, but in Kir. only used of small-pox. Tede za peho; lit. small-pox of coldness,—so called when the pustules do not break out. Tede za moho, Small-pox of heat, — when they break out virulently.
  **Tedekuanga,** *n.* (in Kij., *id.*), small-pox.
**Tegnie, Chegnie,** *n.*, a hoe.
**Tego** (Kij.) (= Tambo). Yudzihenda tego, yudzihega muchewe.
**Tembe,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) a grain of corn.
(2) The seeds and stones of fruits, kernel, berry, when small, the larger ones being called Koko.
(3) A bead.
(4) A little, a few. Tembe ya muvunga. Tembe za ndzambaraho. Una-ni-riva tembetembe, kusa-ni-riva viosi nini? Nidziika tembe za uchi vavo, ndzo, huenende, hukadzumbule.
**Tembe,** *adj.* (rel. to the ya and za class), few. Gnombe tembe, A few heads of cattle. Niumba tembe, A few houses. The root-word of Atembe; kitembe (pl. Vitembe); Matembe; Mutembe; Mitembe.
**Tembe** (Kid. and Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Muanso in Kir.), a fresh vanda, when beginning to be tapped. Uchi wa tembo (in Kir., Uchi wa muanso). Kibangala ki-si-vo dzankue ku fungirua, ndivo uihavo uchi wa tembo (in Kij., Kibuyu ki-si-po tasa ku umikua). Ku dzasa tembo (= Ku dangadza muanso in Kir.).
**Temo,** *n.* (ya, za) (1). *See* Pingi. Lit. a cutter, a hard chisel, for cutting metals only. From Ku tema.
(2) Trop., death, the being cut off. Temoye ka-i-dzafika. Temoye idzifika.
**Tende** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za), dates.
**Tende,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Madzango; Mikodo), rings, made of the fibres of a tree called muniense, or of the skin of a hog, and worn round the legs. Tende za kiravai sere za kikonde cha ngulue, kikaloe-gua.
**Tende,** *n.* (ya, za), the testicles. Tende za musibi, The berries (tembe) of the musibi, so called because they grow two by two.
**Tendeje,** or **Tendeye** (Kig.). Prov., Tendeje yuesua mufiere.
**Tendere** (Kid.), *n.* (= Marathi in Kij.), a sickness, disease. Ni tendere ya Mulungu hino, This disease is of God.
**Tenga,** *v.* *See* Denga.
**Tenge** (Kidigo), *n.* (= Tengere in Kir.), a taking off. From Ku tenga.
**Tengere,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Mudana; Lev. xix. 27. Lit. that of which something is taken off, applied only to the pair left on the crown of the head. Niere dzangu ka-zi-zangue ku demeka tengere, ndo ze ambua zo si dzi sisirua. Ku sisira niere.
**Tenguladzua,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia) (= Kibanzi).
**Teno.** *See* Deno.
**Tere,** *n.* (za), the name of a disease in the palm of the hand, the skin-splitting. Pl. of Luchere.
**Teria.** *See* Deria.
**Tero,** *n.* *See* Mukambe. A sling, platted of milala.
**Tesi,** or **Tezi,** *n.* (ya, za), (K.) excrescence.
**Tete,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Lutete.
**Teza.** *See* Deza.
**Thatha.**
**Thalimu** (Kij.), *v.n.*, to be unjust, false, dishonest to any one. Hunga patana, ela mutu huya yudzi-hu-thalimu, We should have agreed, but that man has been false to us; *e.g.* When he says, Kitu hiki ka ki fua hivio, This thing is not sold thus. Si thalimu Mulungu; nidzieneza, Mulungu bariki, I am not false

*Footer: 358*

---

## [PDF Page 372 — Dictionary Page 359 (Tha — Thu)]

  to God; I have got a sufficiency, God is blessed, or praised; *i.e.* I humbly acknowledge what He has given me. *See* Enesa.
**Thambi.** *See* Dambi.
**Thana** (Kig.) (= Kumuthana, Kir.). Ku mu ra dira, To go to meet.
**Thani** (Arab.), *v.n.*, to suppose. Nidzihenda thani, I went on a supposition.
**Thara** (Kij.), *n.* (in Kir. proper, Dzambo), a matter, a consequence, something that might prove injurious or troublesome; generally used in connection with a deprecation. Atu hia adzifidzania, akasapata thara, These men hid one another, lest they should get a matter, *i.e.* of trouble.
**Tharau** (Arab.), *v.a.*, to slight, to disregard. Kudza amini kuamba yunda-ni-hendera utu, ukahenda hura utu udzao kaniua, ndo ku-m-tharau.
**Thatha,** *n.* (= Muhembo), roughness; a rough, uneven surface. Iwe ra thatha (= Iwe ririro na dzengadzenga).
**Thecha,** or **Theja** (Kig.), *v.n.*, to meet with a good omen. Nidzitheja, I have met with a good omen (in Kir. proper, Nidzipigua ni niuni mudzo; lit. I have been struck by a good bird). *See* Niuni. Sika theja, I have not met with a good omen (= Kir., Nidzipigua ni niuni mui, I have been struck by an evil bird). Kuna ku theja na niuni, kuna tu theja na muthana, There is a meeting with a good omen with a bird, *i.e.* by observing a certain bird, and there is a good omen with, *i.e.* from the meeting with an equal number of persons on first setting out. *See* Muthana.
**Thenga** (Kig.), *v.n.* (= Ku noa uchi in Kir.), to drink toddy.
**Theri, Rere,** *n.* (ra). *See* Maheho. Quietness, peace. From Ku rera.
**Thiaka,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a quiver. Formerly the word meant merely a skin in which the natives wrapped their bows and arrows.
**Thiana,** *v.n.* *See* Ku laula. To spy, to explore as a spy.
**Thifu.** *See* Difu. Der., Muthiani.
**Thiki** (Arab.), *n.*, anxiety, grief, distress. Nidzihenda thiki moyoni kua neno ri nidzaro sikira, moyo ndzi-ni-piga fundo.
**Thiki,** *v.a.*, to cause anxiety to, to distress. Mutu yudzi-hu-thiki hiye!
**Thima,** *v.a.* *See* Radi; Sumbira. To surpass in strength, to prevail over, prevail upon; to get the better of, to overpower, to overcome. Note: The word is sometimes pronounced with an *r* instead of *th*, when it coincides with Ku rima, To cultivate the ground. In fact, the idea of the two words seems to be one and the same, namely, that of subduing.
**Thina,** *v.a.*
**Thingiria** (Kik.), *v.a.*, to shake, to churn. Only used of milk and cream, when making butter. The natives put the cream or milk into a calabash, and shake it to make butter.
**Thioma** (Kig.), *v.n.*, to break, to mangle a language. Kaidima Kiravai, akigomba yuna-thioma.
**Thora,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a bargain. Ku piga thora, To strike a bargain. Thora ridzo, A good bargain.
**Thorima,** *v.a.*, to look after. Only used as regards cattle, as Ku laula refers to a plantation. Ku thorima makundi.
**Thuka** (Kig.), *v.n.* (= Dzukirua in Kir.), to become bad.
**Thumba,** *v.n.*, to leap aside as an arrow.

*Footer: 359*

## [PDF Page 373 — Dictionary Page 360 (Thu — Tin)]

**Thunia** (also pronounced **Thugnia, Rugnia,** and **Runia**), *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), fat, a piece of fat. The word is either borrowed from the Kimasai or is common to both languages. Thunia ra gnonzi, The fat of a sheep; used also as a medicine for the ear-ache. Dim., Kathunia and Kithunia.
**Thura,** *v.n.*, (1) to receive the crowning honours on being promoted from a mumondo to a govu. The individual concerned wears for a few days a crown made of clay, but highly decorated, and, as the completion of the honours bestowed on him, receives on his right arm the lumfo, which he wears ever afterwards. *See* Niambura. Ku thura ni ku bumua lumfo. Ka dza thura iye, yuchari mumondo. Note: As to the radical meaning of the word, we may refer to the Kins. Ku lula or Ku rura, To be efficacious, powerful, the letters *th*, *l*, and *r*, being constantly interchanged.
(2) Fig., to be at an end. Only used of war. This application of the word refers to the circumstance that, after the Ku thura, a man ceases to make contributions to the govu. Viha vidzithura, kakuna utu kaviri, atu adzeria dzoga.
  **Thuria,** *v.a.*, to bestow the crowning honours on the mumondo. Govu hiyu yudzi-m-thuria mumondowe, This govu-man has bestowed the crowning honours on his mumondo. After this he is not allowed to have another honour. Pass., Ku thuriua.
**Thuru.** *See* Duru. The pronunciation with *th* instead of *d* is the more correct one, it being the same as in Arabic, from which it is borrowed.
**Ti,** *n. encl.* (za). Pl. of Luti. Ushanga hiu una ti nire.
**Tia,** *v.a.* *See* Dia.
**Tia,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the giraffe.
**Tia.** *See* Dia.
**Tia,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Siwa. An orphan. From Ku tiatia: Muana hiyu ni tia, This child is an orphan; pl. Ana hia ni tia, These children are orphans. The compound Muana tia, pl. Ana tia, is often used instead of the single word Tia.
**Tiako** (often pronounced **Tshako**) (Kid.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Tako in Kir.; in Kij., *id.*).
**Tide,** or **Tite,** *adj.* *See* Pishi. Small. Nazi tite (pl. *id.*), A small cocoa-nut.
**Tieka.** *See* Dieka.
**Tiho,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) the hair of the tail of a cow.
(2) The beard of a goat, when worn as an ornament. On the animal it is called Kirevu.
(3) The hair from the shoulders of the mbiga, when worn about the arm; worn on the head it is called Kiru. Tiho is called Tiho, even on the animal. Tiho ya mbega, ya kiduroni.
**Tima,** *n.* (wa, hiyu, pl. *id.*, a hia), the name of a species of monkey. Tima ya viha. Tima sa madali, puku, etc.
**Timbiriro,** *n.* (ya, za), a place of refuge, where one flees to. From Ku kimbira. Niumba ya kaya ni timbiriro. Kula mutu yuna timbiriroye, a-yo kimbirira. Unguja ndiko timbiriro yangu, na-ko-kimbirira.
**Tindi,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Mudindi, the shrub), a fruit similar to the love-apple. Tindi singa tungudza, ela zi luakue punde; ni kilungo cha mdzusi sana.
**Tindira,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Mungina. Niasi sidzibula tindira. Vano ni tindira tuvu, ka va viere.
**Tinchikiro,** *n.* (ya, za), a hint; lit.

*Footer: 360*

---

## [PDF Page 374 — Dictionary Page 361 (Tin — Tum)]

  something laid across. From Ku kingika. Yudzigomba maneno ga tinchikiro, be nidzi-ga-mania, yudzi-ni-amba mimi; *e.g.* one says to his boy, in the hearing of some other person, Kaike kure uchi hiu; kuna aivi; aivi ka nuka kuani.
**Tingo,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kikonde. Skin, hide. Only used of animals. Radically, a screen. From Ku tinga. Dim, Katingo and Kitingo.
**Tiru,** *n.* (ya), thirst.
**Tite.** *See* Dide,
**To,** *adv. encl.* *See* Kirobo; Vinda; Hendo. Well; (K.) accurately, thorough, greatly.
**Tobo,** *n.* (ya, za). From Koba (?).
**Tofu,** *n.* (ya, za), the navel. Dim., Kadofu and Kidofu; magn., Dofu and Ridofu.
**Toka,** *v.* *See* Doka.
**Toka** (Kij.), *n.* (ya), lime. Toka ni ya Adzomba, ahafunirayo tumbaku, akandirayo niumba.
**Tomola.** *See* Domola.
**Tondo,** *n.* *See* Kombesi. (1) A small round fruit.
(2) A kind of snail.
**Tondolo,** *v.a.*, to pluck.
**Tondolo,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Muroi.
**Tonga,** *n.* Vana tonga ya nazi hiva; nazi zi bomu i hi! Munazi hio una tonga e.
**Tongo,** *n.* *See* Abisa. Ku longosua tougoni.
**Tongo,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Engelele). *See* Eruka; Munga; Mumbu. From Ku konga. Kironda kidzihenda tongo. Dzino rangu rina tongo. Gnania yuna dzidzo ra tongo. Mutu hiyu yuna tongo; dzidzo menga rina kibalazi, rilonda ku henda tongo. Nidziona atu airi, osi ana tongo. M'egnie tongo, One who is one-eyed.
**Tonsi,** *n.* (= Fionsa?). Ku piga tonsi. Nawe unapiga tonsi ya Kidigo.
**Tosa,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Murao. (1) The bowl of a tobacco-pipe.
(2) A tobacco-pipe. Tosa ni ya ku fuhira tumbaku.
**Tosha.** *See* Dosha.
**Tota,** *v.a.* (= Ku dzota, which is more generally used).
**Totofui,** *n.* (za), a quagmire (?). Totofui zi madzini, ela tove si-ndze.
**Tove,** *n.* (za), mud; (K.) slime, mire, dirt.
**Tove,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a species of animal. Tove ere angi.
**Tu, Du,** *particle encl.* *See* Dondola. Only, merely.
**Tuaha,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luhuaha. Muhoho akisa sikira, m-pige tuaha.
**Tuasi,** *n.* (ya, za), (1) the name of an insect, smaller than the mbosa.
(2) The honey deposited by it. Tuasi akala pangoni dza viratu niuchi. The tuasi live in holes of trees, in the same way as bees. Ni kama nkolokolo.
**Tuba** (Kid.), *v.n.* Madzi ganatuba; ga-sinda.
**Tubu.** *See* Dubu.
**Tuhu,** *n.* (= Tudu in Kij.), a wart.
**Tukuhu,** *n. coll.* (za), underwood.
**Tukana.** *See* Dukana.
**Tulu,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Fuanjo. Akiba; Dula; Murego; Muthego. A starting-hole. Dali ridziduluka tuluni; or, Ridzi duluka na tulu.
**Tulua,** *n.* (ya, za), the fruit of a shrub called mutula, similar to the love-apple. Tulua si-nga tungudza, ela ka-zi-riwa. Ahoho ni ku fuignia tulua. Tulua inadingidia, inafuina.
**Tumba,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Kns., Mumbu), the bud of a flower not yet opened. Tumba ya isu, or, ya mugomba; pl. Tumba za masu. Muhama una tumba (= Kij., Mtama una mimba). Tumba ya mukate.
**Tumbaku.** *See* Dumbako.
**Tumbi** (Kij.), *n.* (ya, za) (= Chungu in Kir.), a kind of basket made of mia, used in fishing (K.).

## [PDF Page 375 — Dictionary Page 362 (Tum — Uak)]

**Tumbiri,** *n.* (hiyu, pl. *id.*, hia), the name of a small monkey.
**Tumbo,** *n.* (ya, za), bowels, intestines. Gnombe hi ina tumbo; idzi ukuha sana. Muche hiyu yuremerua ni tumbo, Kid. (in Kir., Yudzimercrua ni tumbo).
**Tumbulio,** *n.* (ya, za) (= Tundumudzi). *See* Humbula. A starting-hole. Mutu akiona utu ui, u-m-kimbiza-o, kaupuka na mumfiria, ela yunaupuka na tundumudzi, or, na tumbulio.
**Tunda** (Kid.), *n.*, beads, fruits, fruit in general.
**Tunde,** *n.* (za). Pl. of Luhunde. Tunde za miridza. Tunde dzangu.
**Tundo,** *n.* (ya, za), fruit.
**Tundu,** *n.* (ya, za), a hole. Tundu ya sumba, The eye of a needle. Dim., Kadundu; magn., Dundu.
**Tundumudzi.** *See* Tumbulio.
**Tune.** *See* Dune.
**Tune,** *adj.* Gnombe tune.
**Tunga.** *See* Dunga.
  **Tungatunga.** *See* Dungadunga.
  **Tungitungi,** *adj.* (= Ndaundau), ready to run away or to escape.
**Tungu,** *n.* (ya, za), the fruit of the mutungu. It is eatable. Chende sa mbusi ni tune tu.
**Tungu,** *n.* (ya, za) (in Kij., *id.*), a vessel used for milking. From Ku chunga. Tungu ni kia, or, chia cha ku kamira masia. Tungu ya mbuyu, The shell of the baobab fruit, used as a milk-pail. Tungu ya nazi, The shell of a cocoa-nut, with the top cut off; of this the kaha and the kasi are made.
**Tungua,** *n.* (wa, pl. *id.*, a), the name of a species of antelope, somewhat larger than the sa. Ana malo sana.
**Tungudza,** *n.* (ya, za), the love-apple. Tungudza hisi sinasisima, ni mbidzo, ka-zi-udzungu. Mudungudza hiu ni musiru, tungudzase si-udzungu. Tungudza ya kidumbusi. Tungudza ya moyo wa gnombe.
**Turume,** *n.* (ya, za). *See* Kidurume. A ram. Turume ya gnonsi. Dim., Kadurume and Kidurume; magn., Durume and Ridurume (pl. Mi-).
**Turuturu.**
**Tusi,** *n.* (ya, za) (in Kij., Tuso). *See* Tusi in Kij. Remuneration for dancing or playing; lit. something produced or given out, a gift, a present. From Ku tusa. Hudzifuina uira, hudzitesa, be hu-veni tusi. Ku isa tusi.
**Tutu,** *n.* (ya, za), a wart, a pimple. Tutu si-nga ngoma, sipigua majira ga viha na majira ga ku uyiwa. Angue: Yapigua na gansa ra mutu ayeulagua. Nasikira tutu ikirira, visuka vinapigana, vinaroda viha (viha vindakudza).
**Tuvu,** *adj.*, bare, empty, mere. Kavu tuvu, An empty basket. Niumbayangu ni tuvu, ka-i-na kitu. Pinda hi ni tuvu. Ndimi kavu tuvu, ka-i-ingua kuku. Furaha tuvu, Mere joy. Dzima hi ni tuvu, ka-i-na mboga.

## U.

**U,** the twentieth letter of the alphabet; uniformly pronounced as in "full."—[ED.]
**U,** (1) 2nd pers. sing. of the pers. pron. *See* Mulungu; Luambo; Mfaramfara; Dzina; Peho, 2. Thou. Una; Uki; Udzi.
(2) *pron. acc.* *See* Esa; Ekemera; Kilome. It. Uchi u-sinda. Udzi-u-ona-vi we o utu?
**Uaki,** *n.* (wa). Uaki hiu uakao ka-u-nda ku fisha makomo; kundamera

*Footer: 362*

---

## [PDF Page 376 — Dictionary Page 363 (Uan — Udi)]

  lumfui na uaki hiu urio nao; na dzi yehu, ya Ravai, ka-i-henzi mutu muaki; ukiaka hivi kuna maishi.
**Uana,** *n.* (wa). *See* Doi.
**Uanguangu,** *n.* (wa) (= Udzangu), easiness, quickness; (K.) rapidity. N.B.—When quickly pronounced, it is Wanguangu.
**Uasi** (= Muagulu). Nere na uasi wa niumba.
**Ubadi, Ubati** (Kij.), *n.* Niumba ya ubatini.
**Ubagazi,** *n.* (wa).
**Ubahe,** *adj.* Utu hiu ni ubahe.
**Ubana, Upana** (Kij.), *n.* (wa) (in Kir., Walamu), width, breadth.
**Ubanangiko,** *n.* (wa). Ubanangiko dza hiu kahu-dza-ona. Ubanangikowe adzo-o-banangika ka-u-na muyawe.
**Ubanga,** *n.* (wa). *See* Golosera.
**Ubani,** *n.* (wa), (K.) gum.
**Ubau,** *adv.* (= Ungi), much. Utu hiu-wamba ni uchache we? si uchache, ni ubau.
**Ubembo,** *n.* (wa), flattery. Nidzikuenda kua maneno ga ubembo, ela kangalafia uchiwe.
**Ubesi, Upesi** (Kij.), *n.* and *adv.*, quickness, quick. Uhende utu wa upesi, wa haraka, usihende kondue, or, uere. Yuna maneno mapesi kagomba ku kondoefia. Kahale kitu hicho upesi, urehe.
**Ubishi,** *n.* (wa). *See* Golosa. Obstinacy. From Ku bisha. Si-ni-hendere ubishi.
**Ubodo,** *n.*
**Ubomu,** *adj.*, great.
**Ubomu,** *n.* (wa), greatness.
**Ubora,** *n.* *See* Bora. (K.) Energy, vehemence. Mahendo ga ubora (= ga muansa?). Gnania yuna-dzi-ika ubora.
**Ubumbafu, Upumbavu,** *n.* (wa), folly, foolishness.
**Ubuya,** *n.* (wa). Ni ubuya ela kanda-m-lola.
**Uchache,** *adj.* *See* Dzimfi. Few. Utu uchache. Moho ni uchache, nidzi-i-lavia mbidzi.
**Uchangamue,** *n.* (wa). Yudzi kupukua ni uchangamue, ni vidudusi vitite.
**Uche,** *n.* (wa), gruel.
**Uchi,** *n.* (wa). *See* Chayu. Palm-wine. Uchi wa niuki, Honey. Muegnie uchi kalala na ndzala. Dim., Vidzuchi; magn., Madzuchi.
**Uchia,** *n.* (wa), poverty. Uchia wangu nirio nao ni ungi-unionge wangu ni ungi.
**Uda,** *v.a.* *See* Ora. Only used with the reflex. Dzi. Ku-dzi-uda. Nidzi-dzi-uda kiniume, ei! nidzihenda vi.
**Udauda.** Ku tia yudzitia ela kudzi uda kadza mbue, or, kadzangue. Yudzi-dzi udauda yudzi-m-piga mbalahi ya niense. Nidzi dzi udauda nika-m-piga mbalahi ya madzo mairi. Kudzi udauda (= Ku dadalika).
**Udamba** (Kij.), *n.* (wa). *See* Mudamba. Ni utu ui. Dzoka ni udamba we, Mmasai. Ku-ku kenga.
**Udana,** *n.* (wa), (K.) youth, spruceness. Mutu hiyu yunahenza udana yukere fuina uira, ela angine rikasi adziricha kare.
**Udanganifu, Utanganifu** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), fraud, deception.
**Udasa** (Kij.), *n.* (wa) (in Kir., Wari wa kidzomba).
**Udembe,** or **Utembe.** Muhama hiu una udembe utite, or, vidembe vitite.
**Udende, Utende** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), operation, human action. Only used with reference to witchcraft. From Ku tenda (Kij.). Ni ukongo wa utende, or, wa mukono wa mutu, si ukongo wa Mulungu, It is a sickness made, or of the hand of man; it is not a sickness from God.
**Udide, Utite,** *adj.* (rel. to the U- class), small, little.
**Udide, Utite,** *n.* (wa). *See* Muluchiluchi. Smallness.

## [PDF Page 377 — Dictionary Page 364 (Udi — Udz)]

**Udirani, Ujirani,** *n.* (wa), neighbourhood, vicinity.
**Udirimfo,** *n.* (wa), edging. Kavu hina idzidirimfua to, ina udirimfu udzo.
**Udirira, Ujirira,** *v.n.* (= Ukilia in Kij.). *See* Fioga; Dzua; Sani; Mafungu; Mfanga. To purpose, to will, to intend; lit. to start up for. From Ku uka. Utu hiu udzi-u-uchirira, si sani, ni mbujirire. Ho! Mulungu kumba aka-hu-ujirira ku hu-angamisa! kumba ni dziku menga! Der., Mbujirire.
**Udiriri,** *n.* (wa) (= Madiriri), wantonness, spite, mischievousness. From Diririka in Kij. (?). Kare udiriri wari udzai. Mamboge ni ga udiriri udiriri mutu huyu hata kuamba ni hivo kare, angaambua ni mudzai, ela hikara kakuna udzai.
**Udogoi** (Kij.), *n.* (wa) (in Kir., Ndui; Tedekuanga), small-pox.
**Udohodoho,** *n.* (wa). Obs. Udohodoho ungi (= Mambo-mambo mangi).
**Udugu,** *n.* (wa). *See* Difia. Fraternity. Prov., Udugu ka-u-okua ukadzuka. Hata akihenda vi, ni nduguyo vivio, udugu ka-u-okeka, ka-u-uka.
**Udui,** *n.*, small-pox. Madzi ga peho ni udui.
**Uduku,** *n.* (wa). Uduku ni kudza weza hira kazi.
**Udula,** *v.a.* (= Humbulo), to break through. Gnombe yudziudula ta, yudziudula na hiva.
  **Uduka,** *v.n.* *See* Kombora. To burst.
  **Udulana,** *v. reit.* Atu adziudulana mavi.
  **Udulua,** *v.p.* Ei! yudziudulua ivi, si ivi ro!
  **Udulukiza,** *v.a.* (= Fumbulukiza). *See* Fudi; Bidikiza; Sisa. Lit. to let break through upon, to surprise. Nidzirima hata nidzikuenda udulukiza ueru wa dzusi. Hudzirima hata hudzi udulukiza ueru wa dzana, huaorima. Mfaya ya ku udulukiza, mfaya ya ku larikua. Gnania yudzi-ni udulukiza na charo.
**Udumani, Utumani,** *n.* (wa), surety, security. Gnania ndiye ayehala utumani, be hiye mutu ayehewa, si-mu-mania, ela na mania iye ayeingira utamani, or, ayekala mutamani. Gnania naye si mutu; dzusi ni-ki-mu-ingirira utumani nikihala, uchi niki-mu-va vino kahenzi ku riva; m'egniewe yuna-ni-sukasuka mimi hata dzana niki-m-rivira mimi; be mutu hiye kuonania ni mui we?
**Udune,** *n.* (wa), redness.
**Udune,** *adj.*, red.
**U-dza-cho.**
**U-dza-go.**
**Udzai,** *n.* (wa), witchcraft.
**Udzakazi,** *n.* (wa), (K.) gum arabic. Pfugo hi ina muga, ikasarua udzakazi.
**Udzanga,** *adj.* Uhumbo udzanga, The smaller intestines; in contradistinction to Uhumbo ukomu.
**Udzanga,** *n.* (wa), infancy. Ka-dza-niolua niere sa udzangani, He has not yet been shaved the hair of infancy.
**Udzangu,** *n.* (wa) (= Uanguangu), quickness. Opposed to Fuende.
**U-dza-o.**
**U-dza-ro.**
**U-dza-so.**
**Udzaye,** *n.*
**U-dza-yo.**
**Udze.** Muhi udzebua, Gnania udzebua (instead of yudzebua).
**Udzembesi,** *n.* (wa) (= Usinsi).
**Udzengo,** *n.* Uchi wa udzengo. Udzengo wa muansani. Udzengo wa muanso ni kihendo. Mbuzi

*Footer: 364*

---

## [PDF Page 378 — Dictionary Page 365 (Udz — Ufu)]

  ya udzengo mahendo ga muanso ubora.
**Udzerero,** *n.* (wa), the going down, setting, of the sun. From Ku dzerera. Muriango wa niumba yangu udzierekera udzerero wa dzua, or, muakani, or, furi.
**Udzi.**
**Udzigni.** Unga udzigni. Wisua udzigni, Fine chaff, bran.
**Udzikidzi,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kikonde. The fibres of the leaf of a species of palm, called mudzikidzi. Lukue lua udzikidzi ni lomu sana, A string made of udzikidzi is very hard, *i.e.* strong. The Wadigo even use it for bow-strings instead of kano.
**Udzo,** *adj.* *See* Ongoka. Good.
**Udzo,** *n.* (wa), goodness, neatness, beauty.
**Udzoro** (Kig.?), *n.* *See* Pombe. A kind of beer.
**Udzomba.** Unika kuwesa, na udzomba nao kuwesa; haya u-mutu wani we? una kazi yani we?
**Udzovi,** *n.* (wa). Udzovi wa haya. Udzovi wa madzo.
**Udzovi,** *n.* (wa). Udzovi wa muansani.
**Udzuerero** (wa dzua) (= Udzerero). Der. from Ku dzua dzuerera.
**Udzufu,** *n.* (wa).
**Udzumbe,** *n.* (wa). *See* Dzumbe. Gnania yuna-dzi-ika udzumbe!
**Udzumi,** *n.* (wa). Nari siidima ku eaenda kua udzumi.
**Udzungu,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kadzungu, 1. Kitu hiki ki-udzungu, This thing is bitter. Ku lumua ni uzungu, To be in pains of childbirth.
**Uendo,** *n.* (wa) (in Kij. = Charo), the act of going somewhere. Rero sina uendo, nasinda vavadi, nisuke pani zangu.
**Uenendo,** *n.* (wa), gait. The following Uenenzi is more frequently used. Uenendowe unga wa gnania.
**Uenenzi,** *n.* (wa) (= Maenensi), gait.
**Uere,** *n.* (wa), delay.
**Uerefu,** *n.* (wa), subtlety, dexterity.
**Ueru,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kusiko. The open country at a greater distance from the habitations of men than the luanda; but the words are often used promiscuously. Yukola luanda, yudzihenda ueru usima.
**Ueruve,** *adj.* *See* Giema. White. Ulongo wa mau ni ueruve dze.
**Ueruve,** *n.* (wa), whiteness; (K.) purity.
**Ufafui** (Kigir.) (= Uchangamue in Kir.).
**Ufaranga,** *n.* (wa). *See* Mufaranga.
**Ufiarirua,** *n.* (wa). *See* Mfarukira.
**Ufiasi, Uviazi,** *n.* (wa) (= Kifiasi). *See* Mviala. The act of bearing, childbirth, peculiarity of bearing, generation. Uviasi una-m-komia. Mtumche hiye akifisa ku viala, be akilumua ni uzungu, akale na mutu vevi, a-mu-vialuse; kuani udzunguwe ka-u-enderera; ndo uviaziwe u-ri-vio; a-si-vokala na mutu vevi, yundaviala hecheye.
**Ufiere,** *n.* (wa). *See* Niauka; Kidzaye. Seniority, old age. Ku vokana niama za ufiere. Angue: na-m-voka gnania ufierewe.
**Ufiosi,** *n.* (wa), scolding.
**Ufira,** *n.* (wa), pus, matter. Sikiro ri na ufira, u na sia.
**Ufo, Uvo** (Kinguchi), *n.* (= Kij., Uzuri), beauty.
**Uforo.** *See* Umforo.
**Ufu, Uvu,** *adj.* *See* Fu; Kifulusi. Hard, sour. Uchi ni uvu hiu, uhensa ku bisaniua, ka-u-noeka.
**Ufua,** *n.* (wa), inheritance. Muche wa ufua.
**Ufualo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Meneka. Apparel.
**Ufude, Ufuche,** *n.* (wa), a *slight*

## [PDF Page 379 — Dictionary Page 366 (Ufu — Uha)]

  eruption on the skin, thrown out by fever.
**Ufuende** (Kid.), *n.* (wa) (= Fuende in Kir.; Uere).
**Ufuerero** (Kig.), *n.* From Ku fuerera. Ufuerero wa dzua.
**Ufufi,** *n.* (wa). Yuere mufufi tu, ela hangu dzana yuna-dzi-onsola, hata ufufi yudzi-u-richa.
**Ufufu,** *adj.* (rel. to the U- class), narrow. Uriri hiu ni ufufu, ka-u-na ukalo, or, makalo.
**Ufugi,** *n.* (wa). Ufugi wa gnombe wansa, waansa na Abe Mkamba, wala Digo.
**Ufuha,** *n.* (wa), simsim, *Didynamia gymnospermia* (Owen, vol. i. p. 160). Ufuha ka-u-na haja na mvula.
**Ufuhi,** *adj.*, short.
**Ufuhi,** *n.* (wa), shortness.
**Ufuhufu,** *n.* (wa) (= Ni uerefu).
**Ufulana,** *n.* (wa), youth, the state of youth. Ufulanawe ukasisua, or, ukasiwa ni udana. Adzila ufulana.
**Ufumba, Uvumba,** *n.* (wa), scent, perfume.
**Ufumbani, Uvumbani,** *n.* (wa), mint.
**Ufumfu,** *n.* (wa), sadness, sorrow, grief.
**Ufusi,** *n.* (wa) (= Ufugi).
**Uga** (Kid. and Kij.), *n.* *See* Kuga in Kns. An open space in a town.
**Ugala.** *See* Kanani; Koma. Nalumua ni usiku ni ugala. Neno hiri rila usiku, rila ugala. Kitu hicho ki usiku, ki-ugala.
**Ugamamu,** *n.* (wa), mastership, skill in business.
**Ugambani,** *n.* (wa), a slight eruption on the skin. Ni vidudusi vitite.
**Uganga,** *n.* (wa) (in Kig., Bahari), witchcraft. Uganga si wa bule, ni wa mbuzi na gnombe. Gnania yudzilavia mbuzi na kipiga cha uchi, ka dzama ne, yunavima uganga, be dziku dziku ndzoni, hurie uganga. Gnania yun'enda lafiwa ndze uganga rero, huende hukanoe uchi wa uganga.
**Ugema,** *n.* (wa) (= Ngemua), the act of drawing the toddy. Ugemao ka-u-hama, u-foroforo. Ndo ugemawe agemavio.
**Ugeni,** *n.* (wa), strangeness.
**Ugeri.**
**Ugira, Ujira** (Kij.), *n.* (wa) (in Kir., Mafungu), wages.
**Ugnalo,** *n.* (wa), brightness, shining forth. Ugnalo wa dzua ukajira ugnalo wa m'ezi.
**Ugnaro,** *n.* (wa). From Ku gnara.
**Ugniagnanii,** *n.* (wa). *See* M'erefu. Violence.
**Ugnieti,** *n.* (wa).
**Ugosa,** *n.* *See* Uriro. Mukue, M'oria, Musave ka-i-valasika lukue; ina ugosa wa ku vagarira niumba tu.
**Ugula,** *v.n.*, to groan. Ugosa wa murihi ndo u sukuao lukue lua muhambo.
**Ugulo,** *n.* (wa). Ku dimfira mihaso ya fuo,
**Ugungu,** *n.* (wa), (K.) widowhood.
**Uha,** *n.* (wa, pl. Maha), a bow. Uha wangu udzidoroka luvohe. Dim., Kadzuha.
**Uhadaya** (Kij.), *n.* (wa). *See* Hadayo.
**Uhadi** (Kij.), *n.* (wa) (= Hadzidzi). Mudumia hiye yuna uhadi wa kare.
**Uhaki,** *n.* (wa) (= Haki). Hudzialamulua, nidzihewa uhaki mimi.
**Uhali** (Kij.), *n.* (wa). Ku dzi ika uhali (= Ku dzi ika ubomu, or, ud zumbe). Una-dzi-ika uhali; vana adumuao vano, hebo hebu vana muche, wambaye uhenderue ukahewe maguluni? Namba hosini hu alume ni charo kino; kula mutu ni ku henda kasi; ubora hiu u-dzi-ikao ka-u-hama.
**Uhalifu** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), transgression.
**Uhamfi,** *n.* (wa), travelling.

## [PDF Page 380 — Dictionary Page 367 (Uha — Uka)]

**Uhanda,** *n.* (wa), cleanliness. Ungasikira uhanda, be ni hiu; lola, vakue muhalani vadzidzuka.
**Uheresi,** *n.* (wa), slipperiness. From Ku heresa.
**Uhoho,** *n.* (wa), childhood.
**Uhoko,** *n.* (wa). *See* Dioko.
**Uhongolo.**
**Uhongozi,** *n.* (wa). *See* Langasa. Drowsiness.
**Uhuahui,** *n.* (wa). *See* Nianiasa. Uhuahuiwe wa ana ndio udzaojira vava, ukaviogavioga vitu viangu.
**Uhumbo,** *n.* (wa), the bowels, the intestines. Uhumbo ukomu. Uhumbo udzanga.
**Uhumiki,** *n.* (wa). Uhumiki wa punda sindawesa.
**Ui,** *adj.* *See* Omoka. Bad.
**Ui,** *n.* (wa), badness, wickedness.
**Uidi.** Uidi na ambari. *See* Muhaso (Kid.?).
**Uidzi,** *adj.* *See* Luchi.
**Uidzi,** *n.* (wa).
**Uifi, Uivi,** *n.* (wa), thievery.
**Uifu,** *n.* (wa), jealousy.
**Uiji** (Kij.), *n.* (wa) (= Musua in Kir.). Instead of Uji. Sina uiji walu sina udasa; *i.e.* Sina kimenga ni-ri-cho na-cho. Dzengo ridzi-ni-guira, sina uiji.
**Uikane,** *n.* (wa) (= Malagano). Dziku hio mino sindakudza, huna uikane wehu. Ndio uikane wehu huaaikana (= Ndigo malagano gehu huago lagana. A masai a henda uikane, or, malagano.
**Uima,** *n.*, standing. Mahomboge gakere uima. Mahombo ga uima, or, ga imire. Naingira niumbani muangu uima, I enter my house erect, standing.
**Uimbo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Esa. Singing. Gnania yunaimba to, uimbowe ni udzo.
**Uimo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Lenga; Duruma. Standpoint.
**Uina** (contracted from **Miina**), *n.* (wa, pl. Mina). Uina wa koe. Mina ya pania. Dim., Kadzina and Kidzina; magn., Dzina.
**Uinsa,** or **Uinsi,** *n.* (wa), hunting. Hua la uinsa ni, We come from hunting.
**Uira** (Ni uira), *n.* (wa, pl. Mira, Miira). *See* Wari; Kidosi. (1) A dance, dancing.
(2) A song; the words sung at a dance.
**Uira** (Ni uira), *n.* (wa). From Ku ira. Nina uira wa majembe. Atu-angu; muangu mudzini; ana uira sana.
**Uiri,** *n.* (wa).
**Uiru,** *adj.* *See* Funsarere. Black.
**Uiru,** *n.* (wa). *See* Mbawa. Blackness. Uiru wa dzidzo (= Chiru cha dzidzo), The iris.
**Ujiwa.**
**Uka,** *v.n.*, to get up, to rise. Uka, u-mu-vise mufiere kihi, asagale, Get up, give the elder the seat that he may sit down. Uika vo, unakazi yani we! Get up there, what business have you? Ku uka mbere, To start before others, to precede. Ka ki uka. Ka vi uka. Ka va uka. Der., Muikiro.
  **Ukika.**
  **Ukira,** *v. rel.* Ni-ukira-vo ga, nisi-ku-one! or, Nisakudza ku piga! Ni-ukira vo nawe, una kazi yani we! Ima, ni-ku-ukire, usakudza-ni-bimbinda, kuani uso-here ku piga atu! Mutu hiye yudzi-ni-ukira, nika-m-henda-dze? (= Yudzi-ni-mena). Niasi sidziukira, basi napiga mukambe.
  **Ukirana,** *v. reit.* Atu hio akaukirana, kapatana.
  **Ukisa,** *v.a.* (= Nionia). Uwe wamba: muanao kasikira, be kuka-mu-ukisa m'egnie fio? muana ni ku kaniua; ela uwe; kula ahendaro, ku-mu-kania, basi akauka navio (= akakula navio).

## [PDF Page 381 — Dictionary Page 368 (Uka — Ula)]

  **Ukua,** *v.p.* Udziukua we! (= Ni kidzoa), Art thou mad? Niukua ni utu, Something has come upon me.
  **Usa,** *v.a.* *See* Mdzusa; Gaula. To take off, to remove. Kuanza ku-dzi-usa, To begin to take one's self off,—said of growth; to appear to have grown.
  **Usira,** *v.d.* *See* Larika. Uki-mu-ona muyao, yudziniala kitu, be mu-usire, u-ki-ike vadzo; ndivio anadamu a-ri-vio; uki-ki-richa, be u-mui.
  **Usua,** *v.p.*
**Ukadi,** *n.* (wa) (= Makadi). Ukadi hio; hia gnania asiku ari ka-dza-fialua.
**Ukafiri,** *adv.*, unbelieving. Muana hiyu yunaria ukafiri ukafiri.
**Ukaha,** *n.* (wa), laziness.
**Ukala,** *n.* (wa), hunting; lit. an animal to hunt. Niama ya ukala, Venison. Fungu ra ukala. Dziku ya ukala atu akahenda mahunkue ga uchi.
**Ukalo,** *n.* (wa) (= Makalo). *See* Ufufu. Space, room. Ukalo wa dzi ka-u-ambua muyao: sengera hiko, ni ungi. Udzi songesa chingoyo ukaloni wangu (= ukaloni muangu).
**Ukambani,** *n.* (wa), a country some days' journey west of Mombas.
**Ukambi,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kidudusi. A cutaneous disease. Mutu aki kupukua ni ukambi ni ku pigua ulongo muiri osi na madzo gakapigua wanda, dziku tahu.
**Ukamiri,** *n.* (wa), completeness.
**U-ka-o.**
**Ukari,** *n.* (wa). *See* Mukari.
**U-ki.**
**Ukindu,** *n.* (wa).
**Ukobi,** *n.* (wa).
**Ukoko,** *n.* (wa). *See* Koko; Lukoko. Crust; lit. what is friable, fragile. From Ku koka. Ukoko ni wa dzulu, dzini ni makoko (pl. of koko). Wari una ukoko, ela koko ni hakoni mua niungu. Halani ukoko, murie. Wari ukiifua to, ndo uhendavo ukoko. Dim., Kakoko and Kikoko.
**Ukolo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Mafiosi. Dirtiness.
**Ukomo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Fuhira; Vesa; Nche. Limit, termination. Maneno gano gaambuago ukomowe nini? Neno rino ukomowe nini? Nidzisikira maneno gananenua, ela sika-ga-mania ukomowe, ukomowe nini vira? Vituvie ka-vi-na ukomo. Ndo ukomo hio.
**Ukomu,** *adj.* *See* Udzanga. Full-grown, mature.
**Ukonche,** *n.* (wa). *See* Umbuiga.
**Ukongo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Kongo). *See* Kongo. Disease, sickness. Ukongo u-m-luma-o ni ukongo wani? Dim., Kakongo and Kikongo; magn., Kongo (pl. Makongo).
**Ukuaju,** *n.* (wa). Ukihunda makuaju, basi ni ukuaju.
**Ukue,** *n.* (wa), the fibrous bark of a tree called mukue. Nila gaula ukue, wa ku fungira kivesa nina dzengo.
**Ukuha,** *v.n.*, to be satisfied.
  **Ukusha,** *v.a.*, to satisfy. Kaka ukusha, adziuka na ndzala sao, He did not satisfy them, did not give them enough to eat; they have gone off hungry.
  **Ukushua,** *v.p.*, to be satisfied.
**Ukulu,** *adj.*, great.
**Ukulu,** *n.* (wa), greatness.
**Ukurima,** *n.* (wa) (= Makurima; Mirimire), (K.) tillage.
**Ukuyu,** *n.* (wa). *See* Mukuyu. The milky sap of the mukuyu tree, used as a glue in making arrows of reeds.
**Ula** (Kidigo), *v.n.* (= Ugula in Kir.).
**Ulaga,** *v.a.*, to kill, to extinguish. Ku ulaga mfuaho (= Ku vesa). Ku ulaga moho (= Ku simia and Ku fumula). Ku ulaga madzina. Opposed to Mera.

## [PDF Page 382 — Dictionary Page 369 (Ula — Uma)]

  **Ulagana,** *v. reit.*, to kill each other.
  **Ulagira,** *v.d.* *See* Koso; Shononesera.
  **Ulagua,** *v.p.*, to be killed. Kuna mutu aulaguaye, akariwa niama?
**Ulula,** *v.a.*, to rummage. Obs. The Kij. word, Ku tafuta, is now more in use, though the meaning of this is a more general one—to seek. Gnania yukudza niumbani, yudziulula hata akaona niama kidzunguni, aka kata, akaria.
**Ulachu,** *n.* (wa), intelligence, wisdom, craftiness.
**Ulagane,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kilagane. Argument between many.
**Ulairo,** *n.* (wa) (= Uomborero). *See* Erekera.
**Ulaiti,** *n.* (wa). *See* Humbo. English cotton cloth.
**Ulalu** (Kig.) (= Wazimu in Kij.).
**Ulanga,** *n.* (wa), arrow-root. Muhama hiu udzikula, udzila ulanga. Kitu kira kidzila ulanga, ni kitu kidza cho kula.
**Ulave,** *n.* (wa), voraciousness, gluttony. From Ku lava.
**Ulili,** *n.* *See* Giru. Ndzo ulilini.
**Ulimbolimbo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mi-), (1) a species of thorn used by the Wasuahili on the coast for planting hedges. Luchigolue lua, lunawaka lunabula, lunakala muno.
(2) (= Udzadzi in Kig.), a milky juice, sap.
**Ulongo, 1,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kilongo. Clay.
**Ulongo, 2,** *n.* (wa). *See* Onia. A lie. There is a slight difference in the tone in which the two words Ulongo are pronounced.
**Ulosi, Ulozi,** *n.* (wa) (= Malozi), betrothal. Rero kuna ulozi; gnania yunaloza muanawe, be hu'enda hukanoe uchi wa ulozi.
**Ulula,** *v.a.* *See* Ula.
**Ulumbi,** *n.* (wa). Sindagomba ulumbi ungi. Musihende ulumbi wa Kidigo, wa ku enderesa maneno mudzana wadi, ka hunao kazi suino, kahuwesa ulumbi wa kidigo.
**Ulumbui,** *n.* (wa).
**Ulume,** *n.* (wa), (1) manliness.
(2) Membrum genitale maris.
**Ulungo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kilungo. Joint, articulation of limbs. Ulungo wa kigere, The joint of the wrist. Ulungo wa fuindi, The joint of the knee. Ulungo wa kiduro, The joint of the shoulder. Ulungo wa nionga, The joint of the hip. Ulungo wa kigniugnuniu, The joint of the elbow, etc. Kata ulungoni. Kumania ulungo we, kula niama ina ulungo we. Ulungo wa niama, A joint of meat.
**Uma,** *v.a.* *See* Loreka; Logeka; Madaro; Dandaza; Dangadanga; Koko. To harden, to dry. Vitu vidziuma, vidzikamana. Ku uma kigulu. *See* Kota. Muche hiye kauma kua mulume (= Kahurira va mulume). Ku andika ku uma, To begin to dry.
  **Umalala,** *v.n.* (= Fira and Fuka). *See* Kunsumana. To wither, to languish. Muhama udzevia na dzua, udziumalala. Muiri udzi-ni-umalola, siwesa.
  **Umalasa,** *v.a.* *See* Kidunganguo. To cause to dry up, wither.
  **Umia,** *v.a.* *See* Dangadanga; Chengeva. Nidzi-mu-guira, nidzi-mu-umia ndi, mukononi, sika-m-voniosa. U-mukaha mutu uwe! Ku-vi-umia vilungo, uka-vi-regesa dza muche m'egnie mimba; be kuhama we. Ku-mu-umia muana, Ka umia, He does not endure hardness (2 Tim. ii. 3).
  **Umira,** *v.d.* *See* Mbawa. Ku umira niama uimoni. Said

## [PDF Page 383 — Dictionary Page 370 (Umb — Umo)]

  of ants forming an arch; the natives say, Anaumira Mulungu angue unda bua, basi-a, u-lume itu dzalafu ni hadzidzi.
  **Umiria,** *v.n.* (= Fu murira). Mutu yuna umiria ye; hata ukajira vakue, yunaria wari, ka-ku-amba: karibu. Mutu hiye yunaumiria, kaogova kabisa, hata akakala atu kumi ku-mu-dzira iye, kakimbira, ni ku ima vavo ye. Mutu hiye-hata akakala na ndzala, akaumiria vivio, wamba: yudzeria, ka debuereka.
  **Umirisa,** *v.a.* Bumani unga, mu umirise wari, u-musua.
  **Umisa,** *v.a.* (= Fuhusa). *See* Niuluka. Madzere higa ni maidzi, ka-ga-anike dzuani, mukaumise, basi mudze muvonde. Ku umisa waraka kua, or, na mudzanga, To dry a letter with sand, by sprinkling sand on it. Ku umisa vilungo. Gnania ndiye adzaye-hu-umisa moyo, ela hudziamba: hukimbire.
  **Umisua,** *v.p.*, to be dried up.
  **Umizana.** Ku umizana moyo.
**Umba,** *v.a.*, to form, as a potter, to shape. Ku umba niungu, To make a pot. Maneno higa ni ga ku umba-dzi-gasigo lufumulo, wala gasigo kondo. Gnania akaumba mudziwe, kavana muana ahendaye budzo. Aumbaye dzi ni Mulungu; haya-na-we wamba: Nasumfia-dzi, isumbe, hata atu a-ni-kubali mimi, be unasinsa rohoyo m'egnie. Wamba: Una nguvu dza sa Mulungu we? Ela muana'damu yuna nguvu sani? Der., Maumbi; Maumbiri; Muumbi Uumfi; Miumbire; Niumba.
  **Umbana,** *v. reit.* Lukolo hilu lukaumbana to, lukabadana, mumenga wao akiona neno ra muyawe, ni ku-ri-imirira hata rikauka.
  **Umbika,** *v.n.* Mutu aki-ku-huma, ukakuenda humika kazi hira ukayo ambua, be ndiko ku mu-umbika. Muana hiye yudzi-ni-umbika, yudzihenda to. Na-mu-umbika mutu hiye.
  **Umbira,** *v. rel.*
  **Umbua,** *v.p.*
**Umbu,** *n.* (wa), beads. Ku buma umbu.
**Umbuiga,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mimbuiga) (= Lubugu), the name of a creeping plant. Ukonje we una nguvu ku sidi niusi sosi sa mihi mingine; ndo uhenduao kivula. Mutu aki hega muhambo kivula ni cha umbuiga. Luguelue hata lukapigua ni mvula ka-lu-ola haraka. Ka lu toka; ukonje we ni omo sana.
**Umenga,** *adj.*, one.
**Umenga,** *n.* (wa), oneness, unity. Nahuimeni umenga, hulonde gnonsi, huuse kiravo hiki, kikachopigua, kiuke. Kimenga may be used too in this instance for Umenga.
**Umera,** *n.* (wa). Prov., Va-ri-vo kuku ka-va-muagua umera.
**Umiro,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mimiro). *See* Linkua; Mare. (1) The throat. Ku-m-guira mutu umiro, To seize one by the throat.
(2) Voice, sound. Angine ni ku rira na umiro wa bambara. Angine ni ku rira na umiro wa bembere. Angine ni ku rira na umiro musiho. Angine ni ku rira na umiro muvudzu. Angine ni ku rira na umiro wa idzui. Angine ni ku rira na umiro wa ku ruruma. Bugno rina mimiro miiri, umiro musiho na umiro muvudzu.
**Umondo,** *n.* (wa). Ka-dza-timiza umondo wehu. Niama ya umondo.
**Umonkue,** *n.* (wa).

  Kihendo cha umonkue.
**Umvoro,** *n.* *See* Salama; Mbavu. Nidzi ku sia umvoro naenda kuehu.
**Una.**
**Unanasi,** *n.* (wa).
**Unda** (Kij.).
**U-nda.**
**U-nda-o.**
**Undi,** *n.* (wa), multitude, plenty.
**Undu,** *n.* (wa).
**U-nga,** *adv.* *See* Kara. It is like.
**Unga,** *n.* (wa). *See* Fumbula. Flour. Unga udzigni. Unga wa mihi (= muthea).
**Unga,** *v.a.*, to join, to unite. Ku unga maiyi mundani.
  **Ungaunga.** Huna ungaunga mifusi, hu-i-dzome.
  **Ungika,** *v.n.* Ka ku unigika niasi, si-madzi.
  **Ungira,** *v. rel.* Ungira ko, moho usadzupa, uka guira luandala.
  **Ungurira,** *v.d.* (= Kid., Ungula; Ungulula; Fulo ra niungu; Engulula in Kir.), to be bewitched, *e.g.* a plantation. Ku okodea ku ungula mundu.
  **Ungurirana,** *v. ref.*
  **Ungurirua.** Muaka hiu nidziungurirua sipatire kitu.
**Ungi,** *adj.*, much.
**Ungi,** *n.* (wa), plenty.
**Ungo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Maungo, *q.v.*).
**Unguana** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), freedom. Atu ni ku amba; ni munguana mutu hiye, ela kana unguana wa geri.
**Ungumbau,** *n.* (wa), valour, prowess. Mutu hiye ni ngumbau, be ungumbau-we ndo udzao-muulaga. Sudi uhende ungumbau, be na akili sikale simo, ungumbau uvuvu ka-u-fa, unda-ku-richa hata uulague, or, unda-ku-kenga hata uulague.
**Uniama.** *See* Fiarira; Unika. Hangudzana adzifiarirana uniama, kapatana kahiri kamare; kula muyawe, unika and udzomba. Yuna-m-londera muyawe (Kid., Adzigalukirana uniama).
**Unionge,** *n.* (wa). *See* Uchia. Weakness, need.
**Uniumbui,** *n.* (wa) (= Ulumbui).
**Uniunkui** (Kid.), *n.* (wa) (= Niunguniungu in Kij. and Niansi in Kins.).
**Uno.** *See* Himuno; Makira.
**Unoadzi,** *n.* (wa) (= Manoadzi).
**Unula,** *v.a.*, to lift up, to raise, to take up; (K.) uphold. Mu-unule ye muyao, u-mu-ereke, huenende, kasignia. Mu-unule muana, u-mu-rehe. Unula, usiregese! Lift it up, let it not go back, do not relax it. Ku unula madzo dzulu. *See* Angira.
  **Unuka,** *v.n.*, to rise. Yudzi-unuka, yudziima, A child.
  **Unukira,** *v. rel.* Niasi sidziunukira kaviri (= sidziukira). Ku-ni-unukira nini? ku-ni-henda dza muhi.
  **Unurika,** *v.n.* Ni kisiho ela kinaunurika. Ka-ki-unurika, ni kisiho muno.
  **Unurira.** *See* Mukoma.
  **Unurisa,** *v.a.* Gnania naye yuna-dzi-unurisa muno vio! basi dzi yosi kavana a-mu-pita ye, ni iye hecheye? Una-dzi-unurisa muno nawe! ndiwe umaniaye mambo hecheyo, ela atu kamania? Ako akao-ku-pita maneno, saidi ya uwe.
**Uo.** *See* Mau.
**Uokovu** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), deliverance, salvation. Rarely used. Uokovuwe ni ubomu adzi-o-ni-okola. Yudzi-ni-okola uokovu ubomu.
**Uolovu,** *adj.*, soft, mild. Uchi hio ni udzo, ni uolovu, ni wa ku bisania. Nalonda uchi uidzi, nirio nao ni ufu, nibisanie, ukale uolovu.
**Uolovu,** *n.* (wa), softness. Uolovu wa moyo, (K.) Meekness, lenity, etc.
**Uomborero,** *n.* (wa).

**Uongolo,** *n.* (wa), copal. Uongolo ni kithana cha muhi, uihuao muongolo. Uki kala uchache ni ongolo, If you have a little, it is Ongolo, but if much, M'ongolo or Wongolo.
**Upese.** *See* Ubesi.
**Upuka,** *v.n.* *See* Mfamfuka; Galukira; Tulu. To go out, to come forth. Kahu upukire-ndze kua mufungiso wa mvula. Dzua ridzi upuka, The sun has come forth.
  **Upukira,** *v. rel.* Atu hio ana tumbulio ya ku upukira ndze. A upukaye akaupukira ku ulague tu,—said when the Masai came.
  **Upusa,** *v.a.* *See* Ombosa; Kigota; Kogo. Ku upusa tulu. Yudzi-mu-upusa niumbani.
  **Upusana,** *v. reit.* Adziheha, adziupusana niumbani.
  **Upusika,** *v.n.* Kaupusika ndze, kuna peho muno, or, kuna dzua muno.
  **Upusira,** *v.d.* Hala io pfuko, u-mu-upusire kondze.
  **Upusua,** *v.p.*
**Urai** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), prudence, cunning. Nidziona madzi muhoni gadzikuta; nalola-kavana vatu va ku fukira, na mino siidima ku okerera, basi nikahenda urai hata nikapata vatu va ku fukira. Gnania ni muerefu nidzikuenda kua urai, nidzi-m-rai, nidzi-m-rai, hata yudzi-ni-pa kitu hicho.
**Ure,** *adj.*, long.
**U e,** *n.* (wa), length. Kare na ure.
**Urefi,** *n.* (wa), drunkenness.
**Urembo,** *n.* (wa, pl. Marembo), an ornament, decoration.
**Uresi,** *n.* (wa). Muche hiye kana uresi, yuna lukuare. Muche hiye kaidima ku rera muana tia, kamania uresi urivio.
**Urihi,** *n.* (wa).
**U-ri-ko.**
**Urimsi,** *n.*, a watch.
**Uringo,** *n.* (wa). Uringo wa ku rindira niuni. Kuere uringoni, ulagise atu niuni. Hala moho, ukabuse dzulu uringoni, u lorere niuni.
**Urinsi,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kigocho; Ndagisua; Marinsi. Nina urinsi, siidima ku uka kua niuni. Rero urinsi ni wangu, ni isarangu.
**U-ri-o** (rel. to the U- class). *See* Muvilivili. Which is; lit, it is which.
**Uriri,** *n.* (wa, pl. Mariri). *See* Ludzaga. A bedstead, bed, such as the Wanyika use. Uriri wa dandara. Uriri wa dzaga, Made of the boughs of cocoa-nut trees. This is now the common bedstead of an Mnika. *See* Ludzaga.
**Uriro,** *n.* (wa) (= Uniaudege in Kij.), the bark of the muriro. Ugosa wa muriro ndo uibuao uriro. Lukue lua uriro si ludzo kana lua unanasi.
**Urisa,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kindikindi. Yudziguirua ni urisa, kaidima kuenda dzadziga. Yudzihewa urisawe (= Ludzungo?). Udzi gula mbuzi be urisa wangu u-vi? sudi u-ni-pe ludzungo luangu, be uhale mbuziyo. Yudzienenda urisani (= Yudzidua arisa).
**Urogo.** *See* Rogo. Rarely used.
**Uruka,** *v.n.*, to fly.
  **Urukira,** *v. rel.* Yudzi-mu-urukira mutu, ku londa ku-m-piga.
  **Urusa,** *v.a.* *See* Dignia. Ku urusa niuni. Ku urusa ndada, hebu mifui. Yudzi-mu-va muchewe kaguo katite, kadzi-mu-urusa; opposed to Samia. Yudzifuala nguo tide, idzi-mu-urusa.
  **Urusua,** *v.p.*
**Urumengu,** *n.* (wa). *See* Madidimuko; Denga. The world. Utu hiu kahu-dza-ona hangu urumengu ku diekua.

*Footer: 372*

## [PDF Page 386 — Dictionary Page 373 (Uru — Usi)]

**Urungo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kihoho; Hambala; Muhuye. Ka-dza-oneka urungo. *See* Luasa.
**Urunsi,** *n.* (wa) Rero ni urunsi; mbona ka muka muagira urunsi? Resp., Kahunda henda muaka muvia baba yehu kavo. Kuamba peho mbi ijire.
**Usa,** *v.a.* *See* Uka. To remove.
  **Usira,** *v. rel.* *See* Uka.
**Usa, Uza,** *v.a.*, to ask; to ask, to inquire after, about. Nausa muche, nilole, I ask a woman to marry me. Ndiwe ukaye-mu-usa, be huna-ku-ria malu. Si use hiye muhoho, ka use mutu musima. Gnania yuna usa muchewe muno, Gnania asks much after his wife, from jealousy or suspicion, when she is absent.
  **Usana, Uzana,** *v. reit.*
  **Usika, Uzika,** *v.n.* Ka uzika.
  **Usira, Uzira,** *v.n.*, to ask for. Yu kuenda-mu-usira musenawe muche. Enda uka-ni-usire muche, ukiona yunahensa, udze, u-ni-ambire. U-usira-ni we? What are you asking for? Resp., Ah! sina utu, na-dzi-usira tu, ni-vi-manie.
  **Usirua, Uzirua,** *v.p.* Yudziusirua muche ni nduguye.
  **Usua, Uzua,** *v.p.*, to be asked. Yudzikuenda usua maneno, or, habari.
**Usafula,** *n.* (wa). Ku ingira usafulani.
**Usaha.** *See* Ufira.
**Usaha, Ushaha,** *n.* (wa). Ndo ushahawe tu, kibaria cha uchi. Ni ushahawe o-kahu-na-o kazi.
**Usana,** *n.* (wa). *See* Kulula. Smithery, *i.e.* the work done by a smith; but the workshop is called chanda. N'enda usanani, nika sanirue kifiu.
**Usangu,** *n.*, the state of being a contributor (?). Dzina ra usangu. *See* Musangu. Ku dzanga? Contribute.
**Usave,** *n.* (wa). From Musave. Usave wa ku vagarira niumba.
**Usena,** *n.* (wa), friendship.
**Ushaha.** *See* Usaha.
**Ushaka.** *See* Usaka.
**Ushanga, Usanga.**
**Ushangu,** *n.* (wa). *See* Engelele. Beads. Madzere gadzihenda ushanga; lit. The Indian corn has made beads; *i.e.* The grains have become as large as the beads used in their country—as a small pea.
**Ushuru** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), custom, dues, tribute.
**Ushururu,** *n.* (wa), tardiness. Ukiihua, ku uka, kudza haraka, be una ushururu.
**Usichana,** *n.* (wa). Mahombo gadzebua usichana unasira.
**Usiho,** *adj.*, heavy.
**Usiho,** *n.* (wa), (K.) weight, difficulty.
**Usiko** (Kigir.) (= Ukomo in Kir.). *See* Adzala. Meaning, signification.
**Usiku,** *adj.* *See* Ugala; Kanani. Pertaining to the night. Utu usiku.
**Usiku,** *n.* (wa), night. Usiku ukulu.
**Usima, Uzima,** *adj.*, well, whole.
**Usima, Uzima,** *n.* (wa), health, wholeness.
**Usinga** (Kid.), *n.* Usinga wa niumbue; pl. Singa, sa niumbue. In Kir., *n. coll.* (wa). Usinga wa tia. Uha hiu agafungua usinga. Usinga wa mukoma, wa mugumo.
**Usinsi,** *n.* (wa), adultery. Usinsi ni wa dzungu na niama, haya! suino anadamu hunta-u-richa dze? Horrible!
**Usinsisi,** *n.* (wa) (in Kij., Usingisi), sleep? sleeplessness? From Ku sinsira. Ku lala usinsisi, To lie awake. *See* Damana.

*Footer: 373*

## [PDF Page 387 — Dictionary Page 374 (Usi — Uva)]

**U-si-o.**
**Usiri** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), slowness. Mutu hiye yuna usiri, kandakudza haraka, mu-radireni. Una usiri muno we, ukiambirua neno ku uka haraka; u-nga dza ukayesarau atu.
**Usiri,** *n. coll.* (wa) (Kij., Mbu). Mumenga yunagnogna, ela ukikala ungi, wamba: unayoma.
**Usiru,** *adj.*, sour. Uchi hiu ni usiru, unarefia. Uchi wa minazi hio ni usiru.
**Usiru,** *n.* (wa), sourness. Trop., fierceness. Kabu hiri rina usiru.
**Uso,** *n.* (wa). *See* Sasira. Face. Uso na madzo, To one's face. *See* Luambo. Jembe ri dzi uka uso? Gnania yuna uso udzo.
**Usonia.**
**Usorodani** (= Lusonia; Dzonia). Naye yuna-dzi-ika usorodani, vi dze vio? na usorodani si wakue.
**Usubi,** *n. coll.* (wa), a kind of mosquito, a gnat. Usubi ka-u-rira, It does not sing.
**Usungu, Uzungu.** Uzungu wenu.
**Usunie,** *n.* (wa), (K.) bondage. Adigo kaogova usunie, Slavery. Usunie ka-u-dzuka hiraka.
**Usuri, Uzuri** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), beauty.
**Ususi,** *n.* (wa). Rero kuna ususi, aganga an'enda ku susa.
**Ususu,** *n.* (wa), silliness, foolishness.
**Utembe,** *adj.*, little.
**Utha,** *v.n.* Ndzoni huuthe; or, Ndzo huenende uthini, nika-ku-uthe. Ku niutha we. Hu-ve malu; muanao yudziutha kigogo cha kambi, yudzihukana kambi.
  **Uthana,** *v. reit.*
  **Uthika,** *v.n.*
  **Uthira,** *v. rel.* Kigogo cha ku uthira.
**Uthaka,** *n.* Abodaye shuhuku chiru ya ku londe muche (atamaniye), a-dzi-sagarire na uthaka, dzi kuye apate ku lumbaka (Ambrore) (= Ku rumbika).
**Uthalimu** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), iniquity, injustice. Gnania yuna maneno ga uthalimu; ungaona kahupatana, basi ni manenoge iye, ndiye asumfiaye mudzi.
**Uthua,** *v.p.* Hivara mbere viere vikiuthua ni kambi.
**Uthi** (Kij.). Utu hiu udzi-ni-uthi.
  **Uthika.** Yu uthika movoni.
**Uthi,** *n.* (wa), trouble.
**Uthia** (Kij.), *n.* (wa) (= Mosoka), difficulty, uproar. Ni uthia wani huno? Charo hiki chari na uthia ungi tu.
**Uthiki** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), oppression. Gnania yudziingira uthikini kua madeni ga babaye, kana uiji wala kana udasa. Ah! ni uthiki hiu;—baba ku hala madeni ga atu, akasa riva hata akafua, aka-ni-rijira mimi madeni; atu asiirua ufua ni babezao, mimi nidzisiirua madeni; be si uthiki u huno?
**Uthora,** *n.* (wa) (= Thora). A., Nina uthora wangu nagusa. B., Ni thora rani?
**Uthuri,** *n.* (wa). *See* Mudzovi.
**Uthuru** (Kij.), *n.* (wa), matter, cause, affair. Kuamba una kitu ni avasa, nidziguirua ni uthuru.
**Utu,** *n.* (wa), cause, matter, occasion.
**Uumvi,** *n.* (wa), the business of a potter. From Ku umba. Uumviwe ka-u-hama; niunguse ni mbidzi, ka-si-komia ku funsika; ela gnania-niunguse ni niomu, sikaifua.
**Uvalansi,** *n.* and *adj.*? (wa). *See* Soenesa. Unga uvalansi.
**Uvara** (Kig.), *n.* (= Ukali in Kij.). *See* Kidunusi. Maneno ga uvara.
