## [PDF Page 388 — Dictionary Page 375 (Uve — Va)]

**Uvere,** *n.* (wa) (= Pele in Kij.), the name of a cutaneous disease, the itch.
**Uverero,** *n.* (wa) (= Ukomo), the end, the extreme part of anything. From Ku verera. Uverero wa munda, The end of a field. Uverero wa mudzi, The end of a town or village. Uverero wa dzi, The end of a country; also the end of the earth.
**Uvia,** *adj.*, new. Rero hudziona utu uvia. Kudzikudza mambo mavia.
**Uvolue,** *n.* (wa). From Ku vola.
**Uvudzu,** *adj.*, thin.
**Uvudzu,** *n.* (wa), thinness.
**Uvuvu,** *adj.* Manenoge ni ulongo uvuvu. Wari hiu ni uvuvu, ka-u-na mboga.
**Uwe,** *pers. pron.* (in Kij. = Uganga), thou.
**Uya,** *v.n.* *See* Kala. To return. Musigo hiu ni mubomu, ela huno ukauya. Kasha hiri ni siho, ela hirino rikauya.
  **Udza,** *v.a.* *See* Fufuka; Demera. To return, to give or send back, to make turn back. Huende hukauyiwe.
  **Udzidza** (Kid.), *v.a.* (1) (= Udzikisa in Kir.), to answer, to reply. Yudzi-ni-ambira manenoge, ela mino si-mu-udzidzire.
  (2) (= Kumbisa in Kins.), to tantalize.
  **Udzika,** *v.n.* Ninga-i-udza, ela ka-i-udzika, idzi humirua kare (= niungu).
  **Udzikisa,** *v.a.* (= Ku lungukisa). *See* Hongosa. To answer. Yudzi-ni-usa maneno, be mino sika-mu-udzikisa. Yudzigomba nami, nidzi-mu-udzikisa. Nidzigomba naye, kaka-ni-udzikisa; mutu yuya ni ku-nimena hebu dze? Nidzigomba naye, ela yudzi-ni-udzikisa kua koro, I have spoken with him, but he has answered me in anger. N.B.—In this instance Udzikisa cannot be exchanged for Lungukisa.
  **Udzikisania,** *v. reit.*
  **Udzikisua,** *v.p.*
  **Udzira,** *v. rel.* *See* Karakara; Hongosa. Yudzi-ku-udzera neno rani? What did he or she answer you?
  **Udzirua,** *v.p.*
  **Udzua,** *v.p.*, to be returned.
  **Uyika,** *v.n.* Nidziamba niuye, ela ka-vi-uyika kua hiye mukongo.
  **Uyira.** Yuna-ga-uyira gara-tu mai, a-go-kala akihenda kare. Niki-m-kania, yunda-ni-uyira mimi, a-ni-rie malu.
  **Uyirua,** *v.p.* Yudziuyirua ni ukongo.
  **Uyisa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (in Kir., Ku udza), to return, to make return. Ku uyisa gnombe, To cause cattle to return.
  **Uyiwa,** *v.p.*, to be returned, to be driven home.
**Uyu,** *n.*, (1) (ra, pl. Mauyu), the fruit of the baobab.
(2) (wa). *See* Mbuyu. The mealy part of the fruit.
**Uyuya.**

## V.

**V,** the twenty-first letter of the alphabet, often confused with *f*, but must be pronounced uniformly as in English.—[ED.]
**Va,** (1) *gen. part.*, of.
(2) *See* Kokola; Mfaruka; Musiso; Lufundo; Dzimbika; Sikisa. Vaka vana vadzi, etc. Vadza vo vakavo, etc. Va-uke. Muche kiye kahurira va alume.
**Va,** *v. encl.* *See* Pa. Ku va, To give. Muana hiyu si-mu-ve kitu kaviri, uki-mu-va kitu yundaangamisa du.
  **Vana,** or **Vanana** (the latter

*Footer: 375*

---

## [PDF Page 389 — Dictionary Page 376 (Vaa — Vak)]

  form is more frequently used), to give each other. Atu hio anavanana. Ku vanana mikono, To shake hands.
  **Vua,** *v.n.* *See* Howa. To turn out much, to yield much; lit. to be given, increased — *v.p.* in form, but neuter in meaning. Muhama wangu udzevua (= udzila mungi). Madzere gangu gadzevua, gadzikala mangi. Madzere gano ka-ga-ka vua. Madzi gadzevua, gadziidzala muho dele. Wari hio udzevua, nidzievula dzima ningi. Unga wari utembe, ela wari udzevua. Munazi hiu unavua nazi; makumbi ni matite ela nazi ni bomu. Munda hio una nema, or, mbaraka, vituvie, ukifuna, vinavua.
**Vaana** (Kij.), *v. reit.* (= Ku dzuvana mifiu). *See* Odzania. To fight. Hu vaane na ndada, Let us fight with sticks,—in play only.
**Vadide,** or **Vatite,** *adj.* *See* Mfiela. Small.
**Vadide,** or **Vatite,** *adv.*, at most. Gnania yudzihoha madzini, vatite kuamba afue, ela gnania musiku ndiye adzaye-mu-difia, na kuamba seye angafua. Wari vatite kuamba aulague.
**Vadza,** *v.a.*, (1) (Kir.), to bind round, to enclose with cords a calabash. Kirenge kisicho ngada, ndo kivadzua cho kisimfaniuke.
(2) (Kid.) (= Ku vagala in Kir.; Kins., Yanga).
  **Vadzira,** *v.d.* and *instr.*
**Vadzo,** *adj.* (rel. to Vatu, which, if not expressed, is always implied). *See* Larira. Good.
**Vafufu,** *adj.* (rel. to Vatu). *See* Ingisika. Narrow.
**Vaga,** *v.a.*, to set a boundary. Ku vaga munda.
  **Vagala,** *v.a.*
  **Vagana.** Muvaga hiu ni wa gnania na gnania, ndio akao vagana hiva. Dzi ya Ravai na ya Duruma ikavagana. Hukavagana, ela kahuka vagana muvaga jembe.
  **Vagarira,** *v. rel.*
  **Vagarira,** *v. rel.*
  **Vagarirua,** *v.p.*
  **Vagasa,** *v.a.* Ku vagaza p'ekue.
  **Vagasira,** *v.d.* Hudzi-m-vagazira p'ekue, idzisira.
  **Vagasua,** *v.p.* P'ekue ya gnania dzana yavagazua.
  **Vagira,** *v.d.* Kavana kondo kahiri, hudzi-a-vagira. Prov., Mukongo kavagirua nkue.
**Vai,** *adj.* Nidzifu magua vai, nidziremesua.
**Vairi,** *adj.* and *adv.* *See* Kururika; Mani. Two; twice. Vatu vairi, Two places.
**Vaka,** *v.a.*, (1) to smear, to anoint.
(2) (= Ku tasa in Kir.), to touch at the side or edge, to border, to mark off as a boundary, to fix a boundary. In Kid., To touch slightly, in play. Ku-dzi-vaka mafuha, To rub one's self over with oil or grease.
  **Vakana, Tasana** (Kir.).
  **Vakira.**
  **Vakisa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Pakisa in Kir.).
  **Vakua,** *v.p.*
  **Vakuza,** *v.a.*, to wipe off. Ku vakuza fumbi midzanga, etc. U-ni-vakuze.
  **Vakuzana,** *v. reit.*, to wipe or brush one another. Hudzivakuzana midzanga.
  **Vakusika,** *v.n.* Kam'ka vakusika to, muna midzanga.
  **Vakuzira,** *v. rel.* Mutu hiye kana mumfera, yu-nga kuku ariaye, akavakusira-dzi.
  **Vakusua,** *v.p.*

## [PDF Page 390 — Dictionary Page 377 (Vak — Van)]

**Vaka.**
**Vakavo.**
**Vaki.** *See* Erua; Nche.
**Vako.**
**Vakue.** *See* Meneka; Vevera; Kadzeha.
**Valakahi** (Kid.) (= Ivo ra kahi in Kir.). Vanda rikala valakahi (in Kij., Banda lina ngia ndiani).
**Valala,** *n.* (ra, pl. Mavalala), honeycomb.
**Valamu,** *adj.* (= Vaalamu). Vatu hiva ni valamu.
**Valavala,** *v.a.* *See* Vara. To crave, to hunger. N'enda nikavalevale mudzere wa pania ludzagani. Moyo una-ni-valavala kua ndzala.
**Valadza** (Kid.), *v.a.* (in Kins. = Ku rudzurura niama!), to glean. In Kir. the word is obsolete, being superseded by Ku dondola and Ku dzaira. Ku valadza luguani.
**Valala,** *v.n.* (= Regarega). Yudzifuala midirima, ela inavalala kua muiri kuonda. Nidziona, midirima yangu inavalala.
**Valaza,** *v.a.* (= Bandabanda; in Kij., Basa; Ku midza). *See* Mudza. Ku valaza lukue. Ku valaza niere. Ndzo, u-ni-valaze nierezangu, valazire. Ku valaza madzere. Rero navalaza kidzomba, nihende wari wa kidzomba.
  **Valazika,** *v.n.*, to admit of.
  **Valazira,** *v.d.*
  **Valazua,** *v.p.* Lukue hilu ka-lu-ka valazua to, lunafuguka. Ela gnania akavalazua vidzere, kana muyawe.
**Valula** (Kidigo), *v.a.* (= Vavula in Kir.), to pluck off, to tear off. Ku valula madzere, To tear off the leaves from a cob of Indian corn. Ku valula milala.
**Varikiza,** *v.a.* (= Mutikisa; Bumira), to splice.
  **Variravarira,** *v.d.* Ima, nika-ku-varirevarire mudzere wa pania, nawe upate kibaba, ukahendere ahoho.
**Valu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Kota. A spar or pole used in building a hut or house. Mavalu ga chuma, Bars of iron, as imported from Europe.
**Vamenga,** *adj.* *See* Dzua (at the end); Muando. One. Vatu vamenga. Nidziguira mani vatu vairi, ndzo, nika-ku-ve vamenga, nawe urime.
**Vamenga,** *adv.* *See* Nundu. Together, once. Ku buma vamenga.
**Vana,** *v. reit.* *See* Vaana.
**Vana,** *v. reit.* *See* Va. To give one another.
  **Vanana,** *v. reit.* *See* Va. To give one another.
**Va-na,** *adv.* *See* Lambualambua; Fufu; Mudzi; Mbawa; Era; Mudana. Wherewith; there is, there are.
**Vana,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Kij., Bana, pl. Mapana). *See* Malamu. Width, breadth. Nguo hi ka-i-na vana. Vana ra chansa cha niumba.
**Va-nda,** *n.* (pl. Ma-). *See* Dzimbika.
**Vanda,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-) (= Sansu; in Kij., Banda). *See* Chignie; Shamia. The fruit-branch of a palm tree in a state when the flower-buds are still enclosed within the sheath. It is from this that the toddy is procured by binding it tightly, and then tapping it. A slice being cut off every time the toddy is drawn, the branch is finished in about two months, when another is attacked. Vanda ni sansu ri-fiala-ro tundo. Vanda ra munazi-ra mugumo-ra mulala.
**Vanda,** *v.a.* (= Ku niala; in Kir. the latter is more frequently used, while in Kidigo and Kig. the former is exclusive). *See* Mesa. To plant. Suino hunawiha mundani, hukavande.

## [PDF Page 391 — Dictionary Page 378 (Van — Vay)]

**Vanga,** *v.n.* (= Ku vava), to spread. Muhi huno udzivanga muno. Mudzungu na murenge ni ku vanga. Kunde za Kitaita, sikinialua kuehu, ni ku vanga, sikalonda ku hambala dza mikunde ya kuehu, be ka-si-henda muno.
  **Vangula,** *v.a.* (= Dzansula). Ku vangula pfuiho.
  **Vangurika,** *v.n.* Lufuiho hilu luka vangurika to, or, luka vangulua to.
  **Vangurira,** *v.d.*
  **Vangusa,** *v.a.* (= Ku vakuza), to wipe.
**Vangina,** or **Vangine,** *adj.* (rel. to the word Vatu, which, if not expressed, is always implied), other.
**Vangu,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to Vatu). *See* Mfaruka. At mine; *i.e.* at my place.
**Vani.**
**Vano.** *See* Dudula; Fiarira; Meto. Ku la vano hata muhondo. Vano va nani, What.
**Vansi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a noose, a running knot. Dim., Kavansi and Kivansi.
**Vara,** *dem. pron.* *See* Doka; Fufu; Golosa.
**Vara** (Kigiriama), *v.n.* (= Valavala in Kir.), to crave. Only used of hunger. Ndani yangu ina-ni-vara.
**Varatu,** *n. pl.* *See* Mfungu; Mukuyu; Kidzaye. Sandals, shoes.
**Vari** (= Vere?). *See* Futika; Lungukisania; Kelia.
**Va-ri-vo.**
**Vasiku,** *adj.* *See* Gomana; Cha; Deria.
**Vasima.** *See* Kidambo. Vatu vasima.
**Va-si-vo,** (K.) but, save, without.
**Vatite.** *See* Vadide.
**Vatu,** *n.* (va). *See* Dundisa; Umadza. Place. Vatu hiva.
**Vava.** *See* Dzuerera; Kua; Sohesa; Kuku. Vava hurivo, Here, where we are. Vava ni-ri-vo, Here, where I am. Kuamba uere vava dzana, ungahewa niama.
**Vavo.** *See* Mugafii; Rinda. Hangu vavo ana kondo, be vino vidzisidi, basi ndo ku dana. Vatu vava, hu-ri-vo vava, ndi-vo va-vohendeka utu usiku.
**Vava,** *v.n.* (= Ku vanga), to spread. Murenge hiu udzivava, hata udzifika mbere.
**Vavika,** *v.n.*, to vomit.
  **Vavisa,** or **Vaviza,** *v.a.*, to make vomit. Muganga yudzi-ni-pa muhi wa ku-ni-vaviza.
**Vavula,** *v.a.* (= Valula; Mihi ikao demua kansa, etc.). Navavula milalayangu idziuma. Ku vavula madzere, To take off the leaves from cobs of Indian corn.
**Vavarika,** *v.n.* *See* Babarika. Derived from Ku vala, Valavala, with a reduplication of the first syllable. Moyo una-ni-vavarika kua ndzala.
  **Vavarikua,** *v.p.* Ku vavarikua ni moyo (= Ku eresua ni moyo), To feel squeamish.
  **Vavarisa.**
**Vavasa,** *v.n.* *See* Vala. To grope, to grubble. Usiku wa kisa ni ku vavasa. Mukono unaluma uvavasaye hebu dze?
**Vavata** (= Hapahapa).
**Vavayuka,** *v.a.* *See* Wasimu; Raruka. To turn mad.
**Vavika.** *See* Vava.
  **Vavisa.** *See* Vava.
  **Vavula.** *See* Vava.
**Vavo** (= Vava). *See* Gande; Ririra; Omeka; Kita.
**Vaya,** *v.n.*, to jabber. Gnania yunavaya vio, ku vaya kuani ko? Der., Bayo, Luyago, with their dim. forms.
  **Vayavaya,** *v. reit.* (= Ku bayabaya in Kir.). *See* Lufunsu; Elemea; Wayawaya. To be delirious, to talk nonsense. Unavayavaya, dza kuamba una vidzoa.

## [PDF Page 392 — Dictionary Page 379 (Vay — Ven)]

**Vayuya,** *adj.* (rel. to Vatu). *See* Udula. Light, easy.
**Vedaka** (?) (= Yu sidi in Kij.). Ina veduka reale.
**Vegnia,** *v.n.* *See* Kochesa. Der., Pegnie; Kavegnio, etc. Magn., Seka.
  **Vegniavegnia,** *v. reit.* Nidzi-dzi-vegniesa, nikavegniavegnia hata nikaupuka.
  **Vegnieka,** *v.n.* *See* Fufu. Va-gagaga mihi, ka-va-vegnieka.
  **Vegniera,** *v. rel.*
  **Vegnierana,** *v. reit.* Kahuvegnierana niumbani, kahupatana.
  **Vegnieza,** *v.a.*, to wriggle. Ningaenenda atu a vavo njirani, be nika-dzi-vegnieza kura kandakanda, nikajira.
  **Vegniezera,** *v. rel.* Yudzi-ni-vegniezera muhi hiko ndani, basi mino ni-ndze, nika-u-hala.
  **Vegniezua,** *v.p.*
**Veha,** *v.a.* (= Kig., Veda), to bend. Naveha pehe, iveheke. Guira lufuiho, u-lu-vehe hivo chomboni.
  **Vehana,** *v.n.*, to bend with, *i.e.* round anything. Muhi hiu ukavehana na muyawe, This tree has bent with, *i.e.* round its neighbour. Mihi hino ikavehana, These trees have bent round each other.
  **Vehanavehana,** *v. reit.*, to bend with repeatedly.
  **Vehaveha,** *v. reit.* (= Dengeleka). Yudziusa malo, akavehaveha, akaangamika. Niama hiye yudzi-hu-dengeleza, yudzivehaveha muno, ela hudzi-m-dua, hata hudzi-m-pata.
  **Veheka,** *v.n.* (= Kunsika). *See* Koba; Mfuha. Muhi hiu ukaveheka.
**Veka,** *v.a.* (= Va), to bark, to roar. Dzua rinaveka, rinadzoma muno sana. Dzua ridzikola, rinaveka, kakuenendeka, kudzihenda dzapiu. Kuro ni ku veka, A dog barks or yelps. Denge hiyo inaveka, ku amia: ei! inaamia i-henda veka. Mutu hiye yuhenda veka halisi-kurirakue. Ah! mutu hiye yudzihendua-dze ye? yunaveka. Der., Luveko; Veku.
**Vekedza,** *v.a.*, to drill. Ku vekedza moho. Nidzivekedza moho hata nidzi-u-dieka; udzebua, nidzi-u-busa.
  **Vekedzeka,** *v.n.* Moho ka-u-kavekedzeka, ka-u-kabua.
  **Vekedzera,** *v. rel.* *See* Lurindi; Kika.
  **Vekedzerua,** *v.p.*
**Vekera,** *v. rel.* *See* Luveko. To bark at, to bounce out at, to roar out at. Kuro yudzioua-ni akiveka, yuvekera-ni? Kuro yuna vekera mugeni, The dog barks at a stranger. Una-ni-vekera vio, nidzi-ku-henda-dze?
  **Vekerana,** *v. reit.*, to bark at one another, to roar out at one another. Kuro anafumirana, anavekerana. Atu hio anafiererana, ahendavekerana.
  **Vekuka,** *v.n.* Lungo hilu ludzivekuka, lukala veku.
**Veku,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), a winnowing-basket when worn out. Lungo luangu ludzikala veku.
**Vendo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the stomach of birds.
**Venduka,** *v.n.* (= Ogola). *See* Funsa. Mutu hiye yudzivenduka niuma, yuna-ni-lola.
  **Vendukira,** *v. rel.* Yudzi-ni-vindukira niuma, aka-ni-lola.
  **Vendula,** *v.a.*
  **Vendulua,** *v.p.* Niasi sidzivendulua; pindilo zi lola mbere kuko huendako.
**Vendusa,** *v.a.* (= Chakana).
  **Vendusika,** *v.n.* Moho ni mungi, ka-ri-vendusika, nindavia (= dzere).
  **Vendusira,** *v. rel.*
  **Vendusua,** *v.p.*

## [PDF Page 393 — Dictionary Page 380 (Ven — Vi)]

**Venuka,** *v.n.* Nidzi-m-venula muiya, udzivenuka, udzila.
  **Venurika,** *v.n.* Muiya hiu u-kure, ka-u-venurika, ka-u-lafika, udziguira niama dzanga.
  **Venurira,** *v. rel.* Muche hiye yuna luguare yudzi ni venurira nguo.
  **Venula,** *v.a.* (= Funula), to lay open, bare. Namema muiya, be ni-u-venule, I dig for a thorn in the flesh, so that I may lay it open.
  **Venulua,** *v.p.* (= Ku koma).
**Vera,** *v.n.*, to cease growing. Mutu hiyu yudzivera, kakula kahiri. Mugomba hiu ni kigulue, vavo urivo udzivera, ka-u-kula kaviri, ndo kimoche.
  **Verera,** *v. rel.* (= Ku sika, Ku koma), to cease at, to terminate. Munda wangu ukaverera hivora.
  **Veruka,** *v.n.* Yudziveruka (= yudzidzaduzuka), kana mafuha. Abe Gunja yudziveruka, yukala mueruve dze, yudziguira kidzomba.
  **Veruza,** *v.a.* Ku verusa madzo. Der., Uverero.
**Vesa, Veza,** *v.n.* and *a.* (= Sindikiza). *See* Kidahi; Kulukira; Fumikisa; Moro; Dzumbe; Enderesa. (K.) To nictate. Muhama hiu unavesa, varatu uansavo ku henda mimba. Kakula kaviri mutu hiyu, yudzivesa, kimoche kidzikoma, or, yudzikoma ukomo. Na-ku-vesa kare. Gadzivesa-dze maneno higo? Note: To denote cessation of growth, Ku vera and Ku vesa are used promiscuously, but in the other meaning the latter only is used.
  **Vesana,** or **Vezania,** *v. reit.*, to see one another. Huavesania kare ku onana, We did not see each other for a long time.
  **Vesavesa,** *v. reit.*, to twinkle, to see; (K.) to wink. Yunavesavesa mutu hiyu ni muifi. Yunavesavesa mutu hiyu ni mukimbisi, etc. Kuona dzidzore rinavesavesa? Niegniesi ni ku vesavesa, A star twinkles.
  **Vesera,** *v. rel.* *See* Pindo; Ludzidzi. Gadzigombua gadzivesa-dze? Resp., Gadzivesera gnania ndiyei mulongo, arive; ndo gadzavovesera. Gadzigombua, hata gadzivesera hivo. Uveserowe gadzivesera-dze?
**Veruve** (contracted from **Vaeruve**), *adj.* (rel. to Vatu). *See* Yalada. White, clear.
**Veta,** *v.a.*, to winnow.
  **Veteka,** *v.n.* *See* Gaansa. Madzere higa ka-ga-veteka, yudzibuma madzimangi.
  **Vetera,** *v. rel.* *See* Dzungira. Reha, ni-ku-vetere. Lungo lua ku vetera wisua.
**Veva,** *v.n.*, to fly, as a feather, chaff, etc. Ukiveta, wisua ukaveva, ku upuka himura lungoni. Muhama unaveva, udzifira, ka-u-na tembe. Nioga sa kuku ni ku veva dzulu na peho. Der., Kiveveya; Muveveya; Luveveya.
  **Vevaveva.** *See* Nundu.
  **Vevera,** *v. rel.* *See* Funuka. (K.) To fan, ventilate. Muhama udzivevera. Mutu hiye yudzifira, yudzivevera, kana vakue, wala kana muche. Hala kivevero, uvevere moho, uake.
  **Veverua,** *v.p.* Ku veverua, na kivevero.
**Vevi,** *adv.* *See* Mulungu; Kosera. Near, nigh. Na vevi. Ndzo vevi we, Come you near.
  **Vevivevi.** *See* Muroana. Near together, dense, close.
**Vi,** *a prefix* indicating the pl. All words beginning with Ki or Chi form their plurals by changing the Ki or Chi into Vi. *See* Usuia; Shukushula.
**Vi,** *pron. acc.* (rel. to the Vi- class of nouns). *See* Duru; Vindi; Gundisa. Them, they. Si-

## [PDF Page 394 — Dictionary Page 381 (Vi — Vig)]

  vi-manira ukomowe; lit. I not to them know its meaning; I know not the meaning of these things. Vi stands often in a general way for the subject spoken of = these things. Vi fa iye mamoye akadzagula m'egnie. Sometimes the noun to which Vi refers is not expressed, but implied. Vi hama ku ogesua viromda.
**Vi,** *adv.*, where. It is an encl., and therefore stands always at the end of a word or sentence. U-la-vi? Thou comest from where? Yudziviala mutu wa-vi? meaning, of what sex? Resp., Yudziviala muche, or, mulume. But when the stress lies on the question where, and is therefore to be placed first in the sentence, Lua is prefixed. *See* Lua-vi.
**Vi,** *n. pl.*, bad things.
**Vi,** *adv.* *See* Fuina. Badly. Ku nuka vi, To smell badly. In this instance the Vi may also be taken as the acc. of the noun, bad things. Prov., Ka-vi-ola vidzo.
**Via,** *gen. part. pl.* *See* Ndagisua. Of.
**Via,** *v.n. encl.* (Ku via). *See* Vosera; Afiwa. To burn, to be on fire, to be consumed with fire.
  **Viera,** *v.a.* Airi a viera moho, Two were burnt by fire.
  **Vierera,** *v. rel.* Unaricha niumbayo na mifusi dza kuamba ni dzalani; ni-pa lufiero, ni-ku-vierere. Kakahenza kuenda longozua, yudzivierera kaya, yudzilalama m'egnie.
  **Vierua,** *v.p.*, to be burnt.
**Viako.**
**Viakue.**
**Viangu.**
**Viao.**
**Videbe.** Obs.
**Vidembe,** or **Vitembe.** *See* Nionga. Gnombese ni vitembe vivi. Stating the mere fact, you must say correctly, Gnombese ni tembe. Kavana uchi wa keri hiva, ni vitembe. Vana vitembe via uchi vava, ndzo, ni-ku-dzumbuse. Nidzi-mu-va vidembe (obs. videbe).
**Video** (Kij.). *See* Chunu. Yudziingira videoni, or yu-videoni.
**Vidi,** *n.* (via). Pl. of Ludi. Vidi via ushanga. Ushanga hiu una vidi vifuhi, or, vidi vire. Ushanga hiu unagusua muhama, vidi mirongo miiri kua kunsa.
**Vi-dze** (= Vikakaladze?).
**Vidze,** *particles* used in conjugation, 3rd pers. pl. perf. (rel. to the words of the Vi- class). They have varied for euphony according to the antecedent noun.
**Vidzi,** the same as Vidze.
**Vidzi,** *n.* (via). *See* Kula, *n.* A little water. Dim. of Madzi. Reha vidzi, Bring a little water. Kavana madzi? Resp., Vidzi ni vitembe.
**Vidzo,** *adj.*, good.
**Vidzo,** *n.* (via), goodness. Prov., Vidzo ka-vi-ola.
**Vidzoa,** *n.* *See* Raruka. Insanity.
**Vidzuchi,** *n.* (via). *See* Dayu. A little toddy, or palm-wine. Dim. of Uchi.
**Vidzufu.** *See* Fumba. Pl. of Kidzufu (?). Naria vidzufu.
**Vidzunga,** *n. pl.* (= Unga utembe). *See* Kifoyero. A little flour. Dim. of Unga.
**Vidzuniu,** *n. pl.* (via), a little salt. Dim. of Muniu.
**Vie.**
**Viedi,** *n.* (via). Pl. of Chedi. Nidziona vatu, vana viedi via atu.
**Viehu,** *pron.*, our, ours.
**Vienu,** *pron.*, your, yours.
**Viere.** *See* Ngari. Ka-vi-ere viangu.
**Viero,** *n.* *See* Chero. In the same manner.
**Vigongogo,** *n. pl.* (via) (= Viombo), vessels.

## [PDF Page 395 — Dictionary Page 382 (Vih — Vio)]

**Viha,** *n.* (via). *See* Muroana. War, battle. Atu adzifunga viha, kuenda pigana. Amasai adzi-hu-piga viha.
**Vihama,** *n. pl.* (via), a little sorghum, Guinea-corn. Ni-pa vihama vitembe.
**Vima,** *v.a.* *See* Munguchi; Uganga. To inquire. Ku vima uganga, To inquire by witchcraft. Ku vima kihendo cha muansa. Ku lavia vitu borani, ku vima muansa. Yunavima muansa kuamba akale bora. Ka-dza-kala bora, yukere vima, or, yukere musangu.
**Vi-nda** (rel. to the pl. form Vi-, but often used in a general sense, without referring to a particular word). *See* Gundisa. They will the things, etc. Vi-nda-vio, They which will.
**Vinda,** *v.a.* (in Kig., Veda; Kij., Pinda), to bend. Ku vinda uha. Ku vinda luvohe uhani. Ku vinda lufu, ni ku fimba madzo, na milomo, na ku golosa mikono na magulu. Yudzefua ku-dzi-kunsa, ka-vari na mutu wa ku-m-vinda. Ku dzi vinda m'egnie. Mutu hiyu yudzefua to, karakara yudzi-dzi-vinda m'egnie, kaka-dzi kunsa vatu.
  **Vindana,** *v. ref.* Anadida; maneno higo ga ku vindana.
  **Vindika,** *v.n.* Uha hiu ni omu, ka-u-vindika.
  **Vindira,** *v.d.* Na-m-vindira uha.
  **Vindua,** *v.p.* *See* Mufuhufu. To be bent. Der., Pindilo.
**Vindi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Muagalo; Chunu. (1) Lit. a bend, what is bent or wound round; a string of beads, or a chain, such as are worn round the neck and round the waist. Vindi ra ushanga; pl. Mavindi ga ushanga ga chununi, hebu ga dzingoni. Vindi ra mukufu, A chain sufficient to pass round the neck once.
(2) Trop., a trick. Yudzi-ni-piga vindi, be ka-vi-na dzambo, ela nda-ri-dandaula, ka-vi-nda-m-fa, He has played me a trick—lit. wound something round me—well, never mind, I shall wind it off; it will be of no use to him. Dim., Kavindi and Kivindi.
**Vindo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). *See* Fuluka. Udzifulukani mo vindoni?
**Vi-nga.**
**Vingari.** *See* Makira.
**Vingaringari,** *adv.* Ku lala vingaringari. Yudzebua vingaringari.
**Vi-nga-vi,** how many.
**Vingi,** *adj.*
**Vingu,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-). Magn. of Pingu.
**Vinio,** *n.*, wine.
**Vino.** *See* Gada; Kasa; Fumukana; Mudiriri; Peho, 2; Kongo; Boka. Niumba hi idzi vierua to e; idzidzuka; si vidzo vino?
**Vinono.**
**Vinonu** (Kidigo) (= Vidzo in Kir.).
**Vio.**
**Viomu,** *adj.*, harsh, severe.
**Viomu,** *adv.* *See* Chavu; Chignie; Lulaka. Harshly, forcibly. Kare viomu, Very long ago, of time immemorial. Mutu hiye yunanena viomu, yunafiola.
**Vioni,** *n. pl.* Nidziona vioni, kahi ka-vi-onewa, nindufua. Muanakuku hiyu ni vioni; yudzifialua na magulu ga ku vovoka. Kuku hiyu ni vioni; yudzihehera na usiku: yudzi-hu-onia utu undaokudza; be nahu-mu-ulage, utu udzaoroda, upigue ni muthana, usidze. Kuku akidieka na usiku, ni ku ambua ni mui, or, ni vioni, akadzinsua. Kaniama kano kaumbuadze? ni vioni hivi; mu-ulageni. Kid.,

## [PDF Page 396 — Dictionary Page 383 (Vio — Vok)]

  Muana hiyu ni vioni (= jego, pl. Ma-, in Kir.).
**Viosi,** *adj.*, all.
**Vira,** *dem. pron.* *See* Ukomo; Isika; Mafuemfuere; Ririra (ria); Lenga; Gnieta.
**Vira-tu,** *n. pl.* *See* Likira; Tuasi; Mulungu. Sandals, shoes.
**Virenge.** Ku lavirua virenge.
**Viri,** or **Viiri,** *v.n.* *See* Isa.
**Virika,** *v.a.*, to send; (K.) convey, bring. Muche akihalua, wawe ndiye, a-mu-virikaye kua mulume.
  **Virikana,** *v. reit.* Hudzivirikana ku rima.
  **Virikira,** *v. rel.* *See* Funsira. Ku-m-virikira mutu kitu. Hala kitu hiki, uenende, uka-m-virikire nduguyo.
  **Virikirana,** *v. reit.*
  **Virikirua,** *v.p.*
  **Virikua,** *v.p.* *See* Funda.
**Viringania,** *v.a.*, to cross. Ku viringania magulu, To cross the legs. Niukue sidziviringenia, The ropes have crossed each other, have become entangled (= sidzifungana).
  **Viringanika,** *v.n.* Lubugu hilu ludziviringanika muhini (= ludzivongoloka muhini ludziguira muhi muyawe).
**Viriviri** (?). Rero ni viriviri.
**Viru,** *adj.*, black.
**Visa,** *v.a.* (= Pisha in Kij.). *See* Uka; Ishima; Kufia. To let pass. Nidzi-m-visa njirani. Uka! mu-vise kihi, asagale.
  **Visavisa,** *v. reit.* M-loleni mutu iye, yudzi-dzi-visavisa, hata yudzikimbira.
  **Visana,** or **Vizania,** *v. reit.* *See* Moma. To let pass, to miss one another on a journey where it was expected to meet. Hudzivisania njirani. Mudzivisania-vi, kam'kaonana? Where have you let each other pass, that you did not see one another? Yusegere yudzivisania magulu, He is sitting with his legs crossed.
  **Visaniavisania.** Ukikala ukienenda, magula gana visaniavisania.
**Vishuari,** *n.* (via, sing. not in use) (= Ku tokosa in Kij.), provocations, instigations to strife, causes of strife. Especially used of children. Una vishuari, ulonda kondo? Yuari yunalonda vishuari kasidi, kuamba muhehe.
**Visia,** *n. pl.* (via), a little milk. Dim. of Masia.
**Vivi,** *adv.* (= Hivi). *See* Lika; Kuluvisa; Wasimu; Dzuesa; Lola; Muniale; Dovola; Muigni; Kimo; Ampika. (K.) Thus.
**Vivio,** *adv.* *See* Kasa; Dukanisa; Ekemesa; Elemea. Notwithstanding.
**Vivirero,** *adv.*, instantly, immediately.
**Vo,** *pron. acc.* *See* Arivo; Ayo; Osivo; Esa; Lungukisania; Mudana; Sika; Uka; Pigana. Them. Vatu unda-vo-kala vosi; or, Vatu vosi unda-vo-kala. Adzidzoka vo arivo.
**Vo,** *adv.*, there. Luvande lua-vo ikua, lukahalua niani? lit. Piece it was there put, it was taken by whom? The piece put there, by whom was it taken? Ndi-vo a-vo rima mundawe, Here it is where he made his plantation.
**Vodza,** *v.a.* (= Ku hunda). Obs.
  **Vodzerua.**
  **Vodzia** (Kij.), *v.a.*, to spoil the taste for one thing by taking another. Ku vodzia uchi, To take out the taste of toddy by eating meat.
**Vogoka,** *v.n.* (= Ku vovoka). *See* Gome. To be crooked. Der., Pogo; Pogopogo.
  **Vogokavogoka,** *v. reit.*, to be crooked at several places. Mihi hiyo ikavogokavogoka, ka-i-hama.
**Voka,** *v.a.* (= Dzadza in Kir.).

## [PDF Page 397 — Dictionary Page 384 (Vol — Von)]

  *See* Musimu. To take from, to bereave, to deprive, to rob; to dip, in Kig.
  **Vokana,** *v. reit.* *See* Ufiere.
  **Vokeka,** *v.n.* Gnania kavokeka, yudziguira niamaze na ku kimbira tu, atu aka-m-sola, akaremua.
  **Vokera.** *See* Mborera. (1) To hand over, to deliver up. Mutu akidzukula musigo, be uki-m-rajira, ukihala hura musigo, ukidzukula uwe, be udzi-m-vokera.
  (2) To receive. Na mutu aki-ku-va kitu, ukigolosa mukono ku-ki-hala, be unavokera. Uki-ni-pa kitu, ntavokera, sintakahala.
  **Vokerana,** *v. reit.* Ku vokerana misigo ku afuisania.
  **Vokesa** (Kid.?), *v.a.* (in Kir., Richisa; Rikisa).
  **Vokodza,** *v.a.* Ku vokodza tumbaku. Ku vokodza mihaso.
  **Vokodzeka,** *v.n.* Ererangu ka-ri-vokodzeka, u-ni-vokodzere.
  **Vokodzera,** *v.d.*
  **Vokua,** *v.p.* *See* Runda.
**Vola,** *v.n.* *See* Noeka. To cool. Vola we-vola muenehu, siluale! Der., Pola; Uvolue.
  **Vosa,** or **Voza,** *v.a.*, (1) to cool.
  (2) To greet. Obs. Uk'enda, uka-m-voze mucheo.
  (3) To heal. Muganga hiye yudzilagula, kakavoza, yudzikimbira ukongo.
  **Vosera, Vozera,** *v.d.* *See* Rikumba; Cherusa; Dubuikiza; Ku sira; Karakara na wari. Na-mu-vozera muananga wari, uvole, asivie. Nidzcria, ela sikavozera, mdzusi u-sira, ka-u-ka vozera. Mdzusi hiu ni mungi, mundavosera wari.
  **Vosua, Vodzua,** *v.p.* *See* Kiremba. Udzivosua ni gnania.
**Volofu,** *adj.* Vatu hiva ni volofu.
**Volovondo,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the name of a bird. Volovondo ri-nga puembe, ela ro ni bomu.
**Vomu,** *adj.* (= Vaomu). *See* Mfungu; Kilongo; Rimika.
**Vona,** *v.* Ah! nidzivona; nidziamba: nindaria uvuvu; kumba Mulungu yujari na-mi; nidzivona, nidzipata mboga, n'enda nikachite, nihende na wari.
**Vona,** *v.n.*, (K.) to swoon.
  **Vonioka,** *v.n.*, to drop.
  **Voniosa,** *v.a.*, to let drop. Ku vonioza tero. Ukikuera muhi, ukavoniosa, undakua.
**Vonoka,** *v.n.* *See* Ifua. Wrench, contort, writhe. Isu ridziifua, ridzihenda vonoka. Mababayu gadziifua, gadzihenda vonoka.
  **Vonokera,** *v. rel.* Mababayu ga gnania gadziifua, gadzihenda vonokera mumo dzulu, galonda kuola.
  **Vonola,** *v.a.* (= Ponoa in Kij.), to heal. Ku vonola ukonje.
  **Vonoreka,** *v.n.* Ka-u-vonoreka, udziumalala (= ukonje). Konje hiri rinavonoreka to; or, Ka-ri-vonoreka, rinadokadoka.
  **Vonorera,** *v. rel.* *See* Ponola.
**Vonda,** *v.a.* *See* Ku bunda; Ku vioda; Ku ihuaza;—all are different kinds of pounding. To pound in a mortar. The native women clean the husks from rice, etc., by pounding. Mudzere ga ku vonda, Pounded grain of Indian corn.
  **Vondeka,** *v.n.* *See* Niauka.
  **Vondera,** *v.d.*, to pound to, for. Ni-pa madzere, ni-ku-vondere, nipate wishua, Give me the Indian corn; I will pound it for you, that I may get the bran. H'endeni huka vondere wishua, huhende musua, hudzome moyo, Let us go and pound for the chaff (*i.e.* to be given the bran for wages); let us make gruel and warm the heart. Gnania

  yukuenda-vi? Resp., Yukuenda vondera.
  **Vonderua,** *v.p.*, to have another pounding for you.
  **Vondua,** *v.p.*, to be pounded.
**Vongavonga,** *v.n.*
  **Vongoloka,** *v.n.*
  **Vongolokana,** *v.n.* (= Shongolokana).
  **Vongolola,** *v.a.* *See* Loamia. (K.) Crankle, distort. Ndo utu wa mutu mukaha, akisagala ku-dzi-golola, ku-dzi-vongolola. Unahenda ku-dzi-vongolola dza nioka, undahenda kasi rini we? urie vio.
**Vonioga.** *See* Vona.
  **Voniosa.** *See* Vona.
  **Vonoka.** *See* Vona.
  **Vonola.** *See* Vona.
**Vonje,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-), the meat under the wing of a bird, one-half of the breast. Vonje ni ra niuni.
**Vosa.** *See* Vola.
  **Vosera.** *See* Vola.
**Vosi,** *adj.*, all. Vatu vosi.
**Vovoka,** *v.n.* (= Ku vogoka; Ku ogola). *See* Vioni; Dididi. To present a curve, to be circuitous, to be or to get bent. Njira ikavovoka, ka-i-ka goloka, The way is winding, it is not straight. Nidzirima kumba vana iwe-be nikadema, jembe rangu, rikavovoka. Nidzirima, nidzidema musi, jembe rangu rikavovoka.
  **Vovokavovoka,** *v. reit.*, to be curved or crooked in several places, to be circuitous. Used of trees and ways.
  **Vovola,** *v.a.* (= Ku vongolola). Yudzi-lu-vovola (lukuni), hata aka-lu-dosa. Nidzi-lu-vovola, ludzi-ni-remesa. Nidzi-mu-vovola mikono, nidzi-m-lumisa.
  **Vovolavovola,** or **Hoholahohola** (Kig.). Ku dzi hoholahohola.
**Vua.** *See* Va.
**Vuda** (Kig.), *v.a.*, to rob.
  **Vudua,** *v.p.* Hudzivudua njirani, hudzivudua misigo yehu pia.
**Vudi** (Kig.).
**Vudzu,** *adj.*
**Vula,** *v.a.* *See* Dania; Hafunika. To take off as a burden, to relieve. Ku vula musigo, To take down a load from one's head; or, Ku-dzi-vula musigo. The word may be constructed either with or without the reflexive particle Dzi. Navula, or, Na-dzi-vula pfuko yangu. Ndzo, u-ni-vule, Come and take down my load.
**Vukuhika,** *v.n.* (= Bugudika; Kutika). *See* Gniotoka; Ifuira. (K.) Crumble, decay. Nazi zidzivukuhika, be ni ningi; nazi menga wamba: idzigniotoka, idzebua. Maembe gadzivukuhika, gadele dzi. Ulongo hiu unavukuhika, ka-u-hama (= unamuafuka).
**Vukusa,** *v.a.*, to break off the cobs. Ku vukusa madzere. Madzere ga ku vukusa, Indian corn broken off from the cobs.
  **Vukusika,** *v.n.* Dzere hiri rinavukusika to, ni rolofu.
  **Vukusira,** *v.p.* Na-mu-vukusira gnania madzerege.
  **Vukusua,** *v.p.*
**Vulula,** *v.a.*, to strip off, to rub the face in washing it. Ku vulula mbalazi, makodza. Ku vulula uso, To rub the face. Ni-pani madzi, nivulule uso.
**Vulurika,** or **Vururika,** *v.n.* *See* Kutika; Pfu. To come off, to become lean, to be stripped. Mbalazi zidziifua muno, zinavulurikadzi, The peas have not yielded well, I have not gathered them.
  **Vulurisa,** or **Vururiza,** *v.a.* *See* Soenesa. Ku vururiza ushanga.
**Vulumuka.**
  **Vulumula,** *v.a.* (= Furura).
  **Vulumurika.** Musua hiu ka-u-vulumurika, u-moho.

## [PDF Page 399 — Dictionary Page 386 (Vum — Wan)]

  **Vulumuza.**
  **Vurusa** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Gutusha in Kij.), to startle.
**Vuma,** *v.n.* (= Tumuka in Kins.), to throb. Kironda kinavuma bu-bu-bu, The boil throbs.
**Vunga,** *v.a.* *See* Dzapiu. Ku vunga pepo. N'enda nikafunse ufumbani, nikavunge (= nikakute usiri) usiri niumbani, uupuke. Yudzi iha muganga kudza vunga muchewe pepo.
  **Vungira.** *See* Muingo.
  **Vunguka,** went.
  **Vungukirua,** *v.p.* (= Bungukiwa in Kij.; Ku dzikirua = Dusa, or Dusha in Kij.), (K.) derogate. Gnania yudzivungukirua, hangu dzana kana kitu.
  **Vungula,** *v.a.*, to diminish. Uvungule wari hio, usayuva, Take out something from that rice, lest it run over. Nakala muhi, ni-u-vungule visikuvisiku.
  **Vungurira,** *v.n.*, to abate, to subside. Peho idzivungurira (= idzivunguka; idzihurira). Ku-mu-vungurira muyao muhi.
  **Vunganika** (Kig.), *v.n.*, to be ashamed.
**Vuruza,** *v.a.* *See* Vula. To startle.
**Vuva,** *v.a.*
**Vuvu,** *adj.* *See* Lukarekare; Luveve; Ebula; Uvuvu. (K.) Naked, empty. Dzua vuvu. Yu-vuvu, He is naked. Mukamba yu-vuvu.
**Vuvu,** *n.* (ra). *See* Mudindi. Emptiness.

## W.

**W,** the twenty-second letter of the alphabet, pronounced as in English.—[ED.]
**Wa,** (1) *gen. part.* (rel. to the wa class), of.
(2) *pron.*, 3rd pers. pl., they.
(3) *See* Kinuda. It was.
**Wa,** or **Waa.** Mvulapala-wa-ikajira.
**Wacha,** *v.a.*, to grill, to roast. Nawacha niamayangu, nihende mihanda, isaola.
  **Wachawacha,** *v. reit.*
  **Wachira,** *v.n.* Ni-pa kifiu nikawachire niama.
**Wacho,** *n.* (wa, pl. Niacho). Kuanika niama wachoni. Na kota wacho, nianike niama.
**Waeria,** *adv.*
**Wagoria,** or **Wagoroa,** *adv.* Nasinda majero na muhondo, ela wagoroa be nadza.
**Waka,** *v.n.* *See* Mukono. To last long. Luchigo lua ulimbolimbo lunawaka, lunakala muno. Niumba hi inawaka, mihiye, ni miomu. Nabuma mihi ya, kulungire ya muvingo, ndivo niumba inda-vo henda waka. Nguo hi ka-i-daruka hiraka, inawaka.
**Wakili,** *n.*, a steward.
**Wako,** *pron.*, they, their; at their place.
**Wakue,** *pers. pron.* *See* We. He, his. Wangu ni muyuya, ela wakue ni musiho (= musigo).
**Wala,** *adv.* *See* Lukuare. Either, or, neither, nor. Trop., Uala, from Ku ala.
**Wala,** *n.* (wa). Wala ni wa ludzaga.
**Walala,** *adv.*, even, level with the top. Said of dry measures. From Ku lala. Nidzibuma kunsa walala, sikaidzasa.
**Walamu,** *adj.* (rel. to the U- class), wide, broad. Uina walamu, A wide hole.
**Walamu,** *n.* (wa), width, breadth.
**Wali** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, pl. Ma-). *See* Mula.
**Wamba,** or **Waamba.** *See* Malola; Kidzafukusi; Madaha.
**Wamba,** *n.* *See* Luago; Ndulu. Opposed to Lulongo. Atu hio anaenenda wamba, Those men go abreast.
**Wambo,** or **Wambu** (= Niumbo). Ninaambula wambu.
**Wanamo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Luhula. Wax. Kithana cha muhi. Wanamo wa tuasi, ndio ufundiriruao pembe ya kilido,

*Footer: 386*

---

## [PDF Page 400 — Dictionary Page 387 (Wan — Waz)]

  The wax of the tuasi is said to be better than that of the bee. It resembles mudungu.
**Wanda** (Kij.), *n.* (wa, hiu, no pl.). *See* Ukambi. Antimony.
**Wangu, Uangu,** *n.* (wa), quickness, promptitude. Mutu hiye akihenda kaziye, yuna wangu. Ku kakata niumba, kuna wangu, ela ku aka kuna uere.
**Wangu,** *poss. pron.*, my, mine, at my place, my home.
**Wanguangu,** *n.* *See* Uanguangu. Mutu hiye kana wanguangu, makasige ga-pore.
**Wani** (contracted from **Waani**), *interr. pron.* (rel. to the Mu- and U- class). *See* Mudana; Muansa. What?
**Wania** (Kij.). *See* Doroseka.
**Wao,** *poss. pron.*, they, theirs.
**Wao** (= U-ri-o, Kig.). *See* Gansa; Chaje.
**Waraka** (Kij.), *n.* (pl. Niaraka), a letter.
**Warawara,** *adv.* Si hendeni midzi warawara, midzi ya koma.
**Wari.** *See* Futu; Richisa. Mutu hiye wari akaangamika, rero yudzisumbuka.
**Wari,** *n.* (wa). M'ana mudzanga yunanuka wari. Niumba hi inanuka m'ana mudzanga, inanuka wari.
**Wari,** *n.* (wa), food made of rice or of ground Indian or Caffre corn, which constitutes the chief meal of the day, and is eaten in the evening. Wari wa Kidzomba, It is so called when made of dzenga.
**Warikon** (properly **Uariko,** from Ku arika). *See* Muhinio; Muahi. The wound made by circumcision, when fresh.
**Wasiwa,** *n.* Neno ra wasiwa ni neno ra atu a kare, ra kufua mki-sii-rana.
**Wau,** *adv.* *See* Lukarekare; Songa; Dzongo. Gnania waika muhamawe ukisagala wau hata majira ga masika, basi ndo avo-u-amula, ukiriwa. Gnania waika muhamawe wau hata majira ga masika, basi akagusa; ndivo apata-vo thora ridzo. Kuani: majira ga mafuno, atu akipiga muhama, akapima mirongo mine kua reale; ela majira ga masika akapima mirongo miiri na dzano kua reale.
**Wawa,** *v.n.* (= Luafu; Lunafu; Luambe; Lunambe). *See* Luambe. To itch.
  **Wawira,** *v. rel.* (Uwowadze?). *See* Huahuira. Yudzihega unga wangu, yudzi-u-wawira.
  **Wawisa,** *v.a.* *See* Oka. Luambe lua muhama lunawawisa. Luafu uki-lu-kusa, lunda-ku-wawisa.
  **Wawiwa,** *v.p.* *See* Kuna. (K.) Ninawawiwa, To be prurient. Ninawawiwa ni luambe (= Muiri una-ni-dadarika kua luambe). Muhi hiu unawawa, be uka-u-kusa, unawayiwa.
**Wawe,** *n.*, (1) (wa and ya, pl. *id.*, za), grandmother. For the 1st pers. of the poss. pron. (my), wa is used, but for the rest ya. (1) Sing., Wawe wangu; Waweyo; Waweye; Wawe yehu; Wawe yenu; Wawe yao. (2) Pl., Wawe sangu, My grandmothers, seldom or never used, as is the case with Mayo; Waweso, Thy grandmothers; Wawese, His (her) grandmothers; Wawe sehu; Wawe senu; Wawe sao.
(2) (hiyu, pl. hia, *id.*, hia). Yukala misini mua mikoko-kariwa.
**Wayawaya,** *v.n.* Ubume, i-idzale, ela isimuagike wayawawa. Nasikira wayawaya. Yudzinona hata yudziwayawaya.
**Wazimu,** *n.*, giddiness, madness. Ku henda wazimu (= Ku guirua ni kidzoa, or vidzoa, and Ku vavayuka). Mvula

*Footer: 387*

---

## [PDF Page 401 — Dictionary Page 388 (We — Yab)]

  idzi-ni-lavia wazimu; nda dzomekesa niumba yangu vivi rero; usiku-cho nidzifudzirua. Nda-ku-piga, ni-ku-lafie wazimu, uhende akili.
**We,** (1) *poss. pron.* *See* Wakue. His, her, its.
(2) *pers. pron.* *See* Mulungu; Nundu.
**Wegnie** (for **Uegnie**), *pron.* *See* Meguka; Mukuamba; Gumo; Mumondo; Hege. Itself.
**Weha** (Kidigo), *v.a.* (= Ku yeya in Kir.), to seek, to search.
**Wehu,** *poss. pron.* (rel. to M-, Mu-, and U- words), our.
**Weka,** *v.a.* (= Ku samia), to put aslant. Kirenge una-ki-we-ka-uchi unda muagika. Weka luiga, uchi udze vevi, udzove to. Weka sikiro, usikise to, peho i-la-yo kure, i-ingire masikironi, be usikire.
**Wenda** (for **Uenda**). *See* Kidzimbuiriri.
**Wende** (= Uendego). *See* Ganjaganja.
**Wende,** *n.* (wa). Muganga hiyu yuna wende, atu osi pia 'enda kuakue; kula mutu pia yuna-m-londa iye. Kuna wende we ku fialua na-o.
**Wenga,** *n.*, wearisomeness. Makasi higo ganalumisa, gana wenga. Mutu yuna wenga hiyu! ku foya tu, ku foya tu! mu-veni, a-hu-usire wenga, Oh this wearisome man, or woman; being always begging! Give him, to get rid of his teasing us; lit. that he may take from us the wearisomeness. Atu ana wenga muno hia! a-veni, aenende! Muana yuna wenga hiyu, ku rira tu! (= lufunsu).
**Wesa, Weza** (Kij.), *v.n.* *See* Kalanga; Mafungiso; Lilia; Lumbana. To be able, to be well. Si wezi, I cannot; I am unwell.
  **Weseka, Wezeka,** *v.n.* (= Idimika in Kir.). Mulungu kawezeka gakue; sinda shindana na Mulungu, naricha.
**Wiha** (Kidigo), *v.n.* *See* Hua. To go.
**Wimbi,** *n.* (wa). *See* Luinda; Koe. A wave.
**Wino,** *n.* (wa). *See* Funsarere; Gondoera.
**Wio** (Kig.), *n.* (wa, pl. ) (= Luchigo in Kir.). Ku piga wio.
**Wira,** *v.a.*
**Wiriwiri,** properly **Uiriuiri,** *adv.* *See* Darasira; Kuachira. Indistinctly; lit. a state of being twofold, a duplicity. Nidzi-mu-ona mutu wiriwiri.
**Wisira,** *n.* (wa). *See* Nkuadu. Pain, tooth-ache. From Ku isira, Ku isa. Wisira ni wa meno. Meno gangu gadzihenda wisira. Muhaso-we ni mugoti wa nanazi, Its remedy is chewing the stalk of a pineapple.
**Wisua, Wishua,** *n.* (wa), chaff, the husks of rice, bran of Indian corn or millet, etc.; (K.) paddy.
**Wivi,** *n.* (wa, no pl.), a sister-in-law, but only the sister of a husband, the term being used only between the females of each family.
**Wongolo,** *n.* (wa). *See* Uongolo.

## Y.

**Y,** the twenty-third letter of the alphabet, pronounced as in English.—[ED.]
**Ya,** (1) *gen. part.*, of.
(2) *prefix.* *See* Mumera; Dzano. It.
**Yaba,** or **Yabe.** Mutu akidungua ni muiya, be akikala yunalumira, 'ni ku amba: yaba e! or, yabe e!
**Yabayowe,** or **Yabeyowe.** Mutu mulume akifuererua, be akirira, wamba: yabayowe! yabayowe! muchangu we! or m'anangu we! baba e! ndu-

*Footer: 388*

---

## [PDF Page 402 — Dictionary Page 389 (Yaf — Yey)]

  guyangu e! musenangu e! etc.; but, Mutu muche akifuererua, be akirira, wamba: Mayowe! mulumangu e! etc.
**Yafu.**
**Yaha** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Ku fioga in Kir.), to tread.
**Yaika,** *v.n.* *See* Yaya. To melt.
**Yaisha,** *v.a.*, to melt, to smelt.
**Yako,** *pers. pron.*, thy, thine, at thy place.
**Yako,** *adv.*, there, he is there.
**Yakue,** *pers. pron.* *See* Kosi. He, his, at his place.
**Yalada** (Kig.), *n.* (ra, pl. Mayalada, or, contracted, Malada). Vatu hivano vadzikala yalada, ka-va-mera niasi, ni veruve.
**Yamba** (Kid.), *n.* (= Amba in Kir.). Ku-dzi-kukutiza yamba.
**Yangu,** *pers. pron.* *See* Ngombo. My, mine, at my place.
**Yao,** *pers. pron.*, they, theirs, at their place.
**Yari.** *See* Agira.
**Ya-vo.** *See* Nsimo; Digniua.
**Yaya,** *v.n.* *See* Fiaha; Lagula. To melt, to melt away, to disappear, to vanish out of sight. Muniu udziyaya, kua mvula. Wari hiu udziyaya, ka-u-rika kahiri. Huari naye vava; adzo-vo-hu-ukirakahuka-mu-ona, yudziyaya. Na mutu arie na uganga wa damana, wambua: yunayaya, ukasa-mu-ona.
  **Yayahika,** *v.n.* (= Kij., Fasaika?). Niama inayayahika.
  **Yayahuka,** *v.n.* (= Babayaka in Kij.), to scream, to shriek. Yudzihenduadze mutu hiye ayayahukaye. Muana yudzirira hata yudzihenda yayahuka.
  **Yayaisa,** or **Yayaisha,** *v.a.*
**Yayarika** (Kig.), *v.* (= Ku kaya and Ku piga kululu).
**Ya-yo** (= Tarare). *See* Torare.
**Ye,** (1) *poss. pron.* (rel. to the ya class), his, her, its.
(2) *See* Huka; Maruru; Rindikisika; Fukara; Mkuena; Polokania; Dundisa. Abridged of Iye, it is the pers. pron., He, she, it. In this meaning it is often added at the conclusion of a sentence in a way which seems redundant, but imparts a peculiar emphasis to a sentence.
**Ye,** *adj.* *See* Dumbele. Used of what is scattered about in plenty; when repeated, the idea of abundance is implied. Vitu viye, or, vi-ye, ye-ye. Gnombe zi-ye-ueruni. Atu a-ye-anaguira nioe.
**Yega.** Ah-muana yunahafuna madzere 'ye, yuhenda yega, yuhenda yega.
**Yegnie,** *pron.* *See* Manionioda; Lurero. Itself, themselves. Nazi-uki-i-panda, be mura kivoni-ikiuka yegnie, basi ndo uamba-vo: nazi inauka mpata.
**Yehu,** *pron.*, our, ours, at our place.
**Yeka** (Kid.), *v.a.* (= Chinga; Kinga in Kir. and Kij.). Ku yeka niumba (= Kir., Ku sika niumba).
**Yengeheka,** *v.n.*, to ripple. Kisima kidziidzala madzi dele, ganayengeheka.
**Yenu,** *pron.* (= Yehu), our, ours, at our place.
**Yera** (Kigiriama), *v.n.*, to go. Nahuyere bai.
**Yere.** *See* Mera.
**Yesa,** *v.a.* Una-m-hala muana wa mutu kuenda-m-yesa niasi niasi, hata babaye na mameye adzikudza fiola; kumania unda-hu-londera vio? Der., Museyi.
**Yeva** (Kid.), *v.* (= Ebea in Kij.; Evera in Kir.; Lewa in Kins.), to avoid, to evade a blow, etc.
**Yeya,** *v.a.* *See* Dengeleko; Hensia; Funda; Denga. To search, to seek. Muana hiyu yunayeya muno; ni muyezi. Ku-dzi-yeya.
  **Yeyeka,** *v.n.* Kuni udzi-zi-funga ku yeya,

*Footer: 389*

---

## [PDF Page 403 — Dictionary Page 390 (Yig — Yum)]

  be ka-zi-nda dzoloka sikibua vio; zi-funge, zi-ume; ah-uwe unafunga ku yeyeka dza muhoho.
  **Yeyera,** *v. rel.* Rero udzikuenda yeyera-vi?
  **Yeyerua,** *v.p.* Ni nga fika, waraka u na yeyerua mutu.
**Yigayiga,** *v.a.* (= Yugayuga, *q.v.*).
**Yino** (Kid.), *dem. pron.* (= Hino and Ino in Kir.). Hiyino ni fuko yino.
**Yo,** *poss. pron.*, (1) thy, thine.
(2) *rel. part.*, dze ya (= Hiyo). *See* Ngombo; Mioro; Komba; Ika.
**Yo,** or **Jo, Ja.**
**Yogoma,** or **Yoyoma,** *v.n.*, to make a noise. Kuna atu anayogoma, kuna-ni ko?
**Yogomue,** *n.* (= Lonso), noise.
**Yoma,** *v.n.* Usiri ukikala ungi, wambua: unayoma, dza uchi uirao. Usiri hio unayoma.
**Yombo.** *See* Mudzovi. Govu ra yombo.
**Yonga,** *v.n.*, to sway, as a tree or branch, with the wind. Munazi mure hebu muhi mure, muvudzu, be ukipigua ni peho, ukayonga. Mihi inayonga kua peho, hebu kua mutu ku kuera. Mutu huya tu ni mure, yuhenda yonga akienenda. Ni nta vi yonga, I shall sway them.
  **Yongayonga,** *v. reit.*
  **Yongoheka** (Kid.), *v.n.* (= Nemuka in Kir.).
  **Yongoya,** *v.n.* (= Ongoja in Kij.), to wait. Yuhenda yongoya k'amba ni kelia; yunapiga kidzangadza.
**Yosi,** *adj.* (rel. to the I- class). *See* Sasa; Unurisa. All, whole.
**Yoyo,** *adv.* *See* Dzangira. Welcome. Yoyo, mugeni! Welcome, stranger! Yoyo ni neno ra ku dzangira. Yoyo is a word of welcoming a friend or a stranger, etc. Yoyo mulumangu! udzihenda to kudza na afia. Yoyo baba! Yoyo nduguyangu!
**Yoyoma,** *v.n.* (= Ku tembea m'no in Kij.), to stroll about. Unayoyoma u-la-vi? Unahensa ku yoyoma muno, be u-la-vi?
**Yoyozua,** *v.p.* Ku yoyozua ni koma, ni pepo.
**Yu,** *part. interr.* *See* Miemia; Mugumi; Mulungu; Nona; Nga; Lasa. What? Mutu hiye yu-dze? What is that man? *i.e.* What is the matter with him? Yuari and Yuere, He or she was. Yuchari, or Yuchere (= Yukere). Yu kare ku hamba. Gnania yu lua-vi? Resp., Yukuenda gema, ka-dza-kudza. Yu-vi? Where is he or she? Yu-vi-e.
**Yua,** *v.n.*, to move from side to side, to swerve as an unfeathered arrow, to stagger, to reel. Mufui usiohandikirirua to ndio uyuao. Yudziyua, yudzilonda ku bua, He staggers from weakness or intoxication.
  **Yuayua,** *v. reit.* (= Kukutika). Mufui usiohandikirirua korokoro, uki-u-dzuva, ni ku yuayua.
  **Yufia,** *v.a.* *See* Yuva.
**Ynga,** *v.a.* (= Ku tukanisa). Peho inayuga mihi.
  **Yugana,** *v. reit.*
  **Yugayuga,** *v. reit.* (= Ku sukasuka), to shake. Mutu akidzukudza kirenge, kina dzira, be ni ku buma madzi, aka yugayuga, or, yigayiga.
  **Yugua,** *v.p.* Ku yugua ni peho.
**Yuguyugu,** *adv.* Nidzidzukula yuguyugu, pfuko i sinda.
**Yuka,** *v.n.* (= Ku gauka), to come off, as skin. Mutu yudzevia yudziyuka kikonde (= yudzigauka kikonde).
**Yuko,** *adv.*, there, in that place; he is there.
**Yumo,** *adv.*, in, within; he is within.

## [PDF Page 404 — Dictionary Page 391 (Yun — Zo)]

**Yuna,** *prefix*, 3rd pers. sing. pres. *See* Lasira. He is.
**Yunchu** (Kid.), *n.* (= Tundu la uso in Kij.), a hole.
**Yunda.**
**Yu-nga.** *See* Nga; Mbilikimo.
**Yungumika,** *v.n.* Madzi ga sinda, pfuko ina yungumika, gahenda gubu-gubu-gubu.
**Yuno,** *dem. pron.* *See* Hensia; Kikansi.
**Yuva,** *v.n.* (= Yua in Kij. ?). (K.) To wallop, spurt.
  **Yufia, Yuvia,** *v.a.* *See* Vungula. Ku yufia ni ku vosa wari na kibawa usimuagike. Ku yuvia mboga zi yuva-zo.
**Yu-vo,** he or she is there; pl. Avo, They are there.
**Yuya** (abbreviated from **Hiyuya**), *dem. pron.* *See* Mudangidangi; Foyeka. That one. Yuna kitu chani yuya, unga-mu-ona ni mudzufu.
**Yuya,** *v.n.* *See* Muvuye; Niuya. To be light. Der., Kiyuya; Muyuya; Niuya.
**Yuya-tu.**
**Yuyi,** *n.* (ra, pl. Ma-).
**Yuyu,** *dem. pron.* (= Hiyu). *See* Lala; Dzaga; Nga. This one.
**Yuze, Yudze.** *See* Udze; Udzi; Afiwa.
**Yuzi, Yudzi.** Yudzikuenda-vi? Where has he or she gone?

## Z.

**Z,** the twenty-fourth and last letter of the alphabet, much confused with *s*. The student must take care to discriminate between the two sounds, which are as distinct as they are in English.—[ED.]
**Za,** *gen. part.*, of. It denotes the pl. of nouns which have their sing. and pl. the same. Gnombe za, An ox of. Gnombe za, Oxen of.
